# Reframe v1.5 — UI/UX/a11y Audit Ledger (recovered)

**Read the tier before you act on an item.** This file mixes verified defects with unverified
claims, and the distinction is load-bearing.

## Provenance

A 320-agent sweep (16 surfaces x 20 lenses) with a 3-lens adversarial verification stage, run
2026-07-29/30. It consumed **1000 agents / 147.6M subagent tokens / 31,071 tool uses / 12.1 h**
and then **died at the workflow agent cap before its own synthesis step ran**. The work
succeeded — 1192 recorded results, **0 agent errors** — so only the orchestration ceiling
failed.

This ledger was therefore rebuilt deterministically from `journal.jsonl`, joined on `agentId`
(present in both the journal and every agent transcript). `surface` and `lens` are taken from
the PROMPT each agent was sent, not from the agent's self-report — the agents invented **731
distinct** free-text surface strings for 16 real surfaces, which also silently defeated the
original dedup.

Recovery scripts: `docs/validation/tools/join_by_agentid.py` (+ `extract_ledger.py`,
`join_verdicts.py`). These are now **tracked**. They used to live in `.audit/`, which
`.gitignore` declares disposable — so `git clean -xfd` destroyed the regeneration recipe,
i.e. the very property that made deleting the derived bytes safe.

## VOLUME IS NOT EVIDENCE

| tier | meaning | n |
|---|---|---|
| **CONFIRMED** | a majority of 3 independent adversarial verifiers declined to refute | **131** (7 critical, 124 high) |
| REFUTED | a majority refuted — recorded so they are not re-raised | 94 (4 critical, 90 high) |
| **UNVERIFIED** | the agent cap hit before any verifier ran — a **CLAIM**, not a defect | 2393 (45 critical, 617 high, 1219 medium, 512 low) |

Of the 225 findings that were actually checked, **94 were refuted — 42%.** Meanwhile the
agents self-rated `high` confidence on **2323 of 2618 (89%)** of their own findings. Treat any
unverified item as a hypothesis requiring its own evidence pass, and expect roughly 2 in 5 not
to survive one.

Two of the refuted criticals claimed the `aria-controls` bug still dangled on Gallery/Batch and
that "a one-line fix leaves both broken". The verifiers refuted them **correctly** — the fix
had already landed at the `TabBar` level plus MakeShorts' missing panel, so it was neither
one-line nor partial. The adversarial layer earned its cost.

## Already fixed (do not re-open)

The 7 confirmed criticals collapse into 3 root causes, all fixed in PR #310:

| root cause | fix |
|---|---|
| A persisted "Reframe to vertical" hub choice made Edit + the per-video Workspace **permanently unreachable** (restart-durable, no UI to clear) | `resumeFor('reframe')` -> `section`; the card deep-links straight to the Make Shorts owner. Class invariant + Edit<->Workspace seam invariant added. |
| The shared focus ring used `:where()` (**zero specificity**) so its `box-shadow` lost the cascade while its `outline: none` still applied — focused paint byte-identical to resting on ~17 of 18 `.feature-panel` surfaces; and box-shadow-only rings vanish under `forced-colors: active` | transparent real `outline` (survives High Contrast) + specificity-repair rules at (0,2,1) and (0,5,1). The gate was both-states-SILENT (`boxShadow !== 'none'` passes on a resting shadow) and is now a same-element focused-vs-unfocused paint diff. |
| Library "Remove" was a one-click, unconfirmed, unrecoverable delete that bypassed the only-surviving-copy guard | `library.remove({id, destroyManagedCopy?})` now defaults to NOT forcing; the refusal precedes the entity DELETE and both unlinks. |

**Still open from root cause C:** the renderer confirm UI — a two-step inline confirm reusing
`KeepCopyControl`'s established pattern, conditional copy that escalates when the managed copy
is the only one, and relabelling to "Remove from library...". The data-loss hole is closed; the
confirm is UX hardening on top.

## What this audit did NOT cover

- **2393 findings were never adversarially checked.** The 45 unverified CRITICALS are listed
  below as the highest-value queue; the 617 unverified highs and 1731 medium/low are in
  `docs/validation/v15-audit-ledger-unverified.md.gz` (tracked, gzipped — 6.66 MB raw,
  2.26 MB packed; it is the sole copy of those 2348 findings, so it is no longer left on
  one machine). Read it with `python -c "import gzip,sys; sys.stdout.write(gzip.open(...).read().decode())"`.
- ~~`e2e-sidecar`'s 3 failing tests (provider pool selects `local` over a configured cloud
  provider)~~ — **CLOSED.** By CI run 30612141716 this was down to 2 (`test_intel_director_
  plan_real_chat_editplan_over_http`, `test_intel_bestframe_thumbnail_real_jpg`), and both are
  fixed. The steer above ("instrument the pool eligibility filter") pointed at roughly the
  right place but the cause was one level up and was **not a product defect at all**: the
  `_cloud_settings` test fixture set only the legacy `routing.perFunction` map and never
  `routingPolicy`. The M3 RoutingPolicy is deliberately *authoritative* over
  `routing.perFunction` (a GATE-2 privacy fix) **and** fail-closed, so with it absent
  `resolve_route` returned `local` and a LOCAL-ONLY pool was built in which — per
  `_provider_for_function`'s own docstring — "NO cloud entry is built". The mock was never in
  the pool. The two REFUTED hypotheses recorded here were refuted correctly. Fixture fixed in
  the e2e-unblock PR; guard untouched.
- No runtime/performance profiling, no real screen-reader pass (findings are static + Chromium
  measurement), and forced-colors was measured under Playwright emulation rather than a real
  Windows High Contrast theme reaching Electron.

# CONFIRMED CRITICAL (7)

## Library "Remove" is a one-click, unconfirmed, unrecoverable delete that destroys the project manifest and force-destroys the only surviving copy of the video
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Renderer fires the RPC immediately with no confirm and no undo:
- `app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:159-166` — `<button ... aria-label={`Remove ${video.title}`} onClick={(event) => onRemove(video.id, event)}>Remove</button>`
- `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:368-384` — `handleRemove` does `setVideos(prev => prev.filter(...)); unselect(id); await rpc('library.remove', { id })` with zero interstitial
- `app/renderer/src/views/LibraryToolbar.tsx:64-70` + `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:398-414` — "Remove selected" loops `rpc('library.remove', {id})` over the whole selection, also unconfirmed

What the RPC actually destroys (irreversible, no trash):
- `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:143-147` — after `self.library.remove(video_id)` it unconditionally `unlink(missing_ok=True)`s `projects_dir/<id>.json` **and** `data_dir/thumbnails/<id>.jpg`
- `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:494-543` — that manifest holds `transcript`, `tracks`, `clips`, `audioTracks`, `settings`, i.e. every edit the user made to that video
- `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:330-348` — `remove()` calls `self.managed_evict(video_id, force=True)`; the docstring itself says force is used "because the user is deleting the video, so evicting even an irreplaceable copy (whose original is gone) is intended"
- `sidecar/media_studio/keepcopy.py:339-362` — `force=True` bypasses the refusal guard (`if not force and not self._original_exists(row): raise ... "the managed copy is the only surviving copy of the video"`) and then `victim_file.unlink()`

The codebase already has the confirm for exactly this destruction, on the same surface:
- `app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:20-21` — "A managed copy can be evicted back to its original via a two-step in-place CONFIRM (never a silent one-click destructive action)"
- `app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-193` — "Remove the managed copy?" + Remove/Cancel

Styling gives no danger signal at rest: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:386-392` makes `.library__remove-btn` transparent/borderless `--text-muted` (ghost voice); it only turns red on `:hover` (`shell.css:443-447`).

Behaviour is pinned by tests, so it is not a stray oversight: `app/renderer/src/views/Library.test.tsx:376-390` and `:1052-1058` assert the click goes straight to `library.remove`.
- why: A user who clicks the quietest button on a Library card — or "Remove selected" over a multi-video selection — permanently loses (a) all transcription/caption/track/clip edit state for those videos and (b) if they had opted into "Keep a copy" and the original has since moved or been deleted, the ONLY remaining copy of the video file itself. There is no confirm, no undo, and no trash anywhere in the renderer (grep for undo/trash finds only Timeline/Director undo, nothing library-scoped). The failure path only restores the in-memory list (`Library.tsx:380`); the unlinked manifest and unlinked managed bytes are gone regardless. The label "Remove" reads as "remove from this list", which is precisely the wrong mental model for what happens.
- fix: 1) Gate both `handleRemove` and `removeSelected` behind a confirm that states the real scope, reusing the established two-step inline pattern from `KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-193` (or the existing toast/dialog system) rather than a new mechanism. 2) Make the confirm content honest and conditional: name the video(s), and when `library.managedStatus` shows a managed copy whose original is missing, escalate the copy to "this is the only copy of this video — it will be deleted" instead of silently passing force. 3) Split the sidecar contract so the renderer can express intent: have `library.remove` accept `{id, destroyManagedCopy?: boolean}` and default to the non-force `managed_evict` behaviour so `keepcopy.py:352-357`'s existing LOUD refusal actually reaches the user, instead of the renderer inheriting `force=True` unconditionally. 4) Relabel the card action to match the scope (e.g. "Remove from library…" with the ellipsis signalling a confirm) and update `Library.test.tsx:376-390`/`:1052-1058` to assert the confirm arm plus a cancel arm.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim upheld; two scope corrections. (A) The UNCONDITIONAL damage is: a single unconfirmed click on the quietest control on a Library card (LibraryCard.tsx:159-166, ghost/borderless --text-muted at rest per shell.css:386-392, red only on :hover at shell.css:443-447) calls library.remove with no interstitial (Library.tsx:368-384, wired at Library.tsx:588), which hard-unlinks projects_dir/<id>.json and the poster (library_ops.py:145-146) - destroying every edit the user made to that video: transcript, tracks, clips, audioTracks, settings (library.py:497-506, 532-543). There is no trash and no undo (only .bak is the one-time SQLite-migration artifact at library.py:211-217). "Remove selected" repeats this over an arbitrary multi-selection, also unconfirmed (LibraryToolbar.tsx:64-70, Library.tsx:398-414). Both paths are pinned by tests (Library.test.tsx:376-390, 1052-1058). The user's ORIGINAL source file is never deleted (library.py:333), so in the common case the video itself is re-addable and only the edit state is lost. (B) CONDITIONAL arm - the headline should not state this unconditionally: destruction of the ONLY surviving copy of the video requires BOTH that the user opted into "Keep a copy" AND that the original has since moved/been deleted. Under those conditions library.py:343-345 calls managed_evict(video_id, force=True), which bypasses the LOUD refusal at keepcopy.py:352-357 and unlinks the managed bytes at keepcopy.py:359-361. This arm is reachable in shipped code (App.tsx:521 passes provenance={lineageActions}; lineageActionsClient.ts:66-72 wires the real RPCs; Settings.tsx:175 renders ManagedStoreMeter) and is precisely the scenario the feature is sold to protect against (KeepCopyControl.tsx:158). (C) DROP the sentence "the unlinked manifest and unlinked managed bytes are gone regardless" - it is wrong for the common failure modes. library_ops.py:144 runs self.library.remove() BEFORE the unlinks at 145-146, so if the RPC rejects (sidecar down, unknown id, KeepCopyError) the unlinks never execute, nothing was destroyed, and the optimistic restore at Library.tsx:380 is honest. The real (narrow) partial-destruction window is different and worth stating instead: keepcopy.py:359-361 unlinks the managed file OUTSIDE the DB transaction, before the entity DELETE at library.py:346-348, so a failure between those two steps leaves the managed bytes destroyed while the row survives. (D) The proposed fix is sound and its premise verified: library.remove accepts only {id} (library_ops.py:143) while library.managedEvict already accepts force? defaulting to False (library_ops.py:290-293), so threading intent through library.remove reuses an existing default-safe contract rather than inventing one.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim; the finding stands at critical as written. One optional headline tightening only: the headline clause "force-destroys the only surviving copy of the video" reads unconditionally, whereas the force-eviction destroys the managed byte-copy whenever one exists (library.py:343-345, proven by test_library.py:140-143) and that copy is the ONLY surviving copy only when the user opted into "Keep a copy" AND the original source has since moved or been deleted. The finding's own WHY-IT-MATTERS section already states this conditionally and correctly, so this is headline compression rather than a substantive overclaim. Tightened headline: 'Library "Remove" is a one-click, unconfirmed, unrecoverable delete that destroys the project manifest (all transcript/track/clip/audioTrack/settings edit state) and force-destroys the app-managed byte-copy — which is the only surviving copy of the video whenever the original source is gone.'

## Keyboard focus ring never paints on either Transcribe button: the global :where() ring has zero specificity and loses to .feature-panel button, while its `outline: none` still applies
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Live measurement in Chromium 150 against the REAL stylesheets (tokens.css + shell.css + panels.css served verbatim, with the exact DOM from app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:156,175-183):
  Start transcription -> {focusVisible: true, boxShadow: "rgba(255,255,255,0.28) 0px 1px 0px 0px inset, rgba(255,255,255,0.06) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset, rgba(242,163,60,0.3) 0px 2px 10px 0px", IDENTICAL_TO_RESTING: true, outlineStyle: "none"}
  Cancel -> {focusVisible: true, boxShadow: "rgba(255,255,255,0.05) 0px 1px 0px 0px inset, rgba(0,0,0,0.4) 0px 1px 2px 0px", IDENTICAL_TO_RESTING: true, outlineStyle: "none"}
DETECTOR CONTROL (proves the probe can see a real ring): .toptab -> boxShadow "rgb(18,22,32) 0px 0px 0px 2px, rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0px 0px 0px 4px" (= --focus-ring); #transcribe-language -> "rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0px 0px 0px 4px" (= --focus-glow).
CASCADE: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }` -> :where() contributes 0, so specificity is (0,1,0). Beaten for box-shadow by app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:344,353 `.feature-panel button { box-shadow: var(--elev-1) }` = (0,1,1) and by app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:411,417 `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary) { box-shadow: var(--accent-glow) }` = (0,4,1). Its `outline: none` still lands because no competitor sets `outline`.
THE FIX PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN-REPO but was never applied to .feature-panel buttons: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:482 comment "Class-scoped so it beats the global :where() focus-visible ring on these fields" (+ rule at :484-499 for inputs/selects), and app/renderer/src/panels/modelsSystem.css:58-63 `.models-system-panel button:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }`. A repo-wide grep for `button:focus-visible` returns only modelsSystem.css:58 — there is no `.feature-panel button:focus-visible`.
- why: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA, referenced by EN 301 549 / Section 508) fails on the two primary controls of this surface: a keyboard-only user tabbing through the Transcribe panel sees the language select light up, then gets ZERO visual change on "Start transcription" and ZERO on "Cancel" — the focused and unfocused states are byte-identical. They cannot tell which of the two they are on, and Enter either kicks off or kills a multi-minute transcription job. It compounds finding #2: focus is dumped to body at job start, so the user must tab back blind with no indicator. Existing gates cannot catch it — app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 exercises only `.toptab` and asserts `boxShadow !== 'none'`, which a .feature-panel button passes on its resting --elev-1/--accent-glow alone (a both-states-silent detector), and axe does not evaluate focus-ring visibility. BLAST RADIUS (honest scoping): the losing rule is the shared `.feature-panel button`, so every workspace feature panel is affected, not only Transcribe; I measured Transcribe.
- fix: Add a class-scoped button focus rule mirroring the input one already at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:484-499, e.g. `.feature-panel button:focus-visible, .shortmaker button:focus-visible, .timeline__toolbar button:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }` placed AFTER the accent-voice block at shell.css:409-420 so it also outranks `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)` — verify, since that selector is (0,4,1): either raise the focus selector's specificity to match (e.g. `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary):focus-visible`) or compose the ring with the resting shadow (`box-shadow: var(--focus-ring), var(--accent-glow)`). Better still, drop `:where()` from shell.css:49 so the shared ring carries real specificity. Then harden the gate: extend app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts to assert the focused computed box-shadow DIFFERS from the same element's unfocused value (not merely `!== 'none'`), and run it over a .feature-panel button — the current assertion is silent in the broken state.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED, correctly scoped: `:focus-visible` produces ZERO computed-style change on the Transcribe panel's action buttons, so they have no visible keyboard focus indicator (WCAG 2.4.7, AA) — severity SERIOUS/HIGH, not critical.

Mechanism (verified): app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }` is specificity (0,1,0) because `:where()` contributes 0. Its `box-shadow` is beaten by `.feature-panel button` (0,1,1) at shell.css:344,353 (--elev-1) and by `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)` (0,4,1) at shell.css:411,417 (--accent-glow); its `outline: none` still lands because no competing rule declares `outline`. Measured on app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:176 (Start, --accent-glow) and :180 (Cancel `.secondary`, --elev-1): exhaustive unfocused-vs-focused property diff = {} for both.

Harm, correctly scoped: because Transcribe.tsx:176 disables Start while running and :179 renders Cancel only while running, exactly ONE action button is ever tabbable — so there is no Start-vs-Cancel confusion and no wrong-Enter hazard. The real harm is that a keyboard-only user gets no indication at all that focus has reached the panel's primary action: the language select (shell.css:486, --focus-glow) lights up, then focus silently vanishes into an unmarked button. While a job runs, that ringless Cancel is the ONLY tabbable control in the panel.

Reach, correctly scoped: affected = any `<button>` matching `.feature-panel button`, `.shortmaker button`, or `.timeline__toolbar button` (shell.css:344-346) that has NO class-scoped `:focus-visible` rule of specificity ≥ its winning resting rule. That includes the primary `.actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)` of every panel that renders an `.actions` row — ModelsSystemPanel.tsx:649 (measured broken despite modelsSystem.css:58-63), Transcribe.tsx:175 (measured broken), plus Assets.tsx:149, Dub.tsx:360, NleExport.tsx:109, Refine.tsx:232, SemanticSearch.tsx:176, Convert.tsx:308, Diarize.tsx:142, Subtitles.tsx:233, SystemHealth.tsx:123, Tracks.tsx:192 (UNVERIFIED individually — I did not confirm each first-child lacks `.secondary`), and DirectorPanel's plain `.actions` buttons (measured broken). NOT affected (measured): `.models-system-panel` non-accent buttons, `.keep-copy__btn` (keep-copy-control.css:91), `.director-chip` / `.director-op` (directorPanel.css:73-75, :293-295), and the ~40 other class-scoped `:focus-visible` controls repo-wide.

Fix, corrected: a `.feature-panel button:focus-visible` rule at (0,2,1) is NOT sufficient — modelsSystem.css:58-63 proves that shape loses to (0,4,1). The rule must either match the accent selector's specificity (`.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary):focus-visible`) or, preferably, drop `:where()` from shell.css:49 so the shared ring carries real specificity and is composed with the resting shadow (`box-shadow: var(--focus-ring), var(--accent-glow)`) where an accent fill must be preserved.

Gate, corrected (this part of the original finding stands): app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 exercises only `.toptab` and asserts `boxShadow !== 'none'`, which a `.feature-panel` button passes on its resting --elev-1/--accent-glow alone. Replace it with a same-element unfocused-vs-focused computed-style DIFF over at least one `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child` — the current assertion is silent in the broken state.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands unchanged and confirmed: on `.feature-panel` buttons the global zero-specificity `:where(…):focus-visible` ring (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52, specificity (0,1,0)) loses its `box-shadow` to `.feature-panel button` (shell.css:344,353, (0,1,1)) and to `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)` (shell.css:411,417, (0,4,1)), while its `outline: none` still applies and additionally suppresses Chromium's UA focus outline by cascade origin — so both Transcribe buttons' focused computed style is byte-identical to their resting style (WCAG 2.4.7 AA failure). Only two subordinate clauses need tightening: (a) Start and Cancel are never simultaneously enabled-and-focusable (Transcribe.tsx:176 disables Start while running; :179 renders Cancel only while running), so the harm is "each control, when focusable, shows no focus indicator" rather than "the user cannot tell which of the two they are on"; (b) the blast radius is every `.feature-panel`-based panel EXCEPT that `.models-system-panel` non-accent buttons are already covered by app/renderer/src/panels/modelsSystem.css:58-63 — though its (0,2,1) selector would still lose to the (0,4,1) accent rule there.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not critical) — Keyboard focus produces ZERO visual change on .feature-panel buttons, including both Transcribe buttons: the global ring at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 is written with :where(), which contributes zero specificity, so at (0,1,0) its `box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` loses to `.feature-panel button` (shell.css:344,353, (0,1,1)) and to `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)` (shell.css:411,417, (0,4,1)) — while its `outline: none` still applies because no competitor sets `outline`, and tokens.css:206 makes box-shadow the only carrier of the ring. Measured in Chromium against the real tokens.css + shell.css with the DOM from Transcribe.tsx:156,176,180: focused box-shadow is byte-identical to resting on both buttons, outlineStyle "none", borderColor unchanged; a both-states control (injecting the class-scoped rule) does flip Cancel's shadow to --focus-ring, proving the probe is not silent.

Real harm, correctly scoped: the two buttons are NEVER simultaneously tabbable — Start is `disabled={running || !videoId}` (Transcribe.tsx:176) and Cancel only renders when `running && jobId` (:179); the measured running-state tab order is select -> Cancel -> body. So the harm is not "which of the two am I on" but that during a running job the ONE reachable control is Cancel, which aborts a multi-minute transcription on Enter with no focus indicator at all, immediately after the language select DID visibly light up (settled `rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px`) — so the panel teaches the user to expect an indicator and then withholds it. This is a WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) failure, but the app stays fully operable by mouse and by keyboard-with-Enter, and as a locally-installed single-user desktop tool it carries no Section 508 / EN 301 549 procurement obligation — cite those as design intent, not legal exposure. The stronger in-repo argument is that it silently violates the project's own declared contract at shell.css:48 ("One focus language everywhere: a double ring that reads on every surface").

Blast radius: 18 `.feature-panel` surfaces exist; only models-system-panel has its own button focus override (modelsSystem.css:58-63), so ~17 panels' generic buttons are affected. Verified: no `.feature-panel button:focus-visible` exists anywhere.

Fix — the simple class-scoped form is NOT sufficient, verified by measurement: `.feature-panel button:focus-visible` is (0,2,1) and still loses to (0,4,1), leaving the primary Start button ringless (only Cancel gains a ring). Use the higher-specificity selector `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary):focus-visible` alongside it, or compose (`box-shadow: var(--focus-ring), var(--accent-glow)`), or best, drop :where() from shell.css:49 so the shared ring carries real specificity. Gate: app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 currently tests only `.toptab` (:132) and asserts `not.toBe('none')` (:143), which a .feature-panel button passes on its resting --elev-1/--accent-glow alone; change it to assert the focused computed box-shadow DIFFERS from the same element's unfocused value and run it over a .feature-panel button — and allow the box-shadow transition (shell.css:496-498) to settle before reading, or a t=0 read returns transparent mid-interpolation shadows.

## Persisted "Reframe to vertical" hub choice makes the Edit tab permanently unreachable for that video (survives app restart, no UI to clear it)
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: CHAIN (all read, then executed):
- app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:103-113 — picking a hub card persists it: `rpc('settings.set', { [HUB_CHOICE_KEY]: map })`.
- app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:83-85 — `resumeFor('reframe')` returns `{ kind: 'workspace', tab: 'shortmaker' }`.
- app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:86-90 — on every mount the remembered choice is read and, for a workspace verdict, `setTab(resume.tab); setMode('workspace')`.
- app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:135-143 — mounts `<Workspace initialTab={tab} onOpenMakeShorts={onMakeShortsForVideo} />`.
- app/renderer/src/App.tsx:480 — App ALWAYS supplies `onMakeShortsForVideo`, so `onOpenMakeShorts` is never null.
- app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184 — `if (initialTab === 'shortmaker' && onOpenMakeShorts) onOpenMakeShorts(video.id)` fires on every mount → App routes to `makeshorts` (App.tsx:373-375) and unmounts Edit.
- Persistence is real and restart-durable: sidecar/media_studio/settings_store.py:508-528 merges and atomically writes any top-level key.
- No UI clears it: grep for `HUB_CHOICE_KEY` hits only Edit.tsx, taskHub.ts and their tests.

EXECUTED PROBE (temporary vitest file, since deleted): rendered the real `<Edit>` + real `<Workspace>` with `settings.get -> {taskHubChoiceByVideo:{v1:'reframe'}}`. Result: `onMakeShortsForVideo` called 1x on first entry and 1x again after unmount/remount (simulating a second click on the Edit rail tab) = 2/2 entries bounced, and `container.querySelector('.task-hub')` was null both times. Test passed (vitest 3.2.7, 171ms).

Aggravator: app/renderer/src/App.tsx:327-348 restores `lastOpenedVideoId` and does `setRoute({name:'edit'})` on launch, so a user in this state boots straight past Edit into Make Shorts.

Not covered by tests: app/renderer/src/views/Edit.test.tsx:11-27 STUBS Workspace, and app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.test.tsx:730-750 tests the redirect in isolation — the composed loop is untested.
- why: After one click on the "Reframe to vertical" card, the entire Edit phase (Subtitles, Timeline, Diarize, Refine, Dub, Convert, Recipes, Assets, Timeline export...) becomes unreachable for that video: every entry into Edit flashes the hub for one async tick then yanks the user to Make Shorts. Because the choice lives in the sidecar settings file, it survives window close and app restart, and there is no control anywhere in the UI to reset it — the user cannot see the hub long enough to pick a different card.
- fix: Make the 'reframe' resume non-redirecting. Cleanest: in app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:84-85 return `{ kind: 'section' }` for 'reframe' (mark "Last used" on the hub, exactly like 'shorts'/'director' at :91-92) so a remembered choice never auto-navigates out of Edit. Alternative: in app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184 drop the mount-time redirect and redirect only on an explicit tab CLICK (handleSelect, :189-198), leaving the deep-link to fall back to the workspace default. Either way, add a composed Edit+Workspace test that asserts re-entering Edit with a remembered 'reframe' leaves the user inside Edit.
- ⚠ scope correction: Scope corrections that tighten the wording without weakening the verdict (the defect stands):
(a) "the entire Edit phase becomes unreachable" → precisely: the Edit SECTION's Task Hub and the 13-tab per-video Workspace become unreachable for that video. The top-level Caption / Export / Deliver / Director / Make Shorts rails still accept the same video (App.tsx:484-506), and transcription is still reachable outside the Workspace (rpc/client.ts:188, features/repurposeTemplates.ts:36), so the user loses ~12 per-video tool panels, not all text/edit capability.
(b) "no UI to clear it" → literally true for clearing the CHOICE; an undiscoverable, state-forfeiting recovery exists (remove the library entry, then re-add for a new uuid — library.py:301-303 / :313).
(c) the bounce applies to entries #2..∞; entry #1 (the click on the card itself) landing in Make Shorts is the intended single-owner deep-link.
(d) severity better calibrated as HIGH than CRITICAL: no data loss, one video affected per bad choice, and the destination reached is a useful surface — but it is durable across restart, self-inflicted by one click on the most prominent card, and has no in-UI escape.
- ⚠ scope correction: Persisted "Reframe to vertical" hub choice makes the Edit tab effectively unreachable for that video (survives app restart; the only recovery is an undiscoverable race click).

The mechanism, the restart-durability, and the scope are all CONFIRMED as reported (chain verified line-by-line at HEAD dcb59e4b and reproduced executably with both-states controls). Three wording corrections:

1. "There is no control anywhere in the UI to reset it" is too absolute. Edit.tsx:61 initialises mode='hub', so TaskHub — including its "Advanced / all tools" button (TaskHub.tsx:167-172) — DOES render and is clickable on every entry, in the window before the async settings.get resolves. My probe landed that click: it persists {taskHubChoiceByVideo:{v1:'advanced'}}, and a remembered 'advanced' (taskHub.ts:88-89 -> tab:null) does not bounce, so the video is permanently un-trapped from the NEXT entry onward. Correct scoping: the reset control exists and is rendered but is not a usable affordance — winning the race requires clicking inside a sidecar-IPC round-trip window (real-world duration UNVERIFIED; I measured only a jsdom microtask), and nothing in the UI tells the user the button is the escape. State is therefore recoverable in-app, NOT only by hand-editing settings.json.

2. A SECOND defect the finding missed, which makes that escape even worse: the .then at Edit.tsx:81-91 guards only on `cancelled`, never on "the user has already picked", so the stale settings.get result OVERRIDES a landed Advanced click and bounces that entry anyway. Probe: 0 calls immediately after the click (tab bar present), then 1 call the moment the stale 'reframe' read resolves. So the escape click fixes only future entries, never the one it was made in.

3. One item in the illustrative tool list is wrong: "Timeline export" (NleExport) IS reachable outside Edit via the Deliver rail (Deliver.tsx:16, App.tsx:492-495). The other 8 tools named are genuinely trapped.

The proposed fix (taskHub.ts:84-85 return {kind:'section'} for 'reframe', plus a composed Edit+Workspace test) remains correct and should additionally guard the Edit.tsx:81-91 resolve against a user choice made while the read was in flight.
- ⚠ scope correction: A persisted 'reframe' hub choice makes the per-video Edit WORKSPACE unreachable for that library entry: every mount of Edit (app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:87-90) resumes to `initialTab='shortmaker'`, and Workspace's mount-time redirect (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184) fires `onOpenMakeShorts` — always wired at App.tsx:480 — so App re-routes to `makeshorts` (App.tsx:373-375) and unmounts Edit (App.tsx:468-483). 11 of the 13 WORKSPACE_TABS (Workspace.tsx:53-67) lose their only door — Transcribe, Search, Subtitles, Diarize, Refine, Tracks, Convert, Timeline, Dub, Recipes, Assets; `shortmaker` is the destination and `nle`/"Timeline export" retains a twin on the Deliver rail (App.tsx:492-495 → Deliver.tsx:16). The choice is restart-durable (settings_store.py:508-528 merges + :294-311 atomically writes any top-level key, and :385-387/:346-365 read it back unfiltered; the contract validator that would reject the undeclared key is not wired into dispatch per docs/rpc-contract-v2-migration.md:74) and no UI clears it (the only writer is Edit.tsx:109, reachable only from the hub the resume skips). The sole escape is destructive and undocumented: delete the library entry and re-add the file for a fresh random id (library.py:58/:313). Severity: high functional dead-end — no data loss and all other rails still work for that video.

## Picking "Reframe to vertical" once permanently soft-locks the Edit surface for that video (redirect loop)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Chain (all verified):
1. `app/renderer/src/views/TaskHub.tsx:141-159` card click → `onChoose('reframe')`
2. `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:118` `persist(choice)` → `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:109` `rpc('settings.set', {taskHubChoiceByVideo: …})` — durable, per video
3. On EVERY subsequent mount of Edit: `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:73-98` reads it back; `app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:84-85` `resumeFor('reframe')` → `{kind:'workspace', tab:'shortmaker'}` → `Edit.tsx:87-90` `setMode('workspace')` — the Task Hub is skipped
4. `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184` post-commit effect: `if (initialTab === 'shortmaker' && onOpenMakeShorts) onOpenMakeShorts(video.id)`
5. `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375` `setRoute({name:'makeshorts', videoId})` — the `edit` route is abandoned (`App.tsx:470-471` vs `:472-483`, different component types → Edit unmounts)
6. Re-entry re-triggers it: the "Edit" rail tab (`App.tsx:456`, handler `App.tsx:421-422`), re-opening from the Library (`App.tsx:351-353`), AND launch restore (`App.tsx:330-340`) all `setRoute({name:'edit'})`, remounting Edit → step 3 again.
No escape exists: `setMode('hub')` is called only at `Edit.tsx:74`, immediately overwritten by the resume; `Workspace.tsx:305` `← Library` never gets a click because the effect fires in the same post-paint tick.
- why: Nielsen #3 (user control and freedom — no clearly marked exit). After one click on the app's namesake card, the user can never again reach that video's Task Hub OR its Workspace — Transcribe, Search, Subtitles, Diarize, Refine, Tracks, Convert, Timeline, Dub, Timeline-export, Recipes, Assets (12 panels, `Workspace.tsx:53-67`) become unreachable for that video through the UI. Because the choice is persisted server-side, it survives restart, and `App.tsx:330-340` makes it fire on launch. There is no in-app control that clears `taskHubChoiceByVideo`.
- fix: `resumeFor('reframe')` should not return a `workspace` verdict for a choice that routes OUT of the workspace. Either (a) add a `{kind:'section'}` verdict for 'reframe' (`lib/taskHub.ts:84-85`) so it only marks "Last used" like `shorts`/`director` do (`taskHub.ts:90-92`), or (b) give TaskHub a real reframe destination and stop routing it through `shortmaker`. Independently, add a "Back to hub" affordance that calls `setMode('hub')` so ANY remembered choice is reversible.
- ⚠ scope correction: Picking "Reframe to vertical" once permanently soft-locks that video's Task Hub AND Workspace behind a redirect loop (Edit -> Workspace@shortmaker -> Make Shorts -> Edit). Verified executably. The persisted choice (Edit.tsx:109) survives restart because settings.set is schema-permissive (contract.schema.json:45 additionalProperties true; validate.py:64-70) and the store blind-merges it (settings_store.py:523-524), and no in-app control clears it (taskHubChoiceByVideo appears only at lib/taskHub.ts:99). Impact scoped correctly: 11 Workspace panels - Transcribe, Search, Subtitles, Diarize, Refine, Tracks, Convert, Short-maker-in-place, Timeline, Dub, Recipes, plus the non-video-scoped Assets - become unreachable for that video through the UI. NOT 12: Timeline export (NleExport) remains reachable for the same video via the top-level Deliver rail (Deliver.tsx:16,:75 with video={editVideo} from App.tsx:495), and Assets (Workspace.tsx:295) takes no videoId so it is a global panel rather than a per-video loss. The Caption (App.tsx:487), Export (:491) and Deliver (:495) rails also still function for that video, so the lock-out is of the Hub/Workspace surface specifically, not of all per-video editing.
- ⚠ scope correction: Picking "Reframe to vertical" once makes that video's Task Hub and Workspace permanently unreachable through any in-app affordance (12 of the 13 Workspace panels become inaccessible for that video), because the persisted 'reframe' choice resumes to a workspace verdict whose only effect is to route back OUT of the workspace. Precise scoping: the TaskHub is still committed for the sub-second window before the async settings.get resolves (Edit.tsx:61 vs :80-90), and a settings.get REJECTION leaves the user on the hub (Edit.tsx:92-94), so the lock is "no reachable exit affordance" rather than a literal never-rendered hub. The app is not bricked — Make Shorts still performs the reframe, and Caption/Export/Deliver/Director/Library remain reachable — so the defect is a permanent per-video dead-end of the Edit surface with no in-app reset (Nielsen #3), which reads as high-to-critical rather than app-breaking.
- ⚠ scope correction: Picking "Reframe to vertical" once permanently strands THAT VIDEO's Task Hub and Workspace behind an unconditional mount-time redirect to Make Shorts, with no in-app way to clear the remembered choice. Scope corrections to the original wording:

1. "12 panels become unreachable" is too wide. `editVideo` stays set, so the top-level rails still operate on that video: Caption (`App.tsx:484-487`), Export (`:488-491`), Deliver (`:492-495`), Director (`:496+`), Make Shorts (`:470-471`) — giving subtitles/convert/nle working top-level destinations. `assets` is a global panel (`Workspace.tsx:295`, `<Assets />` takes no videoId). Genuinely stranded for that video: transcribe, search, diarize, refine, tracks, timeline, dub, recipes (~8, not 12).

2. "soft-locks the Edit surface" overstates the blast radius: the Edit ROUTE is not locked — only that one video's hub/workspace. The choice map is per-video (`taskHub.ts:118-131`, proven by `Edit.test.tsx:233-249`), so other videos are unaffected, and the always-visible rail keeps every other top-level section reachable. The app is not bricked.

3. "redirect loop" is imprecise: it terminates deterministically on a functional Make Shorts screen with the video pre-selected (`App.tsx:373-375`), not an infinite spin. Because the settings read is async (`Edit.tsx:80`), the hub briefly flashes before the bounce rather than never rendering.

4. Severity is HIGH, not critical: no data loss, crash, or corruption, and the intent the user actually clicked (reframe) is served by the destination. The defect is the unreversible loss of the other per-video panels plus the Nielsen #3 missing exit.

Add the untested-seam finding as its own defect: `Edit.test.tsx:11-27` mocks Workspace without `onOpenMakeShorts`, so `Edit.test.tsx:132-141` asserts a Workspace landing that production wiring (`App.tsx:480`) contradicts — any fix must add a composition test that renders Edit with `onMakeShortsForVideo` wired.

## Edit-phase focus rings are box-shadow-only with `outline: none` — under Windows High Contrast (`forced-colors: active`) they render as NOTHING
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `dark-light-parity` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Only a DARK theme exists: `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:20` sets `color-scheme: dark` in the single `:root` block, and a repo-wide grep for `prefers-color-scheme|data-theme|light-mode|forced-colors|prefers-contrast` over `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe` returns ZERO CSS hits (detector validated: the same regex found `Highlight` in CHANGELOG.md:221, so it does search the tree). So the classic parity checks are N/A — but the app is not safe against the one palette override it cannot refuse.

Edit-phase anchors — all `outline: none` + `box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)`:
- `app/renderer/src/views/taskHub.css:102-106` (`.task-hub__card:focus-visible, .task-hub__advanced:focus-visible`) — the Edit phase's PRIMARY keyboard targets (`app/renderer/src/views/TaskHub.tsx:141-173`)
- `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:189-192` (`.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__export:focus-visible`)
- `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52` (the global `:where(button,[role="button"],[role="tab"],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible` base)
- `--focus-ring` is pure box-shadow: `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206`

EXECUTABLE PROOF (Playwright/Chromium, real `tokens.css` + verbatim CSS excerpts, both-states test):
```
=== forcedColors=none  colorScheme=dark ===
  focusRing_boxShadow = rgb(18,22,32) 0 0 0 2px, rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 4px
  focusRing_outline   = none
=== forcedColors=active  colorScheme=dark ===
  focusRing_boxShadow = none
  focusRing_outline   = none
=== forcedColors=active  colorScheme=light ===
  focusRing_boxShadow = none
  focusRing_outline   = none
```
- why: Chromium force-sets `box-shadow: none` in forced-colors mode. With `outline: none` already declared, a keyboard user in a Windows contrast theme has NO focus indicator anywhere in the Edit phase — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA) hard failure, and Reframe ships Windows-first (`*-win32.png` visual baselines). Windows ships a LIGHT contrast theme ("Desert"), so this is a real, one-toggle-away state, not a hypothetical. UNVERIFIED inline: I measured Chromium under Playwright emulation, not Electron receiving the live OS HC signal — the forcing mechanism is identical Blink code, but the OS→Electron propagation step is untested here; the settling experiment is `win.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` in `app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts` against the built app, or toggling Windows Settings → Accessibility → Contrast themes.
- fix: Change the base rule at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52` from `outline: none` to a transparent real outline, which forced-colors automatically substitutes with a system color while staying invisible normally:
```css
:where(button,[role="button"],[role="tab"],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid transparent;   /* becomes Highlight under forced-colors */
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: var(--focus-ring);
}
```
Apply the same swap at `taskHub.css:104` and `workspace.css:190` (and the ~30 sibling `outline: none` + focus-ring pairs the grep found). `app/renderer/src/views/taskHub.css:183` already shows the pattern that survives — `.task-hub__advanced` uses a real `border: 1px dashed var(--edge-strong)`, whose style is preserved under forced-colors.
- ⚠ scope correction: Edit-phase focus rings are box-shadow-only with `outline: none`, so under `forced-colors: active` every NON-TEXT keyboard target in the Edit phase renders NO focus indicator at all — measured IDENTICAL focused-vs-unfocused paint for the 4 Task Hub job cards and the "Advanced / all tools" escape (app/renderer/src/views/taskHub.css:102-106), the Workspace Export button (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:189-192), and every tab/button/checkbox/select falling through the global base rule (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52), because `--focus-ring` (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206) is pure box-shadow and Chromium force-sets `box-shadow: none` in forced-colors mode. Narrow the SURFACE line's "all tabs/inputs": a focused TEXT `<input>` does retain one cue — the blinking text caret (measured ANIMATED(caret), and it persists even with `caret-color: transparent`, since forced-colors forces the caret color). That caret is a text-insertion cue on text fields only; it is absent on every non-text control and does not soften the WCAG 2.4.7 failure on the primary anchors. Severity CRITICAL stands: the Edit phase's primary keyboard navigation has zero focus affordance one OS toggle away.
- ⚠ scope correction: Partial overclaim in SCOPE only (the defect itself stands): the sentence "a keyboard user in a Windows contrast theme has NO focus indicator anywhere in the Edit phase" is wider than the evidence. Correctly scoped: under forced-colors: active, every focus indicator that relies on the box-shadow-only pattern disappears — which includes the global base rule at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 (all button/[role=button]/[role=tab]/input/select/textarea/[tabindex]), the Task Hub primary targets at app/renderer/src/views/taskHub.css:102-106, and the Workspace Export button at app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:189-192. However, focus indicators built on a REAL outline do survive (outline width/style are preserved, outline-color is forced to a system color): app/renderer/src/panels/directorPanel.css:73-76, :293-296, :370-373 and app/renderer/src/components/captionBox.css:59-62 all use `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)` and remain visible. app/renderer/src/components/player.css:13-15 also survives because it sets box-shadow WITHOUT `outline: none`, leaving the UA outline intact (confirmed by my bare-button control). So the accurate claim is "every box-shadow-only focus ring — including the global base rule and the Task Hub landing's primary keyboard targets — renders as nothing", not "no focus indicator anywhere in the Edit phase". Severity is better calibrated as HIGH/SERIOUS than CRITICAL, because the state requires an OS contrast theme to be enabled; the defect, the WCAG 2.4.7 AA failure against the project's self-adopted gate (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:40,53), and the proposed fix are all confirmed.
- ⚠ scope correction: Focus rings are box-shadow-only with `outline: none` app-wide (the global zero-specificity base rule at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52, plus ~30 sibling pairs incl. app/renderer/src/views/taskHub.css:102-106 and app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:189-192; `--focus-ring` is pure box-shadow at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206). Under `forced-colors: active` Chromium forces `box-shadow: none`, so the designed double ring is annihilated everywhere — CONFIRMED by executable probe.

However, the resulting TOTAL loss of focus indication is confined to controls with NO border geometry, because forced-colors substitutes the system Highlight color into the focused element's `border-color` (measured: off=[1px solid rgb(0,0,0)] -> ON=[1px solid rgb(55,0,110)], reverting on blur). Genuinely-broken set in the Edit phase: the Workspace tab strip `.tab` (`border: none`, app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1047) and the tabbar disclosure `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` (`border: none`, app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:116). These two have no visible keyboard focus indicator under Windows High Contrast — a real WCAG 2.4.7 concern.

The 4 Task Hub job cards and the "Advanced / all tools" escape (app/renderer/src/views/TaskHub.tsx:141-173; borders at taskHub.css:78 and :183), the Export button, and all `input`/`select` controls DO retain a focus-dependent Highlight border and are NOT blank. Severity: serious/moderate for the two borderless controls, NOT critical, and NOT "nothing anywhere in the Edit phase".

Residual disclosed INLINE: the surviving indicator on bordered controls is a 1px COLOR-ONLY change (ButtonBorder -> Highlight) whose perceptibility is palette-dependent, and UNVERIFIED against real Windows High Contrast themes — I measured under Playwright's emulated forced-colors palette, the same channel limitation the original finding admitted, so OS->Electron propagation remains untested. Settling experiment: toggle Windows Settings -> Accessibility -> Contrast themes against the packaged app, or `win.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` in app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts.

The proposed fix (swap `outline: none` for `outline: 2px solid transparent` + `outline-offset`) is CORRECT and verified by probe (-> `solid 2px rgb(55,0,110)` under forced-colors, invisible normally), and should be applied — but prioritized at the two borderless controls, which are the only places focus indication is actually absent.

## Persisted "Reframe to vertical" hub choice permanently locks the user out of the entire per-video Workspace (bounce loop, survives restart, no UI to clear)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Picking the card persists `taskHubChoiceByVideo[videoId]='reframe'` (app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:103-114, key at app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:99). On every later mount of Edit for that video: app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:80-91 reads the choice → `resumeFor('reframe')` returns `{kind:'workspace', tab:'shortmaker'}` (app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:83-85) → `setMode('workspace')` → renders `<Workspace initialTab='shortmaker' onOpenMakeShorts={onMakeShortsForVideo}>` (app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:135-143). Workspace's mount effect then immediately redirects OUT: app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184 calls `onOpenMakeShorts(video.id)` → app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375 `setRoute({name:'makeshorts', videoId})`, unmounting Edit. Clicking the Edit tab again re-enters at App.tsx:421-423 `setRoute({name:'edit'})` and repeats. The only Workspace escape is "← Library" (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:304-311), which is never reachable because the redirect fires on mount. `HUB_CHOICE_KEY` appears in no settings UI (only Edit.tsx, taskHub.ts and their tests). At launch the loop is entered automatically: app/renderer/src/App.tsx:327-348 restores `lastOpenedVideoId` and sets route 'edit' (:339). The Edit tests mock Workspace and never pass `onMakeShortsForVideo` (app/renderer/src/views/Edit.test.tsx:132-141), and App tests mock both Edit and MakeShorts (app/renderer/src/App.wf-other-0.test.tsx:39-40), so no test covers the composed path.
- why: After one click of the Reframe card, that video's whole 13-tab Workspace — Transcribe, Search, Subtitles, Diarize, Refine, Tracks, Convert, Timeline, Dub, Timeline export, Recipes, Assets (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:53-67) — becomes permanently unreachable, and the app boots straight into Make Shorts instead of the Library. The Edit tab silently "does nothing". taskHub.ts:73-74 already documents that a section choice must NOT auto-resume because "it would bounce the user out of the just-opened video" — WU-3a4's shortmaker→section redirect turned 'reframe' into exactly that case without updating `resumeFor`.
- fix: Make `resumeFor('reframe')` return `{kind:'section'}` (app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:83-85) so it only marks "Last used", matching the 'shorts'/'director' rationale at taskHub.ts:73-74. Alternatively, have Edit skip auto-resume for any choice whose Workspace tab redirects out (i.e. 'shortmaker' when `onMakeShortsForVideo` is wired), and add a reachable "Change tool" affordance in the Workspace header that returns to the Task Hub and clears the persisted choice. Add an App-level integration test that renders the real Edit+Workspace with `onMakeShortsForVideo` wired and a persisted 'reframe' choice, asserting the Workspace is reachable.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim; the finding stands as written. If tightened for maximum precision: "A persisted 'reframe' hub choice makes that ONE video's per-video Workspace (the 12 non-Short-maker tabs) unreachable through every in-app path — Edit bounces to Make Shorts on mount (taskHub.ts:83-85 -> Edit.tsx:86-90,137-142 -> Workspace.tsx:180-184 -> App.tsx:373-375), and re-entering via the Edit tab (App.tsx:421-423) repeats it. It persists to settings.json (settings_store.py:523; contract params are additionalProperties:true) so it survives restart, and there is NO settings UI or in-app affordance to clear it ('taskHubChoiceByVideo' appears only at taskHub.ts:99). The only recoveries are non-UI: hand-editing %APPDATA%/media-studio/settings.json, or a settings.get failure (Edit.tsx:92-94) leaving the hub up long enough to re-pick. Other videos and the top-level Caption/Export/Deliver/Director surfaces for that video remain reachable. No unit or e2e test covers the composed path." Also correct the PROPOSED FIX: resumeFor('reframe') -> {kind:'section'} alone is WRONG because Edit.tsx:126-130 falls through to onDirector?.(), sending the reframe card click to the Director section; pair it with an explicit reframe -> onMakeShortsForVideo branch in handleChoose, or prefer the skip-auto-resume-plus-Change-tool-affordance option.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim holds; three wordings are wider than the evidence and should be tightened (C2-style overclaim trim, not a refutation):

1. SEVERITY: high/major, not critical. No data loss, no security impact, no crash. And it IS recoverable out-of-band on this single-user local desktop app — the owner can hand-edit `taskHubChoiceByVideo` out of the on-disk settings JSON (sidecar/media_studio/settings_store.py:508-528 writes plain merged JSON). "No UI to clear" is accurate; "unrecoverable" would not be.

2. "bounce loop" overstates the dynamics. Each Edit entry redirects ONCE and settles at route `{name:'makeshorts', videoId}` (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375); Edit unmounts and nothing re-fires. There is no runaway re-render or CPU spin. Accurate framing: the Edit tab is a one-way dead end / black hole for that video — it silently does nothing.

3. SCOPE is per-video and per-surface, not app-wide. Only the affected video's Edit→Workspace path dies. Other videos still land on the hub (choice map is keyed by videoId, taskHub.ts:105-111), and Library, Make Shorts, Caption, Export, Deliver, Director and Settings all remain reachable via the top tab strip (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:452-464). The app is not bricked.

Correctly-scoped claim: "Persisting the 'reframe' hub choice makes that video's Edit tab a permanent one-way dead end — every entry (including automatic launch restore via lastOpenedVideoId) immediately redirects to Make Shorts, leaving ~10 Workspace panels unreachable for that video with no in-app way to clear the choice; recoverable only by hand-editing the settings JSON. Root cause: resumeFor('reframe') returns a workspace resume onto the one tab the Workspace layer intentionally redirects away from (taskHub.ts:83-85 vs Workspace.tsx:180-184)."

## No focus indicator paints on ANY button in the reframe review loop — the ring is out-specified by the base button rule
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 sets `:where(button, [role="button"], …):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }` — `:where()` zeroes its argument, so the rule's specificity is only (0,1,0). app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:341-363 then sets `.shortmaker button, .feature-panel button, .timeline__toolbar button, … { box-shadow: var(--elev-1); }` at (0,1,1), and shell.css:409-420 sets `box-shadow: var(--accent-glow)` on the accent voice — both beat the focus rule, while `outline: none` still applies. Measured in Chrome against the REAL repo sheets (tokens.css + shell.css + shortmaker.css + shortmaker-p3.css linked into a static harness), focusing each control and reading getComputedStyle: control button with no class rule → `boxShadow: "rgb(18,22,32) 0 0 0 2px, rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 4px"` (positive control — the probe fires); `#reinstate` (.shortmaker button) → `boxShadow: "rgba(255,255,255,0.05) 0 1px 0 inset, rgba(0,0,0,0.4) 0 1px 2px"` (= --elev-1), `outlineStyle: "none"`; `#approve` → `--accent-glow`, `outlineStyle: "none"`; `#factors` (.sm-factors-toggle) → `--elev-1`, `outlineStyle: "none"`. All four reported `matches(':focus-visible') === true`, so the pseudo-class was active and the ring simply lost the cascade. Affected controls: app/renderer/src/features/CandidateList.tsx:155-189 (4 nudge buttons + Reset), :191-207 (Approve/Discard/Reinstate), :121-132 (Factors), app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:968-974 (Export approved). shell.css:482 proves the authors knew the `:where()` ring is weak — "Class-scoped so it beats the global :where() focus-visible ring on these fields" — and patched it for INPUTS at shell.css:484-499, but never for buttons. Every other panel remembered to (features/export/export.css:253,312,334,422,518,549,571; panels/directorPanel.css:73,293; features/caption/*.css) — the ShortMaker/feature-panel button family is the gap. No `.shortmaker button:focus-visible` or `.feature-panel button:focus-visible` rule exists anywhere in app/renderer/src/**/*.css.
- why: A keyboard user pressing Tab through the reframe review loop lands on Approve, Discard, Reinstate, the four crop/boundary nudges, and the terminal "Export approved" action with ZERO visual change — the native outline is suppressed and its replacement never renders. Focus-state contrast is effectively 1.00:1. This is WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level A) plus 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA), i.e. an a11y-law failure, on the surface whose own CSS advertises a keyboard workflow (shortmaker.css:96-117 documents the J/K/Space/A/X loop). Partial mitigation, disclosed: the `.sm-review` container (features/CandidateReview.tsx:93,99 — tabIndex=0) DOES get the ring, so the J/K container loop is indicated; the Tab path through the individual action buttons is not. The e2e a11y gate cannot catch this — app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 tests focus-visible only on `.toptab`, which has no competing box-shadow (components/topTabBar.css sets box-shadow on `.toptabs` at :21, not on `.toptab`), so it passes on the one element that works.
- fix: Add an explicit class-scoped focus rule mirroring the input treatment at shell.css:484-499: `.library__add-btn:focus-visible, .library__remove-btn:focus-visible, .workspace__back:focus-visible, .feature-panel button:focus-visible, .shortmaker button:focus-visible, .timeline__toolbar button:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }` placed after shell.css:420 so it also beats the accent-voice rule. Do NOT stop there: `var(--focus-ring)` alone is under-contrast on the planes these buttons sit on — I measured the `--accent-edge` band at 2.93:1 against `--surface-raised` (a resting `.sm-candidate`) and 2.58:1 against `--surface-hover` (a selected/hovered card, shell.css:1362-1369), both below the 3:1 that 1.4.11 requires, and the inner 2px `--surface-bg` gap ring is 1.12:1 on a raised surface so it contributes nothing. Either raise `--accent-edge` toward the solid `--accent` (`#f2a33c` measures 7.73:1 on raised) for the ring band, or compose the ring as `0 0 0 2px var(--surface-deep), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent)`. Add a conformance test that asserts a focused `.shortmaker button` computes a box-shadow different from its resting one.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped version (widened, and with the false attribution removed): "Focus indicators are suppressed on the ENTIRE raised/accent button family app-wide, not just the ShortMaker review loop. shell.css:49-52 emits the only ring at (0,1,0) because :where() zeroes its argument, while shell.css:341-346 (--elev-1) at (0,1,1), shell.css:409-420 (--accent-glow), shell.css:387-392 (box-shadow:none, same specificity but later), timeline.css:79-99 and shell.css:260-264 (.routing-toggle__btn.is-active) all out-rank it — and `outline: none` (shell.css:50) still applies. Every <button> matched by `.shortmaker button`, `.feature-panel button`, `.timeline__toolbar button`, `.library__add-btn`, `.library__remove-btn`, `.workspace__back`, plus the active routing-toggle segment, therefore paints an unchanged box-shadow on Tab (pixel-hash-identical: app/_fcout.json t-btn). The ShortMaker review loop is the worst-affected instance (CandidateList.tsx:121-132 Factors, :156-188 four nudges + Reset, :193-205 Approve/Discard/Reinstate, CandidateReview.tsx:156-171 sort toggle, ShortMaker.tsx:966-975 Export approved) because that surface advertises a keyboard workflow (shortmaker.css:96-117), NOT because it is the only gap: only models-system (modelsSystem.css:58-63) and director-panel (directorPanel.css:73,293,370) among the `.feature-panel` family added a class-scoped ring; roughly fourteen other feature panels did not. Residual signals, disclosed: the `.sm-review` container itself does get the ring (nothing sets box-shadow on it; shortmaker.css:98-100 sets only outline:none) and shortmaker.css:115 brightens the keyboard legend on :focus-within — neither identifies which control has focus, so WCAG 2.4.7 still fails per-control. The fix must be an `outline`-based (or forced-colors-fallback) ring at >=3:1 — a box-shadow-only ring computes to `none` under forced-colors:active (app/_fcout.json, 'active' block) — and the conformance test should assert focused != resting for `.shortmaker button`, `.feature-panel button` and `.timeline__toolbar button`, because a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 probes only `.toptab` and its `boxShadow !== 'none'` assertion would pass on --elev-1."
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim on substance; only the severity band warrants narrowing. Correctly scoped: "SERIOUS/HIGH (not critical): the eight ShortMaker review-loop buttons paint no focus indicator at all — `.shortmaker button` (shell.css:341-346, (0,1,1)) and the accent voice (shell.css:409-420) out-specify the `:where()` focus ring (shell.css:49-52, (0,1,0)) for box-shadow while its `outline: none` still applies, so focused and resting computed box-shadow are byte-identical (measured 8/8). Focus indication is not merely under-contrast but absent, and moving focus from the `.sm-review` container into a button REMOVES the container ring, leaving nothing indicated. WCAG 2.4.7 (A) and 1.4.11 (AA) fail. It is not critical because the app's advertised J/K/Space/A/X path (aria-keyshortcuts at CandidateReview.tsx:98) retains container-level indication and no data is lost — only the Tab path through the individual action buttons is blind. The `:focus-within` legend brightening at shortmaker.css:115 is not a mitigation: it does not change on container→button or button→button transitions."

# CONFIRMED HIGH (124)

## "Save short" / "Save SRT separately" report success but perform no action
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145 — `const handleSaveShort = useCallback(() => setManualNote('Saved the short.'), []);` and :146 `handleSaveSrt = () => setManualNote('Saved the SRT sidecar.')`. Both are wired into the real tray at MakeShorts.tsx:272-274, and OutputTray.tsx:139-148 renders the buttons precisely because the handlers are present. Neither handler calls any RPC, writes a file, or opens a save dialog. The behaviour is pinned by a passing test: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:497-502 asserts only the note text. The intent is admitted inline at MakeShorts.tsx:143-144 ("save seams … so the action is acknowledged").
- why: Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status) inverted into an actively false signal. Failure scenario: the user exports manual ranges with the default `subtitleMode: 'burn'` (OutputTray.tsx:37), so no SRT file exists anywhere. They click "Save SRT separately" and the UI answers "Saved the SRT sidecar." — a definitive success message for an operation that never ran. The user then goes looking for an SRT that was never written, or ships without it believing it exists. A silent no-op would be less harmful than a confirmed one.
- fix: Either implement the actions (a native save dialog + a copy/`shortmaker.export`-sidecar write, keyed off the clip paths returned at MakeShorts.tsx:177-186 which are currently discarded), or stop passing `onSaveShort`/`onSaveSrt` so OutputTray.tsx:139-148 hides the buttons entirely (the component already gates each button on its handler). If they must stay as seams, label them for what they do ("Reveal in folder") and delete the fabricated past-tense confirmations.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding stands, but the two halves are asymmetric and should be scoped separately rather than both at "high":

(1) "Save SRT separately" — CONFIRMED HIGH, and worse than stated. MakeShorts.tsx:146 fabricates "Saved the SRT sidecar." while calling nothing. No SRT is written by the shortmaker export in any mode (no .srt write in sidecar/media_studio/features/*.py; only a comment at tracks.py:181). The backend explicitly delegates the SRT to subtitles.export via this exact button (shortmaker.py:345-346, :388-392), so with subtitleMode='sidecar' — reachable pre-export through persisted Settings (MakeShorts.tsx:124 -> :169; MakeShorts.test.tsx:448-471) — the user gets a caption-free clip AND no subtitle file, confirmed as saved. Fix is a one-call wiring to the already-exposed client.subtitles.export (rpc/client.ts:208 -> handlers/media_ops.py:85-96), following the app's own pattern at features/Subtitles.tsx:193-198 (surface the returned res.path, never a fabricated past tense).

(2) "Save short" — real but LOWER severity than the finding implies; this is the overclaimed half. The short DOES exist on disk: shortmaker.export writes the clips and returns {clips:[{path}]} (shortmaker.py:1303-1308, _clip_payload :1311-1321). So "Saved the short." is redundant and mechanically false, not artifact-destroying. Its actual defect is INFORMATION REGRESSION: because both handlers write the same `manualNote` state, clicking it overwrites the only true receipt — `Exported ${exported.length} clip(s) from your ranges.` (MakeShorts.tsx:187) — with a fabricated confirmation. Correct remedy is either a real reveal-in-folder using the clip paths currently discarded at MakeShorts.tsx:177-186 (only .length is consumed at :187), or dropping the onSaveShort prop so OutputTray.tsx:139-143 hides the button.
- ⚠ scope correction: Both tray handlers perform no action, but the harm is asymmetric and should be scoped that way. "Save SRT separately" is the genuine false confirmation: under the default subtitleMode:'burn' no .srt is ever produced (shortmaker.py:399-400; writesSubtitleFile at outputOptions.ts:69-71 is never fed because OutputTrayState has no saveSrt field), so "Saved the SRT sidecar." asserts a file that does not exist — high severity, and doubly indefensible because subtitles.export already works and is really called at Subtitles.tsx:193. "Save short", by contrast, is a redundant no-op rather than a factually false one: runManualExport already wrote the clips to disk before the tray is ever shown (MakeShorts.tsx:171-188), so "Saved the short." happens to be true about the file's existence; its real defects are that the button performs no save-as/reveal, discards the clip paths returned at MakeShorts.tsx:177-186, and overwrites the useful "Exported N clip(s)" note. Drop "a silent no-op would be less harmful than a confirmed one" as a blanket claim about both buttons and apply it to the SRT button only.
- ⚠ scope correction: SHARPENING (not an overclaim — the finding stands as written; this only makes the per-button asymmetry explicit): "Save short" and "Save SRT separately" are both dead controls that emit past-tense success text and perform no save action (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145-146, rendered via OutputTray.tsx:139-148, pinned green by MakeShorts.test.tsx:498,500-502 @48e0d717 / :555,557-559 @HEAD). The harms differ: "Save SRT separately" is an ACTIVELY FALSE confirmation — with the default subtitleMode='burn' (OutputTray.tsx:37) no .srt is produced anywhere (zero .srt/.ass writes in sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py) and `saveSrt` never reaches the export payload (MakeShorts.tsx:166-170), so "Saved the SRT sidecar." names a file that does not exist. "Save short" is a REDUNDANT-but-true confirmation: the clip is already durably written to exports/shorts-<videoId>/ and listed by shorts.list (docs/PLAN-P4-REFRAME-OPUSCLIP.md:285), so it misleads about agency (no save-as/reveal happened) rather than about existence. Both fixes are already plumbed: client.subtitles.export (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:207-208 — the contract sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:345-346 explicitly expects the renderer to honor) and shell.showItemInFolder (app/main/preload.ts:25,164); or omit the handlers so OutputTray.tsx:139-148 hides the buttons.

## Caption & style editor is a dead control for the AI moment-pick path — the primary flow
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: MakeShorts.tsx:247-253 mounts the full `CaptionDesigner` (drag-to-position box + style picker + customizer, CaptionDesigner.tsx:82-156) under the heading "Caption & style" with the copy "Drag the caption box to position it, pick a style — previewed live on your video" (MakeShorts.tsx:242-246). Its `design` reaches the AI flow ONLY as `initialControls.captionStyle` (MakeShorts.tsx:233-236), and ShortMaker reads `initialControls` once in a `useState` initializer — `useState<ShortMakerControls>(() => sanitizeControls(initialControls ?? {}))` (ShortMaker.tsx:161-163) — with no key on the element (MakeShorts.tsx:230-237) and no syncing effect. The AI export calls `buildExportParams(videoId, approvedCandidates(items), clean, audioTrackId)` with four args (ShortMaker.tsx:651; same at :744-747), so `output` defaults to `{}` (shortMakerPresets.ts:165) and `captionPosition` / `captionOverride` / `subtitleMode` are never sent (shortMakerPresets.ts:188-190). The AI panel also carries its OWN competing "Caption style" select (ShortMakerControls.tsx:152-162).
- why: Nielsen #2/#4 (match to the real world, consistency). The AI section renders before the designer (MakeShorts.tsx:225 vs :247), so ShortMaker is always already mounted when the user touches the designer — every designer edit is guaranteed not to reach the AI export. Failure scenario: user picks a video, drags the caption box to the top band and selects "Karaoke" in the big live-preview editor, runs AI moment-pick, approves two clips and clicks "Export approved" — the clips come out in the persisted default style at the default bottom band. The manual path below it honours all three fields (MakeShorts.tsx:161-170), so identical on-screen settings produce different output depending on which button you press. Worse, `opusclip-karaoke` is selectable in the designer's full catalog but absent from the AI select, which renders only `CAPTION_STYLES` (shortMakerLogic.ts:202-235, 246-249).
- fix: Make the design authoritative for both paths: pass `captionDesignWire(design)` (position + override + style) and `tray.subtitleMode` down to ShortMaker and have `runExport`/`runBatch` forward them as the 5th `output` argument to `buildExportParams`; replace ShortMakerControls' duplicate "Caption style" select with a read-only reference to the shared design (or lift `controls.captionStyle` into the parent so both controls edit one value). Until wired, move the designer inside the manual section and title it "Caption & style (manual ranges)" so the scope is honest.
- ⚠ scope correction: Caption & style editor does not reach the AI moment-pick export — position, band and every Customize… knob are structurally unreachable; the style swatch only takes effect after an unrelated remount. SURFACE: Make Shorts — front door (Make tab). SEVERITY: high (unchanged). The "Caption & style" section (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:251-264) is presented unscoped, above the manual section and below the AI section, but its output splits three ways for the AI path: (a) design.box (drag + Top/Center/Bottom bands) and design.override (every Customize… knob) are UNCONDITIONALLY dead — ShortMaker.tsx:651 and :746 call buildExportParams with four args so `output` takes its `{}` default (shortMakerPresets.ts:165) and captionPosition/captionOverride are never emitted (:188-190); ShortMaker.tsx contains zero references to either field, and no sidecar fallback exists (shortmaker.py:1382-1390 reads them only from params; the persisted box uses the different key defaultCaptionBox, captionPreferences.ts:55). (b) subtitleMode is doubly dead: never sent by the AI path, and its control (OutputTray) renders only after a completed MANUAL export (MakeShorts.tsx:279-286, trayOpen set at :188), so an AI-only user can never have set it. (c) design.style is NOT permanently dead but is nondeterministic: it reaches ShortMaker only through the useState-once seed (ShortMaker.tsx:161-163; initialControls occurs 3x total, no syncing effect, no `key` at MakeShorts.tsx:240-247), so an in-place designer edit is a no-op — yet the SAME edit silently takes effect after any remount, because `design` (MakeShorts.tsx:84) survives the tab guard (:214, leave to Produced shorts/Batch and return) and the selection guard (:232, re-pick "Select a video…"). Switching to a different video does not remount (ShortMaker.tsx:233-239). Fix unchanged in direction: forward captionDesignWire(design) + subtitleMode as the fifth `output` argument from ShortMaker's runExport/runBatch, and collapse the duplicate select into the shared design (or lift controls.captionStyle to the parent); until then rename the heading to scope it honestly. Add a regression test asserting a designer edit reaches the AI export payload — MakeShorts.test.tsx already exposes data-init-caption-style (:84) but never asserts propagation.

## Switching source video keeps the previous video's manual ranges, note and open tray — exports the new video at the old timestamps
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The picker's `onChange` only sets `selectedId` (MakeShorts.tsx:208-219); MakeShorts has no effect keyed on `selectedId`, so `manualNote`, `manualError` and `trayOpen` (MakeShorts.tsx:78-81) survive the switch. `<ManualInterval onSubmit={…} busy={manualBusy} />` (MakeShorts.tsx:258) carries no `key`, and ManualInterval owns `ranges` in local state (ManualInterval.tsx:35) with no reset path, so the range list persists verbatim. `submit()` (ManualInterval.tsx:59-61) then feeds those stale ranges to `runManualExport`, which exports them against the CURRENT `selectedId` (MakeShorts.tsx:166-171). The identical hazard is explicitly guarded on the AI path — ShortMaker.tsx:234-249 resets per-video state on `videoId` change, with the comment "‘Export approved’ would carve the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps."
- why: Nielsen #5 (error prevention) and #1. Failure scenario: user adds 12:00→12:40 for a 40-minute interview, switches the picker to a 90-second clip, and the range list still reads "12:00 → 12:40" with "Make shorts from ranges" enabled. The export runs past the end of the new source and either fails opaquely or produces garbage. Compounding it, the stale success note ("Exported 3 clip(s) from your ranges.", MakeShorts.tsx:187) and the still-open Output Tray (MakeShorts.tsx:269) now sit under a different video, asserting a result that belongs to the previous one.
- fix: Add a `useEffect` on `selectedId` in MakeShorts that clears `manualNote`, `manualError` and `trayOpen`, and give ManualInterval `key={selectedId}` at MakeShorts.tsx:258 so its range list resets with the source (mirroring the reset ShortMaker.tsx:240-249 already performs).
- ⚠ scope correction: Switching source video keeps the previous video's manual ranges and stale note, and re-arms the export button -- exporting the new video at the old video's timestamps. CONFIRMED: ManualInterval is rendered without a key (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:268) and owns `ranges` in local state with no reset path (ManualInterval.tsx:35, no useEffect in the file); submit() never clears ranges (ManualInterval.tsx:59-61), so the ranges survive both a mid-add switch AND the far more common export-then-switch-to-next-video flow, with the list still visible (ManualInterval.tsx:102-115) and "Make shorts from ranges" still enabled (:117-124). runManualExport then exports them against the current selectedId (MakeShorts.tsx:166,171), and no layer bounds the range against the source: Video.durationSec is available to the renderer (lib/rpc/schemas.ts:220) but never reaches ManualInterval, and shortmaker_ops.py / features/shortmaker.py add no duration check before _lazy_cut maps start/end onto ffmpeg -ss/-to (features/shortmaker.py:192-207). The identical hazard is explicitly guarded on the AI path (ShortMaker.tsx:233-249). TWO SCOPE CORRECTIONS to the original finding: (1) the Output Tray claim is OVERSTATED -- OutputTrayState is toggles only (caption/translate/reframe/subtitleMode/language, components/OutputTray.tsx:22-39) with no reference to the previous export's clips, and the save handlers are note-setting stubs (MakeShorts.tsx:145-146); only the stale success note ("Exported 3 clip(s) from your ranges.", MakeShorts.tsx:187) is a genuine false assertion, while a stale-open toggle panel with sticky preferences is cosmetic. (2) Severity is MEDIUM-HIGH, not HIGH: the failure wastes a slow export and lies in the UI, but the source video is never mutated, the stale state is visible rather than hidden, and recovery is deleting a bad clip or removing the ranges -- no data loss. The proposed fix (a selectedId-keyed effect clearing manualNote/manualError/trayOpen plus key={selectedId} on ManualInterval) is correct; passing durationSec into ManualInterval to reject out-of-source ranges would additionally close the unbounded-range hole, which the reset alone does not.

(2) `manualNote`/`manualError`/`trayOpen` (MakeShorts.tsx:78,79,81) persist across BOTH paths, since MakeShorts itself never unmounts and neither of its two `deps=[]` effects (:91-105, :111-135) is keyed on `selectedId`.
