(3) `submit()` (ManualInterval.tsx:59-61) then exports the stale ranges against the current `selectedId` (MakeShorts.tsx:166, :171; deps :195), and nothing clamps them — no duration prop reaches ManualInterval (:18-25), `buildManualCandidates` does no bounds check (manualIntervalLogic.ts:64-66), and the carve is a raw ffmpeg `-ss`/`-to` (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:205,207). (4) The stale RESULT assertion is carried by `manualNote` ("Exported 3 clip(s) from your ranges.", MakeShorts.tsx:187), not by OutputTray — OutputTray is a video-agnostic options panel (OutputTray.tsx:22-30, :80-81) whose defect is merely being left VISIBLE, implying an export just completed. (5) `selectedId` also changes via `handleReexport` (MakeShorts.tsx:138-141) from the gallery, a second unguarded entry point. The AI sibling already guards this exact hazard (ShortMaker.tsx:233-249, comment :236-237), and MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 mocks ManualInterval so no test can catch it. Fix as proposed: a `useEffect` on `selectedId` clearing `manualNote`/`manualError`/`trayOpen`, plus `key={selectedId}` on ManualInterval.

## Edit-phase alert text uses the FILL red (--status-error) instead of the AA-safe --status-error-text, landing at 4.23:1
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `token-consistency` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1224 — `.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error { border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error); color: var(--status-error); background: var(--status-error-soft); }` and the same pattern at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:561-569 for `.workspace__error`.

Consumers (all `role="alert"`, all mounted inside the Edit Workspace body): app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:195, Subtitles.tsx:355, Tracks.tsx:285, Convert.tsx:347, Dub.tsx:399, Assets.tsx:190, Assets.tsx:195, Diarize.tsx:167, Refine.tsx:270, Recipes.tsx:217, Recipes.tsx:222, NleExport.tsx:122, SemanticSearch.tsx:216, plus app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:383 (`.timeline__error`) and app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:347 (`.workspace__error`).

Backdrop: `.workspace__body` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1017-1021) sets no background, and neither does `.workspace` (:503-510) nor `.app__main` (:316-324), so the alert composites over `body` = `--surface-bg` #121620 (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:14).

Measured with the repo's own WCAG routine (re-derived independently, same formulas as app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:109-127 + the `over()` compositor at :270-274):
  --status-error #e5484d on error-soft over --surface-bg -> 4.23:1  (AA floor 4.5)
  --status-error #e5484d on error-soft over --surface-raised -> 3.75:1
  --status-error-text #ff6b6b on error-soft over --surface-bg -> 5.96:1

The repo already ruled this a defect: app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 asserts the base red FAILS on that wash and its comment states "a component MUST route alert text through --status-error-text, not --status-error". The enforcing guard (:649, :652-658, :688-698) scans only 5 Library sheets — `components/shell.css`, `features/panels.css` and `features/timeline.css` are absent, so the Edit phase kept the sub-AA red. Corroborated by grep: `var(--status-error-text)` appears in library-shell.css, library-cards.css, readinessBadge.css, library-provenance.css, keep-copy-control.css and views/director.css:73 — and in NO Edit-phase sheet.
- why: Every failure message in the Edit workspace (transcription failed, convert failed, dub failed, timeline save failed, project open failed) renders below the WCAG 1.4.3 AA contrast floor the project pins as its own DoD. It is the exact regression class the team already identified, tokenised and fixed for the Library and Director surfaces; the Edit phase was simply never migrated because the conformance guard's file list stops short of it.
- fix: Swap the TEXT colour (not the border/fill) to the AA-safe token in the two rules: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222 and :567 -> `color: var(--status-error-text);`, leaving `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` and `background: var(--status-error-soft)` unchanged (zero fill regression, mirrors the Library migration). Then close the blind spot by adding `resolve(HERE, '..', 'components', 'shell.css')`, `'features/panels.css'` and `'features/timeline.css'` to LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658 so it cannot decay again.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the claim stands as written. If anything it under-states scope: the same sub-AA `color: var(--status-error)` text leak occurs 4x in app/renderer/src/components/shell.css (:446, :567, :1222, :1425) plus 1x in app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:409, not just at the two cited lines. The only correction is to the PROPOSED FIX, not the finding: `features/timeline.css` contains zero leaks, so adding it to LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS is inert; the load-bearing additions are `components/shell.css` and `features/panels.css` (verified by mutation to turn the suite red).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): Edit-phase and Library alert TEXT routes through the FILL red --status-error instead of the AA-safe --status-error-text, landing at 4.23:1 over --surface-bg against the project's own 4.5:1 AA DoD floor — a confirmed but marginal (~6%) shortfall on text that remains clearly red and legible to a normal-vision user in normal lighting, in a single-user local desktop app. Scope is wider than originally stated: 5 leak sites, not 2 — app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:446, :567, :1222, :1425 and app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:409 — and :567 also covers `.library__error`, so the earlier Library migration was itself incomplete. Consumers include two uncited ones (SystemHealth.tsx:142, ShortMaker.tsx:914) alongside the 13 verified. Root cause as stated is correct and proven both-states: the LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS list at tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658 omits these sheets, and the guard's own regex fires 4x on shell.css and 1x on panels.css once pointed at them. Fix as proposed, but add 'components/shell.css' and 'features/panels.css' only — 'features/timeline.css' has zero leaks and is inert.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED (high) with corrected framing and a corrected fix. Alert text across the app — including every Edit-phase failure message — uses the FILL red `var(--status-error)` (#e5484d) instead of the AA-safe `var(--status-error-text)` (#ff6b6b). On the `--status-error-soft` 10% wash it lands at 4.23:1 over `--surface-bg` (the measured Edit-phase backdrop) and 3.75:1 over `--surface-raised`, against the project's own pinned 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 AA floor; the AA-safe token would give 5.96:1. Text is 13px regular (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:145,147) so no large-text exemption applies, and the wash is load-bearing — bare #e5484d on --surface-bg is 4.62:1 and would pass. Two rules carry it: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1224 (`.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error`) and :561-569 (`.library__error, .workspace__error`), with 15 verified `role="alert"` consumers in the Edit workspace plus app/renderer/src/features/Library.tsx:513. CORRECTION 1 — this is NOT an Edit-phase-only gap and the Library/Director were NOT already fixed: `.library__error` shares the :561 rule (live at Library.tsx:513) so the Library's own error banner is equally sub-AA, and app/renderer/src/panels/directorPanel.css:340 still leaks the base red as text; only views/director.css:73 was migrated. CORRECTION 2 — the true blast radius is 33 `color: var(--status-error)` text-leak sites across 24 sheets spanning Library, Edit, Make (views/shorts.css:49,384; views/makeShorts.css:75), Director, Settings (panels/modelsSystem.css:300; features/providersKeys.css x4), job queue (components/jobqueue.css x3), setup (components/setupStatus.css x3) and export (features/export/export.css:470). CORRECTION 3 — the proposed fix is incomplete AND self-breaking: shell.css holds FOUR leaks, not two (:446 `.library__remove-btn:hover`/Discard-hover and :1425 `.sm-status-discarded`, both on the same `--status-error-soft` wash), and features/panels.css:409 is a fifth in the named sheets. Swapping only shell.css:1222 and :567 then adding those sheets to LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS makes the guard's own assertion at tokens.conformance.test.ts:691 go RED — verified by replaying the repo's RED_TEXT_LEAK regex (:649) in a both-states probe. CORRECT FIX: swap the TEXT colour (leaving border-left and background untouched, zero fill regression) at shell.css:567, :1222, :446 and :1425 plus features/panels.css:409, THEN add `components/shell.css` and `features/panels.css` to LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS (tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) and ideally rename the constant to reflect that it is no longer Library-only; adding `features/timeline.css` is inert (0 leaks — `.timeline__error` is styled in shell.css). Sweeping the remaining ~28 sites in the other 22 sheets is the same defect class and should be tracked, though several are non-alert affordances (hover tints, status dots) that need per-site judgement rather than a blanket swap.

## Determinate 0% progress bar during Whisper model load/download — a hang that looks like real progress
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `loading-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:188 renders `<progress max={100} value={pct} />` — always DETERMINATE, seeded `pct=0` (Transcribe.tsx:44) with message 'Starting…' (Transcribe.tsx:72).

The first real tick reaches it only at sidecar/media_studio/features/transcribe.py:357-358 `on_progress(0.0, "transcribing")`. Everything before that emits NOTHING:
- transcribe.py:343 `load_model_with_cpu_fallback(...)` → transcribe.py:152-163 `FasterWhisperLoader.load` → transcribe.py:161 `_WhisperModel(model, device=..., compute_type=...)`, constructed with NO progress callback.
- transcribe.py:348 `whisper_model.transcribe(...)` (VAD + feature extraction + language detect) also runs before the first tick.

On a cache miss that construction downloads the model. Size and intent are explicit: sidecar/media_studio/assets/manifest.py:293 `WHISPER_SIZE_MB = 1600`, and manifest.py:287-288 states the asset manager seeds the same HF_HOME cache "so transcribe.start finds it pre-downloaded" — i.e. when it is NOT pre-downloaded, transcribe.start is the thing that downloads it.

That cache-miss state ships: app/main/installProfiles.ts:95 `minimum: []` gives the Minimum profile no `transcription` bundle (installProfiles.ts:72-78 = the 1600 MB WHISPER asset).

No preflight exists on the wired path: app/../handlers/media_ops.py:419-433 `_transcribe_and_persist` resolves the path, builds the loader, and calls `transcribe_with_engine` with no asset-presence check. Corroborating second signal — a repo-wide `guard_network` grep shows callers in diarize.py:313, reframe_multispeaker.py:1406, tts/dub.py:330, providers_ops.py:111/257, assets/manager.py:686, media_ops.py:124, but NONE in the transcribe path; the sole Whisper reference (features/offline.py:113) is a docstring example, not a call. Sibling contrast: diarize additionally has a model-presence gate (media_ops.py:464-476 `_diarize_models_present`) that transcribe lacks.

UNVERIFIED inline: I did not execute a Minimum-profile install end-to-end; the download leg is inferred from the manifest size + profile omission + absence of any preflight/guard, all three read directly. The zero-progress window itself is CONFIRMED from the call order regardless of download vs. cached load.
- why: The user clicks Start and gets a determinate bar pinned at 0% with 'Starting…'. A determinate bar asserts 'I know how far along this is' — here it knows nothing. On a cached model that is a few seconds of dead air; on a Minimum-profile first run it is a silent 1.6 GB download, i.e. many minutes of a frozen 0% bar that is indistinguishable from a wedged sidecar. This is the exact failure the lens names: a long operation showing a lie instead of real progress. The renderer's own 35-minute ceiling (features/_api.ts:62) means nothing rescues the user either — they will kill the app long before it fires.
- fix: Two parts. (1) Renderer: render an INDETERMINATE bar until the first real progress event arrives — track a `hasProgress` flag set in the `onProgress` handler (Transcribe.tsx:57-61) and emit `<progress max={100} />` with no `value` while it is false, so the widget honestly says 'working, duration unknown'. (2) Sidecar: emit progress before the silent phases — call `on_progress(0.0, "loading model")` immediately on entry to `transcribe_file` (before transcribe.py:343) and, for the download case, either add an asset-presence preflight mirroring `_diarize_models_present` (media_ops.py:464-476) that raises an actionable 'transcription model not installed' error, or route the fetch through the asset manager so its byte-level download progress reaches `job.progress`. The preflight also closes the missing `guard_network` gap for offline mode.
- ⚠ scope correction: Determinate 0% progress bar during Whisper model load/download. CONFIRMED and broader than claimed: the frozen-0% window is not a first-run or Minimum-profile-only condition. It occurs on EVERY transcription for EVERY user because production injects no shared loader (_services.py:46/:79), so media_ops.py:422 builds a fresh FasterWhisperLoader per call and the per-instance model cache (transcribe.py:150) never survives a job — transcribe.py:161 reloads the model into memory each run. The window spans an unbounded GPU-pool queue wait (media_ops.py:394 `gpu=True`; jobs.py:593/604; no initial emit or heartbeat per jobs.py:137-139/:652-665), then model load (transcribe.py:343), then eager audio decode + language detect (transcribe.py:348); even the first tick is 0.0 (transcribe.py:358) and the bar first moves one segment later (transcribe.py:367-369). The cache-miss download leg additionally reaches the RECOMMENDED Default profile, not only Minimum, because transcribe.py:263/:82 request CPU_MODEL "small" on any non-CUDA box while only `whisper-large-v3-turbo` is seeded (manifest.py:285). Two corrections to the write-up: (a) renderer fix (1) — swapping to an indeterminate bar — is cosmetic and does not by itself cure the "looks wedged" harm; the load-bearing fix is sidecar-side (early on_progress + preflight, or route the fetch through the asset manager, which already emits byte-level progress per Assets.test.tsx:177); (b) a partial mitigation exists and should be disclosed — the Assets tab in the same Workspace tab strip (Workspace.tsx:66, :294-295) shows whisper "Not installed · 1.6 GB · [Install]", so the model is pre-installable, just never surfaced at the moment of use. Severity: medium-high rather than high.
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect stands; two sentences in the finding are wider than their evidence and should be re-scoped:

(1) "Everything before that emits NOTHING" → narrow exception at features/transcribe.py:342 (`notify = lambda msg: on_progress(0.0, msg)`) invoked from :197-198 on the GPU→CPU fallback path: when a GPU load attempt raises, ONE message ("GPU unavailable — running on CPU, slower") is emitted before the CPU load. It still carries pct=0.0, so the determinate-bar-pinned-at-0 claim is untouched — only the word "NOTHING" is too wide. And on a CUDA-less box it never fires at all, because resolve_transcribe_target (transcribe.py:254-261, called at :461) picks cpu directly rather than attempting cuda, so the message stays 'Starting…'. Correctly scoped: "no progress event before transcribe.py:357-358 ever carries a non-zero pct, and on the non-GPU path no event is emitted at all."

(2) "a silent 1.6 GB download" → that figure is CUDA-path-specific. transcribe.py:263 + :82 resolve the model to CPU_MODEL='small' on a non-CUDA box, i.e. a several-hundred-MB download, not 1600 MB (the 1600 MB at installProfiles.ts:50 / manifest.py:293 is large-v3-turbo). Correctly scoped: "a silent multi-hundred-MB (CPU/'small') to 1.6 GB (CUDA/large-v3-turbo) download". Separately worth noting as an ADDITIONAL defect, not a correction: the asset manager only pre-seeds large-v3-turbo (manifest.py:289), so a CPU-only machine hits this same 0% cache-miss window even on the Default profile that supposedly pre-installs transcription.

With those two sentences re-scoped, the finding is CONFIRMED as written, and the "high" severity is defensible on the shipped Minimum/Custom profile.
- ⚠ scope correction: Determinate 0% progress bar during Whisper model load/download in the Transcribe panel (severity: medium-to-high). CONFIRMED: app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:188 renders an unconditionally determinate `<progress max={100} value={pct} />`, seeded pct=0 (:44) with message 'Starting...' (:72), and the first real tick only arrives at sidecar/media_studio/features/transcribe.py:357-358. Everything before it is silent: media_ops.py:425 -> transcribe.py:343 load_model_with_cpu_fallback -> :161 `_WhisperModel(...)` (no progress callback) -> :348 whisper_model.transcribe(...). The only earlier emission, transcribe.py:342 `notify`, fires only on a GPU->CPU fallback and also passes pct=0.0, so the bar reads 0% throughout regardless. On a cache miss that construction downloads the model -- CONFIRMED at the library level, not inferred: faster_whisper/transcribe.py:681 calls download_model() for a non-directory arg, utils.py:116 is huggingface_hub.snapshot_download, and utils.py:630 defaults local_files_only=False, which transcribe.py:161 never overrides. No preflight exists on the wired path (composition.py:126 registers svc.transcribe_start; media_ops.py:419-433 resolves the path, builds the loader, and calls transcribe_with_engine with no asset-presence check and no offline.guard_network -- and engine.py:169 enforce_offline_env is re-exported but never called in production, so the defence-in-depth backstop is dead too). CORRECTED SCOPE, two ways: (a) the download SIZE is device-dependent, not a flat 1.6 GB -- transcribe.py:461 resolve_transcribe_target yields large-v3-turbo only when CUDA is detected or the device/model is forced (measured 1,547 MB on disk, matching manifest.py:293's 1600), whereas a non-CUDA box gets CPU_MODEL='small' (transcribe.py:82, :263) which faster_whisper/utils.py:17 maps to Systran/faster-whisper-small, roughly 0.5 GB (UNVERIFIED exact size -- settle it by measuring that repo's snapshot); (b) the cache-miss state is WIDER than the Minimum profile -- installProfiles.ts:95 `minimum: []` omits the transcription bundle (:72-78), but manifest.py:355 registers exactly ONE whisper asset pinned to the large-v3-turbo repo (:289) and NONE for 'small', so a CPU-only machine hits the identical frozen-0% silent download on the Default and Full profiles as well. The sibling contrast should be stated narrowly: transcribe has neither a model-presence probe nor an offline refusal, whereas diarize has both -- but diarize.py:312-316 only calls guard_network when OFFLINE, so that gate would not have prevented an online first-use download either. Fix note: part (1) of the proposed renderer fix must ALSO add an explicit animated indeterminate style, because shell.css:1124-1133 sets `appearance: none` on `.feature-panel progress`, which suppresses Chromium's native indeterminate animation -- omitting `value` alone would ship a static empty track, i.e. less signal than today.

## Space cannot activate ANY button inside the candidate-review group (container keydown preventDefaults ' ' and does not exempt BUTTON)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:828-829 exempts only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT; :842-843 `case ' ': e.preventDefault();`. The handler is bound to the whole group at CandidateReview.tsx:99-101 (`tabIndex={0} onKeyDown={onKeyDown}`), which contains the Rank/Virality buttons (CandidateReview.tsx:156-171) and every row control — Factors (CandidateList.tsx:121-130), the four nudge buttons (CandidateList.tsx:156-183), Reset (CandidateList.tsx:185), Approve/Discard/Reinstate (CandidateList.tsx:193/198/203).
EXECUTABLE PROOF (real Chromium via chrome-devtools MCP, both-states control, C:/Users/Prekzursil/AppData/Local/Temp/reframe-kbd-probe.html which reproduces the handler verbatim):
  with the handler:    {"clicks":0,"spaceHandled":1,"defaultPrevented":true}
  handler removed:     {"clicks":1}  ← the probe DOES detect a working button, so the 0 above is real, not a broken detector.
The existing unit test only proves the INPUT case (ShortMaker.test.tsx:2390-2397); no test presses Space on a button. The e2e a11y gate never selects a video, so .sm-review is never scanned (a11y.a11y.spec.ts:62-68 stops at `.make-shorts`).
- why: Space is a standard activation key for `button` (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard). A keyboard-only user who Tabs to "Approve" and presses Space gets no activation — instead the preview video silently toggles play/pause, which reads as a dead control. Every action of the reframe review loop (approve, discard, reinstate, nudge boundaries, reset, sort, expand factors) is affected. Enter still works, so it is degradation rather than a total block. Same mechanism additionally consumes ArrowLeft/ArrowRight while the native `<video controls>` preview has focus (Player.tsx:164/321 default `controls=true`, mounted inside .sm-review at CandidateReview.tsx:111-124): instead of the native ±5s seek, the keypress re-cuts the selected candidate's in/out points — UNVERIFIED whether Chromium's media-controls seek also still fires (it may listen at target phase), but the destructive nudge definitely does.
- fix: Scope the shortcuts to the group itself instead of blacklisting tag names: `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return;` at the top of handleReviewKeys (ShortMaker.tsx:827). That keeps J/K/Space/A/X live when the group has focus and leaves every descendant control's native keyboard behaviour intact. Minimal alternative: add `tag === 'BUTTON' || tag === 'A' || tag === 'VIDEO'` to the exemption on ShortMaker.tsx:829. Add a regression test that focuses a row's Approve button, presses Space, and asserts the approve handler ran (must be a real-browser/e2e test — jsdom does not implement button Space activation, so a vitest assertion here would be a detector that is silent in both states).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high) — keyboard-nav convention defect, not a WCAG Level-A failure. The container keydown handler at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:826-875 is bound to the whole focusable review group (bound at :954; group at CandidateReview.tsx:99-101) and exempts only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT (:829), so its unconditional `case ' ': e.preventDefault()` (:842-843) suppresses Chromium's Space activation for all 10 descendant buttons — Rank/Virality sort (CandidateReview.tsx:156-171), Factors (CandidateList.tsx:121-130), the four nudge buttons (:156-183), Reset (:185), Approve/Discard/Reinstate (:193/198/203). Measured in real Chromium against the actual component tree with a handler-removed control: Space -> approve:0/discard:0/sort:0/factors-closed with the handler, and 1/1/1/open without it. Enter activates every one of those buttons (measured approve:1 under the shipped handler), so WCAG SC 2.1.1 is NOT failed and no axe rule fires; the correct normative hook is the ARIA APG `button` pattern (Enter AND Space), aggravated by aria-keyshortcuts="J K Space A X ArrowLeft ArrowRight" (CandidateReview.tsx:98) advertising Space as a group shortcut while silently consuming it from every descendant control. Consequence per keypress: with a candidate selected the preview toggles play/pause; with none selected Space is a total no-op (the preventDefault at :843 precedes the playerRef guard at :844). The ArrowLeft/ArrowRight consumption is a REVERSIBLE window slide (original is retained for non-destructive reset per shortMakerLogic.ts:398-399, with a Reset button at CandidateList.tsx:184-188) whose only non-retractable effect is the recordFeedback(...,'nudged') taste-profile RPC at ShortMaker.tsx:582-597 — not "destructive". Fix and its validation stand as proposed: `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return;` at the top of handleReviewKeys — measured to restore every Space activation while all four group shortcuts still fire with the group focused, and it is the same guard already used at DirectorPanel.tsx:744-748 for this exact bug. Regression test must be real-browser/e2e (DirectorPanel.tsx:725 confirms jsdom does not fire button onClick on keydown).
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands as written and needs no narrowing: Space cannot activate ANY button inside the candidate-review group, because the container keydown handler preventDefaults ' ' and does not exempt BUTTON. Only the supporting rationale needs re-scoping: this is NOT a WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) failure — Enter still activates every affected button, so the functionality remains keyboard-operable. Cite instead the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices button pattern (a `button` is expected to activate on both Space and Enter); the defect is expected-behavior/usability degradation plus a destructive side effect (Space silently toggles the preview video at ShortMaker.tsx:844-848; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight silently re-cut the selected candidate's in/out points at ShortMaker.tsx:861-871 while the `<video controls>` preview has focus), not a WCAG Level A violation. Additionally, the proposed fix should be narrowed: `e.target !== e.currentTarget` (and the "add BUTTON/A/VIDEO to the exemption list" alternative) would also disable J/K/A/X whenever focus rests on a descendant control — the normal state right after clicking a row button — and the existing tests cannot detect that regression because they all dispatch keydown on `.sm-review` itself (ShortMaker.test.tsx:2296-2301). Prefer a per-key bail: skip `' '` only for BUTTON/A/VIDEO/SUMMARY and checkbox/radio inputs, and skip ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only for VIDEO.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high), keyboard-convention defect, correctly scoped: because the `.sm-review` container handler preventDefaults ' ' without exempting BUTTON (ShortMaker.tsx:828-829, :842-843; bound group-wide at CandidateReview.tsx:99-100), Space does not activate any button inside the candidate-review group — the preview video toggles play/pause instead. This is a broken platform CONVENTION (WAI-ARIA APG Space+Enter parity for buttons), NOT a WCAG 2.1.1 failure: Enter still activates every affected control (measured) and all controls remain mouse-clickable, so no functionality is unreachable. It is also partly by design — Space is declared at CandidateReview.tsx:98 (aria-keyshortcuts) and advertised in the legend at :191 as play/pause, and the group's J/K/A/X/arrow shortcuts already cover selection, approve, discard and window-nudge without pressing a button. Real residual friction is limited to the controls with NO shortcut equivalent — the four per-edge nudge buttons (CandidateList.tsx:158/165/172/179, which move start OR end independently, unlike the arrows' both-edge slide at ShortMaker.tsx:868), Reset (:185), Reinstate (:203) and Factors (:121) — where a Space-habituated keyboard-only user gets a mysterious non-response until they try Enter. Fix is still worth taking (the `e.target !== e.currentTarget` guard), primarily because the SAME mechanism causes a higher-impact, pointer-reachable defect that should be filed separately: with the preview `<video controls>` focused (one mouse click; confirmed focusable, arrow keydown confirmed reaching the handler), ArrowLeft/ArrowRight silently re-cut the selected candidate's in/out points instead of seeking.

## Advertised A / X / arrow shortcuts act on `selectedId`, which Tab focus never updates — a keyboard user destroys the WRONG candidate
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Shortcuts operate on the container's `selectedId` only: ShortMaker.tsx:854 `if (selectedId) approve(selectedId)`, :859 `discard(selectedId)`, :868 `nudge(selectedId, delta, delta)`. `selectedId` is changed by exactly two things — J/K (ShortMaker.tsx:835/840) and a row CLICK (CandidateList.tsx:86 `onClick={() => onSelect(item.id)}`). The row `<li>` (CandidateList.tsx:79-87) has no `tabIndex`, no `role`, no `onFocus` and no keydown handler, so Tab focus moving into row N never syncs selection. The shortcuts are nevertheless advertised as live for the whole group (`aria-keyshortcuts="J K Space A X ArrowLeft ArrowRight"`, CandidateReview.tsx:98) and by the always-visible legend (CandidateReview.tsx:185-206), and the handler fires for events bubbling from anywhere inside (CandidateReview.tsx:100).
- why: Concrete failure: three candidates are loaded, selection defaults to row 1 (ShortMaker.tsx:291-293). The user Tabs down to row 3's "Approve" button and — following the on-screen legend — presses `A`. Row 1 is approved, row 3 is not, and no focus or selection moved. Press `X` and row 1 is discarded. Press `→` and row 1's in/out boundaries are re-cut by 1s. The wrongly-approved clip then flows straight into "Export approved" (ShortMaker.tsx:968-974), so the user renders the wrong short. Nothing announces the mismatch: `aria-current` (CandidateList.tsx:85) marks a row that does not have focus.
- fix: Couple focus to selection. Either (a) apply the same `e.target !== e.currentTarget` guard as the fix above so the letter shortcuts only fire when the group container itself is focused (making the legend truthful), or (b) turn the list into a real single-select widget: `role="listbox"` on the `<ol>` (CandidateList.tsx:32) with `role="option" aria-selected` + roving `tabIndex` on each `<li>` (CandidateList.tsx:79) and an `onFocus`/arrow-key handler that sets `selectedId` — which also gives the row's click target a keyboard equivalent it currently lacks.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity, reversible-annoyance (not high, not destructive): the A/X/arrow shortcuts fire on `selectedId` for keydown bubbling from anywhere inside the review group (ShortMaker.tsx:826-875 via CandidateReview.tsx:100), while the always-visible legend (CandidateReview.tsx:185-206) and `aria-keyshortcuts` (CandidateReview.tsx:98) advertise them unconditionally. Because rows are not focusable (CandidateList.tsx:79-87), a user who tabs onward to row N's own Approve button and then presses `A` instead of Enter acts on the selected row (default row 1, ShortMaker.tsx:291-293), not row N. Scope of real harm: the state change is fully reversible — Reinstate (CandidateList.tsx:202-206) and Reset (CandidateList.tsx:184-188) restore exact prior state, the reducer never deletes an item (shortMakerLogic.ts:636-649), and export is a separate explicit click next to a live approved-count (ShortMaker.tsx:967-974), so no wrong render occurs without an additional independent user action. The two residual non-obvious effects are (a) an arrow nudge on an off-screen selected row shifts its in/out by 1s with no counter feedback, and (b) each mis-fired A/X writes a persistent `feedback.record` label (ShortMaker.tsx:569/:577) that reinstate (ShortMaker.tsx:581) does not retract. Settling experiment: drive the built app, Tab twice into a row's Approve button, press `A`, and assert which row's status chip changes plus whether a `feedback.record` RPC is emitted.
- ⚠ scope correction: Wording tightening only — the scope, surface, and fix are unchanged. Suggested headline: "Advertised A / X / arrow shortcuts act on the container's `selectedId`, which Tab focus never updates — a keyboard user mis-sets the WRONG candidate and writes an unretractable false taste label." Body corrections: (a) replace "destroys" — the review state is reversible via Reinstate (CandidateList.tsx:202-206) / Reset (CandidateList.tsx:184-188); the IRREVERSIBLE part is the fire-and-forget `recordFeedback` on approve/discard/nudge (ShortMaker.tsx:569/577/588-593 -> shortMakerLogic.ts:595-609), which `reinstate`/`reset` never counter-record; (b) "exactly two things" -> "the only two USER-DRIVEN paths (J/K and a row click); the other two `setSelectedId` sites, ShortMaker.tsx:247 and :292, are non-user-driven bookkeeping"; (c) "Nothing announces the mismatch" -> "Nothing announces it to a screen reader (no live region; `aria-current` sits on a non-focusable `<li>` with no `aria-activedescendant`); a sighted user's only cue is that the focused row keeps its own Approve button (CandidateList.tsx:192)"; (d) "flows straight into Export approved" -> "is then eligible for the explicit Export approved press (ShortMaker.tsx:968-974), whose 'N approved' counter reads exactly what the user expects and so does not catch the error"; (e) delete the fix parenthetical "which also gives the row's click target a keyboard equivalent it currently lacks" — J/K already provides one (ShortMaker.tsx:835/840, asserted by ShortMaker.test.tsx:2312-2328); (f) prefer fix (a), since the `e.target !== e.currentTarget` guard also closes the adjacent Space-swallowing WCAG 2.1.1 defect in the same handler (ShortMaker.tsx:842-843).

## `hidden` on the Deliver cluster is INERT (CSS `display:flex` beats the UA `[hidden]` rule) — five tabs are visible and mouse-clickable but excluded from arrow-key navigation, and one state leaves the tablist arrow-dead
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: TabBar renders the advanced cluster as `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>` (TabBar.tsx:239), and workspace.css:148-152 sets `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; ... }`, an author rule that overrides the UA `[hidden]{display:none}`.
SIGNAL 1 (real Chromium, both-states control, C:/Users/Prekzursil/AppData/Local/Temp/reframe-hidden-probe.html with workspace.css:148-152 copied verbatim): {"advHiddenAttr":true,"advComputedDisplay":"flex","controlHiddenAttr":true,"controlComputedDisplay":"none","convertVisibleRect":{"w":62.69,"h":21},"convertHitTestable":true} — the control element proves the probe detects a real `display:none`.
SIGNAL 2 (independent): the committed Windows baseline C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png shows "DELIVER · CONVERT · TIMELINE EXPORT · RECIPES · ASSE…" fully painted in the strip while `advancedOpen` is still the default `false` (Workspace.tsx:131).
Meanwhile TabBar excludes them from keyboard nav: `orderedIds` omits advanced tabIds unless `advancedOpen` (TabBar.tsx:159-166), non-active tabs are `tabIndex={-1}` (TabBar.tsx:97), and `onKeyDown` returns early for any id not in `orderedIds` (TabBar.tsx:179-181). No `[hidden]` selector exists anywhere in app/renderer (grep over *.css: zero matches). The unit test asserts only the ATTRIBUTE — `expect(panel.hidden).toBe(true)` (Workspace.test.tsx:598/615) — under jsdom, which loads none of this CSS, so it is green in both states.
- why: Two concrete keyboard failures. (1) Convert / Timeline export / Recipes / Assets / Tracks are on screen and clickable with a mouse, but a keyboard user arrowing along the tablist can never land on them — ArrowRight walks transcribe→…→dub and stops. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard, Level A). The only keyboard route is the "Advanced" toggle (TabBar.tsx:245-252), which is pushed off the right edge in the baseline and whose `aria-expanded="false"` contradicts the visibly-expanded cluster; pressing it produces NO visual change while silently restoring arrow reachability. (2) Reachable state: click Export (sets active='convert', advancedOpen=true, Workspace.tsx:137-140), then click Advanced to collapse. Now 'convert' is the only `tabIndex={0}` tab, and because it is still rendered (hidden is inert) the user Tabs onto it — but `orderedIds.indexOf('convert') === -1`, so ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End all no-op (TabBar.tsx:179-181). The tab strip becomes completely arrow-dead; no other tab, including Short-maker, is reachable from there by keyboard.
- fix: Honour the attribute: add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none; }` at workspace.css:152, or stop relying on the attribute and conditionally render (`{advancedOpen ? advanced.map(...) : null}` at TabBar.tsx:238-242). Independently, harden `orderedIds`/`onKeyDown` so the ACTIVE tab is always in the arrow order even when its cluster is collapsed, so the arrow-dead state cannot occur. Replace the `panel.hidden` assertions (Workspace.test.tsx:598/615) with a real-browser computed-`display` check, or the test will stay green through the fix and the regression.
- ⚠ scope correction: `hidden` on the Deliver cluster is INERT: the author rule `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex }` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152) overrides the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` rule, and no `[hidden]` selector exists anywhere in app/renderer. Consequently the five Deliver tabs (convert, nle, recipes, assets, tracks — Workspace.tsx:87) are painted, hit-testable, and exposed in the accessibility tree while `advancedOpen` is false (Workspace.tsx:131), yet TabBar excludes them from arrow-key navigation (TabBar.tsx:159-166, 179-181). Two consequences: (1) a sighted keyboard user sees five tabs the arrow keys silently skip, and the Advanced toggle reports `aria-expanded="false"` (TabBar.tsx:248) while its cluster is fully exposed — a WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value, Level A) failure and an ARIA-APG tabs-pattern violation; NOT a 2.1.1 Keyboard failure, because the cluster stays keyboard-operable through that toggle. (2) Clicking any visible Deliver tab — reachable only because `hidden` is inert — sets `active` without opening the cluster (handleSelect, Workspace.tsx:189-198), leaving that tab as the sole `tabIndex={0}` tab while absent from `orderedIds`, so ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End all no-op. The user is NOT stranded: Tab reaches the Advanced toggle and pressing it restores arrow navigation, so this is a MEDIUM-severity keyboard-navigation defect rather than high. The unit assertions at Workspace.test.tsx:598/615 check only `panel.hidden` under jsdom and are green in both the broken and fixed states, so they cannot gate the fix.
- ⚠ scope correction: `hidden` on the Deliver cluster is INERT — author `display:flex` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152) beats the UA `[hidden]` rule by cascade origin, and no `[hidden]` selector exists anywhere in app/. Confirmed empirically: the committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png paints "DELIVER  CONV" while advancedOpen defaults false (Workspace.tsx:131). Consequences, correctly scoped: (a) the "Advanced" disclosure never shows or hides its cluster — it only brightens the toggle and rotates a caret (workspace.css:132-134, 144-146) while silently changing arrow-key reachability, so it cannot perform its one job; (b) aria-expanded="false" (TabBar.tsx:248) contradicts a rendered, painted, a11y-exposed cluster (WCAG 4.1.2, not 2.1.1 — the tabs remain keyboard-OPERABLE via the toggle); (c) at the captured 1280px width ONE deliver tab ("CONV") is partially visible yet skipped by arrow keys, because orderedIds omits advanced ids unless advancedOpen (TabBar.tsx:159-166) and onKeyDown early-returns on index===-1 (TabBar.tsx:179-181) — the other four sit outside the viewport in the `overflow-x: auto` scroller (workspace.css:36-39), so "five visible and mouse-clickable" is wrong; (d) Export-then-collapse (Workspace.tsx:137-140) reaches a state where the focused active 'convert' tab ignores ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End — arrow-dead, but NOT keyboard-unreachable and NOT a trap, since the Advanced toggle is a tabbable sibling outside the tablist (TabBar.tsx:243-253) that restores arrow nav. Severity MEDIUM, not high: confusing and wrong, but recoverable, mouse-user-invisible, and with no data loss or blocked workflow on a single-user local desktop app. The fix must land the orderedIds/onKeyDown hardening TOGETHER WITH the CSS change, not independently — honouring `hidden` alone leaves the tablist with zero tabbable elements in the Export-then-collapse state, which is worse. Workspace.test.tsx:598/615 assert only `panel.hidden` under jsdom and stay green in both states, so they must be replaced with a real-browser computed-display check or they will pass through both the bug and its regression.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED (medium): `hidden` on the Deliver cluster is inert — workspace.css:148-152's author-origin `display: flex` on `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel` beats the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` by cascade origin, and no `[hidden]` selector or competing `display:none` exists anywhere in app/renderer. So the five-tab Deliver cluster (convert, nle, recipes, assets, tracks — Workspace.tsx:87) renders, is hit-testable, and is focusable while `advancedOpen` is false (Workspace.tsx:131), even though `orderedIds` omits it from arrow navigation (TabBar.tsx:159-166) and `onKeyDown` no-ops for it (TabBar.tsx:178-181). Two consequences, correctly scoped:

(a) PROGRAMMATIC/VISUAL MISMATCH (WCAG 4.1.2 / 1.3.1, not 2.1.1): the Advanced toggle reports `aria-expanded="false"` (TabBar.tsx:248) over a cluster the user can see and click, and pressing it produces no visual change while silently changing arrow reachability. At the pinned 1280px baseline viewport only the "DELIVER" label and a clipped "CONV" are on screen — the remaining four tabs, the Advanced toggle, and Export are past the right edge of the `overflow-x: auto` strip (workspace.css:36-39) and need horizontal scrolling. No functionality is keyboard-inoperable: the Advanced toggle AND Export (TabBar.tsx:254-258 -> Workspace.tsx:137-140) both bring the cluster into the arrow order.

(b) TRANSIENT ARROW-DEAD TABLIST (independent of the CSS bug): activate Export (active='convert', advancedOpen=true — Workspace.tsx:137-140), then collapse via the Advanced toggle (Workspace.tsx:132). `convert` is now the only `tabIndex={0}` tab (TabBar.tsx:97) and, because `hidden` is inert, it stays focusable — but `orderedIds.indexOf('convert') === -1`, so ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End all no-op (TabBar.tsx:178-181). The state is escapable and self-recovering: Tab from `convert` lands on `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` (the next tabbable element in DOM order, TabBar.tsx:245) and Enter restores full arrow nav in three keystrokes — so it is a confusing dead-arrow state, not a keyboard trap. Note this defect is NOT fixed by honouring `hidden`: with `display:none` restored and `orderedIds` unchanged, the same state leaves the tablist with ZERO tabbable elements, which is worse. Both fixes are required.

Test-coverage gap stands as written: every assertion is attribute-only under jsdom with no CSS loaded (Workspace.test.tsx:598/615/687, TabBar.test.tsx:97/105), so the suite is green in both the broken and fixed states; TabBar.test.tsx:258-271 pins the index===-1 no-op but only with a PRIMARY tab active, never with the active tab inside the collapsed cluster — the exact trap in (b).

## Progress live region re-announces on every whisper segment tick, flooding the screen reader for the whole job
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:187 wraps BOTH the changing percentage and the changing message in one polite region: `<div className="progress" aria-live="polite">` … :189 `<span className="progress-pct">{Math.round(pct)}%</span>` … :190 `{message && <span className="progress-message"> · {message}</span>}`. Both are re-set on every notification at Transcribe.tsx:57-62 (`setPct(ev.pct); setMessage(ev.message)`).
Cadence is per-ASR-segment, not throttled: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/features/transcribe.py:367-369 → `if on_progress is not None and duration > 0.0: pct = clamp(...); on_progress(pct, f"segment {len(segments)}")` inside the per-segment loop (:361). The message string changes on EVERY event even when the rounded pct does not.
No throttle anywhere on the wire: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/main/sidecar.ts:520-525 forwards each `job.progress` 1:1 (`this.emit('progress', {jobId, pct, message})`); a repo-wide grep for `throttle` under app/ returns zero hits.
The repo already knows the correct pattern and applied it elsewhere: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/repurposeLogic.ts:165-168 `aggregateUpdate()` returns `null` unless the source token changed, and C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:285 pins it: "announces on source-transition only (debounced), not per pct tick".
- why: A 30-minute source produces on the order of 200-500 whisper segments, so a blind user who starts a transcription gets 200-500 queued polite utterances ("7% · segment 12", "8% · segment 13", …). aria-live="polite" queues rather than replaces, so speech runs minutes behind reality and the user cannot hear anything else in the app until the job ends. The panel becomes unusable during the exact operation it exists to perform, and it is the only Speech & Text panel driven by a high-frequency per-segment stream.
- fix: Stop announcing the raw tick. Keep the visual `%`/message spans OUTSIDE any live region (add `aria-hidden` is not needed if the region wraps only the announced text) and add a separate polite region whose text is recomputed only on a meaningful transition — reuse the existing `aggregateUpdate`-style guard from repurposeLogic.ts:165-168, or coarsen to decile milestones (`Math.floor(pct/10)`) plus phase flips (started / cancelled / done / failed). Mirror `LiveStatusRegion.tsx:38-52` (polite aggregate + assertive alert), which is already the in-repo announcer component.
- ⚠ scope correction: The SHARED panel progress live-region pattern re-announces on every sidecar progress tick, because the changing percentage AND the changing message both sit inside one unthrottled `aria-live="polite"` region. Verified in app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:187-191, fed 1:1 by Transcribe.tsx:57-62 from app/main/sidecar.ts:520-525, driven per-ASR-segment by sidecar/media_studio/features/transcribe.py:367-369 and per-chunk by parakeet_asr.py:381 (the alternate engine seam).

This is a SHARED-PATTERN defect, not unique to Transcribe. The identical live region and identical unthrottled relay recur in 9 other panels, including its own Speech & Text sibling app/renderer/src/features/Diarize.tsx:158-164 / :56-64, which is itself driven per-item by pyannote_backend.py:281 and diarize_backend.py:360. Per Workspace.tsx:80 the Speech & Text group is ['transcribe','search','subtitles','diarize','refine'] and all five carry the shape (SemanticSearch.tsx:204, Subtitles.tsx:342, Refine.tsx:262), as do Assets.tsx:182, Convert.tsx:326, Dub.tsx:391, Recipes.tsx:228 and Tracks.tsx:277.

The repo already contains the correct remedy — repurposeLogic.ts:165-168 `aggregateUpdate()` (token-guarded, pinned by BatchQueue.test.tsx:285 "announces on source-transition only (debounced), not per pct tick") and the LiveStatusRegion.tsx:38-52 announcer — so the fix is to route the shared `.progress` block through that existing pattern (keep the visual `%`/message outside the announced region; announce only on a meaningful transition such as a decile flip or phase change), not to patch Transcribe.tsx alone.

UNVERIFIED inline: the announcement-backlog magnitude. "200-500 queued utterances", "speech minutes behind reality" and "cannot hear anything else until the job ends" are not measured here; polite-queue coalescing is screen-reader-specific and the repo's axe suite cannot detect live-region flooding. Settling experiment: capture an NVDA speech-viewer log across one real 30-minute transcription and count announcements plus end-to-end speech lag; that same run also fixes the segment-count estimate (faster-whisper sentence segments over 1800s land nearer ~180-360).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high), SYSTEMIC (not Transcribe-specific): ~11 job panels wrap a per-tick-changing percentage AND message in a single `aria-live="polite"` region, so screen readers announce every progress notification for the whole job. Transcribe.tsx:187-191 is fed unthrottled per-ASR-segment events (transcribe.py:367-369 -> jobs.py:137-139 -> sidecar.ts:520-525), on the order of 200-500 announcements for a 30-minute source [estimate, UNVERIFIED]. The worst instance is NOT Transcribe but Convert.tsx:325-331, whose identical region is fed by ffmpeg `-progress` (ffmpeg.py:191) through a float-only `pct > last_pct` gate (ffmpeg.py:331-335) at ffmpeg's default ~0.5s cadence -- roughly 3,600 announcements per 30-minute encode. Diarize.tsx:159, Dub.tsx:391, Subtitles.tsx:342, Tracks.tsx:277, Recipes.tsx:228, Refine.tsx:262, Assets.tsx:182, SemanticSearch.tsx:204 and ShortMaker.tsx:925 share the same shape. Real consequence: sustained screen-reader chatter that makes progress speech lag reality and degrades the panel during the operation it exists to perform. NOT a lockout -- NVDA/JAWS flush pending polite speech on keypress and focus change, so Cancel and navigation remain usable [UNVERIFIED: documented default AT behavior, not measured here]. NOT a WCAG failure -- SC 4.1.3 is satisfied; this violates ARIA APG throttling guidance, so it ranks below the CRITICAL dangling `aria-controls="tabpanel-make"`. Correct fix is one shared throttled announcer for all ~11 panels -- a permanently-mounted polite region (the mount-on-start at Transcribe.tsx:186 also means the first "Starting…" is likely never announced) whose text is recomputed only on a meaningful transition, reusing the existing repurposeLogic.ts:165-168 guard and LiveStatusRegion.tsx:38-52 component -- not a Transcribe-only patch, which would leave ten identical floods including the worse one.
- ⚠ scope correction: Transcribe's progress live region re-announces on every un-throttled per-segment tick, and so do its Diarize/Dub siblings. app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:187 puts `aria-live="polite"` on a container that wraps the changing pct (:189) and the changing message (:190); both are re-set per notification at :57-61, and the sidecar emits one notification per ASR segment with a message that always changes (sidecar/media_studio/features/transcribe.py:367-369), with zero throttle anywhere on the path (jobs.py:137-139 → protocol.py:118-119 → app/main/sidecar.ts:520-525 → app/main/preload.ts:286-290; literal `throttle` grep under app/ = 0 hits). This is the documented live-region-flooding anti-pattern; the exact number of utterances a user hears is screen-reader/browser dependent (NVDA/JAWS let user-initiated speech interrupt the polite queue), so the defensible harm is "polite-region text mutated at per-segment rate, unusable announcement channel during the panel's primary operation", not "the user hears nothing else until the job ends" — UNVERIFIED without an NVDA run. Scope the fix to the shared pattern, not one panel: the identical `<div className="progress" aria-live="polite">` + pct + message construction is fed at per-segment/per-cue cadence in Diarize.tsx:159-163 (via pyannote_backend.py:280-281 → diarize.py:326) and Dub.tsx:391-395 (via tts/dub.py:177 and :189), and appears with pct-only in Subtitles.tsx:342 and Tracks.tsx:277. Fix: move the visual pct/message spans out of any live region and add one polite region recomputed only on a meaningful transition (reuse the `aggregateUpdate` guard at repurposeLogic.ts:165-168 or coarsen to `Math.floor(pct/10)` plus phase flips), mirroring LiveStatusRegion.tsx:38-52. Note that dropping only the message span is insufficient — Transcribe.tsx:189 `{Math.round(pct)}%` remains inside the region and still changes up to ~100 times per job.

## Workspace tab strip above the Transcribe panel needs 1651px in a 1080px slot — the "collapsed" Advanced cluster always renders because `display:flex` defeats the `hidden` attribute
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:231 renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`, but app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152 declares `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; ... }`. Specificity (0,2,0) beats the UA sheet's `[hidden] { display:none }` (0,1,0), so the attribute is inert.
MEASURED (Playwright, repo CSS, harness C:/Users/Prekzursil/AppData/Local/Temp/rf-audit/transcribe.html + measure2.mjs, advancedOpen=false):
  ADVANCED_hiddenAttr: true | ADVANCED_display: flex | ADVANCED_rendered_offsetParent: true | ADVANCED_width: 493.3 | ADVANCED_convertTabClickable: true
  tabbar_xoverflow @1280x820 (shipped default, app/main/main.ts:1038-1039): 1651 vs 1080  <== X-OVERFLOW
  tabbar_xoverflow @940x600  (min window, app/main/main.ts:1040-1041):      1651 vs 740   <== X-OVERFLOW
Second, independent symptom — label wrapping: tab heights @1280 and @940 are tab_transcribe_h:36, tab_shortmaker_h:50, tab_nle_h:50; @2560 all three are 36. `.tab` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1041-1058) sets neither `white-space:nowrap` nor `flex-shrink:0` (measured tabWhiteSpace:"normal", tabFlexShrink:"1"), so under width pressure the labels break mid-word ("Short-maker", "Timeline export") BEFORE the strip scrolls — defeating the stated intent of app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:35-39 ("8 tabs must survive narrow windows without wrapping the chrome" + `overflow-x: auto`).
- why: On every shipped window width the chrome directly above the Transcribe panel is horizontally scrollable and 50px tall instead of 36px, and five "Deliver" tabs the app believes are collapsed are visible, hit-testable and occupying 493px of the strip. The user reaching Transcribe sees a cut-off, two-line, side-scrolling tab row out of the box at the default 1280x820 window — not only at some hypothetical narrow size.
- fix: Two independent edits, both in app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css: (1) restore the hidden contract — either scope the rule `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]) { display: flex; ... }` or add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none; }` after line 152; (2) make `overflow-x: auto` actually scroll instead of wrapping — add `white-space: nowrap; flex: none;` to `.tabbar .tab` (and `flex: none` on `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__group`) so tab labels cannot break mid-word. Re-run the harness and assert `tabbar.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` at 1280 with Advanced collapsed. NOTE: this is shared Workspace chrome rendered by Workspace.tsx:336-344 for all 13 panels — dedupe with any sibling auditing Workspace chrome or the a11y lens (a `hidden` control that is focusable/clickable is also an a11y defect).
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect is real and the fix is correct; three statements need tightening, and one consequence should be added.

1. CASCADE RATIONALE IS WRONG (conclusion still right). The finding says specificity (0,2,0) beats the UA sheet's `[hidden] { display:none }` (0,1,0). Specificity is not the operative rule — CASCADE ORIGIN is: any normal AUTHOR declaration beats any normal UA declaration regardless of specificity, so even a single-class `.tabbar__advanced-panel { display:flex }` would defeat `hidden`. Correct wording: "an author-origin `display:flex` declaration outranks the UA sheet's `[hidden] { display:none }` by cascade origin, so the attribute is inert." Both proposed fixes still work (`:not([hidden])` scoping, or an author-origin `[hidden] { display:none }` rule after line 152).

2. "LABELS BREAK MID-WORD" IS WRONG. `overflow-wrap` is never set to break-word/anywhere, so mid-word breaking cannot occur. The two-line tabs break at legitimate opportunities: "Short-maker" at the HYPHEN (confirmed as "SHORT-/MAKER" in workspace-preview-win32.png) and "Timeline export" at the SPACE. Correct wording: "labels wrap at their hyphen/space into two lines, doubling tab height 36px->50px, before the strip scrolls."

3. "ON EVERY SHIPPED WINDOW WIDTH" OVERREACHES. The window is user-resizable and the finding's own data shows all tab heights back to 36 at 2560. Since the strip needs ~1651px, a maximized window on a 1920+ monitor (slot ~1720px) does NOT overflow. Correct scope: "at the shipped DEFAULT (1280x820 -> 1080px slot) and at the MIN window (940x600 -> 740px slot), i.e. both widths main.ts ships (app/main/main.ts:1038-1041); the overflow clears once the slot exceeds ~1651px (roughly a maximized window at >=1920 width)."

4. ADD THE OMITTED (WORSE) CONSEQUENCE. At the default 1280 the Advanced disclosure toggle and the Export button (TabBar.tsx:244-258) are siblings rendered AFTER the tablist and are therefore pushed entirely off the visible strip — the committed baseline shows neither. The "persistent Export affordance" added deliberately by design-review P1 (workspace.css:154-157) is invisible out of the box, and the user cannot even reach the Advanced toggle without horizontally scrolling. Also note `aria-expanded="false"` (TabBar.tsx:248) misreports state to assistive tech.

5. CITATION DRIFT (harmless): the hidden div is at TabBar.tsx:239 at HEAD dcb59e4b, not :231 — #308 inserted an 8-line comment block above it. :231 was correct at the audit's 997669b0 baseline.

6. SURFACE ATTRIBUTION: filed under "Transcribe phase", but this is shared Workspace chrome (Workspace.tsx:336-344) affecting all 13 panels — the finding's own NOTE already says so, so this is breadth UNDER-claimed, not over-claimed. Re-file as Workspace-chrome scope.

7. ADD THE TEST-COVERAGE GAP as part of the fix: TabBar.test.tsx:97/:105 and Workspace.test.tsx:687 assert only markup/DOM-property `hidden`, which jsdom can satisfy while the CSS overrides it. The regression guard must be a computed-style or Playwright-visibility assertion (e.g. assert `getComputedStyle(panel).display === 'none'` and `tabbar.scrollWidth <= tabbar.clientWidth` at 1280 with Advanced collapsed), not a markup regex.
- ⚠ scope correction: Confirmed as reported, with the citation and mechanism corrected: the Workspace tab strip needs 1651px of scrollWidth in the 1080px slot available at the shipped 1280x820 default (740px at the 940x600 minimum), because the collapsed Advanced/Deliver cluster always renders — `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152` sets `display: flex` on `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel`, and a normal AUTHOR declaration outranks the user-agent `[hidden] { display: none }` by cascade ORIGIN (not specificity), so the `hidden={!advancedOpen}` attribute at `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239` (not :231) is inert. Independently measured with the real component + shipped CSS: ADV display flex, offsetParent non-null, width 493.3px, Convert tab hit-testable at the default size. Second, independent symptom: `.tab` (`app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1041-1058`) sets neither `white-space: nowrap` nor `flex-shrink: 0` (computed "normal"/"1"), so labels wrap mid-word before the strip scrolls — the strip is 50px tall at 1280 and 940 versus 36px at 2560. Additional confirmed consequence not in the original report: the persistent Export button lands at x=1835.5, entirely outside the window at both shipped widths, so the design-review P1 affordance is unreachable without horizontal scrolling. Corroborated by the committed CI baseline `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png`, whose producing test (`surfaces.visual.spec.ts:93-101`) never opens the Advanced disclosure yet shows the DELIVER label + CONVERT tab, the two-line SHORT-MAKER label, and the strip's horizontal scrollbar.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim overall — CONFIRMED, with three narrow scope corrections. Correctly-scoped version: "In grouped mode the `hidden` attribute on `.tabbar__advanced-panel` is inert because the author-origin `display: flex` at app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152 beats the user-agent `[hidden]{display:none}` by CASCADE ORIGIN (not by specificity — Chromium's `[hidden]:not([hidden=until-found])` is itself (0,2,0)). Consequently, at the shipped default 1280x820 window (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039) all five collapsed 'Deliver' tabs RENDER, occupy width and are hit-testable, though only DELIVER + CONVERT are VISIBLE without horizontal scrolling — nle/recipes/assets/tracks sit in the scroll overflow. The strip overflows and `.tab` labels wrap mid-word (SHORT-/MAKER two-line) because shell.css:1041-1058 sets neither white-space:nowrap nor flex-shrink:0; the exact 1651-vs-1080 and 50-vs-36 pixel figures are UNVERIFIED by this reviewer (harness not re-run), but the overflow, the clipped strip, the two-line wrap, and the off-screen Advanced toggle and Export button are all directly visible in the repo's current committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png. Surface note: the default landing panel is Subtitles, not Transcribe (Workspace.tsx:96) — this is shared chrome for all 13 panels."

## The Library loading region contains zero announceable text and is never mutated, so list-load start AND completion are both silent
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:544-549 renders `<div className="library__loading" role="status" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading your videos">`, and every descendant is hidden from AT: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:550 `<ul className="library__skeleton" aria-hidden="true">` wrapping the four ghost rows (:551-559). So the live region's accessible text content is the empty string. Timing makes it worse: `loading` initialises to `true` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:171 `useState(true)`), `refresh` is a `useCallback(..., [])` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:220-231) invoked from a single effect keyed on that stable ref (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:233-235), and grep finds no other caller — so `loading` transitions true→false exactly once per mount and never false→true. The region is therefore present at the instance's first paint and then unmounted; neither is a content mutation inside a mounted live region. On completion nothing announces the result: the grid (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:579-595) has no aria-live and no rendered count, and the empty state (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:562-572 'No videos yet') is a plain div. UNVERIFIED inline: whether a given SR speaks a live region's `aria-label` as the announcement payload varies by implementation — I did not measure it; the structurally airtight part is that the region has no text content to announce and is never mutated while mounted.
- why: The whole point of the skeleton is to communicate 'your videos are loading' — the code comment at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:542 claims 'aria-busy + label carry the state to AT', but they cannot: there is no text and no mutation. A screen-reader user arriving at Library hears nothing during the sidecar round-trip, and then nothing when the list (or 'No videos yet') materialises. They must manually re-read the region to discover the state changed — which is precisely what WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages, AA) exists to prevent. The a11y CI gate cannot catch this: app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:56-60 runs axe once on a settled Library, and axe has no rule for 4.1.3.
- fix: Give the region real text and keep it mounted across the transition: render a persistent `<div role="status">` whose content is `loading ? 'Loading your videos…' : videos.length === 0 ? 'No videos yet' : `${visible.length} videos`` (visually hidden — note no sr-only/visually-hidden utility exists yet in app/renderer/src, so add one), and drop `aria-label` from the skeleton wrapper. Keep the aria-hidden skeleton rows as pure layout. This also delivers the completion announcement the surface currently lacks.
- ⚠ scope correction: Optional headline tightening only (the finding is NOT refuted and the body is already correctly scoped): "The Library loading region's live-region announcement payload is empty (all descendants aria-hidden at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:550, and shell.css:600-664 adds no generated content), and it is never mutated while mounted (loading transitions true->false exactly once per mount; sole refresh call site at :234). So neither list-load start nor SUCCESSFUL completion is announced — the grid at :579 has no aria-live or count and the empty state at :562-572 is a plain div. The failure completion is the one exception: it announces via role='alert' at :512-516."
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity, not high. Mechanically accurate as stated: the Library loading region (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:544-549) has zero accessible text because its only child subtree is aria-hidden (:550), and `loading` transitions true→false exactly once per mount (:171, :220-231, :233-235 — one call site, verified by grep), so neither load start nor completion is ever a content mutation inside a mounted live region; the completion is likewise unannounced (grid :579-595 and empty state :562-572 carry no live region or count, and the surface's only aria-live — app/renderer/src/views/LibraryToolbar.tsx:61 — is the batch-select count gated on selectedCount>0 at :59).

But the user-facing consequence is confined to a degraded-sidecar window, not the normal path. In the normal path `loading` lasts one IPC round-trip: the shell is withheld until the sidecar is provisioned and ready (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:593-604), with the genuinely long ~3-min first-run build (App.tsx:585) already correctly announced by FirstRunSetup's own live regions (app/renderer/src/components/FirstRunSetup.tsx:456, :476); the request itself is one SQLite SELECT (sidecar/media_studio/library.py:283-287) over a persistent child process (app/main/sidecar.ts:286, 304, 323, 446) that long jobs cannot block because they run on daemon threads (sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:647). UNVERIFIED inline: latency is inferred from query shape + transport, not instrumented — the settling experiment is to log the true→false delta for `loading` on a warm sidecar; the in-repo 1500ms (app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:81) is a CI stability pad, not a measurement. A transition faster than perception leaves no state for a status message to convey, in either direction.

Drop the WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.3 conformance framing for the completion half: the app presents no visible video count (verified: Library.tsx:469-489, LibraryToolbar.tsx:31-77), and 4.1.3 requires parity with visually-presented status messages rather than an SR-only status with no visual counterpart — a list arriving is content in the normal reading order. UNVERIFIED inline: read from my own knowledge of the SC, not the normative W3C Understanding text (likely, 55-80%).

The defect worth fixing is the narrow one: when the sidecar is crashed or restarting post-provisioning (documented at app/renderer/src/App.tsx:590-591; restart path app/main/sidecar.ts:346-360), `loading` can hold for seconds and the SR user then cannot distinguish "still loading" from "library is empty". The error path is already covered by Library.tsx:512-516 `role="alert"`. The proposed fix (a persistent visually-hidden `role="status"` with real text, dropping aria-label from the skeleton wrapper, plus the missing sr-only utility) is correct and cheap — treat it as a11y polish, applied consistently with the identical empty-region pattern at app/renderer/src/components/ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:145, not as an AA conformance blocker.

## An in-flight multi-file import is orphaned when the Library unmounts on a tab switch; videos added after the remount's single library.list read are invisible until another remount
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:256-282` — `addPaths` loops `await rpc<AddResult>('library.add', { path: p })` sequentially with NO AbortController, no mounted-ref guard, and no `useEffect` cleanup that could cancel it (the only cleanup in the component clears toast timers, `Library.tsx:192-197`). The ONLY `library.list` read is the mount effect `refresh` (`Library.tsx:220-235`); there is no polling, no subscription, and no focus/visibility refresh anywhere in the renderer (grep for `visibilitychange` and `addEventListener('focus'` over `app/renderer/src` → 0 matches). Because `adding` (`Library.tsx:173`) is remount-fresh `false`, the Add button (`Library.tsx:480-487`, `disabled={adding}`) comes back enabled and a second concurrent import can start. The import is also invisible to the global Jobs pill: `library.add` is a synchronous direct-return RPC with no jobId (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:124-132`, docstring "Direct-return"), while the pill counts only `job.list` (`app/renderer/src/components/useActiveJobs.ts:40`). The window is wide because each add spawns an ffprobe: `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:306` `float(self._probe(abspath))` → `library.py:61-69` `ffmpeg.ffprobe_duration`.
- why: Concretely: drop 40 files, and while the sequential ffprobe loop is at file 12 switch to Edit and back. Library remounts, `refresh()` returns the 12-ish rows committed so far, and the orphaned loop keeps adding files 13-40 to the SQLite library while its `setVideos` calls land on a dead mount. The remounted view has no mechanism to learn about them — no poll, no event, no focus refresh — so 28 successfully imported videos are absent from the grid with no spinner, no Jobs-pill entry, and no error. The user concludes the import failed and re-imports (or gives up). Recovering requires navigating away and back a second time, which is not discoverable.
- fix: Two parts. (1) Make the import cancel-aware and re-entrancy-safe: hold an `AbortController`/`cancelled` ref, check it between iterations of the `for (const p of paths)` loop in `Library.tsx:262-275`, and abort it from a `useEffect` cleanup so an unmount stops the loop instead of orphaning it. (2) Give the list a reconciliation path so a remount cannot show a frozen snapshot — either re-run `refresh()` on window focus/visibility, or lift the import into the sidecar job system so it gets a jobId, appears in the Jobs pill (`useActiveJobs.ts:40`) and survives navigation like every other long operation. The second is the durable fix, since it also covers a window close mid-import.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED (medium, not high): because App.tsx:468-527 unmounts Library on a rail switch and Library.tsx:224 is read only by the once-per-mount effect (Library.tsx:233-235), an in-flight multi-file import (Library.tsx:262-264, no abort/mounted guard) keeps committing rows to SQLite (library.py:321) after the remount's single `library.list` snapshot, so those videos are absent from the grid with no spinner, no error, and no Jobs-pill entry (library_ops.py:124-132 is direct-return, no jobId; useActiveJobs.ts:40 counts only job.list) — and there is no focus/visibility/subscription reconciliation anywhere in the renderer (0 grep hits). Corrections to the original wording: (a) recovery is NOT limited to "navigating away and back a second time" — re-adding the same paths also fully repairs the grid, cheaply, because library.py:301-303 returns the existing row and short-circuits BEFORE the ffprobe while Library.tsx:267 prepends each returned row (so the user's own predicted "re-import" is self-healing, not futile); (b) severity is medium, not high — nothing is lost or corrupted (every add is committed at library.py:321 and appears on the next mount or restart), the mis-state is transient, and it requires a mid-import navigation; (c) the window is typically seconds for a healthy 40-file local drop (ffmpeg.py:52 "near-instant for a healthy local file"), widening only for corrupt/slow/network inputs up to PROBE_TIMEOUT_SEC = 60.0 (ffmpeg.py:53); (d) proposed fix part (1) is counterproductive as written — aborting the loop on unmount would silently import 12 of 40 files with no error, and the repo's peer convention (MakeShorts.test.tsx:577, Edit.test.tsx:267) is only a `cancelled` late-setState guard, which here would change nothing observable since post-unmount setState is already a no-op. Only part (2) — a reconciliation path (focus/visibility re-`refresh()`, or lifting the import into the sidecar job system so it carries a jobId) — actually closes the defect.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high) - Library's import loop is not unmount-aware, so a remount landing mid-import shows an under-reported grid until the next remount; nothing is lost and it self-heals three ways.

Scoped statement: `addPaths` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:256-282) has no mounted/cancelled guard, and a tab switch unmounts Library (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:468-527, switch on route.name; rendered at App.tsx:517-525) while the sequential `library.add` loop keeps running. Because the component's only `library.list` read is its mount effect (Library.tsx:220-235) and the renderer has no poll, subscription, or focus/visibility reconciliation (0 matches for visibilitychange / addEventListener('focus') over app/renderer/src), a remount that lands mid-import renders only the rows committed at that instant. Measured window: 320 ms median per file (8 ffprobe runs, 214-844 ms, sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:450-488) => ~13 s for a 40-file import, so the away-and-back is reachable.

Impact is MEDIUM, not high: every row is committed (sidecar/media_studio/library.py:289-322) and library_list reads live SQLite (library_ops.py:119-121), so nothing is lost; and the state self-heals on any Library remount (App.tsx:509-525 -> Library.tsx:233-235), on app restart, or on a re-import - which is idempotent and test-pinned (library.py:299-303; sidecar/tests/test_library.py:85-89) and skips the ffprobe (library.py:306 is in the not-existing branch only), so the user's natural retry renders all rows with no duplicates.

The sharper co-located defect: App.tsx:518-524 passes no `toast` prop, so per-file error and "Added N videos" toasts route to the local fallback strip (Library.tsx:209-215) and are destroyed with the mount - failures among the orphaned files are silent.

Proportionate fix: a `cancelled` ref that suppresses the dead-mount setState (the pattern the codebase already uses at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:93/103 and 117/133, and app/renderer/src/components/useActiveJobs.ts:37/49) PLUS a reconciliation read on remount/focus and a `toast` prop wired from App so import outcomes survive navigation. Do NOT abort the loop on unmount - that turns transient invisibility into 28 files never imported.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED with severity scoped to medium (not high) and two sentences tightened: An in-flight multi-file import in Library keeps running after the component unmounts on a tab switch (App.tsx:468-527, 421-423, 456), because addPaths has no AbortController, no mounted-ref guard, and no useEffect cleanup that cancels it (Library.tsx:256-282; the only cleanup clears toast timers, Library.tsx:192-197). Its setVideos and even its success toast land on the dead instance — App wires no `toast` prop (App.tsx:518-525), so the local fallback strip dies with the instance. The only read that POPULATES the Library grid is the mount-effect refresh (Library.tsx:220-235); other renderer call sites read library.list for unrelated purposes (App.tsx:335, BatchQueue.tsx:90, Timeline.tsx:158). With no polling, subscription, or focus/visibility refresh (0 grep matches; the only two setInterval sites are job polls), any file committed after the remount's read stays absent from the grid until a later Library remount, with no spinner (adding is remount-fresh false, Library.tsx:173) and no Jobs-pill entry (library.add is direct-return with no jobId, library_ops.py:124-132; the pill counts only job.list, useActiveJobs.ts:40). No data is lost: rows are committed (library.py:321) and a later remount lists them all (library.py:283-287). Because library.add is idempotent by resolved path (library.py:301-303), the user's natural re-import recovery does work and creates no duplicates — so the residual harm is the false "import failed" belief and the give-up branch, plus a re-enabled Add button permitting a concurrent duplicate-ffprobe pass (Library.tsx:480-487), not permanent loss.

## Remove button's hover label renders at 2.94:1 — the card's own hover tint compounds the wrong red token
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:443-447 sets `.library__remove-btn:hover { background: var(--status-error-soft); color: var(--status-error); }`. The button (rendered with visible text "Remove", app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:159-166) is a descendant of `li.library__item`, which flips its own background on the SAME pointer event: app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:55-61 `li.library__item:hover { background: var(--surface-hover) }` and :69-72 `li.library__item:active { background: var(--surface-active) }`. Measured (WCAG relative luminance re-derived from the raw token hex in app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css, with rgba(229,72,77,0.10) composited src-over the real parent plane): #e5484d on error-soft over --surface-hover #2c3448 -> effective bg rgb(62,54,72) = **2.94:1**; over --surface-active #353f56 -> rgb(71,64,85) = **2.52:1**; even over the resting --surface-raised = 3.75:1. Text is 12px/600 (--type-control-size, shell.css:354-355) so the AA floor is 4.5:1. The repo's own guard already forbids this exact pairing: app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 asserts `contrast(--status-error, over(--status-error-soft, --surface-raised)) < 4.5` and its comment states "a component MUST route alert text through --status-error-text, not --status-error".
- why: This is the destructive per-card action, and the failing state is precisely the state a user is in while aiming at it — hover, then press. At 2.94:1 (and 2.52:1 on mousedown) the word "Remove" is below AA for low-vision users at exactly the moment a mis-click deletes a library entry. Four sibling consumers on this same surface were already migrated to the lighter red text token (app/renderer/src/components/library-shell.css:56, :181; app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:180; app/renderer/src/features/library-provenance.css:50) — this one was missed, so it is an incomplete rollout, not a deliberate exception.
- fix: Change `color: var(--status-error)` to `color: var(--status-error-text)` at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:446. That alone lifts hover to ~4.14:1 — still short, because the parent card is simultaneously lightened. Fix both halves: either (a) suppress the card-level hover/active tint while the pointer is over the meta lane (`li.library__item:has(.library__item-meta :hover) { background: var(--surface-raised) }`), or (b) give the hovered Remove button an opaque own background instead of a 10%-alpha wash so it stops inheriting the card tint. Then extend the conformance guard (see the INTERACTION_PLANES finding) so the regression cannot return.
