- ⚠ scope correction: Verdict unchanged (CONFIRMED, high) — this is a precision tightening of two supporting sentences, not a downgrade: "app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:443-447 pairs `color: var(--status-error)` with the `--status-error-soft` 10%-alpha wash on the Remove button, whose only backdrop is the card's own simultaneously-tinted `li.library__item` plane (library-cards.css:55-61 hover, :69-72 active, with no intervening opaque background). The 12px/600 'Remove' label therefore renders at 2.93:1 on hover and 2.52:1 on mousedown against a 4.5:1 AA floor (best case, over the unreachable resting `--surface-raised` plane, is still only 3.75:1). The repo's own tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 asserts exactly this pairing fails and states a component MUST route red text through `--status-error-text`. This is a CLASS-wide gap, not one missed instance: the same rule at shell.css:444 hits `.sm-row-decide button[aria-label='Discard']:hover`, and ~20 further sites still use `color: var(--status-error)` for text, several on the same wash. Uncaught because ELEVATION_PLANES (tokens.conformance.test.ts:129-134) excludes the hover/active tints and the Library axe test (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:56-60) scans only the resting state."
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (consistency/polish, not a11y-critical): `.library__remove-btn:hover` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:443-447) routes its label through `--status-error` instead of `--status-error-text`, and because the parent card lightens its own plane on the same pointer event (app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:55-61, :69-72) the 10%-alpha wash composites over a lifted background, putting the 12px/600 label at 2.93:1 on hover and 2.52:1 on press (independently re-derived; 3.75:1 even over the resting --surface-raised) against a 4.5:1 AA floor. This is a real violation of the repo's own documented rule that red STRINGS must use `--status-error-text` (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:73-79) and of the invariant asserted at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304.

Correctly scoped, however: (a) impact is limited — hover/press are post-aim confirmation states, the resting label is comfortably AA, the control carries aria-label="Remove <title>" (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:162), and `library.remove` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:368-384) drops a catalog row without touching the file on disk, re-addable in two clicks — the codebase reserves confirm() for actual file deletion (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:146-147); and (b) it is NOT a missed straggler — the `--status-error-text` migration was deliberately scoped to the 5 sheets named in `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658), which never included shell.css, and ~30 other bare `color: var(--status-error)` text usages remain renderer-wide (e.g. jobqueue.css:150, providersKeys.css:135, setupStatus.css:62, shell.css:567/1222/1425).

The genuinely useful residual — worth filing on its own merits — is that the guard is FILE-scoped rather than SELECTOR-scoped, so any `.library__*` red-text rule that lives outside those 5 sheets escapes it. Fixing the one-token color at shell.css:446 lifts hover to 4.13:1 (still under AA because the card tint compounds), so a complete fix also needs the card-level tint suppressed under the meta lane or an opaque button background. UNVERIFIED: whether any existing axe/visual e2e spec exercises the Library card hover state at all — I did not open app/e2e/visual/*.spec.ts, so I cannot say whether this state is covered by an automated gate; reading those specs would settle it.

## Library's role="alert" error banner is sub-AA at 4.23:1 — uses --status-error where the repo's own test mandates --status-error-text
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:561-569 styles `.library__error` with `color: var(--status-error)` (:567) on `background: var(--status-error-soft)` (:568). It is the surface's error channel, rendered at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:512-516 as `<div className="library__error" role="alert">` — it carries library.list failures, library.remove rollbacks (Library.tsx:378-380) and the batch-remove failure count (Library.tsx:411-413). The banner sits directly on the canvas (`.library` declares no background; html/body is --surface-bg per shell.css:11-19). Measured: rgba(229,72,77,0.10) over #121620 -> effective bg rgb(39,27,36); #e5484d against it = **4.23:1** against a 4.5:1 floor (inherited 13px body text, shell.css:17). app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 is an executable assertion that this exact token pairing fails AA, and app/renderer/src/views/director.css:71-73 shows a sibling view that was migrated with a comment citing the rule verbatim.
- why: An alert is the one string on the surface a user cannot afford to miss, and it is the only feedback channel for a failed import or a failed delete. 4.23:1 is a WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) failure — marginal in number but categorical in kind, and it is the highest-stakes text on the view. That the fix token exists, is tested, and was applied to four neighbours makes this a rollout gap with a one-token remedy rather than a design trade-off.
- fix: Change `color: var(--status-error)` to `color: var(--status-error-text)` at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:567 (this rule also covers `.workspace__error`, so the sibling surface is fixed in the same edit). Keep `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` at :565 — a 3px border is non-text and the solid red is correct there. Then add a conformance assertion that no component sheet pairs `color: var(--status-error)` with `background: var(--status-error-soft)`, which would have caught this and the Remove-button case mechanically.
- ⚠ scope correction: Library's role="alert" error banner is sub-AA at 4.227:1 — shell.css:567 uses `color: var(--status-error)` on the `--status-error-soft` wash (shell.css:568) over the bare canvas `--surface-bg` (shell.css:11-19), the exact pairing the repo's own test proves fails AA at tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 and whose comment at :299 states a component MUST use `--status-error-text` instead. The mechanical guard does not reach this file: RED_TEXT_LEAK (tokens.conformance.test.ts:649) is applied only to the five-sheet LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS allowlist (:652-658), which excludes shell.css — so this is an unenforced rollout gap against a documented repo norm, not a failing test. Six sibling sheets were already migrated (director.css:73, library-cards.css:180, library-shell.css:56/181, readinessBadge.css:34, library-provenance.css:50/111, keep-copy-control.css:112/127), and the fix token is proven >=4.5:1 on this exact backdrop by tokens.conformance.test.ts:287-293.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (recategorized from contrast-harms-users to self-imposed-invariant coverage gap): `.library__error` at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:567 uses `color: var(--status-error)` on `background: var(--status-error-soft)` (:568), which composites to 4.23:1 on --surface-bg — below the 4.5:1 AA floor the repo's own DoD pins (tokens.conformance.test.ts:640) for 13px body text (tokens.css:145). The text remains legible and no information is colour-only, so there is no demonstrated user harm; the defect is that components/shell.css is omitted from the LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS allowlist at tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658, so the guard at :688-698 whose header claims "the Library sheets route their red text through the AA-safe token" does not actually cover the Library's primary error banner. This is one instance of a repo-wide pattern: ~25 bare `color: var(--status-error)` text sites remain against ~8 migrated, and instances on --surface-raised (caption.css:51, lineage.css:113, panels.css:409) are worse at ~3.75:1 — the Library banner is the best case, not the worst. Correct fix is not a new assertion but extending the existing guard to all component sheets and migrating the ~25 sites to --status-error-text in one pass; shell.css alone carries four leaks (:446, :567, :1222, :1425). Treat as a batched consistency cleanup, not a user-facing accessibility defect.
- ⚠ scope correction: Library's role="alert" delete/list error banner renders red text below WCAG AA. `.library__error` (with `.workspace__error`) at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:561-569 pairs `color: var(--status-error)` (:567) with `background: var(--status-error-soft)` (:568); rendered at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:513 on the canvas plane (`.library` sets no background, shell.css:503-510; html/body = --surface-bg, shell.css:14), the composite is rgb(39,27,36) and #e5484d against it measures 4.227:1 at inherited 13px body text (tokens.css:145) — under the 4.5:1 floor. It carries three channels: library.list failure (Library.tsx:227), single-remove rollback (:379) and batch-remove failure count (:412). It does NOT carry import failures — those route to `.library__toast--error` (emitToast at Library.tsx:270/273/294/301/329, styled --text-primary on --surface-overlay at shell.css:914-927), which is AA-clean. The repo already ships the fix token: tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 executably asserts this exact pairing fails AA and its comment (:299) says components MUST use --status-error-text, and 6 sibling sheets were migrated (views/director.css:73, components/library-shell.css:56,181, library-cards.css:180, readinessBadge.css:34, features/library-provenance.css:50,111, keep-copy-control.css:112,127) — but the test's executable no-leak scan (:688-698) enumerates only 5 Library sheets (:652-658) and EXCLUDES shell.css, so nothing is currently red; this is an unenforced rollout gap, not a failing test. Fix: `color: var(--status-error-text)` at shell.css:567 (measures 5.961:1 on the same composite; keep the 3px solid --status-error border at :565). ## Re-running "Start transcription" silently overwrites the persisted transcript, destroying diarization labels and user-typed speaker names — no confirm, no undo
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The action is a bare, unguarded button: `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:176-178` renders `<button onClick={start} disabled={running || !videoId}>Start transcription</button>`; `start` (`Transcribe.tsx:65-88`) fires `transcribe.start` immediately with no existence check, no dialog, no warning copy.

The panel CANNOT warn even if it wanted to: `TranscribeProps` is `{videoId, onTranscript?}` only (`Transcribe.tsx:17-21`) and `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:298` mounts it as `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} />` — no `project`, no `hasTranscript` (the flag exists on the wire at `app/renderer/src/components/api.ts:64` and is rendered as a Library badge at `app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:108`, just never passed here).

The sidecar overwrite is unconditional: `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:435-439` — `if not job_ctx.cancelled: project = self._load_or_create_project(video_id); project.data["transcript"] = transcript; project.save()`.

What that key holds is user work, not just machine output: `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/features/diarize.py:374-377` (`diarize.rename`) writes the user's typed friendly speaker names into the SAME `transcript` key, driven by the "Rename speakers" text inputs at `app/renderer/src/features/Diarize.tsx:183-191`; `diarize.py:343` writes the SPEAKER_NN labels there too.

The authors already treat this data as worth protecting — but only in the other direction: `diarize.py:332-343` refuses to save when `fresh.get("transcript") != transcript`, commenting "if a concurrent transcribe.start re-wrote the transcript while we were clustering, blind-saving would clobber the newer text ... Fail loud instead of last-writer-wins." `transcribe_start` has no symmetric guard.

There is no undo: `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/library.py:546-555` `Project.save()` does a plain `_write_json` with no versioning or `.bak` (the `.bak` at `library.py:211-222` is the library index migration only), and `director.undo` (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/director_ops.py:380-399`) only replays recorded Director inverse ops — it knows nothing about transcripts.

The codebase has the confirm pattern it is missing here: `C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:146-147` — "Confirm before any destructive call (UI confirms first — §2 shorts.delete)".

Collateral: the semantic index built from the old transcript is invalidated and refuses to serve (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/vision_ops.py:715-724`, "semantic index for {video_id} is stale"), forcing a paid/embedding rebuild.
- why: A user who ran Diarize, hand-typed real names for four speakers, then returned to the Transcribe tab and clicked Start (to try a different language hint, or just to re-check) loses every name and every speaker label permanently, with no dialog beforehand and no way back. Because the panel unmounts on tab switch without cancelling the job (`Transcribe.tsx:127-130,146-147` abort only the LOCAL wait — no `job.cancel`), navigating away does not prevent the overwrite either: the server job runs to completion and persists regardless.
- fix: Pass the existing `hasTranscript` (or the loaded `project`) into `Transcribe` from `Workspace.tsx:298`, and when a transcript is already present change the button to a destructive-confirm path following the `Shorts.tsx:146-147` precedent — label it "Re-transcribe (replaces the existing transcript)" and confirm with copy naming exactly what is lost ("speaker labels and any names you typed in Diarize will be discarded"). Independently, make it recoverable server-side: in `media_ops.py:435-439`, before overwriting, stash the prior value (e.g. `project.data["transcriptPrevious"]`) so a one-shot restore is possible — or preserve the per-segment `speaker` / `speakers` roster across a re-transcribe when the segment boundaries still align.
- ⚠ scope correction: The headline claim needs no rescoping and stands as written. Only one secondary sub-claim is wider than its evidence — the semantic-index collateral. Correctly scoped: the stale-index refusal at sidecar/media_studio/handlers/vision_ops.py:715-724 fires only when the re-transcribe actually changes the corpus fingerprint (vision_ops.py:721 compares `transcriptFp`); a re-run yielding byte-identical segment text would still match and keep serving. In the finding's own scenario (a different language hint) the text does differ, so the collateral does fire there. Settling experiment: re-run transcribe.start twice with identical settings and compare `_transcript_fp(_si.build_corpus(...))` across the two saves.
- ⚠ scope correction: Headline stands as written. Two SUPPORTING sentences should be tightened, plus one nuance disclosed:

1. Replace "The panel CANNOT warn even if it wanted to" with: "The panel is never GIVEN the existence signal — `TranscribeProps` is `{videoId, onTranscript?}` (Transcribe.tsx:17-21) and Workspace.tsx:298 passes only `videoId` — so warning requires either a new prop (`hasTranscript`/`project`, already on the wire at components/api.ts:64) or an extra `project.open` read the panel does not currently make. It does hold the RPC bridge (Transcribe.tsx:83), so the gap is a wiring gap, not an impossibility."

2. Replace "forcing a paid/embedding rebuild" with: "forcing an `index.build` rebuild (vision_ops.py:715-725) — compute cost under the privacy-default LocalEmbedder (vision_ops.py:702), monetary cost only when a cloud embedder is configured."

3. Add inline to "loses every name ... no way back": "Exception: friendly names already baked into a subtitle track generated AFTER the rename do survive — subtitles.py:102-163 copies `speaker` into cues and `project.data['tracks']` is untouched by media_ops.py:438 — but that neither restores the transcript nor the Diarize roster, and it only applies if the user generated subtitles after renaming."

## Manual export announces nothing for up to 35 minutes, and disabling the pressed button dumps focus to <body>
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:258 passes busy={manualBusy} into ManualInterval; the ONLY consumer of that prop is disabled={busy || ranges.length === 0} at app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:121. Grep over app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx returns exactly four aria hits (aria-label x2 at :69/:83, role="alert" at :97 for input validation, aria-label "Remove range" at :109) - no aria-live, no role="status", no aria-busy, no <progress>. The wait is a deferred job: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:177-185 calls waitForJobDone(..., EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS), and EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS = DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:729) = 35 * 60 * 1000 (app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:62). The AI sibling path DOES have the region: app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:924-931 role="status" aria-live="polite" + <progress>. The manual path is the one the golden-journey e2e drives (app/e2e/golden-journey.spec.ts:229).
- why: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA) failure on the front door's primary deterministic action. A screen-reader user activates "Make shorts from ranges", the button they are focused on becomes disabled in the same commit (Chromium then moves focus to <body>, losing their place), and nothing is spoken - no "started", no percentage, no "still working" - for anywhere up to 35 minutes. The user cannot distinguish "running" from "the click did nothing" and will re-activate or abandon. On settle, MakeShorts.tsx:187-188 sets the note AND opens the tray in one commit, so a whole new <section aria-label="Output options"> of checkboxes/selects/buttons (OutputTray.tsx:80) is injected with no focus move and no announcement beyond the one-line role="status" note at MakeShorts.tsx:265.
- fix: Mirror the AI path: render a persistent role="status" aria-live="polite" region in the manual section (present in the DOM before the export starts, text swapped rather than the node mounted) carrying "Exporting your ranges..." plus progress when available; set aria-busy="true" on the .make-shorts__manual section while manualBusy. Instead of disabling the activating button, keep it enabled and no-op (or move focus to the status region first) so focus is not dropped to <body>. On settle, move focus to the OutputTray heading (OutputTray.tsx:81) so the new controls are discoverable.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): The manual export path gives NO progress or status feedback of any kind - to any input modality - for the entire duration of a deferred export, bounded by a 35-minute UI ceiling (EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS, shortMakerLogic.ts:729 -> _api.ts:62), though the sidecar's own 30-minute watchdog normally force-finishes first (_api.ts:51-60) and a typical short range settles in seconds.

The single consumer of the busy prop is disabled={busy || ranges.length === 0} (ManualInterval.tsx:121), fed from MakeShorts.tsx:268. ManualInterval.tsx contains no aria-live, role="status", aria-busy or <progress>, and manualInterval.css contains no spinner/animation/busy rule - so the only state change during the export is the browser's default disabled rendering. The first feedback of any kind is the post-settle note at MakeShorts.tsx:187, which the project's own e2e waits up to 30s for (golden-journey.spec.ts:234-237).

This is primarily an INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY defect: 8+ sibling deferred-job flows already implement the house pattern (aria-live + <progress> + aria-busy) - Assets.tsx:182-183, Convert.tsx:326-327, Dub.tsx:391-392, Diarize.tsx:159-160, Refine.tsx:262-263, Recipes.tsx:228-229, ProducedShorts.tsx:208,214, DirectorPanel.tsx:543 - and the AI sibling in the same view does so at ShortMaker.tsx:924-931 using job.progress events that are already on the wire (_api.ts:56-60). It is a WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) status-message gap, but the user-visible harm is not SR-specific: no user learns the export started, and keyboard users additionally lose their place because disabling the focused activating button drops focus to <body> (Chromium behavior - inferred from code, UNVERIFIED by execution in this audit).

FIX (do not literally mirror the AI sibling, which is itself conditionally mounted and gated on non-null progress): render a persistent role="status" aria-live="polite" region in .make-shorts__manual that is present in the DOM before the export starts with its TEXT swapped rather than the node mounted; set aria-busy on the section while manualBusy; add a visible progress affordance fed by the existing job.progress stream; and either keep the activating button enabled as a no-op or move focus to the status region before it is disabled. On settle, move focus to the OutputTray heading (OutputTray.tsx:81).
- ⚠ scope correction: Manual export gives a screen-reader user no in-flight feedback and drops their focus to <body> for the whole run (up to a 35-minute ceiling)

Two defects on the Make Shorts manual path, neither of which is a WCAG 4.1.3 failure:

(1) FOCUS DROP (the normative defect; operability, usually cited under SC 2.4.3 Focus Order, Level A — NOT 4.1.3/AA). Activating "Make shorts from ranges" runs setManualBusy(true) synchronously inside the click handler (MakeShorts.tsx:159, before the first await at :171), so the click and the disable land in ONE React commit. busy's only consumer is disabled={busy || ranges.length === 0} (ManualInterval.tsx:121), so the button the user is focused on becomes disabled while focused; per the HTML Standard focus-fixup rule the focused area resets to the body. Nothing restores it — MakeShorts.tsx contains no .focus() or activeElement reference, and focus is still on <body> after manualBusy clears in the finally at :192. UNVERIFIED empirically: this is spec-grounded (~90-95%), not probed; jsdom does not model focus-fixup so the vitest suite cannot catch it. Settling experiment: Playwright against the packaged app — click .manual-interval__make, assert document.activeElement === document.body.

(2) NO IN-FLIGHT FEEDBACK AT ALL (a real usability/a11y defect and an unmet advisory technique — ARIA22/G13 — but NOT an SC failure, because SC 4.1.3 only requires that an EXISTING status message be programmatically determinable and does not require one to exist). The wait is a deferred job bounded by EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS (MakeShorts.tsx:179-184 → shortMakerLogic.ts:729 → _api.ts:62 = 35 * 60 * 1000). Across that window: ManualInterval.tsx has no aria-live/role="status"/aria-busy/<progress> (full-file read); manualInterval.css (all 49 lines) has no busy/spinner/progress/disabled rule, so the ONLY change of any kind is the UA-default greyed button; and no global announcer exists — JobQueue.tsx carries zero aria-live/role="status"/aria-busy and LiveStatusRegion.tsx is never imported by MakeShorts.tsx. Progress data is available but unsubscribed: waitForJobDone (_api.ts:229-236) listens only to onJobDone/onSidecarStatus, while the job.progress relay the AI path uses (ShortMaker.tsx:165,228; lib/rpc/client.ts:114) is right there. Combined with (1), the user cannot distinguish "running" from "the click did nothing" and will re-activate or abandon. This is the path the golden journey drives (golden-journey.spec.ts:225-229), and MakeShorts.test.tsx stubs ManualInterval (:110-115) so no test exercises it.

RESIDUAL, correctly scoped (not a clean SC failure): the settle-time message DOES exist and DOES carry role="status" (MakeShorts.tsx:275), so 4.1.3 is met on its face; the weakness is that the region is mounted together with its text, which is unreliable across browser/SR pairs (ARIA19/ARIA22 advise it pre-exist). Separately, the OutputTray <section aria-label="Output options"> (OutputTray.tsx:80) is injected in the same commit as the note (MakeShorts.tsx:188, rendered at :279-286) with no focus move.

FIX: add a persistently-mounted role="status" aria-live="polite" region inside .make-shorts__manual whose TEXT is swapped (do NOT copy the AI path here — ShortMaker.tsx:924 gates on {busy && progress && ...} and has the same mount-with-content weakness); subscribe the manual path to the existing job.progress relay so a percentage is available; set aria-busy on the manual section while manualBusy; and either keep the activating button enabled as a no-op or move focus deliberately before disabling it. If focus is moved to the OutputTray heading on settle, give that <h3> (OutputTray.tsx:81) tabIndex={-1} — as written it is not focusable.
- ⚠ scope correction: Manual export gives a screen-reader user no perceivable feedback for the whole duration of a deferred export job, and disabling the pressed button drops focus. During manualBusy the manual section renders no status text at all (MakeShorts.tsx:157 nulls manualNote) and ManualInterval carries no aria-live, role="status", aria-busy or <progress> (ManualInterval.tsx:69-121) - its only use of the busy prop is disabled={busy || ranges.length === 0} at :121 - so the sole state signal is the activating button going disabled, which in Chromium resets focus to <body> (platform behavior, UNVERIFIED-by-execution in this audit). No global channel covers the gap: ToastHost.tsx:73 is a permanently-mounted polite region but MakeShorts.tsx pushes no toast; the App.tsx:544-560 Jobs count sits outside any live region; JobQueue.tsx:175 renders null while closed. The silence lasts until job.done arrives - ordinarily bounded by the sidecar's 30-min watchdog (shortMakerLogic.ts:720-728), and up to the 35-min client ceiling (EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS -> _api.ts:62) if the sidecar wedges while still reporting 'running'. The AI sibling path has the region the manual path lacks (ShortMaker.tsx:924-931), and the manual path is the one the golden journey drives (golden-journey.spec.ts:229). Rather than a clean WCAG 4.1.3 failure for the silent phase (4.1.3 requires that status messages an author DOES present be announced; none is presented here), the precise SC exposure is at settle: MakeShorts.tsx:187-188 mounts a fresh role="status" note plus a whole new <section aria-label="Output options"> (OutputTray.tsx:80) in one commit with no focus move - and this repo's own ToastHost.tsx:61-65 documents that freshly-inserted polite regions are announced unreliably by NVDA/JAWS. The proposed fix (persistent pre-mounted polite region with swapped text, aria-busy on the manual section, keep the button enabled or move focus before disabling, move focus to the OutputTray heading on settle) addresses both halves and matches the pattern the codebase already endorses.

## Raw Python exception text (incl. absolute user paths and internal RPC method names) is rendered verbatim to the user across every Edit-phase panel
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `error-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Full traced chain, every hop verified:
1. sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:810 — a failed job emits `{"error": {"message": str(exc), "type": exc.__class__.__name__}}` (raw `str(exc)` of ANY handler exception).
2. sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:151 — a direct-return handler crash becomes `RpcError(f"internal error in {req.method}: {exc}")`.
3. app/main/sidecar.ts:506-511 — `const message = err.message ?? 'sidecar error'; const wrapped = new Error(message)` (verbatim passthrough).
4. app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:279 — `settleReject(new Error(failure.message))`.
5. Panel catch → bare render, e.g. app/renderer/src/features/Convert.tsx:110 `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err))` → Convert.tsx:346-350 `<p className="error" role="alert">{error}</p>`; identical shape at Subtitles.tsx:100/124/178/200 → Subtitles.tsx:354-358; Transcribe.tsx:113 → Transcribe.tsx:194-198; Timeline.tsx:382-386.
Concrete user-visible strings:
- sidecar/media_studio/features/convert.py:257 — `RuntimeError(f"ffmpeg exited with code {code} converting {in_path}")` → the user's ABSOLUTE source path is printed in the Convert panel (Convert is also the workspace Export destination, Workspace.tsx:105).
- sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:47 — `video {video_id} has no transcript yet (run transcribe.start first)` → shown on the DEFAULT Edit landing tab (Workspace.tsx:96 `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles'`), telling a user to "run transcribe.start", an internal JSON-RPC method with no UI equivalent by that name.
- sidecar/media_studio/handlers/_shared.py:73 — `"videoId (str) is required"`.
The behaviour is pinned by tests: Subtitles.test.tsx:158 asserts the alert contains the raw `'asr down'`; :341-343 `'plain generate error'`; :349 `'edit error obj'`.
The repo already has the correct pattern elsewhere: app/renderer/src/features/export/ExportResult.tsx:80-93 renders a human heading ("Export failed"), the detail, and a "Try again" button.
- why: A non-technical user in the Edit phase sees engine/interpreter internals instead of an explanation — a Python class name, an ffmpeg exit code, a JSON-RPC method name, or their own absolute filesystem path — with no statement of what failed or what to do next. Both of the two most likely first-run Edit errors (no transcript yet; a convert/ffmpeg failure) land in this shape, so this is the modal error experience of the surface, not an edge case. The absolute-path echo also puts the user's directory structure on screen (and into any screenshot they share).
- fix: Introduce one renderer-side mapper (e.g. `lib/errorCopy.ts`) keyed by the sidecar `error.type` + method, returning `{title, body, action}`; have the panels render the ExportResult.tsx:80-93 shape (heading + human body + primary action) and demote the raw string to a collapsed "Technical details" disclosure. Independently, stop composing user-facing prose out of internals on the sidecar side: media_ops.py:47 should say "Transcribe this video first" (not "run transcribe.start"), and convert.py:257 should carry the basename, not the absolute path.
- ⚠ scope correction: Raw sidecar exception TEXT — including the user's absolute filesystem paths, ffmpeg exit codes, and internal JSON-RPC method names — is rendered verbatim to the user in 12 of the 13 Edit-phase Workspace panels (Workspace.tsx:53-67: Subtitles, Convert, Transcribe, Timeline, Tracks, Dub, Diarize, Refine, Recipes, NleExport, plus Search/SemanticSearch.tsx:216 and Assets/Assets.tsx:190+195 which the original finding omitted; only Short-maker was not verified). The exception's Python CLASS NAME is the one internal that does NOT reach the screen: jobs.py:810 emits it as `error.type` and useJob.ts:97-105 preserves it, but _api.ts:279 renders only `failure.message`, consulting `type` solely for the `JobCancelled` check at _api.ts:275. The 4-hop verbatim passthrough (jobs.py:810 / rpc.py:151 → sidecar.ts:506-511 → _api.ts:279 → panel catch → bare `<p role="alert">{error}</p>`) is confirmed, no sanitizer or error-copy layer exists anywhere in app/, and the two most likely first-run errors both land in this shape — media_ops.py:47 ("run transcribe.start first") on the default landing tab, reachable because Subtitles.tsx:234 gates Generate only on `anyBusy || !videoId` with no transcript guard, and convert.py:257 (absolute source path) on the Export destination panel.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM-LOW (copy/UX quality, not security or privacy): Edit-phase panels render the sidecar's error.message verbatim with no renderer-side error-copy layer — 48 instances of the setError(err.message) -> <p role="alert">{error}</p> pair across 16 files in app/renderer/src/features, and no errorCopy/friendlyError mapper exists anywhere under app/renderer/src. The concrete user-visible defect is ONE sidecar string: sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:47 instructs the user to "run transcribe.start first", an internal JSON-RPC method with no UI equivalent (the tab is "Transcribe" per Workspace.tsx:54; the button is "Generate subtitles" per Subtitles.tsx:235), reachable in one click from the default landing tab (Workspace.tsx:96 -> Subtitles.tsx:234) and therefore a plausible first-run dead-end. Secondarily, convert.py:257 echoes the absolute source path where a basename would read better — a polish item, NOT a disclosure, since the app already renders absolute paths by design on success (Convert.tsx:337-341, Subtitles.tsx:349-352) and this is a single-user local app with no adversary. Explicitly NOT claimed: the Python exception class name is never rendered (it dies at _api.ts:279, which takes only failure.message; useJob.ts:97-105 keeps `type` solely for the JobCancelled check), and _shared.py:73 "videoId (str) is required" is UI-unreachable (Subtitles.tsx:234 disables on !videoId; Workspace.tsx:271/279 always pass video.id). Fix worth doing: correct the media_ops.py:47 copy to "Transcribe this video first" and add a shared error-copy mapper rendering the ExportResult.tsx:78-95 heading+action shape — noting that exemplar also renders the raw detail, so the "Technical details" disclosure would be new work, not an existing pattern to copy.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding's headline is accurate and needs no rescoping, but two subsidiary details are overclaimed and should be corrected: (1) rpc.py:151 is NOT a hop on the chain of the three cited concrete strings -- media_ops.py:47 and _shared.py:73 raise RpcError, which is caught earlier at rpc.py:126-128 and serialized by make_error WITHOUT the "internal error in {method}" wrapper, while convert.py:257 travels the job path via jobs.py:810. rpc.py:151 is a genuine, live, INDEPENDENT leak path (any unexpected direct-return handler crash renders "internal error in <method>: <raw exc>" verbatim), so it belongs in the finding as a separate item rather than as a link in those three chains. (2) "a Python class name" in the WHY-IT-MATTERS list is not actually rendered: jobs.py:810 transmits exc.__class__.__name__ as error.type, but _api.ts:279 consumes only failure.message and the panels read `type` solely for the JobCancelled branch, so the class name never reaches the screen. The other three enumerated leaks -- ffmpeg exit code (convert.py:257), JSON-RPC method name (media_ops.py:47 "run transcribe.start first"; rpc.py:151), and the user's absolute filesystem path (convert.py:257 {in_path}) -- are all fully supported. The phrase "raw Python exception text" remains correct, since str(exc) is rendered verbatim.

## Per-card "Remove" is permanently visible at rest and silently deletes the video's transcript/project manifest
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:159-166 renders `<button className="library__remove-btn" aria-label={`Remove ${video.title}`}>Remove</button>` unconditionally on every card. The SAME stylesheet hover-gates the benign checkbox — app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:152-166 sets `.library__select { opacity: 0 }`, revealed only on `:hover`/`:focus-within`/`:checked`, with the stated rationale at :149-151 ("it's the batch scale affordance, not chrome on every card at all times"). Remove gets no such gate (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:386-392, :443-447). No confirmation on either removal path: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:368-384 (`handleRemove` → optimistic `rpc('library.remove')`) and :398-414 (`removeSelected` batch). Server side, sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:144-146 runs `self._project_path(video_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)` plus `(self.data_dir / "thumbnails" / f"{video_id}.jpg").unlink(...)`; that manifest carries the transcript + audio tracks (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:83-85 reads `data.get("transcript")` / `data.get("audioTracks")` from it). Measured resting DOM (throwaway probe rendering Library as App.tsx:518-524 mounts it, 3 videos): `PER_CARD_CONTROLS=5`, with `button[library__remove-btn] "Remove Talk"` present at rest on every card.
- why: One unconfirmed click on a control that is permanently visible in a 215px card grid (library-cards.css:11), directly below the card's own full-body open target, permanently destroys that video's transcript and audio tracks. Nothing in the UI discloses that "Remove" reaches past the list entry, and there is no undo — recovery means re-adding the file (which mints a new id) and re-running transcription. The component already articulated the correct disclosure principle for the checkbox and did not apply it to the destructive control.
- fix: Gate `Remove` exactly as the checkbox is gated (reveal on `:hover`/`:focus-within`), or move it into the existing "Source & storage" disclosure / an overflow menu. Add a confirm that names the collateral ("Also deletes the transcript and poster for this video"), or delete-with-undo-window before unlinking the manifest at library_ops.py:145.
- ⚠ scope correction: Wording tightening only (the finding is CONFIRMED, not refuted): "Per-card Remove is visible at rest — no hover/focus gate, unlike the sibling multi-select checkbox in the same stylesheet — and both removal paths fire with no confirmation, hard-unlinking the video's project manifest. That permanently destroys the transcript (the manifest at projects_dir/<id>.json is its ONLY persisted copy — media_ops.py:437-439; no content-hash cache; recovery = re-add, which mints a new uuid, then re-run transcription) and discards the audioTracks ENTRIES (label, language, and the a:<n> index mapping), orphaning the dub files on disk rather than deleting their bytes. Additionally — not in the original finding — library.remove calls managed_evict(force=True) (library.py:343-345), silently destroying the app-managed byte copy of the source video even when the original path is gone, which is exactly the case library.managedEvict refuses LOUD without an explicit force flag (library.py:476-477, library_ops.py:281-295)."
- ⚠ scope correction: Per-card and batch "Remove" invoke an irrecoverable destructive op with no confirmation and no undo, contradicting the codebase's own documented convention. SEVERITY: medium (not high). LENS: should be destructive-action-confirmation, not progressive-disclosure.

Confirmed substance: Library.tsx:368-384 (handleRemove) and :398-414 (removeSelected, via LibraryToolbar.tsx:65-70) both call rpc('library.remove') with zero confirmation. Server-side, library_ops.py:143-147 unlinks projects_dir/<id>.json, which holds the transcript as an INLINE structured value (not a path ref) plus the clips, caption tracks, and dub audioTracks indexes (library.py:499-500, :532-543). No content-addressed transcript cache exists, and re-adding mints a new uuid (library.py:56-58), so the transcript is unrecoverable without re-running ASR and any produced clips/dubs survive on disk only as orphans.

The defect is an internal inconsistency, not a visibility gap: Shorts.tsx:144-150 already confirms before deleting a single produced short — a REGENERABLE artifact — and names its collateral ("This removes the exported file"). Reframe therefore guards the cheap artifact and leaves the expensive, irrecoverable one unguarded.

Scope bounds that must be stated: library.remove NEVER deletes the user's source video file (library.py:333-334), so raw footage is safe and the loss is expensive derived work, not the primary asset. EXCEPTION worth its own fix: library.py:337-345 force-evicts an opt-in keep-a-copy byte-copy, its docstring conceding this destroys "even an irreplaceable copy (whose original is gone)" — that path can destroy the only remaining video bytes.

Correctly-scoped fix: add a confirm (or delete-with-undo-window) to BOTH removal paths, matching the existing Shorts.tsx:146-149 pattern and naming the collateral ("Also deletes the transcript and poster; produced shorts will be unlinked"), and require an explicit stronger confirm when a keep-a-copy managed copy would be force-evicted. Do NOT hover-gate Remove as the primary remedy — shell.css:383-392 already renders it as a quiet GHOST voice, so gating visibility addresses neither the misclick nor the absence of an undo.

## Produced-short delete has circular confirm ownership — three layers each delegate it and none implements it
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Three layers each assert a DIFFERENT layer owns the confirm: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27-28 "Delete a produced clip (the parent confirms + removes the file)"; app/renderer/src/features/libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44 "the Library confirms + updates its index from the resolved deletion"; app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:52-53 "Delete a produced clip file (the adapter owns any confirm)". Actual code: Library.tsx:437-454 `deleteShort` calls `await api.remove(path)` with no prompt; libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47 calls `client.shorts.delete(path)` with no prompt; app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx passes `onDelete` straight through (:40, :72, :230, :247, :286) and a grep for `confirm` in that file returns nothing. The sidecar contract is a real file delete: sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:20-22 — `shorts.delete {path}` "Delete the ``.mp4`` + its ``.thumb.jpg`` + ``.json``".
- why: A single click on a per-clip delete inside the gallery permanently removes a finished exported render plus its poster and sidecar metadata from disk, with no confirm and no undo; recovery requires a full re-export. The circular hand-off is the mechanism that let it ship: every layer's docstring asserts the guard lives elsewhere, so a reviewer reading any one file sees a guard that does not exist.
- fix: Implement the confirm in exactly ONE named place — `libraryShortsClient.remove` (libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47), since Library.tsx:52-53 already declares the adapter as the owner — and correct the two docstrings (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27-28, libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44) that point elsewhere. Prefer a typed confirm dialog naming the file, or delete + undo toast, over `window.confirm`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Produced-short delete from the Library gallery has NO confirm on a live-wired, irreversible file delete, because FOUR layers each delegate the guard and none implements it — ShortClipActions.tsx:7-8 ("the destructive confirm + reload live where the data does", button at :75-82 calls onDelete raw), ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27 ("the parent confirms"), Library.tsx:53 ("the adapter owns any confirm"), libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44 ("the Library confirms") — with Library.tsx:53 and libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44 forming a true 2-cycle (two named owners, not three distinct ones). The path is reachable: App.tsx:522 passes shorts={libraryShortsClient}, Library.tsx:437-454 calls api.remove(path) unguarded, libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47 and lib/rpc/client.ts:271 pass straight through, and sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:20-22 deletes the .mp4 + .thumb.jpg + .json. Proof the guard is missing rather than relocated: the SIBLING call site of the same ShortClipActions component does implement it at views/Shorts.tsx:144-150 ("UI confirms first — §2 shorts.delete"), and Library.test.tsx:1245-1251 exercises the delete with no window.confirm stub. Fix belongs in Library.tsx:437-454 deleteShort (mirroring Shorts.tsx:144-150), NOT in libraryShortsClient.remove, which libraryShortsClient.test.ts:74-77 pins as a pure RPC passthrough.
- ⚠ scope correction: Produced-short delete in the Library gallery has NO confirm, while the two sibling call sites of the same shorts.delete RPC both do — and FOUR layers each delegate the confirm to another layer.

Verified mechanism: the unguarded chain is Library.tsx:437-454 (deleteShort -> api.remove, no prompt) -> libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47 (-> client.shorts.delete, no prompt) -> sidecar shorts.py:450-455 (hard unlink of .mp4 + .thumb.jpg + .json, no OS trash). Live-wired at App.tsx:522. The delete button is rendered unconditionally at ShortClipActions.tsx:75-82, adjacent to Re-export and Open folder.

Four delegating docstrings, forming a cycle: ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27 (-> parent) -> Library.tsx:53 (-> adapter) -> libraryShortsClient.ts:44 (-> Library), plus ShortClipActions.tsx:8 (-> "both call sites"). Corrects the original "three layers" to four.

The strongest evidence, absent from the original finding: the confirm EXISTS and is tested on the sibling paths — views/Shorts.tsx:144-160 and features/useShortsGallery.ts:97-112 (used by ShortMaker.tsx:1000-1006), asserted by views/Shorts.test.tsx:255-281 and :283-285. The same <ProducedShorts> component thus gets a guarded handler from ShortMaker and an unguarded one from Library, so this is an inconsistency on the newest path against a convention the repo states outright (KeepCopyControl.tsx:21; ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:16).

Severity: medium-high, not high — the loss is a derived artifact (source video untouched; Library.tsx:405 library.remove is index-only), recoverable by re-export, though the .json that shorts.reexport reads to re-prime that export (shorts.py:458-477) is deleted too, so an identical reproduction is not guaranteed.

Dropped as UNVERIFIED: "the circular hand-off is the mechanism that let it ship" — no PR/commit history was examined; what is verified is only that the four docstrings mislead any reader of a single file.

Corrected fix owner: implement the confirm in Library.deleteShort (Library.tsx:437-454), NOT in libraryShortsClient.remove. Both working confirms in this repo live in the view/hook container, never in the data adapter; the original proposal contradicts that precedent. Then correct all four docstrings. Prefer the repo's own in-place two-step confirm pattern (KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-190, ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:183-213) over window.confirm, which the two older call sites use only as legacy.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim, so no down-scoping is needed; this is a precision-sharpened restatement (the original was understated on layer count and wrong on fix location).

"Produced-short delete is unguarded on the Library gallery path only, because a shared action component's 'each call site supplies the confirm' contract was widened to a third call site that never supplied it. FOUR layers each delegate the confirm and none of them implements it: ShortClipActions.tsx:8 ('both call sites supply the behavior, so the destructive confirm + reload live where the data does'), ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27 ('the parent confirms'), Library.tsx:53 ('the adapter owns any confirm'), and libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44 ('the Library confirms') — the last two forming a closed Library<->adapter cycle. One click on ShortClipActions.tsx:75-82 inside the gallery therefore runs Library.tsx:437-454 -> libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47 -> shorts.py:442-455, which hard-unlinks the .mp4, .thumb.jpg and .json with no trash and no undo. Scope is exactly one of three call sites: the standalone Shorts view (Shorts.tsx:144-160) and the ShortMaker gallery (useShortsGallery.ts:97-102) both DO confirm, which proves the guard is required rather than optional. The path is live in the shipped app (App.tsx:522 wires the port; LibraryCard.tsx:149-158 renders the entry button), and the unguarded behavior is currently asserted by a passing test at Library.test.tsx:1245-1250.

FIX: implement the confirm in Library.deleteShort (Library.tsx:437-454) — the container that owns the shorts index and its post-delete update, matching both existing implementations — NOT in libraryShortsClient.remove, which is a non-React RPC data port with no UI context. Then correct all four docstrings to name Library as the single owner, and update Library.test.tsx:1245-1256, which will otherwise fail. Prefer a typed in-app confirm dialog naming the file (or delete + undo toast) over window.confirm, and consider hoisting the shared guard so a future fourth call site cannot silently omit it."

## Job completion is never announced: every Edit-phase terminal status lands outside a live region, or the live region unmounts at the moment of completion
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Variant A — terminal status rendered in a plain <p> with no role/aria-live:
C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:348 `{status && !error && <p className="status">{status}</p>}` — the sole channel for 'Generated' (:98), 'Saved' (:122), 'Translated' (:175), 'Exported' (:198), 'Cancelled' (:217).
.../features/Tracks.tsx:283 — sole channel for 'Renamed'/'Relabelled'/'Added'/'Removed' (:96-112), 'Stripped → <path>' (:126), 'Burned → <path>' (:158), 'Cancelled' (:185).
.../features/NleExport.tsx:115 — sole channel for 'Exported N clips' (:50-54); this panel has NO live region at all.
.../features/Timeline.tsx:387 `{status && <p className="timeline__status">{status}</p>}` — sole channel for 'Saved' (:366).
Variant B — the live region unmounts exactly when the job finishes:
.../features/Dub.tsx:390 `{busy && (<div className="progress" aria-live="polite">…)}` while the success block .../Dub.tsx:404-417 (`<h3>Dub ready</h3>`) sits outside any live region.
.../features/Tracks.tsx:276, .../features/Recipes.tsx:227, .../features/Assets.tsx:181 — same `{busy && <div aria-live="polite">}` shape.
Counter-example proving it is an oversight, not a choice: .../features/Convert.tsx:325 and .../features/Transcribe.tsx:186 both gate on `(running || phase === 'done')` and set `message='Done'` (Convert.tsx:106/144, Transcribe.tsx:105), keeping the region mounted through completion.
Asymmetry: failure IS announced everywhere via `role="alert"` (Subtitles.tsx:355, Tracks.tsx:285, NleExport.tsx:122, Timeline.tsx:383, Dub.tsx:399) — only success is silent.
Blast radius: Subtitles is the DEFAULT Edit tab (.../views/Workspace.tsx:96 `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles'`), so this is the first panel a screen-reader user lands on.
Not caught by the existing gate: axe has no live-region/announcement rule, and .../app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:47-54 asserts only serious/critical axe violations.
- why: A blind user starts a subtitle generation, a track burn, a dub, or an NLE export and gets no audible confirmation it finished — only that it failed. There is no way to distinguish 'done' from 'still running' from 'hung', on the default landing tab of the Edit phase. WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA) requires programmatically-determinable status without receiving focus.
- fix: Two mechanical changes. (1) Put `role="status"` on the terminal-status paragraphs — Subtitles.tsx:348, Tracks.tsx:283, NleExport.tsx:115, Timeline.tsx:387 — so the string that already exists gets announced. (2) Keep the progress live region MOUNTED through completion instead of unmounting on the busy flag: change `{busy && …}` to `{(busy || done) && …}` in Dub.tsx:390, Tracks.tsx:276, Recipes.tsx:227, Assets.tsx:181, copying the `(running || phase === 'done')` idiom already proven in Convert.tsx:325 / Transcribe.tsx:186, and move Dub's `Dub ready` summary (Dub.tsx:404) inside it or give it `role="status"`.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding's BODY is correctly scoped and stands as written; only its one-line headline generalizes past the evidence. Headline "every Edit-phase terminal status lands outside a live region" is wider than measured — Convert (Workspace.tsx:60) and Transcribe (Workspace.tsx:54) are Edit-phase tabs that DO announce completion (Convert.tsx:325-329, Transcribe.tsx:186-190). Correctly scoped: "In 7 of the Edit phase's feature panels — Subtitles, Tracks, Dub, NLE export, Timeline, Recipes, Assets — job SUCCESS is never announced to a screen reader, while failure is announced everywhere via role=\"alert\". Two distinct causes: (A) the terminal status string renders in a plain <p> with no role/aria-live (Subtitles.tsx:348, Tracks.tsx:283, NleExport.tsx:115, Timeline.tsx:387); (B) the only aria-live region unmounts in the same React commit that produces the terminal string (Dub.tsx:390, Tracks.tsx:276, Recipes.tsx:227, Assets.tsx:181) — and in Recipes/Assets the batched setMessage('Done')+unmount means the string is never rendered at all, so it is invisible too. Diarize.tsx:158 shares shape (B) and belongs in the set. Convert.tsx:325 / Transcribe.tsx:186 prove the correct idiom already exists in-tree. No compensating global announcer exists: Workspace.tsx:352 is a plain role=\"tabpanel\", JobQueue.tsx:182 is role=\"complementary\" with no aria-live and closed by default, and although ToastHost.tsx:73 is a correctly-built permanent aria-live region, no feature panel pushes to it and useJob.ts:248 toasts only on error. Fix (1) role=\"status\" on the four paragraphs is mechanical; fix (2) additionally requires introducing a done/phase state in Dub, Recipes, and Assets, which currently have none."
- ⚠ scope correction: Job completion is not announced on 9 of the 13 Workspace (Edit-phase) tabs — two distinct mechanisms, while failure IS announced everywhere via role="alert".

Variant A — terminal status rendered in a plain <p> with no role/aria-live (4 panels): app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:348 (sole channel for 'Generated' :98, 'Saved' :122, 'Translated' :175, 'Exported' :198, 'Cancelled' :217); Tracks.tsx:283 ('Renamed' :96, 'Relabelled' :102, 'Added' :107, 'Removed' :112, 'Stripped → ' :126, 'Burned → ' :158, 'Cancelled' :185); NleExport.tsx:115 ('Exported N clip(s)' :50-54; this file has no aria-live at all); Timeline.tsx:387 ('Saved' :366). The text is visible and stays in the DOM, so a screen-reader user CAN re-navigate the panel and read it — but nothing is announced automatically, which is exactly the WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) failure.

Variant B — the only live region unmounts in the same commit as completion (5 panels): Dub.tsx:390 `{busy && …aria-live="polite"}` with the `<h3>Dub ready</h3>` summary outside it at :404-417; Assets.tsx:181 ('Done' :116 vs `setBusy(false)` :120, message rendered only at :185); Recipes.tsx:227 (gate is `runningId`, not `busy`; 'Done' :172 vs `setRunningId(null)` :176, message only at :231); Diarize.tsx:158 ('Done' :87 vs :91); Refine.tsx:261 ('Done' :133 vs :138). On the last four, `message` renders ONLY inside the unmounting region, so under React 18.3.1 auto-batching (app/package.json:31) the terminal 'Done' is never rendered at all — invisible as well as unannounced. UNVERIFIED by execution: the single-commit behaviour is inferred from React 18 automatic batching; a render test asserting 'Done' never appears in the DOM would settle it, and no current test covers it (Assets.test.tsx has no 'Done' assertion).

NOT universal: 4 of the 13 tabs already do this correctly and are the in-repo precedent for the fix — Convert.tsx:325 and Transcribe.tsx:186 keep the region mounted via `(running || phase === 'done')` with `message='Done'` (Convert.tsx:106/144, Transcribe.tsx:105); SemanticSearch.tsx:211 mounts `<div className="search-status" aria-live="polite">` unconditionally (the most robust idiom, since a freshly-inserted polite region is announced unreliably — see ToastHost.tsx:61-65); ShortMaker.tsx:979 announces terminal success via `<div className="sm-exported" role="status">`.

Blast radius: the Edit phase lands on the Task Hub (views/Edit.tsx:61, :145), not the Workspace. Subtitles is the first WORKSPACE panel — reached via the "Add subtitles" hub card, the Advanced/all-tools escape, or a remembered workspace choice (Edit.tsx:15, :87-90, :120-122, resolving to DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB='subtitles', Workspace.tsx:96) — i.e. one interaction deeper than "the first panel a user lands on".

Not caught by the existing gate: no ancestor live region exists (Workspace.tsx:352-357 is role="tabpanel"), the global polite region (ToastHost.tsx:73) only ever receives ERROR toasts (useJob.ts:248 is the sole job-outcome push; the success path :273-274 pushes nothing; zero `.success(`/`.info(` call sites renderer-wide) and none of these panels use useJob at all, and e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:47-54 asserts only serious/critical axe violations while axe-core has no WCAG 4.1.3 rule.

Fix, unchanged in substance but covering 9 panels: add role="status" to Subtitles.tsx:348, Tracks.tsx:283, NleExport.tsx:115, Timeline.tsx:387; and keep the progress region mounted through completion in Dub.tsx:390, Assets.tsx:181, Recipes.tsx:227, Diarize.tsx:158, Refine.tsx:261 — preferably by mounting it unconditionally as SemanticSearch.tsx:211 does, and give Dub's `Dub ready` summary (Dub.tsx:404) role="status".
- ⚠ scope correction: Terminal job status is not announced to screen readers in 9 of the 13 Workspace (Edit-phase) panels: Subtitles.tsx:348, Tracks.tsx:283, NleExport.tsx:115 and Timeline.tsx:387 render the terminal string in a plain <p> with no role/aria-live; and the polite progress region unmounts at the moment of completion in Dub.tsx:390, Tracks.tsx:276, Recipes.tsx:227, Assets.tsx:181, Diarize.tsx:158 and Refine.tsx:261 (the last two are additional to the original finding), with Dub's 'Dub ready' summary at Dub.tsx:404-417 sitting outside any live region. This is an inconsistency, not a design choice: Convert.tsx:325, Transcribe.tsx:186 (both gating (running || phase === 'done') with setMessage('Done') at Convert.tsx:106/:144) and SemanticSearch.tsx:211 (an unconditionally-mounted .search-status polite region) are Edit-phase tabs that DO announce, and the project's own docs/plans/repurpose/DESIGN.md:181 already cites Subtitles.tsx:342 / Dub.tsx:402 / Assets.tsx:194 as its established "SR-announced progress" idiom. Impact is real but bounded: it is a WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) failure on the default landing tab (Workspace.tsx:96) affecting multi-minute jobs, so a screen-reader user must POLL rather than receive a passive announcement — completion IS still programmatically determinable via the action button's disabled state (Subtitles.tsx:234), its label flip (Subtitles.tsx:235), the Cancel button unmounting (Subtitles.tsx:265, Dub.tsx:369) and Dub's <h3>Dub ready</h3> heading (Dub.tsx:406). Failures are already announced everywhere via role="alert" (Subtitles.tsx:355, Tracks.tsx:285, NleExport.tsx:122, Timeline.tsx:383, Dub.tsx:399), so only success is silent. Severity: MEDIUM, not high. Not caught by the existing gate (a11y.a11y.spec.ts:49-53 asserts only serious/critical, and axe has no dynamic-announcement rule).

## Produced-clip Delete in the Library shorts gallery skips the confirm the identical control has everywhere else — three layers each delegate it to another layer
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The Library path deletes with no confirm:
- `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:437-454` — `deleteShort` = `await api.remove(path)` then prune the index; no confirm anywhere in the function
- `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:606-614` — wired as `onDelete={(path) => void deleteShort(shorts, path)}`
- `app/renderer/src/features/libraryShortsClient.ts:45-47` — `remove: async (path) => { await client.shorts.delete(path); }`

Three comments each assert somebody else confirms, and none does:
- `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:52-54` — "Delete a produced clip file (**the adapter owns any confirm**)"
- `app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27` — "Delete a produced clip (**the parent confirms** + removes the file)"
- `app/renderer/src/features/libraryShortsClient.ts:43-44` — "**the Library confirms** + updates its index from the resolved deletion"
- `app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:8` states the design rule being violated: "It owns NO rpc and NO state — both call sites supply the behavior, so **the destructive confirm** + reload live where the data does"

The sibling call site does confirm, proving the intended contract:
- `app/renderer/src/features/useShortsGallery.ts:97-112` — `confirm('Delete this short?\n\n' + path + '\n\nThis removes the exported file.')`; `if (!ok ...) return;`
- `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:146-147` — "Confirm before any destructive call (UI confirms first — §2 shorts.delete)"

The delete is a hard unlink of three files: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:442-455` — unlinks the clip, `thumbnail_path(clip)` and `metadata_path(clip)`.

The button is a plain `Delete` (`app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:75-82`), and the no-confirm behaviour is pinned by `app/renderer/src/views/Library.test.tsx:1246-1250`.
- why: The same `<ProducedShorts>`/`ShortClipActions` UI, with the same `Delete` button and the same clip list, asks for confirmation when opened from Make Shorts/Shorts but deletes instantly when opened from a Library card's "N shorts" gallery. One misclick in a dense grid permanently deletes an exported render (plus its poster and metadata sidecar) with no dialog, no undo, and no way to recover it short of re-running the export. Because each layer's comment claims a different layer owns the confirm, a reader auditing any single file concludes it is handled.
- fix: Add the confirm in `Library.deleteShort` (`Library.tsx:437-454`) so it sits with the data, matching `useShortsGallery.ts:97-102` — ideally by extracting that confirm+delete into one shared helper both call sites use, so the two paths cannot drift again. Then correct the three now-false comments (`Library.tsx:54`, `ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:27`, `libraryShortsClient.ts:44`) to name the single owner, and extend `Library.test.tsx:1226-1257` with a cancel arm asserting `port.remove` is NOT called.

- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:47 `const [transcript, setTranscript] = useState<Transcript | null>(null);` — the ONLY writer is the in-session success path at :103. C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:298 `return <Transcribe videoId={video.id} />;` — the SINGLE mount site passes only videoId, and omits the panel's own `onTranscript` escape hatch (Transcribe.tsx:20). Cheapest: pass the already-fetched value down — `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} initialTranscript={project?.transcript ?? null} onTranscript={handleTranscribed} />` at Workspace.tsx:298, mirroring the Subtitles `initialTrack` pattern at Workspace.tsx:271, and seed `useState(initialTranscript)` at Transcribe.tsx:47 with a `phase` of 'done' when non-null. Consequence, correctly scoped: on revisiting the Transcribe tab of an already-transcribed video the panel renders no summary, no segment list and no detected language (and no progress element at all, since Transcribe.tsx:186 gates it on running/done), while libraryModel.ts:108,123 badge the same video "Transcript"/"transcript ready". The transcript CONTENT is NOT unreachable — `subtitles.generate` (media_ops.py:44-55) rebuilds a full cue track from the persisted transcript at zero GPU cost via a one-click Generate in Subtitles.tsx:89-94, on the DEFAULT landing tab (Workspace.tsx:96) — so the loss is the summary/segment-list/word-count view unique to Transcribe.tsx:200-218, not the data. The material risk is that the misleading empty panel invites re-clicking "Start transcription", and `transcribe.start` (media_ops.py:385-395) has no idempotence guard — unlike its own sibling shortmaker_ops.py:115, which explicitly avoids a "wasteful re-transcribe" — so the re-run burns a multi-minute GPU job and unconditionally overwrites the manifest transcript at media_ops.py:438, discarding diarization labels persisted through the same store (composition.py:484-492; that this sequence is user-reachable is UNVERIFIED — not traced end to end). Fix as proposed, plus an existing-transcript guard on `transcribe.start`.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM — "The Transcribe panel is the one transcript surface that never rehydrates: after a tab switch or relaunch it renders as if the video was never transcribed, contradicting the Library card's 'Transcript' badge and inviting a needless GPU re-run."

Confirmed mechanism (all verified at HEAD dcb59e4b, tree clean):
- app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:47 seeds `useState<Transcript|null>(null)`. The file has exactly two effects — :55 (progress relay, gated on `jobId`) and :147 (unmount teardown) — and no mount-time load. `setTranscript` has two call sites, :73 (reset-to-null when a run starts) and :103 (the in-session success path); neither can restore persisted state.

No renderer .tsx reads it.

(a) The idle panel does not display "0%" — app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:186 gates the entire progress block on `running || phase === 'done'`, so after a remount the panel renders no progress element, no summary, and no segment list at all: a bare "Start transcription" form indistinguishable from a never-transcribed video. (b) Replace "the transcript CONTENT (segments, timings, word count) becomes permanently unreachable in the UI" with: "the Transcribe panel's own transcript VIEW — detected language, duration, segment count, word count, and the full segment list (the sole renderer of `transcript.segments`, app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:208) — is unreachable without re-running transcription.
