Add, as strengthening detail: because Workspace.tsx:358-360 renders only the single active `renderPanel()` result, the panel is fully unmounted on every tab switch — and Workspace.tsx:96 sets DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles', so a user who transcribes and then navigates anywhere loses the view immediately, not just across a relaunch.

## Gallery loading skeleton keeps animating under prefers-reduced-motion: the global reset omits animation-iteration-count, so an `infinite` pulse degrades into frame-rate flicker instead of holding still
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `reduced-motion` · verifiers 3
- evidence: CONSUMER: `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:218-219` renders `<span className="skeleton shorts__skeleton-thumb" />` and `<span className="skeleton shorts__skeleton-line" />` inside the loading block (`app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:215-221`). `.skeleton` is the surface's ONLY animated element (verified: a repo-wide grep for `infinite` over `app/renderer/src` returns exactly 3 hits — `components/shell.css:581`, `components/jobqueue.css:49`, `components/SidecarBanner.css:47` — and only shell.css:581 is on this surface).

DEFINITION: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:581` → `animation: skeleton-pulse 1.5s var(--ease-in-out) infinite;` with `@keyframes skeleton-pulse` at `shell.css:584-592` (opacity 1 → 0.45 → 1).

THE INCOMPLETE RESET: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:54-61` is the app's only global reduced-motion block and sets ONLY:
```
  transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
```
It does NOT set `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`. `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css` has no reduced-motion block of its own, and the gallery is not inside `.director-view`, so shell.css:54-61 is the only rule that applies.

FALSE IN-CODE GUARANTEE: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:573-575` asserts "Reduced-motion is handled globally at the top of this sheet (animation-duration collapses to ~0), so the pulse simply holds still for motion-sensitive users." Measurement refutes this.

MEASURED (Chromium via Playwright, `emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'})`, page reproducing shell.css:54-61 and shell.css:576-592 verbatim):
  * `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` → true; `animationDuration` → `1e-05s`; `animationIterationCount` → **`infinite`** (NOT reset).
  * Web Animations API: `playState: "running"`, `currentIteration` advanced **107613 → 111073 in ~1.1 s** (≈63,000 iterations/sec). The animation is not stopped, just re-run absurdly fast.
  * RASTERIZER, with an internally-controlled both-states probe — two elements identical except that the control adds `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`, both screenshotted 14× via `page.screenshot({clip, animations:'allow'})`: broken = **6 distinct pixel signatures** (PNG byte lengths 546-609); control = **1 distinct signature** (609 bytes, all 14 identical). Because the ONLY differing declaration is the iteration count, the variation is caused by the infinite iteration, not encoder noise. A first, independent run using a file-backed page gave the same direction (5 distinct / 12).

IN-REPO PRECEDENT THAT THIS IS THE KNOWN FIX: `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` appears exactly once in the whole app — `app/renderer/src/views/director.css:112`, inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .director-view *, … }` (`director.css:107-115`). The Director view got the complete reset; the global block did not. `app/renderer/src/features/caption/captionStage.css:80-82` uses the other correct form, `animation: none`.

UNVERIFIED inline: I reproduced the exact cascade in a standalone Chromium page rather than driving the built Electron app's gallery loading state, so the in-app flicker amplitude is not directly measured. Settling experiment: launch the built app per `app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:79` (reducedMotion emulated), open Make Shorts → Produced shorts while `shorts.list` is in flight, and screenshot `.shorts__skeleton` 10× — byte-identical shots would refute this.
- why: A user who has set an OS-level reduced-motion preference gets, on this surface, output that is worse than no reduced-motion handling at all: the intended calm 1.5 s opacity pulse is replaced by opacity variation resampled every compositor frame. Rapid luminance change is precisely the provocative stimulus that vestibular- and photosensitivity-motivated reduced-motion requests exist to avoid, whereas a slow 1.5 s pulse is not. The gallery shows four of these ghost cards simultaneously (`Shorts.tsx:216` maps `[0,1,2,3]`), and the state persists for as long as `client.shorts.list()` (`Shorts.tsx:82`) takes — unbounded if the sidecar stalls, with no pause/stop affordance. Honest scope limit: I do NOT claim a WCAG 2.3.1 (Three Flashes, Level A) failure — the general flash threshold requires max relative luminance ≥ 0.8, and both `--surface-hover` and `--surface-bg` are dark-theme greys, so the absolute luminance delta is modest. This is real user harm and a broken documented promise, not a demonstrated legal violation.
- fix: Complete the global reset at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:54-61` so it matches the block the team already wrote at `views/director.css:110-114`:
```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;   /* ADD — the missing line */
    animation-delay: 0s !important;            /* ADD — see note */
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}
```
Belt-and-braces (preferred for this specific element, and the pattern already used at `features/caption/captionStage.css:82`): add next to the `.skeleton` rule
```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .skeleton { animation: none; }
}
```
`animation: none` is strictly more robust than duration+iteration clamping because it also discards the staggered `animation-delay: 0.15s / 0.3s / 0.45s` set at `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:108-118` (which the current global block does not reset, and which currently puts the four ghost cards out of phase with each other). Those delays are not an independent defect once the iteration count is fixed — both the 0% and 100% keyframes are `opacity: 1` — so they only need to be swept as part of this fix.
Also correct the now-false comment at `shell.css:573-575`, which currently states the pulse "holds still" under reduced motion.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): Under prefers-reduced-motion, the Make Shorts "Produced shorts" gallery skeleton (and the Library skeleton) keeps animating instead of holding still, because the app's only global reset at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:54-61 collapses animation-duration to 0.01ms but never resets animation-iteration-count, leaving the `infinite` pulse at shell.css:581 running. MEASURED in Chromium (reducedMotion:'reduce'): computed animation-iteration-count remains `infinite`, playState `running`, currentIteration raced to 96,658; the painted centre pixel took 5 distinct values spanning RGB(34,41,58)-(44,52,72) over 20 captures, while both an animation-iteration-count:1 control and a genuinely static element held at exactly one value (so the variation is caused solely by the iteration count, not capture noise), and a static opacity:0.45 reference matched the darkest sample, showing the swing reaches the full designed pulse depth resampled per frame rather than over 1.5s. Severity is MEDIUM, not high: the amplitude is a ~1.17:1 contrast step between near-black greys (max relative luminance ~0.035 vs the 0.8 general-flash threshold, so no WCAG 2.3.1 exposure), there is no functional impact, and the exposure window is bounded by a local client.shorts.list() call (Shorts.tsx:82) -- the "unbounded if the sidecar stalls" escalation is UNVERIFIED. It remains a genuine accessibility-comfort defect rather than noise because it is reproducibly user-visible, it harms precisely the users who set an explicit reduced-motion preference and cannot work around it, the in-code guarantee at shell.css:573-575 is false, and the existing guard test at app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:147-166 checks animationDuration on the non-animated `.toptab` and never checks iteration-count, so it passes in both broken and fixed states and cannot catch regressions. Fix as proposed (add `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` to shell.css:54-61, matching director.css:112, plus `.skeleton { animation: none; }` which also sweeps the shorts.css:108-118 stagger delays), correct the shell.css:573-575 comment, and extend the a11y spec to assert iteration-count on an actually-animated element such as `.skeleton`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Incomplete global reduced-motion reset leaves the `.skeleton` pulse RUNNING (not visibly flickering): `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:54-61` clamps `animation-duration` to 0.01ms but omits `animation-iteration-count`, so `.skeleton`'s `infinite` pulse (`shell.css:581`) keeps iterating at ~99,000 iterations/sec under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` instead of being stopped - measured `playState: running`, `currentIteration` 664,972 in ~6.7s. This ships in the built artifact (`animation-iteration-count` occurs 0 times in `app/out/renderer/assets/index-BVXAZeBx.css`).

Correctly scoped impact - LOW / cosmetic, NOT an accessibility harm: the resolved opacity is measurably STABLE, not flickering. Across 400 animation frames headed with real vsync jitter (frame gaps 0.5-64.2ms) the opacity takes at most 2 distinct values with a total span of 0.02285 (headless: span 0.00000); the reduced-motion-OFF control spans 0.55, a 24x larger amplitude. Composited with the real tokens (`--surface-hover: #2c3448` over `--surface-bg: #121620`, `styles/tokens.css:34`/`:31`), that 0.0228 swing is 0.59/0.69/0.91 per RGB channel - below 8-bit quantization, i.e. not perceptible. The in-code comment at `shell.css:573-575` ("the pulse simply holds still") is therefore substantively CORRECT about the user-visible outcome and only loose about the mechanism (the animation is sampled at a near-fixed phase, not stopped).

Also note: the four ghost cards are NOT out of phase under reduced motion - the `animation-delay: 0.15s / 0.3s / 0.45s` staggers at `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:108-118` are exact integer multiples of the clamped 1e-5s duration, so they contribute zero phase offset (all four cards measured 0.977155 at the same frame); they stagger only when reduced motion is OFF, which is the intended design per `shorts.css:107`.

Blast radius is WIDER than the Shorts gallery, since the defective rule is global: it affects every `.skeleton` consumer app-wide plus the other two `infinite` animations, `components/jobqueue.css:49` and `components/SidecarBanner.css:47`. Not covered by tests: the visual specs emulate reduced motion (`app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:79`) but screenshot with `animations: 'disabled'` (`_visualSetup.ts:107`), which neutralizes infinite animations at capture time.

Recommended fix (worth landing as hygiene, priority low): add `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` to `shell.css:54-61` so the global block matches the complete reset the team already wrote at `views/director.css:110-114` (the only in-repo occurrence, `director.css:112`), and reword the `shell.css:573-575` comment to say the pulse is clamped to a single ~0-duration iteration rather than implying the animation stops. Justification is spec-correctness, consistency with `director.css`, and eliminating a pointless ~99k-iterations/sec compositor animation - NOT a photosensitivity/vestibular risk, and explicitly not a WCAG 2.3.1 failure.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not a downgrade — a refinement, upward in scope and with one stat corrected: The global reduced-motion reset at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:54-61 omits `animation-iteration-count`, so all three `infinite` animations in the app keep running under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` at ~100,000 iterations/sec (not 63,000) and their composited opacity is resampled at arbitrary phase every frame, producing full-pulse-amplitude flicker (measured relative-luminance spread 10.79, identical to the intended 1.5 s swing) instead of holding still. Confirmed surfaces: the Make Shorts → "Produced shorts" loading skeleton (`shell.css:581` via `Shorts.tsx:218-219`), the active job dot (`components/jobqueue.css:49`), and the sidecar reconnecting lamp (`components/SidecarBanner.css:47`). Three in-code comments assert the opposite and are false (`shell.css:573-575`, `jobqueue.css:52`, `SidecarBanner.css:38`). Adding `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` to shell.css:54-61 — the form the team already ships at `views/director.css:112` — is verified safe for all three because each keyframe set's 0%/100% equals the base style.

## Workspace tab strip overflows 571px at the app's default window — the persistent "Export" action and the "Advanced" disclosure render entirely off-screen
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Measured in headless Chromium against the REAL stylesheets (tokens.css + shell.css + workspace.css + topTabBar.css) at the app's own default viewport (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039 `width: 1280, height: 820`) with the 200px left rail (app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:16 `width: 200px`):

  viewport 1280x820 → .tabbar clientWidth=1080, scrollWidth=1651, overflow=571px
    .tabbar__advanced-toggle rect left=1668  (388px PAST the window right edge)
    .tabbar__export          rect left=1761 right=1835 (481-555px PAST the edge), exportVisible=false
  viewport 940x600 (the enforced minimum, app/main/main.ts:1040-1041) → overflow=911px, export 821px off-screen
  viewport 1440 → overflow 411px, export off-screen
  viewport 1600 → overflow 251px, export off-screen
  viewport 1920 → overflow 0, export finally visible (right=1904)

Source anchors:
  app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39 — `.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto; flex: none; }` puts the WHOLE strip (tabs + Advanced toggle + Export) into one horizontal scroller.
  app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:158-160 — `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__export { appearance: none; margin-left: auto; ... }`; with negative free space the auto margin resolves to 0, so Export lands at the far end of the SCROLL CONTENT, not the far end of the visible strip.
  app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:254-258 — Export is a sibling of the tablist inside the same scrolling `.tabbar`.

Corroboration (weaker, note the caveat): the committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png shows the strip clipped mid-word at "ASSE…" with a horizontal scrollbar under it and no Export/Advanced visible — UNVERIFIED as current geometry, that PNG predates the v1.5 left rail (it renders the top tabs as a horizontal strip), so it corroborates the defect class, not the exact 200px-rail numbers.
- why: Export is explicitly designed as the standing, always-reachable primary action: app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:48-56 ("EXPORT is the user's terminal goal, so it gets a standing affordance even though the full Deliver cluster stays collapsed") and app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:99-105 ("the primary Export/Deliver destination"). At every supported window width below 1920px it is invisible. Five of the thirteen panels (Convert, Timeline export, Recipes, Assets, Tracks) plus the Advanced disclosure are also off-screen, reachable only by horizontally scrolling a strip whose only affordance is a 10px scrollbar (`::-webkit-scrollbar` height, app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:32-42) drawn in --surface-active on --surface-raised. A user at the shipped default window cannot see the button that finishes their job.
- fix: Take the non-tab controls out of the scroll region: keep `overflow-x: auto` on the INNER `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__tablist` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:78-81) and revert `.workspace .tabbar` (workspace.css:36-39) to a non-scrolling flex row, then give `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` and `.tabbar__export` `flex: none` so they stay pinned to the visible right edge while only the clusters scroll. Add a scroll-edge fade/shadow on the tablist so the overflow is discoverable. Add an e2e assertion that `.tabbar__export` bounding right <= viewport width at 1280x820 and at the 940x600 minimum.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding's OBSERVABLE claim is fully confirmed and needs no rescoping: at the shipped default window (1280x820, main.ts:1038-1039) and at every width below ~1920px, the persistent Export action and the Advanced disclosure render entirely outside the visible tab strip, reachable only by horizontally scrolling a region whose sole affordance is a 10px scrollbar. Only the CAUSAL attribution needs correcting: 493px of the measured 571px overflow comes from a SECOND, unnamed defect the report does not identify — workspace.css:148-152 `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; }` is an author-origin declaration, and author-origin normal declarations beat the UA `[hidden]` rule regardless of specificity (there is no `[hidden]` reset anywhere in app/renderer, verified by grep). So the "Deliver" cluster collapsed by `advancedOpen=false` (Workspace.tsx:131) is ALWAYS laid out and painted — confirmed in the committed real-app baseline, which shows `DELIVER CONV...` with the disclosure closed. Consequently the report's proposed fix is necessary but NOT sufficient: adding `flex: none` to `.tabbar__advanced-toggle`/`.tabbar__export` and moving `overflow-x: auto` to the inner `.tabbar__tablist` would pin Export to the visible right edge, but would leave the Deliver cluster wrongly visible and leave 5 tabs padding a scroller that should be empty. The complete fix is BOTH: (1) make `hidden` effective on `.tabbar__advanced-panel` (scope the `display: flex` to `:not([hidden])`, or add `[hidden]{display:none}`), which alone drops overflow from 571px to 78px; AND (2) take the non-tab controls out of the scroll region as proposed, which is still required because 78px of overflow remains at 1280x820 (Export at left=1268/right=1342 vs a 1280px viewport) and 418px remains at the 940x600 enforced minimum. The proposed e2e assertion (`.tabbar__export` bounding right <= viewport width at 1280x820 and 940x600) should be added for both states — collapsed AND expanded — since no test in app/e2e currently touches it.
- ⚠ scope correction: Workspace tab strip overflows its container by 571px at the app's default 1280x820 window (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039), pushing the persistent "Export" shortcut and the "Advanced" disclosure entirely outside the visible strip; they only become fully visible at a viewport width of 1836px or more. SEVERITY: medium (not high).

MEASURED (headless Chromium against the real stylesheets, corroborated by the committed real-Electron 1280x820 baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png, regenerated in 27e7189b):
  1280x820 -> .tabbar clientWidth=1080, scrollWidth=1651, overflow=571; .tabbar__advanced-toggle left=1668; .tabbar__export left=1761 right=1835 (fully off-screen)
  940x600 (the enforced minimum, main.ts:1040-1041) -> overflow=911
  1440 -> 411 | 1600 -> 251 | 1835 -> Export still clipped | 1836 -> Export first fully visible | 1920 -> overflow 0, Export right-aligned at 1904
  At 1280, 4 tabs are fully off-screen (Timeline export, Recipes, Assets, Tracks) and Convert is CLIPPED (1231->1319), matching the "CONV" in the baseline PNG.

TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES — the fix needs both:

CAUSE 1 (dominant, 493 of the 571px = 86%): the "Deliver" cluster renders VISIBLE even though it is collapsed. TabBar.tsx:239 sets `hidden={!advancedOpen}` and Workspace.tsx:131 defaults advancedOpen=false, but workspace.css:148-152 `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex }` is an AUTHOR declaration, which beats the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` regardless of specificity. Measured: hidden attribute present, computed display=flex, width=493px. So the "Advanced" progressive disclosure is entirely inert — its 5 tabs are always laid out, and clicking the toggle changes nothing visible. Counterfactual with `hidden` honoured: overflow drops 571 -> 78px. Fix: add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none }` (or drop the unconditional display:flex). TEST GAP: TabBar.test.tsx:92-97 only regex-matches the `hidden` attribute in the rendered HTML string and never asserts computed style, so it passes while the CSS defeats it — assert computed visibility, not markup.

CAUSE 2 (residual 78px): the non-tab controls sit inside the scroller. workspace.css:36-39 puts `overflow-x: auto` on the WHOLE `.tabbar`, and TabBar.tsx:254-258 renders Export as a sibling of the tablist inside it, so with negative free space the `margin-left: auto` at workspace.css:160 resolves to 0px (measured) and Export lands at the far end of the SCROLL CONTENT rather than the visible right edge. Fix: move `overflow-x: auto` onto the inner `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__tablist` — note this declaration does NOT currently exist at workspace.css:78-81, it must be ADDED along with `min-width: 0` so the flex item can shrink below its content size — revert `.workspace .tabbar` to a non-scrolling flex row, and give `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` / `.tabbar__export` `flex: none` so they stay pinned to the visible right edge while only the clusters scroll. Add a scroll-edge fade so the overflow is discoverable (the only current affordance is the 10px `::-webkit-scrollbar`, shell.css:32-42).

REGRESSION GUARD: assert `.tabbar__export` bounding right <= viewport width at 1280x820 AND at the 940x600 minimum, and assert the Deliver cluster is not visible while advancedOpen is false.

NOT CLAIMED (scoped away from the original): the user is NOT stranded. App.tsx:458 registers an always-visible top-level "Export" item in the 200px left rail, and App.tsx:488-491 makes that the guarded-commit render/finish surface for the open video; the off-screen `.tabbar__export` is only a shortcut to the in-workspace Convert panel (Workspace.tsx:105, :137-140). What is lost is a deliberately-designed standing affordance (TabBar.tsx:48-56, Workspace.tsx:99-105) plus discoverability of 5 Deliver tools — a real regression, but not a dead-end for finishing a job.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): At the app's default 1280x820 window (main/main.ts:1038-1039) the grouped Workspace tab strip overflows its 1080px stage by 571px, so the Advanced disclosure toggle (rect left=1668) and the persistent Export shortcut (left=1761, right=1835) render entirely off-screen, along with the five Deliver-cluster tabs — reachable only by horizontally scrolling a strip whose sole affordance is a 10px scrollbar (shell.css:32-42). Confirmed at every supported width below 1920 (940 -> 911px overflow; 1440 -> 411; 1600 -> 251), and corroborated by the committed real-app baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png (1280x820), which shows the strip clipped mid-word at "CONV" with a scrollbar and no Advanced/Export.

Two scope corrections to the original finding:

(1) Users are NOT blocked from exporting. The always-visible 200px left rail carries persistent top-level "Export" and "Deliver" surfaces (App.tsx:458-459) and can never overflow because its labels truncate (topTabBar.css:80-86). The off-screen `.tabbar__export` is a redundant convenience shortcut that only jumps to the Convert panel and expands the Deliver cluster (Workspace.tsx:137-140). The defect is discoverability/polish on the primary editing surface, not an unreachable terminal goal — hence MEDIUM, not HIGH.

(2) The dominant root cause is NOT the scroll container. Measured decomposition at 1280: 493px of the 571px overflow comes from `.tabbar__advanced-panel` rendering at computed `display: flex` DESPITE carrying its `hidden` attribute, because workspace.css:148-152 sets an author `display: flex` that overrides the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` and no `[hidden]` rule exists anywhere in app/**. Forcing the panel to genuinely `display: none` reduces overflow at 1280 from 571px to 78px. This means WU-3a2's "Deliver collapses behind Advanced" progressive disclosure is INERT in the shipped app (the collapsed cluster is always laid out and visible, and the toggle's aria-expanded=false misreports state) — a distinct defect the original finding did not identify. It is invisible to the unit tests because TabBar.test.tsx:97 and Workspace.test.tsx:687 assert only the `hidden` attribute, never computed visibility.

Corrected fix order: FIRST add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none }` (restores the intended disclosure and removes 86% of the overflow), THEN pin the non-tab controls out of the scroll region (`flex: none` on `.tabbar__advanced-toggle`/`.tabbar__export`, keep `overflow-x: auto` on the inner `.tabbar__tablist` at workspace.css:78-81) so Export stays visible at 1280 and at the 940 minimum, where it is still 62px and 402px off-screen respectively even after fix 1. Add both a computed-visibility assertion on the collapsed panel and an e2e assertion that `.tabbar__export` bounding right <= viewport width at 1280x820 and 940x600.

## `hidden` on the collapsed Deliver cluster is defeated by an author `display: flex`, so the Advanced disclosure never collapses and adds 493px to the tab strip
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239 renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`, but app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152 sets `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }` — an author-origin rule that outranks the UA `[hidden] { display: none }`.

Both-states probe (a plain `<div hidden>` control in the same document proves the detector fires):
  { panelHiddenAttr: true, panelComputedDisplay: "flex", controlPlainHiddenDisplay: "none", convertRect: { w: 62.7, h: 21 }, convertTabIndex: -1 }

Layout cost, measured at the real viewports with the real stylesheets:
  asShipped (hidden attr present)  → .tabbar scrollWidth 1651 at EVERY width; overflow 911 @940, 571 @1280, 411 @1440, 251 @1600, 0 @1920
  trulyCollapsed (display:none)    → .tabbar scrollWidth 1158;              overflow 418 @940,  78 @1280,   0 @1440
  ⇒ the defeated `hidden` costs 493px of strip width and moves the width at which Export becomes visible from 1440 to 1920.
  scrollWidth is byte-identical (1651) whether the `hidden` attribute is present or removed — the attribute changes nothing.

Test gap: app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.test.tsx:97 asserts only the attribute STRING (`expect(html).toMatch(/class="tabbar__advanced-panel"[^>]*hidden/)`) — it never checks computed display, so the suite is green while the panel renders.
- why: Two compounding harms. (1) Layout: the collapsed-by-default cluster (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:131 `useState(false)`) is the dominant cause of the strip overflow above — the whole progressive-disclosure design (Workspace.tsx:69-90) is inert. (2) Reachability: those five tabs render visible but are `tabIndex={-1}` (TabBar.tsx:97) AND excluded from the arrow-key `orderedIds` while `advancedOpen` is false (TabBar.tsx:159-166), so they are visible, mouse-clickable, and completely unreachable by keyboard. The "Advanced" toggle also appears to do nothing visually, since the panel it controls was never hidden.
- fix: Scope the display rule so it cannot fight the attribute: `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]) { display: flex; … }` (or add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none; }`) in app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148. Strengthen app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.test.tsx:97 from a markup regex to a computed-style/visibility assertion (e.g. `expect(panel).not.toBeVisible()`), which is the only form that would have caught this.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED with two scoping corrections.

Correctly-scoped claim: "An author-origin `display: flex` at app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152 outranks the UA `[hidden] { display: none }`, so the collapsed Deliver cluster at app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239 renders visible despite `hidden={!advancedOpen}` and Workspace.tsx:131 defaulting to collapsed. No global `[hidden]` guard exists anywhere in app CSS to restore it (verified repo-wide). Consequences, confirmed in the app's own 1280px baseline at app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png: (a) progressive disclosure is wholly inert — 13 tabs render where 8 were designed; (b) the 'Advanced' toggle reveals nothing when clicked, only rotating its caret (workspace.css:144-146); (c) the strip overflows so far that BOTH the 'Advanced' toggle and the design-review-P1 'Export' standing affordance (workspace.css:158-160) are entirely off-screen, forcing a horizontal scroll to reach the app's primary export action."

CORRECTION 1 — the reachability claim is an OVERCLAIM. The finding says the five Deliver tabs are "completely unreachable by keyboard." They are not. The "Advanced" toggle at TabBar.tsx:245-252 is a plain `<button>` with no tabIndex override (default 0), so it is Tab-reachable; activating it adds the Deliver tabIds to `orderedIds` (TabBar.tsx:162-164), after which arrow keys reach them normally. The accurate defect is narrower but still real: the five tabs are VISIBLE yet excluded from arrow-key navigation and carry tabIndex={-1} (TabBar.tsx:97, 159-166) until the toggle is activated — a visible/keyboard-model desync where a keyboard user sees 13 tabs but can only arrow through 8, and where activating the toggle produces no visible confirmation. Not total keyboard inaccessibility.

CORRECTION 2 — the overflow framing omits a material mitigation. `.workspace .tabbar` sets `overflow-x: auto` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39, comment: "8 tabs must survive narrow windows without wrapping the chrome"), and the horizontal scrollbar is visible in the baseline PNG. The strip SCROLLS; it does not clip. So no tab is ever permanently lost or unreachable by mouse. The real cost is scroll friction plus the off-screen Export/Advanced controls — not inaccessible content, which the finding's bare "overflow 911 @940" figures imply.

SEVERITY — medium-high, not high. No data loss, no crash, no security exposure, and every tab stays mouse-reachable by scrolling. But a wholly inert disclosure feature plus the primary Export affordance off-screen at the project's own baseline viewport is genuine user-facing breakage on a core surface, and the proposed fix is a correct one-liner. The proposed fix is sound: add `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none; }` (or scope the rule with `:not([hidden])`) at workspace.css:148, and replace the markup regex at TabBar.test.tsx:97 with a computed-style/visibility assertion — noting that such an assertion requires a real layout engine, so it belongs in the Playwright e2e layer rather than the jsdom unit suite, which cannot evaluate CSS at all.
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect itself needs no rescoping. The single overclaim is the final sentence of PROPOSED FIX — "`expect(panel).not.toBeVisible()`, which is the only form that would have caught this." That is false, and adopting it would install a both-states-silent detector:

(a) app/vitest.config.ts:27-75 declares no `css` option and no `setupFiles`, so Vitest's default `css: false` applies — workspace.css is replaced with an empty module and never injected into jsdom. `getComputedStyle(panel).display` under jsdom therefore reports `none` from jsdom's own UA stylesheet in BOTH the broken and the fixed state, so `not.toBeVisible()` would pass either way and prove nothing.

(b) TabBar.test.tsx:93/101 use `renderToStaticMarkup`, which returns a STRING, not a DOM node — `toBeVisible()` is not even applicable there without first rewriting the test to mount into a DOM.

Correctly scoped version: keep the CSS fix as proposed (scope the rule with `:not([hidden])`, or add an explicit `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel[hidden] { display: none; }` at workspace.css:148). For the regression guard, either (i) assert against the CSS SOURCE — the same pattern the repo already uses in app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts, which reads stylesheet text off disk and asserts on it — or (ii) put the assertion in the real-browser layer (app/e2e/visual/*, where the reporter's own probe ran and where computed style reflects the loaded stylesheet). A unit-level computed-style assertion is the one form that would NOT have caught this.
- ⚠ scope correction: The headline stands as written and needs no narrowing: `hidden` on the collapsed Deliver cluster IS defeated by the author-origin `display: flex` at app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152, the Advanced disclosure never visually collapses, and it adds ~493px to the tab strip (fixture-measured; direction and existence independently confirmed by the shipped app's own baseline, px precision UNVERIFIED by me). Three supporting sentences need re-scoping. (1) Replace "the whole progressive-disclosure design (Workspace.tsx:69-90) is inert" with: "the VISUAL collapse is inert — the four-cluster grouping (Workspace.tsx:76-90) renders correctly, and `advancedOpen` still governs arrow-key reachability (TabBar.tsx:159-166) and the toggle's aria-expanded (TabBar.tsx:248); what is defeated is only the `advanced: true` collapse." (2) Replace "completely unreachable by keyboard" with: "not keyboard-operable in the default state — the five Deliver tabs are visible and mouse-clickable but carry tabIndex -1 (TabBar.tsx:97) and are excluded from orderedIds while advancedOpen is false (TabBar.tsx:159-166). Functionality is not locked away: the Advanced toggle (TabBar.tsx:245-252) and Export (TabBar.tsx:254-258 -> Workspace.tsx:137-140) are both keyboard-operable and admit the tabs to the arrow order, so this is a visible-but-inoperable/dead-toggle defect rather than a WCAG 2.1.1 failure; and because .workspace .tabbar is overflow-x: auto (workspace.css:36-39), the off-screen Export is scroll- and Tab-reachable, not lost." (3) REPLACE the test half of the PROPOSED FIX entirely. Drop "which is the only form that would have caught this" — it is false. `expect(panel).not.toBeVisible()` cannot run at TabBar.test.tsx:97 (no @testing-library/jest-dom in app/package.json, no setupFiles in app/vitest.config.ts), and ANY computed-style assertion there is a both-states-silent probe because app/vitest.config.ts leaves `test.css` at its default false and TabBar.tsx imports no CSS, so workspace.css never reaches jsdom and the assertion would pass in the broken state. The catching form is a REAL-BROWSER check: a Playwright assertion that .tabbar__advanced-panel is hidden (or that .workspace .tabbar scrollWidth <= clientWidth at the shipped 1280 default and the 940 minWidth from app/main/main.ts:1038-1040) in app/e2e/visual/, plus re-blessing workspace-preview-win32.png — which currently encodes the defect as the expected appearance. The CSS fix itself (scoping the display rule with :not([hidden]) or adding an explicit [hidden] { display: none } at workspace.css:148) is correct as proposed.

## Subtitles cue editor: tabbing from one cue to the next always dumps focus on <body> (blur-save disables the whole list)
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:332 `onBlur={() => track && saveEdits(track.cues)}` on every cue input; saveEdits sets `setBusy('saving')` at Subtitles.tsx:113 → `anyBusy` (Subtitles.tsx:222) → every cue input carries `disabled={anyBusy}` at Subtitles.tsx:329. Chromium probe (playwright-core, repo's own install), input#c1 blur disables c1+c2, then a real `Tab` keypress: {"afterCueTab": "BODY#"}. Detector control in the same run — an identical pair with no blur handler: {"control": "INPUT#k2"}. Second probe proving the result is independent of React's flush timing: {"microtask": "BODY#", "macrotask": "BODY#"}. `busy` returns to 'none' only after the RPC resolves (Subtitles.tsx:126) and nothing restores focus.
- why: Editing cues sequentially is the panel's core job and the Workspace's default landing tab (DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles', Workspace.tsx:96). A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot move from cue N to cue N+1 at all: every Tab lands on document.body, so they must re-Tab through the entire app shell (header toggles, jobs pill, 8 nav-rail tabs, back button, player, tab strip) for each cue. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order failure on the primary editing loop.
- fix: Do not gate the cue inputs on the global `anyBusy`. Either scope the disable to the destructive phases only (`disabled={busy === 'generating' || busy === 'translating'}`) or drop the disable entirely for 'saving' and reject concurrent saves in `saveEdits`. If a control genuinely must go inert while a request is in flight, use `aria-disabled="true"` + an early-return guard instead of the `disabled` attribute, which is what strips focus.
- ⚠ scope correction: Subtitles cue editor: every cue blur fires an unconditional save that disables the whole cue list, transiently dumping focus to <body> — costing one extra Tab per cue and an unannounced loss of the focus ring (MEDIUM, focus-management).

Confirmed mechanism: Subtitles.tsx:332 `onBlur={() => track && saveEdits(track.cues)}` fires on ANY blur (even with no edit) → :113 `setBusy('saving')` → :222 `anyBusy` → :329 `disabled={anyBusy}` on every cue input, so the Tab target is disabled during focus fixup and Chromium drops focus to document.body; nothing restores it (no focus/useRef/autoFocus in the file), and `busy` clears only when the RPC resolves (:126).

Correctly-scoped impact: Chromium preserves the sequential focus navigation starting point at the disabled cue's position, so the NEXT Tab lands on cue N+1 — the intended target (measured: probe2 trials A/B `nextTab: "INPUT[Cue 2 text]"`; Shift+Tab → the Export button, vs a virgin-body control that wrapped to cue 3). The user is therefore not blocked and does not re-traverse the app shell; they pay one extra Tab press per cue plus a visible focus ring that vanishes mid-edit.

Degraded worst case (conditional, not universal): if the next Tab arrives while the save is still in flight, the forward scan finds nothing focusable after the panel (the panel is the last element, Workspace.tsx:352-361) and wraps to the top of the shell. Measured at a 150 ms keypress gap with rpc ≥200 ms → `BUTTON#shell-theme`. `subtitles.edit` is a direct-return handler (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:69: in-memory edit + `project.save()`), so this window is normally short but is disk/latency dependent.

Out of scope: Tab from the LAST cue is unaffected (successor lies outside the disabled set). Reachability confirmed — `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles'` (Workspace.tsx:96), in the 'speech' / "Speech & Text" cluster (Workspace.tsx:76-81), not an "Edit phase" group.

UNVERIFIED inline: whether this is a formal WCAG 2.4.3 failure (order and operability are preserved) and what a real screen reader announces on the body landing — settle by running NVDA/JAWS against the panel and logging the announcement on cue blur.

Fix as originally proposed (do not gate cue inputs on the global `anyBusy`; prefer `aria-disabled` + an early-return guard, and/or skip the save when the value is unchanged).
- ⚠ scope correction: Subtitles cue editor: blur-save disables the whole cue list, so every cue-to-cue transition drops focus to <body> and costs a second input action (severity MEDIUM, not high).

app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:332 saves on blur; saveEdits sets `setBusy('saving')` (:113) -> `anyBusy` (:222) -> `disabled={anyBusy}` on every cue input (:329), and `busy` returns to 'none' only after the RPC resolves (:126) with nothing restoring focus. Confirmed on the real component in real Chromium: Tab (or a click) off cue N lands on <body> and all cue inputs go inert together; this fires even with NO text edit. Both interaction modes are affected — the first mouse click on cue N+1 is swallowed and must be repeated. Recovery is ONE extra Tab/click, not a re-traversal of the app shell: Chromium preserves the sequential-focus-navigation starting point (measured: second Tab lands on cue N+1) because the `key={cue.index}` list reconciles rather than remounts, and the inert window is ~18 ms with a fast local sidecar. If the save is still in flight when the user Tabs again, the second Tab overshoots the entire disabled list. No specific WCAG success criterion is failed (focus ORDER is preserved); this is an operability/focus-loss defect on the default landing tab's primary loop (Workspace.tsx:96, :271). Fix as proposed: stop gating the cue inputs on the global `anyBusy` — scope the disable to the destructive phases, or use `aria-disabled` plus an early-return guard instead of the `disabled` attribute, which is what strips focus.
- ⚠ scope correction: Subtitles cue editor: tabbing off any cue input parks focus on <body> instead of the next cue, because the unconditional blur-save (Subtitles.tsx:332) sets busy='saving' (Subtitles.tsx:113) which disables every cue input via anyBusy (Subtitles.tsx:222,329) before Chromium applies the pending focus. Measured 24/24 with the real component at 5-200ms RPC latency; invisible at 0ms, which is why the instant-mock unit tests stay green. COST (measured, not asserted): the keyboard user needs TWO Tab presses per cue instead of one — the recovery Tab does reach cue N+1 (12/12), it does NOT restart at the top of the document (0/24) — and in the gap nothing is focused, so there is no focus ring and a screen reader announces nothing. Pressing Tab again inside the save window skips the remaining still-disabled cues and overshoots to the first control after the panel (12/12). Real WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order failure on the default landing tab (Workspace.tsx:96,271); severity MEDIUM, not high. Fix as proposed (scope the disable off 'saving', or aria-disabled + an early-return guard); additionally add the dirty check the sibling Tracks.tsx:211-214 already has so a no-op Tab-through does not trigger a save at all. No existing test asserts the cue inputs are disabled while saving (Subtitles.test.tsx:123,147 both target the Generate button), so the fix breaks nothing.

## Timeline panel: cue rects and drag handles have no focusable representation, so cue selection — and every editing action gated on it — is mouse-only
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:409-421 — the cue rect is a bare `<div data-cue={pos} ...>` with no `tabIndex`, no `role`, no `onKeyDown`. Timeline.tsx:425-434 — the retime edge handles are `<span data-edge onMouseDown>` only. `selected` is set exclusively inside the mouse handler `handleLaneClick` (Timeline.tsx:246-256) hanging off the lane `<div onClick>` (Timeline.tsx:389-397), which is itself not focusable. - fix: Give the cue rects a real focus representation: `role="option"` inside a `role="listbox"` lane (or `<button>`), roving `tabIndex`, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to move the selection and Home/End to jump, and keyboard retime (e.g. Shift+Arrow nudges the selected edge) so `dragEdge` is reachable without `mousedown`. Measured consequence for a keyboard-only user: cue selection is unreachable, so Split (:458), Merge (:466) and the entire cue-text/retime editor block (:499-537) can never be enabled, and edge-drag retime (:425-434, mousedown-only) is unreachable. Two of the five toolbar buttons are permanently keyboard-disabled — NOT five: Save (:490, `disabled={!track || !history}`) is enabled as soon as a track loads, and keyboard-activating it pushes history (:364 → timelineOps.ts:190-195), which enables Undo (:474) and then Redo (:482). timeline.css has no `:focus`/`:focus-visible` rule, so even a retrofitted focus target would be invisible. Scope note: cue Split/Merge exist nowhere else in the app (`splitAt`/`mergeAt` are called only at Timeline.tsx:299,307), so those two functions are keyboard-unreachable app-wide; cue-text editing does have a keyboard path in the Subtitles tab (Subtitles.tsx:317-337) and keyboard retime exists in the separate Caption phase (CaptionClipLane.tsx:43-62), so the loss is per-view rather than a total loss of those two capabilities. This remains a WCAG 2.1.1 (Level A) failure for the Timeline panel view — a barrier the repo itself documents at CaptionClipLane.tsx:3-5 — and severity high stands.
- ⚠ scope correction: Timeline panel (Edit phase → Workspace → 'timeline' tab): cue rects (app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:409-421) and retime edge handles (:425-434) have no focusable representation — no tabIndex, role, or onKeyDown — and non-null selection is set only from the lane's mouse handler (:254 via :393, on a non-focusable div), with no :focus/:focus-visible rule in app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css (0 "focus" matches). Consequently, for a keyboard-only user: Split (:458) and Merge (:466) are permanently disabled and have NO keyboard path anywhere in the app (splitAt/mergeAt are consumed only at Timeline.tsx:299,307), and this panel's cue editor (:499) never renders. Scope corrections: Save (:487-496) IS enabled and functional from the keyboard, so only two toolbar buttons are directly selection-gated (Undo/Redo at :474/:482 are gated on canUndo/canRedo and are merely transitively unreachable); cue-TEXT editing is fully keyboard-operable on the default Subtitles tab (Subtitles.tsx:325-332, Workspace.tsx:96); and keyboard retime already exists in the Caption phase (CaptionClipLane.tsx:43-62, :74-89, mounted at Caption.tsx:85). Severity MEDIUM — a genuine WCAG 2.1.1 failure the project itself documents as "a locked WCAG-A barrier" (CaptionClipLane.tsx:3-5) and which the axe gate provably cannot see (a11y.a11y.spec.ts:98-103 never activates the timeline tab), but with working keyboard paths for the most common tasks, leaving Split and Merge as the only capabilities lost outright.

## The Workspace 'Advanced' disclosure never actually hides its cluster — CSS `display:flex` beats the `hidden` attribute, leaving 5 visible tabs that no keyboard user can focus
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:231 `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>` vs C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152 `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; }` — an author declaration, which beats the UA-origin `[hidden]{display:none}` regardless of specificity. Chromium probe on that exact markup+rule: {"panelHiddenAttr": true, "panelComputedDisplay": "flex", "convertRect": {"w": 62.6875, "h": 21}, "convertTabIndex": -1}; detector control in the same run, a plain `hidden` div: {"controlPlainHiddenDisplay": "none"}. Those visible tabs get `tabIndex={-1}` (TabBar.tsx:89, roving tabindex) and are excluded from the arrow-key order (TabBar.tsx:151-158, `advancedOpen ? ... : []`). A grep for `[hidden]` across app/renderer/**/*.css returns no reset rule. No test can catch it: TabBar.test.tsx:97/105 regex the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE out of an SSR string, and Workspace.test.tsx:598/615 assert `panel.hidden === true` — the DOM property under jsdom, which never applies workspace.css.
- why: Five of the thirteen Workspace tabs are painted on screen, look identical to their siblings, respond to the mouse — and are unreachable by Tab (tabIndex -1) and by arrow keys (excluded from orderedIds). A keyboard user sees a control and cannot focus it, with no cue that the 'Advanced ▸' toggle (which shows a collapsed caret next to an expanded cluster) is the gate. It also makes the Advanced disclosure dead UI for everyone.
- fix: Scope the layout rule so the attribute wins: `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]) { display: flex; }`, or add a global `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` reset in styles/. Then add a regression test that asserts computed style (Playwright `toBeHidden()` in app/e2e/visual), not the `hidden` property — the jsdom property assertion is a detector that passes in both states.
- ⚠ scope correction: The Workspace grouped tab strip's "Advanced" disclosure does not visually collapse its Deliver cluster: the author-origin rule `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex }` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152) overrides the UA-origin `[hidden] { display: none }` for the panel at app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239, and no `[hidden]` reset exists anywhere in app CSS — so with `advancedOpen=false` (the default, app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:131) the panel stays in flow and lays out its 5 Deliver tabs (convert, nle, recipes, assets, tracks — Workspace.tsx:84-89). Proven in the real built app by the committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png (regenerated at 27e7189b, the same commit that last touched TabBar.tsx), which paints the `DELIVER` caption and the `CONVERT` tab while the cluster is collapsed. At the shipped 1280x820 window (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039) only that caption and a clipped `CONVERT` are on screen; the other four Deliver tabs, the Advanced toggle and the Export CTA sit in the strip's horizontal overflow (`.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto }`, workspace.css:36-39) and all five paint together only in a window widened to roughly ≥1.8k px. While collapsed, those tabs are outside the sequential tab order (tabIndex -1 for every non-active tab, TabBar.tsx:97) and outside arrow-key order (TabBar.tsx:159-166 plus the `index === -1` early return at :181), so a keyboard user must first activate the still-functional Advanced toggle (TabBar.tsx:245-252) or Export (Workspace.tsx:137-140) to reach them — they are not permanently unfocusable, and the toggle is not dead UI (it still flips aria-expanded, rotates the caret at workspace.css:144-146, and gates arrow-key membership). Severity MEDIUM: a broken progressive-disclosure affordance plus a visible-but-not-arrow-reachable control, not a loss of keyboard operability. Nothing guards it: Workspace.test.tsx:598/615 and TabBar.test.tsx:97/105 assert only the `hidden` property/attribute (true in both states under jsdom/SSR), no e2e spec touches `.tabbar__advanced-panel`, and the visual baseline now certifies the broken paint — so the fix must scope the layout rule (`:not([hidden])`) or add a `[hidden]` reset, add a Playwright `toBeHidden()` assertion, AND regenerate workspace-preview-win32.png.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not a refutation — the headline defect stands. Two sub-clauses want tightening, and one consequence is UNDER-claimed:

(a) "leaving 5 visible tabs" is window-width dependent. `.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto }` at app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39 clips the row, so in the committed 1280px baseline only `DELIVER` + part of `CONVERT` paint inside the viewport; the other 4 are laid out (non-zero boxes, offsetParent non-null) but scrolled out. Correctly scoped: "the collapsed cluster is laid out and painted instead of removed — how many of its 5 tabs are on-screen depends on window width."

(b) "no keyboard user can focus" is exact for the state the app opens in (advancedOpen=false, active='subtitles' → all 5 at tabIndex -1 and absent from orderedIds; my probe measured keyboard-reachable buttons = subtitles + Advanced + Export only). Strictly, TabBar.tsx:97 gives the ACTIVE tab tabIndex 0, so ONE of the 5 becomes Tab-focusable if it is active (an `initialTab` deep-link, or after a mouse click) — and even then it is still excluded from arrow nav by TabBar.tsx:177-181. Correctly scoped: "at most one of the five is ever keyboard-focusable, and none is ever reachable by the arrow keys while the disclosure reads collapsed."

(c) UNDER-claimed: because the cluster consumes the flex row, the baseline shows the Advanced toggle AND the Export button pushed off the visible strip — so the design-review P1 "standing Export affordance" (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:99-105, app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:254-258) is also lost at 1280px, and the very control that gates the cluster is unreachable without horizontal scrolling. That strengthens the high severity rather than softening it.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim (it under-claims impact), but the correctly-scoped version is: "The Workspace 'Advanced' disclosure never hides its Deliver cluster - the author rule `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex }` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152) beats the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` against `hidden={!advancedOpen}` (app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239), with no [hidden] reset anywhere in the app CSS. Confirmed in the committed render baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png, captured with no toggle interaction (surfaces.visual.spec.ts:93-101, advancedOpen=false per Workspace.tsx:131). Three user-visible consequences, in descending severity: (a) the 5 extra tabs overflow the nowrap `overflow-x: auto` strip (workspace.css:36-39), pushing the Advanced toggle AND the persistent Export button - rendered as siblings after the tablist, TabBar.tsx:244-258 - off-screen at the 1280px default width, neutralising the standing Export affordance in an app whose terminal goal is exporting; (b) the disclosure is dead UI for every user, its collapsed caret (workspace.css:137-146) contradicting an expanded cluster; (c) while collapsed the 5 visible tabs are absent from both the tab order (tabIndex=-1, TabBar.tsx:97) and the arrow order (TabBar.tsx:159-166, early return at :181), so they are not directly focusable - reachable only by first activating the Advanced button (TabBar.tsx:244-252), which is itself off-screen - and mouse-clicking one leaves arrow keys dead because handleSelect never opens the cluster (Workspace.tsx:189-198). No existing test can catch any of this: TabBar.test.tsx:97/105 regex the hidden attribute out of an SSR string and Workspace.test.tsx:598/615 assert the jsdom panel.hidden property, both of which pass in the broken and fixed states."

## Batch & Templates sub-tab has ZERO token CSS — every control renders as unthemed browser chrome
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `token-consistency` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `grep` for `batch-queue__|template-editor__|export-presets__|\.batch-queue|\.template-editor|\.export-presets|\.repurpose|make-shorts__panel` across `app/**/*.css` returns **0 occurrences across 0 files**. The three panels behind the Batch tab are `app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:27` (`.repurpose`) → `:30` (`.repurpose__panel`) → `app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:261` (`.batch-queue`), `app/renderer/src/features/TemplateEditor.tsx:83` (`.template-editor`), `app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:182` (`.export-presets`). All three import `./panels.css`, but every rule in that sheet is scoped to `.feature-panel` / a named `*-panel` class (`app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:12,23,32`) and none of the three carries `feature-panel` (all 18 real consumers do, e.g. `app/renderer/src/features/Convert.tsx:175`). The shared control voices in `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css` are likewise class-gated: raised button `:344`, accent primary `:410-411`, inputs/selects/textareas `:452-454`, hover `:471-473`, focus glow `:485-487`, field label caps `:1184-1185`, panel `h2` `:1166`, `<progress>` `:1124`. The ONLY bare element rule for a form control in the entire renderer is `button { font-family: inherit }` at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:335` (verified by grep for `^(input|select|textarea|button|fieldset|legend|table|td|th|tr|h4|section|ul|li)[\s,{:]` over `app/renderer/src/**/*.css` → 1 hit). Concretely unstyled: the template `<select>` `BatchQueue.tsx:303`, source checkboxes `:291`, the primary `Run batch` button `:316-323`, the `<fieldset>/<legend>` `:287-288`, the `h4` "Incomplete batches" `:270`, `.batch-queue__row-status[data-status]` `:348` (no `--status-*` colour anywhere — cf. the app convention `app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:345-351`), TemplateEditor's 2 inputs + select + checkbox fieldset + Save button `TemplateEditor.tsx:93,102,118,126-138,140` and its `h4` `:146`, and all 7 inputs/selects per row plus the `<table>` in `ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:41-102,199`. The defect is already documented in-repo for a sibling control: `app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css:27-33` says "the shared input rule (shell.css) styles .feature-panel / .shortmaker selects but NOT this view, so the picker fell back to a raw native OS <select> … that broke the dark-editorial theme" — that fix (`makeShorts.css:34-64`) was applied ONLY to `.make-shorts__picker select`, not to the Batch panels one tab over. `.make-shorts__panel` (`MakeShorts.tsx:201`) also has no rule, so the Batch content gets no gutter under the tab strip (the Gallery escapes this only because `.shorts` supplies its own `--space-6` padding, `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:22`). No visual baseline covers it: `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts:41-49` screenshots `.make-shorts` on the default `make` sub-tab only, and `:59-68` explicitly notes "the batch/templates surface it once captured moved into Make Shorts → Batch" while asserting nothing but the Edit tab's selected state.
- why: An entire top-level sub-tab of the primary novice flow renders outside the design system: default control geometry (no `--radius-sm`, no `--edge` hairline, no `--control-pad-input`, no `--surface-deep` fill, no `--focus-glow`), default `h4`/`legend` typography instead of the tracked-caps subhead voice, and — worst — `Run batch` is visually identical to `Delete`/`Resume` because the rationed `--accent` primary voice (`shell.css:410-420`) never reaches it, so the surface has no primary action affordance. Batch item status carries no semantic colour at all. UNVERIFIED: I did not launch the app, so the exact rendered pixels are inferred from CSS reachability, not observed; note `color-scheme: dark` (`app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:20`) means Chromium's native controls render dark rather than the "light fill" the makeShorts.css comment describes, so the mismatch is geometry/voice rather than a light-on-dark flash.
- fix: Add `feature-panel` to the three roots (`BatchQueue.tsx:261`, `TemplateEditor.tsx:83`, `ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:182`) so the whole shared control layer in `shell.css:344-499` applies for free, and give the `Run batch` / `Save template` buttons the accent voice by wrapping them in `.actions` (matching `shell.css:411`) or adding an explicit selector. Then add a `repurpose.css` (imported by `Repurpose.tsx`) for the panel gutter, a `.make-shorts__panel` padding rule in `makeShorts.css`, `h4` in the panels' tracked-caps subhead voice, and `.batch-queue__row-status[data-status=...]` colours off `--status-success`/`--status-error-text`/`--status-warn` (text label already present, so colour stays redundant). Extend `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts` with a Batch sub-tab screenshot so this cannot silently regress again.
- ⚠ scope correction: Batch & Templates sub-tab: the three panels have no per-component CSS, so their FORM-CONTROL CHROME and panel layout fall outside the design system — while the surface's chrome-level furniture (tab strip, progress bar, focus ring, base typography) is on-token.

Scope actually measured:
(a) Zero CSS rules exist for `.batch-queue*`, `.template-editor*`, `.export-presets*`, `.batch-consent*`, `.repurpose*`, or `.make-shorts__panel` (grep over app/**/*.css → 0 matches). BatchConsentCard (`BatchConsentCard.tsx:37-80`) is unstyled too.
(b) None of the roots (`BatchQueue.tsx:261`, `TemplateEditor.tsx:83`, `ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:182`) carries `feature-panel`/`shortmaker`, so the class-gated shared control layer never applies: raised-button geometry (`shell.css:341-346`), accent primary (`:409-414`), input fill/padding/edge (`:451-459`), hover (`:471-476`), accent focus glow (`:484-492`), tracked-caps field labels (`:1184-1186`), panel h2 (`:1166-1168`). Only `button { font-family: inherit }` (`shell.css:335`) reaches them as an element rule.
(c) Concretely default-chrome: the template `<select>` (`BatchQueue.tsx:303`), source checkboxes (`:291`), `Run batch` (`:316-323`), `<fieldset>/<legend>` (`:287-288`), `h4` (`:270`); TemplateEditor's 2 inputs + select + checkbox fieldset + Save (`:93,102,118,126-138,140`) and its `h4` (`:146`); every input/select and the `<table>` in ExportPresetsPanel (`:41-102,199`). `.batch-queue__row-status[data-status]` (`:348`) has no semantic colour (no `[data-status]` rule exists anywhere), unlike the app convention at `panels.css:345-351`.
(d) The primary-action affordance point holds and is in fact stronger than stated: `Run batch` (`BatchQueue.tsx:316-317`) and `Save template` (`TemplateEditor.tsx:140`) are both `type="button"` and neither sits in an `.actions` wrapper, so they miss `shell.css:409-414` on BOTH arms — adding `feature-panel` alone would NOT grant them the accent voice.
(e) NOT true: these controls are not wholly unthemed. `.progress*` (`shell.css:1094-1121`, ungated, rendered via `BatchQueue.tsx:343` → `ProgressBar.tsx:22-34`) and `.tabbar`/`.tab` (`shell.css:1033-1090`, ungated, rendered via `Repurpose.tsx:28` → `TabBar.tsx:215,98`) are fully token-driven, the global `:where(...):focus-visible` ring (`shell.css:49-52`) applies token `--focus-ring` to every control, base typography/colour inherit from `shell.css:9-19`, and `.make-shorts { gap: var(--space-3) }` (`makeShorts.css:8-12`) supplies an 8px gutter rather than none.
(f) Blast radius extends beyond Make Shorts: `Deliver.tsx:71-72` mounts BatchQueue + ExportPresetsPanel under `.deliver-view__panel`, also without a `feature-panel` ancestor.
(g) No visual baseline covers either mount (`surfaces.visual.spec.ts:41-50`, `:59-69`).

Severity: MEDIUM (control chrome + missing primary-action affordance on two surfaces), not HIGH-as-"entire sub-tab renders outside the design system".
- ⚠ scope correction: Batch & Templates sub-tab has ZERO PANEL-SCOPED token CSS: no CSS rule anywhere in the renderer selects `.repurpose`, `.repurpose__panel`, `.make-shorts__panel`, `.batch-queue`, `.template-editor`, or `.export-presets` (0 matches across all 59 renderer stylesheets), and none of the three panel roots (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:261, TemplateEditor.tsx:83, ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:182) nor any ancestor carries `feature-panel`, so the shared control layer in app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:344-499 — which is written as descendant selectors — never reaches them. Consequence, correctly scoped: these controls keep NATIVE geometry and fill (no --radius-sm, no --edge hairline, no --control-pad-input, no --surface-deep) and get no accent-primary voice, so `Run batch` (BatchQueue.tsx:316-323) is visually identical to Delete/Resume and the surface has no primary-action affordance; `h4`/`legend` use default typography instead of the tracked-caps subhead voice; and `.batch-queue__row-status[data-status]` (BatchQueue.tsx:348) carries no semantic colour since no `data-status` selector exists in any stylesheet. They are NOT fully unthemed, however: token-driven text colour, UI font and body size DO reach them by inheritance from `html, body, #root` (shell.css:9-19), and focus IS themed app-wide by the global `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }` at shell.css:49 — what is missing is the richer `--focus-glow`/`--accent-edge` field-focus upgrade (shell.css:485-499), not focus styling itself. Also correcting one citation: the Gallery's gutter comes from `.shorts__header` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:22), not from `.shorts`, which has no padding (shorts.css:10-16). Severity high stands for a token-consistency lens: an entire top-level sub-tab of the primary novice flow renders outside the design system's control geometry and action hierarchy, with no visual baseline covering it (app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts:41-49, :59-68).
- ⚠ scope correction: Batch & Templates sub-tab has no token CSS for control GEOMETRY, FILL, or TYPOGRAPHIC VOICE — severity medium, not high.

Scoped version that holds: the three panels behind Make Shorts -> "Batch & Templates" (BatchQueue.tsx:261 .batch-queue, TemplateEditor.tsx:83 .template-editor, ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:182 .export-presets) each import features/panels.css (BatchQueue.tsx:31, TemplateEditor.tsx:17, ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:18) but none carries the `feature-panel` root class, so that import is a no-op and the entire shared control layer in shell.css:341-499 misses them. Consequences that are real and verified: no --radius-sm / --edge / --control-pad-input / --surface-deep on ~15 inputs, selects and checkboxes; `Run batch` (BatchQueue.tsx:316-323) never receives the rationed accent voice (shell.css:409-414) so it is visually identical to Delete/Resume, leaving the surface with no primary-action affordance; bare h4/fieldset/legend/table fall to UA defaults while three sibling surfaces have dedicated legend classes; .batch-queue__row-status[data-status] (BatchQueue.tsx:348) carries no semantic colour (cf. the convention at panels.css:345-351); and .make-shorts__panel has no rule so the content gets no gutter under the tab strip.

TWO SUB-CLAIMS TO FIX. First, "ZERO token CSS" and "unthemed browser chrome" are too absolute: the global :where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) } at shell.css:49 DOES reach this surface, so keyboard focus visibility — the accessibility-critical property — is intact, as are the inherited font/colour from shell.css:9-19 and button { font-family: inherit } at :335. The defect is geometry/fill/voice, not total absence of theming. Second, the Gallery's escape padding lives on .shorts__header (shorts.css:22), not on .shorts (shorts.css:10-16 has no padding) — correct line, wrong selector.

SEVERITY medium, not high: nothing is unusable, mislabeled, unreachable, or keyboard-inaccessible; every control functions and carries an aria-label; for a single-user local desktop app there is no brand or conversion cost. But it is NOT noise — 15+ controls sit off-system on a section the code itself calls the novice front door, the no-op stylesheet import proves the omission was unintentional, maintainers already treated this exact defect class as a real theme-breaking bug one tab over (makeShorts.css:27-33), and nothing in CI can catch a regression: tokens.conformance.test.ts pins token VALUES not surface coverage, and surfaces.visual.spec.ts never opens the Batch sub-tab. The proposed fix (add `feature-panel` to the three roots, give Run batch/Save template the accent voice, add the panel gutter, status colours, and a Batch screenshot) is correct and low-risk.

## Workspace "Advanced" disclosure permanently reports aria-expanded="false" while the panel it hides is fully rendered — and its 5 tabs are excluded from the tablist's keyboard model
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `axe-a11y` · verifiers 3
- evidence: ROOT CAUSE — the `hidden` attribute is overridden by author CSS:
- `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:231` renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`.
- `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152` sets `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }`. An AUTHOR `display` declaration beats the UA-origin `[hidden] { display: none }` rule regardless of specificity.
- Grep of every `*.css` under `app/renderer/src` for `hidden` returns ONLY `overflow: hidden` / `visibility: hidden` — there is NO `[hidden]` reset anywhere in the renderer.

INDEPENDENT REAL-BROWSER PROOF (not jsdom): the committed baseline `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png` is captured with the DEFAULT `advancedOpen=false` (`app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:124-130` `openVideo` clicks `button.task-hub__advanced` and never touches the Advanced toggle; `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:131` initialises `advancedOpen` to `false`). The strip in that PNG renders `SPEECH & TEXT … FRAME & CUT … AUDIO DUB | DELIVER CONVERT TIMELINE EXPORT RECIPES ASSE…` — the Deliver cluster is visible while `hidden` is set.

KEYBOARD CONSEQUENCE (executed, vitest+jsdom, real `TabBar` + real `WORKSPACE_TABS`/`WORKSPACE_TAB_GROUPS`, `active="dub"`, `advancedOpen={false}`):
```
ArrowRight from the last primary tab 'dub' -> ["transcribe"]     (wraps; skips 'convert')
convert   tabIndex=-1  aria-selected=false
nle       tabIndex=-1  aria-selected=false
recipes   tabIndex=-1  aria-selected=false
assets    tabIndex=-1  aria-selected=false
tracks    tabIndex=-1  aria-selected=false
Advanced toggle: aria-expanded=false aria-controls=(none)
Advanced panel : id=(none) hiddenAttr=true
```
`app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:151-158` omits advanced groups from `orderedIds` when `!advancedOpen`, so arrow-key nav skips 5 tabs the user can see and click.

WHY IT SHIPPED: `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.test.tsx:97` asserts only `toMatch(/class="tabbar__advanced-panel"[^>]*hidden/)` — the ATTRIBUTE in the markup string, never the computed `display`. No test loads the CSS.

Also reachable via `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:137-140` (`handleExport` sets `active='convert'` + `advancedOpen=true`), then one click on the Advanced toggle (`TabBar.tsx:236-244`) puts the `aria-selected="true"` tab back inside the `hidden` container.
- why: WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value — Level A): a control's programmatic state must match reality. Screen-reader users are told "Advanced, collapsed" while all five Deliver tabs (Convert, Timeline export, Recipes, Assets, Tracks) are rendered, exposed and mouse-operable — the exact same defect class as a dangling `aria-controls`: an ARIA attribute asserting something the DOM does not back. Keyboard users get a tablist whose arrow-key model silently omits 5 visible tabs, and can only rejoin them by pressing a button that claims they are already hidden. Functionally, the entire WU-3a2 progressive-disclosure feature is inert, which is also why the strip overflows past 1280px (`.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto }`, workspace.css:36-39) and pushes `Tracks`, the Advanced toggle and the design-review-P1 `Export` button out of the initial viewport. No axe rule detects expanded-state-vs-reality, and the CI a11y gate only reads `results.violations` filtered to serious/critical (`app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:49-53`), so this is invisible to every existing check.
- fix: Guard the layout rule so the UA hidden semantics survive — in `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148`:
```css

Then, in `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx`, give the panel an `id` and point the toggle at it: `<div id="tabbar-advanced-panel" className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>` + `aria-controls="tabbar-advanced-panel"` on the button at line 236-244. Correctly scoped: "the DELIVER cluster label and the leading edge of CONVERT are visible in the committed baseline while `hidden` is set" — which is still sufficient proof that the panel is displayed.

2. LINE NUMBERS ARE PRE-#308. HEAD is now dcb59e4b (PRs #308 and #309 merged after the audited baseline). The cited numbers are correct at 91240473 but have shifted +8 on HEAD: the panel div 231 -> 239, the toggle 236-244 -> 245-252, orderedIds 151-158 -> 159-166. workspace.css:148-152, TabBar.test.tsx:97 and a11y.a11y.spec.ts:49-53 are unchanged. 3. SEVERITY ATTRIBUTION. "High" is defensible, but the dominant harm is FUNCTIONAL/LAYOUT (inert WU-3a2 disclosure + a 408px-wider strip that pushes Export and the Advanced toggle off the default viewport), not the WCAG 4.1.2 aria-expanded mismatch the axe-a11y lens leads with. For this app's single sighted local user the screen-reader-only harm would by itself be modest; the finding should be filed as a functional/layout regression WITH an a11y consequence.

4. THE PROPOSED FIX IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT (additional, verified by the same mechanical computation). Via Workspace.tsx:137-140 handleExport (active='convert', advancedOpen=true) followed by one Advanced-toggle click, the state active='convert' + advancedOpen=false leaves the ACTIVE tab outside orderedIds, so every arrow key dead-ends at the TabBar.tsx:181 early return while the ONLY tabIndex=0 button is the one inside the collapsed panel. REAL-BROWSER EVIDENCE (scoped to what the artifact actually shows): the committed baseline `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png`, captured with `advancedOpen=false` (`Workspace.tsx:131`; `app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:124-130` clicks only the unrelated TaskHub escape at `app/renderer/src/views/TaskHub.tsx:164`), visibly renders the `DELIVER` cluster caption and the `CONV` tab while `hidden` is set. The remaining 4 Deliver tabs are rendered and in the a11y tree but sit beyond the 1280px edge, reachable only by scrolling `.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto }` (`workspace.css:36-39`) — so all 5 are screen-reader-exposed, but only 1 is visible/clickable without scrolling.

(b) `TabBar.tsx:159-166` omits advanced groups from `orderedIds` while collapsed and `TabBar.tsx:181` early-returns on `index === -1`, so ArrowRight from the last primary tab `dub` wraps to `transcribe`, skipping 5 tabs the user can see. (c) The un-hidden cluster overflows the strip past 1280px, pushing the design-review-P1 `Export` button and the `Advanced` toggle itself out of the initial viewport — both absent from the baseline PNG.

WHY IT SHIPPED (wider than originally cited): `TabBar.test.tsx:97` AND `Workspace.test.tsx:594` and `:687` all assert the `hidden` attribute/property in markup or the DOM, never the computed `display`; no test loads the CSS. axe has no expanded-state-vs-reality rule, and the gate filters to serious/critical (`app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:49-53`) — the Workspace IS scanned (`:98`) and passes.

CITATION NOTE: all TabBar.tsx line numbers in the original finding are 8 lines low because PR #308 inserted an 8-line comment at `TabBar.tsx:86-93`; the above are re-anchored to HEAD dcb59e4b. #308 also already closed the dangling `aria-controls` at `TabBar.tsx:94`.
