Its 5 Deliver tabs are simultaneously excluded from the tablist's arrow-key model (TabBar.tsx:159-166)."

2) Evidence: the PNG transcription "SPEECH & TEXT … AUDIO DUB | DELIVER CONVERT TIMELINE EXPORT RECIPES ASSE…" is over-specified relative to the artifact. workspace-preview-win32.png actually renders "SPEECH & TEXT TRANSCRIBE SEARCH SUBTITLES DIARIZE REFINE | FRAME & CUT SHORT-MAKER TIMELINE | AUDIO DUB | DELIVER CONV…" — clipped at the 1280px viewport edge; TIMELINE belongs to the FRAME & CUT cluster, and no "EXPORT RECIPES ASSE" text is visible in the strip. The load-bearing claim the artifact does support is exactly: "the DELIVER cluster label and its first tab (CONVERT) are rendered in the strip while the `hidden` attribute is set, and the rest of the cluster plus the Advanced toggle and the Export button are pushed outside the 1280px viewport."

## ShortsGalleryModal is an aria-modal dialog with no focus trap, no focus restore, and an Escape handler that dies the moment focus leaves it
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:75-81 declares `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` but attaches nothing except a React `onKeyDown` (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63-68) to the dialog div. Tab is never trapped. Focus-on-open is an ad-hoc callback ref (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47, attached at :85) whose unmount call receives `null`, so `node?.focus()` is a no-op — focus is never restored to the "N shorts" trigger (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:150-157).

The repo already ships the fix and uses it in three sibling dialogs: `useFocusTrap` (app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:53) traps Tab (:85-100), handles Escape via a real DOM listener (:79-84, :103) and restores focus on unmount (:106). Adopted by app/renderer/src/components/FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, app/renderer/src/components/ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44, app/renderer/src/components/DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45. ShortsGalleryModal does not import it.

The modal is a live production path, not dead code: `shorts={libraryShortsClient}` at app/renderer/src/App.tsx:522, gated open at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:606-615.

Backdrop is a full-screen scrim that hides any background focus ring: app/renderer/src/components/library-shell.css:192-202 (`position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 100; background: var(--overlay-scrim)`).

Tests confirm the gap: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:130 asserts focus-on-open and :161-164 asserts Escape dispatched ON the dialog element — there is no Tab-containment test and no focus-restore test.
- why: Concrete keyboard-only failure: open a video's gallery, Tab to a clip's Delete and press Enter. Library.tsx:437-454 rebuilds `shortsByVideo`, so that clip's `<li>` (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:171, keyed by `short.id`) unmounts with focus inside it — the browser resets `document.activeElement` to `document.body`. From there Escape is inert, because a keydown on `body` is not on the React path through the dialog div, so ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63 never fires. Continuing to Tab walks focus into the Library grid *behind* the z-index:100 scrim, where the focus ring is invisible. The keyboard user is left with no visible focus, a dead Escape, and an `aria-modal="true"` element that has not actually hidden or contained anything — WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured) failures on the app's own "zero serious/critical" a11y surface.
- fix: Replace the ad-hoc ref + onKeyDown with the shared hook, exactly as FirstRunChooser does:
`const trapRef = useFocusTrap<HTMLDivElement>({ onEscape: onClose, initialFocus: '.shorts-modal__close' });`
attach `ref={trapRef}` to the `.shorts-modal` div, and delete `focusOnOpen` (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47) and `onKeyDown` (:63-68). Add two tests to ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx: (a) Tab from the last focusable control wraps to the first; (b) after deleting a clip, Escape still calls `onClose`.
- ⚠ scope correction: ShortsGalleryModal is the one aria-modal dialog in the renderer with no focus containment and no focus restore, and its Escape handler only works while focus is inside the dialog subtree — but the shared useFocusTrap hook closes only two of the three gaps, so adopting it is necessary and NOT sufficient.

SCOPE OF THE DEFECT (executably confirmed):
* No focus restore on close. app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47 is a callback ref whose unmount invocation receives null, so node?.focus() is a no-op. Measured: after unmount document.activeElement === document.body, never the "N shorts" trigger (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:150-157). Unconditional — fires on every close.
* No Tab containment. The dialog div (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:74-81) attaches only a React onKeyDown (:63-68); Tab on the last focusable is not preventDefaulted, so focus leaves the dialog into the Library grid behind the z-index:100 scrim (app/renderer/src/components/library-shell.css:192-202). Unconditional.
* Escape is subtree-scoped. Because React 18.3.1 (app/package.json:31) delegates at the root container, a keydown whose target is not a descendant of the dialog div never reaches ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63. Once focus leaves the dialog, Escape is inert. Reproducible trigger: focus a clip's Delete (app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:75-82 — one click, no confirm) and activate it; app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:437-454 rebuilds shortsByVideo, the clip's <li> unmounts with focus inside it, activeElement resets to body, and Escape yields 0 onClose calls. There is no document-level fallback anywhere in the renderer (the only keydown DOM listener is app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:103, and it is node-scoped).
* Test gap is real: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:130 asserts focus-on-open and :161-164 dispatches Escape ON the dialog element; there is no Tab-containment test and no focus-restore test in the file.
* Not covered by any gate: app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:56-103 never opens this modal, and axe-core has no focus-trap rule — so nothing would have caught it.

CORRECTLY-SCOPED WCAG: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) degradation, plus a WAI-ARIA APG modal-dialog focus-management violation. NOT WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — --overlay-scrim is rgba(9, 11, 16, 0.62) (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:267; alpha < 1 is asserted deliberately at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:598-602) and there is no backdrop-filter on the backdrop, so the focused element behind it is dimmed, not "entirely hidden". A 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast failure on the ring seen through the scrim is plausible but UNVERIFIED — settle it by screenshotting a Tab-focused Library control with the modal open and measuring the ring's contrast against the scrimmed backdrop. Note also that aria-modal="true" DOES hide background content from assistive tech; it is keyboard containment, not AT exposure, that is missing.

SEVERITY: medium, not high. The gaps are real and on a live path (App.tsx:522, Library.tsx:606-615), but the modal is the last element in Library's JSX so Tab from body re-enters it and Escape recovers; no axe impact.

CORRECTLY-SCOPED FIX (three parts, not one):
1. Attach useFocusTrap to the .shorts-modal div and delete focusOnOpen + onKeyDown — this genuinely closes focus-restore and in-dialog Tab wrap (both proven by control probes against FirstRunChooser).
2. ALSO fix the shared hook, because step 1 alone leaves the post-delete failure intact — measured with the prescribed patch applied: activeElement = BODY, onClose calls = 0, Tab defaultPrevented = false. Either bind the Escape/Tab listener at document level and filter on container containment, or add a focusout/MutationObserver guard that re-homes focus into the container when the active element leaves it. This benefits FirstRunChooser, ModelsOnboarding and DirectorOnboarding too, which carry the same hole and only escape it for lack of removable children.
3. Tests: (a) Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first; (b) focus returns to the "N shorts" trigger on close; (c) after deleting a clip, Escape still calls onClose — and note (c) is RED against step 1 alone, which is exactly why step 2 is required. Guard (b) against the delete-the-last-clip branch, where the trigger itself unmounts (LibraryCard.tsx:149 / Library.tsx:589) and a document.body fallback is the correct expectation.
- ⚠ scope correction: ShortsGalleryModal is an aria-modal dialog with no focus trap and no focus restore, and its Escape handler dies once focus leaves the dialog subtree. MEDIUM severity (not high). Correctly-scoped version: (1) The unconditional harm is focus restore - the callback ref at app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47 receives null on unmount, so focus lands on document.body after EVERY close, and a keyboard user must re-traverse the app from the top to get back to the "N shorts" trigger (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:150-157). (2) Escape dies after any interaction that unmounts the focused node - most concretely deleting a clip, which is a one-click no-confirm action (app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:75-82 -> app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:612 -> :437-454) whose <li> is keyed by short.id (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:277-279, li at :171). Verified: the renderer registers NO document/window keydown listener anywhere (only FirstRunSetup.tsx:322-323 online/offline) and the React root is #root (app/renderer/src/main.tsx:9,:18), so a body keydown reaches no React handler. Corroborated by the repo's own Library.test.tsx:1226-1257, which proves the modal stays open through delete-to-empty. (3) DROP the WCAG 2.4.11 citation: --overlay-scrim is rgba(9,11,16,0.62) (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:267), so a background focus ring is dimmed, not entirely hidden - 2.4.11 (AA) only requires the component not be entirely hidden (entirely-obscured is 2.4.12, AAA), and 2.4.11 is WCAG 2.2, outside this repo's declared WCAG 2.0/2.1 A+AA target (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:40). WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) is the SC that holds. (4) DROP "on the app's own zero serious/critical a11y surface": no e2e test ever opens this modal (grep for shorts-modal / shorts-label over app/e2e = zero hits); app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:56-103 scans Library with the modal CLOSED plus Make Shorts / Director / Edit / two Settings sections / Workspace preview, and axe-core has no focus-trap rule, so the gate could never have detected this. The surface is UNSCANNED, not passing-while-broken - which is itself an argument for adding the two proposed tests. (5) The proposed fix is unchanged and correct: adopt the shared useFocusTrap (app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:53) exactly as the three sibling dialogs do (FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44, DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45); 3 of 4 modal dialogs already use it, so this is an inconsistency cheap to close.
- ⚠ scope correction: ShortsGalleryModal is an aria-modal dialog with no focus trap and no focus restore, and its Escape handler is container-scoped so it dies the moment focus leaves the dialog subtree. Verified: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:74-81 sets role="dialog" aria-modal="true" but attaches only a React onKeyDown (:63-68 / :80); nothing traps Tab; the focus-on-open callback ref (:45-47, attached :85) receives null on unmount so node?.focus() is a no-op and focus never returns to the LibraryCard.tsx:150-157 trigger. Executable-proven: after a clip's Delete is focused and Library.tsx:437-454 rebuilds shortsByVideo (React key={short.id} at ProducedShorts.tsx:279) the clip's <li> unmounts, document.activeElement becomes <body>, and Escape from there calls onClose 0 times; a Tab keydown on the dialog is not defaultPrevented. Only one keydown listener exists in the entire non-test renderer (useFocusTrap.ts:103), so no global Escape fallback exists. The simplest always-reproducible failure needs no delete at all: open the gallery, press Escape, and focus lands on <body> rather than the "N shorts" trigger — WCAG 2.4.3. Live path: App.tsx:522, Library.tsx:606-615.

CORRECTION to the remedy: adopting the shared useFocusTrap hook is necessary but NOT sufficient, and does NOT fix the delete-induced failure this finding leads with. Because the hook binds its keydown listener to the container node (useFocusTrap.ts:103), once focus falls to document.body Escape is equally dead (0 calls) and Tab is equally uncontained — executable-proven, against a passing both-states control (Escape with focus inside the trap = 1 call). What the hook does fix is focus-on-open, focus-restore-on-unmount (:106), and Tab/Escape while focus remains inside the dialog. A complete fix must additionally survive focus loss from an unmounting descendant: bind Escape at the document level, or re-focus on focusout / via a MutationObserver, or migrate to native <dialog>.showModal() for browser-native containment, restore, and Escape. Tests should assert (a) Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first, (b) focus returns to the "N shorts" trigger on close, and (c) after deleting a clip, Escape dispatched from the REAL document.activeElement (not from the dialog element, as ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:161-164 does) still calls onClose — note (c) fails against the useFocusTrap-only fix.

## Keyboard focus ring on every gallery card's play-preview button is 100% clipped away by the thumbnail well's overflow:hidden
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-51 is the ONLY focus style that applies to this control: `:where(button, …):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }` — it explicitly kills the native outline. app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206 defines `--focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-edge)` — zero offset, zero blur, spread-only, i.e. an annulus painted ENTIRELY OUTSIDE the element's border box. app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:212-218 `.shorts__thumb { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 9/16; overflow: hidden; }` with no padding; app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:220-234 `.shorts__thumb-btn { border: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }` — the button's border box coincides exactly with the clipping (padding) box, so all 4px of ring lies outside the clip and is discarded. app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:236-238 shows the ONLY state style is `:hover { color: var(--accent) }` — there is no `:focus` / `:focus-visible` rule for this class anywhere (grep `shorts__thumb` over *.css returns only shorts.css:212-251 + shortmaker-p3.css:220). Button itself: app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:293-298.
- why: A keyboard user tabbing through the gallery gets ZERO visual indication when focus lands on the primary affordance of each card — the outline is removed and its replacement is clipped to nothing. That is a WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) failure on a control repeated once per clip; under the brief's rubric ("violates a11y law") it is arguably critical rather than high. The same class pair is used by the per-video gallery (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:176-181), so the defect is duplicated wherever that gallery mounts. UNVERIFIED at runtime: I derived this from the CSS cascade + CSS box-shadow clipping semantics by reading the files, not by rendering the built app; the ~10% residual is whether a UA/Electron quirk paints part of the ring. The settling experiment is one line in a real window: focus `.shorts__thumb-btn` via keyboard and screenshot-diff against its unfocused state.
- fix: Give this button a clip-proof indicator. Cheapest correct fix: add `.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-bg), inset 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-edge); }` to app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css so the ring is painted INSIDE the clipped box. Equivalent alternatives: `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: -3px;` (negative offset survives the clip), or drop `overflow: hidden` from `.shorts__thumb` and round the child instead. Then add a `--focus-ring-inset` token beside tokens.css:206 so the next author inside an `overflow:hidden` well has the right primitive.
- ⚠ scope correction: Keyboard focus indication on the gallery card's play-preview button (`.shorts__thumb-btn`) is effectively absent: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-51 removes the native outline and replaces it with the spread-only OUTSET `--focus-ring` (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206), while `.shorts__thumb`'s `overflow:hidden` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:216) clips at a box that runtime measurement shows coincides exactly with the button's border box (both 185x328.88 at the same origin), and no `.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible` rule exists in any stylesheet. Measured in Chromium against the real stylesheets: in the default theme 99.97% of the ring is clipped, leaving 24 sub-perceptual pixels (of 91,829 captured) at max delta 13/255 and 1.076:1 contrast as a rounded-corner antialiasing fringe — far below the >=3:1 WCAG 2.4.11 threshold and not a perceptible indicator; under `forced-colors: active` (Windows High Contrast) `box-shadow` is discarded entirely while the authored `outline: none` persists, giving exactly ZERO changed pixels. This is a WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) Focus Visible failure on the primary affordance of every card, on three live mount points: app/renderer/src/App.tsx:471 -> app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:17 -> Shorts (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:293-298), app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:1000 -> ProducedShorts (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:176-181), and app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:607 -> app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:98 -> ProducedShorts. Severity high stands. Preferred fix is `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: -3px` (negative offset survives the clip AND survives forced-colors) rather than an inset box-shadow, which forced-colors discards.
- ⚠ scope correction: Two narrow overclaims need rescoping; the defect itself stands.

(1) Quantitative absolute. Replace "100% clipped away" / "clipped to nothing" with: approximately 99.4% of the focus ring is discarded. Measured in Chromium against the real cascade, keyboard focus on .shorts__thumb-btn changes 24 pixels versus 4152 with the clip removed; all 24 are antialiasing bleed on the border-radius:6px clip curve (6 per corner), max per-channel delta 13/255, and ZERO pixels reach a perceptibility floor of 16/255. So: no perceptible focus indicator is painted, with a 0.58% sub-threshold residual at the rounded corners.

(2) Severity framing. Drop "violates a11y law" and "arguably critical". For a single-user local desktop video tool there is no procurement or public-accommodation obligation, and focus is never actually lost — Enter/Space still activates the button and the resulting action (play a preview, which swaps the thumb for <Player>) is non-destructive and immediately self-evident. Correct severity: MEDIUM-HIGH. It is a genuine WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) Focus Visible failure against the project's OWN declared a11y contract (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:13), duplicated across both galleries (views/Shorts.tsx:293-298 and features/ProducedShorts.tsx:176-181), and it is invisible to the existing gate because a11y.a11y.spec.ts:138-144 checks computed boxShadow !== 'none' rather than painted pixels.

The proposed fix is correct as written and should also close the detector hole: the inset box-shadow variant paints 4004 px and the `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: -3px` variant 2036 px, both verified live. Add the --focus-ring-inset token beside tokens.css:206 as proposed, and upgrade the a11y gate from a computed-style read to a focused-vs-unfocused pixel diff so this class of defect cannot pass in the broken state again.
- ⚠ scope correction: The keyboard focus ring on every gallery card's play-preview button is effectively eliminated by the thumbnail well's `overflow: hidden`: 99.41% of the ring's pixels are clipped (measured 16 surviving px vs 2728 in an identical `overflow: visible` control), and the 0.59% residual is sub-perceptual corner antialiasing at the well's 6px radius (max delta 13/765 ≈ 1.7%; setting `border-radius: 0` drops it to exactly 0 px). No user-perceptible focus indication survives, so a keyboard user still gets zero visual indication when focus lands on the control — the WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible failure and the proposed inset-ring fix both stand unchanged.

## "Saved the short." / "Saved the SRT sidecar." claim a completed save that never happens
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145-146 — `const handleSaveShort = useCallback(() => setManualNote('Saved the short.'), []);` / `const handleSaveSrt = useCallback(() => setManualNote('Saved the SRT sidecar.'), []);`. Both handlers only set a note; no RPC, no file write. Wired at MakeShorts.tsx:273-274. The authors' own comment at MakeShorts.tsx:143-144 calls these "save seams … so the action is acknowledged" — acknowledgement, not completion. The test at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:496-502 asserts the strings and asserts no call, confirming the copy is live and intentionally backed by nothing.
- why: Past-tense first-person-plural completion copy ("Saved the …") is the strongest possible assertion the UI can make. A user clicks "Save short", reads "Saved the short.", and reasonably goes looking for a newly written file. Worse, `manualNote` is a single state slot (MakeShorts.tsx:78), so this note OVERWRITES the only evidence of the real export — "Exported 1 clip(s) from your ranges." (MakeShorts.tsx:187). The user is left with a confirmation of an action that did not occur, having lost the confirmation of the action that did.
- fix: Until the save seam is real, the copy must not claim completion. Either (a) hide the buttons (OutputTray already gates each on a provided handler — OutputTray.tsx:139-148 — so dropping `onSaveShort`/`onSaveSrt` removes them cleanly), or (b) state only what is true, e.g. "Your short is already in the gallery — open Produced shorts" / "A separate subtitle file is written when you pick Separate file above". Also render the acknowledgement in a second slot so it cannot overwrite the export result.
- ⚠ scope correction: Two peripheral sentences in the finding are wider than the evidence; the defect and the high severity both stand. (1) The test at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:496-502 asserts ONLY the two note strings — it contains no negative assertion, so "asserts no call" mis-describes it. The correct statement: the test locks in the exact completion strings, proving the copy is live and deliberate; the "backed by nothing" half comes from the handler bodies at MakeShorts.tsx:145-146, not from the test. (2) The two strings are not equally false. "Saved the short." is MISLEADING but not world-false — the export at MakeShorts.tsx:187 already wrote the clip, so the harm is that a click which performs no action claims completion and overwrites the export confirmation (single manualNote slot, :78/:187/:145-146, one render site at :274-278). "Saved the SRT sidecar." IS world-false under the shipped default subtitleMode 'burn' (OutputTray.tsx:37, shortmaker.py:350-353, :399-400; writesSubtitleFile false at outputOptions.ts:69-71): no subtitle file is ever produced, and a real un-called RPC exists for it (client.ts:207-208 `subtitles.export` -> {path}, named as this button's backing in shortmaker.py:345-346). Also cite HEAD line numbers alongside the base: at dcb59e4b the wiring is MakeShorts.tsx:283-284 and the test is :533-560 (handlers unchanged at :145-146). Feasibility caveat on the proposed fix: `subtitles.export` needs a trackId and MakeShorts.tsx holds no track state, so the reporter's option (a) hide the buttons or (b) retext to verifiable copy is the correct near-term path.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high), and split by string. Two OutputTray save buttons in the Make Shorts front door emit past-tense completion copy for handlers that perform no action, and they clobber the note slot holding the real export result. (a) "Saved the SRT sidecar." (MakeShorts.tsx:146, wired at :284) is FALSE ABOUT STATE under the default configuration: an SRT sidecar is written only when subtitleMode === 'sidecar' (app/renderer/src/lib/outputOptions.ts:70; sidecar delivery proven at sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker_export_delivery.py:74-81), yet the tray default is 'burn' (OutputTray.tsx:37), and the saveSrt intent is never forwarded to the export (MakeShorts.tsx:166-170) — so under defaults the copy asserts a file that exists nowhere and that the click cannot produce. Changing subtitleMode after the export also cannot retroactively affect the finished export; it only affects the next one (dependency at MakeShorts.tsx:195). This is the severe half. (b) "Saved the short." (MakeShorts.tsx:145, wired at :283) is REDUNDANT rather than false in the dominant case: the tray is reachable only after a successful export that already wrote the file (trayOpen set at MakeShorts.tsx:188; error path leaves it false, asserted at MakeShorts.test.tsx:512), so the short genuinely is on disk. The defect is that the copy implies the click performed a save when the click is a no-op — it is state-false only in the 0-clip success edge case (MakeShorts.tsx:186-188). (c) Because manualNote is a single slot (MakeShorts.tsx:78), either click overwrites "Exported N clip(s) from your ranges." (:187) — a real regression in feedback, though not the "only" evidence of the export, since the tray stays open and the short appears in the Produced shorts gallery (MakeShorts.tsx:49, :212). Fix: drop onSaveShort/onSaveSrt so OutputTray.tsx:139-148 hides both buttons until the seam is wired, or replace the copy with state-true text; render any acknowledgement in a second slot so it cannot overwrite the export result. Evidence note: the intent booleans saveShort/saveSrt exist only as an unconsumed model at outputOptions.ts:38-42 and reach neither the RPC contract nor the sidecar, so the absence of a write is provable from the handler source at MakeShorts.tsx:145-146 — NOT from the test, which asserts only the two strings (MakeShorts.test.tsx:533-560) and contains no negative assertion.
- ⚠ scope correction: The Output Tray's two save buttons in Make Shorts report past-tense completion while calling nothing (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145-146, wired at :283-284), but the two halves differ in severity:

(a) "Saved the SRT sidecar." is FALSE in every configuration — a genuine defect. shortmaker.py never writes a subtitle file (zero .srt occurrences; contract is {clips:[{path}]} at shortmaker.py:22, :1304-1313), and the sidecar's own comment at shortmaker.py:345-346 says this button is supposed to call subtitles.export — a real implemented RPC (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:195-208) that the handler never invokes. Reachable on the default path in live UI (App.tsx:471; tray opens after every successful export, MakeShorts.tsx:188) and announced via role="status" (MakeShorts.tsx:275).

(b) "Saved the short." misstates CAUSATION, not outcome. The short is genuinely on disk before the tray can appear (shortmaker.py:1126-1160) and is listed in "Produced shorts" (MakeShorts.tsx:48, :212), so a user who goes looking for the file finds it. The copy wrongly implies this click did the saving.

Severity: MEDIUM, not high — single-user local desktop app, no data loss or security exposure, and a working SRT export already exists at Subtitles.tsx:193-198.

Secondary, correctly scoped: manualNote is a single slot (MakeShorts.tsx:78), so either note overwrites the export result from MakeShorts.tsx:187 — a minor loss, since the gallery is the authoritative record.

Evidence correction: the test at MakeShorts.test.tsx:533-560 asserts ONLY the note strings (:555, :557-559); it does NOT assert that no call is made. The original finding's "asserts no call" and its line cites (:273-274, :496-502) are wrong.

Fix: wire Save SRT to the existing client.subtitles.export and report the real returned path (the Subtitles.tsx:197-198 pattern); for the short, restate as location rather than action ("Your short is in Produced shorts"); render the acknowledgement in a second slot so it cannot overwrite the export result. Dropping the props also cleanly removes the buttons (OutputTray.tsx:139-148).

## "Caption & style" never says it governs only the manual path — the dragged caption position is silently discarded by AI moment-pick
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Heading + sub-copy: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:242-246 — "Caption & style" / "Drag the caption box to position it, pick a style — previewed live on your video." No scope stated. The design's position and tuning reach an export ONLY from MakeShorts.tsx:166-170 (`captionPosition: wire.captionPosition, captionOverride: wire.captionOverride`), i.e. the manual path. The AI path calls `buildExportParams(videoId, approvedCandidates(items), clean, audioTrackId)` with 4 args (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:651), so `output` defaults to `{}` and app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerPresets.ts:189-190 spreads nothing. Only the STYLE reaches the AI panel, once, via `initialControls` (MakeShorts.tsx:233-236) read in a lazy useState initializer that runs a single time (ShortMaker.tsx:161-163) — acknowledged in MakeShorts.tsx:85-88. The AI section also has its OWN competing control labelled "Caption style" (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:152-156).
- why: On-screen order is "AI moment-pick" (MakeShorts.tsx:226) → "Caption & style" (242) → "Manual intervals" (257). A section that governs only the LAST of the three sits directly beneath the first, with copy written as a global statement about "your video". A user drags the caption to the top band, picks a style, runs AI moment-pick, exports — and the position is dropped entirely while the style silently comes from the other picker. A deliberate design choice is lost with no message, and the copy is what conceals it.
- fix: Scope the copy to what it actually drives: heading "Caption & style for manual ranges", sub-copy "…applies to the shorts you export from Manual intervals below. AI moment-pick uses its own Caption style setting." Move the section beneath "Manual intervals" so proximity matches scope. Rename the AI control or this section so one concept does not carry two names ("Caption style" vs "Caption & style"). The alternative fix is to wire `captionPosition`/`captionOverride` into ShortMaker's export and make the copy's global promise true.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the claim stands as written. Tightened restatement with corrected line numbers, for the fix ticket: "The 'Caption & style' section (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:252-256) is written as a global statement about 'your video' but its position box and tuning override reach an export ONLY via the manual path (MakeShorts.tsx:166-170). Both AI export paths call buildExportParams with 4 args (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:651 approve-and-export, :746 batch), so `output` defaults to {} (shortMakerPresets.ts:165) and captionPosition/captionOverride are never sent; the sidecar then falls back to its hardcoded bottom-centred default (sidecar/media_studio/features/caption.py:352-356), so a caption deliberately dragged to the top band is burned at the bottom with no message. Style is seeded into the AI panel once, at mount, in a lazy useState initializer (ShortMaker.tsx:161-163) with no `key` to force a remount — so the first-mount style DOES agree with the designer, and only POST-mount style changes diverge, thereafter driven solely by the AI panel's own competing 'Caption style' select (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:151-164)."
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — this is a citation-drift correction plus one phrase tightened, with the scope UNCHANGED and two additions.

"Caption & style" (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:252-256) states no scope, and neither does the CaptionDesigner it renders. The caption POSITION and the V1.1 tuning override the user sets there reach an export only via the manual path (MakeShorts.tsx:166-170, the sole caller passing buildExportParams' 5th `output` arg). Both AI paths — interactive export at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:651 and unattended batch at :746 — call it with 4 args, so `output` defaults to {} (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerPresets.ts:165) and the conditional spreads at :188-190 emit nothing. The position is therefore dropped for every AI export, silently. The loss is behaviourally real: the sidecar does honour the field (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1382-1384 -> sidecar/media_studio/features/caption.py:354), and no caption-position control exists anywhere in the AI panel (zero matches for CaptionBox|positionBand|CaptionDesigner across ShortMaker*.tsx), so the section is the app's only position affordance and the AI path has no substitute. Of the design, only the STYLE reaches the AI panel, and only as a mount-time seed: `initialControls` is consumed solely at ShortMaker.tsx:162 in a lazy useState initializer with no re-sync effect (acknowledged at MakeShorts.tsx:85-88), so the seed value comes from persisted preferences (MakeShorts.tsx:123) and any later in-section style edit is ignored while the AI export uses its own "Caption style" picker (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:152-156). On-screen order is AI moment-pick (:236) -> Caption & style (:252) -> Manual intervals (:267), so the section governing only the manual export sits directly beneath the AI panel. Existing tests already encode the split (MakeShorts.test.tsx:443, :719 manual carries the fields; :732-748 the AI seed carries only style+language). Proposed fix unchanged.

## DISCARDED status chip renders at 1.71:1 — wrong red token, and the surface's own filter+opacity compound it far past what the repo's AA guard models
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `token-consistency` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1423-1426 — `.sm-status-discarded { background: var(--status-error-soft); color: var(--status-error); }`. The repo created a dedicated red-TEXT token for exactly this (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:71-80) and PROVES the fill token fails on that wash: app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 asserts `contrast(--status-error, wash over --surface-raised) < 4.5` (I re-derived it: 3.75:1). But that guard's enforcement list is Library-only — app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658 (`LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` = library-cards / library-shell / readinessBadge / library-provenance / keep-copy-control), so shell.css is unchecked. On THIS surface the chip is never rendered bare: its ancestor card carries `filter: saturate(0.35)` (app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:80-82, selector `.shortmaker .sm-candidate.sm-discarded`) AND `opacity: 0.55` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1375-1377) — both on the same element, and the chip is a descendant (app/renderer/src/features/CandidateList.tsx:80 emits `sm-candidate sm-discarded`, :113 emits `sm-status sm-status-discarded`). Re-deriving with the repo's own WCAG math plus the sRGB saturate matrix and source-over compositing onto the canvas (--surface-bg #121620): naive 3.75:1 → +saturate 2.84:1 → +opacity 1.71:1. Swapping to --status-error-text only reaches 2.25:1, still under AA.
- why: The word "discarded" is the chip's only content, and at 1.71:1 it is effectively unreadable — a WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) failure on a shipped, clickable state (the card stays selectable/reinstatable). The repo believes it is protected: it wrote the token, wrote the proof, and scoped the guard to five Library sheets, so this surface silently sits ~2.6x below the floor the DoD pins.
- fix: Two parts, because the token swap alone is NOT sufficient (measured 2.25:1): (1) route the chip through `var(--status-error-text)` at shell.css:1425 — mirrors the Library migration; (2) stop stacking two de-emphasis effects on text: drop `opacity: 0.55` from `.sm-discarded` (shell.css:1375-1377) and express "receded" via the surface ladder (e.g. `background: var(--surface-bg)` + `--text-faint`) so the chip's own contrast is computable, keeping `filter: saturate(0.35)` for the thumbnail only rather than the whole card. Then extend `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) to cover shell.css and the Reframe-phase sheets, and add a case that composites through an ancestor filter/opacity so the guard models what this surface actually paints.
- ⚠ scope correction: Technical core CONFIRMED as written; only the surface label needs tightening. Precise version: "ShortMaker candidate-review card (discarded state), app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:879 section — not the Reframe phase. The DISCARDED status chip renders at ~1.71:1 (≈1.73:1 if the opacity backdrop is --surface-raised rather than --surface-bg; I did not trace the literal painted ancestor). Wrong red token (shell.css:1425 uses the fill-only --status-error instead of --status-error-text) compounded by two de-emphasis effects stacked on the same <li> — filter: saturate(0.35) (shortmaker.css:80-82) and opacity: 0.55 (shell.css:1375-1377). The repo's sheet-level red-text guard (tokens.conformance.test.ts:688-698) scans only LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS (:652-658), leaving shell.css unchecked. Blast radius is wider than the chip: the same opacity group also degrades the Approve/Discard/Reinstate button labels at CandidateList.tsx:192-206."
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly scoped (broader, and re-attributed): The ShortMaker discarded candidate card stacks TWO de-emphasis effects on the same element — filter: saturate(0.35) (app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:80-82) and opacity: 0.55 (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1375-1377) — which composite the entire subtree and push FOUR always-rendered text roles below the 4.5:1 AA floor, on a state that remains fully interactive (unconditional onClick at app/renderer/src/features/CandidateList.tsx:86; Reinstate/Approve buttons at :202/:192, so WCAG's inactive-component exception does not apply): the DISCARDED status chip at 1.71:1 (shell.css:1425, --status-error), .sm-why at 3.33:1 (shell.css:1440, --text-secondary), the .sm-row-actions/.sm-row-decide button labels at 3.28:1 (shell.css:1472, --text-muted), and .sm-times at 3.12:1 (shell.css:1448, --text-faint). The root cause is the ancestor de-emphasis, NOT the red token: measured loss is opacity -1.80 vs saturate -0.91, and swapping the chip to --status-error-text still fails at 2.25:1. The --text-faint case is the sharpest evidence of the guard gap, because tokens.conformance.test.ts:198-204 explicitly pins --text-faint at >=4.5:1 on every elevation plane and the ancestor opacity silently defeats that existing guard. Two secondary scope fixes to the original: the red-text guard gap is repo-wide, not shell.css-specific — bare `color: var(--status-error)` appears at ~35 sites across ~25 sheets (shell.css:446,567,1222,1425; jobqueue.css:150,211,293; providersKeys.css:135,270,386,521; setupStatus.css:62,81,136; directorPanel.css:340; and others) — so extending LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS (tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) to only shell.css plus the Reframe-phase sheets leaves most of the leak unguarded; and the correct primary fix is to express "receded" via the surface/text ladder rather than ancestor opacity on text (optionally keeping saturate on the thumbnail only), with the --status-error -> --status-error-text swap as a necessary but insufficient secondary. Contrast figures are spec-model derived (saturate in sRGB per filter-effects, then group opacity), UNVERIFIED against rendered pixels in the shipped Electron build; a screenshot pixel-probe of the discarded card would settle exact values, and there is currently no e2e coverage of this state at all.
- ⚠ scope correction: DISCARDED status chip renders at 1.71:1 — a real but LOW-severity WCAG 1.4.3 failure on a redundant confirmation label, root-caused to whole-card `opacity: 0.55` rather than to the red token.

Confirmed: `.sm-status-discarded` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1423-1426) uses bare `color: var(--status-error)` on `--status-error-soft`, and the AA guard's enforcement list (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) is Library-only, so shell.css is unchecked. The chip's ancestor `<li>` carries BOTH `filter: saturate(0.35)` (app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:80-82) and `opacity: 0.55` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1375-1377) (CandidateList.tsx:80, :113). Re-derived: naive 3.75:1 -> +saturate 2.84:1 -> +opacity 1.71:1; swapping to `--status-error-text` only reaches 2.25:1.

Correctly scoped: (a) the DOMINANT term is opacity, not the token — opacity alone gives 1.96:1, and a token-only fix still fails at 2.25:1, so this is not a token-consistency defect; (b) shell.css:1425 is one of ~33 bare `color: var(--status-error)` text sites repo-wide (jobqueue.css:150,211,293; providersKeys.css:135,270,386,521; setupStatus.css:62,81,136; shell.css:446,567,1222; views/shorts.css:49,384), i.e. an unfinished migration rather than a uniquely unguarded chip; (c) user impact is minimal because the state is redundantly encoded at higher contrast on the same card — the Reinstate/Discard button label reads 3.33:1 and the button set itself changes (CandidateList.tsx:197-206) — and `.sm-hook`, the clip content a user would need before reinstating, still measures 5.38:1 and PASSES AA.

The better-rooted finding on this surface is broader and is NOT a chip fix: `opacity: 0.55` applied to an interactive card also drags `.sm-times` (--text-faint) to 3.12:1 and button labels (--text-secondary) to 3.33:1. Fix by expressing "receded" via the surface/text ladder instead of group opacity, then extend the conformance guard to model ancestor filter/opacity — and finish the red-text token migration across all ~33 sites, not just this chip.

All figures analytic (spec-conformant sRGB saturate + source-over model that reproduces the repo's own 3.75:1 figure exactly); UNVERIFIED against a browser render because no e2e/visual test covers the discarded state (grep `discard` across app/e2e: no matches).

## The reframe "degraded" signal the sidecar emits explicitly for the UI has zero renderer consumer — a silent center-crop fallback
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `error-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Sidecar produces it and says why: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1171-1175` ("surface the per-clip reframe degraded signal (speaker tracking fell back to a center crop) so the UI can render a real/degraded badge") and puts it on the wire clip records at `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1319-1320`. Notice text is built at `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_claudeshorts.py:193-209` (`"reframe: speaker tracking unavailable ({reason}) — used center crop"`, comment at :187-189 "so the UI can show a real/degraded badge instead of the degrade being swallowed") and `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_multispeaker.py:882-894`. Renderer side: `app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:664-669` declares `ExportedClipInfo` as only `{path, fillersRemoved?, fillerSeconds?}`, and the render site `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:978-995` prints only path + filler stats. A repo-wide Grep for `reframeDegraded` matches ONLY `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py` and `sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py` — no `app/` hit. A Grep for `degrad` across `app/renderer/src` returns nothing reframe-related. The only other channel is `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1256-1261`, which emits the notice once per export as a `job.progress` message; `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:924` renders progress only while `busy && progress`, and `:691` sets `setProgress(null)` in the export `finally`, so the line is gone by the time the user reads the result.
- why: The whole point of the reframe phase is subject-following vertical crop. When tracking is lost the engine silently ships a dumb center crop — the exact outcome the sidecar's "WU-3 NO-SILENT-FALLBACK" contract was written to prevent — and the user gets a badly-framed short with no indication anything degraded. They will publish it believing tracking worked.
- fix: Add `reframeDegraded?: {type: string; message: string; reason: string}` to `ExportedClipInfo` (`app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:665`) and render a persistent per-clip badge in the exported-clips list (`ShortMaker.tsx:978-995`) and in the produced-shorts gallery, e.g. "Framing: center crop — subject tracking was lost (<reason>)", with a link to re-run that clip with a different engine. Pin it with a test the way the sidecar already pins it (`sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py:1129-1131`).
- ⚠ scope correction: The reframe "degraded" signal the sidecar emits explicitly for the UI has zero renderer consumer, so a per-clip reframe degrade reaches the user only as a progress line that is erased on completion.

Both producers route through one sink (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1035-1037) and land on the wire clip payload as clip["reframeDegraded"] (:1174-1175, :1319-1320), but they mean DIFFERENT things and only one is a center crop:
  - reframe_claudeshorts.make_degraded_notice (:193-209) — "speaker tracking unavailable ({reason}) — used center crop". This IS the dumb-center-crop outcome, fired at :1075 (detector raised) and :1081 (no trackable subject) on the DEFAULT engine ("auto" -> claudeshorts, shortmaker.py:1240). This is the high-severity case.
  - reframe_multispeaker.make_engine_degrade_notice (:882-894) — "multi-speaker engine unavailable ({reason}) — used the single-speaker tracker instead" (message at :108-110). Still real subject tracking, a quality downgrade, NOT a framing collapse. The repo marks the distinction at :885-888 and docs/WU-R1-MULTISPEAKER-ENGINE.md:85.

The renderer drops both: ExportedClipInfo (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:665-669) omits the field and the exported-clips list (ShortMaker.tsx:978-995) never reads it. No durable fallback exists — the persisted <clip>.json carries no degraded field (_write_short_metadata, shortmaker.py:860-887, and it runs at :1147 before the flag is set at :1174), so the produced-shorts gallery cannot show it; ShortMaker imports no toast; and the sole progress channel is gated on busy && progress (:924) then nulled in the export finally (:691) and the batch finally (:771). Affects both the manual export (:672) and the batch "Make N" flow (runBatch, :701-773) through the one render site; there is no separate "MakeShorts" component.

FIX (follows an existing in-repo precedent): add reframeDegraded?: {type: string; message: string; reason: string} to ExportedClipInfo (shortMakerLogic.ts:665) and render the sidecar's own message string as a persistent per-clip badge at ShortMaker.tsx:978-995 — rendering message verbatim keeps the center-crop vs single-speaker-tracker wording correct without the UI re-deriving it. Model it on ProducedShorts.tsx:43,217, which already renders a durable degrade note gated on phase === 'done' && degraded for the best-frame thumbnail degrade. To make the badge survive an app restart, also thread the flag into _shorts.build_metadata and move the _write_short_metadata call after the flag is computed. Pin it with a renderer test mirroring sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py:1129-1131 and the absent-case assertions at :1149-1150.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): The sidecar emits a per-clip `reframeDegraded` signal explicitly for the UI, and no renderer consumer exists — the degrade reason is also never persisted, so it is destroyed at job end.

Confirmed and correctly scoped: the sidecar produces the typed notice (`sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1171-1175`), puts it on the §2 wire payload (`:1317-1320`), and pins it with a test whose own comment calls that payload "the UI badge source" (`sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py:1130`). No renderer type or render site consumes it: `app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:665-669`, `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:978-995`, and `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:186-187` (which discards everything but `exported.length`). The only other channel is a single `job.progress` line that is overwritten by the next clip's progress message (`shortmaker.py:1283`) and cleared at `ShortMaker.tsx:691`. It is additionally NOT persisted — `shorts.py:64-` (`META_FIELDS`) and `:140-148` (`build_metadata`) omit it — so it cannot be recovered after the export.

This violates an owner-approved requirement: `docs/V1-GRILL-DECISIONS.md:105` and `:122` specify a "results grid w/ real/degraded badge".

The harm is MISATTRIBUTION AND NO RECOVERY PATH, not blind publication. Drop the claim "they will publish it believing tracking worked" — the clip is playable and a mis-framed talking-head crop is visible on playback, and `views/Shorts.tsx:282` does auto-generate a poster in the global gallery. What the user actually loses is the ability to tell "tracking failed on THIS clip because <reason>; try the multi-speaker engine" apart from "this app frames badly", plus the diagnostic reason is gone from disk. Severity is medium: no data loss, no security impact, output is inspectable, and a meaningful share of firings ("no trackable subject located" on genuine b-roll/screen recordings) are informational-only because center crop was the correct output there. It is still a real defect because the path is reachable on ordinary footage (`reframe_claudeshorts.py:1071-1082`, `MIN_SUBJECT_HIT_FRAC = 0.15` at `:100`), it is the app's marquee feature, and immediately post-export `features/ProducedShorts.tsx:160,182-188` shows only a ▶ glyph (it does not use `useShortThumbnail`, and export writes no poster), so nothing prompts the user to look.

The proposed fix is INCOMPLETE as written: adding `reframeDegraded?: {type; message; reason}` to `ExportedClipInfo` and rendering in `ShortMaker.tsx:978-995` covers the exported-clips list (and must also cover `MakeShorts.tsx:186`), but it CANNOT reach the produced-shorts gallery, because `ProducedShorts` is fed by `shorts.list` reconstructing from `<clip>.json` — that additionally requires adding the field to `build_metadata` and `META_FIELDS` in `sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py`. Note `ProducedShorts.tsx:217` already renders a `shorts__degrade-note`, but for the unrelated thumbnail best-frame degrade (`app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:170`), so the badge pattern exists and is cheap to mirror.

## Raw Python exception text — including absolute filesystem paths, env-var names and internal RPC method names — is the user-facing error copy for a failed reframe
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `error-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Wire: `sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:798-810` emits `job.done {result:{error:{message: str(exc), type: exc.__class__.__name__}}}` — the raw exception string, no mapping. Genuine job FAILURES are correctly distinguished (they `settleReject` at `_api.ts:279` -> `role="alert"`, pinned by MakeShorts.test.tsx:652-669), so three terminal states collapse, not four. Severity MEDIUM: misleading copy plus a stub `Save short` affordance (handleSaveShort is a no-op note at MakeShorts.tsx:145, stubbed for every outcome including success), no data loss, and the user knows they cancelled. Correct fix is at the SHARED layer only: make `waitForJobDone` return a discriminated terminal state (or reject with a `JobCancelledError` sibling to `JobAbortedError`, _api.ts:70-75) so every one of its ~10 call sites can branch cancel / unconfirmed / empty-success, and gate `setTrayOpen(true)` on `exported.length > 0`. - ⚠ scope correction: Cancelling an in-flight `shortmaker.export` from the app-global Jobs drawer is reported as a SUCCESS on the Make Shorts front door: the sidecar's cancel emits a terminal `job.done` carrying `{"error":{"type":"JobCancelled"}}` (sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:793-796, reached via shortmaker.py:1275 → jobs.py:720-721), the shared wait maps that to `null` (app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:275-278), and MakeShorts collapses it with `clips ?? []` into `"Exported 0 clip(s) from your ranges."` rendered in the `role="status"` success channel (MakeShorts.tsx:186-188, :275) while also opening the Output Tray (`setTrayOpen(true)`). The SAME string is the outcome for a missing `onJobDone` channel and for an unrecognised payload — both deliberately pinned by tests at MakeShorts.test.tsx:682-691 and :693-701 — so cancel, bridge anomaly, and a genuine zero-clip result are indistinguishable. The defect is NOT specific to MakeShorts and is NOT caused by the missing AbortSignal: the sibling AI flow collapses identically on a drawer cancel (ShortMaker.tsx:671-672, `ctrl.signal.aborted` is false because only its in-view Cancel at :787-800 aborts the controller) and additionally records bogus `'exported'` feedback at :675-677. Severity is MEDIUM, not high: the tray's "Save short" is an inert stub (MakeShorts.tsx:145 sets a note only; OutputTray.tsx:139-143 renders the button merely because a handler is passed), so nothing is written to disk and no state is corrupted — the cost is a misleading message and a redundant re-run. The fix must therefore distinguish the terminal states in the SHARED wait (a `JobCancelledError` sibling to `JobAbortedError`, or a discriminated result) so BOTH MakeShorts and ShortMaker branch correctly, not just thread an AbortController into MakeShorts.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): A manual export cancelled from the app-global Jobs drawer settles as an affirmative status. MakeShorts.tsx:186-188 collapses waitForJobDone's JobCancelled->null (_api.ts:275-278, re-exported at shortMakerLogic.ts:22,24) onto `?? []`, renders "Exported 0 clip(s) from your ranges." in the SUCCESS channel (role="status", MakeShorts.tsx:274-278, versus role="alert" at :269-273) and opens the Output Tray (:279-286). Because this surface renders no Cancel affordance (MakeShorts.tsx:268 passes only onSubmit/busy), the drawer is the only cancel route, so this is the default cancel experience.

Severity is MEDIUM, not high: no data loss, crash, or corruption. The tray is clip-agnostic and never receives or displays a path (OutputTray.tsx:22-30,41-56,133-149), and this surface's save handlers are note-only stubs (MakeShorts.tsx:145-146), so "Save short" performs NO file operation - it only fabricates "Saved the short." The state is fully recoverable by re-running the export.

Three framings in the original do not hold:

Its AbortController is aborted only by its own in-view Cancel button (ShortMaker.tsx:778), so on a drawer cancel ctrl.signal.aborted is false at ShortMaker.tsx:671 and it hits the identical `?? []` collapse at :672 - and additionally records false 'exported' feedback labels for every approved candidate at :675-676 (a real data-quality harm). The defect is SYSTEMIC to the JobCancelled-null collapse, not specific to the Make Shorts front door.
(2) The "no onJobDone channel" sibling path is NOT production-reachable: app/main/preload.ts:154,292 exposes onJobDone as a required bridge member, so _api.ts:236-238 is test-stub-only. Only the cancel path and the malformed-payload path are live.

Citation corrections: the two pinned tests are at MakeShorts.test.tsx:683-691 and :693-701 (the cited :625-634 and :636-644 are unmount-guard and happy-path tests); export's job start is shortmaker.py:1444-1445 (:1362 is the select handler).
