## Sidecar death mid-batch leaves the Batch queue permanently "Running" — no timeout, no supervisor-status subscription
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:127-154` — the live batch has exactly two channels: `onProgress` (:128, gated to `parentJobIdRef`) and `onJobDone` (:150). Both are sidecar-emitted, so neither can fire once the sidecar process dies.
`app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:11-20` imports only `onJobDone, onProgress` from `../lib/rpc`. That barrel (`app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/index.ts:4-6` → `lib/rpc/client.ts`) exports `onProgress` (client.ts:115), `onJobDone` (:120), `onProxyState` (:130) and **no `onSidecarStatus` wrapper at all** — even though the preload bridge exposes it (`app/main/preload.ts:185`, `:324`). The batch surface has no wired path to the signal.
The canonical fix exists twice elsewhere and is explicitly labelled: `app/renderer/src/components/useJob.ts:279-295` ("v1.5 crash fix … fail the job instead of leaving the panel spinning forever") and `app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:286-292` ("The sidecar stopped mid-job; please retry."). BatchQueue uses neither — and unlike every other deferred-job surface it also has **no timeout ceiling** (contrast `_api.ts:62` `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS = 35*60*1000` + `_api.ts:293-302`).
Why it never self-heals: `app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:41-45` — "a transition AWAY from 'running' … means the sidecar PROCESS died, so any job that was in flight in it is gone — a fresh sidecar never resumes it." The parent job's `job.done` never arrives; `sidecar/media_studio/__main__.py:124-125` confirms an interrupted job is rehydrated as INTERRUPTED and "never auto-restarted".
The global banner does not compensate: `app/renderer/src/components/SidecarBanner.tsx:155` returns `null` the instant the supervisor is back to 'running', so after an auto-restart the only on-screen state is a batch claiming to be Running.
- why: A batch run is the longest operation in the app (30+ sources, potentially an hour). After a sidecar crash the panel keeps showing `ProgressBar pct` frozen at its last value (BatchQueue.tsx:343) and every row rendering "Running" (repurposeLogic.ts:91-92), with no `role="alert"` error. A user's only rational read is "still working" — so they wait indefinitely on a run that is dead. Mitigation, disclosed: the Jobs drawer does surface the parent as `interrupted` with a Resume button (`sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:82-94`, `app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:36-42`), so recovery is possible — but on a different surface that now actively contradicts this one.
- fix: Export an `onSidecarStatus` wrapper from `lib/rpc/client.ts` alongside `onProgress`/`onJobDone`, then in BatchQueue subscribe to it and, when a non-'running' status arrives while `parentJobIdRef.current !== ''`, clear the parent jobId and `setError('The sidecar stopped mid-batch — resume the run to continue.')` plus flip the local `batch.status` off 'running'. Mirror `useJob.ts:287-293` exactly. Additionally add a last-resort ceiling (reuse `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`) armed on `batch.start`/`batch.resume` and disarmed on the parent `job.done`, so a wedged-but-alive sidecar also settles.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): Sidecar death mid-batch leaves the Batch queue panel showing a frozen ProgressBar and "Running" rows with no in-panel error, because BatchQueue subscribes only to onProgress (BatchQueue.tsx:127-134) and onJobDone (:149-154) — both sidecar-emitted, neither able to fire after the process dies (ipc.ts:105 vs :115) — and no onSidecarStatus wrapper is exported from lib/rpc/client.ts, unlike the crash fix already shipped at useJob.ts:279-295 and _api.ts:286-292. It also has no timeout ceiling (contrast _api.ts:62). Scope corrections: the panel is not the ONLY contradicting on-screen state — the always-visible header Jobs pill loses its count and amber pulse within ~5s (App.tsx:546-559 via useActiveJobs.ts:14,17-19), and a tab bounce surfaces an in-panel "Incomplete batches" Resume row (BatchQueue.tsx:268-284 + repurposeLogic.ts:173). The transient role="alert" banner (SidecarBanner.tsx:160) is a sub-second flash, since sidecar.ts:324 emits 'running' on spawn with a 250ms backoff. No data is lost and recovery is available (batch.py:448,464,474,481-482,489-490); the harm is wasted wall-clock on the app's longest operation plus a misleading UI, and the gap is untested (BatchQueue.test.tsx has no sidecar/timeout coverage). Crash frequency is UNVERIFIED.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped version (severity: LOW, category: error-surfacing/cosmetic — not "permanently Running with no recovery path"): After a sidecar crash and successful auto-restart, BatchQueue DOES receive a synthetic terminal job.done (sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:530-541) and DOES re-read the authoritative checkpoint via its ungated onJobDone listener (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:150 -> refreshBatch -> client.batch.status). Two narrow gaps remain: (1) BatchQueue DISCARDS the event payload — onJobDone(() => {...}) at BatchQueue.tsx:150 ignores its argument, so the JobInterrupted message ("job interrupted by restart") is never surfaced and no role="alert" explanation appears in the panel; and (2) the durable checkpoint deliberately persists the interrupted source as status "running" (batch.py:448) because that IS the crash marker resume keys off (batch.py:474 _RESUMABLE_STATUSES, :481-482 "a running item is a source the crash interrupted mid-flight"). Net user-visible result: the aggregate ProgressBar stops advancing and exactly ONE row keeps reading "Running" while the tail reads "Queued", with no inline explanation until the user switches tabs and back — which then surfaces the batch in BatchQueue's own "Incomplete batches" list with a Resume button (BatchQueue.tsx:268-284). Correctly-scoped fix (much smaller than proposed): read the DoneEvent argument already delivered at BatchQueue.tsx:150, and when its result carries a JobInterrupted error for the tracked parentJobIdRef, setError('The sidecar stopped mid-batch — resume the run to continue.') and clear parentJobIdRef. Optionally re-run reload() there so the same-panel Resume affordance appears without requiring a tab switch. Subscribing to a new onSidecarStatus wrapper is NOT required (the signal already arrives), and the proposed renderer-side DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling is largely redundant with the sidecar's own 30-min watchdog (rpc.py:39-43), which force-finishes a wedged-but-alive handler with a job.done ERROR that the same ungated listener already catches.
- ⚠ scope correction: Sidecar death mid-batch leaves the Batch queue showing "Running" indefinitely. BatchQueue has no `onSidecarStatus` subscription (the `lib/rpc/client.ts` barrel exports no such wrapper — client.ts:115-134 — even though `app/main/preload.ts:185` exposes it) and no timeout ceiling (contrast `_api.ts:62` DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS + `_api.ts:293-302`). CORRECTION to the mechanism: it is NOT true that no event arrives. `sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:530-541` emits a synthetic terminal `job.done` with `{error:{type:'JobInterrupted'}}` for every rehydrated interrupted job on restart, and BatchQueue's `onJobDone` (BatchQueue.tsx:150) is UNGATED by jobId, so it fires and calls `refreshBatch`. The panel still fails to settle because (a) BatchQueue.tsx:150 discards the DoneEvent and never reads its error payload — unlike `useJob.ts:260` / `_api.ts:272` which call `extractJobError`; and (b) the refresh returns 'running' again: `features/batch.py:448` durably persists the in-flight item as `status="running"`, no BatchStore re-mark happens at startup (`batch.py:474` only treats it as crashed at resume time), `derive_status` (`batch.py:186-187`) maps any running item to aggregate 'running', and `_merge_live_status` (`batch.py:714-722`) leaves the aggregate alone since `_parent_jobs` is in-memory only (`batch.py:772-775`). `announceTransitions` (BatchQueue.tsx:388) then skips the unchanged items, so there is no `role="alert"` and pct stays frozen (BatchQueue.tsx:343). Cheapest correct fix: read the `DoneEvent` in BatchQueue's onJobDone via `extractJobError` and settle on `type==='JobInterrupted'`; additionally subscribe to `onSidecarStatus` (mirroring `useJob.ts:287-293`) to cover the 'down' case where no restart ever emits the synthetic done, plus a `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` ceiling for a wedged-but-alive sidecar.

## Export-presets table has no length-absorption and no horizontal scroll container — Save/Delete are pushed off-screen
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `i18n-length` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:199-222` renders an 8-column `<table className="export-presets__table">`; each row (`ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:39-112`) puts 2 free-text inputs (`:41`, `:48`), 3 number inputs (`:55`, `:63`, `:71`), 2 selects (`:79`, `:92`) and a Save+Delete cell (`:104-111`) side by side. There is ZERO CSS for `.export-presets*` — `Grep '.batch|export-presets|template-editor|batch-consent'` over `**/*.{css,scss,less}` returns "No matches found", and `Grep '^table|table\b.*\{|overflow-x'` over `**/*.css` returns exactly ONE hit: `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:37`, scoped to `.workspace .tabbar` (`workspace.css:36`). This surface is not inside `.workspace`: it mounts as `.make-shorts__panel` (`app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:201`) → `.repurpose__panel` (`app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:29-34`), and neither class has any CSS rule (`Grep 'make-shorts__panel'` and `Grep 'repurpose'` over `*.css` → no matches; `Grep 'overflow'` over `app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css` → no matches). Because `.export-presets` is not `.feature-panel`, the shared input rule at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:451-469` never applies, so every input keeps its UA-default `size=20` intrinsic width (~150px each). Available stage width is the 1280px window minus the fixed 200px rail (`app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:16`) = 1080px, and `app/main/main.ts:1038-1041` allows the user down to `minWidth: 940` = ~740px stage. Estimated table min-content ≈ 1150px (5×~150px inputs + ~85px + ~155px selects + ~100px actions + `<td>`/border-spacing overhead) — UNVERIFIED at runtime (no measurement taken; figures are Chromium UA-default estimates), but the ordering (min-content > 1080px) holds under any plausible input-width value and is certain at the 940px minWidth.
- why: The last column holds the only Save and Delete controls for an export preset. With no `overflow-x: auto` anywhere in the ancestor chain, the overflow escapes to the document, so the user must horizontally scroll the ENTIRE app shell (bar + rail included, since `.app` is `height:100%` at `shell.css:70-79` with no overflow) to reach them — or cannot reach them at all at narrower widths. Any label growth (a localized `<th>`, a longer engine id) is entirely unabsorbed because there is no `table-layout`, no column widths, and no input width.
- fix: Add an `.export-presets__table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; }` container (or `.export-presets { overflow-x: auto; }`), plus `.export-presets__table { table-layout: fixed; width: 100%; }` with explicit per-column `width`/`min-width`, and `.export-presets__row input, .export-presets__row select { width: 100%; min-width: 0; }` so the fields shrink instead of forcing the table wide. Give `.repurpose__panel` / `.make-shorts__panel` `min-width: 0; overflow: auto;` so the Batch surface scrolls inside the stage rather than the whole shell.
- ⚠ scope correction: Export-presets table has no length-absorption and no horizontal-scroll container, so Save/Delete render off-viewport at the app's default window size. MEASURED in Chromium against the real cascade (two independent harnesses agreeing): table min-content = 1195px vs a 1080px stage at the default-and-only launch geometry 1280x820 (app/main/main.ts:1038-1041; app/main has zero maximize/windowState/setBounds), putting Save's right edge at 1381px and Delete's at 1392px — both outside the 1280px viewport, with hit-testing at Save's position returning the engine <td>. There is no `.export-presets` CSS anywhere (repo-wide grep over **/*.{css,scss,less,html} for export-presets|table-layout|overflow-x yields exactly one hit, app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:37, scoped to `.workspace .tabbar`), and every ancestor computes overflow-x: visible, so the overflow escapes to the document and the user must horizontally scroll the ENTIRE app shell (bar + 200px rail included) to reach the only Save/Delete controls for a preset. Because the draft is row-local useState (ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:27) resynced by the useEffect at :30-32, an edit made without reaching Save is silently discarded. This is NOT an i18n-length risk: it reproduces with the shipped English seed data (sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:168-192) and needs no localization — label growth only widens an already-overflowing table. Scope corrections vs the original: the controls remain reachable by document scroll at every width tested including the 940px minWidth (documentElement.scrollWidth 1395 > clientWidth; html/body overflow-x = visible), so "cannot reach them at all" is false; and the defect has TWO live mounts — Make Shorts -> Batch (MakeShorts.tsx:213 -> Repurpose.tsx:37) and Deliver -> Platform presets (Deliver.tsx:72, under .deliver-view__panel whose only rule is min-width:0 at deliver.css:91-93) — so any fix must cover .deliver-view__panel as well as .repurpose__panel/.make-shorts__panel. No e2e or visual baseline opens this tab, so CI cannot catch it.
- ⚠ scope correction: Export-presets table has no length-absorption and no horizontal scroll container — Save/Delete are pushed off-screen at the default window size, on BOTH surfaces that host the panel.

MEASURED at the default 1280x820 window (main/main.ts:1038-1041): stage width 1080px, table width 1197.4px, overflow 117.4px; the Save and Delete buttons' right edges land at 1384.9px and 1394.4px, i.e. ~115px beyond the 1280px viewport. At the 940px minWidth the overflow is 457.4px. Column widths are 179|179|179|179|179|73|153|58.4.

overflow-x computes 'visible' on every ancestor from the table up through section.export-presets -> .repurpose__panel -> .repurpose -> .make-shorts__panel -> .make-shorts -> main.app__main -> .app -> body, so the overflow escapes to the document: documentElement.scrollWidth 1397 vs clientWidth 1280. The user must horizontally scroll the ENTIRE app shell (bar + rail included) to reach Save/Delete. CORRECTION to the original wording: they are never unreachable — the document scroll exists at every allowed width, including 940px — so drop 'or cannot reach them at all at narrower widths'.

SCOPE (broader than originally reported): the panel mounts on Make Shorts -> BATCH (Repurpose.tsx:37, via .make-shorts__panel at MakeShorts.tsx:206-211 -> .repurpose__panel at Repurpose.tsx:29-34) and ALSO on the Deliver rail destination (Deliver.tsx:72, inside .deliver-view__panel at deliver.css:91-93), where .deliver-view's padding: var(--space-5) (deliver.css:3-8) narrows the stage further and worsens the overflow. Not 'gallery'.

CAUSE (corrected): nothing anywhere sets a width — there is no .export-presets CSS at all (Grep over **/*.css => No matches; panels.css, imported at ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:18, has no such rule), no table-layout, no column widths, no input/select width, and no overflow-x container (the renderer's only overflow-x:auto is workspace.css:37, scoped to '.workspace .tabbar'). It is NOT that shell.css:451-469 fails to match: that rule sets no width at all (only appearance/padding/background/border/radius/color/font/transition), so if it DID apply the table would be wider still. Consequently any label growth (a localized <th>, a longer engine id such as 'reframe_multispeaker') is entirely unabsorbed.

Additionally, shell.css:319-320's comment asserting that min-width:0 on .app__main prevents 'a wide child (a table, the timeline) forcing horizontal overflow of the whole shell' is measurably incomplete: it stops the 1fr grid track from expanding but the shell still h-scrolls (.app scrollWidth 1397 vs clientWidth 1280).
- ⚠ scope correction: The Export-presets table has no length-absorption and no horizontal scroll container, so at the SHIPPED DEFAULT window size its Save/Delete cell is rendered off-screen and is reachable only by horizontally scrolling the entire app shell.

MEASURED (Chromium, real CSS chain): `app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:199` renders the renderer's only `<table>` — 8 columns (`:202-209`), each row (`:39-112`) holding 2 text inputs (`:41`,`:48`) and 3 number inputs (`:55`,`:63`,`:71`) at 177px each (UA `width:177px`, `min-width:0`), a 71px and a 151px select (`:79`,`:92`), and the Save+Delete cell (`:104-111`). Table min-content = 1195px. Stage = 1080px at the default 1280x820 window (`app/main/main.ts:1038-1039` minus the 200px rail at `app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:16`) → 115px overflow, Delete's right edge at x=1392 vs a 1280 viewport. At the 940px minWidth (`main.ts:1040`) the stage is 740px and the overflow is 455px.

CAUSE: there is no CSS for `.export-presets*` at all (Grep over `*.css` → no matches), no `table` selector anywhere in the app, no `table-layout`, no column widths and no input width — so nothing absorbs the min-content. This is independent of the `.feature-panel` scoping of the shared input rule at `components/shell.css:451-469`: measured, forcing that rule to apply still leaves the table at 1161px with Delete off-stage.

CONTAINMENT: every ancestor from the table to `<body>` computes `overflow-x: visible`; the only `overflow-x` in the corpus is `views/workspace.css:37`, scoped to `.workspace .tabbar` (`:36`), which is not in this chain. `html/body/#root` (`shell.css:9-19`) and `.app` (`shell.css:70-79`) set no overflow either, so the overflow propagates to the document: measured `scrollWidth 1395` vs `clientWidth 1280`, and scrolling fully right drags the app bar and the nav rail off-screen with it. Because nothing clips, the controls are always reachable by that document scroll (and Tab auto-scrolls them into view) — they are never unreachable, but there is no in-panel scroll affordance.

SCOPE: two surfaces, not one — Make Shorts → Batch → Export presets (`views/MakeShorts.tsx:206-213` `.make-shorts__panel` → `views/Repurpose.tsx:29-37` `.repurpose__panel`, neither class having any CSS rule) AND the Deliver rail (`App.tsx:495` → `views/Deliver.tsx:72` under `.deliver-view__panel`, whose only rule is `min-width: 0` at `views/deliver.css:91-93`).

LENS: this is a layout/reflow defect present in en-US at the default window size, not an i18n-length one — `app/package.json` carries no i18n dependency and all labels are hardcoded English literals. Localized `<th>` labels or a longer engine id would widen it further, since `table-layout: auto` passes every added character straight into the table width.

FIX (measured to resolve it): `.export-presets__table { table-layout: fixed; width: 100%; }` plus `.export-presets__row input, .export-presets__row select { width: 100%; min-width: 0; }` brings the table to exactly 1080px with 0 overflow and Delete inside the stage; add an `overflow-x: auto` wrapper so the residual min-content at the 740px minWidth stage scrolls inside the panel rather than in the document. Apply to both mounts.

## SemanticSearch reports a FAILED index.build as success — job.done error payload is never inspected
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:79-85 hand-rolls the terminal-job wait:
```
const offDone = api.onJobDone
  ? api.onJobDone((ev) => {
      if (ev.jobId !== jobId) return;
      setBuilt(true);
      setBuild(null);
    })
  : () => undefined;
```
There is no `extractJobError(ev.result)` branch. The A3 failure payload is `result:{error:{message,type}}` — emitted by `sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py` `_finish_error`, and synthetically on restart at `sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:537-541` (`{"error":{"message":"job interrupted by restart","type":"JobInterrupted"}}`). The build body can raise: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/vision_ops.py:522` `vectors = embedder.embed(corpus)` (CloudEmbedder network/key failure, LocalEmbedder missing weights). Every sibling panel routes through the shared reader that DOES handle it — `app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:272-281` rejects on `extractJobError`. `startBuild`'s try/catch (SemanticSearch.tsx:105-107) only covers the *start* rpc rejection, not the terminal notification. The test suite pins only the success payload (app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.test.tsx:224-228) — no error-payload case exists.
- why: A cloud-embedder failure, a missing local embedding model, or a sidecar crash+restart mid-build all land as `built = true` with the progress region cleared and no `role="alert"`. The user is told the semantic index exists; the search box enables; the next search then fails against a nonexistent/partial index with an unrelated downstream message ("run index.build to rebuild it first"). The actual cause is never surfaced anywhere in the UI.
- fix: Replace the hand-rolled `onJobDone` subscription with the shared `waitForJobDone(getApi(), jobId, (r) => r, DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS, signal)` from `features/_api.ts` (as Transcribe/Convert/Dub/Refine/Diarize/Recipes already do), setting `built` only on the resolve path and `setError(...)` on the reject path. Minimal alternative: add `const failure = extractJobError(ev.result); if (failure) { setBuild(null); setError(failure.message); return; }` before `setBuilt(true)`.
- ⚠ scope correction: SemanticSearch's hand-rolled onJobDone subscription (app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:79-85) sets built=true for ANY terminal job.done matching its build jobId, including the A3 failure payload result:{error:{message,type}}. A cloud-embedder failure (models/embedder.py:116-152 EmbedderError, raised from vision_ops.py:522 inside the unguarded work body at models/ai_job.py:338 -> jobs.py:722-724 _finish_error), an index-write failure (vision_ops.py:534), or a sidecar crash+restart (jobs.py:537-541 JobInterrupted) therefore lands as built=true with the progress region cleared and NO role="alert" — the actual cause is discarded, and no other surface recovers it (useJob.ts:255-275 handles error payloads but only for its own activeJobId, and SemanticSearch does not use useJob). The next search then reports vision_ops.py:646 "video <id> has no semantic index yet (run index.build first)", contradicting the enabled search box. Scope corrections to the original write-up: (1) SemanticSearch is NOT the only hand-rolled site — ProducedShorts.tsx:106-107, BatchQueue.tsx:150, ShortMaker.tsx:418 and panels/DirectorPanel.tsx:288 also subscribe without extractJobError; only the six panels named in the fix section (Transcribe/Convert/Dub/Refine/Diarize/Recipes) use the shared waitForJobDone. (2) "missing local embedding model" is not a real failure mode — LocalEmbedder (embedder.py:209-237) is a pure sha256 hash with no model file and no I/O. (3) The index is never "partial" and the downstream message is vision_ops.py:646, not the dim-mismatch string at vision_ops.py:710. (4) Severity is MEDIUM, not high: the false built self-corrects on the next mount because Workspace.tsx:292-293 conditionally mounts the panel and SemanticSearch.tsx:52-66 re-probes index.status, and SemanticSearch.tsx:186-190 always offers Rebuild — the durable loss is the error message, not access. The proposed fix (route through waitForJobDone from _api.ts, or add the extractJobError guard before setBuilt) is correct as written, and a job.done error-payload test is genuinely absent (SemanticSearch.test.tsx pins only the success payload at :226-231).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): SemanticSearch's hand-rolled onJobDone (app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:79-85) never inspects the job.done error payload, so a failed index.build renders as success -- built=true, progress cleared, no role="alert" -- for any failure inside work() (vision_ops.py:516-522: embedder resolution, cloud network/key, missing local weights) or a sidecar crash+restart (jobs.py:537-541). The shared reader used by every sibling panel handles this (_api.ts:270-283, e.g. Transcribe.tsx:94), and no build-error test exists (SemanticSearch.test.tsx:224-233). User-visible consequence: the next search returns "video <id> has no semantic index yet (run index.build first)" (vision_ops.py:646) -- contradicting the panel's own success claim -- and the failure CAUSE is rendered on no surface, so a persistent embedder failure loops with no diagnostic. Severity is MEDIUM rather than high because (a) the FACT of failure is discoverable in the Jobs panel, which shows status "error" plus a Retry button (JobQueue.tsx:32,213-214), though not the message (JobInfo has no error field -- schemas.ts:1311-1318); (b) the false built state self-corrects on panel remount via the index.status re-probe (SemanticSearch.tsx:52-66 + vision_ops.py:599-601); (c) a "Rebuild index" affordance exists (SemanticSearch.tsx:186-190); and (d) there is no data loss, corruption, or security impact in this single-user local app, and semantic search is an auxiliary feature. The proposed fix (route through waitForJobDone, or add the extractJobError branch) remains correct and is ~4 lines against an already-proven shared helper.

## ShortsGalleryModal declares aria-modal="true" but does not contain focus, hide the background, or restore focus — the repo's own useFocusTrap is unused here
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `axe-a11y` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:75-81 renders `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label={...}`. Its only focus handling is a one-shot callback ref that focuses the close button, app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47, and an Escape handler bound to the (non-focusable) dialog div, app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63-68 wired at :80. There is no Tab/Shift+Tab containment, no `inert`/`aria-hidden` applied to the Library behind it, and no focus restore on unmount.

The shared fix already exists and is used by every other dialog: app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:53, consumed at app/renderer/src/components/FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, app/renderer/src/components/DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45 and app/renderer/src/components/ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44. The hook's header, app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:1-14, describes this exact defect verbatim: dialogs that "set role=\"dialog\" + aria-modal but ... did nothing to keep keyboard focus inside: Tab walked straight out into the page behind them, Escape did nothing, and focus was never restored".

The modal is rendered inline as the last child of `.library` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:606-615), i.e. inside `<main role="tabpanel">` (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:565-570), so the whole Library grid stays in the tab order behind it.
- why: Concrete failure: open a card's "N shorts" gallery, press Shift+Tab once from the close button — focus lands on a Library card's Remove button behind the "modal". Escape now does nothing (the handler only fires via bubbling from a dialog descendant), so a keyboard-only user is stranded with a dialog they cannot dismiss. Because `aria-modal="true"` makes VoiceOver and JAWS virtual-cursor prune everything outside the dialog subtree, a screen-reader user can move DOM focus onto controls the AT reports as non-existent, and activating them mutates the library invisibly. Closing the modal also drops focus to `<body>` instead of the "N shorts" button that opened it (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order, Level A). axe has no rule for any of this, which is why the green a11y gate says nothing.
- fix: Swap the ad-hoc ref for the shared hook in app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx: `const trapRef = useFocusTrap<HTMLDivElement>({ onEscape: onClose, initialFocus: '.shorts-modal__close' })`, attach `ref={trapRef}` to the `.shorts-modal` div, and delete the `focusOnOpen` callback (:45-47) and the local `onKeyDown` (:63-68). That buys Tab containment, Escape, and focus restore in one line. Additionally either portal the dialog to `document.body` and mark `.app` `inert` while it is open, or drop `aria-modal="true"` so the exposed tree stops contradicting what is actually focusable.
- ⚠ scope correction: NOT an overclaim — the headline stands as written and needs no rescoping. The only wording I would narrow is one sentence in WHY IT MATTERS, offered as a precision fix rather than a refutation: replace "a keyboard-only user is stranded with a dialog they cannot dismiss" with "Escape is dead while focus sits behind the dialog; because the modal is rendered AFTER the card list in DOM order (Library.tsx:606-615), the user can Tab forward to re-enter the dialog and dismiss it — the state is recoverable but silent and tedious, not a permanent trap." Everything else — the aria-modal/focusability contradiction, the absent Tab containment, the absent background hiding, the absent focus restore, the unused shared useFocusTrap, and the silent green gate — is confirmed at the cited lines.
- ⚠ scope correction: ShortsGalleryModal (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:76-78) declares role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" but implements none of the three behaviours the attribute promises: no Tab/Shift+Tab containment, no inert/aria-hidden on the Library behind it, and no focus restore (the callback ref at :45-47 no-ops on unmount because node is null). The repo's own useFocusTrap.ts:53 — whose header at :3-6 describes this exact defect — is consumed by all 3 other aria-modal dialogs (FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45, ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44) and is the sole missing piece here.

Severity: MEDIUM, not high. Correctly-scoped consequence: with the modal open (live path — App.tsx:518-522 wires it), one Shift+Tab from the close button moves focus to the last Library card's Remove button (LibraryCard.tsx:159-166), which sits behind the backdrop and invisible; Tab order equals document order because no positive tabIndex exists in app/renderer/src. Escape is then dead, because the handler at :63-68 is a React onKeyDown on the dialog div and the card is a sibling subtree. Enter there calls handleRemove (Library.tsx:368-378) with NO confirmation, and library.remove deletes that video's project manifest and thumbnail from disk (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/composition.py:95) — source media is untouched.

Drop the "stranded with a dialog they cannot dismiss" claim: the modal is the LAST focusable subtree inside `.library` (Library.tsx:606-615), so one Tab-forward returns focus to .shorts-modal__close and Enter closes it. This is a disorienting excursion onto invisible destructive controls plus a WCAG 2.4.3 (Level A) focus-restore failure, not a keyboard trap. Mouse users are entirely unaffected (backdrop click at :71 and the close button both dismiss).

Two additions to the evidence: the existing Escape test (ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:150-165) dispatches the keydown on the dialog element itself and therefore cannot detect this; and the a11y e2e gate (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:56-60) never opens the modal, so the green gate is silent for a structural reason independent of axe's rule set.

## Refine: a stale in-flight preview lands after invalidation and re-enables Apply with parameters that match none of the displayed numbers
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `loading-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/Refine.tsx:95-111 — `preview()` closes over `params` and unconditionally does `setPlan(extractPlan(res))` when the RPC resolves; there is no request-id guard and no AbortController. :90-93 `invalidatePreview()` clears the plan on any knob change, but the knobs (:192-230) are never disabled while `previewing` is true, and the file's own comment at :86-89 claims this 'prevents Apply from silently writing a cut that differs from every displayed number'.

EXECUTED PROBE (temporary vitest file, since deleted), logged output:
  in-flight: any progress element = 0 · role=status count = 0 · aria-busy count = 0
  in-flight: preview btn label = "Previewing…" · knobs disabled? minSilence = false
  after retune: Apply disabled = true          <- invalidation works
  after STALE resolve: Apply disabled = false  <- stale plan re-enables it
  after STALE resolve: displayed silenceRemovedSec = 12
  preview was called with minSilenceSec = 0.6
  apply was called with minSilenceSec = 2.5
- why: `refine.preview` runs ffmpeg silencedetect over the whole video, so the in-flight window is long — and its only feedback is a button label (0 progress elements, 0 role=status, 0 aria-busy), which invites the user to fiddle with the knobs while waiting. Doing so produces an Apply that writes a new *.refined.mp4 using 2.5s min-silence while every stat on screen was computed at 0.6s. The panel's whole 'see before you cut' promise is void, and the file it writes is not the cut that was previewed.
- fix: Scope the response to the request that produced it: capture a monotonically increasing request id (or an AbortController) in `preview()` and drop/abort the result if `params` changed since dispatch. Separately, give the in-flight preview a real indicator — an indeterminate `role="status"` + `aria-busy` region (or an elapsed counter) next to the button, and disable the tuning knobs while `previewing` so the stale-input path cannot be entered at all.
- ⚠ scope correction: Refine: a preview response is applied unconditionally, so a stale in-flight preview that lands AFTER a mid-flight knob change re-enables Apply — and Apply then dispatches the CURRENT knob values while the displayed plan stats and keep-list are the ones computed from the SUPERSEDED values.

Scope: reachable only in the mid-flight-retune window (user edits a knob between the Preview dispatch and its resolution). On the settled path the invalidation at Refine.tsx:90-93 holds correctly — Apply re-disables and the stats vanish (proven by control). The window is real, not theoretical: refine.preview runs a whole-file `ffmpeg silencedetect` decode pass (sidecar/media_studio/features/boundary.py:481-492) with no bound, and the only in-flight affordance is the button label ("Previewing…"); the panel emits 0 progress elements, 0 role=status, 0 aria-busy, 0 aria-live while previewing, and none of the five knobs (Refine.tsx:165-230) is disabled. This violates the invariant the file itself asserts at Refine.tsx:88-89.

Impact: Apply writes a new *.refined.mp4 whose cut does not match the previewed plan on screen. Non-destructive (original untouched, refine.py:363) and recoverable by re-previewing, so severity is medium-high rather than unqualified high.

Fix: scope the response to the request that produced it — a monotonic request id or an AbortController in preview(), dropping the result if params changed since dispatch (the abortRef pattern already used at Transcribe.tsx:49-52 and ShortMaker.tsx:212). Separately, add a real in-flight indicator (role="status" + aria-busy) next to the button. Do NOT disable the knobs — that is unnecessary once the guard exists and would lock the UI for the length of a full-file ffmpeg pass.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW (display-consistency, not correctness): if the user changes a Refine knob while a preview is in flight, the stale preview resolves and repopulates the stats/keep-list panel (app/renderer/src/features/Refine.tsx:104-105) with numbers computed from the superseded parameter set, re-enabling Apply (:245). The written file is NOT wrong — refine.apply re-derives the plan server-side from the current params (sidecar/media_studio/features/refine.py:353, sent at Refine.tsx:81-84,123) and writes a new {stem}.refined.mp4 leaving the original untouched (refine.py:363) — so the mismatch is between two on-screen surfaces (fresh knob values at :198/:211/:223 versus stale derived stats at :275-296), not between intent and output. Worst realistic cost is one wasted re-encode (refine.py:364-366) plus a re-preview; no data loss, fully recoverable, and only one stale variant is reachable because :237 disables the preview button while previewing. Two cheap fixes: (a) bump a generation counter in invalidatePreview (:90-93) and drop a resolved preview whose generation is stale; (b) stop discarding the authoritative plan the apply job already returns — refine.py:371-373 ships {plan, stats} in job.done, but Refine.tsx:129-130 extracts only `path`, so feeding it into setPlan would self-heal the display after every apply. Add the missing regression test alongside Refine.test.tsx:381,404. An indeterminate role="status"/aria-busy region during preview is a reasonable a11y nicety, but note refine.preview is a direct RPC that emits no progress (refine.py:311-324), so a determinate progress bar is not available by design.

## Library "Remove" destroys the video's project/edit manifest and force-evicts its keep-a-copy with no confirmation and no undo
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:159-166 renders a bare `Remove` button wired straight to `onRemove`; app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:368-384 calls `rpc('library.remove',{id})` immediately (only an optimistic list splice, no prompt); app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:398-414 (`removeSelected`) does the same for N videos at once. Downstream that RPC is not a de-index: sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:145-146 unlinks the per-video project manifest (`projects_dir/<id>.json`) and the poster, and sidecar/media_studio/library.py:343-345 calls `self.managed_evict(video_id, force=True)`. The manifest is the user's edit state — sidecar/media_studio/library.py:499-500 documents it as `{"tracks":[...], "clips":[...], "audioTracks":[...], "settings":{...}}`. The `force=True` deliberately bypasses the sidecar's own guard, sidecar/media_studio/library.py:476-478: "Refuses LOUD when the original source is gone (the managed copy is the only surviving copy) unless ``force=True`` — never silently destroys the only copy." That managed copy is creatable from this very card: App.tsx:521 passes `provenance={lineageActions}`, and app/renderer/src/features/lineageActionsClient.ts:65-74 wires `library.keepCopy`/`managedEvict`, surfaced through app/renderer/src/views/CardProvenanceDisclosure.tsx:42-58. CONSISTENCY CONTRAST: the same app confirms far smaller destructive acts — app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:146-147 `confirm()` before `shorts.delete`, and app/renderer/src/components/ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:183-206 requires a two-step inline "Remove copy?" confirm to evict ONE managed copy.
- why: Nielsen #3 (user control and freedom) and #5 (error prevention). One misclick on a 3-word button permanently discards a video's whole edit project, and — if the user opted into keep-a-copy and the original has since moved or been deleted — the only surviving copy of the media, defeating a guard the sidecar wrote specifically to prevent that. The same codebase gates the strictly smaller action (evicting one copy) behind two clicks, so a user who has learned that safety expectation is actively misled here.
- fix: Gate both remove paths behind the app's existing two-step inline confirm pattern (ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:183-206), and make the prompt name the collateral: "Remove <title>? This also discards its edits/project and its kept copy. Your original file stays on disk." Better still: (a) do not pass `force=True` from `library.remove` — let the sidecar's only-copy guard fire and surface it as a distinct confirm ("this is the only copy left"), and (b) offer an undo window on the toast for the DB row + manifest (move the manifest to a trash dir instead of `unlink`).
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — offered only as a precision-tightened restatement: Library "Remove" (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:159-166 -> Library.tsx:368-384, and the batch path Library.tsx:398-414 via LibraryToolbar.tsx:67-69) performs an unconfirmed, non-undoable destructive sequence: it hard-deletes the library entity row (library.py:347), unlinks the video's per-video edit manifest projects_dir/<id>.json and its poster (handlers/library_ops.py:145-146), and force-evicts any opt-in managed byte-copy (library.py:343-345 -> keepcopy.py:352-361), which destroys the media itself when the original source has moved or been deleted (proven by sidecar/tests/test_library.py:128-143 and sidecar/tests/test_keepcopy.py:374-385). The sidecar documents force=True as intentional BECAUSE the user is deleting the video (library.py:336-339) and refuses without force precisely to protect an only-copy (library.py:476-478, keepcopy.py:352-357) — so the defect is a broken layering contract: the sidecar relies on the UI having established destructive intent, and the UI establishes none, even though the SAME card gates the strictly smaller "evict this managed copy" action behind a documented two-step confirm (features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:20-21, :160-189, rendered by features/LibraryProvenance.tsx:253-258) and Settings does likewise (components/ManagedStoreMeter.tsx:183-206).

## "Remove selected" deletes videos that the active search has filtered out of view
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Selection is an id Set (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:187) that nothing prunes when the query or sort changes — the only writers are `unselect` on a single remove (Library.tsx:359-366, called at :375) and the explicit `clearSelection` (:395). The visible grid is a separate derivation: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:457-460 `sortVideos(filterVideos(videos, query), …)`. `removeSelected` (Library.tsx:398-414) iterates `[...selected]` with no intersection against `visible`. The batch bar is rendered unconditionally from `selected.size` (Library.tsx:496-504 → app/renderer/src/views/LibraryToolbar.tsx:59-75), so it stays on screen even when the filter matches nothing and the body shows the "No matches" state (Library.tsx:573-577). Repro: check 3 cards → type a non-matching query → the screen reads "No matches" with "3 selected / Remove selected" above it → clicking removes 3 videos the user cannot see.
- why: Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status) and #5 (error prevention): a destructive batch action operates on objects that are not on screen. Combined with the absence of any confirm (finding 1), the user cannot review, cannot see, and cannot undo what they just deleted — and the count in the bar is the only clue that the scope exceeds the viewport.
- fix: Either scope the action to what is visible — `removeSelected` should act on `visible.filter(v => selected.has(v.id))` and the bar should read "N selected (M hidden by filter)" — or prune the selection down to `visible` whenever `query`/`sortMode` change. At minimum, when `selected.size > visible.filter(selected).length`, label the button "Remove N selected (M not shown)" and require confirmation.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands unchanged and CONFIRMED. Only two supporting evidence sentences need tightening: (1) "Selection is an id Set (Library.tsx:187) that nothing prunes when the query or sort changes — its four writers are `toggleSelect` (:386-393), `unselect` on a single remove (:359-366, called at :375), `clearSelection` (:395), and the reset inside `removeSelected` (:400); none is keyed to `query`/`sortMode`, and no effect (:192, :233, :247) depends on either." (2) "The batch bar's render gate (LibraryToolbar.tsx:59) is `selectedCount > 0` — a function of `selected.size` alone, never of `visible` or `query` — so it persists above the 'No matches' body (Library.tsx:496-504 renders outside the conditional body at 540-595)." Optional severity precision: `library.remove` (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:135-147) destroys the library entry, the saved project manifest `projects_dir/<id>.json`, and the poster, but not the source video file.
- ⚠ scope correction: "Remove selected" acts on the whole selection, including videos the active search has filtered off screen — de-indexing them and destroying their per-video edit state, not their source files. Selection is an id Set (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:187) that no code path prunes when query or sortMode changes (the only writers are unselect :359-366 on a single remove, toggleSelect :386-393, clearSelection :395, and removeSelected :400); the visible grid is an independent derivation (Library.tsx:457-460 over filterVideos, libraryModel.ts:47-51); and removeSelected iterates [...selected] (Library.tsx:399) with no intersection against visible. Because the batch bar's gate is filter-blind (`selectedCount > 0`, LibraryToolbar.tsx:59), it stays on screen showing "3 selected / Remove selected" above the "No matches" empty state (Library.tsx:573-577), and there is no confirm (Library.tsx:502). SCOPED IMPACT: library.remove does NOT delete the user's video file — "The USER's source file on disk is never deleted" (sidecar/media_studio/library.py:333-334) — so the library row (library.py:347) is re-addable and the poster (library_ops.py:146) regenerable. The unrecoverable loss is (a) the per-video project manifest — tracks, clips, audioTracks, settings (library.py:499-500) — unlinked at library_ops.py:145, i.e. the user's editing work on videos they cannot see, and (b) in the opt-in keep-a-copy case, the managed byte-copy force-evicted at library.py:344-345, which bypasses the guard that otherwise "Refuses LOUD when the original source is gone (the managed copy is the only surviving copy)" (library.py:476-477). Severity: MEDIUM for the modal de-index case (surprising, off-screen, unconfirmed, but the footage survives); HIGH only for path (b), where a filtered-out selection can silently destroy the only surviving copy of a video. Fix: prune selected down to visible whenever query/sortMode changes, or surface the off-screen count in the bar ("N selected, M not shown") and require confirmation — but do NOT silently narrow removeSelected to visible.filter(selected), which discards the user's off-screen selection without telling them. Untested either way: Library.test.tsx covers filtering (~:1000-1017) and batch remove (:1038-1060) but never their interaction.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim in substance; the defect, the repro, and the high severity all hold. Three wording imprecisions worth tightening (none flips the verdict): (1) "rendered unconditionally from selected.size" is loose — LibraryToolbar.tsx:59 gates on `selectedCount > 0`; the bar is unconditional only with respect to FILTER state, which is the substantive claim and is confirmed. (2) The writer enumeration is incomplete — it omits `toggleSelect` (Library.tsx:386-393) and `setSelected(new Set())` (Library.tsx:400); neither prunes on filter change, so the conclusion stands. (3) `sortMode` in the proposed fix is inert — sorting reorders but never hides, so only `query` can strand a selection; the fix should key on `query` alone. Scope the damage precisely: source video files DO survive (library.py:333-334), so typical-case loss is the project manifest (edit state) plus re-import friction, not lost footage; the irreplaceable-media case additionally requires opt-in keep-a-copy AND a missing original. Correctly-scoped severity: HIGH at ~75-85% confidence (evidence: executable repro + the force=True interlock bypass at library.py:343-345 vs library.py:476-477), rather than a catastrophic footage-loss reading. Settling experiment for the residual: enable keep-a-copy, delete the original, then batch-remove the video while a non-matching query is active, and check whether the managed copy survives on disk.

## Space is swallowed for every button inside the candidate-review group — 10 controls are dead to the Space key
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:829 filters only `INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT` (`if (tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'TEXTAREA' || tag === 'SELECT') return;`) — BUTTON is not exempt; app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:843 then unconditionally `e.preventDefault()` on Space. The handler is bound to the `.sm-review` container at app/renderer/src/features/CandidateReview.tsx:100 (`onKeyDown={onKeyDown}`, tabIndex 0 at :99), and every review control is a DESCENDANT of it, so keydown bubbles up: Sort Rank/Virality (CandidateReview.tsx:156, :164), Factors toggle (CandidateList.tsx:121), the 4 nudge buttons (CandidateList.tsx:156, :164, :170, :177), Reset (CandidateList.tsx:185), Approve/Discard/Reinstate (CandidateList.tsx:193, :198, :203).
MEASURED in Chromium via Playwright (both-states control run, per single-signal-verification §3b):
  ancestor preventDefault ON  -> {"log":["handled-space"],"active":"b"}      (no CLICK)
  ancestor preventDefault OFF -> {"log":["handled-space-NO-preventDefault","CLICK"]}  (CLICK fires)
So the button's activation really is cancelled, not merely reordered.
Not covered by tests: app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.test.tsx:2296-2301 dispatches keydown on `.sm-review` itself, never on a descendant button.
- why: Space is a universal `<button>` activation key. A keyboard-only user who tabs to "Approve" and presses Space gets no approval and no feedback — instead the preview video silently toggles play/pause, so the control reads as broken. Enter still works, so WCAG 2.1.1 is technically met, but 10 of the surface's review controls fail the platform convention with a misleading side effect.
- fix: Add BUTTON (and `[role="button"]`/`A`) to the early-return filter at ShortMaker.tsx:829 — e.g. `if (['INPUT','TEXTAREA','SELECT','BUTTON','A'].includes(tag) || (e.target as HTMLElement).isContentEditable) return;`. Better: only run the shortcut handler when `e.target === e.currentTarget` (focus is on the group itself), which is the behaviour the existing tests already exercise.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM-LOW (not high): Space is swallowed for buttons inside the candidate-review group, so Tab+Space does not activate them — a platform-convention break with a visible-but-self-signalling side effect, NOT a blocked workflow.

CONFIRMED MECHANISM: the handler bound to .sm-review (app/renderer/src/features/CandidateReview.tsx:100, tabIndex 0 at :99) exempts only INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:829), so a Space keydown bubbling from a descendant button reaches the unconditional e.preventDefault() at ShortMaker.tsx:843, which cancels the button's activation click (independently measured in Chromium at both container and root-delegation positions, with no-handler and Enter controls validating the detector). Up to 10 controls render simultaneously on a nudged row: Sort Rank/Virality (CandidateReview.tsx:156, :164), Factors (CandidateList.tsx:121), 4 nudge (CandidateList.tsx:156, :164, :170, :177), Reset (:185), and 2 of 3 decide buttons (:193, :198, :203).

CORRECTLY SCOPED IMPACT: every affected control remains operable by mouse AND by Tab+Enter (Enter activation measured intact). Approve and Discard additionally have documented shortcuts A/X (ShortMaker.tsx:851-860) exposed via aria-keyshortcuts (CandidateReview.tsx:98) and the visible legend (:185-206). The residual gap is the other 8 controls, which have no letter-shortcut equivalent — notably the 4 nudge buttons, since the ArrowLeft/Right shortcut slides BOTH window edges (ShortMaker.tsx:868) whereas the buttons move ONE edge (CandidateList.tsx:158). WCAG 2.1.1 is met; no data loss, no incorrect state, instantly recoverable.

CORRECTED FIX — do NOT apply either fix as proposed. Adding BUTTON to the ShortMaker.tsx:829 early-return, or gating on e.target === e.currentTarget, would also disable J/K/A/X/arrows while focus is on a descendant, which the design deliberately keeps live (shortmaker.css:115 .sm-review:focus-within .sm-kbd-hints, "the legend brightens exactly while the keys are live"; ShortMaker.tsx:823-825). Instead scope the exemption to the Space branch ONLY — inside case ' ' at ShortMaker.tsx:842, return before preventDefault() when the target is a BUTTON, [role="button"], A, or isContentEditable — preserving every other shortcut group-wide.

TEST GAP (accurate as cited): ShortMaker.test.tsx:2296-2301 dispatches keydown on .sm-review itself and :2390-2397 only covers an INPUT with 'j'; no test dispatches Space on a descendant button. Note jsdom does not synthesize button activation from keyboard events, so a regression test for this must run in a real browser (Playwright), not the vitest/jsdom suite.

## An existing transcript is never loaded — the Transcribe panel shows the identical blank state whether or not the video is already transcribed
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `empty-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:47 seeds `const [transcript, setTranscript] = useState<Transcript | null>(null)` and the file's only two effects are the progress relay (:55-63) and the unmount teardown (:147) — there is NO mount-time read of an existing transcript anywhere in the file. The data is already in the parent: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:141 holds `project`, :166 fetches it via `rpc('project.open', {id: video.id})`, and :298 mounts `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} />` — passing only the id. The Project type carries it: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/api.ts:76 `transcript?: Transcript`. The sidecar persists it (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:438 `project.data["transcript"] = transcript`, :441 `set_has_transcript(video_id, True)`) and returns it whole (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:322 `return {"project": project.data}`). The library model even renders a 'Transcript' badge off `video.hasTranscript` (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:108).
- why: Transcription is the most expensive job in the app (a multi-GB model plus minutes-to-tens-of-minutes of decode). A user who transcribes, clicks to Subtitles, then clicks back to Transcribe — or simply restarts the app — is shown a pristine 'Start transcription' panel with no segments, no language, no word count. The empty state actively asserts 'no transcript exists' when one does, so the rational response is to re-run the job. It is also the only place to review the transcript text, and that review is unreachable after navigation.
- fix: Pass the already-fetched transcript down (`<Transcribe videoId={video.id} initialTranscript={project?.transcript ?? null} />` at Workspace.tsx:298) and seed `useState<Transcript|null>(initialTranscript)` at Transcribe.tsx:47; relabel the primary button 'Re-transcribe' when a transcript is present. Reserve the truly-empty branch for `!transcript`, and give that branch real copy (see the bare-void finding).
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands unchanged. Narrow ONE supporting sentence: "It is also the only place to review the transcript text" is slightly wide — the same speech text is reviewable as editable cues in the Subtitles panel (app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:319-336, seeded from the project at Workspace.tsx:271) once `subtitles.generate` has been run. Correctly scoped: Transcribe.tsx:200-218 is the ONLY surface for the transcript OBJECT (language, durationSec, segment count, word count, per-segment timings), and after any navigation or restart that review is unreachable; the raw text survives only indirectly via a derived subtitle track that may not exist.
- ⚠ scope correction: Headline unchanged and CONFIRMED. Only one supporting clause in WHY-IT-MATTERS needs tightening: replace "It is also the only place to review the transcript text" with "It is the only place that shows the transcript itself (language, duration, segment/word counts, full segment list); derived text is reachable elsewhere only after running another job — the cue editor at app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:317-332 (needs a subtitles build; cues are re-split text), SemanticSearch.tsx (query hits only, needs an index build), and Diarize.tsx:20-34 (needs a diarize run) — and none of those hydrate on mount either."
- ⚠ scope correction: An existing transcript is never loaded into the Transcribe panel: app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:47 seeds `useState<Transcript | null>(null)`, its only two effects are the progress relay (:55-63) and the unmount teardown (:147), and app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:298 mounts `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} />` passing only the id — even though the parent already holds the transcript (Workspace.tsx:141/:166, api.ts:76, library_ops.py:322). Because renderPanel() (Workspace.tsx:268-300) is a switch, the panel unmounts on any tab change, so the panel renders an identical "Start transcription" state — no segments, no language, no word count — both after in-session navigation and after an app restart, and re-running is the full expensive ASR job (no existing-transcript short-circuit in media_ops.py:398-444). Scope corrections vs the original: (1) it is NOT the only surface showing transcript TEXT — Subtitles.tsx:317-332 renders the full editable cue list seeded from persisted `initialTrack` (:26/:52, Workspace.tsx:271) and SemanticSearch.tsx:227 renders matching segment text; Transcribe is, however, the only surface for the transcript's own metadata (language / durationSec / segment + word counts, Transcribe.tsx:200-206) and for reviewing it ungated by a generated track or a built index; (2) severity is medium-high, not high — nothing is lost or blocked (downstream consumers reuse the persisted transcript, media_ops.py:415-416), libraryModel.ts:108 still badges 'Transcript' in the Library, and Workspace.tsx:96 lands the user on Subtitles rather than Transcribe; the real harm is an avoidable user-initiated re-run of the app's most expensive job plus the unreachable review surface. Fix as proposed (pass `initialTranscript={project?.transcript ?? null}`, seed it at :47, relabel the button 'Re-transcribe'), which matches the sibling Subtitles `initialTrack` convention.

Corrected scope, three changes:
- AFFECTS ALL FOUR INSTALL PROFILES, not just Minimum/Custom. With torch absent from the sidecar (requirements-sidecar.txt:3, requirements.lock.txt), `_default_cuda_probe` always returns False, so resolve_transcribe_target yields device=cpu and model="small" (transcribe.py:82, :263). Every profile that includes transcription installs `mobiuslabsgmbh/faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo` (manifest.py:285/:289) instead, so the model actually loaded is pre-fetched by NO profile — Default and Full stall identically.
- THE DOWNLOAD IS faster-whisper "small", NOT 1.6 GB. Drop the 1600 MB figure (that is installProfiles.ts:50's size for a different, unused weight). Exact size of `small` UNVERIFIED — not executed.
- DROP the offline assertion. Offline mode does not reach the whisper load at all (no guard_network in media_ops.py:357-444; enforce_offline_env unused in production; no HF offline env in sidecar.ts:168-197), so offline+network yields a silent download that bypasses offline.py:1-7 — a separate defect to file, not a variant of this one.

Two independent latent defects surfaced by the same trace, worth filing separately: (a) GPU whisper is unreachable on any machine because the CUDA probe depends on a package the sidecar forbids, even though CUDA DLL registration (transcribe.py:157) and ctranslate2 are shipped; (b) the transcription install bundle pre-fetches a weight the default code path never loads, so its ~1.6 GB is downloaded and then unused.

The proposed fix still applies with one correction: emit an explicit `on_progress(0.0, "loading the speech model")` before transcribe.py:343, and gate/label the idle state on real asset state — but resolve the label against the model resolve_transcribe_target actually returns, not the manifest bundle, or the panel will promise the wrong weight and size.
- ⚠ scope correction: Sustained with tightened scope. Correctly-scoped version: "On a first transcribe with no cached whisper weight, the Transcribe panel parks at a MOTIONLESS DETERMINATE '0% · Starting…' bar for the entire blocking model download, and Cancel does not stop it. Mechanism: Transcribe.tsx:44/:72 seed pct=0 + 'Starting…'; :186-192 renders <progress max={100} value={pct} /> (value=0 => no indeterminate animation); transcribe.py:342 wires `notify` only as on_fallback, :343-345 blocks in FasterWhisperLoader.load -> :161 _WhisperModel(...) (no local_files_only, no progress callback), and the first emit is :357-358 on_progress(0.0,'transcribing') only AFTER the model exists. The live handler has no pre-ensure (media_ops.py:385-395, :425-433). Cancel is ineffective because should_cancel is first polled at transcribe.py:362 inside the segment loop while :161 has no cancel probe, so Transcribe.tsx:142-143 shows idle while the download continues. The app's own point-of-use `needsDownload`+`assets.ensure` machinery exists but excludes the speech model (_capabilities.py:61-83 covers only reframe/reframe.saliency/scene.detect; _wire.py:62-75 _COMPONENT_ASSETS has no whisper key)."

Two corrections to the original wording:
(1) MAGNITUDE is device-dependent, not a flat 1.6 GB. 1.6 GB (installProfiles.ts:50; manifest.py:293) applies only to the CUDA/large-v3-turbo path (transcribe.py:74, :263). A non-CUDA box resolves CPU_MODEL='small' (transcribe.py:82, :263) — a smaller fetch (exact size UNVERIFIED). Offsetting this, the affected population is WIDER than "Minimum/Custom": no Systran/faster-whisper-small entry exists in the repo (manifest pins only mobiuslabsgmbh/faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo, manifest.py:289), so a CPU-only machine stalls identically even on the recommended Default profile (installProfiles.ts:96, :124).
(2) The OFFLINE sub-claim mis-attributes cause and must be dropped as written. transcribe.py never calls guard_network (guards exist at diarize.py:313, reframe_multispeaker.py:1406, vlm_backbone.py:390, dub.py:330, manager.py:686, providers_ops.py:111/:257 — not transcribe), and enforce_offline_env returns a COPY (offline.py:135-138) that nothing merges into the sidecar's os.environ. So flipping the `offline` setting (offline.py:46) does NOT produce a raw huggingface exception; it produces an UNGUARDED network download — an offline-mode bypass, a separate defect worth its own finding. The raw-exception-in-the-alert outcome (Transcribe.tsx:194-198) requires a genuinely unreachable network, not the setting.
(3) The proposed fix needs one amendment: driving `assets.ensure` first only covers the manifest-known whisper-large-v3-turbo (manifest.py:355-363); it cannot cover the CPU 'small' model, which has no manifest entry. The unconditional `on_progress(0.0, 'loading the speech model')` before transcribe.py:343 (plus a determinate->indeterminate bar while pct is 0 and unstarted) is the part that fixes every path.

## Zero forced-colors handling: `outline: none` + a box-shadow-only focus ring means the gallery has NO visible focus indicator in Windows High Contrast
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `dark-light-parity` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52` is the app's single focus language: `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }`. `--focus-ring` is box-shadow-only — `0 0 0 2px var(--surface-bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-edge)` at `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206`. A repo-wide grep for `forced-colors|prefers-contrast|-ms-high-contrast` across `app/renderer` returns 0 hits, so there is no alternate-theme fallback anywhere. On this surface that rule is the sole focus indicator for every interactive control: `.shorts__thumb-btn` (`views/shorts.css:220-234`, the card's primary Play affordance, rendered at `views/Shorts.tsx:293-307`), `.shorts__sort-btn` (`shorts.css:405-419`, `Shorts.tsx:173-188`), and `.shorts__actions button` (`shorts.css:356-371`, `components/ShortClipActions.tsx:49`). Per CSS Color Adjust, forced-colors mode forces `box-shadow` to `none`; `outline: none` is not restored, so nothing remains. UNVERIFIED inline: I did not run the app under `forced-colors: active` — the settling experiment is `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` in the e2e suite, tab to `.shorts__thumb-btn`, and assert a non-zero-width focus indicator.

COMPOUNDING (independently CONFIRMED by geometry, and true even in normal dark mode): `.shorts__thumb` sets `overflow: hidden` (`shorts.css:212-218`) with no padding, and `.shorts__thumb-btn` is `width: 100%; height: 100%; margin: 0; padding: 0` (`shorts.css:225-228`). `--focus-ring` has 0 offset and 0 blur, so it draws entirely OUTSIDE the button's border box — which coincides exactly with the parent's clip rect. The ring on the gallery's primary control is therefore fully clipped away today, before forced-colors is even considered.
- why: Windows High Contrast is the alternate — and usually LIGHT — theme this Windows-targeted Electron app (win32-only baselines) will actually be viewed in, and it is the closest thing to a second theme that exists. In it, a keyboard user on the produced-shorts grid can tab through every Play button, both sort toggles, and all five per-card actions (Play / Open folder / Re-export / Package / Delete — one of which is destructive and guarded only by a `window.confirm` at `Shorts.tsx:147`) with no visible indication of where focus is. That is a WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) failure, and the clipping defect means the Play button already fails it in the shipped dark theme.
- fix: Two independent fixes. (1) Add a forced-colors fallback next to `shell.css:49-52`: `@media (forced-colors: active) { :where(button,[role="button"],[role="tab"],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 2px; } }` — `outline` survives forced-colors where `box-shadow` does not. (2) Un-clip the ring: either move `overflow: hidden` off `.shorts__thumb` onto the `<img>`/`<Player>` children, or give `.shorts__thumb-btn` an inset indicator (`outline-offset: -4px`, or `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent-edge)`) so the ring is drawn inside the clip rect.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands as written; two sentences need tightening. (1) Scope the premise: "On the produced-shorts gallery, shell.css:49-52 is the ONLY focus language — app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css declares no `outline` and no `--focus-ring`, and features/shortmaker.css:99 explicitly defers to the shared ring — so every card control there depends on a box-shadow-only indicator. App-wide it is not the single language: panels/directorPanel.css:73-76 and components/captionBox.css:59-63 already use `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px` on `:focus-visible`, which is precedent for the proposed fix, not a counterexample." (2) Scope the clipping sentence: "the ring is EFFECTIVELY clipped away today — measured in headless Chromium, focusing `.shorts__thumb-btn` changes only 24 of 34,128 pixels, all antialiased arcs of the parent's 6px rounded corners at <=13/255 delta, versus 740 changed pixels for an unclipped control 1/9th the area — i.e. no perceptible focus indicator, not literally zero pixels." The forced-colors claim needs no correction and can drop its UNVERIFIED tag for the CSS mechanism: measured with `forcedColors:'active'`, computed box-shadow becomes `none`, `outline-style` stays `none`, and focused/unfocused screenshots are byte-identical for both the clipped and an unclipped control. The remaining UNVERIFIED is narrower: whether Electron 43 enters forced-colors mode from the Windows High Contrast OS setting.
- ⚠ scope correction: Scope correction is UPWARD for the defect and downward only for the remedy and rationale:

(1) FORCED-COLORS (app-wide, executable-proven — not gallery-scoped): The app has zero forced-colors handling (0 hits repo-wide for forced-colors|prefers-contrast|-ms-high-contrast, confirmed by ripgrep + git grep). Its single focus language — `outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52, with the box-shadow-only token at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206, repeated verbatim by ~60 per-component rules — produces NO focus indicator under `forced-colors: active`: measured `computed box-shadow: none`, `outline-style` remains `none`, 0 changed pixels of 82,720 on both a clipped and an unclipped control. This is a WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) failure on EVERY keyboard-reachable control in the app, not just the Produced-shorts gallery. Severity high; blast radius app-wide.

(2) CLIPPING (gallery-specific, executable-proven, live in the shipped dark theme): `.shorts__thumb` sets `overflow: hidden` with no padding (shorts.css:212-218) and `.shorts__thumb-btn` is `width/height:100%; margin:0; padding:0; border:none` (shorts.css:220-234), so the button's border box coincides exactly with the parent's clip rect (measured: both (40,40,200,355.55)). The 0-offset/0-blur ring therefore paints entirely outside the clip and reduces to 24 anti-aliased pixels at the four 6px-radius corners (24 of 82,720; max 6 px per row) — not a perceivable focus indicator. So the gallery's primary Play affordance already fails WCAG 2.4.7 today in normal dark mode, before forced-colors is considered.

(3) CORRECTED FIX (the finding's fix 1 does not work as written): the two fixes are DEPENDENT, not independent. `@media (forced-colors: active) { … outline: 2px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 2px }` measured 0 changed px on this surface because a positive outline-offset is clipped by the same ancestor `overflow: hidden` that eats the box-shadow. Use an INSET indicator on clipped surfaces — `outline: 2px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: -4px` measured 2196 changed px in normal mode and 2172 under forced-colors — or move `overflow: hidden` off `.shorts__thumb` onto the `<img>`/`<Player>` children FIRST, after which the positive-offset form works.

(4) Drop the unsupported rationale: do not claim Windows High Contrast is "usually LIGHT" (3 of Windows 11's 4 contrast themes are dark; Chromium's forced-colors default resolves to a dark palette), and do not file this under `dark-light-parity` — the app is dark-only (tokens.css:20 `color-scheme: dark`, zero prefers-color-scheme/data-theme repo-wide). It is an accessibility/forced-colors finding.

(5) Regression guard: the existing gate cannot catch either half — app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145 checks only `.toptab` and asserts a non-`none` COMPUTED box-shadow, which is blind to ancestor clipping, and :64-66 confirms the gallery sub-tab is never opened so `.shorts` is outside the axe run. A regression test must assert RENDERED indicator pixels (or a negative-offset outline) on `.shorts__thumb-btn` under both default and `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` — the harness already calls emulateMedia at app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:79, so the hook exists.
- ⚠ scope correction: Split into two correctly-scoped findings.

(1) MEDIUM, keep — "`.shorts__thumb-btn` has no visible focus indicator in the shipped dark theme, because its focus ring is fully clipped by the parent's overflow." Scope: `.shorts__thumb-btn` ONLY (not the sort toggles, not the card actions — those render their ring fine today). Evidence: `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:216` (`.shorts__thumb { overflow: hidden }`, no padding) + `shorts.css:223-226` (`.shorts__thumb-btn { margin:0; padding:0; width:100%; height:100% }`) + `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:289-307` (direct parent/child) + `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206` (ring at 0 offset / 0 blur, so it paints entirely outside the border box = outside the clip rect). No focus rule in `shorts.css` overrides `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52`, and `.shorts__thumb-btn` has only a `:hover` color shift (`shorts.css:236-238`). WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) failure, normal dark mode, no forced-colors emulation required. Fix: the finding's fix (2) — inset the indicator (`outline-offset: -4px` or `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent-edge)`), or move `overflow: hidden` onto the media children. Settling experiment: tab to `.shorts__thumb-btn` and compare a screenshot against the unfocused state — the existing `a11y.a11y.spec.ts:127-145` computed-`boxShadow` assertion CANNOT detect this and must not be cited as coverage.

(2) LOW, app-wide, re-filed off this surface — "no forced-colors fallback anywhere in the renderer; `outline: none` + a box-shadow-only ring means no focus indicator under Windows High Contrast." Scope: global, against `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52` and `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206`, affecting all 41 `--focus-ring` consumers across ~28 stylesheets — not the Make Shorts gallery, and not a dark-light-parity finding (there is no light theme). Grep for `forced-colors|prefers-contrast|-ms-high-contrast` across `app/` = 0 hits, so the absence is confirmed; the box-shadow→none behavior is per the CSS Color Adjust spec but UNVERIFIED by execution here. Priority LOW for a single-user dark-only local desktop tool where HCM was evidently never a supported mode; the finding's fix (1) (`@media (forced-colors: active) { … outline: 2px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 2px }`) is correct and cheap if adopted, but it is a one-line global hardening, not a high-severity gallery bug.

## "Auto (verthor, falls back)" states the wrong engine — Auto never runs verthor
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Label: app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:267 `auto: 'Auto (verthor, falls back)'`, rendered at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:175 inside the "Reframe engine" select (ShortMakerControls.tsx:167-179), mounted unconditionally via app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:882 → app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:240. Actual behaviour (three independent signals): (1) code — sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:450-452 `if requested in (ENGINE_AUTO, ENGINE_CLAUDESHORTS): return ENGINE_CLAUDESHORTS, None`; (2) contract doc — sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:66-67 "'auto' now resolves to the in-sidecar claudeshorts engine (no WSL); verthor is an explicit opt-in"; (3) the repo's own e2e fixture — app/e2e/fixtures.ts:252 "the default `reframeEngine:\"auto\"` (claudeshorts) path". The stale renderer JSDoc that seeded the label is at shortMakerLogic.ts:254-255.
- why: The default option in the reframe-engine picker names an engine that is never selected and promises a fallback chain that no longer exists. `verthor` requires WSL2 (reframe.py:15-19), so a user on a WSL-less machine may abandon "Auto" believing it needs WSL, and a user with WSL expects the GPU/YOLO engine and silently gets the in-sidecar OpenCV crop instead — with different output quality and no notice (get_engine returns `notice=None` since P3, reframe.py:476-478). "falls back" also has no object: falls back to what?
- fix: Rewrite the option to describe the outcome, not the codename: `auto: 'Automatic (recommended) — runs on this computer, no extra setup'`. Delete the stale "verthor with claudeshorts fallback" JSDoc at shortMakerLogic.ts:254-255. Add a conformance test pinning the Auto label against `reframe.resolve_engine_name('auto')` so the copy cannot drift from the resolver again.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (copy-microcopy, not high): the default option label at app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:267 `auto: 'Auto (verthor, falls back)'` is factually stale — reframe.py:449-452 resolves `auto` straight to claudeshorts and reframe.py:476-479 confirms no fallback notice exists — and the app never discloses the engine that actually ran (shortmaker.py:1240-1241 discards the notice; ExportStage.test.tsx:60 pins the codename out of the export stage). The ONLY user-visible consequence is for the narrow subset who have WSL on PATH and know verthor: they may read the label as a promise of the WSL/MediaPipe path (called "high-quality" at README.md:101, though no in-repo benchmark measures the delta — UNVERIFIED) and never explicitly opt in. It costs no data, no crash, nothing blocked, and is reversible in one dropdown click per export. Strike the WSL-less harm scenario entirely: `auto` and `claudeshorts` resolve identically (reframe.py:450-452), so switching away from Auto is a no-op, and an explicit `verthor` on a WSL-less host fails loudly (reframe.py:460-463), never silently. Also strike "GPU/YOLO" — verthor is MediaPipe (reframe.py:15, README.md:101) and the pinned ONNX CNN (YuNet) is in the DEFAULT engine (reframe_claudeshorts.py:12-28). Fix is still worth taking as a cheap copy edit, and must also delete the same stale claim at reframe.py:3-13 and CONTRACTS.md:165-166, ideally with label text that names the outcome AND points at the WSL opt-in rather than hiding it.

## Reframe picker leaks raw engine codenames and "WSL"/"GPU", violating the project's own enforced no-jargon rule
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:266-271 — `verthor: 'verthor (WSL)'`, `claudeshorts: 'claude-shorts (in-app)'`, `reframe_multispeaker: 'Multi-speaker (hybrid, WSL/GPU)'` — rendered as visible option text at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:173-177 with no tooltip or hint (no `title` on the select, ShortMakerControls.tsx:168-172). The project has an explicit, opposite rule for the identical concept: app/renderer/src/features/export/exportModel.ts:203-208 "the raw engine id is NEVER surfaced (it is a model codename — the no-jargon rule)"; app/renderer/src/lib/captionStyleNames.ts:5 "FORBIDS surfacing any font/codec/model/brand name in a user-visible string"; and it is machine-enforced for captions at app/renderer/src/lib/captionStyleNames.test.ts:35-43 (banned regex `/libass|remotion|hormozi|.../i`). No equivalent de-jargon map or test exists for reframe engines. This picker sits on what App.tsx:6-7 calls "the novice front door".
- why: A novice choosing how their video gets cropped to vertical is shown three internal project codenames and two unexplained abbreviations. "verthor" and "claude-shorts" are meaningless outside this repo; "WSL" (Windows Subsystem for Linux) and "GPU" are never expanded anywhere in the picker. The user cannot tell which option produces better framing, which needs extra setup, or what the trade-off is — so the control is effectively unusable and they will leave it on a default whose own label is wrong (see the Auto finding).
- fix: Add `lib/reframeEngineNames.ts` mirroring the caption solution: map each id to an outcome-based name + blurb (e.g. `claudeshorts` → "Follow the speaker · runs on this computer"; `verthor` → "Motion tracking · needs the optional Linux add-on"; `reframe_multispeaker` → "Multi-person split screen · needs a graphics card"). Extend the existing banned-jargon test to cover the reframe labels (add `verthor|claudeshorts|multispeaker|wsl` to the regex) so this cannot regress.
