- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim, but the SCOPE is too narrow and should be widened: the same picker leaks caption jargon too, so reframe engines are not uniquely unprotected. app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:158-162 renders raw CAPTION_STYLES labels - the exact brand names app/renderer/src/lib/captionStyleNames.ts:6-8 names as violations ("Hormozi", "MrBeast", "TikTok", "OpusClip Karaoke", "libass") - and app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:84-101 renders bare ids for BOTH caption styles and reframe engines ({style}, {engine} - literally "verthor", "claudeshorts", "reframe_multispeaker", with no label map at all). The de-jargon rule (captionStyleNames.ts) is applied ONLY in the Caption-gallery module; the Make-Shorts picker and the Export-presets table both bypass it. Correctly scoped claim: "The Make Shorts picker and the Export-presets table bypass the project's enforced no-jargon rule for BOTH reframe engines and caption styles; the reframe case is the most severe because two of the four labels are internal codenames whose only differentiator is an unexpanded 'WSL'/'GPU' that silently marks a hard-failure precondition (ReframeError at sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:463)." The proposed fix should therefore also route the Make-Shorts caption select through the existing lookNamedCatalog() (captionStyleNames.ts:124-137) rather than only adding reframeEngineNames.ts.
- ⚠ scope correction: The reframe-engine picker on the Make Shorts novice front door surfaces engine jargon in all FOUR of its visible option labels (shortMakerLogic.ts:267-270, rendered at ShortMakerControls.tsx:175): 2 distinct internal codenames ("verthor" — leaked twice, including in the `auto` label; "claude-shorts") and 2 never-expanded abbreviations ("WSL", "GPU"; verified expanded nowhere in the renderer). This violates the project's own no-jargon rule, stated for engine ids at exportModel.ts:204-205 and for user-visible strings at captionStyleNames.ts:5, and machine-enforced — for captions only — at captionStyleNames.test.ts:36-42. No de-jargon map or test exists for reframe engines (no `reframeEngineNames.ts`; repurposeLogic.ts:50-56 has raw ids and no labels). Scope-down on one rhetorical point: the control is functional and operable, so "effectively unusable" overstates it — the accurate claim is that the user cannot make an informed choice (no way to tell which option frames better, which needs extra setup, or what the trade-off is). The picker is NOT behind an Advanced disclosure (it is a flat field in `sm-controls`, ShortMakerControls.tsx:90), so novice exposure is direct.
- ⚠ scope correction: The legacy Make Shorts controls form (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx) bypasses the project's plain-language convention for BOTH of its model/engine pickers, not just reframe engines. The reframe-engine select renders codenames plus unexplained abbreviations — 'verthor (WSL)', 'claude-shorts (in-app)', 'Auto (verthor, falls back)', 'Multi-speaker (hybrid, WSL/GPU)' (shortMakerLogic.ts:266-271 via ShortMakerControls.tsx:173-177, no `title`/hint; the file's only `title=` is line 310) — and the caption-style select 10 lines above renders raw brand/engine labels — 'Hormozi (green pop)', 'MrBeast (yellow pop)', 'TikTok (card)', 'Classic (libass, fast)' (shortMakerLogic.ts:203-213 via ShortMakerControls.tsx:158-162). Both are visible on the novice front door (MakeShorts.tsx:214-248 -> ShortMaker.tsx:882) with no Advanced disclosure.

Correctly scoped, the defect is SURFACE-level, not engine-specific: the de-jargon layer (lib/captionStyleNames.ts) exists but is wired only into the Caption-phase gallery (CaptionGallery.tsx:44-48), and its banned-jargon test (captionStyleNames.test.ts:35-43) asserts over the CAPTION_STYLE_LOOKS table only — no gate covers this form's rendered labels (ShortMakerControls.test.tsx:150-151 asserts the value only). So this picker is outside the convention's enforcement, not in violation of an active gate. The convention itself is genuine and recurring (exportModel.ts:205, PresetMatrix.tsx:6, LineageActions.tsx:18, directorHandoff.test.ts:77).

Severity: MEDIUM (comprehension/copy on an optional control that defaults to 'auto'; no functional breakage, nothing blocks the novice path).

Fix: rewire BOTH selects in ShortMakerControls.tsx to outcome-based name maps (reuse lookNamedCatalog for captions; add an engine equivalent with a blurb), and gate it with a RENDERED-TEXT assertion on the mounted form — template at export/ExportStage.test.tsx:60 (`expect(textContent).not.toContain('verthor')`) — because a table-level regex alone would pass green while the leak still ships.

## Subtitles panel re-seeds from a stale mount-time project snapshot; the next blur-save silently reverts cue edits that were already persisted
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: - app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:163-175 — `project.open` runs only when `video.id` changes; `reloadProject` is never re-invoked on tab switch.
- app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:266 — `const tracks = (project?.tracks ?? [])` is that one-shot snapshot.
- app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:271 — `<Subtitles videoId={video.id} initialTrack={tracks[0] ?? null} />`; `onTrackChange` (declared at app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:28) is NOT passed, so saves never flow back into `project`.
- app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:52 — `useState<SubtitleTrack | null>(initialTrack)`: every remount re-seeds from the stale snapshot.
- app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:332 — `onBlur={() => track && saveEdits(track.cues)}` writes the WHOLE cue array; sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:74-82 replaces the stored track with it and `project.save()`s.

EXECUTED PROBE #3: rendered the real `<Workspace>`, clicked subtitles→timeline→subtitles; `project.open` call count stayed at 1 and the stubbed panel's `initialTrack` was byte-identical across the churn (printed `PROJECT.OPEN CALLS AFTER TAB CHURN: 1`).

EXECUTED PROBE #2: rendered the real `<Subtitles>` with a two-cue track, edited cue 1 to `EDITED-ONE`, blurred (first `subtitles.edit` payload carried `EDITED-ONE`), unmounted, remounted with the SAME stale `initialTrack` (what Workspace does), edited cue 2 and blurred. Second payload printed:
`[{"index":1,...,"text":"ORIGINAL-ONE"},{"index":2,...,"text":"EDITED-TWO"}]`
— cue 1's persisted edit was overwritten with its pre-edit text. Test passed.
- why: Silent data loss on a normal workflow: fix a caption, hop to the Timeline tab to check timing, hop back, fix another caption — and the first fix is gone from disk with no error, no warning, and no visible cue that the panel is showing stale text. The user only discovers it on export. The Timeline panel reads live data via `tracks.list` (app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:128-137), so the two Edit panels disagree about the same track.
- fix: Stop treating the mount-time project as the source of truth for the Subtitles panel. Either (a) have Subtitles load its own track via `tracks.list` on mount (mirroring Timeline.tsx:128-137), or (b) pass `onTrackChange` from Workspace.tsx:271 and use it to update `project.tracks` in Workspace state so the snapshot tracks reality. (b) is smaller and uses a prop Subtitles already exposes. Add a regression test: save a cue, unmount/remount the panel, save a different cue, assert the first cue's new text survives in the payload.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped version (a TIGHTENING, not a refutation — the finding is confirmed): "The Subtitles panel seeds its track state ONCE per mount from Workspace's mount-time project snapshot (Workspace.tsx:266,271 -> Subtitles.tsx:52), and that snapshot is never refreshed because project.open is keyed on video.id alone (Workspace.tsx:163-175) and no onTrackChange is wired. Because the blur handler POSTs the entire cue array (Subtitles.tsx:332) and the sidecar replaces the stored track wholesale (media_ops.py:74-82, subtitles.py:300-307), ANY Subtitles mount that happens after the on-disk track has diverged from that snapshot will, on the next blur, overwrite every previously-persisted cue edit with its pre-edit text — with no error and a 'Saved' status. This needs neither a Subtitles remount nor a prior edit in Subtitles: divergence introduced by the Timeline panel's own wholesale subtitles.edit (Timeline.tsx:356-358) is clobbered on the FIRST ever Subtitles mount (probe-verified). Preconditions: the project must already hold the track at Workspace mount (with tracks: [] the panel instead shows only 'Generate subtitles' — a visible symptom, not a silent revert), and the stale text IS displayed in the cue input, so the staleness is detectable on inspection even though nothing warns. Fix (b) (wire onTrackChange) is insufficient because it does not cover Timeline's writes; fix (a) (load via tracks.list on mount, mirroring Timeline.tsx:124-137) is required."
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim; the headline and mechanism are accurate as written. Two refinements worth folding in (both make it sharper, neither weakens it):

(1) PRECONDITION to state explicitly: the destructive case requires `project.tracks[0]` to be non-empty at Workspace mount - i.e. a project whose subtitle track was generated BEFORE this mount (app restart, or a Library -> back -> re-open round-trip). In the same-session generate-then-edit-then-tab-churn case, `project.tracks` is still `[]`, so `initialTrack` is null and the panel comes back EMPTY instead - a different, non-destructive symptom (edits stay safe on disk; no cue inputs render, so no blur can fire).

(2) AMPLIFICATION: the revert does not require editing a second cue. Because `onBlur={() => track && saveEdits(track.cues)}` (Subtitles.tsx:332) fires on any blur regardless of whether the value changed, merely clicking into and out of ANY cue field after returning to the tab rewrites the entire stale array and reverts every previously-persisted edit (executable-proven).

Correctly-scoped version: "On a project whose subtitle track was persisted before the current Workspace mount, the Subtitles panel re-seeds from the stale mount-time `project` snapshot on every tab remount (Workspace.tsx:266,271 + Subtitles.tsx:52), and the next blur on ANY cue input - typing not required - writes that stale cue array back through subtitles.edit, which replaces the stored cues wholesale (media_ops.py:74-82 -> subtitles.py:300-307), silently and unrecoverably destroying cue edits already on disk."

## Timeline cue edits live only in unsaved component state — a tab switch, a nav away, or closing the window discards them with no dirty indicator and no confirm
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: - app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:100-111 — `history` (the undo stack holding every split/merge/retime/drag/text edit), `draft`, `selected`, `playhead` are plain `useState`.
- app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:225-230 — `commit()` only pushes into that in-memory history and clears the status line, so there is not even a "Saved"/"unsaved" marker left on screen.
- app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:350-371 — `handleSave` (the manual Save button, :487-496) is the ONLY path that persists via `subtitles.edit`.
- app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:268-300 — `renderPanel()` returns a different component per `active`, so changing tab unmounts Timeline outright. Proven in EXECUTED PROBE #3: after switching to Dub, `[data-panel="Dub"]` was present; after re-entry it was gone and the default panel rendered.
- No close/navigation guard exists anywhere: grep for `beforeunload|before-quit|onbeforeunload|dirty` across app/ returns exactly one hit — a comment at app/renderer/src/components/useAutosave.ts:26. app/main/main.ts has no `win.on('close')` prevention (only `window-all-closed` at :1513 and `will-quit` at :1521).
- No renderer-side scratch persistence at all: grep for `localStorage|sessionStorage` across app/renderer/src returns zero matches.
- why: A user who splits, merges and retimes twenty cues and then clicks the "Subtitles" tab (or the Library rail tab, or the window X) loses every edit instantly and silently. The undo stack is destroyed with it, so the work is unrecoverable. Nothing on screen distinguishes a saved timeline from one with twenty pending edits.
- fix: Track a dirty flag (`history.past.length > 0` since the last save) and (a) render a persistent "Unsaved changes" marker beside the Save button, (b) intercept tab selection in Workspace.tsx:189-198 with a confirm when the outgoing panel is dirty, and (c) register a `beforeunload` handler (or an Electron `win.on('close')` guard in app/main/main.ts) for the window-close case. Wiring the already-built `useAutosave` (see the next finding) would remove most of the exposure.
- ⚠ scope correction: Timeline cue edits live only in unsaved component state (Timeline.tsx:100-111); `commit()` performs no I/O (:225-230) and `handleSave` (:350-371, button :487-496) is the only persistence path, with no save-on-unmount (the sole effect cleanup is `alive = false`, :169-171). Because `renderPanel()` is a `switch (active)` that mounts Timeline only at case 'timeline' (Workspace.tsx:268-300, :282-285) and `handleSelect` is a bare `setActive` (:189-198), switching tabs — or leaving Edit, or returning to the TaskHub (Edit.tsx:135-145) — unmounts Timeline and discards every pending edit plus the undo stack (bounded at MAX_HISTORY=100, timelineOps.ts:23), with no confirm. Window close is equally unguarded: no `win.on('close')` exists and will-quit (main.ts:1521-1583) only tears down the sidecar before `app.exit(0)`. There is no scratch persistence (zero localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB in app/renderer/src) and no dirty tracking (the only `dirty|beforeunload` hit in app/ is a comment at useAutosave.ts:26, a hook that is never wired). There is no POSITIVE unsaved-changes indicator: the only signal is the disappearance of the transient "Saved" status (set :366, cleared :229, rendered :387), which is indistinguishable from a freshly-loaded, never-saved timeline — so a pristine timeline and one with twenty pending edits look identical, and the Save button (`disabled={!track || !history}`, :490) looks the same either way.

## The computed batch cost estimate (requests / egress bytes / free-limit headroom) is never rendered on the egress-authorization control
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:669-676 returns `costEst` and `budget` on the consent surface; sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:595-612 `_sum_egress_cost` aggregates `{requests, egressBytes, withinFreeLimits}` over the egressing plans. The wire type carries them: app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:1142-1143, plus per-decision `willEgress`/`cacheHit` at schemas.ts:1133-1134. app/renderer/src/features/BatchConsentCard.tsx reads ONLY `consent.decisions` (:33) and `consent.willRun`/`willSkip` (:39-42) - `costEst`, `budget`, `willEgress` and `cacheHit` appear nowhere in the component. Its own test fixture sets `costEst: { usd: 0.2 }` (app/renderer/src/features/BatchConsentCard.test.tsx:49), so the data is expected to be present. Contrast the app's other cloud-spend gate, which does surface it: app/renderer/src/panels/DirectorPanel.tsx:661-666 renders `row.willEgress` and "· cached (free re-run)".
- why: The user is asked to authorize cloud spend with zero cost information: no request count, no bytes-leaving-the-machine figure, and no indication that `withinFreeLimits` is already false. When it is false, the server then silently skips every egressing source after the click (batch.py:590-591 SKIP_NO_HEADROOM), so the user gets neither the cost nor a correct expectation of the outcome. A 2-source batch and a 20-source batch render an identical card modulo one integer.
- fix: Render `consent.costEst.requests` / `egressBytes` in the card body, and surface `withinFreeLimits === false` as an inline warning before the ack (it predicts a SKIP_NO_HEADROOM outcome). Mark each run decision with its `willEgress` / `cacheHit` flag the way DirectorPanel.tsx:661-666 already does, so cached free re-runs are distinguishable from paid ones.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (down from high) — The batch egress-authorization card omits the computed cost MAGNITUDE and the free-limit headroom warning, so the acknowledgement is less informed than DESIGN.md:255 requires.

`plan_consent` computes and returns an aggregate `costEst`/`budget` of `{requests, egressBytes, withinFreeLimits}` over the egressing plans (sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:595-612, :669-676) and the wire type carries it (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:1142-1143), but neither app/renderer/src/features/BatchConsentCard.tsx (reads only `consent.decisions` :33 and `willRun`/`willSkip` :39-42) nor its parent (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:326-337) renders any of it. This leaves docs/plans/repurpose/DESIGN.md:255 — "Estimated cost (`costEst`) aggregated across the egressing sources, and the budget headroom … so the single acknowledgement is informed" — unimplemented, along with the per-shape route rows and explicit local/cache-hit-vs-egressing marking of DESIGN.md:253-254.

Correctly scoped: the card is NOT information-free. Because the ack is only offered in the pre-ack state (BatchQueue.tsx:205-208), every egressing source is already listed BY NAME with the reason "would egress — not acknowledged" (batch.py:588-589 feeding BatchConsentCard.tsx:44-56), so the user does see which and how many sources would egress. What is missing is the request count, the bytes-leaving-the-machine figure, and an inline `withinFreeLimits === false` warning that would predict the SKIP_NO_HEADROOM outcome one screen earlier.

The outcome is also NOT silent: a no-headroom skip is recorded terminal with the reason "no budget headroom" (batch.py:93, :437-439) and rendered per row (BatchQueue.tsx:351-355) per the visible-skip contract (DESIGN.md:258-261). The failure mode is fail-CLOSED — no bytes egress, no spend is incurred, nothing is destroyed, and the source stays re-runnable (DESIGN.md:261) — which is why this is a medium informed-consent/UX gap on a single-user local desktop app, not a high-severity destructive-action defect.

Fix (unchanged in substance, reduced in urgency): render `consent.costEst.requests` and `egressBytes` in the card body, surface `withinFreeLimits === false` as an inline pre-ack warning, and mark each decision's `willEgress`/`cacheHit` the way DirectorPanel.tsx:666-671 already does so cached free re-runs are distinguishable from paid ones.
- ⚠ scope correction: The batch egress-consent card omits the QUANTITATIVE half of the consent surface it is handed: BatchConsentCard.tsx:33-79 renders the run/skip split, the named+attributed skips and the ack button, but never the aggregated costEst fields (requests, egressBytes) nor the withinFreeLimits headroom flag that batch.py:612/669-676 computes and schemas.ts:1142-1143 delivers, nor the per-decision willEgress/cacheHit flags (schemas.ts:1133-1134) that would distinguish a paid egress from a free cached re-run. The parent adds nothing (BatchQueue.tsx:326-337). Scope corrections vs the original finding: (a) this is an APP-WIDE omission, not a localized one - requests/egressBytes/withinFreeLimits are rendered in no non-test renderer source (only declared at useAiJob.ts:17-21, whose hook has no consumer), and the cited "sibling that does it right", DirectorPanel.tsx:654-675, likewise withholds its own row.costEst (schemas.ts:1251) while surfacing only qualitative flags (visible egress text via egressWarning, directorTypes.ts:240-245; the cached/free-re-run marker at :666; willEgress only as a non-visible data-egress attribute at :661); (b) a no-headroom outcome is NOT silent - the reason is rendered post-run at BatchQueue.tsx:351-355 per the visible-skip contract (batch.py:91-93) - the defect is that it is not PREDICTED before the click, since the card hides withinFreeLimits even though the ack path (BatchQueue.tsx:222-229) starts the batch without re-planning; (c) an aggregate withinFreeLimits=false skips only the sources of the step-SHAPES that individually lack headroom (per-plan check at batch.py:590 vs the cross-shape AND at batch.py:611), not necessarily every egressing source; (d) the missing figure is request-count/bytes/free-cap headroom, not money - the model carries no dollar amount (budget.py:124-131). Fix: render costEst.requests and egressBytes in the card body (ai_job.py:238-250 already produces the exact wording), surface withinFreeLimits === false as an inline pre-ack warning because it predicts a SKIP_NO_HEADROOM outcome, and mark each run decision with willEgress/cacheHit. Severity: medium.
- ⚠ scope correction: BatchConsentCard.tsx (84 lines, whole file) renders only the run/skip split (:39-42) and the named skip list (:44-56); it never renders the `costEst`/`budget` aggregate the sidecar computes (`{requests, egressBytes, withinFreeLimits}`, batch.py:595-612, returned at :669-676) nor the per-decision `willEgress`/`cacheHit` flags (schemas.ts:1133-1134), and its only consumer BatchQueue.tsx:326-337 adds none of them — so the "Acknowledge cloud egress" control (:58-67) is uninformed, violating docs/plans/repurpose/DESIGN.md:253-255 which requires the card to show estimated cost, budget headroom, and the local-only/cache-hit vs egressing split "so the single acknowledgement is informed". Consequence, stated precisely: the user cannot see request count, bytes-leaving-the-machine, or that `withinFreeLimits` is already false, and therefore cannot predict the SKIP_NO_HEADROOM outcome (batch.py:590-591) before clicking — compounded by BatchQueue.tsx:205-208/:222-229, which computes consent with `acknowledged: false` and never recomputes it, so the card's own skip list is stale after the ack. The skip is NOT silent afterwards (the reason renders per live row, BatchQueue.tsx:351-355). This is an app-wide omission rather than an inconsistency with DirectorPanel: DirectorPanel.tsx renders no numeric cost either (its `costEst: number`, schemas.ts:1251, is unused; `willEgress` at :661 is only a `data-egress` attribute), and repo-wide there are zero numeric-cost render sites. Fix must narrow the untyped `Record<string, unknown>` (schemas.ts:1142-1143) — ideally retype it to the existing `AiBudget` shape (useAiJob.ts:17-21) — and the `{usd: 0.2}` test fixture (BatchConsentCard.test.tsx:49) must be corrected to the real server shape. Severity: medium-high (spec violation on a privacy/consent surface), not a dollar-spend risk.

## "Reset to defaults" wipes every user-authored export preset on one unguarded click, and silently orphans saved templates
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:187-189 renders the button; :170-179 `handleReset` calls `client.exportPresets.reset()` with no confirm. sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:275-279 `PresetStore.reset()` - docstring: "Restore the three vertical seeds, overwriting any edits" - and `_write` (:237-241) `os.replace`s the catalog, so there is no prior copy. The unguarded path is proven by app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.test.tsx:202-208 (single click -> reset RPC, no `confirm` stub). The button sits beside "New preset" in the same toolbar (:184-190) with no destructive styling (nothing in app/renderer/src/features/panels.css targets it, unlike app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:382-385 and app/renderer/src/features/keep-copy-control.css:111). Cascade: preset ids are baked into saved templates at app/renderer/src/features/repurposeTemplates.ts:91 (`params.exportTargets`), and sidecar/media_studio/features/templates.py:175-179 raises INVALID_PARAMS "export target not found in presets" for a missing id.
- why: One misclick next to "New preset" permanently destroys the entire authored preset catalog - label, aspect, window, count, caption style, engine for every custom platform target - with no confirm, no undo and no export. Worse, it also breaks saved templates that targeted those preset ids; the breakage is invisible at reset time and only surfaces later as a raw error string in the batch rows (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:356-360), so the user cannot connect cause to effect.
- fix: Gate it with the two-step in-place confirm the codebase already uses for destructive actions (app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-190, whose header states "never a silent one-click destructive action"), naming the count of presets that will be lost. Style it destructively like `.shorts__delete` (shorts.css:382-385). Before resetting or deleting, check `templates.list()` for `exportTargets` referencing the affected ids and warn which templates will break.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM - "The Export Presets panel has no destructive-action confirm at all." Both "Reset to defaults" (app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:170-179, :187-189) and the per-row "Delete" (:108-110) mutate the persisted catalog on one unguarded click; PresetStore._write's os.replace (sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:237-241) leaves no prior copy, so the loss is irreversible and there is no export path (only list/save/delete/reset are registered, :335-338). Both toolbar buttons carry zero styling - no `.export-presets` rule exists in any repo .css - so "Reset to defaults" is visually identical to the adjacent "New preset". This contradicts the project's own stated standard at app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:21 ("never a silent one-click destructive action"), implemented as a two-step in-place confirm at :160-193. Scope of loss is CONFIG ONLY: six retypeable scalar fields per preset, aspect bounded to 9:16/1:1/4:5 (sidecar/media_studio/features/aspect.py:32-38); no media, renders or transcripts. Reset restores the three seeds rather than emptying the catalog (export_presets.py:164-198). Cascade, correctly scoped: templates targeting the seed ids tiktok/reels/shorts SURVIVE (ids preserved, export_presets.py:140-142); only templates targeting user-created uuid ids break, and they fail LOUD before any job spawns (sidecar/media_studio/features/templates.py:330-333) - the fair complaint is that the message surfaces a raw 12-hex uuid (export_presets.py:142) instead of the preset label, reaching the user as a raw string via batch.py:451-457 -> BatchQueue.tsx:356-360. The genuinely SILENT consequence is different from the one claimed: preset fields override template controls on every run (templates.py:161-163), so after a reset a template on a surviving seed id renders with reverted seed values (a tuned Reels count reverts to 3, export_presets.py:176-186) with no error at all. Fix: apply the existing KeepCopyControl two-step confirm to BOTH Reset and Delete, naming the count at risk, and give them the destructive affordance already used by `.shorts__delete` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:382-385).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): "Reset to defaults" in the Export Presets panel destroys the entire user-authored preset catalog on one unguarded, undifferentiated click, and can silently break saved templates that target custom presets. Scope: the panel is a config sub-tab two levels deep — Make Shorts -> "Batch & Templates" (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:50,213) -> Repurpose -> "Export presets" (app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:14,37) — and is independently mounted at app/renderer/src/views/Deliver.tsx:72. The button (ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:187-189) sits immediately beside "New preset" in the same toolbar (:184-190) and is visually identical to it: `.export-presets*` is targeted by NO stylesheet anywhere in the renderer, so there is no destructive affordance, unlike views/shorts.css:382-385 and features/keep-copy-control.css:111. handleReset (:170-179) calls client.exportPresets.reset() with no confirmation; lib/rpc/client.ts:639 is a bare RPC pass-through and app/main has no guard. Server-side, PresetStore.reset() (sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:275-279) returns only the three hardcoded seeds and _write (:237-241) os.replace's the single catalog file data_dir/"export-presets.json" (handlers/composition.py:441) — no prior copy, and no backup/export mechanism exists anywhere in sidecar/media_studio/features. Lost per custom preset: the 7 scalar fields at export_presets.py:144-153 (label, aspect, minSec, maxSec, count, captionStyle, reframeEngine); user EDITS to the three seeds are silently reverted too. Severity is MEDIUM rather than high because this is small, retypeable configuration rather than media or irrecoverable creative work, and the button is honestly labeled. Cascade (correctly scoped): only templates whose exportTargets include a CUSTOM (uuid) preset id break — the seed ids tiktok/reels/shorts (export_presets.py:167,178,189) are re-created identically, so seed-only templates are unaffected. Custom ids do reach templates: TemplateEditor.tsx:128-137 renders a checkbox for every live preset, :59 -> repurposeTemplates.ts:91 bakes the ids into params.exportTargets, and at run time templates.py:333 -> :175-179 raises INVALID_PARAMS "export target not found in presets", which batch.py:404-411 isolates per source (continue_on_error=True) and BatchQueue.tsx:356-360 renders as a raw error string — invisible at reset time, so cause and effect are unlinkable. Also in scope (same defect class, same fix): the per-row Delete button (ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:108-110, single-click confirmed by ExportPresetsPanel.test.tsx:184-191) is equally unguarded and orphans templates identically. Fix: gate BOTH reset and delete with the two-step in-place confirm the codebase already uses in TWO places — KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-193 (header at :21: "never a silent one-click destructive action") and export/ExportInspector.tsx:103-138 — naming the count of presets to be lost; style destructively per shorts.css:382-385; and before either action check templates.list() for exportTargets referencing the affected ids and name the templates that will break.

## Sidecar's `reframeDegraded` "no-silent-fallback" signal is dropped at the renderer boundary — a center-cropped short is reported as a successful tracked reframe
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Sidecar emits the degrade on BOTH wire channels: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1319-1320` puts it on the §2 clips payload (`clip["reframeDegraded"] = item["reframeDegraded"]`, comment at :1317-1318 says "the UI reads it off the clips list to flag real-vs-degraded tracking"), and `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1035-1037` also forwards it to `on_notice` -> `job.progress` (`shortmaker.py:1256-1261`). Payload built at `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_claudeshorts.py:205-209` (`"reframe: speaker tracking unavailable ({reason}) — used center crop"`). Sidecar test pins both channels: `sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py:1129-1131`.
Renderer drops both: repo-wide `rg reframeDegraded app/` -> **0 hits** (detector control: the same grep finds the sibling field `fillersRemoved` at `app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:116`). The two clip types omit the field — `app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:665-669` and `app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:114-118` are `{path, fillersRemoved?, fillerSeconds?}` only. The exported-clip list renders only `path` + filler stats: `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:982-992`. The progress channel is also lossy: the region is gated on `busy` (`app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:924`) and `setProgress(null)` runs in every `finally` (`ShortMaker.tsx:558`, `:691`, `:771`), so the one-line notice is overwritten by the next `job.progress` and destroyed on completion. `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx` subscribes to no progress at all (grep for `onProgress` in that file: 0 hits).
- why: Subject tracking is the product's marquee promise (16:9 -> 9:16 following the speaker). When YuNet finds no trackable subject, or the multi-speaker engine is unavailable, the engine silently falls back to a dumb center crop that can cut the speaker's head off. The sidecar was deliberately engineered so this is never silent, and shipped the flag on the durable clips payload — the renderer never declares or reads it, so the user exports and publishes a center-cropped short believing tracking ran. Compounding: `_emit_notice` de-dupes by `type` (`shortmaker.py:1257-1260`) and the multi-speaker unavailable notice reuses the SAME type constant (`sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_multispeaker.py:891`), so when both fire only the first ever reaches `job.progress` — the clips payload the renderer ignores is the only complete channel.
- fix: Add `reframeDegraded?: { type: string; message: string; reason: string }` to `ExportedClipInfo` (`app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:665`) and `ExportedClip` (`app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:114`). Render a persistent per-clip badge in the exported list at `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:983-991`, beside the existing filler chip (e.g. `Center-cropped — speaker tracking unavailable (<reason>)`), and fold a degraded count into the manual note at `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:187`. Persist it onto `ShortInfo` so the produced-shorts gallery card keeps the badge after the job is gone. Add a renderer test asserting the badge appears when `clips[0].reframeDegraded` is present — the mirror of `sidecar/tests/test_shortmaker.py:1129-1131` — so the two sides cannot drift again.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM-LOW (provenance / dead-wire-contract): the sidecar's `reframeDegraded` no-silent-fallback signal is emitted on both wire channels (shortmaker.py:1319-1320 clips payload, :1035-1037 on_notice) and pinned by a sidecar test (test_shortmaker.py:1129-1131), but has ZERO consumers in the renderer — it is absent from ExportedClipInfo (shortMakerLogic.ts:665-669) and ExportedClip (schemas.ts:114-118), the exported list renders only path + filler stats (ShortMaker.tsx:982-992), and the transient job.progress line is busy-gated (ShortMaker.tsx:924) and overwritten (shortmaker.py:1283/:1303), with MakeShorts.tsx:187 carrying no degrade at all. Consequence, correctly scoped: the user gets no PROVENANCE for a degraded reframe — they cannot tell which of N exported clips fell back to a center crop or why, so triage after a bad export is manual re-review of every clip. This is NOT an invisible bad publish: the produced-shorts card shows a poster frame extracted from the final exported clip (shorts.py:432, ProducedShorts.tsx:182-183) with one-click playback (ProducedShorts.tsx:180), so the actual framing is directly inspectable before publishing; the most frequent degrade reason ("no trackable subject located", reframe_claudeshorts.py:1081) makes center crop the correct framing rather than a defect worth badging; a missing model/backend is already a LOUD error, not this notice (reframe_claudeshorts.py:198-203); and the detector-exception path is already logged (reframe_claudeshorts.py:1074). The residual real-harm window is narrow — a detector exception (reframe_claudeshorts.py:1075) or an unavailable multi-speaker engine (reframe_multispeaker.py:1390) on a clip whose speaker is off-center or drifts out of frame after the poster frame, compounded because the type-dedupe at shortmaker.py:1256-1261 lets only the first notice of a shared type constant (reframe_multispeaker.py:891) reach job.progress. Worth implementing the proposed badge + the mirror renderer test to kill the dead-wire drift, prioritized as polish rather than as a blocking high-severity defect.
- ⚠ scope correction: Sidecar's `reframeDegraded` no-silent-fallback signal reaches the renderer at runtime but is never declared or read, so no durable UI surface distinguishes a center-cropped fallback from a real tracked reframe.

Two tightenings to the original wording (substance unchanged):

1. "dropped at the renderer boundary" -> "carried across the boundary but never consumed." There is no runtime stripping: `app/renderer/src/lib/rpc` has zero `zod`/`.parse(`/`safeParse` hits, and `extractClips` (`app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:688-694`) casts the array without copying, so `reframeDegraded` is physically present on the objects `setExportedClips` stores (`app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:672`, `:758`). This makes the fix strictly cheaper than the title implies — no IPC/preload/schema-transport change is needed, only the two type declarations plus a render site.

2. "a center-cropped short is reported as a successful tracked reframe" -> "is indistinguishable from a successful tracked reframe." The UI makes no affirmative tracking claim; it reports only "Exported N clip(s)" (`app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:980`) and "Exported N clip(s) from your ranges." (`app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:187`). The defect is omission, not affirmative misreport — same user outcome (publishes a center-cropped short with no indication tracking failed), same fix.

Add to the evidence: the global Jobs slide-over is a third blind surface — `app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:67-78` discards the progress `message` (keeps pct + status only) — and the gallery path cannot be fixed by types alone, because `_write_short_metadata` runs at `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1147` before the flag is stamped at `:1174`, so persisting it onto `ShortInfo` requires moving/extending that write as well.

## ReframeOverridePanel is fully built and tested but never mounted — a wrong auto-crop has no correction path
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:73-158` implements the whole manual-correction surface ("Fix the framing", flip speaker, switch layout, nudge/zoom crop, per-shot Reset, "Re-render N shots"), backed by 100%-covered pure logic in `app/renderer/src/lib/reframeOverride.ts`.
Two independent probes confirm it is unreachable:
(1) repo-wide grep for `ReframeOverridePanel` returns only the component itself, `panels/ReframeOverridePanel.test.tsx`, `.audit/classify_branches.json`, and `docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46` — no import site.
(2) grep for `panels/` imports across `app/renderer/src` returns only `views/Settings.tsx:46` (ModelsSystemPanel) and `views/Director.tsx:22` (DirectorPanel); grep for `import(` returns no dynamic specifier that could reach it.
The plan names it explicitly as an unbuilt sub-unit: `docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46` "PROMOTE reframe-to-vertical to first-class (wire the orphaned ReframeOverridePanel)" and `:76` "WU-3a: SPLIT into >=4 ADDITIVE sub-units (Task Hub / 13->4 tab regroup / ReframeOverridePanel wiring / ShortMaker single-source-by-deep-link)" — the other three shipped (WU-3a1/3a2/3a4 tags are live in the code); the wiring one did not.
- why: Nielsen #3 (user control/undo) and #9 (help users recover from errors). Active-speaker detection is probabilistic — the panel's own header says so (`ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:3-5` "Makes an imperfect active-speaker-detection (ASD) result shippable"). When the auto-reframe follows the wrong person or crops off a subject, the shipping UI offers zero recourse: no flip, no nudge, no crop edit, no per-shot re-render. The user's only move is to re-run the whole export with a different engine and hope. Because the panel is 100% unit-covered in isolation, the coverage gate stays green and nothing flags the orphan.
- fix: Mount it. The natural host is the review stage after `shortmaker.select` (beside `CandidateReview`, `features/ShortMaker.tsx:943-963`) or as a step on the reframe destination, wired to the R1 per-shot re-render with the `affectedShotIndices` set the panel already computes (`ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:118`). Add a smoke test that asserts the panel renders from a real user path, not only in isolation.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED with a re-scoped fix and severity basis: `ReframeOverridePanel` (`app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:73-158`) plus its 100%-covered pure logic (`app/renderer/src/lib/reframeOverride.ts`), its RPC pair (`app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:759-772`) and its sidecar decision layer (`sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_override.py`) are all built and tested, yet nothing in the shipping renderer imports the panel or calls `client.reframe.*` — so the user has no in-app way to flip the followed speaker, switch layout, nudge/zoom a crop, or re-render a single shot when auto-reframe follows the wrong person. Two corrections to the finding: (1) "Mount it" is NOT the whole fix — the panel's `onRerender` has no consumer anywhere (no per-shot re-render exists; `reframe_override.py:17` defers it to R1 and no R1 code implements it) and `reframe.shotPlan`'s required `trace` has no producer reachable from the renderer (no handler returns a `ReframeTrace`), so wiring requires trace emission + a trace-fetch RPC + a per-shot re-render engine + the mount, i.e. 4 pieces not 1; (2) the panel's ShotPlan derives only from the R1 `reframe_multispeaker` trace, and that engine is a non-default explicit opt-in (`features/shortMakerLogic.ts:257-271`, DEFAULT = `auto`), so even fully wired the panel serves only R1 users — the missing-correction-path gap is broader than the panel-shaped fix, and the smallest honest first step is a smoke test asserting the panel renders from a real user path plus an orphan-module gate (knip/ts-prune) so a 100%-covered unmounted surface can no longer pass every gate.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped version — the DIAGNOSIS stands as written; only the remediation must be re-scoped:

"WU-3a3 never shipped: the entire Lane-R manual-reframe-correction rail is built and unit-tested but unreachable from the shipping app — the panel (`app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.tsx`), its pure logic (`app/renderer/src/lib/reframeOverride.ts`), its RPC client methods (`app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:759-773`), and its registered sidecar handlers (`sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_override.py:432-433`) all have zero production callers, and the panel is tree-shaken out of the built bundle entirely (absent from `app/out/renderer/assets/`). Consequently a mis-framed auto-crop has no in-app framing correction: Export never re-crops (`exportModel.ts:13`), the mounted Director's `reframe` op is only a center-crop-to-aspect (`director_op_engines.py:771-793`), and CandidateReview's nudge moves clip time, not crop (`ShortMaker.tsx:582-584`). The only recourse is re-running with a different engine (`ShortMakerControls.tsx:167-179`).

FIX IS NOT 'mount it' — it is three work units, and the finding's premise that the re-render already exists is FALSE:
 (1) Persist/emit the ReframeTrace: `reframe_multispeaker.py:1438-1453` builds it and throws it away, returning only an output path — the panel currently has no data source.
 (2) Build a per-shot subset re-render RPC: none exists. Both shipped `reframe.*` RPCs are pure compose (`reframe_override.py:32-33`); the per-shot re-render is aspirational throughout (`:17`, `:406`, `:5-7` 'once it lands').
 (3) Only then mount the panel (host: beside `CandidateReview`, `ShortMaker.tsx:943-963`) and add a smoke test asserting it renders from a real user path.

Severity: keep high on user impact (probabilistic ASD with zero recourse), but label it UNSHIPPED PLANNED WORK rather than a regression — `docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46,76` names it, no changelog claims it shipped, and remediation is a feature-sized effort, not a wiring one."
- ⚠ scope correction: ReframeOverridePanel is built, tested, and sits on a fully registered sidecar+RPC stack, but is never mounted — so a wrong auto-crop has no correction path. Correctly scoped:

SEVERITY: medium-high, not high. The multi-shot ASD failure the panel corrects only arises on an EXPLICIT opt-in engine — sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:360-362 states reframe_multispeaker is "EXPLICIT opt-in only — 'auto' stays claudeshorts", so the default path resolves to the single-speaker claudeshorts engine. It additionally requires WSL/GPU plus cached weights (availability_reason gate, sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_multispeaker.py:1388). Blast radius is opt-in multi-speaker users, not every user.

DROP the clause "nothing flags the orphan" — REFUTED. docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46 explicitly names "the orphaned ReframeOverridePanel" and :76 tracks "ReframeOverridePanel wiring" as a WU-3a sub-unit. It is known, tracked, deferred work. Only the narrower observation survives: the coverage gate stays green because the panel is 100% covered in isolation, so no AUTOMATED gate flags it.

REPLACE the fix "Mount it" — it understates the work by two missing dependencies, neither of which exists today:
(1) No trace reaches the renderer. reframe.shotPlan requires a `trace` argument (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:762), but MultiSpeakerReframeEngine.reframe() returns only `str`, the output path (sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_multispeaker.py:1371-1379). The ReframeTrace built at :913 never escapes the sidecar, and sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py contains zero "trace" references, as does app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts.
(2) No per-shot re-render entry point exists. sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_override.py:17 states "the heavy per-shot re-render is the R1 engine's job", and :5-7 defers the R1-produced plan to "once it lands". The engine only re-renders the whole clip to out_path.
So the real fix is a three-part build — surface/persist the trace to the renderer, add a shot-subset re-render entry point, THEN mount the panel and add a smoke test asserting it renders from a real user path. The panel's affectedShotIndices output (ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:118) currently has no consumer to hand the set to.

## Timeline cue blocks and the playhead are drawn with background-tone + inset box-shadow only (no real border) — they become 1.00:1 invisible when the OS forces a palette
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `dark-light-parity` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `.timeline__cue` has NO `border` property anywhere — its hairline is an inset box-shadow: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1651-1659` (`background: var(--surface-active)`) and `app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:29-40` (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--edge)`). Selected state likewise: `app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:43-50` (`background: var(--accent-soft); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--accent-edge), 0 0 10px var(--accent-soft)`). Playhead: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1686-1693` + `app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:72-75` (`background: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent-edge)`), rendered as a 1px-wide div at `app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:441-449`. Cue divs at `app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:409-421` carry only inline `left/width/top/bottom`.

EXECUTABLE PROOF (same probe):
```
=== forcedColors=active  colorScheme=light ===
  lane_bgColor          = rgb(255,255,255)
  cue_bgColor           = rgb(255,255,255)   <-- identical to the lane, 1.00:1
  cue_boxShadow         = none
  cue_borderWidth       = 0px
  cueSelected_bgColor   = rgba(255,255,255,0.14)
  cueSelected_boxShadow = none
  playhead_bgColor      = rgb(255,255,255)
  playhead_boxShadow    = none
=== forcedColors=active  colorScheme=dark ===
  lane_bgColor = rgb(0,0,0) ; cue_bgColor = rgb(0,0,0) ; playhead_bgColor = rgb(0,0,0)
```
(Baseline `forcedColors=none`: cue `rgb(53,63,86)` on lane `rgb(11,13,18)` — clearly visible.)
- why: The Timeline is the Edit phase's cue-editing tool. With every cue rectangle painted exactly the lane color, no border, and no shadow, a user in a Windows contrast theme sees a blank strip: they cannot see how many cues exist, which one is selected, where the playhead is, or where to click to seek. The panel is functionally dead. This is the specific failure mode of the tokens.css design rule at line 7 — "depth comes from the surface ladder + shadow, not borders-everywhere" — which is exactly the pattern forced-colors erases.
- fix: Convert the tone/shadow-only affordances to real borders so `border-style` survives, and add the one missing media query. In `app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css`:
```css
.timeline .timeline__cue { border: 1px solid var(--edge); box-shadow: none; }
.timeline .timeline__cue--selected { border-color: var(--accent-edge); }
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .timeline .timeline__cue { border-color: CanvasText; }
  .timeline .timeline__cue--selected { border: 2px solid Highlight; }
  .timeline .timeline__playhead { background: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none; }
}
```
(Compensate the 1px border in `cueRectStyle` box-sizing if the lane math assumes a borderless box — `*` is already `border-box` per `shell.css:21-25`, so no change needed.)
- ⚠ scope correction: Keep the finding as CONFIRMED at high severity; only tighten the impact sentence. Instead of "The panel is functionally dead", say: "The cue lane is functionally dead — the cue rectangles and the playhead all paint exactly the lane color (1.00:1) with box-shadow forced to none and no border to fall back on, so the user cannot see how many cues exist, which one is selected, where the playhead is, or where to click to seek. The Timeline's toolbar buttons and cue-editor inputs remain visible (native form controls keep UA-forced borders), but reaching the editor requires a blind click on an invisible cue."
- ⚠ scope correction: In the Workspace "Timeline" panel, the in-lane GRAPHICAL layer is drawn only with properties that forced-colors erases (background-colour tone + box-shadow, zero `border`): cue rectangles (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1651-1659 + app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:29-40), the selected-cue wash (app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:43-50), the selected cue's amber drag-grip pull-tabs (app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:53-61), and the 1px playhead (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1686-1693 + app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:72-75, width pinned to 1 inline at app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:449). Under `forced-colors: active` all four composite to exactly the lane colour - measured 0 of 920 px on the cue row differing from lane background, in BOTH light (Canvas #fff) and dark (Canvas #000). This is a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA) failure: cue count, cue positions and durations, which cue is selected POSITIONALLY, the drag-to-retime edge handles, and the playhead position all become unavailable, so direct-manipulation editing inside the lane is unusable. It does NOT make the panel functionally dead. The waveform canvas still renders (2.04:1 forced-light, 7.61:1 forced-dark) because app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:209 reads its colour from the custom property `--timeline-wave` (-> `--text-faint` #a6aebd) and custom properties plus canvas bitmaps are outside the forced-colors substitution set, so the time axis and the lane's clickable extent stay visible and click-to-seek still works. The Split/Merge/Undo/Redo/Save toolbar and the whole cue editor (text + start/end number inputs) render at 21:1 with surviving 1px CanvasText borders, so every edit remains reachable by numeric entry, and since the editor renders only for the selected cue (app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:499) the user can still identify the selected cue and its exact times. Scope note: there is ZERO forced-colors handling anywhere under app/ (0 matches for forced-colors|forced-color-adjust), so this is one instance of an app-wide gap rather than a Timeline-only bug. The border-based fix is the right shape and is already proven in the same file - the toolbar buttons survive forced-colors precisely because they use a real `border: 1px solid var(--edge)` - but it must also clear the inset shadows at app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:37-40 and app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1665-1668, which the proposed patch leaves in place.
- ⚠ scope correction: Timeline cue blocks, the selected-cue highlight, its amber drag grips and the playhead are drawn with background-tone + inset box-shadow only (no real border), so under forced-colors they render pixel-identical to the lane (1.00:1) and disappear. MEASURED (Playwright forcedColors emulation, pixel readback): the whole 920px cue row collapses to exactly 1 distinct colour — rgb(255,255,255) light / rgb(0,0,0) dark — vs 29 colours at baseline. Evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1651-1659, 1686-1693; app/renderer/src/features/timeline.css:29-35, 43-50, 53-61, 72-75; app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:409-421, 449. No `forced-colors` block exists anywhere under app/.

SEVERITY: MEDIUM, not high. The panel is degraded to blind-but-operable, NOT dead: (a) the canvas waveform is exempt from forced-color-adjust and stays visible (measured rgb(149,156,169) on black, ~7.6:1), so the time axis survives and the lane is NOT a blank strip; (b) cues remain hit-testable and click-to-select still works (Timeline.tsx:246-256, shell.css:1657); (c) every editing operation — cue text, numeric Start/End retime, Split, Merge, Undo, Redo, Save — is text/number based and fully legible under forced colors (Timeline.tsx:311-321, 454-534). What is genuinely lost is the visual overview: cue count/boundaries, which cue is selected on the strip, the drag grips, and playhead position.

RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED: OS→packaged-Electron propagation is UNVERIFIED — both this and the original probe use Playwright's DevTools `forcedColors` emulation, not a real Win11 Contrast theme against the built 1.4.2 binary; nothing in app/main suppresses forced colors. The proposed fix is sound (border-color → CanvasText survives; `*` is already border-box per shell.css:21-25), but it should be a shared forced-colors block, since the same tone+inset-hairline pattern appears at shell.css:701, 776, 1551, 1610 and 1667.

## Make Shorts panel is not a scroll container: the produced-shorts gallery scrolls the WHOLE window and pushes the app bar + nav rail off-screen
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:201 renders `<div className="make-shorts__panel">`, but NO CSS rule for `.make-shorts__panel` exists anywhere (Grep `make-shorts__panel` over the repo returns only MakeShorts.tsx:201; 0 hits in any *.css). Its parent app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css:8-12 `.make-shorts { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap: var(--space-3) }` sets no `height`, `min-height:0` or `overflow`, so the bounded stage handed down by app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:326-329 (`.app__main > * { flex: 1; min-height: 0 }`) is dropped one level in. Consequence: app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:13 `.shorts { height: 100% }` resolves against an indefinite height (=auto) and app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:188 `.shorts__grid { overflow: auto }` never becomes a scroller.

MEASURED in Chromium against the real stylesheets (tokens.css + shell.css + topTabBar.css + makeShorts.css + shorts.css) with a DOM mirroring MakeShorts.tsx:199-201 -> Shorts.tsx:163-249:
- DEFAULT window 1280x820 (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039), 6 clips: documentElement.scrollHeight 1340 vs clientHeight 820; `.make-shorts__panel` height 1249 vs `.app__main` height 774; `.shorts__grid` clientHeight === scrollHeight (its overflow:auto is inert). 4 clips = no overflow, so the defect starts at the 5th produced clip.
- MIN window 940x600 (app/main/main.ts:1040-1041), 24 clips: doc scrollHeight 4394 / clientHeight 600; panel height 4303.
- `window.scrollTo(0,900)` -> `.app__bar` getBoundingClientRect().top = -900 and the `.toptabs` rail bottom = -300: header toggles, Jobs pill and the ENTIRE left nav rail leave the viewport.
- BOTH-STATES CONTROL: the identical `.shorts` markup + 24 cards mounted inside `.settings__panel` (app/renderer/src/views/settings.css:12-15 `flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto`) -> docScrollsY false, `.shorts__grid` scrolls internally (clientHeight 396 / scrollHeight 4247), chrome stays pinned. So the probe fires only in the broken state.
- The Batch sub-tab has the same gap one level deeper: app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:29-34 renders `.repurpose__panel` and Grep `\.repurpose` over *.css returns 0 hits. Measured @940x600 with 20 sources + 12 live rows: doc 629 / client 600.

Why CI misses it: app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37-38,76-77 pins 1280x820 and app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts:49 snapshots `win` (viewport-only, no `fullPage`) on a seeded app with no produced shorts; app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx has zero scroll/overflow assertions (jsdom cannot measure layout).
- why: Every sibling view keeps its chrome fixed and scrolls its own panel (settings.css:12-15, shell.css:1017-1021 `.workspace__body { flex:1; overflow:auto }`, shell.css:815-820 `.library__list { overflow:auto }`). Make Shorts is the outlier — the same class of one-view-forgot-it defect as the missing `role="tabpanel"`/`id` axe violation on the very next line. A user with 5+ produced clips at the shipped default window loses the nav rail, the AI-model/routing toggles, the Jobs pill AND the gallery's own Sort toggle as soon as they scroll to reach a card; they must scroll back to the top to navigate anywhere. The gallery also loses its sticky-header design intent.
- fix: Restore the bounded chain in app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css so `.shorts__grid`'s existing `overflow:auto` becomes the scroller (exactly as it already does under `.settings__panel`):

.make-shorts { height: 100%; min-height: 0; }
.make-shorts__panel { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.make-shorts__panel > * { flex: 1; min-height: 0; }

The Make sub-tab's own long column (`.make-shorts__make`) needs `overflow: auto` since it has no inner scroller. Add the matching pair for the Batch sub-tab (`.repurpose { display:flex; flex-direction:column; min-height:0; height:100% }` + `.repurpose__panel { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto }`) — fixing only `.make-shorts__panel` leaves Batch broken. Guard it with an e2e assertion that `documentElement.scrollHeight === clientHeight` on the Make Shorts tab with >=6 seeded shorts (a viewport-only screenshot cannot see this).
- ⚠ scope correction: Neither `.make-shorts__panel` nor `.repurpose__panel` has ANY CSS rule (0 hits repo-wide in *.css), so the Make Shorts sub-panel never becomes a scroll container: `.make-shorts` receives the bounded stage from shell.css:326-329 (`.app__main > *{flex:1;min-height:0}`), but `.make-shorts__panel` keeps the default `flex:0 1 auto`/`min-height:auto`, grows to content height, and — because no ancestor sets `overflow:hidden` (shell.css:9-19, :70-79, :316-324) — the overflow reaches the viewport and the DOCUMENT scrolls. `.shorts{height:100%}` (shorts.css:13) then resolves against an indefinite height and `.shorts__grid{overflow:auto}` (shorts.css:188) stays inert. Because `.app__bar` (shell.css:92) and `.toptabs` (topTabBar.css:26) are both `position:relative`, scrolling to reach a card pushes the app bar and the left nav rail out of the viewport. MEASURED at the shipped default 1280x820 (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039): docScrollsY=true, doc 1067/820, panel 976 vs `.app__main` 774, `.shorts__grid` clientHeight===scrollHeight; at the 940x600 minimum (main.ts:1040-1041) with 24 clips: doc 3683/600 and after scrolling `app__bar.top=-900`, `toptabs.bottom=-300` (both fully off-screen). Control: the same `.shorts` markup under `.settings__panel` (settings.css:12-15) does NOT scroll the document and the grid scrolls internally (616/2644), so the probe fires only in the broken state.

SCOPE CORRECTION (this is the part the original finding got wrong): Make Shorts is NOT the outlier. The identical "root bounded by `.app__main > *` but no inner scroller" gap also exists in three other views mounted directly under `.app__main` — `.caption-view` (caption.css:3-9) with `.caption-view__body` (caption.css:58-63), `.export-view` (export.css:3-9) with `.export-view__body` (export.css:49-54), and `.deliver-view` (deliver.css, which contains ZERO `overflow` declarations) — plus `.task-hub` (taskHub.css:7-14). Injected with non-shrinkable content these leak identically (doc=1942/820, app__bar.top=-1122, toptabs.bottom=-302). Only Library/Workspace (shell.css:503-510 + `.library__list` :819 / `.workspace__body` :1019) and Settings (settings.css:5-17) actually hold the chain.

SEVERITY SPLIT: Make Shorts / Batch is DEFINITELY LIVE and the highest priority because the gallery's height grows without bound with the number of produced clips, so it will exceed any viewport. Caption / Export / Deliver / Task Hub share the same missing-scroller mechanism but it is UNVERIFIED whether their real content ever exceeds the stage (a real Deliver markup mirror at 4 sections still fit inside 774px) — treat those as latent until measured with seeded real content. FIX: apply the bounded pair (`flex:1; min-height:0` on the panel, with `overflow:auto` on whichever descendant should scroll) to all of them, not just `.make-shorts__panel`, and guard with an e2e assertion that `documentElement.scrollHeight === clientHeight` per view — app/e2e currently contains zero `overflow`/`scrollHeight`/`clientHeight`/`scrollTo` assertions, and app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts snapshots viewport-only (no fullPage), which cannot see this.

Consequence: `.shorts` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:13 `height:100%`) resolves against an indefinite height and `.shorts__grid`'s `overflow:auto` (shorts.css:188) never becomes a scroller — measured clientHeight === scrollHeight in every overflowing state.

Measured in the real built Electron app at the shipped default 1280x820 (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039): selecting a video on the Make sub-tab with ZERO produced shorts already gives documentElement.scrollHeight 1689 vs clientHeight 820; the Gallery crosses over at the 5th produced clip (4 cards bounded 820/820, 5 cards 1239/820) and reaches 3335/820 at 24. `window.scrollTo(0,900)` puts `.app__bar` at top -900 and the `.toptabs` rail bottom at -80, so the header toggles, the Jobs pill and the entire left nav rail leave the viewport and the user must scroll back up to navigate. Scope corrections vs. the original finding: (a) Make Shorts is the WORST case, not the only one — the Director view also scrolls the document at the 940x600 min window (700/600); (b) the Batch sub-tab shares the structural gap (`.repurpose`/`.repurpose__panel` have zero CSS, and `.repurpose` only ever mounts nested inside `.make-shorts__panel`) but I could not reproduce the cited 629/600 measurement — Batch measured bounded at both window sizes with `.repurpose` only 114px tall, so that half of the fix is justified structurally, UNVERIFIED at real content volume; (c) the comparison to the dangling `aria-controls` axe violation is stale — PR #308 (27e7189b) fixed it and MakeShorts.tsx:206-211 now carries `role="tabpanel"`/`id`/`aria-labelledby`.

Not caught by CI because app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37-38,76-77 pins 1280x820 and app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts:49 takes a viewport-only screenshot (`fullPage` appears 0 times in app/e2e/visual/*.ts) on a seeded app with no produced shorts and no video selected, while app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx has 0 scroll/overflow assertions (jsdom cannot measure layout). Guard the fix with an e2e assertion that `documentElement.scrollHeight === clientHeight` on the Make Shorts tab both with a video selected and with >=6 seeded shorts.

## The whole Batch surface ships with ZERO CSS: source checkboxes flow as inline text, 2-3 per line, and 7 of 20 labels split across lines separating a checkbox from its video title
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Grep `batch-queue` restricted to *.css returns 0 files across the entire renderer. app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:31 imports `./panels.css`, but that sheet only styles `.feature-panel` and named panels (app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:12, :23, :32, :48, :116, :177 ...), and the shared control voices in shell.css are scoped to `.feature-panel` / `.shortmaker` / `.timeline__toolbar` / `.library__*` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:341-346 buttons, :451-459 inputs). The section root `.batch-queue` (BatchQueue.tsx:261) matches none of them, so nothing styles `.batch-queue__setup` (:286), `.batch-queue__sources` (:287), `.batch-queue__source` (:290), `.batch-queue__template` (:301), `.batch-queue__run` (:318) or `.batch-queue__rows/__row` (:344-346).

MEASURED in Chromium at the minimum window 940x600 (app/main/main.ts:1040-1041 -> 740px stage after the 200px rail from topTabBar.css:16), with 20 seeded sources carrying realistic multi-word titles:
- `.batch-queue__source` computed `display: inline` (UA default for <label>) -> the 20 checkboxes flow as one paragraph across 8 lines, packing 2 or 3 per line (measured per-line counts: 3,3,2,3,2,2,3,2).
- 7 of the 20 labels return more than one client rect, i.e. the label is broken across two lines with its <input type=checkbox> on a different line from part of its title.
- The controls are raw UA dark-mode natives, off the token system: `<select>` computed background rgb(59,59,59), `.batch-queue__run` background rgb(107,107,107), `appearance: auto`. Compare app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css:34-54, whose comment documents fixing exactly this class of bug for the Make picker ("the picker fell back to a raw native OS <select> ... that broke the dark-editorial theme").
- `.batch-queue__run` measured height 23px, under the `--size-target-min: 24px` floor declared at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:192.
- why: This is the one destructive-cost control on the surface: BatchQueue.tsx:188 creates a batch over exactly the checked `selected` ids and BatchQueue.tsx:213/225 starts it. When checkbox N sits visually beside title N+1 (or beside the tail of a title that wrapped from the previous line), the user cannot verify what they selected, and the mis-read gets worse the longer the library and the narrower the window — the failure mode is 'ran the batch on the wrong sources', not just 'looks unstyled'. The inline packing is unconditional (`display:inline`); the 7/20 mid-label split figure is title-length dependent, so on short titles you get dense multi-per-line packing without the split.
- fix: Add a `.batch-queue` block to app/renderer/src/features/panels.css (or a new batchQueue.css imported at BatchQueue.tsx:31) that at minimum makes the source list a real list and puts the controls on the token system:

.batch-queue__sources { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); border: 1px solid var(--edge); border-radius: var(--radius-md); }
.batch-queue__source { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); min-height: var(--size-target-min); }
.batch-queue__setup { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: var(--space-4); }
.batch-queue__rows { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
.batch-queue__row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-4); min-width: 0; }

Cheapest correct route for the controls: add `.batch-queue` to the existing shared selector lists at shell.css:341-346 and shell.css:451-459 (and the accent rule at shell.css:409-420 for `.batch-queue__run`) so the batch surface inherits the same button/input voice as every other panel, then re-check `.batch-queue__run` clears the 24px target floor.
- ⚠ scope correction: Headline overclaim ("ZERO CSS") corrected; the body was right. Correctly scoped:

"Every `.batch-queue__*` layout class is unstyled: `batch-queue` matches zero rules in any .css file repo-wide, the only sheet BatchQueue.tsx:31 imports (panels.css) contains only `.feature-panel*`/`.<name>-panel*` selectors, and the shared token voices at shell.css:344-346/:452-459/:410-414 are `.feature-panel`/`.shortmaker`/`.timeline__toolbar`-scoped descendant selectors that the actual ancestor chain never satisfies (`.make-shorts` > `.make-shorts__panel` > `.repurpose` > `.repurpose__panel` > `.batch-queue`, and `.deliver-view` > `.deliver-view__panel` > `.batch-queue`). Consequently `.batch-queue__source` (BatchQueue.tsx:290) computes UA `display: inline` and the source checkboxes flow as inline text inside the `<fieldset>` at :287, packing multiple per line and — at sufficient title length — splitting a label mid-way so its `<input type=checkbox>` sits on a different line from part of its title. The controls (`.batch-queue__template` select at :303, `.batch-queue__run` at :316) render as `appearance: auto` natives off the token system."

Three scope fixes: (a) NOT literally zero CSS — the `ProgressBar` child (BatchQueue.tsx:343) is fully styled at shell.css:1094-1121, the global focus ring (shell.css:49) and `box-sizing` reset (:21-24) apply, and body typography inherits from shell.css:14-18; only the `.batch-queue__*` classes are unstyled. (b) The specific per-line counts (3,3,2,3,2,2,3,2), the 7-of-20 mid-label split and the 23px button height are the reporter's own-seed measurements, not independently reproduced — the `display:inline` mechanism is deterministic, the tallies are title-length- and harness-dependent. (c) Surface attribution is loose and understates reach: the batch surface is Make Shorts -> "Batch & Templates" (MakeShorts.tsx:50/:213), not the gallery, and it is ALSO the DEFAULT landing of the Deliver rail (Deliver.tsx:41/:71) — it renders on first open of that tab.

Scope the severity honestly: impact scales with library size (`videos` comes from `client.library.list()`), so at 1-3 sources it is cosmetic; the "wrong sources" risk needs a non-trivial library. It is genuinely unmitigated at that point, since the consent card never lists the RUN set (BatchConsentCard.tsx:39-56). Settling experiment: seed the library at N=20 with real titles, open Deliver (no clicks needed), and assert `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.batch-queue__source')).display === 'flex'` plus `getClientRects().length === 1` for every source label.

(1) Literalism: "ZERO CSS" should read "zero CSS matching any `.batch-queue*` class". Two global rules do reach the subtree — app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:335 `button { font-family: inherit }` (verified live: the run button resolves fontFamily "Inter, Geist, system-ui, ...") and shell.css:49 `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible`. Nothing else does; the fix and the severity are unaffected.

(2) Scope is WIDER than claimed, not narrower — three additions the finding missed:

Both siblings also import panels.css (TemplateEditor.tsx:17, ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:18) and match nothing in it.

- The 24px target breach is worse on the `<select>` (measured 19px) than on `.batch-queue__run` (22px measured / 23px reported); the proposed fix should clear `--size-target-min` on both, and should add `accent-color: var(--accent)` to `.batch-queue__source input` to match the sanctioned checkbox treatment at shortmaker-p3.css:20 / library-cards.css:172 / shell.css:1199.

Correctly-scoped headline: "The Make Shorts -> Batch & Templates surface (and the same BatchQueue reused at Deliver -> Batch publish) has no author CSS for any of its own classes in either source or the built bundle: source checkboxes are UA-default inline labels that pack multiple-per-line and split checkbox from title, and the select/button/checkbox render as raw dark-mode UA natives, with both the select (19px) and the Run button (22px) under the declared --size-target-min: 24px floor."
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding stands; two sub-claims need tightening before it ships. (1) Scope "ZERO CSS": no COMPONENT CSS targets any .batch-queue__* or .batch-consent* class (0 hits across every *.css), but the global base in shell.css does still reach the subtree — html/body/#root background+color+font-family (shell.css:9-19), universal box-sizing (:21-25), the :where(...) focus-visible ring (:49-52), the reduced-motion block (:54-61) and `button { font-family: inherit }` (:335-337). Say "no layout or control-voice CSS", not "zero CSS". (2) "the one destructive-cost control" overstates the failure mode: a batch run CREATES output clips, it does not delete or overwrite user data — the real cost is wasted multi-video render time plus metered cloud spend (the confirmCloudBudget / spend-cap path), so the accurate wording is "costly and not un-spendable", not "destructive". (3) Report the split figure as measured-with-your-titles: at 940x600 with Inter loaded I reproduce 7 lines at 4,3,3,3,3,2,2 and 6 of 20 labels split, so state it as "5-7 of 20 labels split, title-length dependent; the inline packing itself is unconditional (display:inline)". Add the uncited adjacent defect: .batch-queue__rows renders as a UA bulleted list (list-style disc, padding-left 40px) with title and status concatenated with no separator ("...Burnoutrunning"), BatchQueue.tsx:344-350.

## Two live, divergent "Caption style" controls on one screen; which one applies depends on which button you press
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: MakeShorts.tsx:225-238 (AI section) and MakeShorts.tsx:241-254 (Caption & style) are sibling children of the same fragment (MakeShorts.tsx:223-278), so BOTH caption-style controls are on screen at once:
  (a) ShortMakerControls.tsx:151-164 — a <select aria-label="Caption style"> bound to `controls.captionStyle`;
  (b) CaptionDesigner.tsx:145-149 -> CaptionStylePicker.tsx:45,50-74 — a 17-swatch grid bound to `design.style` (no `styles` prop is passed at MakeShorts.tsx:247-253, so it defaults to ALL_CAPTION_STYLES = 17 entries, shortMakerLogic.ts:202-249).
The sync is ONE-WAY and ONCE-ONLY: MakeShorts.tsx:233-236 passes `initialControls`, and ShortMaker.tsx:161-163 reads it in a lazy `useState` initializer. `initialControls` occurs at exactly three places in ShortMaker.tsx — :141 (prop type), :155 (destructure), :162 (initializer) — with NO syncing `useEffect`, and MakeShorts.tsx:230 renders <ShortMaker> without a `key`, so the instance is never remounted on a design change.
Divergent consumers: the AI path exports with `controls.captionStyle` (ShortMaker.tsx:632,651 -> buildExportParams), the manual path with `captionDesignWire(design)` (MakeShorts.tsx:161-171; captionDesign.ts:52-59). A third setter, the Brand kit's "Default caption template" (ShortMakerBrandKit.tsx:86-100), seeds only `controls.captionStyle` (ShortMaker.tsx:314-325).
Untested: MakeShorts.test.tsx:426-439 asserts only the designer's own `data-style`, though the mock already exposes `data-init-caption-style` (MakeShorts.test.tsx:84) and never checks it.
- why: The surface presents one concept ("Caption style") through two identically-named, simultaneously-visible controls that hold different values. A user picks "MrBeast (yellow pop)" in the swatch grid, the dropdown 40px above still reads "Classic (libass, fast)", and the style that actually ships depends on whether they press "Find clips"/"Make N shorts" (uses the dropdown) or "Make shorts from ranges" (uses the swatch). The live caption preview reinforces the wrong expectation for the AI path — it previews `design.style`, which the AI export ignores. This is the exact failure mode disclosure prevents: duplicate controls with no visible ownership.
- fix: Make `design` the single source of truth for caption look on this surface and delete the duplicate. Remove the "Caption style" <select> from ShortMakerControls.tsx:151-164 on the Make front door, and pass the live design down as a controlled prop (`captionStyle={design.style}` + `onCaptionStyleChange`) instead of the fire-once `initialControls` (MakeShorts.tsx:233-236). If the dropdown must stay for the Batch/Workspace hosts, gate it behind that host rather than rendering it beside the designer. Add a regression test asserting the ShortMaker mock's `data-init-caption-style` follows `designer-pick-karaoke` (extend MakeShorts.test.tsx:426-439).

They are on the same scroll surface, NOT necessarily in one viewport — the intervening reframe/audio selects, 8 toggles, presets row, actions row and brand-kit disclosure make the "40px apart" figure wrong (exact pixel separation UNVERIFIED; jsdom has no layout, so it needs a real-browser measurement or a Playwright boundingBox check to settle). Measured consequence in ONE session: pick "MrBeast (yellow pop)" in the grid -> grid reads mrbeast, dropdown still reads libass; the AI flow ships captionStyle:"libass" (shortmaker.select payload; export at ShortMaker.tsx:632/651 and the batch button at :708/746 both use sanitizeControls(controls) -> shortMakerPresets.ts:171) while "Make shorts from ranges" ships captionStyle:"mrbeast" (MakeShorts.tsx:161-171 -> captionDesign.ts:52-59). `ShortMaker` seeds `controls` from `initialControls` exactly once, in a lazy `useState` initializer (ShortMaker.tsx:161-163; the prop occurs only at :141, :155, :162), with no syncing effect and no `key` at the render site (MakeShorts.tsx:240). The AND is test-pinned: MakeShorts.test.tsx:296-303 'reveals AI moment-pick + manual intervals once a video is selected'.

Two collapsed panels exist alongside 52 exposed controls, so the disclosure budget is spent on the two smallest groups.
