## Workspace tab strip has no length budget: it already wraps and clips at the default 1280px window in English, and the persistent Export action is pushed off-screen
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `i18n-length` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Committed baseline `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png` (viewport pinned to 1280x820 by `app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37` and `app/main/main.ts:1038-1039`) shows, in English, at the DEFAULT window size: (a) `SHORT-MAKER` rendered on two lines (`SHORT-` / `MAKER`), (b) `TIMELINE EXPORT` rendered on two lines, (c) the strip clipped mid-word at the right edge (`ASSE` for the ASSETS tab), (d) a horizontal scrollbar under the strip, (e) the `Advanced` toggle and the `Export` button not visible at all.

Mechanism A - no nowrap guard: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1041-1058` defines `.tab` with `text-transform: uppercase` + `letter-spacing: var(--type-caption-tracking)` (0.08em, tokens.css:152) and NO `white-space` declaration. `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39` sets `.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto; flex: none; }` under the comment at `workspace.css:35` "8 tabs must survive narrow windows without wrapping the chrome" - but flex items shrink to their min-content size (longest word) BEFORE the container overflows, so multi-word labels wrap first and `overflow-x: auto` only engages afterwards. The chrome-level rail solves exactly this and says so: `app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:78-86` gives `.toptab__label` `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap;` with the comment "a long surface name can never force horizontal overflow". The workspace sub-tabs got no such guard.

Mechanism B - the budget is 13 tabs, not 8: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:53-67` now defines 13 `WORKSPACE_TABS`, plus 4 group captions that are pinned `white-space: nowrap` and therefore cannot shrink at all (`workspace.css:101-109`), plus `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` (`workspace.css:112-126`) and `.tabbar__export` which is also `white-space: nowrap` (`workspace.css:158-177`).

Aggravating cause (separate defect, cited because it is why the budget is blown): `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:231` renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`, but `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152` sets `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; }`, which overrides the UA `[hidden] { display: none }` rule. There is no author `[hidden]` reset anywhere in `app/renderer/src/**/*.css`. The e2e test never clicks Advanced (`surfaces.visual.spec.ts:93-101`), yet the baseline shows DELIVER / CONVERT / TIMELINE EXPORT / RECIPES / ASSETS rendered - so 5 extra tabs and a 5th nowrap group caption are always on the strip.
- why: This is the navigation the user must hit to reach Transcribe, and it is already over budget in the shortest language the app will ever ship. Any localization inflates it further: `Transcribe` -> `Transkribieren` (+40%), `Subtitles` -> `Untertitel`, `Search` -> `Suchen`, `Diarize` -> `Sprechertrennung`, and the uncompressible group captions grow too (`Speech & Text` -> `Sprache & Text`). Concretely: the `Export` button - added by design-review P1 specifically as "a persistent, standing affordance" for the user's terminal goal (`TabBar.tsx:48-56`, `workspace.css:154-157`) - is invisible without horizontal scrolling TODAY, and every extra character of translation pushes more of the strip (eventually the Transcribe tab itself, which sits leftmost) past the clip. The visual gate cannot catch the regression because the wrapped, clipped strip IS the accepted golden baseline.
- fix: 1) Add `white-space: nowrap` to `.tab` in `shell.css:1041` so a label never wraps mid-word and the strip degrades into the intended single-row scroller. 2) Fix the disclosure so the collapsed cluster really collapses - either drop `display: flex` from `workspace.css:148-152` and use a `[hidden]`-compatible pattern (`.tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]) { display: flex }`), or add a global `[hidden] { display: none !important }` reset; this also removes the keyboard inconsistency where `TabBar.tsx:151-158` excludes those visible tabs from arrow navigation. 3) Give `.tabbar__export` (and the Advanced toggle) `position: sticky; right: 0` inside the scroller, or move them out of the scrolling row, so the primary action is never scrolled away regardless of label length. 4) Add a long-label visual case: re-snapshot the workspace with a pseudo-localized label set (or simply a 1.5x-padded label fixture) so the strip's length budget is pinned by CI.
- ⚠ scope correction: Workspace tab strip has no length budget: in English at the default 1280px window it already wraps mid-word and clips, and the persistent Export action is off-screen. Correctly-scoped evidence from the committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png: (a) SHORT-MAKER renders on two lines (`SHORT-` / `MAKER`) - min-content, breaking at the hyphen; (b) the strip is clipped mid-word at the right edge on the CONVERT tab (visible as `CONV`) - NOT on ASSETS, which together with RECIPES and TRACKS is entirely off-screen beyond the clip; (c) a horizontal scrollbar thumb sits under the strip (shell.css:37-42 styling); (d) the Advanced toggle and the Export button are not visible at all. TIMELINE EXPORT is also past the clip, so its wrap is UNVERIFIED visually (expected from mechanism A but not shown). Mechanism A (no `white-space` on `.tab`, shell.css:1041-1058, vs the guard at topTabBar.css:80-86) and the aggravating cause (`display:flex` at workspace.css:148-152 defeating UA `[hidden]{display:none}` with no author reset anywhere in app/, so the collapsed Deliver cluster always renders) are both fully confirmed. Mechanism B is 13 tabs (Workspace.tsx:53-67) plus FOUR nowrap group captions (Workspace.tsx:76-90, not five), the Advanced toggle, and the nowrap Export button.
- ⚠ scope correction: Workspace tab strip has no length budget: at the DEFAULT 1280x820 window in English it already wraps multi-word tab labels mid-word and clips the strip, and the persistent Export action plus the Advanced toggle are scrolled out of view — and the committed visual baseline blesses that state.

CONFIRMED TODAY, IN ENGLISH (not a localization projection). Committed baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png (viewport pinned by app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37 and app/main/main.ts:1038-1039) shows SHORT-/MAKER and TIMELINE/EXPORT each broken onto two lines, the strip clipped mid-word at the right edge, a horizontal scrollbar, and neither the Advanced toggle nor the Export button visible. On current HEAD it is WORSE: the left nav rail cut usable width to ~1080px, so the strip now clips at CONV (Convert), putting TIMELINE EXPORT / RECIPES / ASSETS / Advanced / Export all off-screen.

Mechanism A — no nowrap guard: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1041-1058 gives `.tab` text-transform:uppercase + letter-spacing 0.08em (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:152) and NO white-space; an exhaustive grep confirms no rule anywhere in app/renderer/src/**/*.css gives `.tab` a nowrap guard. app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39 sets overflow-x:auto under the :35 comment "8 tabs must survive narrow windows without wrapping the chrome", but flex items shrink to min-content (longest word) BEFORE the container overflows, so labels wrap first and the scroller only engages afterwards. The chrome rail already solves exactly this at app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:78-86 (min-width:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap, commented "a long surface name can never force horizontal overflow"); the workspace sub-tabs got no equivalent.

Mechanism B — the budget is 13 tabs, not 8: app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:53-67 defines 13 WORKSPACE_TABS (including {id:'nle', label:'Timeline export'} at :64), plus FOUR pinned-nowrap group captions (workspace.css:101-109) that cannot shrink at all, plus `.tabbar__advanced-toggle` (:112-126) and `.tabbar__export`, which is nowrap at :172 and margin-left:auto at :160 INSIDE the scroller — so the primary action is scrolled away rather than pinned to the visible edge.

Aggravating cause (a separate, genuine functional + a11y defect): app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:231 renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`, but workspace.css:148-152 sets `display: flex` on it, and a grep for `[hidden]` across app/renderer/src returns ZERO matches — with no author reset the author rule overrides UA `[hidden]{display:none}`, so the "collapsed" Deliver cluster is permanently visible. app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts:93-101 never clicks Advanced, yet the baseline renders DELIVER/CONVERT/TIMELINE EXPORT/RECIPES/ASSETS — 5 extra tabs and a 4th nowrap caption always on the strip. Those visible tabs are simultaneously excluded from arrow-key navigation by TabBar.tsx:151-158, so keyboard reachability contradicts what is on screen.

CORRECTLY SCOPED RESIDUALS: (1) TRANSCRIBE will NOT be pushed past the clip — in an LTR overflow-x scroller at scrollLeft=0 the leftmost item stays anchored and growth clips the right edge only; the earlier claim that it eventually goes off-screen is mechanically wrong. (2) There is currently NO i18n infrastructure (no i18next/react-intl/useTranslation, no locale files in app/renderer/src) — localization inflation (Transcribe->Transkribieren, Diarize->Sprechertrennung) is FUTURE risk that would deepen this, not present evidence; the severity rests entirely on the English baseline. (3) The pixel-exact visual gate WOULD fail on a future layout change; its actual failure is that it accepts the present overflowing strip as correct, so it cannot flag this defect or measure remaining headroom.

FIX (unchanged in substance): add white-space:nowrap to `.tab` so the strip degrades into the intended single-row scroller; make the disclosure really collapse (`.tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]){display:flex}`, or a global `[hidden]{display:none !important}` reset), which also removes the arrow-nav inconsistency; give `.tabbar__export` and the Advanced toggle `position:sticky; right:0` or move them out of the scrolling row; and pin the length budget in CI with a long-label / pseudo-localized fixture case.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high), and it is a layout/disclosure defect, not an i18n-length defect. At the DEFAULT 1280x820 window (`app/main/main.ts:1038-1039`) in English, the workspace tab strip already wraps and clips: the committed golden `app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png` shows `SHORT-MAKER` broken onto two lines, a mid-word clip at the right edge (`CONV`), a horizontal scrollbar, and neither the Advanced toggle nor the persistent Export button on screen. Root cause is two-part: (1) `.tab` (`app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1041-1058`) has no `white-space` guard, so flex items floor at min-content and multi-word/hyphenated labels wrap before `overflow-x: auto` (`app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:36-39`) engages — the chrome rail already solves this at `app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:78-86`; and (2) `workspace.css:148-152` `display: flex` on `.tabbar__advanced-panel` is author-origin and defeats the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` on `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239` (no `[hidden]` reset exists anywhere in `app/renderer/src`), so the "collapsed" 5-tab Deliver cluster plus its nowrap caption render unconditionally — the progressive-disclosure feature is functionally broken and its unit test (`app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.test.tsx:92-98`) cannot detect it because it string-renders and regexes the `hidden` attribute with no CSS. Consequence: the design-review P1 requirement that Export be "a persistent, standing affordance" (`TabBar.tsx:48-56`, `workspace.css:154-157`) is not met at the shipped default size, and `minWidth: 940` (`app/main/main.ts:1040`) sanctions windows 340px narrower still. Export is NOT unreachable — the always-visible left rail carries top-level Export and Deliver (`app/renderer/src/App.tsx:458-459`) and the strip scrolls — so this is degraded discoverability plus a broken disclosure, not a blocked flow. Drop the i18n framing entirely: the repo has no i18n library, no locales directory, and hardcoded English labels (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:53-67`; the only `locale` references are `localeCompare` sorts), so translation inflation is speculative. Also drop the unsupported specifics: "TIMELINE EXPORT on two lines" (that tab is clipped off-screen, not wrapped), "`ASSE` for the ASSETS tab" (it is `CONV`), and "eventually the Transcribe tab itself past the clip" (impossible in LTR — `TRANSCRIBE` is fully visible at scroll-0). The claim that the visual gate cannot catch the regression stands: the wrapped, clipped strip is the accepted baseline.

## Live caption preview: hook title and caption line overlap and spill out of the phone stage (cqw units with no container-type anywhere)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/captionOverlay.css:25 (`clamp(0.9rem, 4.5cqw, 1.4rem)`) and :43 (`clamp(0.95rem, 5cqw, 1.55rem)`) size the overlay in CONTAINER-QUERY units, but `container-type`/`container:` appears NOWHERE in app/renderer/src/**/*.css (Grep for `container-type|container-name|cqw|cqi` returns exactly those two `cqw` lines and zero container declarations). With no eligible query container, cqw resolves against the small viewport, not the 248px stage (app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:20-22, `.sm-phone { width: min(248px, 100%) }`).

MEASURED in Chromium against the real stylesheets (harness at file:///C:/Users/Prekzursil/AppData/Local/Temp/rf-resp/caption.html):
  vw=1600 phone=248x441 line font=20.15px | vw=1280 → 20.15px | vw=924 → 20.15px | vw=640 → 20.15px | vw=320 → 16px
The stage is a CONSTANT 248px at every viewport yet the font tracks the VIEWPORT → viewport-derived, confirmed.
BOTH-STATES CONTROL (adds `container-type: inline-size` to .sm-phone): vw=1600 → 12.4px, vw=320 → 12.4px (constant = container-relative). The probe fires differently in the two states, so it measures something real.

OVERLAP MEASUREMENT (caption2.html, 17-word active phrase + 12-word hook, both on by default):
  AS SHIPPED, identical at vw=1600/1280/924: hook[top=22 h=126 bottom=148] line[top=-9 h=388] → OVERLAP=+157px, line top is -9px (ABOVE the stage, clipped by `.caption-overlay { overflow: hidden }` captionOverlay.css:11), text coverage = 117% of the 441px stage.
  WITH the container fix: hook[top=22 h=54 bottom=76] line[top=252 h=128] → 176px clearance, coverage 41%.

Reachable on DEFAULTS: app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:238 `DEFAULT_CAPTION_STYLE = 'libass'` (not 'none') and :295 `hookTitle: true`; app/renderer/src/features/CandidateReview.tsx:128-136 mounts CaptionOverlay for any non-'none' template and passes the hook when `controls.hookTitle`.
- why: CandidateReview.tsx:125-127 states this overlay exists so "the reviewer sees how captions would look" before approving a clip. At 20.15px inside a 248px stage the caption block is 388px tall in a 441px stage, collides with the hook title by 157px, and is clipped at the top — so the one surface the user relies on to judge caption styling shows an overlapping, cropped mess that does not resemble the 1080x1920 export. The bug is width-independent (the clamp max is hit at every reachable window size), so no amount of resizing relieves it.
- fix: Add `container-type: inline-size;` to `.shortmaker .sm-phone` in app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:20 (measured: keeps the 248x441 box intact, restores 12.4px/11.7px and 176px of hook clearance). Alternatively replace the `cqw` terms with `%`- or `em`-based sizing relative to the stage. Add a regression assertion that `getComputedStyle('.caption-overlay__line').fontSize` is invariant across two very different viewport widths.
- ⚠ scope correction: Do not drop the surface entirely — a narrower, differently-caused defect survives, at MEDIUM severity (cosmetic, preview-only; export unaffected):

"CandidateReview's live caption preview wraps at half the stage width, so long spoken phrases overlap the hook title. `.caption-overlay__line` is `position:absolute; left:50%` with `right:auto` (app/renderer/src/components/captionOverlay.css:33-34), so its shrink-to-fit available width is only 248-124 = 124px of the 248px stage and `max-width:92%` (228px) never binds (MEASURED: lineBoxW=124). The export wraps at 1000 of 1080px (92.6%; margin_l/margin_r=40, sidecar/media_studio/features/caption.py:356) — a 1.85x wrap-width gap that roughly doubles the preview's line count. Combined with `activeLine` growing the line across an entire utterance while inter-word gaps stay <= LINE_GAP_SEC=0.8s (app/renderer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:118-119) and the bottom-anchored `bottom:14%` block having no max-height, the caption grows upward into the hook. MEASURED at vw=1600 with the shipped defaults (DEFAULT_CAPTION_STYLE='libass' shortMakerLogic.ts:238, hookTitle:true :295): 12 words = 19px clearance; 17 words = +84px overlap, 100% stage coverage; 24 words = +161px overlap with 35px clipped off the top. Overlap begins at ~13-14 words, which is roughly 5s of continuous speech and therefore routine in a 20-60s clip. Contained by `overflow:hidden` (captionOverlay.css:11) so nothing escapes the stage; `pointer-events:none` (:10) and `aria-hidden` (CaptionOverlay.tsx:217) mean no interaction or a11y impact, and the shipped export is unaffected (CaptionOverlay.tsx:4-7)."

CORRECT FIX (not container-type, which would shrink the caption 1.6x below export scale): give the line box the export's wrap width — replace `left:50%`/`translateX(-50%)` with `left:0; right:0` plus `margin-inline:4%` (or `width:92%`), preserving the 92% inline extent the `max-width` already intends. Optionally cap the line (`max-height` + clamp of the displayed word run) so a very long utterance cannot reach the hook. Regression assertion should pin the RATIO, not viewport-invariance: `getComputedStyle('.caption-overlay__line').fontSize / stageHeight` stays within ~10% of the sidecar's 0.045 constant, and the rendered line box width is >= 90% of the stage width.

The dead `cqw` terms are best deleted as cleanup — they resolve to the clamp max at every reachable width, so removing them is behaviour-preserving in production.

## Arrow-keying the Workspace tablist teleports the user out of the Edit section and drops focus to <body>
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `TabBar` uses automatic activation: `move()` calls `onSelect(nextId)` then unconditionally focuses that tab (`app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:160-167`), driven by ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/Home/End (`TabBar.tsx:175-194`). Roving tabindex puts only the active tab in the Tab order (`TabBar.tsx:89`), so arrow keys are the ONLY keyboard route between tabs. But the Workspace host diverts one tab id into a top-level route change instead of a panel switch: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:189-198` (`if (id === 'shortmaker' && onOpenMakeShorts) { onOpenMakeShorts(video.id); return; }`), and `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375` implements that as `setRoute({ name: 'makeshorts', videoId })`, which unmounts Workspace (`App.tsx:470-471` renders `<MakeShorts/>` instead of `<Edit/>`). The thread is fully wired in the Edit path: `App.tsx:480` -> `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:141` -> Workspace `onOpenMakeShorts`. 'shortmaker' sits at index 5 of the reachable order while the default active tab is 'subtitles' at index 2 (`Workspace.tsx:76-90`, `Workspace.tsx:96`).

Executable probe 1 (vitest+jsdom, real Workspace with onOpenMakeShorts wired), verbatim:
  PROBE default active tab: [ 'subtitles' ]
  PROBE step 1: ArrowRight from "subtitles" -> selected=["diarize"] onOpenMakeShorts calls=0 activeEl=diarize
  PROBE step 2: ArrowRight from "diarize" -> selected=["refine"] onOpenMakeShorts calls=0 activeEl=refine
  PROBE step 3: ArrowRight from "refine" -> selected=["refine"] onOpenMakeShorts calls=1 activeEl=shortmaker
  PROBE >>> EJECTED to Make Shorts after 3 ArrowRight presses
(note the desync at step 3: selection stayed on 'refine' while focus moved to the unselected 'shortmaker'.)

Executable probe 2 (host mimics App.tsx by swapping Workspace for another section on the callback), verbatim:
  P2 ArrowRight from refine: workspaceStillMounted=false section=MakeShorts activeEl=BODY activeElInDoc=true
  P2 FINAL: html= <div data-section="MakeShorts">Make Shorts section</div> | document.activeElement= BODY

`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.test.tsx:709-723` covers only the CLICK path for this intercept; no arrow-key test exists.
- why: Three ArrowRight presses from the Edit workspace's default state throw the user out of the Edit section entirely and leave `document.activeElement` on `<body>` — a keyboard or screen-reader user loses their place with no warning and must re-navigate from the top of the document. WAI-ARIA APG prescribes MANUAL activation precisely when activating a tab has side effects; here the side effect is a whole-app route change, which is a defensible WCAG 3.2.2 On Input (Level A) failure (changing a control's setting causes an unannounced change of context), compounded by the focus loss. It also makes the tablist a one-way barrier: 'timeline', 'dub' and every tab in the Advanced/Deliver cluster sit past index 5, so they are reachable ONLY by ArrowLeft-wrapping backward through the end of the list — forward traversal can never get there.
- fix: Preferred (smallest, matches existing intent): when `onOpenMakeShorts` is wired the 'shortmaker' tab never renders a panel anyway (`Workspace.tsx:122-128` already redirects its `initialTab`), so stop rendering it as a `role="tab"` in that mode — drop it from `WORKSPACE_TAB_GROUPS.frame.tabIds` when the callback is present and surface it as an ordinary sibling button next to Export (`TabBar.tsx:246-250`). That removes the diverting entry from the roving order entirely and restores clean forward traversal. Alternative: switch `TabBar` to manual activation per WAI-ARIA APG — have arrow keys move focus only (update a `focusedId` and its roving `tabIndex`) and require Enter/Space to call `onSelect`. Independently, harden `TabBar.move()` (`TabBar.tsx:166`): it should not focus a tab the host declined to select — either let `onSelect` return a boolean/`false` veto, or move focus from an effect keyed on the committed `active` prop so focus and `aria-selected` can never desync.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped version (severity MEDIUM, not high): "In the Edit section's Workspace, three ArrowRight presses from the default state (subtitles, index 2) reach the 'shortmaker' tab (index 5), whose selection is diverted into a top-level route change (Workspace.tsx:189-198 -> App.tsx:373-375) instead of a panel switch. Because TabBar uses automatic activation (TabBar.tsx:168-175) and roving tabindex makes arrow keys the only keyboard route between tabs (TabBar.tsx:97), a keyboard user traversing the tablist is navigated out of Edit into Make Shorts incidentally, and the unmount leaves document.activeElement on <body> (measured in jsdom against the real App; UNVERIFIED in Chromium/Electron, though spec behavior makes agreement almost certain). The section change is visible to a sighted user (the top tab strip switches to 'Make Shorts') but has no programmatic announcement or focus move for AT users (App.tsx:565-572). FORWARD arrow traversal cannot pass index 5, so 'timeline' and 'dub' are unreachable going right - but they ARE reachable via End (measured: End selects 'dub' with the Workspace still mounted) and End+ArrowLeft ('timeline'); the Deliver-cluster tabs are not in the arrow order at all while collapsed (TabBar.tsx:159-166) and are reached via the Advanced toggle or Export. Defensible WCAG 3.2.2 On Input (A) plus focus-order concern; WAI-ARIA APG prescribes manual activation when activation has side effects. No test covers this: Workspace.test.tsx has no keydown tests (the intercept is click-only at :708-728), TabBar.test.tsx:181-280 tests arrows against an always-accepting onSelect, and app/e2e has no tablist keyboard test. Not data-destructive, and Make Shorts is an intended one-click destination from the Task Hub's first card (taskHub.ts:84-85), so the defect is the incidental TRIGGER plus the focus drop, not the destination. The proposed fix (drop 'shortmaker' from the roving order when onOpenMakeShorts is wired and surface it as a sibling button) stands; the TabBar.move() veto/effect hardening is latent robustness - the reported focus/selection desync is a stub artifact and is never committed in the wired app."
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly-scoped: "The Workspace tablist uses AUTOMATIC activation, so merely traversing it with ArrowRight unintentionally fires a whole-app route change. `TabBar.move()` calls `onSelect(nextId)` for every arrow/Home/End key (app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:168-175, :177-204), and the Workspace diverts exactly ONE id — 'shortmaker' at index 5 of the 8-tab reachable order — into a top-level route change instead of a panel switch (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:189-198 -> App.tsx:373-375 -> :470-471), which is only wired via the Edit path (Edit.tsx:141). Measured: from the workspace default 'subtitles' (Workspace.tsx:96), 3 ArrowRight presses leave the Edit section. WAI-ARIA APG prescribes manual activation exactly when activation has side effects, so this is a defensible WCAG 3.2.2 On Input concern; severity MEDIUM, not high. Two things the original claim got wrong and must not be repeated: (1) focus landing on <body> is NOT caused by the arrow keys — it is inherent to the intended single-owner deep-link and reproduces identically on the CLICK path (measured), so it is a SEPARATE pre-existing finding (unmounting the focused control with no route-change focus management) that the proposed arrow-key fix does not address; (2) the tablist is NOT a one-way barrier — `End` reaches the last reachable tab ('dub') in one keystroke (TabBar.tsx:198-201, tested at TabBar.test.tsx:242-249), the keyboard-reachable Export sibling (TabBar.tsx:254-258 + Workspace.tsx:137-140) jumps to 'convert' and opens the Deliver cluster with clean forward traversal, and the collapsed Deliver tabs are excluded from the arrow order regardless (TabBar.tsx:159-166). Only the narrow fact holds: any forward ArrowRight walk starting at index <=5 terminates on the diverting tab. The aria-selected/focus desync inside `move()` is a latent robustness gap with no shipped manifestation (no real host vetoes selection while staying mounted), so it is worth hardening but is not evidence of user-visible harm. Test gap is real: Workspace.test.tsx:708-728 covers only the click path."
- ⚠ scope correction: Headline stands as written: three ArrowRight presses from the Workspace's default 'subtitles' tab unmount the Edit section, route to Make Shorts, and leave document.activeElement on <body> (TabBar.tsx:168-175 + Workspace.tsx:189-198 + App.tsx:373-375/470-483; executable-proven twice, independently).

Rescope these three supporting sentences:

1. REPLACE "'timeline', 'dub' and every tab in the Advanced/Deliver cluster sit past index 5, so they are reachable ONLY by ArrowLeft-wrapping backward through the end of the list — forward traversal can never get there" WITH: "the 'shortmaker' entry is a one-way barrier for ArrowRight specifically: repeated ArrowRight from any tab at index <=4 can never advance past index 5. It does NOT make any tab unreachable — End (same handler, TabBar.tsx:198-201) jumps to 'dub' in one press with no intercept (measured: PEND End -> selected=dub), and the Export sibling button (TabBar.tsx:254-258 -> Workspace.tsx:137-140) selects 'convert' inside the Deliver cluster and expands it, after which forward ArrowRight traversal through the Deliver cluster works normally (measured: PEXP ArrowRight from convert -> selected=nle)."

2. REPLACE "arrow keys are the ONLY keyboard route between tabs" WITH: "arrow keys are the primary keyboard route between tabs; Home/End (TabBar.tsx:193-201) and the Export sibling button also change the selected tab."

3. REPLACE the parenthetical "(note the desync at step 3: selection stayed on 'refine' while focus moved to the unselected 'shortmaker')" WITH: "probe 1's step-3 desync is an artifact of its inert vi.fn() host, not a production state — the only shipped host wiring onOpenMakeShorts is App->Edit, which always navigates, so on the real thread step 3 yields selected=null / focus=BODY instead. The underlying gap in move() is real but LATENT: it focuses a tab regardless of whether the host committed the selection, so any future host that declines a selection would desync focus from aria-selected. Proposed fix #3 (veto or effect-driven focus keyed on the committed `active` prop) is the right hardening and should be framed as defense-in-depth, not as fixing an observable bug."

Severity: the confirmed core (unannounced whole-section context change on arrow-key activation + total focus loss, 3 keypresses from a default state, no test coverage) supports high; the WCAG framing is arguably stronger as 3.2.1 On Focus (Level A) than the cited 3.2.2 On Input, since arrowing both focuses and activates.

## The Workspace "Advanced" disclosure hides nothing — author `display:flex` beats the UA `[hidden]` rule, so all 13 tabs are always on screen
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: CODE: `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239` renders `<div className="tabbar__advanced-panel" hidden={!advancedOpen}>`, but `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152` declares `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; ... }`. An AUTHOR `display` declaration outranks the UA-origin `[hidden]{display:none}` rule, so the attribute is inert. `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:84-89` puts convert/nle/recipes/assets/tracks in the `advanced:true` "Deliver" group; `Workspace.tsx:2` imports workspace.css and its own header comment (workspace.css:5) confirms it ships in the entry chunk.
MEASURED (real Chromium, file:// page linking tokens.css + workspace.css + shell.css, exact TabBar collapsed markup):
  CONTROL `<div hidden>` with NO author display rule -> display:"none", rect 0x0, an injected child button `.focus()` FAILED  <- detector validated against the known-hidden state
  `#advPanel` ([hidden] + the author rule) -> display:"flex", visibility:"visible", offsetParent != null, rect {w:513,h:37}, `checkVisibility()===true`
  the "Tracks" tab inside it -> rect {w:73,h:37}, `checkVisibility()===true`, `document.elementFromPoint(center)` returns the Tracks tab itself, `.focus()` succeeded, `.click()` fired
KEYBOARD/AT DIVERGENCE: `TabBar.tsx:159-166` drops advanced tabs from `orderedIds` while collapsed and `TabBar.tsx:97` gives every non-active tab `tabIndex={-1}`, so those 5 visible, mouse-clickable tabs have NO keyboard path, while the `hidden` attribute simultaneously removes them from the accessibility tree — the `aria-expanded="false"` toggle at `TabBar.tsx:244-253` reports a state that is visually false.
TESTS ARE BLIND: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.test.tsx:598` and `:615` assert only `panel.hidden === true`, and `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.test.tsx:97,105` only regex the serialized `hidden` attribute; `app/vitest.config.ts` sets no `css: true`, so Vitest never applies workspace.css and jsdom's own UA rule makes the assertion pass.
COUNTER-EXAMPLE (proves this is a bug, not a house convention): `app/renderer/src/components/CardProvenanceDisclosure.tsx:57` uses the identical `hidden={!open}` pattern and `app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:266-268` sets only `padding-top` — no `display` — so that disclosure really does collapse.
- why: The entire progressive-disclosure feature for the Edit phase is non-functional in production while CI stays green. Every user who opens a video into the Workspace is shown 13 tabs across 4 clusters, not the intended 8 — the exact cognitive-load dump the WU was written to prevent. The "Advanced" button is a dead control (clicking it produces no visible change), and `handleExport` at `Workspace.tsx:137-140`, whose stated job is to "reveal the Deliver cluster", is a no-op. Worse, the collapsed state creates a mouse-only control set: 5 tabs a sighted pointer user can see and click, a screen-reader user is told do not exist, and a keyboard user cannot reach. If a user clicks one of those "collapsed" tabs, the active tab ends up inside the `hidden` subtree, so the tablist exposes no selected tab at all and the roving-tabindex entry point vanishes.
- fix: Scope the layout rule so it cannot resurrect a hidden element: `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden]) { display: flex; ... }` (workspace.css:148). Belt-and-braces: add a single global reset `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` near the top of `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css` so no future author rule can re-break any disclosure. Then add a CSS-aware regression assertion — Vitest cannot catch this — e.g. in `app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts` or `surfaces.visual.spec.ts`, open a video into the Workspace and assert `await expect(win.locator('.tabbar__advanced-panel')).toBeHidden()` before the Advanced click and `.toBeVisible()` after. Keep the `hidden` attribute (it is the right mechanism) — only the CSS is wrong.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED (correctly scoped): The Workspace "Advanced" disclosure does not visually collapse anything. The author rule `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel { display: flex; ... }` (app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:148-152) is author-origin and therefore outranks the UA-origin `[hidden]{display:none}`, so the `hidden={!advancedOpen}` attribute at app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:239 is inert and no `[hidden]` reset exists anywhere in the project CSS. All 13 tabs — including the 5-tab "Deliver" cluster flagged advanced:true at app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:84-89 — are always RENDERED and occupy layout in the tab strip; because `.workspace .tabbar { overflow-x: auto }` (workspace.css:36-39) clips the strip at the 1280px baseline viewport, roughly 9 are on screen and the rest — plus the Advanced toggle and the design-review-P1 "standing" Export button — are pushed into horizontal-scroll overflow. Proven twice independently: the committed CI baseline app/e2e/visual/surfaces.visual.spec.ts-snapshots/workspace-preview-win32.png shows `DELIVER` + `CONV` rendered in the default collapsed state, and a Chromium computed-style probe returns display:"flex" / rect 137x37 / checkVisibility()===true against a display:"none" / 0x0 control.

The residual behavioural gap is KEYBOARD-ONLY, not assistive-technology: those 5 visible, clickable tabs are excluded from `orderedIds` (TabBar.tsx:159-166), `onKeyDown` early-returns for them (:181), and non-active tabs carry `tabIndex={-1}` (:97), so a keyboard-only user can see 5 tabs they cannot focus by Tab or arrow key until a pointer click makes one active. They ARE exposed to screen readers — a CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` read of the exact markup reports `tab | TRACKS | ignored=false`, because Chromium's hidden-attribute a11y exclusion is mediated entirely through the UA display:none. All 13 panels remain reachable by mouse, keyboard (Tab to Advanced → activate → arrow keys), and screen reader. `handleExport` (`Workspace.tsx:137-140`) is not a no-op — its `setActive('convert')` correctly mounts the Convert panel. No data loss, no security impact, no crash, no unreachable functionality.

WHY CI IS GREEN: `app/vitest.config.ts` sets no `css: true`, so jsdom applies its own UA `[hidden]` rule and never loads `workspace.css`; `Workspace.test.tsx:598,615` and `TabBar.test.tsx:97,105` assert only the `hidden` attribute. A CSS-aware Playwright assertion is required to catch this class of bug.

FIX: scope the layout rule at `workspace.css:148` to `.tabbar--grouped .tabbar__advanced-panel:not([hidden])`, optionally add a global `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` reset, and add an e2e assertion (`toBeHidden()` before the Advanced click, `toBeVisible()` after). Keep the `hidden` attribute — only the CSS is wrong.

Citation corrections to the original finding: the counter-example lives at `app/renderer/src/views/CardProvenanceDisclosure.tsx:57` (not `components/`), and `elementFromPoint` returning the Tracks tab did not reproduce (4 of the 5 advanced tabs are hit-testable; Tracks is overlapped in the measured layout).

## A repeat export from Make Shorts silently overwrites the previously produced shorts (deterministic filename + ffmpeg -y)
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Output dir is FIXED per video: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:41` -> `out_dir_for=lambda vid: str(self.exports_dir / f"shorts-{vid}")`. Output filename is deterministic from rank + the source file stem: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1270` (`base_stem = Path(source_path).stem or "clip"`), `:1281` (`final_stem = _hook_card.rank_ordered_stem(base_stem, clip_rank, max_rank)`), `sidecar/media_studio/features/hook_card.py:177` (`return f"{order_prefix(rank, max_rank)}-{base}"`), `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1126` (`final_path = str(out_dir / f"{final_stem or stem}.mp4")`). ffmpeg is invoked with overwrite-without-asking: `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:157` (docstring: "``-y`` to overwrite the output") and `:160` (`argv = [ffmpeg_path(settings), "-hide_banner", "-nostdin", "-y", "-i", in_path]`), used by the final EXPORT stage at `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:455`. The `.json` sidecar is overwritten too: `:1147` (`_write_short_metadata(final_path, ...)`). Manual candidates are ALWAYS ranked 1..n: `app/renderer/src/features/manualIntervalLogic.ts:65` (`ranges.map((r, i) => intervalToCandidate(r.start, r.end, i + 1))`). No collision guard exists anywhere — Grep for `exists()|_unique|suffix|counter|dedupe` in `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py` returns "No matches found"; Grep for `overwrit|will replace|already exist` across `app/renderer/src` returns no user-facing warning. The success copy never mentions replacement: `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:187` (`setManualNote(`Exported ${exported.length} clip(s) from your ranges.`)`) and `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:980` (`<h3>Exported {exportedClips.length} clip(s)</h3>`).
- why: Every write path on this front door — "Make shorts from ranges" (`MakeShorts.tsx:258`), "Export approved" (`ShortMaker.tsx:968-975`), and the unattended "Make N shorts" batch (`ShortMakerControls.tsx:325-333`) — targets the same `exports/shorts-<videoId>/<NN>-<sourceStem>.mp4` paths. A user who exports 3 AI clips, then adds two manual ranges and clicks "Make shorts from ranges", destroys AI clips #1 and #2 with zero prompt and no visible error; the "Produced shorts" grid on the same screen simply stops growing. The loss is irreversible (ffmpeg has already truncated and re-encoded the file). The app's own doctrine contradicts this: `app/renderer/src/features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:1-8` states Export is "the ONE irreversible, spend/file-writing action" and guards it with a preflight summary plus a "TWO-STEP guarded commit", while Make Shorts writes files irreversibly with no preflight, no confirm, and no replacement notice.
- fix: Make the produced-short path collision-free before the render starts: derive the stem from the candidate's source window or an export-run id (e.g. `<NN>-<sourceStem>-<startSec>-<endSec>.mp4`, or a per-run subfolder `shorts-<videoId>/run-<jobId>/`), so a second export never lands on an existing deliverable. If the fixed-name scheme must stay, do a pre-export existence probe in `run_export` and return the colliding paths to the renderer, then gate the action behind the same explicit confirm gate `ExportInspector` already implements (`role="alertdialog"`, `ExportInspector.tsx:104-131`) with copy naming how many existing shorts will be replaced. At minimum, stop claiming a clean "Exported N clip(s)" — say "Exported N clip(s) (replaced M existing)."
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding stands as written. If anything it under-scopes: the collision is not limited to mixing manual ranges with AI clips. Because `order_prefix` pads to a MINIMUM width of 2 (`sidecar/media_studio/features/hook_card.py:171`), ANY two exports of the same video with <=99 clips each reuse the same `exports/shorts-<videoId>/<NN>-<sourceStem>.mp4` names — so re-running AI select with a different prompt and exporting also destroys the earlier deliverables, as does the unattended "Make N shorts" batch. The only escape is a batch that crosses the padding-width boundary (a 100+-clip batch widens to `001-` and does not collide with a 2-clip batch; probed). One citation correction: the "Make shorts from ranges" button is at `app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:123`, not `MakeShorts.tsx:258`; the manual write path is `MakeShorts.tsx:154-196` (`runManualExport`).
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding stands as written. Offered only as a precision refinement (does NOT change severity or verdict): "A repeat export from Make Shorts silently overwrites the rank-overlapping subset of the previously produced shorts. Because `HOOK_CARD_MIN_ORDER_WIDTH = 2` (sidecar/media_studio/features/hook_card.py:77) fixes the zero-pad width for every export of 1..99 clips, and the output dir (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:41, plus a second identical site at sidecar/media_studio/handlers/composition.py:359) and base stem (shortmaker.py:1270) are constant per video, a second run of n clips deterministically clobbers ranks 1..n of the first via ffmpeg `-y` (ffmpeg.py:160 through shortmaker.py:455) with no prompt, no warning, and no replaced-count. Clips at ranks above n are NOT overwritten but survive as stale orphans, so the gallery silently mixes fresh and stale renders under one rank sequence while its file count (shorts.py:379) stays flat. Manual ranges make this reachable in one ordinary sequence because they are always renumbered 1..n (manualIntervalLogic.ts:65) and inline candidates override the select cache (shortmaker.py:1460-1461). The destroyed file is unrecoverable in-app (no undo/versioning); the content is machine-regenerable from the untouched source at compute cost, but any per-clip approve/nudge decisions baked into that render are lost. Any fix must preserve `shorts.reexport`'s intended replace semantic (sidecar/tests/test_shorts.py:519) rather than making all names unconditionally unique."
- ⚠ scope correction: A repeat export from Make Shorts silently overwrites previously produced shorts whose rank prefix collides. All three write paths (ManualInterval.tsx:123 "Make shorts from ranges" via MakeShorts.tsx:268, ShortMaker's "Export approved", and the unattended batch at ShortMakerControls.tsx:325-333) target the same exports/shorts-<videoId>/<NN>-<sourceStem>.mp4 (shortmaker_ops.py:41; shortmaker.py:1126,1270,1281; hook_card.py:177) and the final encode passes ffmpeg -y (shortmaker.py:564 -> :451-459 -> ffmpeg.py:160), with the .json sidecar rewritten (shortmaker.py:1147). Collision occurs when two runs share a rank AND the same zero-pad width, which is every realistic case (width is 2 for max_rank 1-99, hook_card.py:165-172); a single run of >=100 candidates widens to 3 and would not collide. There is no existence probe, no confirm, and no replacement notice, and run_export never cleans stale files (shortmaker.py:1243-1244), so a second smaller run leaves orphans from the first blended into the same gallery (shorts.py:379,393-414). The overwritten file is irrecoverable; the clip itself is a derivative that can be re-rendered from the retained source + persisted transcript, but not reliably reproduced, because select is LLM-backed (shortmaker.py:82,147) and the candidate cache is in-memory only (handlers/_services.py:157). The repo already guards this exact hazard for convert (convert.py:123-141, ".converted" infix "so a re-encode never silently clobbers the original"). Any fix must preserve batch resume's documented "earlier outputs are idempotent overwrites" behaviour (batch.py:507-517), so prefer a pre-export existence probe + explicit confirm gate + "Exported N clip(s) (replaced M existing)" copy over unconditional per-run unique paths.

## Manual interval ranges survive a source-video switch, so the next "Make shorts from ranges" renders the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The source picker mutates only `selectedId` (`app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:208-219`), and `ManualInterval` is rendered at a stable position with no `key` and no reset prop (`MakeShorts.tsx:258` -> `<ManualInterval onSubmit={(c) => void runManualExport(c)} busy={manualBusy} />`), so React preserves its internal state across an A -> B video switch. That state is the range list: `app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35` (`const [ranges, setRanges] = useState<ManualRange[]>([])`) and `:59-61` (`submit()` hands `buildManualCandidates(ranges)` up unchanged). `runManualExport` then exports them against the NEW `selectedId` (`MakeShorts.tsx:171`). The sibling AI panel guards the identical hazard explicitly: `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:236-239` -> "without this the previous video's candidate list ... persist — and \"Export approved\" would carve the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps", implemented as a `videoId`-keyed reset at `:240-249`. MakeShorts has no equivalent reset: `manualNote`, `manualError` and `trayOpen` (`MakeShorts.tsx:78-81`) are also never cleared on a `selectedId` change. The behaviour is untested because the suite mocks `ManualInterval` stateless: `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122`.
- why: Pick video A (30 min), add range 10:00 -> 10:30, switch the picker to video B, click "Make shorts from ranges" — the still-listed A range is carved out of B. If B is long the output looks plausible but is the wrong content; if B is shorter than the range the ffmpeg cut (`sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:947-948`) produces an empty or broken clip. Either way it burns a full multi-stage GPU render (cut -> stabilize -> reframe -> caption -> encode) and, per the overwrite finding above, lands on B's `01-<stem>.mp4` and destroys any short already produced there. The stale "Exported N clip(s)" note and the still-open Output Tray also remain on screen after the switch, attributing the old video's result to the new one.
- fix: Key the manual control to the selected video so its ranges cannot outlive it: `<ManualInterval key={selectedId} ... />` at `MakeShorts.tsx:258`. Add a `useEffect` on `[selectedId]` in `MakeShorts` clearing `manualNote`, `manualError` and `trayOpen`, mirroring the per-video reset at `ShortMaker.tsx:240-249`. Then replace the stateless `ManualInterval` mock in `MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122` with a stateful stub (or use the real component) and add a regression test: add a range under v1, switch to v2, assert the range list is empty and no export fires with v1's timestamps.
- ⚠ scope correction: Citation-corrected, scope-tightened (substance unchanged, severity high stands): Picking a different source video DIRECTLY in the picker (`onChange` sets only selectedId — app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:218-222) leaves ManualInterval mounted at a stable, un-keyed tree position (MakeShorts.tsx:268, inside the `selectedId ?` branch at :232), so its `ranges` state survives (ManualInterval.tsx:35, :59-61) and the next "Make shorts from ranges" exports video A's timestamps against video B (MakeShorts.tsx:166,171 -> sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1460-1461 inline-candidates path -> :945-948 cut with no duration clamp at :192-220). manualNote/manualError/trayOpen (MakeShorts.tsx:78-81) are likewise never cleared on a selectedId change, so a stale success note and open Output Tray misattribute A's result to B. The sibling AI panel guards the identical hazard with a [videoId]-keyed reset (ShortMaker.tsx:233-249). Scope: the hazard requires a direct A->B pick — passing through "Select a video…" (:232) or arriving via the gallery re-export (:138-141, gallery unmounts the make subtree at :214) unmounts the control and clears ranges. Untested: MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 mocks ManualInterval stateless and no test or e2e switches videos before submitting.

The panel's mount-stability across a videoId change is asserted by the suite itself (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:382-402). Scope bounds to state explicitly: routing through the empty 'Select a video...' option (v1 -> '' -> v2) DOES reset the list, because the falsy branch at MakeShorts.tsx:289 unmounts the control — only a direct A->B pick preserves it. Regression test must replace the stateless mock at MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 with the real component or a stateful stub, and must drive the inputs via the native value setter (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set, the idiom already used at ManualInterval.test.tsx:34-38) — assigning .value directly does NOT fire React onChange and yields a silently passing no-op test."

## Focus ring on every gallery card's poster/Play button is clipped to zero visible pixels (WCAG 2.4.7 fail)
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Three ingredients, all read directly:
1. `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:216` — `.shorts__thumb { overflow: hidden }` (block 212-218; no padding, so the clip edge == the child's border box).
2. `app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:225-226` — `.shorts__thumb-btn { width: 100%; height: 100% }` with `padding:0; margin:0; border:none` (221-224) — the button exactly fills the clipping parent.
3. `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52` — the only focus rule is `:where(button, …):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }`, and `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206` defines `--focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-edge)` — spread-only, no `inset`. `outline` is explicitly removed, so there is no fallback. No `.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible` override exists anywhere (Grep for `shorts__thumb` across all *.css returns only shorts.css:212/220/236/240/248/262).

MEASURED with the repo's own Playwright (`app/node_modules/playwright`, Chromium 149.0.7827.55), replicating those three rules verbatim, keyboard-originated focus via Tab:
```
clipped: { focused: "clipped", focusVisible: true,
           computedBoxShadow: "rgb(14,16,20) 0px 0px 0px 2px, rgb(255,176,32) 0px 0px 0px 4px",
           pixelLeftOfEdge: "rgb(14,16,20)" }   <- page background: NO ring painted
control: { focused: "control", focusVisible: true,
           pixelLeftOfEdge: "rgb(255,176,32)" } <- ring painted
```
The control (identical button in a wrapper with `overflow:hidden` removed) DOES paint the ring, so the detector fires in the known-good state — the silence in the clipped case is real, not a broken probe.

Render sites: `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:293-308` (gallery sub-tab, `MakeShorts.tsx:202`) and `app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:176-189` (the "Produced shorts" grid). The real `--accent-edge` is `rgba(242,163,60,0.5)` (`tokens.css:66`), i.e. a 50%-alpha ring — even fainter than my opaque stand-in, but clipping is alpha-independent.
- why: Every card in the produced-shorts gallery contributes one Tab stop ("Play preview of <title>") that paints no focus indicator at all — not a weak one, zero pixels. A keyboard-only user tabbing the grid periodically loses all sense of position. This is a WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA) failure, and axe cannot detect it (axe has no focus-appearance rule), which is why the a11y gate is green. The card's other controls (`.shorts__actions button`) are NOT affected — `.shorts__card` has no `overflow:hidden` — so the failure is silent and intermittent, the worst shape for a user to reason about.
- fix: Give the button an INSET ring so it is drawn inside the clip: add to `shorts.css` `.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--surface-bg), inset 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-edge); }` (class-scoped, so it beats the `:where()` rule, same technique already used for inputs at `shell.css:484-495`). Alternative: hoist the ring to the unclipped wrapper with `.shorts__thumb:has(.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible) { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }`. Prefer the inset form — `--accent-edge` at 0.5 alpha over `--surface-deep` should also be checked against the 3:1 contrast requirement of WCAG 2.4.11.
- ⚠ scope correction: The core defect claim needs no rescoping and stands as written: on both `.shorts__thumb-btn` render sites (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:293-307 and app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:176-189) the keyboard focus ring paints ZERO pixels on all four edges, because the button's border box exactly fills the `overflow:hidden` clip box of `.shorts__thumb` (shorts.css:212-218, 220-234) while the only focus rule supplies a spread-only, non-inset `box-shadow` and explicitly removes `outline` (shell.css:49-52, tokens.css:206) — measured, with a passing `overflow:visible` control. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) fail; the a11y gate cannot see it (a11y.a11y.spec.ts:138-144 checks computed `boxShadow !== 'none'`, not paint).

Only the PROPOSED FIX must be corrected: prefer the ALTERNATIVE, not the inset form. Use `.shorts__thumb:has(.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible) { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }` (hoists the ring to the unclipped wrapper; `.shorts__card` at shorts.css:191-202 has no `overflow`). The inset form is measured to fail whenever a poster is present: `.shorts__thumb-img` is `position:absolute; inset:0; object-fit:cover` (shorts.css:240-246) and paints above the button's inset shadow, hiding the ring completely (0 amber px; band reads uniformly the poster color). The finding's separate note that `--accent-edge` at 0.5 alpha should be checked against WCAG 2.4.11's 3:1 requirement remains valid and unmeasured here.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): The poster/Play button in every shorts gallery card paints NO PERCEPTIBLE focus indicator when keyboard-focused, a WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) failure. `.shorts__thumb` sets `overflow:hidden` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:216) with no padding, and `.shorts__thumb-btn` exactly fills its clip box (`border:none;margin:0;padding:0;width:100%;height:100%`, shorts.css:222-226), while the only focus rule (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52) removes `outline` and supplies a spread-only, non-inset `box-shadow` (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206) — so the entire ring is clipped. Measured with the repo's own Playwright: 0 changed pixels outside the button's border box vs 4512 in an `overflow:visible` control. Precisely scoped: not literally zero pixels — 24 antialiasing pixels survive at the four rounded corners, 2.16% of the 1112px perimeter with max delta-luminance 8.3/255, which is sub-perceptual and cannot serve as an indicator. Impact is bounded, not critical: the control remains fully operable, and the adjacent `.shorts__actions button` (outside the clip, shorts.css:349-356) does paint a ring, so a keyboard user regains orientation within one Tab; the harm is the intermittent invisible/visible alternation down a multi-card grid (shorts.css:180-189). Blast radius is TWO elements, not one: `player.css:13-15` gives `.player__video:focus-visible` the same spread-only ring and `.shorts__player` fills the same clipped box (shorts.css:253-259), so the playing state is affected identically. Affects both render sites (Shorts.tsx:293-308, ProducedShorts.tsx:176-189). axe cannot detect this class of defect, so the green a11y gate is not evidence of compliance. Fix: class-scoped inset ring on `.shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible` (and `.shorts__player:focus-visible`), the same technique already used at shell.css:482-495; separately check `--accent-edge` at 0.5 alpha over `--surface-deep` against the 3:1 requirement of WCAG 2.4.11.
- ⚠ scope correction: Keyboard focus on the gallery card poster/Play button (.shorts__thumb-btn) paints no perceivable focus indicator: the shared spread-only ring (shell.css:49-52 + tokens.css:206, outline explicitly removed, no inset, no class-scoped override) is drawn entirely outside the button's border box, which exactly coincides with the overflow:hidden clip edge of .shorts__thumb (shorts.css:212-218, 220-234). Measured with the repo's own Playwright against the real CSS files: 16 changed pixels at max channel delta 13/255, confined to six scanlines at the four rounded corners (border-radius antialiasing), versus 4152 pixels at delta 107/255 for an identical overflow:visible control -- 0.4% of the ring, stable at dsf=1 and dsf=2.
