Affected surfaces are FOUR, not "gallery / batch": Make Shorts -> Gallery (MakeShorts.tsx:212 -> Shorts.tsx:293-308), Make Shorts -> Make (MakeShorts.tsx:240 -> ShortMaker.tsx:1000 -> ProducedShorts.tsx:176-189), Workspace (Workspace.tsx:281 -> ShortMaker -> ProducedShorts), and Library (Library.tsx:607 -> ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:98 -> ProducedShorts). The "batch" sub-tab is NOT affected -- MakeShorts.tsx:213 renders <Repurpose>, which contains no shorts cards. Sibling .shorts__actions buttons are unaffected (.shorts__card, shorts.css:191-202, has no overflow). Fix as proposed: a class-scoped .shorts__thumb-btn:focus-visible inset ring, matching the existing precedent at shell.css:484-495.

## Unbounded per-card `library.thumbnail` fan-out starves the strictly-serial sidecar RPC channel; the ffmpeg run is un-cancellable and un-timed, so one bad source can wedge every RPC in the app
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Renderer fires one RPC per card with no cap or queue: `app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:116` mounts `<VideoThumb>` for every card, `app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:45` calls `useVideoThumbnail(thumbnailRpc, video.id, video.thumbnailPath ?? '')`, and `app/renderer/src/components/useVideoThumbnail.ts:65` issues `rpc.thumbnail(videoId)` in a mount effect. `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:580` maps EVERY visible video (no virtualization — grep for react-window/react-virtual/IntersectionObserver over app/renderer/src returns zero matches), and freshly imported videos always have an empty poster path (`sidecar/media_studio/library.py:319`: `"thumbnailPath": ""`). The sidecar is strictly serial: `sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:163` `for line in self._in: self.handle_line(line)` and `sidecar/media_studio/protocol.py:185` `result = handler(req.params, ctx)` invoke the handler INLINE on the stdin loop thread. `library.thumbnail` is a direct-return handler that spawns ffmpeg and blocks: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:171` `code = run(argv, total_sec=0.0)` — `on_progress` and `should_cancel` both default to None, so no cancel watchdog is armed (`sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:309` only starts one `if should_cancel is not None`) — and `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:338` `code = proc.wait()` has no timeout. The renderer-side timeout is armed at SEND time, not at start-of-service: `app/main/sidecar.ts:431` sets the 60 s timer inside `request()` before `stdin.write`, with `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (`app/main/sidecar.ts:73`).
- why: On the common first-run path (multi-select import of N videos, then the Library grid), N ffmpeg poster extractions serialize behind one another while every other RPC the app issues — `library.remove`, `library.add`, `project.open`, the 5 s `job.list` heartbeat at `app/renderer/src/components/useActiveJobs.ts:47` — queues behind them and burns its own 60 s budget while merely waiting. Once the queue depth exceeds the budget, later thumbnails and any concurrent user action fail with `sidecar request '<m>' timed out after 60000ms`. Escalation (likely, ~60-80%): a source on a disconnected network share or a stalled device makes `proc.wait()` block for an unbounded time; because the process is still ALIVE, the supervisor emits no 'exit'/'down' (`app/main/sidecar.ts:548`, `app/main/ipc.ts:115`), so `SidecarBanner` stays hidden (`app/renderer/src/components/SidecarBanner.tsx:155`) and the user gets an app where every RPC fails after 60 s with no banner, no Restart affordance, and no explanation.
- fix: Two independent fixes, both needed. (1) Renderer: cap thumbnail concurrency — a shared module-level promise queue (2-4 slots) in `useVideoThumbnail`, and/or only fetch when the card intersects the viewport. (2) Sidecar: `library.thumbnail` must not be a direct-return handler that blocks the stdin loop — either run it through `JobRegistry` (which has the 30 min watchdog, `sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:43`) or at minimum pass a `should_cancel`/deadline into `ffmpeg.run` and bound `proc.wait()` so a hung poster extraction cannot hold the channel.
- ⚠ scope correction: Un-capped per-card `library.thumbnail` fan-out (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:45,116 -> useVideoThumbnail.ts:65, over an unvirtualized list at Library.tsx:580) serializes N inline ffmpeg poster extractions on the sidecar's single stdin-loop thread (rpc.py:163-164, protocol.py:185, library_ops.py:171), so every concurrent RPC waits behind the whole backlog. MEASURED: 589 ms median per poster (790 ms on a 1080p/5-min source); a 35 ms `library.remove` waited 6.87 s behind only 12 posters. Consequence scales with library size: at ~40 un-postered videos the UI is unresponsive for ~24 s; past ~76-100 un-postered videos on one screen the backlog exceeds app/main/sidecar.ts:73's 60 s REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and a concurrent user action hard-fails — and because Library.tsx:372-380 removes optimistically with snapshot restore, the card vanishes and reappears a minute later with an error. This is a FIRST-RUN-ONLY cost per video (posters are cached: library_ops.py:165 short-circuit measured at 5.6 ms on a second pass), and a failed thumbnail alone is benign (useVideoThumbnail.ts:69-71 falls back to the play glyph). SEPARATELY, and independent of library size, `library.thumbnail` passes no `should_cancel`, so ffmpeg.py:309's cancel watchdog never arms and ffmpeg.py:338's `proc.wait()` is untimed: a single source on a stalled share or spun-down drive (low probability, ~5-15%, but the mechanism is near-certain) wedges the entire RPC channel indefinitely with no banner and no Restart affordance, since SidecarBanner.tsx:155 renders nothing while status is 'running'. Severity: medium for the fan-out (bounded, one-time, size-dependent), high for the unbounded proc.wait wedge. The job.list heartbeat does NOT contribute user-visible harm (its failure is swallowed at useActiveJobs.ts:42-44) though it does aggravate the backlog.
- ⚠ scope correction: `library.thumbnail` is a direct-return handler invoked INLINE on the sidecar's strictly-serial stdin loop (sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:163, protocol.py:185) that spawns ffmpeg with neither a cancel watchdog nor a wait timeout (library_ops.py:171 passes no should_cancel, so ffmpeg.py:309 never arms the watchdog and ffmpeg.py:338 proc.wait() is unbounded; the poster argv at shorts.py:209-226 has no -rw_timeout either). PRIMARY DEFECT (high, needs no fan-out): a SINGLE video whose source is on a disconnected network share or stalled device blocks the stdin loop indefinitely, so every subsequent RPC — library.remove, library.add, project.open, the 5s job.list heartbeat (useActiveJobs.ts:47) — fails after 60s (sidecar.ts:73,431), while the process stays ALIVE so sidecar.ts:548 emits no 'exit', ipc.ts:115 never broadcasts, and SidecarBanner.tsx:155 keeps the banner and Restart button hidden. The user gets an error toast (Library.tsx:442,450) carrying only `sidecar request '<m>' timed out after 60000ms` — a message, but no cause, no banner, no Restart affordance, and no automatic recovery. SECONDARY DEFECT (medium): the Library grid fires one uncapped, unqueued library.thumbnail per card (LibraryCard.tsx:45,116; useVideoThumbnail.ts:65) over an unvirtualized, unpaginated list (Library.tsx:457-460,580), and freshly imported videos all have an empty poster (library.py:319), so first-run N posters serialize head-of-line on that channel. At a per-poster cost of roughly 100-500ms for a local file (UNVERIFIED — not measured), this degrades latency proportionally and only reaches the 60s send-time budget on a large library (order 120+ videos) or with large/slow/remote sources — it is not a timeout cascade at the typical N of 10-20. Both fixes are still needed independently: cap renderer thumbnail concurrency (or fetch on viewport intersection), and bound the sidecar side by routing library.thumbnail through JobRegistry (30-min watchdog, rpc.py:43) or at minimum passing a should_cancel/deadline into ffmpeg.run and bounding proc.wait(). Settling experiment for the arithmetic: time `library.thumbnail` end-to-end over a 200-video local import and measure when the job.list heartbeat first rejects at 60s.
- ⚠ scope correction: Split into two correctly-scoped findings.

FINDING A (severity: MEDIUM — was the "starvation" half). Uncapped per-card `library.thumbnail` fan-out adds serial latency to every other RPC, and degrades to request timeouts only in LARGE libraries. The renderer issues one `library.thumbnail` RPC per posterless card with no cap, queue, or virtualization (`app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:116` + :45 -> `app/renderer/src/components/useVideoThumbnail.ts:65`; `Library.tsx:580` maps the uncapped `visible` from `Library.tsx:457`; `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:283-287` `list()` has no LIMIT; zero react-window/react-virtual/IntersectionObserver matches under `app/renderer/src`). The sidecar services them strictly serially (`sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:163-164`, `protocol.py:185`) and `library.thumbnail` blocks the loop inline (`handlers/library_ops.py:171`), so every other RPC issued in that window — `library.remove`, `project.open`, the 5 s `job.list` heartbeat (`useActiveJobs.ts:47`) — waits behind N posters. MEASURED cost of the frozen argv (`features/shorts.py:209-226`) on 1080p30 h264 / local SSD with the repo's own `build/ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe`: warm mean 604 ms (min 217, max 804, n=11). Because all N 60 s timers arm at send time (`app/main/sidecar.ts:431`, before the write at :446; `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` at :73), the observable is: ~0.6 s x N of added latency for concurrent actions, crossing into `sidecar request '<m>' timed out after 60000ms` only at N ~ 99 posterless videos (~276 at min cost). At a typical first-run N of 5-30 there are NO timeouts — just 3-18 s of sluggishness. Fix: cap thumbnail concurrency to 2-4 via a shared module-level promise queue in `useVideoThumbnail`, and/or fetch only on viewport intersection. Settling experiment: seed a library with 120 posterless videos, open Library, and assert no `timed out after 60000ms` rejection and that a `project.open` issued 1 s in resolves within 2 s.

FINDING B (severity: HIGH — the real channel-wedge, and it is NOT thumbnail-specific). ANY direct-return handler that spawns ffmpeg can wedge the entire serial RPC channel indefinitely with no banner and no cancel path. `ffmpeg.run` arms its cancel watchdog only when `should_cancel is not None` (`sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:309`) and has no bound on the child; a child that stops emitting `-progress` lines blocks the handler in the stdout iteration at `ffmpeg.py:319` (NOT at `proc.wait()`, :338). At least three direct-return call sites pass no cancel seam: `library.thumbnail` (`handlers/library_ops.py:171`, `total_sec=0.0`, no `on_progress`/`should_cancel`), `tracks.strip` (`handlers/media_ops.py:263-282` passes no `ctx` at :279, so `features/tracks.py:572` sets `should_cancel = None` — for a FULL subtitle re-mux, from one click), and `library.add`'s inline ffprobe (`library.py:306`). Because the process stays ALIVE, the supervisor emits no `exit`/`down` (`app/main/sidecar.ts:548`; `app/main/ipc.ts:115`), so `SidecarBanner` stays hidden (`SidecarBanner.tsx:155`) and every subsequent RPC fails at 60 s with no Restart affordance. Fan-out is NOT required — one source on a dead network share or a stalled device is enough. Fix: route blocking-ffmpeg work through `JobRegistry` (which arms the 30 min watchdog, `rpc.py:43`), or at minimum thread a `should_cancel`/deadline into `ffmpeg.run` and bound the stdout read + `proc.wait()` for every direct-return ffmpeg call site. UNVERIFIED: whether ffmpeg reading a disconnected SMB share actually blocks unboundedly on Windows (SMB has its own session timeouts) — settle by pointing `library.thumbnail` at a path on a share that is disconnected mid-read and measuring whether the handler ever returns.

## Every Library card mount fires a synchronous ffmpeg poster extraction onto a strictly serial sidecar pipe, wedging the whole app and timing out unrelated RPCs
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `perf-render` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Full chain verified: `Library.tsx:579-594` maps EVERY visible video to a `LibraryCard`; `LibraryCard.tsx:45` calls `useVideoThumbnail(thumbnailRpc, video.id, video.thumbnailPath ?? '')`; `useVideoThumbnail.ts:65` fires `rpc.thumbnail(videoId)` from the mount effect for every card whose `thumbnailPath` is empty — all in the same commit, no cap, no viewport gating (grep confirms ZERO `IntersectionObserver` in `app/renderer/src`). `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:319` sets `"thumbnailPath": ""` on every `library.add`, so a fresh import guarantees the fan-out. `app/renderer/src/components/api.ts:122-124` → `app/main/ipc.ts:75-79` (bare pass-through, no queue) → `app/main/sidecar.ts:446` writes each request to stdin IMMEDIATELY with a per-request `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (`app/main/sidecar.ts:73`). The sidecar consumes it strictly serially: `sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:160-165` `def serve(): for line in self._in: self.handle_line(line)`. `library.thumbnail` is a DIRECT-RETURN handler that runs ffmpeg synchronously inside dispatch: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:171` `code = run(argv, total_sec=0.0)` (not a job — so it never leaves the dispatch path).
- why: `LibraryToolbar.tsx:4-5` states the design target explicitly ("must not replace in-context filtering at hundreds of videos"). Open a Library of 60 un-postered 4K clips (or drag-drop-import them): 60 `library.thumbnail` requests hit stdin at once and the sidecar runs 60 sequential ffmpeg processes. For that entire window EVERY other sidecar RPC is stuck behind them in the pipe — the `job.list` heartbeat (`useActiveJobs.ts:47`), `library.list`, transcribe, export. At ~0.3-1.5 s per 4K seek+encode the 60 s renderer timeout is crossed around 40-200 videos, after which the tail rejects: those cards silently fall back to the ▶ glyph (`useVideoThumbnail.ts:69-71` swallows the error with no negative caching) and unrelated user actions fail with "sidecar request … timed out" while the sidecar is actually healthy. A video whose extraction genuinely fails (`library_ops.py:172-176` raises without persisting) never gets a `thumbnailPath`, so it re-fires the RPC on every single Library visit forever.
- fix: Three independent layers, any one of which breaks the wedge: (1) move `library.thumbnail` off the serial dispatch path — register it as a JOB, or run it on a bounded worker pool inside the sidecar so `rpc.py:163` keeps draining stdin; (2) cap renderer-side concurrency — put the thumbnail RPC behind a small promise queue (2-4 in flight) shared across cards rather than one unthrottled effect per card; (3) only request a poster for cards actually in the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver` in `useVideoThumbnail`, plus `loading="lazy"` on the `<img>`). Also add a negative cache so a hard ffmpeg failure is not retried on every mount.
- ⚠ scope correction: Narrowed scope for the surviving finding (mechanism confirmed + measured; severity medium-high rather than high): On the FIRST Library render after a multi-file import, every un-postered card fires an unthrottled, non-viewport-gated `library.thumbnail` RPC (useVideoThumbnail.ts:53-71; no cap, no IntersectionObserver anywhere in app/renderer/src), each of which runs ffmpeg SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the sidecar's strictly serial dispatch loop (library_ops.py:171 + rpc.py:160-165). Measured ~0.95-1.7 s per 4K poster on Windows (spawn floor alone ~0.4-0.5 s), so N videos monopolise the app's only RPC channel for ~N seconds: every new sidecar dispatch (opening a video, starting a reframe/export, library.list, job.list) is dead for that window and, beyond ~35-63 4K videos, fails with `sidecar request '<method>' timed out after 60000ms` (sidecar.ts:434) while the sidecar is healthy. Corrections to the original write-up: the burst is ONE-TIME per import batch, not permanent - the renderer's 60 s timeout does not cancel sidecar-side work, so every queued extraction still completes and persists thumbnailPath (library_ops.py:177, short-circuit at :165-167) and later visits fire zero RPCs; the "re-fires on every visit forever" case is limited to extractions that hard-fail (library_ops.py:172-176 raises without persisting), which is what the negative cache is for. The job.list heartbeat is NOT damage (useActiveJobs.ts:42-44 swallows it silently), and already-running jobs are unaffected because jobs.py:647-650 runs each on its own daemon thread - only STARTING new work queues behind the burst.
- ⚠ scope correction: On the first Library render after a bulk import, every card whose persisted `thumbnailPath` is empty fires an uncapped, non-viewport-gated `library.thumbnail` RPC in one commit (Library.tsx:580, LibraryCard.tsx:45, useVideoThumbnail.ts:65; no IntersectionObserver or virtualization anywhere in app/renderer/src; `visible` uncapped at Library.tsx:457-460). Because `library.thumbnail` is a direct-return handler that runs ffmpeg synchronously inside dispatch (library_ops.py:171) on a strictly serial single-threaded stdin loop (rpc.py:160-165, dispatch inline at rpc.py:125), those N requests are serviced FIFO while all N 60s timers are already armed from write time (sidecar.ts:431-446, sidecar.ts:73). This head-of-line-blocks the single sidecar RPC channel — the `job.list` heartbeat (useActiveJobs.ts:47), `library.list`, transcribe and export all stall behind the queue — violating the channel's own documented quick-ack contract (sidecar.ts:66-72). The renderer and Electron main thread are NOT blocked (ipc.ts:75-79 is async, sidecar.ts:446 is a non-blocking write), so local search/sort/select stay responsive; the stall is confined to sidecar-dependent actions. Scope limits: a card with a persisted poster fires no RPC at all (useVideoThumbnail.ts:55-58, asserted by Library.test.tsx:748-749) and an already-extracted poster short-circuits without ffmpeg (library_ops.py:165-167), and library_ops.py:177 persists the result — so this is once per video per lifetime, not once per mount, and a fully-postered library fans out zero requests. Stall duration scales as N x per-extraction cost; that cost is UNVERIFIED (the argv uses ffmpeg's fast pre-`-i` input seek plus a single frame, shorts.py:214-221, so it sits at the cheap end and the 60s timeout tail requires the app's own stated "hundreds of videos" scale, LibraryToolbar.tsx:4-5, rather than dozens). Separately CONFIRMED and unaffected by the above: a genuine ffmpeg failure raises without persisting (library_ops.py:172-176) and the renderer swallows it with no negative cache (useVideoThumbnail.ts:69-71), so that video re-fires the extraction on every Library visit indefinitely.
- ⚠ scope correction: Importing or first-viewing N un-postered videos fans out N concurrent library.thumbnail RPCs onto a strictly serial sidecar pipe, starving unrelated RPCs until they hit the renderer's 60s timeout. Scope corrections to the original: (1) NOT "every card mount" — useVideoThumbnail.ts:55-58 serves an already-set thumbnailPath with NO RPC, and library_ops.py:165-167 returns an existing data_dir/thumbnails/<id>.jpg WITHOUT invoking ffmpeg. Because library.set_thumbnail persists (library.py:362; test_library.py:223 asserts persistence), the ffmpeg fan-out is a ONE-TIME cost per video per import, not a per-visit wedge. The trigger set is "cards whose thumbnailPath is empty AND whose poster jpg is absent" — i.e. a fresh multi-file import or drag-drop, exactly the "hundreds of videos" case LibraryToolbar.tsx:4-5 names as the design target. The finding's body scoped this correctly; only its headline generalized to "every". (2) The "re-fires on every Library visit forever" claim holds ONLY when a failed ffmpeg leaves NO output file. Given `-y` at shorts.py:213, if ffmpeg creates a partial/zero-byte output before failing, library_ops.py:165-167 short-circuits on the next call and persists a path to a BROKEN jpg — the card then fails at <img> load (LibraryCard.tsx:57 onError) instead of re-firing. Which branch dominates in practice is UNVERIFIED. (3) The latency figures are the reporter's arithmetic on an unmeasured per-call cost, not a measurement: "~0.3-1.5s per 4K seek+encode" and "the 60s timeout is crossed around 40-200 videos" are UNVERIFIED. The seek itself is the CHEAP input-side path (`-ss 1` precedes `-i`, shorts.py:214-217), so the real per-call cost is process spawn plus one 4K keyframe decode plus a FULL-RESOLUTION JPEG encode (no scale filter in the argv, shorts.py:209-226). The settling experiment is a direct measurement: time N sequential build_thumbnail_argv runs against representative 4K sources on Windows and compare N*latency against REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS. (4) One collateral item is milder than stated: the job.list heartbeat swallows its failure and keeps the last known count (useActiveJobs.ts:42-44), so it degrades to a stale badge rather than an error; the user-visible "sidecar request ... timed out" failures land on error-surfacing actions (transcribe/export/library.list). The core architectural defect stands unrefuted and is confirmed by two in-repo corroborations the reporter did not cite (app/e2e/fixtures.ts:230-232 "library.thumbnail is a SYNC RPC"; app/main/sidecar.ts:66-71 documenting head-of-line blocking and the quick-ack {jobId} invariant this handler violates), so all three proposed fix layers remain valid — layer (1), moving library.thumbnail off the serial dispatch path, is the one that restores the documented invariant.

## Opening the Produced-shorts gallery spawns one blocking ffprobe per clip, every time — on the sidecar's single serial RPC loop
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `perf-render` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `shorts.py:64-72` META_FIELDS deliberately omits width/height; `shorts.py:117-148` build_metadata writes neither; `shortmaker.py:879-887` (the only production writer) passes neither. So the guard at `sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:382` — `if meta is None or not (meta.get("width") and meta.get("height"))` — is ALWAYS true for every clip the app produces, and `self._probe(...)` (`shorts.py:385`) runs unconditionally. `shorts.py:349` `self._probe = probe or probe_dims`, and production registration passes no probe override (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/composition.py:357-363`), so it is the real `probe_dims` → `subprocess.run(ffprobe…)` (`shorts.py:254-258`). `shorts.list` is a DIRECT-return handler, and `sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:160-165` is a strictly serial `for line in self._in: self.handle_line(line)` loop — the ffprobe spawns block the whole app's RPC channel. Triggered on gallery mount (`app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:96-98`), after every delete (`Shorts.tsx:154-159`), and again on every tab switch back because `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:202` conditionally renders `<Shorts/>` (unmount → remount). The probed value is a known constant (`shortmaker.py:68-69` OUT_WIDTH=1080/OUT_HEIGHT=1920) and neither `Shorts.tsx` nor `ProducedShorts.tsx` reads `width`/`height` at all.
- why: After a batch run produces e.g. 60 clips, clicking "Produced shorts" issues 60 serialized ffprobe process spawns before the grid can paint. At a conservative 50-150 ms per Windows process spawn that is 3-9 s of first-paint delay, and because the sidecar loop is serial it is also 3-9 s in which every other RPC in the app (Jobs pill counts, `batch.status` for a running batch, settings writes) is head-of-line blocked. The cost is paid again on every tab switch and every delete, and it buys a value that is a compile-time constant and is never read by the UI.
- fix: Persist `width`/`height` into the `.json` at export time — they are already known as OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT in `shortmaker.py:68-69` — by adding them to `build_metadata` (`shorts.py:117-148`) and to the `_export_one` writer (`shortmaker.py:879-887`), so `_scan_dir`'s fallback branch stops firing. Belt-and-braces: since no consumer on this surface reads the dims, drop the per-clip probe from `_scan_dir` entirely (or memoise dims keyed on path+mtime+size) and let width/height be 0 for legacy clips.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): shorts.list runs one blocking ffprobe per clip on the sidecar's serial RPC loop, on every gallery mount, every Library visit, and after every single delete -- for a value no UI reads. Confirmed: META_FIELDS (shorts.py:64-72) and build_metadata (:117-148) omit width/height, the only production writer passes neither (shortmaker.py:860-887), production registration supplies no probe override (composition.py:357-363), so the guard at shorts.py:382 is always true and shorts.py:385 always spawns the real probe_dims (:245-258); shorts.list is a direct handler (:506) dispatched inline on the serial stdin loop (rpc.py:124-125, :160-165).

Measured cost: 51 ms median / 65 ms mean per probe (n=15, build/ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe, the argv from shorts.py:229-242) -- ~3.1 s at 60 clips, NOT 3-9 s.

The real driver is library growth, not batch size: shorts.list() is un-filtered and scans every shorts-* dir (shorts.py:407-408), so ~300 accumulated clips costs ~15 s. It is re-paid on every tab switch back (MakeShorts.tsx:212 unmount/remount), after every single delete (Shorts.tsx:153-154), and by a third uncited caller -- libraryShortsClient.ts:26-33 pays the entire scan just to render the Library's per-card count badge.

Concurrent victim, correctly named: the global Jobs slide-over (App.tsx:574) polls job.list every 2000 ms while open (JobQueue.tsx:17, :126, :136-149) and that poll queues behind the scan. NOT blocked: job progress notifications, which are pushed from each job's own daemon thread (jobs.py:647) via a write-lock-only path (rpc.py:78, :82-85). NOT possible: batch.status contention -- BatchQueue (Deliver.tsx:71, Repurpose.tsx:35) is never mounted alongside the gallery.

Severity is capped by a designed skeleton loading state (Shorts.tsx:205-223) and by the fact that first mount after a batch is co-dominated by one shorts.thumbnail ffmpeg spawn per card on the same serial loop (useShortThumbnail.ts:48-66; shortmaker.py writes no thumbnail), so removing the probe alone would not fix the "60 clips feels slow" first paint -- it fixes the recurring per-visit and per-delete cost.

Proposed fix stands as written (persist width/height in build_metadata + _write_short_metadata; drop or memoise the _scan_dir probe).
- ⚠ scope correction: Opening any produced-shorts gallery spawns one blocking ffprobe per clip, every time, inline on the sidecar's single serial stdin RPC loop — and the probed value is discarded unread.

Verified chain: shorts.py:64-72 (META_FIELDS omits width/height) -> shorts.py:140-148 (build_metadata returns neither) -> shortmaker.py:879-887 (the ONLY production writer of the sidecar .json; grep confirms the sole other caller, shorts.py:196 write_thumbnail_metadata, merges only thumbnailFrameSec) -> so the shorts.py:382 guard `meta is None or not (meta.get("width") and meta.get("height"))` is always true for every app-produced clip -> shorts.py:385 self._probe runs unconditionally -> shorts.py:349 `probe or probe_dims` with no probe= override at composition.py:357-363 -> shorts.py:254-258 subprocess.run(ffprobe). shorts.list executes inline (protocol.py:185 `result = handler(req.params, ctx)`) on the strictly serial loop at rpc.py:163-164, so N clips = N serialized process spawns before the response is written. No memoisation anywhere in _scan_dir. Triggers: Shorts.tsx:96-98 on mount, Shorts.tsx:153-154 after every delete, and unmount/remount on every tab switch back via the conditional render at MakeShorts.tsx:212 (NOT :202 — that line is now a comment; drift from PR #308). No production consumer reads the dims: every `.width`/`.height` hit in app/renderer/src is a test fixture or an unrelated progress-bar style.

Scope corrections to the original finding:
1. DROP the "compile-time constant" premise. Output dims are NOT constant 1080x1920. shortmaker.py:1225 reads `aspect` from settings and shortmaker.py:1039 passes it to the reframe stage; aspect.py:94-109 output_dimensions() resolves three curated presets — (1080,1920) 9:16, (1080,1080) 1:1, (1080,1350) 4:5 (aspect.py:103-105, corroborated test_aspect.py:88-98) — plus a generic even-rounded fallback. shortmaker.py:68-69 OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT are the caption/zoom canvas size only (used at shortmaker.py:312-313 and 1097-1098), not the final clip dims.
2. Therefore the proposed fix must persist `aspect.output_dimensions(aspect)`, NOT OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT. Writing the constants would stamp 1080x1920 onto a 1:1 or 4:5 export and then permanently suppress the corrective probe via the shorts.py:382 guard — trading a perf bug for a silent data bug.
3. Scale is larger than stated, not smaller: Shorts.tsx:82 calls client.shorts.list() with no videoId, so shorts.py:408 scans EVERY `shorts-*` dir — all clips ever produced, not one batch's 60. libraryShortsClient.ts:31 is a third un-cited trigger.
4. Narrow the blocking claim: new requests (e.g. batch.status polls, settings writes) are genuinely head-of-line blocked, but in-flight job.progress/job.done is NOT — those are emitted from pool threads through the separately-locked writer at rpc.py:82-87.
5. Magnitude UNVERIFIED: the "50-150 ms per spawn / 3-9 s first paint" figure is an estimate; I did not measure ffprobe spawn latency on this machine. Settling experiment: time shorts.list against a populated exports root with N=60.

Severity: high stands on the confirmed mechanism (unbounded serialized process spawns on the app's only RPC channel, on a hot path, for a value nothing reads).
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding stands as written; this only fixes two line citations and widens the scope the reporter under-stated: "Opening the Produced-shorts gallery spawns one blocking ffprobe per clip, every time, on the sidecar's single serial RPC loop. `build_metadata` (shorts.py:117-148) has no width/height parameter at all, so the only production writer (shortmaker.py:879-887) cannot persist dims and the `shorts.py:382` guard is always true — measured: 5 clips -> 5 probes, and 80.4 ms per real ffprobe spawn (= 4.83 s of head-of-line RPC blocking at 60 clips). Because `Shorts.tsx:82` calls `shorts.list()` with NO videoId, `shorts.py:407-408` scans every `shorts-*` dir, so the cost scales with the LIFETIME clip count across all sources, not one batch. Re-triggered on mount (`Shorts.tsx:96-98`), after each delete (`Shorts.tsx:153-154`), and on every tab switch back via the conditional render at `MakeShorts.tsx:212` (NOT 202 — that line is inside a comment). The probed value is the compile-time constant OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT (shortmaker.py:68-69) and no production renderer reads `ShortInfo.width`/`.height`."

## Gallery mount fires one `shorts.thumbnail` RPC per poster-less card with no viewport gating and no concurrency cap — each is a blocking ffmpeg spawn on the same serial loop
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `perf-render` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Every card calls `useShortThumbnail(hasApi() ? client.shorts : null, short.path, short.thumbnailPath)` at `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:283-286`; the hook's effect (`app/renderer/src/components/useShortThumbnail.ts:48-70`) unconditionally calls `rpc.thumbnail(clipPath)` whenever `thumbnailPath === ''`, with no queue, no cap, no IntersectionObserver. `thumbnailPath` is `""` for every clip whose `.thumb.jpg` does not yet exist (`shorts.py:320` `"thumbnailPath": str(thumb) if thumb.exists() else ""`), and nothing in the export path writes one — the hook's own header documents this (`useShortThumbnail.ts:5-7`). All cards mount at once (`Shorts.tsx:235-249`, no windowing). Server side, `shorts.thumbnail` runs `self._run(argv, total_sec=0.0)` (`shorts.py:432-433`) = the real blocking `ffmpeg.run` (`shorts.py:350`), on the serial stdio loop (`rpc.py:160-165`). The 1:1 call-per-card behaviour is pinned by `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.test.tsx:373-385`. Grep over `app/` returns zero hits for `react-window`/`react-virtual`/`IntersectionObserver`/`loading="lazy"`.
- why: The worst case is the normal case: the user finishes a batch and immediately opens the gallery, where every clip is poster-less. 60 fresh clips = 60 queued `shorts.thumbnail` RPCs, each an ffmpeg spawn + seek + JPEG encode (~100-400 ms) executed one at a time, so the app's only RPC channel is wedged for roughly 6-24 s. The grid shows ▶ glyphs with no indication anything is loading, the Jobs pill freezes, and a concurrently running batch's `batch.status` refreshes stall behind the queue.
- fix: Generate the poster once at export time, next to the existing `.json` write in `_export_one` (`shortmaker.py:879-887`), so `shorts.list` returns a populated `thumbnailPath` and the hook never needs an RPC. If on-demand generation must stay, gate `useShortThumbnail` on an IntersectionObserver (only visible cards) and route the calls through a shared semaphore capped at 2-3 in flight.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW (perf polish): the Shorts gallery generates poster frames on demand — one ungated `shorts.thumbnail` RPC per poster-less card, each a blocking ffmpeg spawn on the sidecar's serial stdin loop (Shorts.tsx:282-286, useShortThumbnail.ts:48-70, shorts.py:432-433, rpc.py:160-165) — because nothing in the export path writes a `.thumb.jpg` (zero `thumb` hits in shortmaker.py; shorts.py:320 emits "" when it is absent). Measured cost is 141 ms median per call (12 runs, exact build_thumbnail_argv, 1080x1920/30s h264), so at the default count of 5 (select.py:625, DEFAULT_COUNT=5) the burst is ~0.7 s and invisible; a 12-video batch producing ~60 poster-less clips gives a one-time ~8.5 s progressive fill-in at ~7 posters/sec. The cost is paid once per clip ever, because the sidecar persists `<clip>.thumb.jpg` and the next shorts.list returns it (shorts.py:320/428-439, useShortThumbnail.ts:50-52, pinned at Shorts.test.tsx:393-408). The user-facing signals are all on unblocked paths: batch progress is a worker-thread push (BatchQueue.tsx:127-134, jobs.py:647, rpc.py:82-93), and poster/playback bytes resolve in Electron main with no sidecar hop (main.ts:1402-1404). The only genuine papercut is that shorts.delete / reexport / package.export clicked in the first seconds after opening a large freshly-exported gallery waits behind the remaining queue (worst case ~8.5 s at 60 clips) with no spinner explaining it. Fix is still worth taking: generate the poster at export time next to the existing .json write (shortmaker.py:860-887) so thumbnailPath is populated and the RPC never fires.
- ⚠ scope correction: Opening the Make Shorts > Gallery tab (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:212) mounts every card at once with no windowing, and each poster-less card fires one shorts.thumbnail RPC with no viewport gating and no concurrency cap (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:282-286, app/renderer/src/components/useShortThumbnail.ts:48-70). thumbnailPath is "" for every freshly exported clip because the export path writes no poster (sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:320; zero /thumb/i matches in shortmaker.py). Each RPC is a blocking ffmpeg spawn executed inline on the sidecar's single-threaded stdio loop (shorts.py:507 plain method -> shorts.py:432-433 -> ffmpeg.py:338 proc.wait(); rpc.py:125 dispatch inside the rpc.py:160-165 serve loop), and nothing in the transport caps in-flight requests (preload.ts:283, ipc.ts, sidecar.ts:419-453). Consequence, correctly scoped: this is a ONE-TIME, self-healing stall on the FIRST Gallery open after a fresh batch (posters persist, so a later shorts.list returns a populated thumbnailPath and fires no RPCs). While the queue drains, request/response methods on the shared channel are head-of-line blocked -- so the header Jobs pill's 5 s job.list poll (app/renderer/src/components/useActiveJobs.ts:40,47) shows a STALE COUNT (the renderer thread and CSS pulse are unaffected -- not a "freeze"), and BatchQueue's one-shot onJobDone batch.status refresh (features/batch.py:1040; app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:140,150-152) is delayed. Live batch progress is NOT affected: it rides PUSH job.progress notifications written from job threads under rpc.py:65's _write_lock, which never traverse the blocked read loop. Cards show only a bare ▶ glyph with no per-card loading affordance (Shorts.tsx:299-305; the skeleton at Shorts.tsx:205-223 covers only shorts.list). Magnitude UNVERIFIED: the specific "60 clips = 6-24 s" figure is an estimate -- poster-extract latency was not measured on this machine and no per-batch clip cap bounding N was found; settle it by timing build_thumbnail_argv (shorts.py:209-226) on representative clips. Residual the original finding did not claim: sidecar.ts:73 REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, so a sufficiently large gallery pushes queued requests into hard timeouts, not just latency. Evidence-pin correction: Shorts.test.tsx:373-391 uses a ONE-card fixture, so it pins "poster-less card -> one RPC", not an N:N fan-out. Severity: medium-high rather than high -- a one-time, self-healing, no-data-loss perf stall with live progress unaffected.
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect is CONFIRMED; only two peripheral evidence sentences need tightening. (a) The claim "the 1:1 call-per-card behaviour is pinned by app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.test.tsx:373-385" is too strong — that test renders a SINGLE short and pins only "a poster-less card fires shorts.thumbnail". The N-card 1:1 fan-out is STRUCTURALLY guaranteed (a per-ShortCard hook with stable deps: client.shorts is a module-level const at app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:142) but is NOT test-pinned; a regression test over N poster-less cards asserting exactly N calls would settle it. (b) The per-call cost "~100-400 ms" and the derived "roughly 6-24 s" wedge for 60 clips are UNVERIFIED estimates — I did not time ffmpeg on this box. What IS verified is the structure: N serial ffmpeg process spawns (build_thumbnail_argv uses input-side `-ss 1` fast seek + `-frames:v 1`, shorts.py:203-226) executed one at a time on the single stdio loop, so the wedge scales linearly with poster-less clip count and is seconds-scale, not milliseconds. The settling experiment is to time shorts.thumbnail against a real 1080x1920 clip and multiply by the gallery size. Additionally, the react-window/loading="lazy" grep is decorative rather than load-bearing: loading="lazy" could not help here because the RPC fires from a mount effect before the <img> ever gets a src. Finally, the finding's scope should be widened, not narrowed: the same unbounded on-demand pattern is cloned for the source library (app/renderer/src/components/useVideoThumbnail.ts:4 over library.thumbnail, sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:170), and once the serial queue exceeds REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 (app/main/sidecar.ts:73) the tail RPCs hard-reject with a user-visible timeout error rather than merely stalling.

## Cancelling the manual export reports it as a SUCCESS ("Exported 0 clip(s)") and opens the save tray
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:177-188 — `let clips = extractClips(res); if (clips === null && isJobHandle(res)) { clips = await waitForJobDone(...) } const exported = clips ?? []; setManualNote(`Exported ${exported.length} clip(s) from your ranges.`); setTrayOpen(true);`
app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:274-278 — on a JobCancelled payload `waitForJobDone` does `settleResolve(null)` (deliberately NOT a rejection).
sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:793-796 — `_finish_cancelled` emits a TERMINAL `job.done` with `{"error": {"message": "cancelled", "type": "JobCancelled"}}`.
app/renderer/src/components/useJob.ts:97-105 — `extractJobError` parses that into `{message:'cancelled', type:'JobCancelled'}`.
app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:26-28 + 228-234 + 151-154 — any `queued`/`running` job (unfiltered by feature; `shortmaker` is a labelled feature at useJob.ts:115) gets a Cancel button wired to `job.cancel`.
Test gap: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:606-644 covers the job.done ERROR path and two `null` paths but never delivers a `type:'JobCancelled'` payload.
- why: The user's own cancel is reported back to them as a completed export. `null` from `waitForJobDone` is three different outcomes collapsed into one (no-onJobDone bridge, empty success payload, and USER CANCELLED), and MakeShorts maps all three to `?? []` -> a positive `role="status"` note (MakeShorts.tsx:264-268, announced to screen readers) plus `setTrayOpen(true)`, which presents Save-short / Save-SRT buttons for clips that were never produced. The user cannot tell a cancel from a genuinely empty export, and the optimistic success note is never rolled back.
- fix: Distinguish cancel from empty success at the boundary instead of collapsing to `null`. Either (a) have `waitForJobDone` reject with a dedicated `JobCancelledError` (mirroring the existing `JobAbortedError` at _api.ts:70-75) and have `runManualExport` catch it to reset to idle with a neutral "Export cancelled." note and `trayOpen=false`; or (b) keep `null` but treat it distinctly in MakeShorts.tsx:186-188 — only set the success note + open the tray when `clips !== null`, and surface "Export did not return any clips." otherwise. Add a test that pushes `{jobId, result:{error:{message:'cancelled', type:'JobCancelled'}}}` and asserts no success note and no tray.
- ⚠ scope correction: Cancelling a shortmaker EXPORT from the global Jobs slide-over (the only cancel route the manual path has) makes the renderer report the cancel on its SUCCESS surface — `.make-shorts__note` `role="status"` reading "Exported 0 clip(s) from your ranges." — and opens the Output Tray, whose Save short then answers "Saved the short." for a clip that was never produced. Mechanism: sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:793-796 emits a terminal JobCancelled `job.done`; app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:275-278 resolves it as `null`; app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:186-188 collapses `null` to `?? []`. The manual path is the worst case only because it passes no AbortSignal (MakeShorts.tsx:179-185); the SAME collapse hits the AI export at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:672 whenever the cancel comes from the global JobQueue rather than that panel's own Cancel button. Severity: medium (misreport + a lying save affordance; no data loss, no security impact, sidecar job state is correct). Test gap is real: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:634-701 covers the error path and two `null` paths but never delivers a `type:'JobCancelled'` payload.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding stands. Two precision tightenings only: (1) the three outcomes collapsed into `null` are more exactly (i) no onJobDone bridge on the api object (_api.ts:236-237 returns Promise.resolve(null)), (ii) a job.done success payload lacking a `clips` key entirely, and (iii) a user cancel (_api.ts:276) — note a genuinely EMPTY success `{clips: []}` returns a non-null `[]` from extractClips (shortMakerLogic.ts:688-693), so the ambiguity is 'success payload with no clips key', not 'empty success payload'. (2) waitForJobDone reaches MakeShorts through the shortMakerLogic re-export barrel (shortMakerLogic.ts:22-24), though the implementation cited at _api.ts is the one that executes. Severity is better stated as medium-to-high: a user-visible false success report on a front-door flow with no data-loss or security consequence.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (UX polish), not high: cancelling a manual export leaves a neutral-styled, literally-accurate note "Exported 0 clip(s) from your ranges." (MakeShorts.tsx:186-188; `.make-shorts__note` is `--text-secondary`, makeShorts.css:78-81 — no success styling) and spuriously opens the Output Tray. The tray-opening is the only genuine defect: `waitForJobDone` collapses cancel into the same `null` as an empty/absent result (_api.ts:275-277) after the sidecar emits a terminal JobCancelled `job.done` (jobs.py:780-796), so MakeShorts cannot distinguish them. It is NOT a false success claim (the count is a truthful zero), the user authored the cancel and sees "cancelled" in the very JobQueue row they clicked (JobQueue.tsx:151-161, 212-215; jobs.py:783), and the tray's Save-short/Save-SRT buttons are inert note-setting stubs (MakeShorts.tsx:145-146) that write no files — so no data loss, corruption, spend, or bogus write is possible. Fix is worth doing as polish: gate `setTrayOpen(true)` on `clips !== null` and emit a neutral "Export cancelled." note; add the missing JobCancelled test (absent per grep of MakeShorts.test.tsx). Separately, fix the now-false CONTRACT-NOTE at useJob.ts:263-264 claiming cancelled jobs emit no job.done, which jobs.py:785-796 contradicts.

## "Save short" / "Save SRT separately" announce a completed save with zero IPC — nothing crosses the boundary
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `ipc-boundary` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145-146 — `const handleSaveShort = useCallback(() => setManualNote('Saved the short.'), []); const handleSaveSrt = useCallback(() => setManualNote('Saved the SRT sidecar.'), []);` — no `client.*`, no `rpc`, no `openInFolder`.
Wired at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:272-274 (`onSaveShort={handleSaveShort} onSaveSrt={handleSaveSrt}`).
app/renderer/src/components/OutputTray.tsx:139-148 — the tray is purely presentational; the `onSaveShort`/`onSaveSrt` callbacks are the ENTIRE behaviour behind those buttons (confirmed by the file header at OutputTray.tsx:11-12 "It is a CONTROLLED, presentational component").
Rendered into the `role="status"` live region at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:264-268.
- why: Clicking "Save short" states "Saved the short." — a claim that a file was written — while no request ever reaches main or the sidecar and no file is created anywhere. A user who then closes the app or looks for the SRT finds nothing, with a screen-reader-announced confirmation that it succeeded. The code comment at MakeShorts.tsx:143-144 frames these as seams that "record what the user chose to save so the action is acknowledged", so the placeholder is deliberate — but the shipped user-facing string asserts completion rather than acknowledging a choice, which is the defect regardless of intent.
- fix: Until the real save path exists, stop asserting completion: either hide the save buttons (omit `onSaveShort`/`onSaveSrt` — OutputTray.tsx:139/144 already gate each button on the handler being provided, so passing `undefined` removes them cleanly), or change the copy to a non-completion string and disable the control. When implemented, route them through a real RPC (the sidecar already returns clip paths in `job.done.result.clips`, and the bridge exposes `openInFolder` per _api.ts:89) and only set the note on a resolved promise, with the rejection surfaced into `manualError`.
- ⚠ scope correction: "Save short" / "Save SRT separately" are IPC-free no-ops that announce a completed save into a `role="status"` live region (MakeShorts.tsx:145-146, wired at 283-284, announced at 274-278; OutputTray.tsx:139-148 holds no logic). Correctly scoped harm: (1) "Saved the SRT sidecar." is flatly false — no code path writes a standalone .srt (shortmaker.py:342-346, 388-391 defer it to `subtitles.export`, client.ts:207-208, which MakeShorts never calls), so a user who chose the "Separate file" delivery mode gets neither embedded captions nor an SRT; (2) "Saved the short." is misleading about what the CLICK did, but the .mp4 is NOT lost — `client.shortmaker.export` (MakeShorts.tsx:171) already wrote it to `exports_dir/shorts-<videoId>` (shortmaker_ops.py:41) before the tray could open (MakeShorts.tsx:188), and it appears in the Produced shorts gallery. Drop "no file is created anywhere" / "closes the app and finds nothing" as applied to the short; keep it for the SRT. Severity is high for the SRT path, medium (misleading copy, no data loss) for the short.
- ⚠ scope correction: "Save short" and "Save SRT separately" are dead controls: both handlers do zero IPC (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:145-146 — pure `setManualNote`), and the tray's buttons have no other behaviour (app/renderer/src/components/OutputTray.tsx:140,145), on the only production tray render in the app (MakeShorts.tsx:280). The two buttons fail DIFFERENTLY and only one is a false completion claim. (a) "Save SRT separately" — MEDIUM, a genuinely false completion claim. "Saved the SRT sidecar." asserts a deliverable that no code path ever produces: sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:388-392 and :399-400 skip captioning entirely in `sidecar` mode and defer the subtitle file to a separate `subtitles.export` RPC that MakeShorts never calls, and the `saveSrt` intent modelled at app/renderer/src/lib/outputOptions.ts:41-42,69-71 is wired neither into `OutputTrayState` (OutputTray.tsx:22-30) nor into the export params (MakeShorts.tsx:166-170). No SRT exists in any subtitleMode, and the string is announced through the already-mounted `role="status"` region (MakeShorts.tsx:274-278 at HEAD / :264-268 at 997669b0). (b) "Save short" — LOW, a redundant no-op with ambiguous copy, NOT a fabricated file. The tray only mounts after a successful export (`setTrayOpen(false)` MakeShorts.tsx:158; `setTrayOpen(true)` only at :188; gated at :279), so the `.mp4` (shortmaker.py:1126) and its `<clip>.json` (:1147) already exist in the durable exports root (handlers/composition.py:359) and are discoverable in the "Produced shorts" gallery with a working Open-folder action (MakeShorts.tsx:49; Shorts.tsx:104-118). The user loses nothing; "Saved the short." merely overwrites the truthful "Exported N clip(s) from your ranges." (:187) and implies a save-to-destination action that never ran. FIX: for the SRT button, either omit `onSaveSrt` (OutputTray.tsx:144 already hides it when undefined) or route it through a real `subtitles.export` RPC and set the note only on a resolved promise, with rejections into `manualError`. For the short button, retarget it to the capability that already exists — `window.api.openInFolder` (_api.ts:89) on the exported clip path from `job.done.result.clips` — and change the copy from a completion assertion to the action performed.
- ⚠ scope correction: "Save SRT separately" announces a completed save with zero IPC — the promised subtitle file is never written (HIGH). app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:146 sets the note "Saved the SRT sidecar." with no RPC; the only code path that materialises an SRT is subtitles.export (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:86-93, registered at handlers/composition.py:131, already exposed to the renderer per lib/rpc.test.ts:399) and it is never called. shortmaker.py writes no .srt (grep: only comments at 345-346), and for subtitleMode sidecar/none it also SKIPS embedding captions (shortmaker.py:388-392, 399-400) — so a user whose Settings default is "Separate file" (components/CaptionPreferences.tsx:116; UI promise at lib/outputOptions.ts:26-29) receives neither burned captions nor a subtitle file, while the role="status" live region (MakeShorts.tsx:274-278) announces the SRT was saved. The sidecar's own comment at shortmaker.py:345-346 documents the renderer route that does not exist. The misleading string is pinned by a green test at MakeShorts.test.tsx:558.

SEPARATELY, and much lower severity: "Save short" (MakeShorts.tsx:145) is also a zero-IPC no-op, but it is NOT data loss — the tray only opens after a successful export (MakeShorts.tsx:81/158/188) that already wrote and persisted the clips (MakeShorts.tsx:186-188; visible in the gallery per views/Shorts.tsx:82,231). Its defect is a redundant/confusing confirmation of an action the user did not actually trigger, not a missing file. The original finding's "no file is created anywhere" and "a user who then closes the app... finds nothing" is wrong as applied to the short.

FIX SCOPE: route "Save SRT separately" through client.subtitles.export and set the note only on the resolved promise (rejection into manualError); until then omit onSaveSrt so OutputTray.tsx:144 hides it. For "Save short", either omit onSaveShort or replace the copy with a non-completion string (e.g. reveal the already-exported clip via window.api.openInFolder, wired at app/main/preload.ts:167,308 and used correctly by views/Shorts.tsx:105 and views/Export.tsx:158).

- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `axe-a11y` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:50-52: `<button type="button" aria-label={`Play ${label}`} ...>{playing ? 'Stop' : 'Play'}</button>` — the aria-label is FIXED while the visible text flips.
