- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (was: high), scoped: "The gallery's Play/Stop toggle keeps a fixed accessible name — the ONE card currently previewing renders visible text 'Stop' while its aria-label stays 'Play <title>' (ShortClipActions.tsx:50-52), and the Package button likewise renders 'Packaging…' under the name 'Package <label> for upload' (:66-73). This is a genuine WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, Level A) failure — confirmed executably: axe-core 4.12.1's `label-content-name-mismatch` (impact serious) flags both buttons when the rule is run. Real but bounded impact: at most one control is affected at a time (playingId is a single value, Shorts.tsx:66), the control still works, and during playback a correctly-labelled native `<video controls>` (Shorts.tsx:291 → Player.tsx:321) offers a redundant way to stop, so no user is stranded; the concrete residual harm is voice-control ('click Stop' will not match) and a screen reader announcing the inverse action.

IMPORTANT — the gate does NOT miss this for lack of a Play-pressing test: the rule is tagged `experimental` (axe.js:32545) and axe's default `tagExclude = ['experimental','deprecated']` (axe.js:29218) removes it from the run set entirely under the gate's tag-based options (_visualSetup.ts:171). Verified: `rule present in run set: false`. Any fix that wants gate enforcement must ALSO opt the rule in, e.g. `rules: { 'label-content-name-mismatch': { enabled: true } }` in runAxe, which I verified makes it fire under the existing WCAG_TAGS.

Fix: `aria-label={playing ? `Stop ${label}` : `Play ${label}`}` and make the Package name track its rendered word. This is a BREAKING change to the existing tests — ShortClipActions.test.tsx:82-85 finds the button by `aria-label === 'Play Clip'` and asserts its text is 'Stop', and `clickLabel` (:27-33) addresses buttons by accessible name — so migrate those hooks to `data-testid` (the component comment at ShortClipActions.tsx:5-7 currently justifies the stale label as 'test-addressable', which is the root cause) before changing the labels."
- ⚠ scope correction: The shared per-clip action row hardcodes the Play/Stop button's accessible name, so whenever a clip is previewing, the control that STOPS playback renders the word "Stop" while announcing as "Play <title>" — a WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, Level A) failure and an axe `label-content-name-mismatch` violation of impact `serious`. Root cause: app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:50 fixes `aria-label={`Play ${label}`}` while :51 flips the text via `{playing ? 'Stop' : 'Play'}`. It affects BOTH call sites of the shared component, not just the gallery: app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:330-340 (`playing={playing}` at :333, from `playingId === short.id` at :240) and app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:223-231 (`playing={playing}` at :226, the Produced-shorts grid reached via ShortMaker/Workspace). Because `playingId` is single-valued (`useState<string | null>` at Shorts.tsx:66, toggled at :101), at most ONE node violates at any instant — the defect is latent per-card, but an axe scan reports one violating node, not one per card. The Package button at ShortClipActions.tsx:66-73 shares the mechanism but NOT the severity: its name/content mismatch ("Packaging…" vs "Package <label> for upload") exists only while the button is `disabled={packaging}` (:69), so axe still flags it but the voice-control harm does not apply to a non-activatable control; it is gallery-only, since `onPackage` is supplied at Shorts.tsx:339 and omitted at ProducedShorts.tsx:223-231. The gate would genuinely block this once it reaches the state — WCAG_TAGS includes `wcag21a` (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:40) and it fails on `serious` (:49-53), and the rule's `experimental` tag (axe.js:32545) does not exempt it under tag-based `runOnly` (_visualSetup.ts:171). It is invisible today for TWO reasons, not one: no test presses Play, AND the axe gate never mounts the gallery at all (`.shorts` mounts only in the non-default 'gallery' sub-tab, a11y.a11y.spec.ts:64-65). FIX: derive the label from the same state as the text — `aria-label={playing ? `Stop ${label}` : `Play ${label}`}` — in the shared component, which fixes both call sites at once. The fix MUST also update the tests that currently encode the mismatch, or they will fail: ShortClipActions.test.tsx:82-85 (asserts aria-label 'Play Clip' while `playing` is true) and Shorts.test.tsx:625 (`button[aria-label^="Play"]` re-queried in the playing state). Add an assertion that the accessible name contains the rendered text in both the resting and playing states.
- ⚠ scope correction: Both gallery/clip-list call sites render a Stop control whose accessible name stays "Play <title>" — a genuine WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, Level A) failure, but one the current a11y gate can never catch. app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:50-52 hardcodes `aria-label={`Play ${label}`}` while the visible child flips to 'Stop' (`playing` from Shorts.tsx:240 -> :333, and ProducedShorts.tsx:223-231). At most one card is affected at a time (`playingId` is a single `string | null`, Shorts.tsx:66). The same shape affects the Package button's transient "Packaging…" state (ShortClipActions.tsx:66-73). Executable proof: axe-core flags `label-content-name-mismatch` (serious) on this exact markup when the rule is forced, and clears it once the name carries the rendered word. Severity is MEDIUM, not high: the axe gate cannot report it, because the rule is tagged `experimental` (axe.js:32545) and axe's default `tagExclude = ['experimental','deprecated']` (axe.js:29218) removes it from the tag-scoped run used at _visualSetup.ts:171 — measured EMPTY violations under the gate's own options — and the gallery is not mounted in the 'Make Shorts' scan anyway (a11y.a11y.spec.ts:64-66). Fix by deriving the label from the same state (`playing ? `Stop ${label}` : `Play ${label}``), and note that doing so REQUIRES updating two existing tests that key on the playing-state "Play…" label: ShortClipActions.test.tsx:82-85 and Shorts.test.tsx:625-627.

## The Aspect control on the Reframe surface is inert — export always renders 9:16 regardless of what the user picks
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: UI: app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:126-139 renders a closed `Aspect` select over ASPECT_OPTIONS = ['9:16','1:1','4:5','16:9'] (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:308), writing controls.aspect.
Wire (renderer): app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerPresets.ts:167-191 (buildExportParams) emits captionStyle/reframeEngine/hookTitle/hookCard/hookCardTopN/removeFillers/autoZoom/silenceTrim/stabilize — there is NO `aspect` key.
Wire (sidecar): sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1376 allowlists only ('reframeEngine','captionStyle','subtitleMode') from params into settings; sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1225 then reads `aspect = str(settings.get("aspect") or DEFAULT_ASPECT)` (DEFAULT_ASPECT='9:16', shortmaker.py:70) and passes it to _export_one(aspect=aspect) (shortmaker.py:1291) -> stages.reframe(stage_clip, reframed_path, aspect, ...) (shortmaker.py:1039).
Nothing ever writes settings['aspect']: grep for `aspect` in app/main -> 0 hits; grep in app/renderer/src/**/*.ts -> only shortmaker controls + Export-preset DISPLAY models, no settings.set; grep for '"aspect"' in sidecar/media_studio -> only the read at shortmaker.py:1225, export_presets.py preset records, templates.py:107, director_op_engines op params.
Select side is dead too: sidecar/media_studio/features/select.py:196 declares Controls.aspect and grep for `\.aspect\b` across sidecar/media_studio returns exactly one hit — a docstring alias in reframe.py:115. No code reads it.
Batch path repeats it: templates.py:106-113 puts `aspect` in PRESET_CONTROL_FIELDS, commented "exactly the knobs shortmaker.export consumes" (false), and app/renderer/src/features/ExportPresetsPanel.tsx:48-52 exposes a free-text "Aspect ratio" input with the same fate.
- why: Aspect is THE defining parameter of a reframe phase. A user who picks 16:9 (to keep original framing) or 4:5 gets a 9:16 crop anyway, with no warning — silently wrong output after a long render. From the disclosure lens it is worse than clutter: four cells of the control grid, a preset table column, and a free-text field all cost attention and teach a false mental model.
- fix: Either (a) wire it: add 'aspect' to the shortmaker.export param allowlist (shortmaker.py:1376) and emit it from buildExportParams (shortMakerPresets.ts:167); or (b) the disclosure answer — remove the Aspect select from the novice front door, state the output as a fixed "Vertical 9:16" fact, and re-expose aspect only on a surface that can honour it. Pin whichever with a renderer->sidecar contract test (the parity.test.ts pattern already exists at app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/generated/parity.test.ts:67).
- ⚠ scope correction: The Aspect control on the Reframe/MakeShorts surface is inert: `shortmaker.export` drops `params['aspect']` (allowlist is only reframeEngine/captionStyle/subtitleMode at sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1376), buildExportParams never emits it (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerPresets.ts:167-191), and no UI path writes `settings['aspect']`, so every export renders DEFAULT_ASPECT 9:16 (shortmaker.py:70,1225). Scope precision: the fallback is "9:16 unless settings['aspect'] is present" — a persisted aspect IS honoured (proven executably), but no shipped UI path writes it, so in practice output is always 9:16. Blast radius: the one-tap TikTok/Reels/Shorts presets all specify 9:16 (shortMakerPresets.ts:87-89) and are therefore unaffected; the defect bites a manual Aspect change and any saved custom export preset (whose 4:5/1:1 value is validated and persisted at export_presets.py:120,147 and forwarded by templates.py:161-163, then dropped). Severity high stands on correctness grounds — 1:1 and 4:5 are fully implemented downstream (aspect.py:31-35, both reframe engines), so this is a 2-line wire gap producing silently wrong renders, not a missing feature. Fix (a) must ALSO reconcile ASPECT_OPTIONS (shortMakerLogic.ts:308, includes 16:9) with SUPPORTED_ASPECTS (aspect.py:31-38, excludes 16:9), or a 16:9 pick will fail require_supported_aspect / take the generic 1920-long-edge fallback.
- ⚠ scope correction: The Aspect control on the Reframe/ShortMaker front door is inert: shortmaker.export renders at the DEFAULT_ASPECT 9:16 regardless of the user's pick, because buildExportParams (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerPresets.ts:160-192) never emits an `aspect` key and the sidecar handler's per-export allowlist (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1376) admits only reframeEngine/captionStyle/subtitleMode into settings, while run_export reads aspect ONLY from settings (shortmaker.py:1225). Nothing in the renderer or app/main ever writes settings['aspect'] (the sole ShortMaker settings.set patch is brandSettingsPatch's three brand keys, shortMakerPresets.ts:238-244), so the settings route is never populated. The batch path is affected identically: templates.py:161-163 merges the preset's `aspect` into the shortmaker.export step params and recipes.py:328-329 dispatches to the SAME allowlisted handler, which drops it — and the templates.py:104-105 comment claiming PRESET_CONTROL_FIELDS are "exactly the knobs shortmaker.export consumes" is false for aspect.

Three scope corrections to the original wording: (1) the cited `\.aspect\b` grep is a broken detector — it cannot match `settings.get("aspect")` or `op.params.get("aspect")`, and director_op_engines.py:783 DOES read and honour `op.params.get("aspect")`; the defensible narrower claim is that selection ignores aspect and the shortmaker.export wire hop drops it, not that "no code reads it". (2) The report missed sidecar/media_studio/features/aspect.py, a complete functional aspect registry (output_dimensions/ASPECT_PRESETS) consumed by all three reframe engines — the downstream plumbing is fully built, so only the renderer->sidecar hop is missing (a smaller fix than implied). (3) "Same fate" is wrong for 16:9 on the Batch preset path: export_presets.py:120 -> aspect.py:80-91 require_supported_aspect rejects anything outside {9:16, 1:1, 4:5}, so a preset typed 16:9 FAILS LOUD at save rather than silently rendering 9:16; the silent-drop applies to the valid non-default aspects (1:1, 4:5). Separately, ShortMaker's ASPECT_OPTIONS offers 16:9 that the preset catalog deems unsupported.

Additionally, proposed fix (a) is incomplete as written: adding 'aspect' to the allowlist alone introduces a new defect, because the CAPTION stage (shortmaker.py:1097-1098) and ZOOM stage (shortmaker.py:312-313) hardcode OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT = 1080x1920 (shortmaker.py:68-69) instead of deriving from aspect.output_dimensions(aspect); a 1:1/4:5 export would be reframed correctly then re-stretched to 1080x1920. Any wiring fix must thread aspect through those two stages as well.

## The Reframe phase's only corrective UI (ReframeOverridePanel, "Fix the framing") is mounted nowhere — disclosure level zero
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:121-157 is a complete surface: heading "Fix the framing" (:122), per-shot speaker Flip / Layout select / 4 crop nudges / 2 zoom steps / Reset (:194-264), and the primary action "Re-render N shot(s)" (:145-154).
It is never mounted. Repo-wide grep for `ReframeOverridePanel` returns only its own file, its test (app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.test.tsx:13), and docs.
Detector verified against known-present cases (single-signal rule): a `panels/` scan over app/renderer/src/**/*.tsx finds the static import DirectorPanel (app/renderer/src/views/Director.tsx:22) AND the lazy dynamic import ModelsSystemPanel (app/renderer/src/views/Settings.tsx:46) — so it would have found a dynamic mount of ReframeOverridePanel had one existed.
Its backing RPCs are equally unreached: client.reframe.shotPlan / client.reframe.applyOverrides (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:759-773) are called only from app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ce.test.ts:104-122.
The repo states it: docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46 — "PROMOTE reframe-to-vertical to first-class (wire the orphaned ReframeOverridePanel)"; :76 lists "ReframeOverridePanel wiring" as a WU-3a sub-unit. Its siblings shipped (WU-3a1/3a2/3a4 appear 38x across 14 renderer files); WU-3a3 appears 0 times.
- why: When the auto-crop follows the wrong speaker — the single most likely failure of an auto-reframe — the user has no affordance at any disclosure level. The only recourse is to change an engine dropdown and re-run the entire select->export pipeline, re-rendering every clip instead of the affected shots the panel was built to isolate (affectedShotIndices, ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:81).
- fix: Mount it as the reframe review step: after a select/export produces a trace, render ReframeOverridePanel behind a "Fix the framing" disclosure on the produced-clip surface (or as the Reframe destination in finding 5), wired to client.reframe.shotPlan -> applyOverrides -> re-render the `affected` set. Everything below the mount point (pure logic + RPCs + 100%-covered component) already exists.
- ⚠ scope correction: Correctly scoped: "Reframe ships NO manual framing correction at any disclosure level, and a complete, 100%-covered panel for it (ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:121-157, 'Fix the framing') sits orphaned — imported by no production code (only production panels/ mounts are Director.tsx:22 and Settings.tsx:46)." Severity MEDIUM (missing feature, not a defect): the orphan itself has zero runtime footprint and the app never advertises the affordance, so there is no disclosure defect — only an unbuilt capability the repo already tracks (docs/plans/v1.4-experience-overhaul.md:46,76-78). Explicitly DROP the mount-only fix: wiring it is NOT a mount, because (a) no trace is produced for the renderer (shortmaker.py and reframe_claudeshorts.py both have 0 hits for "trace"; reframe_multispeaker.py:913 builds one in-process and never persists it; schemas.generated.ts carries no trace/shotPlan/shots), and (b) no engine path re-renders the `affected` shot set (only reframe.eval/shotPlan/applyOverrides are registered; shortmaker.py:1388 takes captionOverride only). The prerequisite work is a trace producer surfaced over RPC plus a per-shot re-render parameter in the export path. Additionally scope the failure mode to the OPT-IN reframe_multispeaker engine: on the default auto->claudeshorts path (reframe.py:449-452) there are no per-shot speaker candidates or layouts at all (reframe_claudeshorts.py:101-117), so the panel as written could not correct the default user's wrong-subject crop.
- ⚠ scope correction: The FINDING headline needs no narrowing and stands as written at HIGH severity: ReframeOverridePanel ("Fix the framing", app/renderer/src/panels/ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:121-157) is the Reframe phase's only per-shot corrective UI, is mounted nowhere (disclosure level zero), and its RPCs (client.ts:759-773) are reached only by a unit test (client.ce.test.ts:105-122).

The one sentence that IS wider than its evidence is in the PROPOSED FIX: "Everything below the mount point (pure logic + RPCs + 100%-covered component) already exists." That is false — this is NOT a pure mount. Correctly scoped:

"The component, its pure edit math (lib/reframeOverride.ts), the typed RPC wrappers (client.ts:759-773) and the sidecar implementation (reframe_override.py:432-433) all exist and are covered. What does NOT exist is the data path that would feed the mount. The panel requires plan: ShotPlan (ReframeOverridePanel.tsx:68), derived by client.reframe.shotPlan({trace, sourceWidth, sourceHeight, fps}) (client.ts:761-766) from an R0 trace — and no renderer code ever obtains a trace: the only occurrences of `trace` under app/renderer/src are the RPC signature (client.ts:756,760,762) and its unit test (client.ce.test.ts:105-110). shortMakerLogic.ts sends reframeEngine outbound (:375) and receives no trace back, and sidecar/media_studio/handlers/composition.py emits no trace in any job result, though the producer exists sidecar-side (reframe_multispeaker.py:913 build_trace). The cross-phase channel the fix would ride is itself inert: setCropPlan is defined in the reducer (editorState.ts:104,150) but dispatched NOWHERE in production — only in editorState.test.ts:152-154 — so state.cropPlan is always null in the shipped app. Independent second signal: directorHandoff.ts:127 can therefore only ever read 'No crop plan yet — framing starts from center', and exportModel.ts:208 framingSummary can only ever return 'Original framing' — consistent with ExportInspector.test.tsx:53,64,72 and ExportStage.test.tsx:66, which assert only 'Original framing' and never 'Reframed'.

Therefore WU-3a3 is not a one-line mount but three additive pieces: (a) sidecar returns the ReframeTrace in the reframe/select job result, (b) renderer persists it (dispatch setCropPlan / hold the trace), (c) mount ReframeOverridePanel behind a 'Fix the framing' disclosure wired to shotPlan -> applyOverrides -> re-render the `affected` set."

This correction ENLARGES the defect (the whole reframe review channel is inert, not just the panel) and enlarges the fix estimate; it does not reduce the finding's severity.

## All Reframe/short-maker review work is destroyed by any top-tab navigation — candidates, approvals and boundary nudges are unrecoverable
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `renderRoute()` returns a different component per route inside one `<main>` (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:468-527), so leaving the `makeshorts` route unmounts `<MakeShorts>` and with it `<ShortMaker>`. Every piece of review state is component-local: `prompt`, `controls`, `phase`, `items` (the reducer holding candidates + approve/discard/nudge/reset), `exportedClips`, `audioTrackId`, `selectedId`, `sortMode` — app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:160-185, with the reducer at :170. Nothing writes any of it to the settings store; the renderer has no read-back RPC either — the client exposes only `shortmaker.select` and `shortmaker.export` (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:238-258) and the generated client lists only `shortmaker.select`. No unload/navigation guard exists anywhere in App.tsx.
- why: `shortmaker.select` is a long deferred job (it is waited on with `EXPORT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`, app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:522-539). A user who runs the reframe/moment-pick, reviews a dozen candidates, approves five and hand-nudges their in/out points, then clicks "Library" (or the Jobs pill route) to check something, returns to an empty panel with no warning and must pay for the whole selection job again. The sidecar even keeps a selection cache (referenced at ShortMaker.tsx:636-641) that the renderer can never read back.
- fix: Lift the per-video review session (prompt, sanitized controls, the `items` reducer state, `audioTrackId`, `selectedId`) into App shell state keyed by videoId — the same place `editVideo` already lives (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:268) — or persist it under a frozen settings key alongside `taskHubChoiceByVideo`. Minimum viable mitigation: add a `shortmaker.candidates {videoId}` read RPC so a remount can rehydrate the sidecar's cached selection, plus a confirm-on-navigate when `items.length > 0 && approvedIds(items).length > 0`.
- ⚠ scope correction: A user's short-maker review SESSION — the candidate list, approve/discard decisions and hand-nudged in/out boundaries — is silently and unrecoverably destroyed whenever `<ShortMaker>` unmounts, which happens on ANY top-tab navigation away from Make Shorts (App.tsx:468-527 + :565-572; 7 sibling tabs via :415-446) AND on switching the in-section "Produced shorts"/"Batch & Templates" tab (MakeShorts.tsx:212-214). All review state is component-local (ShortMaker.tsx:160-185, reducer :170); there is no client persistence (zero localStorage/sessionStorage in the renderer), no read-back RPC (only shortmaker.select/export are registered — client.ts:238-259, composition.py:144-145), and no navigation or unload guard anywhere. Recovery requires re-running the deferred `shortmaker.select` job in full — the sidecar handler has no cache short-circuit (shortmaker_ops.py:131-152) — and even then the approvals and nudges do not come back. The taste-profile labels DO survive (approve/discard/nudge fire `feedback.record`, ShortMaker.tsx:565-597), so what is lost is the actionable/exportable session, not the learning signal. Opening the Jobs slide-over does NOT trigger this (JobQueue renders outside `<main>`, App.tsx:574). Severity high stands: the loss is silent, unwarned, and costs a paid LLM selection job plus all manual review.
- ⚠ scope correction: The core claim is CONFIRMED verbatim, but three supporting details are overclaimed and one is under-scoped. Correctly-scoped version:

"ShortMaker's entire review session — candidate list, approve/discard decisions, and boundary nudges — is component-local (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:160-206) with no persistence and no read-back RPC (client.ts:238-259; composition.py:144-145), so it is silently and unrecoverably destroyed by ANY unmount of the panel, with no warning. Measured triggers: (a) any top-tab navigation away from `makeshorts` (App.tsx:468-527), and — more likely and NOT in the original finding — (b) a one-click switch to an adjacent sub-tab INSIDE Make Shorts (Make → Produced shorts / Batch & Templates, MakeShorts.tsx:200, 212-214)."

Corrections:
1. WRONG: "or the Jobs pill route". There is no `jobs` route — the `Route` union has no such member (App.tsx:97-105); the Jobs pill only toggles `jobsOpen` (App.tsx:544-560) and `<JobQueue>` renders as a sibling OUTSIDE the routed `<main>` (App.tsx:574). Opening the Jobs drawer does NOT unmount ShortMaker. One of the two destructive user actions the finding names is not destructive.
2. OVERSTATED: "must pay for the whole selection job again". Transcription — the most expensive stage — is cached in the manifest and is NOT re-paid (`_ensure_transcript` skips a usable transcript, shortmaker_ops.py:101-116). What IS re-paid: uncached boundary detection (:47-62) plus the LLM select call.
3. OVERSTATED: "ALL review work is destroyed". The implicit taste labels survive — every approve/discard/nudge fires fire-and-forget `recordFeedback` (ShortMaker.tsx:565-598), so the feedback flywheel's learning persists server-side. The candidate list and the decisions are lost; the learning is not.
4. UNDER-SCOPED (worse than claimed): unmount aborts only the renderer's wait, never the sidecar job (ShortMaker.tsx:809-810 vs :787-800), so a mid-select navigation lets the job complete and populate a cache (shortmaker_ops.py:151) that no RPC can read.

The proposed fix stands; `taskHubChoiceByVideo` is a real persisted key (app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:99), so the settings-key route is viable. The minimum mitigation should also cover the in-section sub-tab case, not just top-tab navigation.
- ⚠ scope correction: Leaving the Make Shorts tab discards the UNEXPORTED ShortMaker review SESSION, with no warning and no rehydration path. Switching to any of the 7 other top-level tabs (App.tsx:415-446) unmounts `<MakeShorts>` via the per-route switch in `renderRoute()` (App.tsx:468-527, :470-471), destroying the component-local session state: the candidate list and its pending/approved/discarded marks as a resumable set, the in-situ nudged boundaries, `prompt`, sanitized `controls`, `phase`, `audioTrackId`, `selectedId` and `sortMode` (ShortMaker.tsx:160-185, reducer at :170). Nothing persists this session and no read-back exists — the renderer's only shortmaker methods are `select` and `export` (client.ts:243-244, :258; sidecar registry shortmaker.py:1480-1481) — and there is no navigation guard anywhere in app/. Recovering the candidate list therefore requires re-running the full `shortmaker.select` job (no cache short-circuit: shortmaker_ops.py:142-151), even though the sidecar still holds the results in its in-memory `_selection_cache` (_services.py:157).

Scope corrections vs. the original: (a) the Jobs pill does NOT trigger this — it is a slide-over toggling `jobsOpen` (App.tsx:549) rendered outside `<main>` (App.tsx:574), and re-clicking the active Make Shorts tab is likewise a no-op; (b) the approve/discard/nudge DECISIONS are not destroyed — each is appended to an on-disk JSONL with post-nudge boundaries (ShortMaker.tsx:569/:577/:588-593 → feedback.py:116-124), they are simply not re-loadable by the UI; (c) exported clips are fully recoverable via `shorts.list` (client.ts:263-266) and the Library gallery (App.tsx:517-524). Severity: medium-high (a re-paid select job plus a redone review pass), not high data loss.

The mitigation still stands as proposed: lift the per-video session into App shell state beside `editVideo` (App.tsx:268) or persist it under a frozen settings key, and/or add a `shortmaker.candidates {videoId}` read RPC to rehydrate `_selection_cache`, plus a confirm-on-navigate gated on unexported approvals.

## ArrowRight from the Transcribe tab ejects the user out of the whole Workspace on the 5th press, dropping focus to <body>
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `keyboard-nav` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Probe (temporary vitest file, since deleted) driving the REAL `WORKSPACE_TABS`/`WORKSPACE_TAB_GROUPS` with `Workspace.handleSelect`'s logic mirrored: `press#5 from=refine -> onSelect=shortmaker` and `ejects (shortmaker deep-link fired) = 1`. Order derives from `app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:151-158` (`orderedIds`) over `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:76-90`: transcribe(0), search(1), subtitles(2), diarize(3), refine(4), shortmaker(5), timeline(6), dub(7). `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:191-193` intercepts `'shortmaker'` and calls `onOpenMakeShorts(video.id)` instead of `setActive`. That prop is LIVE in production: `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:480` passes `openMakeShortsForVideo` into `<Edit>`, `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:141` forwards it to `<Workspace>`, and `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375` does `setRoute({ name: 'makeshorts', videoId })` — unmounting the entire Workspace. `TabBar.tsx:166` then calls `btnRefs.current[nextId]!.focus()` on a button that the pending route flush is about to remove, so focus lands on `<body>`. My probe confirmed focus does move to the shortmaker button (`press#5 ... activeElement data-tab-id = shortmaker`) — it is the subsequent unmount that orphans it. No global keyboard shortcut layer mitigates this: Grep for `onKeyDown|addEventListener('keydown')|accessKey` in `app/renderer/src/App.tsx` returned no matches.
- why: A keyboard user on the Transcribe tab who presses ArrowRight to walk the tab strip is teleported out of the per-video Workspace into a different top-level section on the 5th press, losing the workspace context AND their focus position (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order / 2.4.7 Focus Visible — focus on `<body>` has no visible indicator). Worse, forward arrow navigation can never reach the tabs BEYOND shortmaker: `timeline`, `dub` and the whole Deliver cluster are unreachable via ArrowRight from Transcribe, because the traversal terminates the surface. They remain reachable only by the non-obvious backwards route (ArrowLeft wraps to `dub`) or `End`. A mouse user never encounters this — they click `Timeline` directly and never pass through `shortmaker`. This is a keyboard-only dead end.
- fix: Primary: adopt manual activation in `TabBar.tsx:160-167` (see the sibling finding) so arrow keys move focus only and the cross-section deep-link fires solely on deliberate Enter/Space/click. Belt-and-braces for the deliberate case: in `Workspace.tsx:191-193`, before calling `onOpenMakeShorts`, hand off focus explicitly (the destination view should focus its heading/first control) — the repo already has this pattern in `app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:107-113`, which focuses the panel on open and restores focus to the invoker on close. Add a regression test asserting ArrowRight from `data-tab-id="transcribe"` never invokes `onOpenMakeShorts`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Scope/calibration refinement only (the defect itself is CONFIRMED as written): "TabBar's activation-follows-focus arrow navigation (app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:168-175) fires the cross-section 'shortmaker' deep-link (Workspace.tsx:189-198 → Edit.tsx:141 → App.tsx:480 → App.tsx:373-375) during mere arrow-key traversal, unmounting the Workspace mid-keystroke and orphaning focus to <body>. Reachable in 3 ArrowRight presses from the DEFAULT landing tab 'subtitles' (not 5 from Transcribe — Transcribe is not the default), and unavoidable for keyboard users because roving tabindex (TabBar.tsx:97) makes arrow keys the only tab-switching mechanism. Consequence: Timeline and Dub are unreachable by forward arrow traversal, and the next Tab press restarts at the document top. Violates WCAG 3.2.1 On Focus (primary) and 2.4.3 Focus Order; 2.4.7 Focus Visible does not strictly apply. Severity: medium (functional keyboard dead-end + WCAG failure on an a11y-gated project, but recoverable, no data loss, mouse users unaffected) rather than high. Not caught by the existing axe gate (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts), which is static."
- ⚠ scope correction: Arrow-key traversal of the Workspace tablist ejects the user out of the Workspace whenever focus lands on the `shortmaker` tab (index 5 of `orderedIds`). TabBar's arrow nav uses AUTOMATIC activation — `move()` calls `onSelect(nextId)` then focuses it (app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:168-175) — and `Workspace.handleSelect` intercepts `'shortmaker'` to fire the cross-section deep-link `onOpenMakeShorts` instead of `setActive` (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:189-198). That prop is live in production (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375 -> App.tsx:480 -> app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:141), and `setRoute({name:'makeshorts'})` replaces the entire Edit subtree (App.tsx:469-471), so the button TabBar.tsx:174 just focused is unmounted and `document.activeElement` becomes `<body>` (measured). Nothing restores focus: App.tsx has no keydown/focus handling (only `focusable="false"` on an SVG at App.tsx:154) and MakeShorts.tsx has no focus/autoFocus.

TRIGGER (broader than "5th press from Transcribe"): from the DEFAULT landing tab `subtitles` (Workspace.tsx:96) it fires on ArrowRight press #3; from `transcribe` on press #5; and BACKWARD traversal fires too — ArrowLeft from transcribe wraps to `dub`, then `timeline`, then ejects on press #3 (same via `End` + two ArrowLefts). Opening the Advanced disclosure does not help (still ejects forward on press #5).

CONSEQUENCE, correctly scoped: `timeline` and `dub` are unreachable by forward ArrowRight and only transiently reachable backwards before the next press ejects. The Deliver tabs (`convert`, `nle`, `recipes`, `assets`, `tracks`, Workspace.tsx:84-89) must be DROPPED from this consequence in the default state — with `advancedOpen=false` (Workspace.tsx:131) they are excluded from `orderedIds` altogether by the collapsed-advanced filter (TabBar.tsx:159-166), a separate deliberate behavior documented at TabBar.tsx:155-158, not an effect of this defect.

Primary WCAG mapping is 3.2.2 On Input (Level A) — an arrow-key setting change causing an unrequested change of context — rather than the cited 2.4.7 Focus Visible. Fix and regression test as proposed (manual activation in TabBar's keydown handler; explicit focus hand-off before the deep-link, per the existing pattern at app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:107-113), but assert the invariant as "no arrow/Home/End key ever invokes onOpenMakeShorts, from ANY starting tab and in BOTH directions" rather than only ArrowRight from `transcribe`.

## Library has ONE theme (dark) and every focus indicator disappears under Windows forced-colors, because the ring is box-shadow-only with outline explicitly removed
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `dark-light-parity` · verifiers 3
- evidence: THEME DETERMINATION (dark-only): app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:20 declares `color-scheme: dark` on `:root` and that is the ONLY theme mechanism in the renderer. Grep over app/renderer for `prefers-color-scheme|data-theme|\.light|\.dark` returns exactly ONE hit — tokens.css:20 itself. Grep over all of app/ for `forced-colors|forcedColors|high-contrast|prefers-contrast`: NO MATCHES. So there is no light theme and no forced-colors handling anywhere.

THE DEFECT: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52 — `:where(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); }`. Re-declared on the Library surface at app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:63-67 (the card's primary open button), library-cards.css:256-259 (card provenance toggle), and app/renderer/src/features/library-provenance.css:80-83 (reveal/relink buttons). tokens.css:206 defines `--focus-ring` purely as a box-shadow.

EMPIRICAL PROBE (independent 2nd signal — Chromium via playwright-core 1.61.1, `newContext({forcedColors:'active'})`, the verbatim CSS above):
  forced-colors:none   -> focusedOpenBtn { outlineStyle:"none", boxShadow:"rgb(18,22,32) 0 0 0 2px, rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 4px" }
  forced-colors:active -> focusedOpenBtn { outlineStyle:"none", boxShadow:"none" }
Both the outline AND the box-shadow are absent, so NOTHING is painted. `outlineWidth:3px`/`outlineColor` are set but inert because `outlineStyle` is `none`.
- why: Only a dark theme exists, so the codebase never had to think about a foreign palette — but Windows 11 ships four Contrast themes (Desert is LIGHT: near-white background, Aquatic/Dusk/Night sky are dark) and forced-colors overrides `color-scheme: dark` entirely (the same probe shows `pageBg` becomes `rgb(255,255,255)` despite tokens.css:20). In that mode a keyboard user gets zero focus indication across the whole Library — Add videos, Lineage view, search, sort select, batch Remove/Clear, the per-card select checkbox, the card open button, "N shorts", Remove, the provenance toggle and its reveal/relink actions, and the shorts-modal close. That is a WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) failure, and it lands on precisely the user population that enables High Contrast in the first place. It is invisible to CI: app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:79 emulates only `reducedMotion`, and app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts never enters forced-colors.
- fix: Make the ring an `outline`, not a `box-shadow`, so it survives forced-colors and gets a real transparent gap for free: in tokens.css keep `--focus-ring` for decoration but drive the indicator with `outline: 2px solid var(--accent-edge); outline-offset: 2px;` in shell.css:49-52 (dropping `outline: none`), then delete the redundant `outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` overrides at library-cards.css:63-67, library-cards.css:256-259 and library-provenance.css:80-83. If the box-shadow ring must stay, add a global `@media (forced-colors: active) { :where(button,[role="button"],[role="tab"],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px; } }`. Pin it with a spec that calls `win.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` in app/e2e/visual/ and asserts a non-`none` computed `outlineStyle` on `.library__item-open`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Under Windows forced-colors (High Contrast), NO Library control retains a WCAG-2.4.7-conformant focus indicator, because the one shared focus rule sets `outline: none` and paints the ring purely with box-shadow — and forced-colors forces box-shadow to `none`. Mechanism: shell.css:49-52 `:where(button,[role="button"],[role="tab"],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) }`, with `--focus-ring` defined box-shadow-only at tokens.css:206, re-declared on Library at library-cards.css:63-67, library-cards.css:256-259 and library-provenance.css:80-83. Confirmed by probe (Chromium forcedColors:'active' -> outlineStyle:"none" AND boxShadow:"none" on button, native checkbox and select), with a same-run control proving the repo's existing outline-based rule at directorPanel.css:74-75 SURVIVES (outlineStyle:"solid", color forced to system Highlight). No forced-colors handling exists anywhere in app/ (grep: 0 matches), and CI cannot see it — `emulateMedia` occurs exactly once in app/, at _visualSetup.ts:79, for reducedMotion only.

TWO TRIMS to the original wording:
(a) DROP the "Library has ONE theme (dark)" clause as a defect. It is factually true (tokens.css:20 is the only theme mechanism) but dark-only is deliberate, documented product direction (tokens.css:1-14, "DIRECTION: dark editorial for a video tool"). With no light theme there is nothing to be out of "dark-light-parity" with, so the clause is scene-setting that inflates the headline, not a second defect. The lens label is a poor fit; the defect is forced-colors focus loss, full stop.
(b) SOFTEN "nothing is painted" / "zero focus indication across the whole Library". library-cards.css:162-166 raises the per-card select checkbox on `:focus-within` via `opacity`, and opacity is NOT forced in forced-colors mode, so tabbing into a card does yield one observable cue (which card you are in). It is not a conformant indicator — not on the focused component, and it cannot disambiguate controls within a card — and it does nothing for Add videos, search, the sort select, batch Remove/Clear, or the shorts-modal close. Accurate phrasing: "no conformant focus indicator on any Library control; the sole residual cue is the card-level checkbox reveal."

Settling experiment (as proposed, and validated by my probe): add a spec calling `win.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` in app/e2e/visual/ asserting computed `outlineStyle !== 'none'` on `.library__item-open`; it must FAIL on today's tree and PASS after the outline-based fix.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim in its load-bearing content; the defect is real and executable-proven. Two sub-claims need tightening, and one fix-scope item must be added:

"The Library surface has ONE theme (dark: tokens.css:20 `color-scheme: dark`, the only theme mechanism in the renderer AND no `nativeTheme`/`themeSource` anywhere in app/), and under Windows forced-colors EVERY Library focus indicator paints zero pixels, because each Library ring is box-shadow-only with `outline: none` (shell.css:49-52, library-cards.css:63-67 and :256-259, library-provenance.css:80-83) and forced-colors forces `box-shadow` to `none`. Proven at pixel level: focused vs unfocused screenshots are byte-identical under `forcedColors:'active'`, and Chromium paints no substitute UA ring.

Scope corrections: (a) `outline: none` is Library-wide but NOT repo-wide — directorPanel.css:73-76/293-296/370-373 and captionBox.css:59-62 already use outline-based rings, which the same probe shows DO survive forced-colors; (b) the cited grep regex `prefers-color-scheme|data-theme|\.light|\.dark` returns ZERO hits, not one — reproducing the tokens.css:20 hit requires adding `color-scheme` to the alternation.

Fix scope must additionally include app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:143, which asserts `getComputedStyle(el).boxShadow).not.toBe('none')` and will break if the ring is migrated from box-shadow to outline."
- ⚠ scope correction: Library's keyboard focus indicator is box-shadow-only with `outline` explicitly removed (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:49-52; `--focus-ring` is a pure box-shadow at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:206; re-declared at library-cards.css:63-67, library-cards.css:256-259, library-provenance.css:80-83), so it fails in two distinct ways:

(1) ALREADY BROKEN, no forced-colors needed, default dark theme, every user: "Add videos" (`.library__add-btn`, Library.tsx:482) and the per-card "Remove" (`.library__remove-btn`, LibraryCard.tsx:159-166) paint NOTHING on keyboard focus — measured 0px and 1px of changed pixels. `:where()` contributes zero specificity, so shell.css:49-52 computes to (0,1,0) and loses the source-order tie to shell.css:417 `box-shadow: var(--accent-glow)` and shell.css:390 `box-shadow: none` later in the same file. This is a live WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) failure right now and the highest-value part of the finding.

(2) UNDER Windows forced-colors (all four Windows 11 Contrast themes), `box-shadow` is forced to `none` while `outline-style: none` is NOT restored, so the ring vanishes for the FOCUSED CONTROL on: `.library__item-open`, `.library__select-box`, `.library__shorts-label`, `.library__remove-btn`, `.card-provenance__toggle`, `.library-provenance__btn` (+`--relink`), `.library-toolbar__batch-remove`, `.library-toolbar__batch-clear`, `.library__add-btn`, `.library__lineage-toggle`, `.shorts-modal__close` — measured 0 changed pixels each. TWO Library controls DO retain a usable indicator and must be excluded from the claim: `.library-toolbar__search` (815px) and `.library-toolbar__sort-select` (244px), whose 1px borders are recoloured by the UA from rgb(0,0,0) to rgb(55,0,110) on focus. A card-level side-effect also survives — the multi-select checkbox materialises via `li.library__item:focus-within .library__select { opacity: 1 }` (library-cards.css:163-166), 178px, `opacity` not being a forced property — but it is identical for all six card controls, so it signals "focus is somewhere in this card" without identifying which control, and does not satisfy 2.4.7.

Scope note: shell.css:49-52 is GLOBAL, so (2) is app-wide, not Library-specific — 40+ sites across app/renderer/src re-declare `outline: none`, while only captionBox.css:59-61 and directorPanel.css:73-75/293-295/370-372 use a real `outline` that survives. Dark-only is a deliberate documented direction (tokens.css:1-14) and is a premise, not part of the defect.

Both gaps are invisible to CI: app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:79 emulates only `reducedMotion`, `forced-colors` appears nowhere in app/, and the one focus assertion (app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:138-145) reads `boxShadow !== 'none'` on `.toptab` only — which also means the finding's PRIMARY fix (replace the box-shadow ring with an outline) would break that assertion; prefer the additive `@media (forced-colors: active) { ... outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px }` block plus a `!important`-or-reordered ring so it beats shell.css:390/417, and pin it with specs that assert a non-`none` computed `outlineStyle` under `emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'})` AND a non-zero focus-vs-unfocus pixel delta on `.library__add-btn` and `.library__remove-btn` in the DEFAULT theme.

## Reframe stage's real per-frame progress is never wired into the export job — the bar freezes at a per-clip integer (0% for the entire render on a 1-clip export)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `loading-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The orchestrator drops the channel: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:254` declares `def _lazy_reframe(in_path, out_path, aspect, *, settings=None, on_notice=None)` — no `on_progress` param — and `:262` calls `engine.reframe(in_path, out_path, aspect, on_notice=on_notice)`. Call site `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1039`: `stages.reframe(stage_clip, reframed_path, aspect, settings=settings, on_notice=_reframe_notice)`.
Every engine implements the channel: `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_claudeshorts.py:1144-1149` (`self._runner(argv, total_sec=duration, on_progress=on_progress, should_cancel=should_cancel)`) with `-progress pipe:1 -nostats` already in the argv at `reframe_claudeshorts.py:479-481`; `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe_multispeaker.py:1435` (`backend.analyze(..., on_progress=on_progress, ...)`) and `:1451`; `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:247-250` + `:328-335` convert ffmpeg `out_time` into a pct.
The ONLY export ticks are `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1282-1283`: `_pct[0] = int(100 * i / total)` / `ctx.progress(_pct[0], f"exporting clip {i+1}/{total}")`.
EXECUTED probe (temporary script against the sidecar venv, since deleted) driving `sm.run_export` with a recording ctx and a kwargs-capturing reframe stage:
  `n=5 events=[(2,'loading source'),(0,'exporting clip 1/5'),(20,...),(40,...),(60,...),(80,...),(100,'exported 5 clip(s)')]`
  `n=1 events=[(2,'loading source'),(0,'exporting clip 1/1'),(100,'exported 1 clip(s)')]`
  `reframe stage kwargs seen = [{'settings','on_notice'}]`  ← no on_progress, no should_cancel
UI consumers render that value as a DETERMINATE bar with no indeterminate/pulse styling: `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:926` (`<progress max={100} value={displayPct(progress.pct)} />`), styled at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1125-1144`; `app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:222-224` shows the same number.
In-repo precedent that the whole chain works: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:431` and `sidecar/media_studio/features/convert.py:338` both pass `on_progress=lambda pct,msg: job_ctx.progress(pct,msg)`, and `app/renderer/src/features/Convert.tsx:63-67,327` renders the resulting smooth bar.
- why: REFRAME is the longest stage of the app's flagship operation (MediaPipe/YuNet subject tracking or GPU multi-speaker ASD, then a full re-encode). With the default `count: 5` the bar advances exactly 5 times; with a single approved clip it sits at a determinate 0% for the entire multi-minute render and then jumps to 100%. A determinate bar pinned at 0% reads as "stuck/broken", not "working" — the classic progress lie this lens exists to catch. The fix is not new plumbing: the source, the transport (`job.progress`), and the renderer are all already built and used by Convert/Transcribe; only the reframe call site is unplugged.
- fix: Add `on_progress` (and `should_cancel`) to the `ReframeStage` contract at `shortmaker.py:110-112`, thread it through `_lazy_reframe` (`shortmaker.py:254-262`), and at the call site (`shortmaker.py:1039`) pass a band-scaled sink so the engine's 0-100 lands inside this clip's slice, e.g. `on_progress=lambda p, m: ctx.progress(clip_lo + (clip_hi - clip_lo) * p / 100, m)` where `clip_lo/clip_hi` are the current clip's percent band. Mirror the same treatment for the other heavy stages (`_lazy_stabilize`, `_lazy_caption`, `_lazy_export`), which are equally unplugged.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands unchanged and CONFIRMED: Reframe stage's real per-frame progress is never wired into the export job — the bar advances only once per clip (0% for the entire render on a 1-clip export). Two supporting sentences need tightening, and one fix-scope caveat should be added: (1) instead of "Every engine implements the channel", say "the DEFAULT engine (claudeshorts, per reframe.py:450-452) and the flagship multispeaker engine both implement and forward the channel (reframe_claudeshorts.py:1123,1144-1149; reframe_multispeaker.py:1435,1451); the opt-in verthor engine accepts on_progress but intentionally no-ops it because tracking runs inside WSL (reframe.py:305,330, documented :323-327)". (2) instead of "The fix is not new plumbing", say "the source, transport (job.progress) and renderer already exist and are used by Convert/Transcribe; the fix adds one parameter to the ReframeStage contract (shortmaker.py:110-112), to _lazy_reframe (:254-262), and to _export_one (:890-907, which today receives only the ctx-capturing on_notice closure built at :1256-1261) — a small signature change in three places, not new transport". (3) Add inline: even once wired, only the ffmpeg re-encode pass reports progress; the claudeshorts subject-detection pass (compute_plan, reframe_claudeshorts.py:1134) has no progress channel (on_progress occurs only at :1123/:1147), so the bar will still sit still during MediaPipe/YuNet tracking unless compute_plan gains its own channel.
- ⚠ scope correction: Reframe stage's real per-frame progress AND cancellation are never wired into the export job. `on_progress`/`should_cancel` appear zero times in `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py`: `_lazy_reframe` (:254) omits both and `:262`/`:1039` pass only `settings`/`on_notice`, and `_lazy_cut` (:217) / `_lazy_export` (:456) likewise call `_ffmpeg.run(argv)` bare — even though `-progress pipe:1 -nostats` is already in the argv (:212-214). The only export ticks are `int(100*i/total)` (:1282-1283) plus 2% at :1218 and 100% at :1303, so a 1-clip export shows a DETERMINATE 0% for the entire multi-minute render, after first stepping BACKWARD from 2% to 0% (violating the forward-only invariant asserted at :1251-1254). Two user-visible consequences: (1) the bar affirmatively misreports "no work done" with no indeterminate styling available (`ShortMaker.tsx:926`, `shell.css:1123-1144`, `JobQueue.tsx:222-224`) and a `role="status"` live region that announces once then goes silent (`ShortMaker.tsx:925`); (2) more seriously, the Cancel button is offered for running jobs (`JobQueue.tsx:26-27`) but is inert for the whole render, because `ctx.raise_if_cancelled()` only runs at the per-clip loop top (:1275) and `ffmpeg.run`'s cancel watchdog only arms when `should_cancel` is passed (`ffmpeg.py:261-266`) — so the realistic outcome is the user force-quitting a healthy export. Scope corrections: this affects the DEFAULT engine path only in the sense that 2 of 3 engines emit progress — claudeshorts (default via `auto`, `reframe.py:437-452`; emits at `reframe_claudeshorts.py:1123,1147`) and multispeaker (`reframe_multispeaker.py:1435,1451`) — while the explicit-opt-in verthor engine deliberately no-ops `on_progress` (`reframe.py:330`, documented :323-327), so wiring yields nothing for verthor users. REFRAME is not verifiably the single longest stage (detection is capped at 90 sampled windows, `reframe_claudeshorts.py:75-76`); the defensible framing is that the entire multi-encode per-clip pipeline is silent. The fix must band-scale into the current clip's percent slice and override ffmpeg's raw "12.3%"/"done" messages (`ffmpeg.py:327-335`), and will still leave `compute_plan` (`reframe_claudeshorts.py:1134`) unreported. In-repo precedent: `convert.py:338`, `media_ops.py:431,513`, `system_ops.py:350,405`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Headline stands unchanged: "Reframe stage's real per-frame progress is never wired into the export job — the bar freezes at a per-clip integer (0% for the entire render on a 1-clip export)." Three supporting sentences should be narrowed:

(1) "Every engine implements the channel" -> "Both IN-SIDECAR engines implement the channel — `reframe_claudeshorts.py:1123,1144-1149` and `reframe_multispeaker.py:1421,1435,1451` — and `auto` resolves to claudeshorts by default (`reframe.py:437-443`), so the default path is affected. The third (verthor) engine at `reframe.py:300-330` accepts `on_progress` but intentionally discards it (`_ = on_progress`, `reframe.py:330`) because tracking runs inside WSL; its docstring at `reframe.py:323-325` nonetheless names `shortmaker._lazy_reframe` as the intended threader."

(2) "Mirror the same treatment for the other heavy stages (`_lazy_stabilize`, `_lazy_caption`, `_lazy_export`), which are equally unplugged" -> "`_lazy_caption` and `_lazy_export` receive no `on_progress` at the orchestrator seam (probe-confirmed), so those are threadable in the same way. `_lazy_stabilize` is NOT symmetric: its downstream seam `stabilize.stabilize_clip` (`stabilize.py:360-369`) does not accept `on_progress` at all — the channel exists only deeper (`stabilize.py:330,342`) and in the standalone RPC handler (`stabilize.py:460`), so that stage needs new plumbing inside the feature module, not just a forwarded kwarg. Same for `silencetrim.trim_clip` (`silencetrim.py:237-249`)."

(3) "The ONLY export ticks are `shortmaker.py:1282-1283`" -> "The only ticks INSIDE the per-clip render loop are `shortmaker.py:1282-1283`; `run_export` also emits `:1218` (2%, 'loading source'), `:1261` (notice re-emit at the current pct) and `:1303` (terminal 100%)."

(4) "REFRAME is the longest stage of the app's flagship operation" is UNVERIFIED — no timing measurement was taken; it is inferred from the code path (MediaPipe/YuNet tracking plus a full re-encode). The defect and its severity do not depend on it, since the bar is pinned at one integer for the whole clip regardless of which stage dominates. Settling experiment: time each stage of a 1-clip export with per-stage wall-clock logging.

Additionally worth folding into the finding: `should_cancel` is unwired on the same seam (0 occurrences in shortmaker.py vs 12 `should_cancel=lambda: job_ctx.cancelled` sites elsewhere; `reframe.py:317-321` documents the intended wiring), and cancellation is only polled at `shortmaker.py:1275`, so Cancel cannot interrupt a multi-minute single-clip reframe. And the 1-clip progress sequence is non-monotonic (2% -> 0%) because `jobs.py:137-139` clamps only to 0..100 with no forward-only guard.

## Cancelling a reframe is a pending-state lie: the UI resets to idle instantly while the sidecar renders the current clip to completion
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `loading-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Renderer resets synchronously, before/independently of the sidecar: `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:787-791` — `const cancel = useCallback(async () => { const jobId = activeJobRef.current; tearDownWait(); setPhase('idle'); setProgress(null); ... })`, then fires `job.cancel` at `:796`. `busy` goes false, the progress block at `:924` unmounts, and "Export approved" (`:968-975`) re-enables.
Sidecar cancellation is cooperative only: `sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:119-121` ("The handler is expected to poll `cancelled`") and `:108-112` ("the handler thread may still be stuck in a blocking native call (Python cannot kill it)"). The ENTIRE export body has exactly one checkpoint — `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1275` `ctx.raise_if_cancelled()` at the top of each clip iteration (grep for `should_cancel|raise_if_cancelled` in that file returns only lines 786, 801, 1275).
No stage gets a cancel probe — probe-confirmed kwargs at the reframe seam: `reframe stage kwargs seen = [{'settings','on_notice'}]`.
The engines each implement prompt termination that is therefore unreachable from this path: `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:254-273` (`_await_verthor` terminates the child when `should_cancel()` fires) and `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:398-425` (`watch_cancel` tears the child down). `sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:317-321` even documents the wiring as done — "`should_cancel` (wired from the job as `lambda: job_ctx.cancelled`) is polled while verthor runs" — which is false for this call path.
- why: The user presses Cancel because a render is taking too long; the UI immediately says nothing is running while ffmpeg/GPU keeps burning through the current clip (for a single-clip export, the whole remaining render). Two concrete harms: (a) the machine stays pegged with no visible job, and (b) with `max_workers: 2` (`sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:226,241`) the user can immediately click "Export approved" again, so a second export runs concurrently against the same `out_dir_for(videoId)` and the same intermediate stems (`{base_stem}-{rank}.cut.mp4`, `.trimmed.mp4`) written in `_export_one` — a plausible clobber I did NOT execute (marked inferred). Cancel is the one escape hatch a frozen progress bar leaves the user, and it is cosmetic.
- fix: Thread `should_cancel=lambda: job_ctx.cancelled` into every stage seam the same way `media_ops.py:432` and `:514` already do — minimally `_lazy_reframe` (`shortmaker.py:254-262`) and the `stages.reframe(...)` call at `shortmaker.py:1039`, so `ffmpeg.run`'s `watch_cancel` / `_await_verthor` can terminate the child. On the renderer side, keep the pending UI up in a `cancelling…` state until the sidecar confirms (job.done with `type: 'JobCancelled'`) rather than flipping to idle optimistically, and keep the export button disabled until then.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM — Short-maker Cancel is a partial-stop misreported as a full stop: the panel flips to idle while the CURRENT clip finishes rendering uncancellably. `cancel()` sets `setPhase('idle')` synchronously at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:790, before/independently of the `job.cancel` RPC at :796. Sidecar cancellation is cooperative (sidecar/media_studio/jobs.py:119-121) and `JobRegistry.cancel` on a RUNNING job only sets the flag (jobs.py:829-830). `run_export` has exactly ONE checkpoint — `ctx.raise_if_cancelled()` at the top of each clip iteration (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1275); `_export_one` (:890-1178) has none, and no stage receives a cancel probe: `_lazy_reframe` (:254-262) and the `stages.reframe(...)` call (:1039) pass only `on_notice`. Because shortmaker.py:262 is the ONLY production call site of `get_engine(...).reframe(...)`, all three engines' termination paths are unreachable in production — `_await_verthor` (sidecar/media_studio/features/reframe.py:254-273) and `ffmpeg.py:398-425 watch_cancel` never run — which makes reframe.py:317-321's docstring ("`should_cancel` … wired from the job as `lambda: job_ctx.cancelled` … is polled while verthor runs") false for every live path. SCOPED IMPACT: with the default `count: 5` (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:288), cancel DOES abort every not-yet-started clip, so it is not cosmetic — the uncancellable residual is one clip's ffmpeg/GPU render (the whole export only for a single-clip export or a cancel during the last clip), bounded at 30 min by the watchdog (sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:43). The harm is NOT an invisible job: the header "Jobs" pill (App.tsx:544-560, useActiveJobs.ts 5s poll of job.list) and the JobQueue panel (JobQueue.tsx:126,213-214) both keep showing it `running`, so the app CONTRADICTS itself — header says 1 job running, panel says idle. The real harms are (i) that contradiction plus a lost progress bar for work still in flight, and (ii) "Export approved" re-enabling immediately (ShortMaker.tsx:620 guards only on `busy`; :965 is not phase-gated), which dispatches a second export that runs CONCURRENTLY — the job is not gpu-tagged (shortmaker.py:1444; gpu default False at jobs.py:586) and production uses max_workers=2 (rpc.py:72-77) — against the same `out_dir_for(videoId)` and the same intermediate stems (`{base_stem}-{rank}.cut.mp4`, `.trimmed.mp4`) written in `_export_one`; the resulting clobber is INFERRED, not executed. FIX (unchanged in direction): thread `should_cancel=lambda: job_ctx.cancelled` through `_lazy_reframe` and every `stages.*` seam the way handlers/media_ops.py:432,514 already do, and hold a `cancelling…` pending state (button still disabled) until the sidecar's terminal `job.done` with `{"error":{"type":"JobCancelled"}}` arrives (jobs.py:793-796 does emit it) instead of flipping to idle optimistically.

## "Remove" and "Strip" sit side by side and neither label says what it destroys
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.tsx:235-251 renders `Remove`, `Burn in`, and `Strip` as three adjacent one-click buttons per row, with no confirmation and no explanatory copy (the panel's only prose is the `<h2>Subtitle tracks</h2>` at Tracks.tsx:190). The sidecar semantics are entirely different: `remove_track` deletes the subtitle track and its cues from the project (sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:124-136), while `strip_track` re-muxes the media file omitting an embedded subtitle stream and writes a NEW output path (tracks.py:557-568). `Burn in` likewise produces a new file (tracks.py:468-482) but the label does not say so. Button text corroborated by app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.test.tsx:182 (`Remove`), :219 (`Strip`), :250 (`Burn in`).
- why: "Remove" and "Strip" are near-synonyms in plain English. A user wanting to get embedded subtitles out of their media file will reach for the plainer word, "Remove", and instead delete the subtitle track they hand-edited in the Timeline panel — there is no undo control anywhere in Tracks.tsx. The label gives them no way to tell the two apart before clicking.
- fix: Name the object and the consequence: `Delete track` (destructive, on the project) vs `Save a copy without embedded subtitles` (or `Export without subtitles`), and `Burn in` → `Burn into a new video`. Add a one-line panel intro stating that Delete affects only this project while the other two write new files.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM-HIGH (copy-microcopy, Edit phase -> Workspace -> Tracks panel, behind the default-closed Advanced disclosure at app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:87-88 and :131):

Within one `.track-ops` control cluster, `Remove` (app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.tsx:235-237) and `Strip` (:249-251) are near-synonyms in plain English whose consequences are ASYMMETRIC, and neither label discloses which is which. `Remove` is the only destructive one: `remove_track` (sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:124-136) deletes the track row together with its `cues`, and sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:254-259 persists that with `project.save()` — irreversibly, since Tracks.tsx offers no undo and Timeline.tsx:473-477's Undo is an in-memory cue history that cannot resurrect a saved manifest deletion. `Strip` is NON-destructive: it re-muxes to a new sibling `-stripped` file (tracks.py:568, `-map 0 -map -0:s:N -c copy` at build_strip_argv:420-435), leaving the source intact. `Burn in` (:238-240) likewise writes a new `-hardsub.mp4` (tracks.py:490) without saying so.

Failure path: a user wanting embedded subtitles out of their media file reaches for the plainer word `Remove` and permanently loses the cues they hand-edited in the Timeline tab (Workspace.tsx:41 aliases TimelinePanel to features/Timeline; Timeline.tsx:8 loads via `tracks.list`, :356 saves via `subtitles.edit`). All three ops fire on a single click through `runOp` (Tracks.tsx:70-92) with no confirmation, and no `title`/`aria-describedby`/intro copy distinguishes them — a Tracks-specific gap, since the codebase already uses tooltips (Assets.tsx:208) and an explicit consent gate (BatchConsentCard.tsx). `HardSubtitleError` (tracks.py:132-133) guards only `kind=="hard"`, so the hand-edited soft track at risk is unprotected.

Scope corrections vs. the original finding: the two buttons are NOT adjacent (`Burn in` at :238-240 and a conditional `Cancel` at :244-248 sit between them); `Strip` destroys nothing, so the defect is an asymmetry rather than two unlabelled destructive ops; and the panel's prose is not limited to the `<h2>` at :190 (see also :199, :260, :283-288) — it simply contains nothing that explains these three ops.

Fix as proposed: `Delete track` vs `Export without subtitles` vs `Burn into a new video`, plus a one-line panel intro stating that Delete affects only this project while the other two write new files. Verified accurate. Given the irreversible persisted write, a confirmation on Delete is worth adding alongside the rename.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding is CONFIRMED as written; two tightenings only, neither reducing severity.

(a) Minor precision: "the panel's only prose is the <h2> at Tracks.tsx:190" should read "the panel carries no explanatory prose — only the <h2>Subtitle tracks</h2> at :190, the empty-state 'No subtitle tracks.' at :199, and the <h3>Add an existing track</h3> at :260, none of which explain what any button destroys."

(b) Material: the proposed fix for Strip is incomplete. Relabelling Strip to "Save a copy without embedded subtitles"/"Export without subtitles" would still mislead, because tracks_strip validates trackId at sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:271 then discards it and calls strip_track(in_path, ...) at :279 with no sub_stream_index, defaulting to 0 (sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:561). Per-row Strip always strips subtitle stream 0 regardless of the row clicked, so a per-row label implying it acts on THAT row is wrong at the behaviour level too. The copy fix must be paired with either threading the row's stream index through tracks_strip, or moving Strip out of the per-row control group to a panel-level action.

Additionally, the fix should reuse the existing in-repo destructive-confirm pattern (app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.tsx:160-166) rather than inventing one, since KeepCopyControl.tsx:21 already declares the governing rule "never a silent one-click destructive action."
- ⚠ scope correction: "Remove" and "Strip" sit side by side in one `.track-ops` div (app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.tsx:235-251) and neither label names what it destroys. `Remove` calls `tracks.remove`, which deletes the track and its hand-edited cues from the project (sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:131-136) and PERSISTS that deletion immediately via `project.save()` (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:259), with no confirmation and no undo in the panel. `Strip` and `Burn in` instead write NEW output files (tracks.py:568, :490) and leave the project untouched. No explanatory copy or tooltip distinguishes them: the buttons carry no `title`/`aria-describedby` and `panels.css:140` adds none — the panel's prose (Tracks.tsx:190, :199, :260, :283-288) never describes any of the three operations. Exposure is reduced but not removed by the Tracks tab living behind the `advanced: true` "Deliver" disclosure (app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:84-89).

## Make front door has no scroll container: 575-919px of the surface (incl. the primary CTA and the whole Output Tray) sits below the fold and the app bar + Jobs button scroll away
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `.make-shorts__panel` (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:201) has NO CSS rule anywhere — a repo-wide grep for `make-shorts__(panel|ai|captions|manual|sub)` returns only MakeShorts.tsx:201/225/241/243/256 and app/_scratch_axe_probe.mjs:17. app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:326-329 (`.app__main > * { flex: 1; min-height: 0 }`) pins `.make-shorts` to the exact stage height, so its taller content has nowhere to go. Every sibling view owns a scroll container: app/renderer/src/views/settings.css:12-17 (`.settings__panel { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto; padding: var(--space-6) }`), shell.css:1017-1020 (`.workspace__body`), shell.css:815-819 (`.library__list`), app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:180-189 (`.shorts__grid`), and app/renderer/src/features/export/export.css:171-178 whose comment states the rationale verbatim: "overflow-y:auto so the primary CTA is never clipped at short window heights." MEASURED (Chromium laying out the repo's real stylesheets over a replica of MakeShorts.tsx:199-291 with a video selected; ShortMaker modelled conservatively at 260px, CaptionCustomizer collapsed): at 1280x820 — the app's default window (app/main/main.ts:1038-1039) and the exact viewport the visual specs pin (app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37-38) — `.make-shorts` clientHeight=774 / scrollHeight=1349 => overflowPx=575; document scrollHeight=1395 vs clientHeight=820 (the DOCUMENT becomes the scroller); `#probe-primary-cta` ("Make shorts from ranges") bottom = 575px below the fold; scrolled to the bottom: `.app__bar` top = -575 (barOnScreen=false, so QUALITY/AI-routing/Jobs are gone) and blankBelowRail=575px of empty canvas under the 245px-tall visible rail. At the app's MINIMUM window (app/main/main.ts:1040-1041 minWidth 940 / minHeight 600 => ~924x561 content): stage=714x515, overflowPx=919, CTA 919px below the fold. Both runs are internally consistent (overflowPx == CTA-below-fold px, since the CTA is the last element). Horizontal axis is clean at both widths (scrollWidth == clientWidth). The e2e journey cannot catch this: app/e2e/golden-journey.spec.ts:229 reaches that CTA with Playwright `.click()`, which auto-scrolls.
- why: This is the novice front door (MakeShorts.tsx:1-14) and the two things that finish the job — "Make shorts from ranges" and the Output Tray that appears after an export (MakeShorts.tsx:269-276) — are the LAST elements in the stack, so they are exactly what falls off. The user can still reach them by scrolling, but because the shell's grid (shell.css:70-79) was designed for a non-scrolling document, scrolling drags the header off-screen: the Jobs pill (App.tsx:544-560), the only view onto running renders, becomes unreachable while you operate the bottom of the surface, and the 200px nav rail leaves a 575px empty column. At the minimum permitted window height the surface is ~2.7x the stage.
- fix: Mirror Settings exactly, in app/renderer/src/views/makeShorts.css: add `.make-shorts__panel { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; }` (`.make-shorts` already receives `flex:1; min-height:0` from shell.css:326-329), and add `.make-shorts > .tabbar { flex: none; }` so the sub-tab strip can never be squeezed — the same guard workspace.css:36-39 already applies to its own tab strip. Bonus: giving the panel a definite height also makes the nested gallery's own scroller work, since `.shorts { height: 100% }` (shorts.css:10-16) currently resolves against an auto-height parent, defeating `.shorts__grid { overflow: auto }` (shorts.css:188).
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding stands as written. Two non-substantive refreshes only, for a parent acting on current main (dcb59e4b): (a) line citations in MakeShorts.tsx have shifted since PR #308 — `.make-shorts__panel` is now :207 (was :201), the OutputTray block :279-286 (was :269-276), the return body :198-305 (was :199-291); the CSS/main.ts/e2e citations are all unchanged and exact. (b) The exact figures 575px @1280x820 and 919px @minimum are replica-derived (real repo stylesheets over a reconstructed DOM with ShortMaker modelled at 260px), which the finding already disclosed inline; the EXISTENCE of the overflow and its order of magnitude are independently certain from the CSS alone (`.caption-designer__phone` = a definite 480px vs a 774px stage; content ≥923px even counting ShortMaker and CaptionCustomizer as zero), while the precise px will move with those two components' real rendered heights. The settling measurement is a `fullPage` screenshot or a `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` probe on the real built Electron app with a video selected — which no current spec performs, since all baselines are viewport-only 1280x820 and capture the empty state.

Taller content therefore overflows visibly and the DOCUMENT becomes the scroller, dragging the non-sticky `.app__bar` (`position:relative`, shell.css:92) and its Jobs button (App.tsx:544-560) off-screen. On Make Shorts with a video selected the overflow is large enough to push the last-in-stack primary CTA "Make shorts from ranges" (ManualInterval.tsx:123) and the conditional Output Tray (MakeShorts.tsx:279-286) below the fold: `.caption-designer__phone` alone is 480px tall (270px at aspect-ratio 9/16, captionDesigner.css:11-13) and is rendered unconditionally (MakeShorts.tsx:257-263).
