Correctly-scoped fix: put the scroller in the shell, not in one view -- add `overflow: auto` to `.app__main` (shell.css:316-324), which fixes all 5 views at once and stops the app bar from scrolling. If a per-view scroller is preferred, `.make-shorts__panel { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto }` fixes Make Shorts only and leaves Caption/Export/Deliver/Director still broken; in that case `.make-shorts` must also give the panel `flex:1` (the panel currently cannot shrink because its default `min-height:auto` floors it at content height). Either way add `.make-shorts > .tabbar { flex: none }` (mirroring workspace.css:36-39) and note that giving the panel a definite height is also what makes the nested `.shorts__grid { overflow:auto }` (shorts.css:188) work, since `.shorts { height:100% }` (shorts.css:10-16) currently resolves against an auto-height parent.
- ⚠ scope correction: Make front door has no scroll container: on the default 1280x820 window with a video selected, roughly 575px (>=919px at the 940x600 minimum) of the surface — including the primary CTA "Make shorts from ranges" and the whole Output Tray — sits below the fold, and because nothing in the Make chain owns `overflow`, the DOCUMENT becomes the scroller, so the app bar (QUALITY, AI-routing, Jobs pill) scrolls off the top and the 200px nav rail is left above an empty column. Content remains reachable by scrolling and an already-open Jobs drawer stays put (`.jobqueue{position:fixed}`, jobqueue.css:84-85), so this is a layout/chrome-integrity defect rather than a functional block — medium-to-high, not critical. `.make-shorts__panel` is at MakeShorts.tsx:207 and has zero CSS rules; the overflow floor is set by the unconditional 480px `.caption-designer__phone` (captionDesigner.css:9-18, CaptionDesigner.tsx:83 — the surface renders CaptionDesigner, not CaptionCustomizer). The committed visual baselines are all viewport-only 1280x820 captures of the no-video-selected empty state, so the suite cannot detect it.

## `.sm-discarded` opacity 0.55 drops every text run in a still-interactive candidate card below AA (1.96:1 worst case)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1375-1377 `.sm-discarded { opacity: 0.55; }` plus app/renderer/src/features/shortmaker.css:80-82 `.shortmaker .sm-candidate.sm-discarded { filter: saturate(0.35); }`. Confirmed live in Chrome against the real sheets: the `.sm-candidate.sm-discarded` node computes `opacity: "0.55", filter: "saturate(0.35)", backgroundColor: "rgb(27, 33, 46)"`. The card composites over the app canvas (`--surface-bg` #121620 — neither `.sm-review`, `.shortmaker`, `.app__main` nor `.app` sets a background). Ratios, computed twice by independent methods that agreed (hand arithmetic + a WCAG script whose sanity controls returned black-on-white 21.00 and text-primary-on-canvas 16.58): `.sm-why` (CandidateList.tsx:117, 13px) 3.33:1; `.sm-score`/`.sm-status` (:100,:113, 11px) 3.28:1; `.sm-times` (:150-153, 11px mono) 3.12:1; `.sm-status-discarded` chip 1.96:1; the Approve button's `--accent-ink`-on-`--accent` label 3.44:1; `.sm-row-actions` buttons 3.28:1. Only `.sm-hook` (:116) clears at 5.37:1. The WCAG 1.4.3 "inactive user interface component" exemption does NOT apply: app/renderer/src/features/CandidateList.tsx:79-87 renders the card as a clickable `<li onClick={() => onSelect(item.id)}>` with no `disabled` and no `aria-disabled`, and :191-207 renders Approve and Reinstate as fully enabled buttons inside it — a discarded card is a live, re-selectable control, not a disabled one.
- why: Discard is a one-keystroke action in the documented J/K/Space/A/X review loop, so discarded cards accumulate on screen during normal use — and the user must still read them to decide what to reinstate. The single element carrying the card's most important information, the `sm-status-discarded` chip that says which state it is in, is the least readable thing on the card at 1.96:1 — below even the 3:1 large-text floor, and the fade is the only other signal that the card is out of the running. The e2e a11y gate cannot see any of this: app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts:62-68 scans `.app__main` right after `openTopTab(win, 'Make Shorts')`, and that route (app/renderer/src/App.tsx:366-368 → `setRoute({name:'makeshorts'})` with no videoId) leaves `selectedId === ''` (views/MakeShorts.tsx:76), so MakeShorts renders the empty state at :289-300 and ShortMaker never mounts during the scan.
- fix: Stop dimming the whole subtree. Either (a) move the recede signal off text — keep `filter: saturate(0.35)` and add a tonal background step plus a muted left rail (the `.sm-candidate::before` rail at shell.css:1350-1360 is already the state channel), leaving opacity at 1; or (b) if the fade must stay, raise it to `opacity: 0.75` — I measured that as the threshold at which the weakest run, `.sm-times` (`--text-faint`), reaches 4.67:1 (0.70 → 4.24:1 still fails). Either way the status chip needs its own fix (see the `--status-error-text` finding): swapping the token alone only lifts the chip from 1.96:1 to 2.49:1 inside a 0.55 card, so both changes are required. Pin the result with a conformance test that composites `--text-faint` at the discarded opacity over `--surface-bg` and asserts >= 4.5:1.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — if anything an underclaim. Numeric corrections only, mostly conservative: the .sm-status-discarded chip is 1.71:1, not 1.96:1 (the finding appears not to apply saturate(0.35) to it); the Approve label is 3.30:1, not 3.44:1; and non-discarded .sm-status is 3.63:1, not 3.28:1, because .sm-status carries its own background: var(--surface-deep) (shell.css:1414) which .sm-status-discarded then replaces with the 10%-alpha error wash (shell.css:1423-1426). Add the missed worst case: a SELECTED discarded card (.sm-selected → --surface-hover, shell.css:1366-1369) drops .sm-times to 2.75:1, .sm-score to 2.89:1 and .sm-why to 2.94:1 — and J/K navigation lands there because moveSelection (shortMakerLogic.ts:483-492) does not skip by status. One rhetorical softening: the chip's information is partially REDUNDANT — the fade plus saturate carry the state and the accessible name still reads "discarded" (CandidateList.tsx:113) — so it is not "the single element carrying the card's most important information"; the load-bearing failures are .sm-why (the reason) and .sm-times (the timecodes), which carry non-redundant reinstatement-decision data. The strongest framing of the fix is that it closes a known hole in the project's own regime: extend the existing tokens.conformance.test.ts:198-215 --text-faint AA guard to composite the .sm-discarded opacity, exactly as :268-303 already composites the error wash.

## Reframe phase uses the solid `--status-error` as TEXT (4.23:1 / 3.75:1) although the repo already defines an AA-safe `--status-error-text` for exactly this
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:73-80 documents the defect class in the repo's own words — "the solid #e5484d is only ~4.1:1 on --surface-raised … so red STRINGS … read from this lighter tone instead" — and defines `--status-error-text: #ff6b6b`. Swapping to `--status-error-text` measures 5.96:1 (error on canvas wash) and 5.29:1 (chip on card wash). The existing guard does not cover these files: app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:648-649 defines the `RED_TEXT_LEAK` regex but :651-658 scopes `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` to only library-cards.css, library-shell.css, readinessBadge.css, library-provenance.css and keep-copy-control.css — shell.css, shortmaker.css, makeShorts.css, manualInterval.css and panels.css are absent, so the test at :688-698 passes while the leak is live.
- why: The `.sm-error` string is the only place the reframe phase tells the user why moment-picking failed, and it is a `role="alert"` — the highest-urgency text on the surface — sitting at 4.23:1. The fix already exists as a token and was already applied across the whole Library family; the reframe phase was simply missed, and the conformance guard's allow-list shape means it will stay missed and can silently spread to any new `.sm-*` rule. Compounding: the discarded chip inherits the 0.55 card opacity, which takes it to 1.96:1 (see the `.sm-discarded` finding).
- fix: Swap `color: var(--status-error)` → `color: var(--status-error-text)` at shell.css:1222, shell.css:1425 and shell.css:446 (leave `--status-error` on the 3px `border-left` at shell.css:1220 and on every fill/dot — that is what the token split is for). Also check panels.css:409 (`.health-verdict.bad`) and manualInterval.css:27 / makeShorts.css:75 while in there — those two currently render on the bare canvas at 4.62:1 and pass, but only by 0.12, so any surface change breaks them. Then close the guard: rename `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` and extend it to every sheet under app/renderer/src (or invert it to a glob-all-CSS scan with an explicit allow-list of fill-only usages), so the invariant holds repo-wide rather than for five files.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (was: high). ONE reframe-phase rule renders red TEXT below the repo's own 4.5:1 AA floor in a state a user actually sees: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222 (`.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error { color: var(--status-error) }`) puts the ShortMaker role="alert" string (features/ShortMaker.tsx:913-915, 13px body) at 4.23:1 on the --status-error-soft wash over --surface-bg, against a repo whose own guard at app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 states "a component MUST route alert text through --status-error-text, not --status-error". Swapping that one declaration to var(--status-error-text) measures 5.96:1 and clears AA. The other two cited surfaces do NOT survive: (a) shell.css:1425 (`.sm-status-discarded`) never renders at the claimed 3.75:1 — CandidateList.tsx:80/:113 guarantee the chip is always inside `.sm-discarded`, which applies opacity:0.55 (shell.css:1376) and filter:saturate(0.35) (features/shortmaker.css:80-82), giving a real ~1.72:1 that the proposed token swap only lifts to ~2.26:1, so that surface needs the recession redesigned, not the token changed; (b) shell.css:446 is a transient hover on a 12px label under the user's own cursor (7.90:1 at rest -> 3.75:1 on hover, source-order win at equal (0,3,1) specificity confirmed) and it is the SHARED .library__remove-btn:hover rule, i.e. not reframe-phase-specific. Correspondingly, the guard gap is repo-wide, not a reframe-phase omission: ~30 bare `color: var(--status-error)` text sites across ~20 sheets sit outside LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS (tokens.conformance.test.ts:651-658), so the honest framing is "the AA-safe token was adopted in 5 Library sheets and nowhere else", and the durable fix is to invert the guard to a glob-all-CSS scan with an explicit allow-list of fill-only usages.
- ⚠ scope correction: CONFIRMED with the surface re-labelled and the breadth widened (the original was too NARROW, not too wide):

"The Make Shorts phase -- not a 'Reframe phase', which does not exist in the app's IA (App.tsx:3-14) -- uses the solid `--status-error` as TEXT where the repo's own AA-safe `--status-error-text` was designed for exactly this (tokens.css:71-80). Three shell.css rules leak: shell.css:1222 (`.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error`) puts the `role=\"alert\"` ShortMaker error string (ShortMaker.tsx:913-922, 13px via tokens.css:145) at 4.23:1 on the soft wash over the canvas, below the 4.5:1 AA floor; shell.css:1425 (`.sm-status-discarded`) and shell.css:446 (`.sm-row-decide button[aria-label=\"Discard\"]:hover`) both measure 3.75:1 on the wash over `.sm-candidate`'s `--surface-raised` (shell.css:1342), degrading to 2.93:1 once the card is selected or hovered (shell.css:1362-1369) -- which the Discard hover always triggers. The Discard rule beats `.shortmaker button:hover` (shell.css:371) on source order at equal (0,3,1) specificity, so hover actively lowers contrast from `--text-primary`. Swapping to `--status-error-text` yields 5.96:1 / 5.29:1.

Two corrections of scope: (a) the cited selectors are NOT ShortMaker-only -- shell.css:1215-1217 also governs `.feature-panel .error` (Assets.tsx:190,195; ModelsSystemPanel.tsx:681) and `.timeline__error` across Edit/Settings/Timeline, and shell.css:443 also governs `.library__remove-btn:hover`, so the one-line fix at :446 changes a LIBRARY control that the guard's own allow-list implies is already done; (b) the leak is repo-wide, not a three-rule miss -- rescanning with the guard's own RED_TEXT_LEAK regex finds 33 bare `color: var(--status-error)` declarations across 20 renderer sheets (shell.css x4, providersKeys.css x4, jobqueue.css x3, setupStatus.css x3, managed-store-meter.css x2, lineage.css x2, shorts.css x2, and 13 more), and ZERO fall inside tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658 -- the 5 allow-listed library sheets are already clean, which is precisely why the guard runs green (verified: 4 passed).

The fix is therefore not 3 edits + 3 spot-checks but a repo-wide token swap plus inverting the guard from a 5-file allow-list to a glob-all-CSS scan with an explicit allow-list of fill/border-only usages -- otherwise every one of the other 17 unguarded sheets stays broken and any new rule can regress silently."

## Panel never reflects the already-persisted transcript — the accent primary action invites a redundant multi-minute GPU re-run
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Transcribe.tsx:40-63 has NO effect that loads an existing transcript — the only `useEffect` is the per-job progress relay (:55-63); state starts at `phase='idle'`, `transcript=null` (:42,:47). The Workspace mounts it with the videoId ONLY: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:298 `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} />`. The data is right there and unused: Workspace already holds the opened project (Workspace.tsx:141, :166-167) whose type carries `transcript?: Transcript` (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/api.ts:76) and whose video carries `hasTranscript: boolean` (api.ts:64). The sidecar really does persist and return it: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:438 (`project.data["transcript"] = transcript`) and :441 (`set_has_transcript(video_id, True)`), returned by C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:322 (`return {"project": project.data}`). The hydration pattern exists one line away — Workspace.tsx:271 passes `initialTrack={tracks[0] ?? null}` to Subtitles. And the user has already been TOLD the transcript exists: the Library card shows a "Transcript" badge from the same flag (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:108).
- why: On an already-transcribed video the panel presents the cold empty state, and the loudest thing on it is an accent-styled "Start transcription" (the accent rule fires on `.feature-panel .actions > button:first-child:not(.secondary)`, shell.css:411). So the app's most prominent affordance on this surface is the one action the user must NOT take: a GPU-serialized re-transcription (media_ops.py:390-394 tags the job `gpu=True` precisely because it is multi-GB/multi-minute) that overwrites the persisted transcript. It also directly contradicts the Library badge the user just clicked through, which is a trust break, not just friction.
- fix: Thread the project data down: `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} initialTranscript={project?.transcript ?? null} />` at Workspace.tsx:298, matching the Subtitles pattern at :271. Seed `transcript`/`phase` from it so the done-state (summary + collapsed segments) renders immediately, and demote the primary action to a secondary "Re-transcribe" when a transcript is present — reserving the accent CTA for the state where it is genuinely the next step.
- ⚠ scope correction: Transcribe panel does not hydrate from the already-persisted transcript, and its accent CTA triggers an unguarded re-run that can silently discard diarization labels — MEDIUM, lens = destructive-action-confirmation (not progressive-disclosure exposure).

The panel mounts at phase='idle' / transcript=null (Transcribe.tsx:42,:47) and neither of its two effects (:55-63 progress relay, :147 wait-teardown) loads project data; Workspace.tsx:298 passes only videoId although the opened project (Workspace.tsx:141,:166-167) carries transcript?: Transcript (api.ts:76) and the sibling Subtitles mount hydrates one line away (Workspace.tsx:271). So on an already-transcribed video the accent-styled primary action (shell.css:411 over Transcribe.tsx:176-178) reads "Start transcription", and transcribe.start honors it: media_ops.py:385-388 calls _transcribe_and_persist with no cached-transcript guard — unlike the Make-Shorts path, which skips a wasteful re-run via _is_empty_transcript (shortmaker_ops.py:115) — re-running a gpu=True job (media_ops.py:394) and overwriting project.data["transcript"] (media_ops.py:438).

The bite is data loss, not just time: diarize.py:343 persists speaker labels into project["transcript"], and diarize.py:334-342 explicitly guards the reverse direction against a concurrent transcribe.start clobbering it; media_ops.py:438 has no reciprocal guard, so a re-transcribe drops diarization labels with no warning.

Severity is MEDIUM, not high, because exposure is low and deliberate: opening a video lands on the Task Hub (Edit.tsx:1-11) whose cards include no Transcribe destination (taskHub.ts:42-65) and whose resumeFor never yields 'transcribe' (taskHub.ts:82-96); the Workspace defaults to Subtitles because Transcribe is "a one-time prerequisite, NOT a destination" (Workspace.tsx:92-96). Drop the "contradicts the badge the user just clicked through" trust-break claim — the panel is ~3 deliberate steps behind that badge.

Fix (superset of the original): thread `initialTranscript={project?.transcript ?? null}` at Workspace.tsx:298 matching the Subtitles pattern at :271 and seed transcript/phase so the done-state renders immediately; demote the CTA to a secondary "Re-transcribe" when a transcript is present; and — the part the original fix misses — confirm before overwriting, or add a cached-transcript guard to transcribe.start mirroring shortmaker_ops.py:115, so diarization labels cannot be silently discarded.

## A failed shorts.list renders the "No shorts yet" empty state and "0 clips" — the error is presented as a confirmed-empty gallery
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `error-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:81-90 — the catch calls only `setError(errText(err))`; `setShorts` is never touched, so `shorts` stays `[]`. app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:205/224 — the render is a flat ternary `loading ? <skeleton> : shorts.length === 0 ? <empty> : <grid>`, so with `loading===false` and `shorts.length===0` the `.shorts__empty` branch runs REGARDLESS of `error`. app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:229-232 renders "No shorts yet" + "Open a video, run the Short-maker, and export clips — they show up here." app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:166-168 header renders "0 clips". Two existing EXECUTED tests jointly corroborate: app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.test.tsx:436-438 proves the reject path ends with loading cleared + error set, and Shorts.test.tsx:449-460 proves `.shorts__empty` renders whenever `!loading && shorts.length===0`. Neither test asserts the empty state is suppressed on error. This is the exact anti-pattern the project itself forbids: docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:45 "the 'No candidates proposed' copy is reserved for a confirmed zero-result", under the V1 contract at docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:30 "no silent fallbacks — fail LOUD + clear".
- why: A user with 40 produced shorts whose sidecar is down or whose exports root is unreadable is told they have zero clips and instructed to go make some. The header count corroborates the lie ("0 clips"). The error alert above it is easy to miss next to a large, confident empty-state illustration, so the likely user action is to re-run the Short-maker rather than fix the sidecar — and re-running is exactly what will also fail.
- fix: Track load outcome as a discriminated state instead of inferring empty from `shorts.length`. Minimal change: gate the empty branch on `error === null` at app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:224 (`: error ? null : shorts.length === 0 ? <empty>`), suppress the `shorts__count` chip while `error !== null` (Shorts.tsx:166-168), and add a test asserting `.shorts__empty` is absent when `shorts.list` rejects.
- ⚠ scope correction: A failed `shorts.list` renders the "No shorts yet" empty state and a "0 clips" header count SIMULTANEOUSLY with the error alert, because the render is a flat `loading ? … : shorts.length === 0 ? …` ternary (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:205/224) that never consults `error`, and the catch at Shorts.tsx:86-88 leaves `shorts` at `[]`. The error is not silent — a `role="alert"` banner does render (Shorts.tsx:193-197) — but it is contradicted on the same screen by a confident zero-result illustration, the copy "No shorts yet" + "run the Short-maker … they show up here" (Shorts.tsx:229-232), and a corroborating "0 clips" chip (Shorts.tsx:166-168), which is the exact "failed job renders as empty success" anti-pattern the project rates HIGH at docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:35-45. Severity high stands. Note the same shape also exists at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:540/562, so the fix should be applied as a shared pattern rather than a one-view patch.
- ⚠ scope correction: NOT a scope refutation — the finding as written is accurate for its stated scenario; this is only an optional precision tightening of the headline: "A shorts.list failure while the gallery list is empty — i.e. on every fresh mount of the Make Shorts > 'Produced shorts' tab (MakeShorts.tsx:212 mounts <Shorts> conditionally, so shorts always starts []) — renders the 'No shorts yet' empty state and '0 clips', byte-identical to a genuine zero-result (executable-proven). A failure on the post-delete refresh (Shorts.tsx:154) instead leaves a STALE grid and count, which is a separate second-order defect."
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW (was: high) — Contradictory empty state alongside a visible error on the FIRST load of the Shorts gallery. When shorts.list rejects while the stored list is still empty (initial mount; a mid-session refresh failure retains the prior grid because setShorts is untouched at Shorts.tsx:85-87), the flat ternary at Shorts.tsx:224 renders .shorts__empty ("No shorts yet" + "run the Short-maker", Shorts.tsx:229-232) and the header chip renders "0 clips" (Shorts.tsx:166-168) — even though the real error is ALSO rendered in a role="alert" error-styled banner directly above it (Shorts.tsx:193-197; shorts.css:44-51), and, in the sidecar-down case, a second global "Sidecar stopped" + [Restart] banner fires (App.tsx:575; SidecarBanner.tsx:155-169). So this is NOT silent error-masking and is NOT the docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:35-45 F1 class (which is about a job {error} payload swallowed into an empty success with no error shown); the V1 fail-loud contract is met. It is a copy/consistency defect: a confirmed-zero-result empty state and a "0 clips" count should not render while error !== null. Fix remains the cheap guard at Shorts.tsx:224 plus suppressing the count chip at Shorts.tsx:166-168, with a test asserting .shorts__empty is absent when shorts.list rejects. Impact is momentary confusion in an already-flagged error state on a read-only view — no data loss, self-correcting on reload.

## Batch "Resume" on a partially-failed batch is a permanent silent no-op; the sidecar's retryErrors capability is never wired from the renderer
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `error-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:477-492 `resumable_video_ids` re-enqueues only `queued`/`running`; `error` items are included ONLY when `retry_errors=True`, which defaults False (batch.py:501). sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:896-921 documents `batch.resume({id, retryErrors?})` and reads `params.get("retryErrors", False)` — the capability exists server-side. app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:684-685 sends only `{id}`; Grep for `retryErrors|retry_errors|continueOnError` across `app/` returned **No matches found** (0 occurrences), so the renderer can never request it. Reachability: with the default `continue_on_error=True` (batch.py:389), one bad source records `error` and the run continues; 1 done + N error is "all terminal, ≥1 done, ≥1 non-done" → `derive_status` returns `partial` (batch.py:180), and app/renderer/src/features/repurposeLogic.ts:173 includes `partial` in INCOMPLETE → the Resume row renders (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:268-284). Clicking it: BatchQueue.tsx:231-246 → `resume_batch` finds nothing pending and returns `{jobId: None, ...}` (batch.py:519-521) → `jobIdOf` (BatchQueue.tsx:33-40) returns `''` because `typeof null !== 'string'` → `refreshBatch` + `reload` change nothing, and no error or note is set. `remainingCount` (repurposeLogic.ts:190 = total-done-skipped) keeps reporting "N of M left" forever. Untested: app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:160 only mocks `{jobId: 'job-2'}`; the null-jobId path has no test.
- why: This is the ONLY recovery affordance the batch surface offers. A user whose 30-source batch had 6 sources fail sees "6 of 30 left" and a Resume button; clicking it produces no job, no progress, no error, no message, and the counter never moves. There is no other way to retry those sources — the failed items are permanently terminal from the UI's point of view. A false affordance on a failure-recovery path is worse than no affordance: it consumes the user's trust and their time before they conclude the app is broken.
- fix: Two parts. (1) Wire the parameter: add `retryErrors?: boolean` to `client.batch.resume` (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:684-685) and offer "Retry failed sources" as an explicit control on rows whose status is `error` (BatchQueue.tsx:356-360) and/or alongside Resume when the batch has error items. (2) Make the no-op honest: in `resume` (BatchQueue.tsx:231-246) check the resolved `jobId` and, when it is absent, set a human note such as "Nothing left to resume — N sources failed. Retry them?" instead of silently returning. Add a test for the `{jobId: null}` response.
- ⚠ scope correction: Clicking "Resume" on a `partial` batch is a guaranteed, permanent no-op that is never disclosed as such. Proven exhaustively: across all 1-4-item status combinations, every one of the 216 that derive to `partial` (batch.py:172-198) yields zero resumable sources at the default `retry_errors=False` (batch.py:490), and 130 of them would be resumable with `retryErrors=True` — a parameter the sidecar accepts (batch.py:897, 915) but which appears zero times in `app/`, since client.ts:684-685 sends `{id}` only. `resume_batch` therefore returns `{jobId: None}` (batch.py:527-528), `jobIdOf` collapses it to `''` (BatchQueue.tsx:34-40), no job starts, no `role="alert"` or note is set (BatchQueue.tsx:231-246), and the "N of M left" copy (BatchQueue.tsx:275, remainingCount at repurposeLogic.ts:189-191) never changes. Because `batch.delete` is wired to no UI (client.ts:686), the dead row persists across every launch — and the same batch also drives the Repurpose tab badge and a launch toast claiming it "was interrupted — N of M sources left" with a Resume action (App.tsx:224-248). Correctly scoped impact: the user is NOT left with zero information — the first click renders each failed source's status token and error text (BatchQueue.tsx:341-365) and announces them to a screen reader (BatchQueue.tsx:375-398), and the work IS recoverable by re-selecting those sources and clicking Run batch (BatchQueue.tsx:287-323), which creates a new batch. What is broken is narrower: a recovery control that can never do anything, on three surfaces, with a permanently wrong "N left" counter, no way to dismiss the record, and zero test or e2e coverage of the `{jobId: null}` path (BatchQueue.test.tsx:160, :374-388; no matches for resume in app/e2e). Root cause is a design self-contradiction, not a wiring omission: DESIGN.md:270 makes error-retry "(optionally `error`)" and DESIGN.md:152 specifies the wire as `{id}`, while DESIGN.md:196 explicitly admits `partial` to the resume-surface predicate. Severity: medium-high rather than high — real dead affordance and stale counter, but the failure reasons are visible and a retry path exists. (Related, separate: DESIGN.md:261 promises resume "re-evaluates skipped items", which batch.py:485/490 never does.)
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM/LOW — mislabeled control and misleading counter on the batch resume surface, not a silent dead end. When a batch ends `partial` with only `error` (or `skipped`/`cancelled`) items left, the "Resume" row (BatchQueue.tsx:268-284) and the launch toast (App.tsx:236-239) both present the batch as resumable and report those sources as "N of M left" (repurposeLogic.ts:190), but `resumable_video_ids` re-enqueues `error` items only when `retry_errors=True` (batch.py:477-492) and the renderer never sends it (client.ts:684-685 vs batch.py:915), so no job starts (batch.py:528) and the counter never moves. The click is NOT silent and NOT a dead end: it renders the full per-source failure breakdown with each error string (BatchQueue.tsx:341-365, verified by executing a {jobId:null} probe — rows 0 -> 3) plus an assertive screen-reader announcement per failure (repurposeLogic.ts:132-136), and the user can immediately re-run exactly those sources via the Sources fieldset + "Run batch" on the same screen (BatchQueue.tsx:287-323) — equivalent work, since a resumed source re-runs its template path from step one regardless (batch.py:513-517, docstring — UNVERIFIED by execution). Fix is cosmetic-plus-plumbing, not a rescue: thread `retryErrors` through client.batch.resume and label the control honestly ("Retry 6 failed sources" vs "Resume"), stop counting errored items in remainingCount, and correct the toast's "was interrupted" copy for the error case. Settling experiment for the residual: mock `{jobId:null}` in BatchQueue.test.tsx and assert the rendered copy matches what the click actually does.
- ⚠ scope correction: Batch "Resume" cannot recover a partially-failed batch: the sidecar's `retryErrors` capability (batch.py:897, :915) is never wired from the renderer (client.ts:684-685 sends only `{id}`; 0 occurrences of retryErrors in app/), so `error` and `skipped` items are never re-enqueued (batch.py:474, :490) and `resume_batch` returns `{jobId: None}` (batch.py:527-528) for every `partial` batch — while the Resume affordance still renders in the queue row (BatchQueue.tsx:268-284), the launch toast (App.tsx:236-239) and the tab badge (App.tsx:232), with a "N of M left" counter that can never move (repurposeLogic.ts:189-191). Two scope corrections to the original write-up: (a) the click is NOT literally silent on the FIRST press — `refreshBatch` populates `batch` from null, so the per-source rows appear with each failed source's error text (BatchQueue.tsx:341-365, :356-360) and `announceTransitions` (:375-398) emits an assertive "<title> — failed: <error>" (repurposeLogic.ts:132-136); it is a fully silent no-op from the second press onward, and at no point does the UI disclose that the resume itself accomplished nothing; (b) the failed work is not permanently unrecoverable — the user can re-select those sources and press "Run batch" (BatchQueue.tsx:287-299, :316-323) to create a FRESH batch; what is impossible is retrying them within the existing batch record, which therefore stays `partial` and keeps advertising an inert Resume forever. Severity: medium-high (false failure-recovery affordance on a live default-landing surface) rather than high-on-unrecoverable-data. Settling experiment: mock `client.batch.resume` to resolve `{jobId: null, status: 'partial'}` in BatchQueue.test.tsx and assert the row/counter/error region are unchanged — no test covers that response today (BatchQueue.test.tsx:160).

## Re-exporting a reframed video silently overwrites the previously produced shorts (no confirm, no warning, no undo)
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Output path is deterministic per (source video, rank): `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:1270` `base_stem = Path(source_path).stem or "clip"`; `:1281` `final_stem = _hook_card.rank_ordered_stem(base_stem, clip_rank, max_rank)`; `:1126` `final_path = str(out_dir / f"{final_stem or stem}.mp4")`. `sidecar/media_studio/features/hook_card.py:175-177` -> `f"{order_prefix(rank, max_rank)}-{base}"` (i.e. `01-talk.mp4`, `02-talk.mp4`, ...). The dir is stable per video, not per run: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:41` `out_dir_for=lambda vid: str(self.exports_dir / f"shorts-{vid}")`, and `shortmaker.py:1243-1244` only does `dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` — no existence check. The final encode passes `-y`: `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:157,160` ("``-y`` to overwrite the output", `argv = [ffmpeg_path(settings), "-hide_banner", "-nostdin", "-y", "-i", in_path]`) via `shortmaker.py:451-459 _lazy_export`. The sidecar `.json` is truncated too (`sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:158-162`, `open(json_path, "w")`). Renderer side has no guard: `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:968-974` ("Export approved", `disabled={busy || approved.length === 0}` only) and `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerControls.tsx:325-333` ("Make {controls.count} shorts") fire straight into `runExport`/`runBatch` (`ShortMaker.tsx:617-693`, `:701-773`) with no confirm. A repo-wide grep for `overwrit|will replace|already exported` across `app/renderer/src` returns zero user-facing copy.
- why: The Reframe-to-vertical journey (`app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:42-47` -> Workspace @ shortmaker) ends in an export whose output filenames depend only on the source filename and the candidate rank. Running "Find clips" again with a different prompt, a different reframe engine, or different caption settings and clicking "Export approved" a second time rewrites `01-<source>.mp4` .. `NN-<source>.mp4` in place. Rendered clips the user may already have reviewed, thumbnailed, or scheduled are destroyed with no confirmation and no recoverable copy. The gallery listing them is rendered directly below the export button (`ShortMaker.tsx:1000-1007`), so the app visibly knows the files exist and still says nothing. Corroborating symptom: the AI-picked poster `<clip>.mp4.thumb.jpg` is NOT rewritten (it is only removed by `shorts.delete`, `shorts.py:450`), while `thumbnailPath` is resolved purely by file existence (`shorts.py:320`) — so after an overwrite the card shows the OLD clip's chosen frame over the NEW clip's content.
- fix: Either (a) make the output path collision-free — append a short export-run token/timestamp to `final_stem` in `shortmaker.py:1281` and keep a `latest` view in the gallery, or (b) have `run_export` pre-scan `dest` for the target `final_path` set and return a typed `wouldOverwrite: string[]` that the renderer surfaces as an explicit confirm ("Re-exporting will replace N existing shorts") before `shortmaker.export` is dispatched. Minimum acceptable: add the overwrite warning to the "Export approved" / "Make N shorts" affordances when `videoShorts.length > 0`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Severity should be MEDIUM, not high, and the `-y` flag should not be named as the defect.

Correctly-scoped claim: "Re-exporting a video's shorts silently overwrites the previously produced clips in place — no confirm, no warning, no trash/undo — and the gallery then shows the OLD clip's poster frame over the NEW clip's content."

Two scope corrections to the original:

(1) SEVERITY -> MEDIUM. What is destroyed is a DERIVED artifact in a known exports folder (`exports_dir / shorts-<videoId>`); the source video, the project manifest, and the library are untouched, and the loss is bounded to a re-encodable output rather than user-authored source content. "High" in this repo's own vocabulary is reserved for unrecoverable/irreplaceable loss or a security impact. It stays a genuine MEDIUM (not noise) because (a) the loss IS unrecoverable in practice — LLM clip selection plus manual nudges cannot be reproduced (`ShortMaker.tsx:733`), and (b) the stale-thumbnail bug makes the app misreport the post-overwrite state.

(2) `-y` IS NOT THE DEFECT. `ffmpeg.py:160` passes `-y` alongside `-nostdin`; without `-y` a non-interactive subprocess would hang or fail on ffmpeg's overwrite prompt, so `-y` is correct engineering. The defect is the deterministic `final_path` (`shortmaker.py:1126`) combined with the absent existence pre-scan (`shortmaker.py:1243-1244`) and the absent renderer confirm. Proposed fix (b) — a `run_export` pre-scan returning typed `wouldOverwrite: string[]` for the renderer to confirm — correctly targets this; fix (a) would also work.

(3) COLLISION SCOPE, stated precisely (the original implied it is always total): collision is TOTAL on the "Make N shorts" batch path, because `runBatch` auto-approves `topByVirality(candidates, clean.count)` so ranks are 1..N on every run. On the manual "Export approved" path it is PARTIAL — only overlapping `rank` values collide (`hook_card.py:132-144` `resolve_rank`), which in practice always includes rank 1 since users approve the best clip. Filenames diverge only if `max_rank` crosses 99 and widens the zero-pad to 3 (`hook_card.py:171`), which is unreachable at realistic clip counts.

Minimum acceptable fix is unchanged and should additionally cover the stale poster: delete or regenerate `<clip>.mp4.thumb.jpg` when a clip is rewritten, since `shorts.py:429-430` will otherwise never refresh it (asserted by `sidecar/tests/test_shorts.py:427-434`).

## "Change…" the data folder is a one-click, unconfirmed action that orphans every model, env and exported short and forces a full re-provision on restart
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The control is rendered on this surface inside the Short-maker (the Reframe-to-vertical destination): `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerBrandKit.tsx:116-142` — a bare `Change…` button, hint "Where models, environments, exports and caches are stored." and, only after the fact, "Restart to apply the new data folder." The handler `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:364-385` picks a directory and immediately calls `setDataFolder(chosen)` — no confirm, no consequence disclosure. Main process states plainly that nothing is moved: `app/main/dataFolderIpc.ts:14` "It does NOT move any files — a restart applies the new root via resolveDataRoot." And the marker tier is unconditional, so an EMPTY new root still wins: `app/main/dataRoot.ts:126-131` (`markerContent` returned before any provisioned-content check) and `app/main/dataRootPlan.ts:70-71` "explicit env / marker override … wins UNCONDITIONALLY, returned as a `use` plan". The only migration that exists is the packaged legacy `<exeDir>/data` -> `%APPDATA%` rescue (`dataRootPlan.ts:15-19,72-74`), which does not apply to a user-chosen folder.
- why: After Change… + restart the app resolves to the new, empty root: the library is empty, every produced short from the Reframe phase is gone from the UI, and first-run provisioning re-downloads the whole model/env set (the manifest tiers at `sidecar/media_studio/assets/manifest.py:67-77` include GPU/env stacks). Nothing in the UI says the existing data stays behind, that it will not be migrated, or that a multi-GB re-download follows. The user's only recovery is to remember and re-enter the old path — which the UI never shows again once the field is overwritten (`ShortMaker.tsx:380` optimistically replaces the displayed path).
- fix: Gate `changeDataFolder` behind an explicit confirm that states the three consequences: existing models/exports are NOT moved, the library will appear empty until you point back, and the app will re-download models on next launch. Show the OLD path alongside the new one until the restart happens so the change is trivially reversible, and offer a "Move my data" path (or link to the manual steps) rather than only a marker rewrite.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (was: high) — The data-folder change discloses no consequences, so a user who expects their data to move instead gets an apparently-empty app after restart. Reached deliberately (Brand kit is collapsed by default, `ShortMaker.tsx:190`; the OS directory picker at `dataFolderIpc.ts:41-47,88-91` is the only gate), the flow persists the marker with no consequence confirm (`ShortMaker.tsx:364-385`) and no UI string anywhere states that files are not moved (verified: zero user-facing matches in `*.tsx|*.ts|*.css`), even though `dataFolderIpc.ts:14` records that internally. Because the marker tier is returned before any provisioned-content check (`dataRoot.ts:126-131`; the anti-brick at `:138-146` guards only the exe-data tier) and wins unconditionally (`dataRootPlan.ts:70-71`), an EMPTY chosen root does win on restart: exports under `<root>/exports` (`_services.py:74`) disappear from the library, and the absent first-run marker re-triggers provisioning (`firstRunGate.ts:225-237`). SCOPE, corrected: that re-provision is CORE-ONLY — the pip env plus ~4.3 MB of weights (`firstRunGate.ts:6-12,50`; `manifest.py:455,502`) — not the multi-GB model set; the `gpu` tier is Full-profile-only and outside the marker (`manifest.py:83-88`); HF-cached models survive in `~/.cache/huggingface/hub` (`manager.py:416-426`, no `HF_HOME` set anywhere); and pip's out-of-root wheel cache is used (no `--no-cache-dir`, `bootstrap.py:285-311`). Nothing is deleted or moved and the change is fully reversible by re-pointing — a designed property (`docs/plans/ux-qol/DESIGN.md:177`) — so this is a recoverable misconfiguration, not data loss. FIX (right-sized): put the three consequences in the UI BEFORE the write — existing data is not moved, the library will look empty until you point back, and core provisioning re-runs — and keep the OLD path visible until restart. Note the Settings → Storage surface (`Settings.tsx:164-178`) already retains the old paths incidentally, because `PathsPanel`'s `describe()` rows are fetched once on `[rpc]` and never refetched (`PathsPanel.tsx:101-117,151-175`); the ShortMaker duplicate (`ShortMaker.tsx:380`) is the surface that loses it, so making that breadcrumb intentional on both is the cheap half of the fix.
- ⚠ scope correction: The data-folder "Change…" control is a one-click, unconfirmed action that re-points the app's single data root without moving anything, orphaning the existing library, models, envs and exported shorts and forcing a re-provision on restart. Confirmed at both call sites — ShortMakerBrandKit.tsx:118-124 + ShortMaker.tsx:373-381, and the same unguarded flow at PathsPanel.tsx:151-175,190-198. Nothing is moved (dataFolderIpc.ts:14, :121-132) and the marker tier wins unconditionally with no content-aware guard (dataRoot.ts:126-131; the A4 probe at :143-145 covers only tier 3 and planDataRoot never supplies it, dataRootPlan.ts:88-95), while writing a marker also disables the sole legacy migration (dataRootPlan.ts:97-101). On restart the new empty root has no .first-run-complete.json, so classifyFirstRun returns 'first-ever' (firstRunGate.ts:233-236) and bootstrap rebuilds the multi-GB pip env at <newroot>/envs/sidecar (bootstrap.py:483,494,846) plus re-fetches the two CORE face/ASD weights — NOT the entire model set: the GGUFs, TTS voices and the Full-only `gpu` tier return only via a re-picked profile or at point-of-use (firstRunGate.ts:50; bootstrap.py:550-572,608; manifest.py:75,83-88). No bytes are deleted, but the old path is erased from the UI (ShortMaker.tsx:380, asserted by ShortMaker.test.tsx:2459) and both markers are overwritten (dataFolderIpc.ts:129-130), so recovery depends on the user remembering the previous root. The fix must gate BOTH call sites and keep the old path visible until the restart.
- ⚠ scope correction: Changing the data folder is an UNCONFIRMED action — no consequence disclosure, no migration — that strands the existing models, envs, library and exported shorts at the old path and re-triggers first-run provisioning on the next launch. It is exposed on TWO surfaces, both unguarded: the canonical Settings > Storage panel (`app/renderer/src/components/PathsPanel.tsx:151-175,190-198`, mounted at `app/renderer/src/features/Settings.tsx:174`) and a duplicate inside the Short-maker's collapsed Brand-kit section (`app/renderer/src/features/ShortMakerBrandKit.tsx:116-142` + `app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:364-385`); the Short-maker copy renders in every Short-maker phase (`ShortMaker.tsx:901-911`), so this is not specific to the Reframe phase. Mechanism: `setDataFolder` writes only marker files and moves nothing (`app/main/dataFolderIpc.ts:14,121-132`); the marker tier returns before any provisioned-content check (`app/main/dataRoot.ts:126-131` vs the tier-3 guard at 143-145) and "wins UNCONDITIONALLY" (`app/main/dataRootPlan.ts:70-71`), a precedence explicitly test-locked at `app/main/dataRoot.test.ts:301-307`, so an EMPTY chosen root beats a fully provisioned one. The legacy `<exeDir>/data` rescue cannot help, being gated on `!overrideChosen` (`dataRootPlan.ts:101-103`). Exports cannot be redirected clear of this: `Services.exports_dir = base / "exports"` (`sidecar/media_studio/_services.py:74`) with no `outputDir` override (`sidecar/media_studio/features/brandkit.py:19`). Re-provisioning re-fires because `.first-run-complete.json` lives inside the root (`app/main/dataRoot.ts:80`) and drives `needsFirstRunSetup` (`app/main/firstRunGate.ts`) — but the download volume is PROFILE-dependent, not unconditionally multi-GB: `minimum` pulls nothing and the `gpu` tier is Full-only (`sidecar/media_studio/assets/manifest.py:83-88`). Recovery is not uniformly impossible: pre-restart, Settings > Storage still renders the OLD dataDir/exportsDir/libraryPath with working "Open folder" buttons because `rpc.describe()` is never refetched after the change (`PathsPanel.tsx:101-117,165,209-229`), and the picker opens at the still-live old root (`dataFolderIpc.ts:141-142`); post-restart, and on the Short-maker surface at any time, the old path is genuinely unrecoverable from the UI. A fix must gate BOTH handlers (`changeDataFolder` and `PathsPanel.handleChangeRoot`) and should keep the old path visible until the restart.

## Reframe/pipeline stage intermediates are written into the gallery-scanned export dir, never deleted, and are listed as produced shorts
- surface `Reframe phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Every stage writes a full intermediate render into the SAME per-video export dir: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:947` (`{stem}.cut.mp4`), `:977` (`.trimmed.mp4`), `:995` (`.stabilized.mp4`), `:1012` (`.defilled.mp4`), `:1032` (`.reframed.mp4`), `:1048` (`.zoomed.mp4`), `:1090` (`.captioned.mp4`), `:1114` (`.branded.mp4`), `:1133` (`.encoded.mp4`) — all `out_dir / ...` where `out_dir = exports_dir/shorts-<videoId>` (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:41`). No cleanup exists: grep for `cleanup|unlink|remove\(` in `shortmaker.py` returns only doc text (`:912` "Each stage writes its own intermediate so a failure is localized."), and a `media_studio`-wide grep for cleanup/rmtree finds only engine-internal temp dirs (`reframe_claudeshorts.py:994`, `saliency.py:372`) and the multispeaker failure path (`reframe_multispeaker.py:1575`) — none touch the export dir. The gallery scan is unfiltered: `sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:379` `for mp4 in sorted(directory.glob("*.mp4")):`. Defaults make almost every stage run: `app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:298-305` sets `removeFillers/autoZoom/silenceTrim/stabilize` all `true`.
- why: A single 5-clip reframe export leaves up to ~7 extra full-length 1080x1920 h264 renders per clip (~35 stray files) permanently on disk, and `shorts.list` reports every one of them, so `ProducedShorts` (`app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx:276-289`) shows ~40 cards where 5 are the real deliverables. The disk cost is never disclosed and never reclaimed by the app. Worse for this lens: each stray card carries the same Delete / Pick-best-frame / Re-export actions (`ProducedShorts.tsx:223-231`), so the user's destructive Delete clicks land on artifacts they cannot distinguish from their outputs, and a genuine deliverable is easy to delete by mistake among the near-identically named `<source>-1.reframed.mp4` / `01-<source>.mp4` pairs. (Exact GB figure is source-dependent — UNVERIFIED as a number; the file count and the absence of cleanup are CONFIRMED.)
- fix: Write stage intermediates to a per-export temp dir (`tempfile.mkdtemp` or `out_dir/.work-<runid>`) and remove it in a `finally` in `_export_one`/`run_export`, mirroring what `reframe_claudeshorts.py:994` already does for its own temp tree. Belt-and-braces: filter `shorts.py:379` to files that have a sibling `<clip>.json` (the export-metadata marker written at `shortmaker.py:1147`) so non-deliverables can never reach the gallery or its Delete button.
- ⚠ scope correction: Pipeline stage intermediates are written into the gallery-scanned per-video export dir, are never cleaned up, and are listed by shorts.list as if they were produced shorts. Neither consumer filters (Shorts.tsx:82-85, useShortsGallery.ts:57-58), so ProducedShorts.tsx:276-289 renders a card per intermediate, each with Delete/Re-export/Pick-best-frame (:204-231). The repo already documents this in app/e2e/golden-journey.spec.ts:31-35 ("INTERMEDIATES ... live in the same dir but carry NO .json, so they surface with videoId=''"), but that filter exists only in the e2e test, never in product code. CORRECTED SCOPE on volume: under the cited all-on defaults (shortMakerLogic.ts:301-305) the stages that actually emit a file are .cut, .trimmed, .stabilized, .reframed, .zoomed and .captioned = 6 intermediates per clip (5 when libvidstab is absent, since stabilize passes through — shortmaker.py:123-124), NOT 7. `.defilled.mp4` never runs under those defaults at all, because silenceTrim:true disables removeFillers at the mutual-exclusion gate shortmaker.py:1008; `.branded` needs brandLogoPath (:1113) and `.encoded` needs an audioTrackId (:1127), both default-off. - ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high), and it is a resource-leak + gallery-pollution/dead-action defect, not a destructive-actions defect.

Short-maker stage intermediates are written into the same per-video export dir the gallery scans (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:947,977,995,1012,1032,1048,1090,1114,1133, all out_dir/...; out_dir = exports_dir/shorts-<videoId> per handlers/shortmaker_ops.py:41 and handlers/composition.py:358-359), are never deleted (no unlink/rmtree/mkdtemp anywhere in shortmaker.py), and are listed as produced shorts because the scan globs *.mp4 unfiltered (features/shorts.py:379) while only the final clip gets a .json (shortmaker.py:1147) and neither gallery filters (useShortsGallery.ts:57-58, views/Shorts.tsx:82-85). The repo's own keystone e2e documents and works around this at app/e2e/golden-journey.spec.ts:31-35.

With DEFAULT_CONTROLS (app/renderer/src/features/shortMakerLogic.ts:301-305) that is SIX intermediates per clip -- cut, trimmed, stabilized, reframed, zoomed, captioned -- not seven-to-nine: .defilled.mp4 can never coexist with .trimmed.mp4 (shortmaker.py:1008), .branded.mp4 requires brandLogoPath (:1113), .encoded.mp4 requires an audioTrackId (:1127), and stabilize/trim_silence may pass through without writing (:265-295). The four pre-reframe intermediates are at SOURCE resolution, not 1080x1920 (the vertical canvas begins at :1032/:1039), so a 4K source costs MORE than the finding estimated. Exact GB is source-dependent -- UNVERIFIED as a number; the file count and the total absence of cleanup are CONFIRMED.

User impact is real but is NOT accidental deletion of a deliverable: (1) undisclosed, never-reclaimed disk growth of roughly 6x the deliverable bytes per export run, compounding across runs, with no size disclosure or cleanup surface anywhere in the sidecar; (2) the gallery shows ~7x the cards, and every stray card's "Pick best frame" is a guaranteed error because ProducedShorts.tsx:144-149 forwards videoId '' into vision_ops.py:269 _require_str(params, "videoId"), while shorts.reexport returns videoId '' (shorts.py:477). Strays are visually distinct (raw path as title, "--:--" duration, no virality badge, no template chip, no poster) and the default virality sort places them last (shortsGallery.ts:38-39, ProducedShorts.tsx:252), so mis-deleting a real deliverable is NOT an established risk and deleting a stray removes only garbage (shorts.py:442-455).

The proposed fix is still correct and is the right one for the corrected claim: write stage intermediates to a per-export work dir (tempfile.mkdtemp or out_dir/.work-<runid>) removed in a finally in _export_one/run_export, mirroring reframe_claudeshorts.py:994; and belt-and-braces, restrict shorts.py:379 to mp4s that have a sibling <clip>.json so a non-deliverable can never reach the gallery or its per-card actions.

## "Re-export" button exports nothing — it navigates to the Make tab; the same button is documented elsewhere as "Edit in Studio"
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Label + accessible name at app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:60-64 (`Re-export` / `aria-label={`Re-export ${label}`}`). What it actually does: app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:117-128 calls `client.shorts.reexport(path)` and forwards the result; app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:138-141 `handleReexport` = `setSelectedId(hint.videoId)` + `setActive('make')`. The RPC starts no work: app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:272-273 "the reopen-in-short-maker hint (no job)"; sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:459-465 "No job is started here." The same control is named differently in the modal that reuses this gallery: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:29-30 documents it as `"Edit in Studio" — reopen the short for further editing` and wires `onEdit` into `onReexport` at :57-61, so "Edit in Studio" never reaches the DOM.
- why: The label names an operation (export a file) that never happens, and hides the operation that does (jump to Make with this video pre-selected, losing the gallery scroll position and any sort choice). Both directions cost the user: someone who wants a fresh render clicks it and gets bounced with no new file; someone looking for "edit this short again" avoids the only button that leads there because "Re-export" sounds like a long re-render they don't want. Because it sits in a per-clip row (ShortClipActions is rendered once per card), the mistake repeats per clip.
- fix: Rename the visible label and aria-label to what happens — "Edit again" (or "Open in Make"), aria-label `Edit ${label} again`. Keep the prop name `onReexport` if the wire contract must not churn, but stop surfacing it as copy. If a true one-click re-render is wanted, that is a separate button that actually calls `shortmaker.export`.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — the finding is accurate and under-scoped. The correctly-scoped version widens it and tightens the surface: The per-clip "Re-export" control (app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:61-62, visible text + `aria-label="Re-export ${label}"`, no tooltip) performs no export on ANY of its three wire paths — Shorts.tsx:117-128, useShortsGallery.ts:83-93 (used by ShortMaker.tsx:1005), and Library.tsx:613 -> App.tsx:380-383 — because `shorts.reexport` is a hint-only RPC (client.ts:272; sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:464,477). All three merely navigate to Make Shorts with the source video pre-selected (MakeShorts.tsx:138-141; App.tsx:373-375), unmounting the gallery and discarding its sort state (MakeShorts.tsx:212; Shorts.tsx:68). It therefore appears on the Make Shorts "Produced shorts" gallery tab AND the "Make" tab's inline produced-shorts list AND the Library per-video gallery modal — but NOT on the Batch tab (Repurpose at MakeShorts.tsx:213 is passed no `onReexport`). The same control is documented as "Edit in Studio" at ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:29 and wired at :57-61, a string that exists only in comments repo-wide and never renders. Severity: medium-high.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity (polish, not high): in the produced-shorts card row, "Re-export" (app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:60-64) sits beside "Open folder" and "Delete", which are both immediate file operations, so it reads as an immediate re-render. It is instead the first step of a two-step flow — Shorts.tsx:117-128 fires shorts.reexport and MakeShorts.tsx:138-141 switches to the Make tab with the SOURCE video pre-selected — and the Shorts view emits no status note acknowledging the hand-off. A trailing ellipsis ("Re-export...") or "Open in Make" would set the right expectation at zero behavioural risk. Do NOT rename it to "Edit again": MakeShorts.tsx:139 drops the `candidate` skeleton returned by shorts.py:471-476 and App.tsx:380-383 routes on short.videoId only, so the short itself is never reopened for editing and that label would be more misleading than the current one. The separate "Edit in Studio" wording (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:29) is a JSDoc comment on the onEdit prop, never rendered — an internal naming inconsistency worth tidying for maintainers, with no user-visible consequence.
- ⚠ scope correction: The per-clip action row labels a pure-navigation control "Re-export" (visible text and accessible name `Re-export ${label}`, app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:61-62), and its own JSDoc claims it "re-runs the export for this clip" (:20-24). No wired call site exports anything: shorts.reexport returns a hint and starts no job (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:272-273; sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:464), and the handler only does setSelectedId(hint.videoId) + setActive('make'), discarding hint.candidate (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:138-141). It renders on three surfaces, none of them the batch tab: (a) Make Shorts -> "Produced shorts" gallery (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:330) — navigates to the Make tab, losing the gallery's local sort mode (Shorts.tsx:68 unmounted at MakeShorts.tsx:212); (b) Library card "N shorts" modal (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:98 via Library.tsx:607-613 -> App.tsx:380-383) — routes away from Library with no RPC, and the modal's own prop contract calls this affordance "Edit in Studio" (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:29), a name that never reaches the DOM; (c) the inline exported-clips list inside ShortMaker on the Make tab (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:1000-1007) — here both state writes are no-ops because the list is already scoped to the selected video (useShortsGallery.ts:57 + shorts.py:477), making it an observably dead click (static inference; UNVERIFIED at runtime). Severity: medium as a copy defect on (a) and (b); the dead click on (c) is the higher-severity part and warrants its own fix. Fix: rename the visible label and aria-label to the action ("Edit again" / "Open in Make", aria-label `Edit ${label} again`), correct the ShortClipActions JSDoc, and either make (c) do something observable or omit the button there.

## Every batch is hard-coded to the name "Batch run", so the Incomplete-batches resume list is unidentifiable
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `copy-microcopy` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:188 — `client.batch.create('Batch run', templateId, selected)`: the name is a literal, never derived from the template or the selected sources. The resume row renders only that name plus counts: app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:273-280 `{b.name} — {remainingCount(b.counts)} of {b.counts.total} left`. `BatchSummary` carries `createdAt` and `templateId` (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:1118-1125) and `incompleteBatches` deliberately returns a newest-first LIST (app/renderer/src/features/repurposeLogic.ts:181-186), i.e. the multi-row case is the designed case — yet neither field is shown.
- why: With two unfinished batches the list renders two rows of identical text (e.g. "Batch run — 4 of 10 left" twice) and the only control is an equally bare "Resume". The user has no way to tell which run is which, so picking wrong re-dispatches the wrong sources — real GPU time and, on cloud sources, real spend. The disambiguating data is already in hand and simply not written into the copy.
- fix: Name the batch from its inputs at creation, e.g. `` `${templateName} · ${selected.length} source(s)` `` (the template name is already loaded in `templates` state), and add the date to the row: `{b.name} — started {formatDate(b.createdAt)} · {remainingCount} of {total} left`.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW / copy-polish: `client.batch.create` is called with the literal `'Batch run'` at app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:188 (its only call site), so every batch carries one generic label and the Incomplete-batches rows (BatchQueue.tsx:274-276) are distinguished only by their `{remaining} of {total} left` counts plus the newest-first ordering (app/renderer/src/features/repurposeLogic.ts:182-185). Consequence, correctly scoped: when two incomplete batches happen to have the SAME remaining and SAME total, their rows read identically and the user must fall back on recency to pick. There is NO cost or data risk - resume re-enqueues only non-terminal sources (sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:474-492), is a strict no-op for an all-terminal `partial` batch (batch.py:527-528), and threads no budget ack so an egressing source is refused rather than billed (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/ai_ops.py:266-275). Fix is naming-only polish: derive the name at create time from the already-loaded template plus the selected source count (templates state, BatchQueue.tsx:50,97). Adding `createdAt` to the row would require a new date formatter - the renderer currently formats no dates anywhere.
- ⚠ scope correction: Every UI-created batch is hard-coded to the name "Batch run" (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:188, the sole production `client.batch.create` call site; the sidecar persists it verbatim at sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:786-792 and no rename affordance exists), and the Incomplete-batches resume row shows only that constant name plus remaining/total counts with a bare "Resume" button (BatchQueue.tsx:273-280). Since `incompleteBatches` returns a newest-first LIST (app/renderer/src/features/repurposeLogic.ts:181-186) and `partial` batches persist there (batch.py:180,197 + repurposeLogic.ts:173), multiple rows are reachable and mutually indistinguishable — identical text when counts coincide, and otherwise still not identifying WHICH run. Picking wrong re-dispatches the wrong batch's pending sources through the full template path from step one (batch.py:507-517), wasting real GPU time; the additional cloud-spend risk is UNVERIFIED because batch.resume threads no consent flags (batch.py:896-921 vs :844-845) and the downstream provider gate was not traced. The disambiguating `createdAt`/`templateId` are already on `BatchSummary` (app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/schemas.ts:1118-1125) and simply unused in the copy.
- ⚠ scope correction: Every batch created by the shipped UI is hard-coded to the name "Batch run" (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:188 — the only production caller of client.batch.create, and batch.py:787 is the only persistence path), and the Incomplete-batches list renders nothing but that name plus counts (BatchQueue.tsx:273-280), so rows in a deliberately multi-row list (repurposeLogic.ts:181-186; badge at App.tsx:231-232; 'partial' batches accumulate per repurposeLogic.ts:173 + batch.py:196-197) are not distinguishable by identity — only, incidentally, by differing counts and by the undisclosed newest-first sort order. The same bare name is the sole identifier in the resume toast (App.tsx:236-239) and the job label (batch.py:547), so there is no cross-reference. Corrected harm: a mis-picked Resume does NOT redo finished work (batch.py:477-492, 509-514) — it dispatches the wrong batch's PENDING sources, costing unplanned local GPU time; cloud spend occurs only with confirmCloudBudget OFF, because resume passes no consent (batch.py:910-917) and ai_ops.py:256-269 refuses un-acked egress under the default-ON gate, which instead marks those sources 'error' and drops them from the default resume set (retry_errors=False, batch.py:490).

## Every Edit-panel error message is sub-AA red text (4.23:1) despite the repo shipping an AA-safe red-text token for exactly this
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222` — `.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error { color: var(--status-error); background: var(--status-error-soft); }`, and the same pair at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:567` for `.library__error, .workspace__error`.

Measured (WCAG 2.x relative-luminance, recomputed twice): `--status-error` #e5484d on `--status-error-soft` rgba(229,72,77,0.10) composited over the panel's actual plane. `.workspace__body` (`shell.css:1017-1021`) sets no background, and neither does `.workspace` (`:503-510`), `.app__main` (`:316-324`) or `.app` (`:70-79`), so the plane is `body`'s `--surface-bg` #121620 (`shell.css:9-19`) → wash composite **#271b24**.
  • shipped  #e5484d on #271b24 = **4.23:1**  (AA body needs 4.5:1)
  • `--status-error-text` #ff6b6b on #271b24 = **5.96:1**  (PASS)
Text is 13px/400 (`--type-body-size`, inherited — the rule sets no font-size), so the 4.5:1 floor applies, not 3:1.

Live consumers in the Edit phase (`<p className="error" role="alert">`): `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:195`, `Subtitles.tsx:355`, `Tracks.tsx:285`, `Convert.tsx:347`, `Dub.tsx:399`, `Diarize.tsx:167`, `Refine.tsx:270`, `Recipes.tsx:217` and `:222`, `NleExport.tsx:122`, `SemanticSearch.tsx:216`, `Assets.tsx:190` and `:195`; plus `Timeline.tsx:383` (`.timeline__error`) and `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:347` (`.workspace__error`).

The repo already knows: `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304` asserts the base red FAILS on that wash and its comment states "a component MUST route alert text through --status-error-text, not --status-error". The enforcement regex `RED_TEXT_LEAK` (`tokens.conformance.test.ts:649`) is applied only to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (`:652-658`) — five Library sheets. `components/shell.css` is not in that list, so the Edit-phase leaks are unguarded and the suite stays green.
- why: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (AA) failure on the highest-stakes text class in the app — the string that tells a user why a transcribe/translate/convert/dub job failed. Low-vision users reading a red-on-red-wash alert at 4.23:1 are the exact population most likely to be already struggling. It is the only class of Edit-phase text I measured below AA; every other text/surface pair in the phase clears it (text-faint on surface-active is the next-thinnest at 4.71:1).
- fix: Swap `color: var(--status-error)` → `color: var(--status-error-text)` at `shell.css:1222` and `shell.css:567` (leave the `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` rails alone — the solid fill red is correct there and measures 4.23:1 vs the wash, above the 3:1 non-text floor). Then close the guard hole: add `components/shell.css`, `features/panels.css` and `features/timeline.css` to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (`tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658`), or better, glob every `renderer/src/**/*.css` so the next sheet cannot re-leak.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not an overclaim — if anything it undercounts. Tightened version:

1) COUNT: `components/shell.css` carries FOUR bare `color: var(--status-error)` text leaks, not two. Beyond `:1222` and `:567`, line `:446` (the destructive `.library__remove-btn:hover` / `.sm-row-decide button[aria-label="Discard"]:hover` text) and line `:1425` (`.sm-status-discarded`, on `--status-error-soft` at `:1424`) are the identical failing pair — and both are Edit-phase (ShortMaker). Therefore the finding's sub-claim "It is the only class of Edit-phase text I measured below AA" is FALSE; at least three classes are.

2) "EVERY" is imprecise at one margin: `.workspace__player-error` (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:330`, `role="alert"`) has NO rule in any `app/**/*.css`, so it renders inherited `--text-primary` and is NOT sub-AA red. The finding's own SURFACE line ("all 13 Workspace feature panels + the Workspace shell error banner") already excludes it, so this is headline-vs-surface drift, not a wrong diagnosis. (Separately: an unstyled `role="alert"` is its own minor defect.)

3) 4.23:1 is the BEST case, correctly computed for the actual plane. The repo's own test comment (`tokens.conformance.test.ts:298`) records ~3.75:1 for the same pair over `--surface-raised`; I confirm 3.753:1. Since no panel root sets a background, 4.23:1 is the operative number for the 13 panels — the claim is conservative either way.

4) THE PROPOSED FIX IS INCOMPLETE AS WRITTEN: adding `components/shell.css` to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` while changing only `:1222` and `:567` leaves `:446` and `:1425` matching `RED_TEXT_LEAK`, so the suite goes RED. All four must be migrated to `--status-error-text` (the `border-left` rails and `background` fills stay — those are `border-left:`/`background:`, which the regex's `[^-]color:` correctly ignores). The "glob every renderer/src/**/*.css" variant would additionally trip ~15 further sheets (e.g. `components/jobqueue.css:150`, `components/captionPreferences.css:83`, `views/caption.css:51`, `features/lineage.css:113`, `components/setupStatus.css:62`) — real leaks, but that widens the change well beyond the Edit phase and should be staged.

Severity HIGH stands, at its low end: the miss is marginal (4.23 vs 4.5) and colour is not the sole signal (`role="alert"` + text), but it is a shipped violation of the project's OWN pinned 4.5:1 DoD floor, with the corrective token already defined and a conformance test asserting the base red fails.
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect claim needs no narrowing — it is confirmed as stated (if anything it undercounts: SystemHealth.tsx:142 is a 14th `className="error"` consumer beyond the 13 listed). Only the PROPOSED FIX needs re-scoping:

"Swap `color: var(--status-error)` -> `var(--status-error-text)` at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222 and :567, leaving the `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` rails alone (measured 4.62:1 vs #121620 and 4.23:1 vs the wash — both clear the 3:1 non-text floor).

Then close the guard hole — but note the hole is far larger than two sheets. A repo-wide run of the existing RED_TEXT_LEAK regex (tokens.conformance.test.ts:649) over `app/renderer/src/**/*.css` finds 33 bare `color: var(--status-error)` leaks across 20 sheets, not 2. Do NOT add `features/timeline.css` — it has ZERO leaks (`.timeline__error` is styled in shell.css, so it is already covered by adding shell.css). `features/panels.css` does have one real leak (`.health-verdict.bad`, panels.css:409). Other notable leakers: components/jobqueue.css (3), features/providersKeys.css (4), components/setupStatus.css (3), components/managed-store-meter.css (2), features/lineage.css (2), views/shorts.css (2).

Globbing every renderer sheet into the guard is the right end state, but it is a materially bigger change than 'add three sheets' implies and requires per-sheet triage: contrast depends on each leak's own compositing plane, so some of the 33 may already clear AA on a darker plane and others may need the fill red retained for a non-text role."
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): Edit-phase error text renders at 4.23:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor the repo's own DoD pins, because `shell.css:1222` and `shell.css:567` route alert text through `--status-error` instead of the AA-safe `--status-error-text` that the repo created for exactly this purpose. The defect is real and violates the project's own stated contract, and the guard hole is real: the `RED_TEXT_LEAK` check (tokens.conformance.test.ts:649) is applied only to five Library sheets (:652-658), so `components/shell.css` is unchecked — executably confirmed at 4 leaks in shell.css and 1 in features/panels.css. Two scope corrections to the original finding: (a) it UNDERSTATES reach — roughly 20 renderer sheets leak the same token app-wide (views/shorts.css:49, views/caption.css:51, components/jobqueue.css:150, features/export/export.css:470, components/setupStatus.css:62, features/lineage.css:113, among others), not just the Edit phase; (b) the 4.23:1 figure is plane-specific — over the `--surface-raised` wash it is 3.75:1, so the conclusion holds on every elevation plane but the single number should not be quoted as universal. Severity is medium rather than high because impact on a single-user local desktop video app is modest: a ~6% contrast shortfall that stays legible for typical vision, with redundant non-colour signals (3px solid red rail at :1220/:565, tinted background wash, and `role="alert"` so the string is announced), and no regulatory exposure. Proposed fix stands as written and is sound on both planes (#ff6b6b measures 5.97:1 over the bg wash and 5.29:1 over the raised wash), and globbing `renderer/src/**/*.css` into the guard is the right closure given the ~20-sheet true scope.

## Delete button's hover label renders at 2.94:1 — the destructive action becomes least readable exactly when targeted
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:382-385 sets `.shorts__actions .shorts__delete:hover { background: var(--status-error-soft); color: var(--status-error); }`. Class is live: `className="shorts__delete"` at app/renderer/src/components/ShortClipActions.tsx:77, rendered per card from app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:330. Hovering the button necessarily hovers its ancestor `<li class="shorts__card">`, which swaps to `background: var(--surface-hover)` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:204-208). Measured stack: --surface-hover #2c3448 = (44,52,72); --status-error-soft rgba(229,72,77,0.10) composited over it = (62,54,72); --status-error #e5484d on that = **2.94:1**. Text is 11px / weight 600 (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:365-366) → normal-size, AA floor 4.5:1. Specificity verified: (0,3,0) for `.shorts__actions .shorts__delete:hover` beats (0,2,1) for `.shorts__actions button:hover` (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:373), so both the red color AND the red-soft background win. On a non-hovered card the same pair still measures only 3.75:1.
- why: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum, AA) failure at 65% of the required ratio — the worst measured on this surface. The affected control is the irreversible Delete action (Shorts.tsx:144-160 removes the exported file). The label degrades from a passing 6.09:1 at rest to 2.94:1 precisely at the moment the pointer is on it and the user is confirming intent, so the one word that distinguishes destructive from benign is hardest to read at the decision point. Not reachable by the existing axe gate: hover states are never rendered during an axe scan.
- fix: Swap the text token: `color: var(--status-error-text)` at app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:384. That token exists for exactly this purpose (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:75-80) and measures 4.14:1 on the same stack — still short of 4.5:1 because of the compounded hover tint, so also pin the button's own background rather than relying on a 10% wash, e.g. `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--status-error) 18%, var(--surface-raised))` or keep `--surface-active` as the fill and let only the text carry red (`--status-error-text` on --surface-active = 3.79:1, still short → prefer darkening the fill). Simplest compliant combination: `background: var(--surface-deep); color: var(--status-error-text)` = 7.00:1. Add shorts.css to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) so the existing `RED_TEXT_LEAK` regex guards it.
- ⚠ scope correction: Precision refinement only (the finding is CONFIRMED, not an overclaim): "The Delete button's label renders at 2.93:1 (not 2.94 — the composited backdrop is (62.5,54,72.5), not (62,54,72)) whenever the pointer is on it, a WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 AA failure at 65% of the 4.5:1 floor for 11px/600 text (app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:365-366,382-385). The sub-AA window is pointer-only and transient — keyboard users never reach it (no .shorts__delete:focus-visible rule exists) and the intent confirmation is a separate native confirm() dialog fired after the click (app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:147-150) — so the ergonomic impact is narrower than 'hardest to read at the decision point' implies, but 1.4.3 grants no hover/transient exemption and the failure is real and un-gated (axe never renders hover: app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts runAxe; zero 'hover' occurrences in app/e2e). Fix must also migrate shorts.css:49 (.shorts__error), or adding shorts.css to LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS will fail the RED_TEXT_LEAK guard on that second, always-visible instance."
- ⚠ scope correction: Downgrade to MEDIUM and re-frame as a legibility/consistency regression, not a destructive-action-safety defect.

The overclaim is the risk narrative, not the measurement.
