## Inner-tab round-trip re-fires batch.resume on the deep-linked batch, starting a duplicate parent job
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: MEASURED (repro test, now deleted): mounting `Repurpose resumeId="bZ"` behind the exact conditional at `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:203`, then clicking Batch→Make→Batch, printed `RESUME CALL COUNT AFTER TAB ROUNDTRIP = 2` (expected 1). Mechanism: the once-per-resumeId guard is a per-mount ref — `app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:250` `const resumedRef = useRef<string | null>(null)` + the effect at `app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:251-256`. `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:203` renders the batch panel conditionally (`{active === 'batch' ? <Repurpose resumeId={resumeId} /> : null}`), so every section switch UNMOUNTS Repurpose→BatchQueue and the guard is reborn null while the `resumeId` prop is unchanged. Sidecar consequence: `sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:477-492` `resumable_video_ids` treats `running` items as resumable, `sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:529-532` resets them to `queued` ON DISK, and `sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:547` starts a FRESH parent job. The renderer resume path also skips the §9.1 consent card entirely (`app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:231-246` calls `client.batch.resume` with no consent params, unlike `runBatch` at `:198-211`). No test covers this: `app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:385-388` only asserts the single-mount deep-link.
- why: A user who arrives via the interrupted-batch Resume toast lands on Batch, peeks at Make or Produced shorts, and comes back — with no click on any Resume button, a second parent job now runs the same N sources concurrently with the first. Each round-trip adds another. On a 30-source folder batch that is double (then triple) compute and double cloud egress/spend, with the cloud-budget consent gate bypassed on every one of those runs. The two jobs also race on the same durable item-status writes.
- fix: Move the fired-resume guard above the unmount boundary: hold `resumedRef` in `MakeShorts` (or key it off route state in `App.tsx`) and pass a `resumeConsumed` flag down, or have `App.tsx` clear `route.resumeId` after the first successful resume. Alternatively stop unmounting: render all three section panels and hide the inactive ones (`hidden` attr / CSS) instead of the `active === …` conditionals at `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:202-204`, which fixes this plus the sibling state-loss findings in one change.
- ⚠ scope correction: Inner-tab round-trip re-fires batch.resume on the deep-linked batch, starting an UNBOUNDED number of duplicate parent jobs on the same batch — severity HIGH.

Trigger (executable-proven, resume calls 1 -> 2): arriving via the interrupted-batch Resume toast and switching away from and back to the batch panel, with no click on any Resume button. TWO independent remount boundaries, not one: the outer section conditional at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:213 (Batch -> Make -> Batch) AND the inner tab conditional at app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:35 (Batch queue -> Templates -> Batch queue). Each unmounts BatchQueue, so the once-per-resumeId guard (a per-mount ref, app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:250, effect :251-256) is reborn null while the resumeId prop is unchanged — App.tsx:366-368/:471 never clears route.resumeId. Every round-trip adds another job; the sidecar has no idempotency guard (BatchService.resume, sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:896-921) because 'running' items are resumable (batch.py:474), are reset to queued on disk (batch.py:531-532), and a fresh parent job is started unconditionally (batch.py:547).

Actual consequences (default config, confirmCloudBudget=True per sidecar/media_studio/settings_store.py:115):
1. DOUBLE LOCAL COMPUTE for every local-only/cache-hit source. run_batch snapshots items at job start (batch.py:413, :422) and gates on the snapshot status (batch.py:429), so job 1 never sees job 2's resets — the overlap is genuine and concurrent.
2. EGRESSING SOURCES ARE STRANDED, NOT DOUBLE-BILLED. The resume path threads no confirmBudget (batch.py:536-545 -> :418-420 -> :376-379), so ai_ops.py:266-275 raises; per-source isolation (batch.py:456-457) records the item terminal 'error'; and because retry_errors defaults False (batch.py:501, :915) resumable_video_ids (batch.py:490) will NOT re-enqueue it — a later legitimate Resume silently skips that source permanently. Double cloud spend occurs ONLY if the user has already disabled confirmCloudBudget, in which case no consent gate is being bypassed.
3. NONDETERMINISTIC DURABLE STATE: both jobs call store.update_item on the same batch_id; last write wins.
4. THE FIRST JOB BECOMES UNCANCELLABLE: batch.py:920 overwrites self._parent_jobs[batch_id], so batch.cancel/batch.status can no longer reach the orphaned run.

Fix: clear route.resumeId in App.tsx after the first successful resume (the only renderer point above BOTH boundaries — hoisting the guard into MakeShorts does not fix the Repurpose.tsx:35 path), and add a sidecar idempotency guard in BatchService.resume refusing a resume while a live parent job exists for that batch_id (which also closes Resume-button double-clicks). Separately, resume bypassing the §9.1 consent computation (BatchQueue.tsx:237 vs runBatch's :198-211) is a real independent gap, but its effect is refusal-and-strand, not unconsented egress.
- ⚠ scope correction: Inner-tab round-trip re-fires `batch.resume` on the deep-linked batch, starting a second parent job for the same batch. MEASURED (repro, deleted): mounting the real `MakeShorts resumeId="bZ"` and clicking Batch->Make->Batch yields 2 `client.batch.resume('bZ')` calls, and Batch->Produced shorts->Batch yields 3 — one per round-trip, plus the same on Repurpose's inner queue/templates/presets tabs (`Repurpose.tsx:35`). Cause: the once-per-resumeId guard is a per-mount ref (`BatchQueue.tsx:250-256`) while `MakeShorts.tsx:213` unmounts `Repurpose` on every section switch and `App.tsx:366-368/471` never clears `route.resumeId`. Sidecar effect: `batch.py:474/490/531-532` resets even the currently-`running` source to `queued` ON DISK and `:547` starts a fresh parent job with no single-flight guard, and `:920` overwrites `_parent_jobs[batch_id]` so `batch.cancel` can no longer reach the first, still-running parent. SEVERITY: medium, not high. The harm is a stalled or churned batch plus a Cancel that no longer cancels — NOT doubled cloud spend: the resume path passes no consent, so `_enforce_cloud_budget_ack` (`ai_ops.py:266-275`) fail-CLOSES against the default-ON `confirmCloudBudget` (`settings_store.py:115`) and an egressing source ERRORS rather than egressing, on the first resume as much as the duplicates. And because `JobRegistry` caps at `max_workers=2` (`jobs.py:226-227/241/619`) while a batch parent holds its slot busy-waiting on its sub-job (`recipes.py:347-383`), the duplicate contends for the pool instead of doubling throughput — pool-starvation stall, not 2x-then-3x compute (UNVERIFIED which occurs; settling experiment = a pytest driving two `batch.resume` calls against a real `JobRegistry(max_workers=2)`). No test covers a remount (`BatchQueue.test.tsx:385-388` is single-mount only).
- ⚠ scope correction: Inner-tab round-trip re-fires batch.resume on the deep-linked batch, starting a duplicate parent job (CONFIRMED, live at dcb59e4b). The once-per-resumeId guard is a per-mount ref (`app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:250-256`) sitting BELOW an unmount boundary: `app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:213` and, independently, `app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:35` both render their panel via an `active === …` conditional, so any section OR inner-tab switch unmounts BatchQueue while the `resumeId` prop stays unchanged (never cleared — `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:366-367`, `:471`). Measured on the real component tree: 1 resume call on mount, 2 after one round-trip, 3 after two — with zero clicks on any Resume button. Sidecar-side each call resets not-yet-done sources (including an in-flight `running` one) to `queued` on disk and starts a fresh parent job with no already-running guard (`sidecar/media_studio/features/batch.py:474`, `:531-532`, `:547`, handler `:896-921`, which also overwrites `_parent_jobs[batch_id]` and orphans the first job for cancel/status).

DAMAGE, correctly scoped: for LOCAL (non-egressing) sources this is genuine duplicate concurrent compute plus a durable item-status write race between the two parent jobs (`batch.py:448`/`:457`/`:464` rewriting the same batch file, and `:531-532` flipping a source the other job is actively running back to `queued`). It is NOT un-consented cloud egress: the resume path threads no consent token, and `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/ai_ops.py:256-275` is fail-closed, so with `confirmCloudBudget` ON (the default, `BatchQueue.tsx:63`) an egressing source on ANY resume — first or duplicate — is REFUSED and recorded `error` (`batch.py:456-457`). Cloud spend doubles only where the user has already disabled the gate. Two separable defects therefore exist: (a) the remount re-fire above, and (b) a pre-existing one where resume never threads §9.1 consent at all, so resuming a cloud batch errors out its egressing sources instead of offering the consent card. Settling experiment for the untested half: run two concurrent `batch.resume` calls against a live sidecar on a multi-source local batch and assert one parent job and no interleaved item-status writes.

## A keyboard-focused caption clip and a keyboard-focused active style swatch render with NO focus indicator at all (WCAG 2.4.7 AA)
- surface `Caption phase` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Real-Chromium computed-style probe (@playwright/test chromium, actual tokens.css + component CSS, Tab-driven so `:focus-visible` matches):
```
#clipSel UNFOCUSED         boxShadow = rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px   outlineStyle=none
#clipSel KEYBOARD-FOCUSED  boxShadow = rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px   outlineStyle=none  focusVisible=true
#swActive UNFOCUSED        boxShadow = rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px   outlineStyle=none
#swActive KEYBOARD-FOCUSED boxShadow = rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px   outlineStyle=none  focusVisible=true
(control) #clipPlain KEYBOARD-FOCUSED boxShadow = rgb(18,22,32) 0 0 0 2px, rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 4px
```
Byte-identical focused vs unfocused. Cause is a cascade tie: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/caption/captionClipLane.css:56-59 sets `outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` at specificity (0,2,0), and captionClipLane.css:62-67 `.caption-clip.is-selected` re-sets `box-shadow: var(--focus-glow)` at the SAME (0,2,0) but LATER in source order, so it wins while `outline: none` still applies. Identical shape at captionGallery.css:110-113 vs captionGallery.css:116-119. Tokens: tokens.css:206 (`--focus-ring`) / tokens.css:212 (`--focus-glow`).
- why: This is not a weak indicator, it is the ABSENCE of one, and it fires on the surface's core keyboard loop. app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionClipLane.tsx:46-50 makes Enter/Space on a clip dispatch `selectCue` — so the very first keystroke the lane's own aria-label instructs ("Enter seeks", CaptionClipLane.tsx:68) turns the focused clip into the selected clip and erases its focus ring. The user then nudges timing with arrows (CaptionClipLane.tsx:52-61) on an element whose focus is invisible. Same in the gallery: Tab onto the currently-applied style (or press Enter to apply one, CaptionGallery.tsx:82) and the indicator vanishes. WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible is Level AA and normative under EN 301 549.
- fix: Give the focused+selected state its own composed indicator instead of letting selection overwrite focus. E.g. in captionClipLane.css add after line 67: `.caption-clip.is-selected:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }` and the mirror `.caption-gallery__swatch.is-active:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }` after captionGallery.css:119. Better still, stop using `outline: none` + `box-shadow` for focus here: a real `outline` is not subject to this collision and, unlike a box-shadow, is not clipped by the lane's `overflow: hidden` (captionClipLane.css:28 — measured: a clip at `left: 0%` has 0px of room, so its whole left-side ring is clipped today).
- ⚠ scope correction: Selection styling overwrites the focus ring via an equal-specificity cascade tie, so a keyboard-focused element that is ALSO selected shows zero visual change from its unfocused selected state — focus becomes indistinguishable from selection. MEDIUM severity (not high): an amber ring is still visible, so the user can locate focus; what is lost is the ability to tell focus from selection.

Mechanism (verified): `.caption-clip:focus-visible` (captionClipLane.css:56-59) sets `outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` at (0,2,0); `.caption-clip.is-selected` (captionClipLane.css:62-67) re-sets `box-shadow: var(--focus-glow)` at the SAME (0,2,0) but later in source order, so it wins while `outline: none` persists. Measured in real Chromium (tokens.css:206/212): focused == unfocused, `rgba(242,163,60,0.5) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(242,163,60,0.14) 0 0 0 4px`, outlineStyle=none, focusVisible=true. Mirrors at captionGallery.css:110-113 vs 116-119. Fires on the real keyboard loop (CaptionClipLane.tsx:46-50 selects on Enter/Space; CaptionGallery.tsx:82 applies on activate) in live routed views (App.tsx:487 -> Caption.tsx:85/:87 -> CaptionInspector.tsx:65). The app-wide ring at shell.css:49-52 cannot help — `:where()` makes it (0,1,0).

Conformance: definitively fails WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) — identical focused/unfocused pixels is 1:1 against its >=3:1 requirement. Failure of 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) is arguable, not established, because a visible ring remains.

Full scope — 5+ live sites, a design-system defect not a caption one: captionClipLane.css:56-67; captionGallery.css:110-119; captionDelivery.css:48-58; export.css:68-77 (worst — override is `var(--elev-2)`, a neutral shadow with no accent); shell.css:206-209 and 260-263 plus modelsSystem.css:697-699 (these beat the global (0,1,0) `:where()` rule).

Fix: compose instead of replace, e.g. `.caption-clip.is-selected:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }` and the `.caption-gallery__swatch.is-active:focus-visible` mirror — best applied as one design-system rule covering all sites above. Do NOT adopt the "switch to a real outline to escape the clipping" rationale: measured, an ancestor `overflow: hidden` (captionClipLane.css:28) clips an outline just as it clips a box-shadow (author's own app/__probe_overflow2.mjs: redOutsideTrack 0 hidden vs 105 visible). Escaping the clip needs `overflow: visible` on the track, `outline-offset`/inset rings, or lane padding — a separate, minor, cosmetic issue affecting only the left band of a `left: 0%` clip (~105 of ~1160 ring px).
- ⚠ scope correction: A keyboard-focused caption clip and a keyboard-focused active style swatch receive NO focus-specific visual change — the focused state is byte-identical to the unfocused state at the rendered-pixel level, so focus is not indicated on those two elements (WCAG 2.4.7 AA). Severity: MEDIUM, not high.

Scope, measured: the defect affects only the element where focus coincides with selection (one clip, one swatch at a time). Non-selected siblings show a correct, clearly visible ring (confirmed: #clipPlain/#swPlain differ in both computed style and rendered pixels). The element is not unstyled — it carries an amber 1px edge + 4px wash + amber background/border — but focus adds nothing to it. Partial compensation exists and lowers real-world harm: the selected clip is uniquely amber (captionClipLane.css:62-67) and arrow-nudging visibly moves the clip, so the user is degraded rather than lost. It still matters because it fires on the primary advertised path (Enter selects and retains focus, CaptionClipLane.tsx:46-50 + :68) in a component whose stated purpose is keyboard-first caption editing (CaptionClipLane.tsx:1-12), on a mounted first-class phase (views/Caption.tsx:85, App.tsx:487).

Cause (unchanged, verified): a same-specificity cascade tie — `.caption-clip:focus-visible` (0,2,0) at captionClipLane.css:56-59 vs `.caption-clip.is-selected` (0,2,0) at :62-67, the latter later in source order, so `--focus-glow` overwrites `--focus-ring` while `outline: none` still applies. Mirror at captionGallery.css:110-113 vs :116-119.

Fix: compose the two indicators instead of letting selection overwrite focus — `.caption-clip.is-selected:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }` and `.caption-gallery__swatch.is-active:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }`.

CORRECTION to the original proposed fix: switching to a real `outline` does NOT escape the lane's `overflow: hidden` (captionClipLane.css:28). An ancestor's overflow:hidden clips a descendant's outline exactly as it clips a box-shadow; outline is not exempt. The separate clipping issue — real, since --space-2 is 4px (tokens.css:167) against the ring's 4px outer spread (tokens.css:206), leaving the ring flush with the track edge and fully cut on the left for a clip at left:0% — requires track padding, overflow:visible, a negative outline-offset, or an inset box-shadow ring.
- ⚠ scope correction: The headline claim stands as written and needs no rescoping: at HEAD dcb59e4b a keyboard-focused caption clip that is also the selected clip (captionClipLane.css:56-59 vs :62-67), and a keyboard-focused active style swatch (captionGallery.css:110-113 vs :116-119), render with ZERO visual delta versus their unfocused state (byte-identical rendered PNGs; outline none, box-shadow = --focus-glow in both states) — WCAG 2.4.7 AA. Scope note worth making explicit: the defect fires only when the focused element IS the selected/active one; a focused NON-selected clip or swatch does paint --focus-ring correctly (measured), and since Enter/Space on a clip makes focus == selection (CaptionClipLane.tsx:46-50), that state is reached on the first keystroke the lane's own aria-label advertises.

ONE SUB-CLAIM MUST BE CORRECTED. Wrong as written: "a real outline ... unlike a box-shadow, is not clipped by the lane's overflow: hidden". Correctly scoped: switching to a real `outline` fixes only the CASCADE collision (an `outline` declaration does not compete with `.is-selected`'s `box-shadow`, so it survives regardless of source order) — it does NOT escape the clipping. Measured: a 3px outline on a clip at left:0 painted 1056 px inside the track and 0 px outside it under overflow:hidden, while the same detector found 105 px outside once the track was set to overflow:visible. Fixing the clipped left-side ring therefore requires track-side room — overflow:visible (plus a different way to keep clips from escaping the lane), horizontal padding on .caption-clip-lane__track, or inset ring geometry (box-shadow: inset / outline-offset negative) — and is a SEPARATE remediation from the cascade fix. The proposed composed-box-shadow one-liners (`.caption-clip.is-selected:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-glow), var(--focus-ring); }` and the gallery mirror) do correctly restore a focus delta; I verified the composed value computes to all four shadow layers.

## Caption clips are effectively invisible on the timeline lane — 1.31:1 fill / 1.74:1 border against the track, and at real cue densities they clamp to an 8px sliver with zero visible text
- surface `Caption phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/caption/captionClipLane.css:23-49 — track `background: var(--atmos-well), var(--surface-deep)` (:27); clip `background: var(--surface-overlay)` (:41), `border: 1px solid var(--edge)` (:42), `min-width: 8px` (:35), `padding: 0 var(--space-2)` = 4px each side (:36).
Measured (need 3:1, WCAG 1.4.11 non-text): clip fill #252d3d vs the well track = **1.31:1** at the gradient's light top stop, **1.42:1** at the dark bottom; clip border (9% white composited on #252d3d) vs track = **1.74:1**.
The text does not rescue it. Width comes from C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionClipLane.tsx:83 (`(cue.end-cue.start)/span`), and `span` is the FULL video window seeded at app/renderer/src/views/Caption.tsx:110-116 (0..durationSec). A 2s cue in a 10-minute video = 0.33% of the lane -> clamps to the 8px `min-width`; with 8px horizontal padding + 2px border and `box-sizing: border-box` (shell.css:21-25) the content box is 0px, so the `.caption-clip__text` span (CaptionClipLane.tsx:88) renders nothing.
Selection does not help either: captionClipLane.css:62-67 swaps the fill to `--accent-soft` = **1.28:1** vs the track — LOWER than the unselected fill; only the `--accent-edge` border reaches 3.61:1, and the unselected-vs-selected fill change is 1.02:1.
- why: The lane is the surface's only keyboard-operable cue-timing control (CaptionClipLane.tsx:43-62 — arrows move, Shift+arrow resizes). If a user cannot see where the clips are, they cannot aim at one, cannot tell how many there are, and cannot see the effect of a nudge. At any realistic video length this is not an edge case — it is every clip on the lane.
- fix: Lift the clip off the media well so the control clears 3:1: on a `--surface-deep` + atmos-well track the fill needs relative luminance >= ~0.124 (roughly #5a6274 or lighter) — `--surface-overlay`/`--surface-active` are both too dark. Cheapest robust combination: (a) give `.caption-clip` a lighter dedicated fill token, (b) raise the hairline from `--edge` to a >=3:1 outline, and (c) raise `min-width` (and/or clamp `span` to a visible window) so the 10px label actually has a content box. Also drop `--accent-soft` as the selected fill — it darkens the clip relative to unselected.
- ⚠ scope correction: Caption clips are effectively invisible on the timeline lane and carry no visible text at real cue densities. Confirmed measurements against the atmos-well track: unselected fill 1.31:1 (light top stop) / 1.42:1 (dark bottom), --edge border 1.74:1, and the selected --accent-soft fill 1.28:1 — LOWER than unselected, a 1.02:1 selected-vs-unselected delta — all far below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 bar for an interactive control (captionClipLane.css:27,41,42,62-67; tokens.css:30,33,38,65,254). Only the selected --accent-edge border (3.61:1) and the :focus-visible ring band (3.06:1, captionClipLane.css:56-59) clear 3:1, so a keyboard user can see the ONE clip they have focused, but not the clips at rest, their count, or a mouse target. Because Caption.tsx:113 seeds the window to the full 0..durationSec and editorState.ts:95-104 provides no window-narrowing action, width (CaptionClipLane.tsx:83) collapses to min-width; with padding+border = 10px against min-width 8px under universal border-box (shell.css:21-25) the clip renders a 10px sliver (not 8px — a border box cannot compress below its padding+border) with a 0px content box, so the .caption-clip__text span renders nothing. This surface loads WORD-LEVEL cues (Caption.tsx:5,48-51), so at ~0.4s per cue the content box is 0px even in a 1-minute video — every clip, at essentially every video length. Severity high stands: CaptionClipLane is live (Caption.tsx:85) and is the phase's only cue-timing control (CaptionInspector.tsx:63-77 has none).
- ⚠ scope correction: Caption clips fail WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast on the timeline lane at every video length: the clip fill is 1.31:1 (light top stop) to 1.42:1 (dark bottom) against the atmos-well track and the --edge hairline only reaches 1.74:1, so no visual indicator of this keyboard-operable <button> control (CaptionClipLane.tsx:74) clears the required 3:1 (captionClipLane.css:27,41,42). Selecting a clip does not fix it and slightly regresses the fill: --accent-soft measures 1.28:1 vs the track, LOWER than the unselected 1.31:1, with unselected-vs-selected only 1.02:1; only the --accent-edge border reaches 3.61:1, so the selected state alone is 1.4.11-conformant (captionClipLane.css:62-67).

Separately and CONDITIONALLY, the clip also loses its label whenever a cue occupies under ~1.27% of the window (8px min-width against the 628px track at the shipped 1280x820 viewport): min-width:8px is a border-box floor and border+padding total 10px, so the content box computes to 0px and the .caption-clip__text span paints nothing (captionClipLane.css:35,36,45,75; shell.css:21-25). Because span is seeded to the FULL video duration (Caption.tsx:113) and the view loads WORD-LEVEL cues (Caption.tsx:4-5, MIN_CUE_SEC=0.05 at timelineOps.ts:20), this covers any video longer than ~24s at 0.3s cues - i.e. effectively always in practice. It does NOT hold for coarse phrase-level cues on a short video (a 2s cue in a 30s short renders 41.9px wide with a 31.9px content box and visible text), so the "zero visible text" half is regime-dependent rather than universal.

Neither defect is caught by any existing gate: CaptionClipLane.test.tsx asserts behavior only, app/e2e/visual/a11y.a11y.spec.ts has no Caption-phase coverage, axe-core implements no 1.4.11 rule, and tokens.conformance.test.ts:193-195 pins this exact token pair at merely >=1.3:1 as decorative plane separation - so the measured 1.312 passes the codebase's own conformance suite.

Fix note: the required fill luminance is >=0.124 for 3:1 against the gradient's light top stop, but #5a6274 measures 2.961:1 and is marginally short - use #5f6779 or lighter.
- ⚠ scope correction: On the Caption phase's clip lane, caption clips fail WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast in their RESTING state and lose their text label entirely on sources longer than about 4 minutes.

Contrast (all recomputed from tokens): clip fill --surface-overlay #252d3d against the --atmos-well over --surface-deep track = 1.31:1 at the gradient's light top stop and 1.43:1 at the dark bottom (captionClipLane.css:27, :41; tokens.css:30, :33, :254); the --edge hairline = 1.74:1 (captionClipLane.css:42; tokens.css:38). Selecting a clip DARKENS its fill — --accent-soft composites to 1.28:1, below the 1.31:1 unselected value (captionClipLane.css:64; tokens.css:65). This is not lane-specific: the shipped mouse Timeline's cue block is --surface-active #353f56 on the same well at 1.72:1 (timeline.css:30 with timeline.css:2-3), so both timeline surfaces sit under 3:1.

Width: clip width is (cue.end-cue.start)/span (CaptionClipLane.tsx:83) where span is the FULL video duration, seeded 0..durationSec at Caption.tsx:113 with no zoom available — the EditorAction union (editorState.ts:95-104) has no window-narrowing action. At a roughly 950px lane the 8px min-width (captionClipLane.css:35) therefore fires for any cue under 0.84% of the window, i.e. a typical 2s SRT line on any source longer than about 4 minutes. Under the global box-sizing: border-box (shell.css:24) the 8px min-width is exceeded by 8px padding plus 2px border, so the clip renders 10px wide with a 0px content box and the .caption-clip__text span (CaptionClipLane.tsx:88) shows nothing. Consecutive clamped clips are then positioned closer together than their rendered 10px width, so they overlap and occlude each other in DOM order.

Consequence, correctly scoped: this is the only timing map on the surface — CaptionStage shows only the player plus the caption at the playhead (CaptionStage.tsx:48-96) and CaptionInspector shows only gallery/customizer/delivery (CaptionInspector.tsx:63-77) — on a live top-level tab (App.tsx:457, :484-487). On a long source the user gets a row of near-indistinguishable, textless, overlapping 10px blocks and cannot tell how many cues there are or which one to aim at. NOT "effectively invisible" in absolute terms: the fill sits about 11 deltaL* above the track and is perceptible on a good panel in dim light. Screen-reader users are unaffected (aria-label "Caption N: <text>" plus aria-pressed, CaptionClipLane.tsx:79-80), and the focused/selected clip is clearly marked — --focus-ring and --focus-glow put --accent-edge at about 3.08:1 over the well (tokens.css:206, :212) and the selected border reaches 3.62:1. The defect is the resting-state boundary plus the lost overview, and the load-bearing half is the width math, not the contrast.

UNVERIFIED inline: computed from tokens and CSS, not sampled from a render — no caption visual baseline or a11y case exists in app/e2e/visual. Settling experiment: a caption-win32.png baseline plus an axe non-text-contrast pass on the Caption surface.

## Caption generation (a multi-minute async job) has zero screen-reader feedback in any state — start, in-flight, or completion
- surface `Caption phase` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/views/Caption.tsx:54-67` — `generate()` sets `generating`, awaits `client.subtitles.generate(video.id)` then `client.captions.cues`, and dispatches `setCues`. The ONLY feedback is a label swap on the button itself: `app/renderer/src/components/../features/caption/CaptionInspector.tsx:50-57` (`disabled={generating}`, `{generating ? 'Generating…' : 'Generate captions'}`).
Grep for `aria-live|role="status"|role="alert"|aria-busy|aria-atomic` over `app/renderer/src/features/caption/` → **No matches found**.
Probe output (jsdom, real components):
```
live regions while idle       = 0
live regions while generating = 0
button disabled=true label="Generating…"
AFTER : focus=body live=0 btnStillInDom=false galleryMounted=true
```
The completion transition is a full unmount: `CaptionInspector.tsx:41` (`if (!transcriptReady(state))`) stops early-returning once `setCues` lands, so the whole empty block — including the button the user just activated — is removed and `CaptionGallery`/`CaptionCustomizer`/`CaptionDelivery` mount in its place. Nothing in `app/renderer/src/features/caption/` is a live region, so none of it is spoken. `app/renderer/src/views/Caption.test.tsx` has zero assertions matching `aria-live|role=|alert|status|announce|generating`.
- why: Transcription is the longest-running operation in the phase. A screen-reader user activates "Generate captions" and receives no confirmation that it started, no progress, and no completion announcement — the UI silently rebuilds itself minutes later. Because the button is `disabled` while in flight it also cannot hold focus (probe: `.focus()` on the disabled button left `document.activeElement === body`), so in Chromium the focus point is destroyed at the moment work begins and there is nothing to return to. This is WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.3 (Status Messages). Note the error path IS correct — `Caption.tsx:77-81` conditionally mounts `<p role="alert">` — so only the busy/success half is missing.
- fix: Add one polite live region owned by `CaptionWorkspace` (e.g. a visually-hidden `<p role="status">` beside `Caption.tsx:77`) driven by the same `generating`/cue-count state: "Generating captions…" on start, "Captions ready — N cues" when `setCues` resolves. Set `aria-busy` on the inspector while generating. Replace `disabled={generating}` with `aria-disabled={generating}` + a no-op click guard so the control keeps focus, or move focus deliberately to the gallery heading on completion.
- ⚠ scope correction: Caption generation gives no screen-reader announcement on the SUCCESS path, and destroys the user's focus point when it completes.

`app/renderer/src/views/Caption.tsx:54-67` awaits `client.subtitles.generate` then `client.captions.cues` and dispatches `setCues`. Because `transcriptReady` is `state.cues.length > 0` (`app/renderer/src/lib/editorState.ts:107-108`), `app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionInspector.tsx:41` stops early-returning, so the empty block — including the "Generate captions" button the user just activated (`CaptionInspector.tsx:50-57`) — unmounts and `CaptionGallery`/`CaptionCustomizer`/`CaptionDelivery` mount in its place. Nothing announces the outcome: there is no `aria-live`, `role="status"` or `aria-busy` anywhere in the caption generate path (the only `role=` in the view is the error alert at `Caption.tsx:78`). Because the button carries `disabled={generating}` (`CaptionInspector.tsx:53`), Chromium had already blurred it to `body` at click time, so on completion there is no focus point to return to. `app/renderer/src/views/Caption.test.tsx:106-146` asserts only via CSS class selectors, so no test protects any of this.

Correctly scoped severity: LOW-MEDIUM, not high. `subtitles.generate` is a direct-return RPC (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:37`; `app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:196-197` — a bare `Promise<{track}>`, no `JobHandle`), not a job and not ASR: it requires a pre-existing transcript and fails fast with `INVALID_PARAMS` otherwise (`media_ops.py:45-47`). So (a) there is no multi-minute in-flight window to narrate, and (b) the failure branch — the guaranteed outcome for a video with no transcript, i.e. exactly the state this empty gate targets — IS already announced via `Caption.tsx:77-81` `<p role="alert">`. The genuinely long ASR job is `transcribe.start` (`media_ops.py:358-360`), which the Caption phase never calls and which already announces progress politely at `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:187`.

This is a WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.3 (Status Messages) gap on the success transition only, plus a focus-management gap. Fix is cheap because the infrastructure is already mounted: push a message into the app-level polite region via `useToast()` (`app/renderer/src/components/toast/ToastHost.tsx:73`, mounted at `App.tsx:578`) on `setCues` — e.g. "Captions ready — N cues" — and/or move focus deliberately to the gallery heading. Optionally swap `disabled={generating}` for `aria-disabled={generating}` plus a no-op click guard so the control retains focus. The repo already ships this exact pattern at `app/renderer/src/features/KeepCopyControl.test.tsx:166` ("Progress is announced (role=status), and the button is disabled mid-flight"), so this is a local inconsistency, not a missing capability.
- ⚠ scope correction: Caption generation (a long-running Whisper transcription) has no screen-reader status feedback at start, in flight, or on completion: no live region in the Caption phase carries job status, and the phase never feeds the app's existing announcer. `app/renderer/src/views/Caption.tsx:54-67` runs `client.subtitles.generate` -> `client.captions.cues` -> `setCues` with the only feedback being a label swap on a simultaneously-disabled button (`app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionInspector.tsx:53,56`); on completion `CaptionInspector.tsx:41` (`transcriptReady` = `cues.length > 0`) unmounts that button entirely. The one live region in the composed subtree, `app/renderer/src/components/CaptionCustomizer.tsx:283`, cannot announce completion because it mounts only after cues land (a freshly-inserted live region does not announce its initial content) and it reports a resolved tuning value, not job status. The app-level `aria-live="polite"` announcer at `app/renderer/src/components/toast/ToastHost.tsx:73` is never used by this phase (zero `useToast` imports). This violates the project's own convention for the identical RPC — `app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:94` calls the same `subtitles.generate` and does carry `aria-live="polite"` progress at `:342-344`. WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.3 (Status Messages). Additionally UNVERIFIED-but-likely: because `disabled={generating}` is applied to the focused button, real Chromium/Blink blurs it and the focus point is lost at the moment work begins — jsdom does NOT reproduce this behavior, so it must be settled by reading `document.activeElement` across the `generating` transition in the packaged Electron app or Playwright Chromium.

## Clip-lane arrow-key retiming changes cue timing but the accessible name is byte-identical — the edit is completely silent
- surface `Caption phase` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionClipLane.tsx:43-62` — `onClipKeyDown` handles Arrow/Shift+Arrow and dispatches `setCues` with `retimeAt`/`dragEdge` results. The clip's only accessible name is `app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionClipLane.tsx:80`: ``aria-label={`Caption ${pos + 1}: ${cue.text}`}`` — it carries no timing, so it never changes when the timing does.
Probe output:
```
CLIP0 name BEFORE nudge = Caption 1: Hello
CLIP0 name AFTER  nudge = Caption 1: Hello
LIVE REGIONS in ready state = 0
```
That the underlying edit really happened is proved by the repo's own test `app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionClipLane.test.tsx:105-110` (`keyClip(0,'ArrowRight')` → `c0start` > 2, `c0end` > 3). Only the visual `left`/`width` percentages at `CaptionClipLane.tsx:82-83` reflect the change.
- why: This component exists specifically to be the keyboard-first replacement for the mouse-only Timeline (its own header comment, `CaptionClipLane.tsx:1-12`, calls that a "locked WCAG-A barrier"). It fixed operability but not perceivability: a blind user can press ArrowRight thirty times and receive no indication of the new in/out times, no confirmation any change occurred, and — because `retimeAt`/`dragEdge` silently neighbour-clamp — no way to tell a successful nudge from one that hit the clamp and did nothing. WCAG 4.1.2 / 1.3.1.
- fix: Put the timing in the name so every edit mutates the a11y tree: ``aria-label={`Caption ${pos+1}: ${cue.text}, ${fmt(cue.start)} to ${fmt(cue.end)}`}``. Add a single polite live region in the lane that reports the post-edit times (and "clamped by neighbour" when `retimeAt`/`dragEdge` returned an unchanged cue).

## CaptionBox arrow-key move/resize mutates only inline CSS — no accessible-tree change and no announcement
- surface `Caption phase` · lens `screen-reader` · verifiers 1
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/components/CaptionBox.tsx:122-128` (`onBoxKeyDown` → `onChange(moveBox(box, d.dx, d.dy))`) and `app/renderer/src/components/CaptionBox.tsx:131-139` (`onHandleKeyDown` → `resizeBox`). The rendered output is only `style={boxToCss(box)}` at `CaptionBox.tsx:158`; the accessible name at `CaptionBox.tsx:161` is a fixed instruction string.
Probe output:
```
BOX style BEFORE = left: 10%; top: 76%; width: 80%; height: 16%;
BOX style AFTER  = left: 12%; top: 76%; width: 80%; height: 16%;
BOX name = Caption region — arrow keys move; Tab to a handle then arrow keys to resize | live now = 0
```
Mounted in this phase at `app/renderer/src/features/caption/CaptionStage.tsx:58`.
- why: The box is the on-canvas caption-position editor and the code comment at `CaptionBox.tsx:119-121` explicitly frames the arrow keys as the WCAG 2.1.1 fix. Same shape as the clip lane: operable, imperceptible. A screen-reader user moving the caption region gets no position readback, cannot tell when `moveBox` clamps at the frame edge, and cannot verify the caption is out of the safe area — the exact task the control exists for.
- fix: Expose position/size in the accessible tree so each nudge is announced: add `aria-valuetext` (or regenerate `aria-label`) as e.g. "Caption region, left 12%, top 76%, width 80%, height 16%", and mirror the same string into a polite live region shared with the clip lane.
- ⚠ scope correction: Core claim stands as written; only the probe framing and the fix need tightening: "CaptionBox arrow-key move/resize changes no ARIA state, property, value, or accessible name — the only box-dependent render output is `style={boxToCss(box)}` (CaptionBox.tsx:158) while the accessible name (CaptionBox.tsx:161) is a constant instruction string — and no live region in the Caption phase is written with the new geometry (CaptionStage.tsx:58 -> editorState.ts:146; no useToast/announce in features/caption/**). The app's one always-mounted polite region (ToastHost.tsx:73, App.tsx:578) is empty and never receives the position, so a document-wide aria-live count of >=1 does not constitute an announcement. Fix by regenerating `aria-label` (or adding a shared polite live region) — NOT by adding `aria-valuetext`, which ARIA does not permit on `role=\"application\"` and which AT would ignore."

## Manual interval ranges survive a source-video switch and export against the WRONG video
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:258 renders `<ManualInterval onSubmit={...} busy={manualBusy} />` with no `key` and no videoId prop, so its `ranges` state (app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35) is preserved across a `selectedId` change (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:211). `runManualExport` then uses the CURRENT `selectedId` (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:166 and :171) with the OLD video's ranges.

CONFIRMED by executed probe (temporary vitest file, since deleted, using the REAL ManualInterval): select v1 -> add range 1:00->1:30 -> switch picker to v2. Output:
  RANGES AFTER VIDEO SWITCH = 1
  EXPORT CALLED WITH videoId = v2 candidateIds = ["1@60"]

This is the exact defect the AI path was already patched for: app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:233-249 adds a `useEffect(..., [videoId])` reset whose comment reads "the previous video's candidate list ... persist - and 'Export approved' would carve the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps." The manual path never received that fix.
- why: The user picks video A, types precise timecodes, changes their mind and picks video B, then clicks "Make shorts from ranges". The app silently renders clips from B at A's timestamps - wrong content, or out-of-range/zero-length clips if B is shorter. There is no warning and no visible cue that the range list belongs to a different video. The render cost (and cloud spend, if routing is cloud) is paid for garbage output. Existing tests cannot catch it because MakeShorts.test.tsx mocks ManualInterval away (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122).
- fix: Mirror the ShortMaker fix on the manual path: either give ManualInterval a `key={selectedId}` at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:258 (cheapest, forces a clean remount per video), or pass `videoId={selectedId}` and add the same `useEffect(() => { setRanges([]); setStartText(''); setEndText(''); setError(null); }, [videoId])` reset inside ManualInterval that ShortMaker.tsx:240-249 already implements. Add a regression test that renders the real ManualInterval, switches videos, and asserts the range list is empty.
- ⚠ scope correction: Manual interval ranges survive a DIRECT source-video switch and export against the wrong video. At app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:268 ManualInterval is rendered with no `key` and no videoId, so its `ranges` state (app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35) persists when the picker at MakeShorts.tsx:221 moves from one video option straight to another (both truthy -> the `{selectedId ? ...}` subtree at :232 reconciles instead of remounting). `runManualExport` then pairs the OLD ranges with the NEW `selectedId` at :166/:171 (probe: videoId="v2", candidateIds=["1@60"]). Scope: routing through the empty "Select a video..." option (or leaving the Make tab) unmounts the subtree and does clear the list, so only the direct switch leaks. Same root cause as the AI-path fix at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:233-249; also unfixed for `manualNote`/`manualError`/`tray`/`trayOpen` (MakeShorts.tsx:78-81), which likewise carry the previous video's result note and open OutputTray across the switch. Untestable by the current suite because MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 mocks ManualInterval away. Severity: medium-high (silently wrong-content clips plus wasted render/cloud spend; recoverable, no data loss).
- ⚠ scope correction: Manual interval ranges survive a source-video switch and export against the WRONG video. ManualInterval is rendered with no `key` and no `videoId` prop at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:268 (not :258 — the finding predates PR #308, which inserted the role="tabpanel" block at :201-211), so its `ranges` state (app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35) survives a `selectedId` change (MakeShorts.tsx:221, not :211). runManualExport then pairs the NEW selectedId (MakeShorts.tsx:166, :171) with the OLD video's ranges. CONFIRMED by executed probe on HEAD dcb59e4b: switching a 600s video to a 20s video leaves the "5:00 -> 5:30" row visible with the submit button ENABLED and zero role="alert", and export fires with videoId=v2 and candidate {start:300,end:330}. Downstream, sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:196-216 passes those seconds to ffmpeg as -ss/-to with no duration probe and no clamp (durationSec is clamped only at select time, shortmaker.py:873, which the manual path bypasses), so a correct clip is impossible; the exact resulting artifact — a silently empty/near-empty clip on ffmpeg exit 0, versus an unexplained "ffmpeg cut failed" on nonzero (shortmaker.py:218-219) — is UNVERIFIED because ffmpeg was not executed. The AI path already carries the corresponding reset (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:233-249); the manual path is the straggler. No existing test can catch it: MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 mocks ManualInterval away.
- ⚠ scope correction: Manual interval ranges survive a DIRECT source-video switch (video A → video B in the picker, without passing through "Select a video…" and without leaving the Make tab) and then export against the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps.

app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:268 renders `<ManualInterval onSubmit={…} busy={manualBusy} />` with no `key` and no `videoId` prop, so its `ranges` state (app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35) survives a `selectedId` change made via the picker's onChange (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:221; state declared at :76). `runManualExport` then pairs the CURRENT `selectedId` (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:166 and :171) with the OLD video's ranges. ManualInterval.tsx contains no useEffect at all, so nothing resets it.

Executable proof (full-view probe, real picker + real ManualInterval): select v1 → add 1:00→1:30 → switch picker to v2 → the range list still reads ["1:00 → 1:30"], the "Make shorts from ranges" button stays ENABLED, and `shortmaker.export` is called with videoId="v2", candidateIds=["1@60"], candidates=[{start:60,end:90,sourceStart:60}].

SCOPE BOUNDS (measured, and NOT part of the defect): the ranges DO reset when the user routes through the empty option (v1 → "Select a video…" → v2), because the `selectedId ? (…)` ternary at MakeShorts.tsx:232 unmounts the subtree; and when the user leaves and re-enters the Make tab, via the `active === 'make'` ternary at MakeShorts.tsx:214.

IMPACT: the stale ranges remain VISIBLE in the list (ManualInterval.tsx:102-115) but carry no indication of which video they belong to, and nothing warns on switch — so a user who switches source and clicks through renders B at A's timestamps: wrong content when B is long enough, or an out-of-range cut when it is not (sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py:948 passes source_start/end to cut_clip with no clamp against the real source duration; whether ffmpeg then yields a zero-length file or an error is UNVERIFIED). Render cost (and cloud spend, if routing is cloud) is paid for unusable output.

This is the same failure mode the AI path was explicitly patched for at app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:233-249, whose comment reads "…would carve the NEW video at the OLD video's timestamps"; the manual path never received that fix. Existing tests cannot catch it: MakeShorts.test.tsx:103-122 mocks ManualInterval away, and ManualInterval.test.tsx exercises the component in isolation where the parent's videoId is not observable.

SEVERITY: medium-high — silently wrong paid output and an already-acknowledged bug class, but the trigger needs a specific in-tab sequence, the stale state is on-screen and removable via the ✕ button, and no data is lost.

FIX: `key={selectedId}` on the ManualInterval element at app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:268 (note: NOT :258, which is CaptionDesigner's videoId prop), or pass `videoId={selectedId}` and mirror ShortMaker.tsx:240-249 with `useEffect(() => { setRanges([]); setStartText(''); setEndText(''); setError(null); }, [videoId])` — those four setters cover all of ManualInterval's state (ManualInterval.tsx:33-36). Add a regression test that renders the REAL ManualInterval inside MakeShorts, switches video directly A→B, and asserts the range list is empty.

## Switching section tabs silently destroys the entire Make workspace (AI candidates, approvals, typed ranges)
- surface `Make Shorts - front door` · lens `state-persistence` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:202-204 mounts exactly one of the three sections (`{active === 'gallery' ? <Shorts/> : null}` / `{active === 'batch' ? <Repurpose/> : null}` / `{active === 'make' ? (<div className="make-shorts__make">...) : null}`), so leaving "Make" UNMOUNTS the whole subtree - `ShortMaker` (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:230) and `ManualInterval` (:258) included. Everything ShortMaker holds goes with it: the reviewed candidate list, approvals/discards, nudged boundaries, prompt, audio-track pick, sort mode and exported-clip list (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:160-206).

CONFIRMED by executed probe: add two ranges on Make -> click "Produced shorts" -> click "Make". Output:
  RANGES AFTER TAB ROUND TRIP = 0
while `picker().value` still returned 'v1' - the source video still reads as selected, so the UI looks unchanged.

Nothing on this surface writes state anywhere durable: MakeShorts only ever calls `client.settings.get()` (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:118); there is no `settings.set`, and a repo-wide grep found zero `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` uses under app/.
- why: The most natural click after a successful export is "Produced shorts" - to look at the clips you just made. That single click throws away the review state you need to export MORE candidates from the same run, and rebuilding it requires re-running the `shortmaker.select` job (a long, possibly cloud-billed LLM/analysis pass). Because `selectedId` lives one level up in MakeShorts and survives, the picker still shows the video, so the loss is invisible until the user scrolls down and finds an empty review area. No confirmation, no warning, no restore.
- fix: Stop unmounting the panels on tab change: render all three and hide the inactive ones (e.g. keep them mounted with `hidden`/CSS `display:none`, which also fixes the missing `role="tabpanel"`/`id` wiring), or lift the expensive state (ShortMaker's `items`/approvals and ManualInterval's `ranges`) into MakeShorts so it outlives the section switch. If unmounting must stay, at minimum warn before discarding a non-empty candidate list or range list.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM: leaving the Make section — via either sibling section tab (MakeShorts.tsx:212-214) or any of the 8 top-level tabs (App.tsx:468-471) — unmounts ShortMaker and silently discards the in-flight AI review working set (candidate list, approvals/discards, nudged boundaries, prompt, audio-track pick, sort mode; ShortMaker.tsx:160-206) and ManualInterval's typed ranges (ManualInterval.tsx:35), with no warning and no recovery path: the renderer has no RPC to read back the sidecar's cached candidates (client.generated.ts:28-35 vs shortmaker_ops.py:252-258) and app/ uses no web storage. Rebuilding costs one `shortmaker.select` re-run (a reasoning-ON two-pass LLM call, select.py:776-833; local llama.cpp by default, cloud only if routing is switched) plus the manual re-review. Nothing irreversible is lost — exported clips remain on disk/shorts.list, and taste labels persist via feedback.record (ShortMaker.tsx:565-597,675-677) — and the immediate post-export need is already served inline by the exported-paths list and per-video ProducedShorts on the Make tab (ShortMaker.tsx:978-1007), so the realistic trigger is leaving mid-review (or wanting the all-videos gallery), not the "obvious next click". Remedy: lift/persist the candidate set above the route switch (keeping the three sections mounted only covers the section tabs, not the top-level nav), or at minimum confirm before discarding a non-empty candidate/range list.
- ⚠ scope correction: Switching section tabs unmounts the Make panel and silently discards all review state held INSIDE ShortMaker and ManualInterval — the AI candidate list with approvals/discards/nudged boundaries, the prompt, audio-track pick, sort mode and exported-clip list (app/renderer/src/features/ShortMaker.tsx:160-206), plus the typed manual ranges (app/renderer/src/features/ManualInterval.tsx:35) — because the three sections are mutually-exclusive conditional renders (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:212-214 at HEAD dcb59e4b; :202-204 at the audited 91240473) with no confirm on the transition (:200). State lifted into MakeShorts survives (video selection :76, caption design + position :84, Output Tray :80-81, notes :78-79), and ShortMaker's brand kit is durably persisted via settings.set (ShortMaker.tsx:484), so the loss is scoped to review state, not the "entire workspace" — and because the picker still reads the selected video, the loss is invisible until the user looks for the empty review area. Recovery requires re-running the uncached, provider-key-injected shortmaker.select job (sidecar/contract/spec.py:254; no cache in sidecar/media_studio/features/shortmaker.py) and retyping the ranges. Fix: keep the panels mounted (hidden) or lift ShortMaker's items/approvals and ManualInterval's ranges into MakeShorts; drop the fix's obsolete a11y parenthetical — the role="tabpanel"/id/aria-labelledby wiring already landed in PR #308 (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:206-211).
- ⚠ scope correction: Switching section tabs discards the in-progress AI review session and the typed manual ranges on Make Shorts (medium). Because MakeShorts.tsx:212-214 mounts exactly one section, leaving "Make" unmounts ShortMaker (MakeShorts.tsx:240) and ManualInterval (MakeShorts.tsx:268), and no review-session state is persisted (all useState/useReducer at ShortMaker.tsx:160-206 and ManualInterval.tsx:35; zero localStorage/sessionStorage under app/). Measured across one Make -> Produced shorts -> Make round trip: candidates 2->0, "1 approved"->gone, ranges 2->0, prompt cleared, ShortMaker remounted (tracks.audio.list 1->2, settings.get 2->3). Recovering the candidate list requires re-running `shortmaker.select` — the sidecar's `_selection_cache` (shortmaker_ops.py:96,252-258) is reachable only by export resolution and `shortmaker_select` (shortmaker_ops.py:119-155) never short-circuits on it. It is NOT the whole workspace: the parent-owned caption design incl. the dragged position (MakeShorts.tsx:84,251-264 — measured surviving), the output-tray delivery choices (MakeShorts.tsx:80-81), the selected video (MakeShorts.tsx:76), and the settings-backed brand kit / caption-style seed (ShortMaker.tsx:189,475-490; MakeShorts.tsx:243-246) all survive, and exported clips stay on disk and are re-listed by `shorts.list`. Fix as proposed (keep the three panels mounted and hidden, or lift ShortMaker's `items`/approvals and ManualInterval's `ranges` into MakeShorts, or warn before discarding a non-empty list) — but drop the "also fixes the missing role=tabpanel/id wiring" rationale: MakeShorts.tsx:206-211 already wires it (PR #308).

## Picking "Reframe to vertical" once permanently hijacks the Edit tab for that video
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Chain, all verified: `app/renderer/src/lib/taskHub.ts:84-85` classifies `'reframe'` as `{ kind: 'workspace', tab: 'shortmaker' }`. `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:86-90` acts on that on EVERY mount — `if (resume.kind === 'workspace') { setTab(resume.tab); setMode('workspace'); }`. `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:141` passes `onOpenMakeShorts={onMakeShortsForVideo}`, and `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:180-184` fires on mount: `if (initialTab === 'shortmaker' && onOpenMakeShorts) { onOpenMakeShorts(video.id); }` with no once-guard. `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:373-375` turns that into `setRoute({ name: 'makeshorts', videoId })`, and `App.tsx:480` supplies the callback unconditionally. The redirect-on-mount is pinned by an existing test: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.test.tsx:730-749` ("redirects an initialTab=\"shortmaker\" deep-link on mount"). The choice is persisted at `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:103-114` and there is NO clear/reset anywhere — a repo-wide grep for `HUB_CHOICE_KEY|taskHubChoiceByVideo` returns only `Edit.tsx`, `lib/taskHub.ts` and their tests. Launch amplifies it: `app/renderer/src/App.tsx:327-348` restores `lastOpenedVideoId` and sets `route = {name:'edit'}`.
- why: After one click on the first hub card, the Edit phase becomes unreachable for that video forever. Clicking "Edit" in the left rail mounts Edit → resumes → mounts Workspace → immediately re-routes to Make Shorts; re-opening the video from the Library does the same; the app now even LAUNCHES into Make Shorts instead of Edit. There is no in-app way to clear the remembered choice, so the user cannot recover (Nielsen #3 user control and freedom — no emergency exit, no undo). The model file itself states the intent that is being violated: `taskHub.ts:72-74` says a section choice is deliberately NOT auto-resumed because "it would bounce the user out of the just-opened video" — WU-3a4 turned the shortmaker tab into exactly such a section deep-link, but `resumeFor` still labels it `kind:'workspace'`, so the guard never applies.
- fix: Reclassify `'reframe'` in `resumeFor` (`lib/taskHub.ts:84-85`) as `{ kind: 'section' }` so it marks "Last used" on the hub instead of auto-resuming — matching how `'shorts'`/`'director'` are already handled at `taskHub.ts:90-92`. That is a one-line change and preserves the intended first-click behaviour (the card still routes to Make Shorts via `handleChoose`). Independently, add a once-per-mount guard to the `Workspace.tsx:180-184` redirect effect, and give the user a way to clear the remembered choice (see the separate "no route back to the hub" finding).
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect claim itself needs no rescoping — it is accurate as written. The PROPOSED FIX, however, is defective and must not be applied as stated.

Reclassifying `'reframe'` to `{ kind: 'section' }` in `resumeFor` would route the "Reframe to vertical" card to the **Director** section, not Make Shorts. `app/renderer/src/views/Edit.tsx:116-133` `handleChoose` special-cases ONLY `'shorts'` (`:126-128`); every other non-workspace choice falls through to `onDirector?.()` at `:130`. So the finding's parenthetical — "preserves the intended first-click behaviour (the card still routes to Make Shorts via handleChoose)" — is FALSE. The one-line change silently breaks the card's first click.

A correct minimal fix is two lines, not one: reclassify `'reframe'` as `{ kind: 'section' }` in `taskHub.ts:84-85` AND widen the `Edit.tsx:126` branch to `if (choice === 'shorts' || choice === 'reframe') { onMakeShorts?.(); return; }` — or better, have the reframe card call `onMakeShortsForVideo?.(videoId)` so the first click keeps its video pre-selection, which plain `onMakeShorts()` (`App.tsx:366-368`, no videoId) would drop.

Worth flagging separately: because WU-3a4 turned the `shortmaker` tab into a deep-link out of the Workspace, "Reframe to vertical" and "Make shorts" now land on the SAME top-level surface, so `taskHub.ts:36-38`'s comment that reframe routes to "the per-video Workspace @ the Short-maker tab (owns the reframe engine)" is stale — no in-Workspace reframe destination survives for that card to reach.
- ⚠ scope correction: Picking "Reframe to vertical" once makes the per-video Workspace and Task Hub effectively unreachable for that video across restarts. Verified: taskHub.ts:84-85 classifies 'reframe' as {kind:'workspace', tab:'shortmaker'}; Edit.tsx:87-90 auto-resumes that on every mount; Workspace.tsx:180-184 then redirects to Make Shorts on mount with no once-guard (App.tsx:373-375/480); Edit.tsx:103-114 persists the choice and settings_store.py:508-528 writes it durably to the per-user settings.json; App.tsx:327-348 makes the app even launch into it. No clear/reset exists anywhere (grep-verified). Precise scope: what becomes unreachable is the 13-tab Workspace (Workspace.tsx:53-67 — Transcribe, Search, Subtitles, Diarize, Refine, Tracks, Convert, Timeline, Dub, Timeline export, Recipes, Assets) plus the hub itself, mounted only at Edit.tsx:137; the top-level Caption/Export/Deliver rails still accept that video (App.tsx:457-459, 484-495). The only escape is an undiscoverable sub-100ms race: Edit.tsx:74 renders the hub synchronously before the async settings.get at Edit.tsx:80-91 resolves, so a click landing in that window overwrites the choice — not a designed exit. Only that video is affected (mergeHubChoice is per-video, taskHub.ts:118-131). CORRECTED FIX: reclassifying 'reframe' as {kind:'section'} alone MISROUTES the card to the AI Director, because Edit.tsx:126-130 falls through to onDirector?.() for every non-'shorts' section choice. The fix must also add a 'reframe' arm to handleChoose dispatching to onMakeShortsForVideo(video.id) (not onMakeShorts, which takes no videoId and loses the pre-selection), plus a once-per-mount guard on Workspace.tsx:180-184 and a user-facing way to clear the remembered choice. Test note: Edit.test.tsx:11-27 stubs Workspace and drops onOpenMakeShorts, and Edit.test.tsx:243 asserts the pre-bounce state as correct — so any fix needs an integration test exercising the real Workspace with onMakeShortsForVideo wired.
- ⚠ scope correction: Re-scoping is a WIDENING plus a remedy correction, not a narrowing. Tightened claim: "Picking 'Reframe to vertical' once persistently redirects every subsequent entry into the Edit route for that video straight to Make Shorts, making the entire per-video Workspace -- all 13 panels (Workspace.tsx:53-67), whose only production mount site is Edit.tsx:137 -- unreachable, including at app launch (App.tsx:327-348), with no in-app reset (HUB_CHOICE_KEY appears only in Edit.tsx/taskHub.ts and their tests) and no back affordance in the destination (MakeShorts.tsx declares no onBack). The redirect itself is intended (documented at Workspace.tsx:19-28); the defect is the absence of any escape, and the fact that the two pinned halves (Edit.test.tsx:11-27 mocks Workspace; Workspace.test.tsx:730-750 tests the redirect alone) are never composed in any test. Only recovery is deleting and re-importing the video for a fresh id (library.py:58, :313, :301-303)." Corrected fix: reclassifying 'reframe' to {kind:'section'} ALONE is a regression -- handleChoose (Edit.tsx:120-130) would fall through to onDirector?.() and send the card to AI Director. The change must also add a 'reframe' branch calling onMakeShortsForVideo?.(video.id) and include that callback in the dep array at Edit.tsx:132.

## Library card title has zero overflow handling — long filename titles are silently cut mid-word with no ellipsis and spill over the neighbouring card
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `i18n-length` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845` — `.library__item-title` sets only `font-weight`/`font-size`/`letter-spacing`/`color`. No `white-space`, no `overflow`, no `text-overflow`, no `overflow-wrap`/`word-break`, no `-webkit-line-clamp`. The rule IMMEDIATELY BELOW it, `.library__item-path` (`shell.css:847-854`), does have all three (`white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`) — so the truncation contract exists in this file and the title was simply left out of it.

Titles are the raw, unbounded filename stem: `sidecar/media_studio/library.py:315` → `"title": title or src.stem` (SQLite `title TEXT`, no length bound, `library.py:96`; `sidecar/tests/test_library.py:53` pins "stem default").

MEASURED in real Chromium against the real tokens.css+shell.css+library-cards.css at the app's pinned 1280x820 viewport (`app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37-38`), rendering the exact `LibraryCard.tsx:98-169` markup, title = `Interview_with_the_CEO_about_Q3_earnings_and_the_2027_roadmap_final_v2`:
  {"cardW":246, "titleClientW":230, "titleScrollW":496, "titleOverflowsCard":266,
   "titleWhiteSpace":"normal", "titleOverflow":"visible", "titleTextOverflow":"clip",
   "titleWordBreak":"normal/normal", "cardScrollOverflow":258}
266px of text escapes a 230px content box. Underscore (U+005F) is UAX#14 line-break class AL, so an underscore-joined filename is ONE unbreakable token and cannot wrap.

At the app's minimum window width (`minWidth: 940`, `app/main/main.ts:1040`) it also produces a spurious horizontal scrollbar on the video grid:
  N4 @940x700: {"listClientW":740, "listHScroll":24, "titleOverflowPx":292}
(vs `listHScroll: 0` for every short-title baseline pass.)

Rendered screenshot confirms independently: card 2 reads `Interview_with_the_CEO_about_Q3_earn`, cut mid-word with NO ellipsis, bleeding through the 16px gutter until the next card's opaque `--surface-raised: #1b212e` (`app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:32`) paints over it.

No hover recovery either: `LibraryCard.tsx:118` renders the title with no `title` attribute, while the tiny badges beside it DO get one (`LibraryCard.tsx:126` `title={badge.label}`) and the path line did (`LibraryCard.tsx:133`).
- why: The Library grid is the app's home surface and the video title is its primary identifier. Camera/OBS/Zoom exports are exactly the underscore-heavy long-token case (`Zoom_Meeting_2026-07-26_Product_Review_Recording_3`), so this fires on ordinary real data, not an edge case. Because there is no ellipsis, the user gets no signal that the name was truncated — two recordings differing only in the tail (`..._take1` vs `..._take2`) are visually identical in the grid, so the user opens the wrong video. Screen-reader users are unaffected (the full title is in the accessible name via `cardAriaLabel`, `app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:118-126`); this is a sighted-user-only information loss. Any UI localization would compound it, but the defect is live today with English + real filenames.
- fix: Give `.library__item-title` (`shell.css:840-845`) the same treatment its sibling path line already has, preferring a 2-line clamp so short names keep one line and long ones degrade with a visible ellipsis:

  .library__item-title {
    /* ...existing font props... */
    display: -webkit-box;
    -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
    -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
    overflow: hidden;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere;   /* lets an underscore/camelCase token break */
  }

`overflow-wrap: anywhere` is the load-bearing half — `text-overflow: ellipsis` alone still leaves an unbreakable token overflowing in some engines, and it is what kills the 24px phantom scrollbar at 940px. Also add `title={video.title}` to the span at `LibraryCard.tsx:118` so the full name is recoverable on hover, matching the badge/path precedent. Chromium-only engine, so `-webkit-line-clamp` is safe here.
- ⚠ scope correction: Library card title has no overflow/wrap handling: `.library__item-title` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845) is the only rule for that class anywhere in the repo and sets no `white-space`, `overflow`, `text-overflow`, `overflow-wrap`/`word-break`, or `-webkit-line-clamp`, while its sibling `.library__item-path` (shell.css:847-854) has the full nowrap+hidden+ellipsis contract; `li.library__item` (app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:22-36) adds no `overflow: hidden`.

Trigger (narrower than originally claimed): titles are the unbounded filename stem (sidecar/media_studio/library.py:315 `"title": title or src.stem`; `title TEXT`, library.py:96), and a stem of roughly 49+ characters containing NO break opportunity — no space and no hyphen, i.e. an all-underscore or camelCase run — cannot wrap, because U+005F LOW LINE is UAX#14 class AL. Measured in real Chromium at the pinned 1280x820 viewport (app/e2e/visual/_visualSetup.ts:37-38) against the real tokens.css+shell.css+library-cards.css: `Interview_with_the_CEO_about_Q3_earnings_and_the_2027_roadmap_final_v2` gives titleClientW 218 / titleScrollW 496, ink extending 270px past the card box, rendered cut mid-word with no ellipsis. This does NOT fire on typical device/tool default exports — 8 of 12 realistic names measured wrap and fit, including the originally-cited `Zoom_Meeting_2026-07-26_Product_Review_Recording_3` (wraps to 2 lines, 17px to spare, because the date's hyphens are UAX#14 class HY), Zoom cloud `GMT20260726-140302_Recording_1920x1080`, `OBS_2026-07-26_14-03-02`, macOS `Screen Recording 2026-07-26 at 14.03.02`, and Android `VID_20260726_140302`. It is a human-typed-descriptive-filename case.

Visible symptom (corrected): the overflow is NOT painted on top of the neighbouring card — `li.library__item` is `position: relative` with `z-index: auto` (library-cards.css:23) and an opaque `background: var(--surface-raised)` (:29), so the next card paints later in tree order and occludes it. What the user actually sees is the title cut mid-word with no ellipsis, plus stray text surviving in the 16px inter-card gutters (`--space-5: 16px`, app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:170) — including reappearing in LATER gutters (the `_v2` tail shows up in the gutter between cards 3 and 4, ~250px from its own card, where it reads as belonging to a different card).

Secondary effect (conditional): a spurious horizontal scrollbar on `ul.library__list` (`overflow: auto`, shell.css:819) appears only when a long-title card lands in the LAST grid column — measured 196px there vs 0px in a middle column and 0px for an all-short baseline.

Severity: MEDIUM, not high. Sighted-user-only (the full title is in the accessible name via `cardAriaLabel`, app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts), it requires a specific filename shape, and the full name is already hover-recoverable from the path line directly beneath, which carries `title={video.path}` (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:133) and contains the same stem — though only when `provenance` is falsy (LibraryCard.tsx:132 renders it conditionally). No test or visual baseline covers a long title.

Fix as proposed is correct: give `.library__item-title` a 2-line clamp plus `overflow: hidden` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (the load-bearing half — ellipsis alone cannot break an underscore-joined token), and add `title={video.title}` to the span at LibraryCard.tsx:118 to match the badge/path precedent.
- ⚠ scope correction: `.library__item-title` (`app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845`) has no overflow handling of any kind — no `white-space`, `overflow`, `text-overflow`, `overflow-wrap`/`word-break` or `-webkit-line-clamp` — while its sibling `.library__item-path` (`shell.css:847-854`) does, and no other stylesheet supplies it. MEASURED in real Chromium against the shipping layout (200px rail per `topTabBar.css:16`, provenance wired per `App.tsx:521`, real Inter): a filename stem (`library.py:315` `title or src.stem`, unbounded) whose first ~30 characters contain NO UAX#14 break opportunity — i.e. underscores/letters only, no hyphen, space or period — cannot wrap and overflows the 230px title box: `Interview_with_the_CEO_..._final_v2` renders 519px of ink, 289px past the card, cut mid-token with no ellipsis, with fragments visibly floating in the 16px gutter and re-emerging past the neighbouring card into the grid margin. At the shipped `minWidth: 940` (`app/main/main.ts:1040`) it also produces a 53px phantom horizontal scrollbar on the grid (0px at the default 1280x820). Names that DO carry a break opportunity early — including the common dated recorder form `Zoom_Meeting_2026-07-26_Product_Review_Recording_3` — wrap to 2 lines and render in full (measured -9px at 1280), so the trigger is narrower than "ordinary real data". Identity loss is real but recoverable in-app: no hover `title` on `LibraryCard.tsx:118` (unlike the badge at `:126`), but full-title search (`libraryModel.ts:47-50`) and the per-card "Source & storage" disclosure showing the full path wrapped in full (`library-provenance.css:15-24`) both expose the untruncated name, and the poster frame/duration/Added date discriminate further. SEVERITY: medium — a visible layout/polish defect on the home surface with a narrower trigger and in-app recovery, not a high-severity wrong-file-opened hazard. Fix as proposed (2-line clamp + `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, which is load-bearing because an unbreakable run produces no line overflow for the clamp to ellipsise; plus `title={video.title}`).
- ⚠ scope correction: `.library__item-title` (`app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845`) has no overflow handling — no `white-space`, `overflow`, `text-overflow`, `overflow-wrap`/`word-break`, or `-webkit-line-clamp` — while its immediate sibling `.library__item-path` (`shell.css:847-854`) has the full `nowrap`/`hidden`/`ellipsis` contract. Measured in Chromium against the real stylesheets and the real `LibraryCard.tsx:98-169` markup at 234px card width: a title containing a run of ~30+ characters with NO space, hyphen, period or slash (e.g. `Interview_with_the_CEO_about_Q3_earnings_and_the_2027_roadmap_final_v2` -> 301px, or a long camelCase stem -> 247px) cannot wrap (underscore is UAX#14 class AL) and paints 293px outside the card border box with NO ellipsis. Visible result: the title is cut mid-word with no truncation signal — occluded by the next card's opaque `--surface-raised` (`tokens.css:32`) — and the remainder re-emerges as a garbled fragment in each subsequent inter-card gutter, beside other cards' titles. When the affected card is LAST in a row the overflow reaches the scroll edge and adds ~269px of spurious horizontal scroll to `.library__list` (`shell.css:819`, `overflow: auto`); mid-row cards produce none. `LibraryCard.tsx:118` also omits the `title` attribute that the sibling badge (`:125`) and path (`:133`) both carry, so there is no hover recovery. Screen-reader users are unaffected (`libraryModel.ts:118-126` carries the full title in the accessible name). SCOPE CORRECTION vs the original: this does NOT fire on ordinary Zoom/OBS/camera exports — `Zoom_Meeting_2026-07-26_Product_Review_Recording_3` wraps cleanly to 2 lines on its date hyphens, OBS `2026-07-26 14-33-02` and `DJI_0042` do not overflow at all. The trigger is the no-break-opportunity long stem specifically, which makes this a medium-severity cosmetic/information-loss defect rather than high.

## Search tab auto-mints the cloud-budget acknowledgement, silently defeating the user's `confirmCloudBudget` gate
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:101-103` — `const plan = await getApi().rpc<AiPlan>('index.plan', {videoId}); const params = plan.willEgress ? { videoId, confirmBudget: plan.cacheKey } : { videoId };` and the identical pattern for search at `SemanticSearch.tsx:122-127`. The ack token is minted and consumed inside the SAME click handler — no dialog, no cost figure, no user action between plan and spend. The gate it satisfies: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/ai_ops.py:256-275` `_enforce_cloud_budget_ack`, whose docstring says `ack` must equal the cacheKey "proving the client previewed THIS exact request's cost/egress budget". The setting is ON by default and its own comment states the intended contract: `sidecar/media_studio/settings_store.py:111-115` — "when True, a cloud run that WOULD egress must be acknowledged via ai.planJob first (**the renderer shows the cost/egress budget and the user confirms**). Default True = safe-by-default". The correct sibling implementation exists: `app/renderer/src/features/BatchConsentCard.tsx:58-67` renders an explicit "Acknowledge cloud egress for this batch" button gated on `confirmCloudBudget`. Real money is charged: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/vision_ops.py:689-697` calls `_enforce_egress_gates(...)` then `self._record_egress_cost(envelope)`. `AiPlan` already carries the numbers the UI never shows (`costEst`, `budget.egressBytes`, `willEgress`) — `app/renderer/src/components/useAiJob.ts:33-41`. Reachability: the Search tab is in the non-advanced `speech` cluster (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:80`) and mounts SemanticSearch at `Workspace.tsx:292-293`.
- why: A user who left the safe-by-default "confirm cloud budget" setting on gets zero confirmation and zero cost display before "Build the search index" (`SemanticSearch.tsx:197`) embeds every transcript segment of a long video against a paid cloud embedder, and before every subsequent `Search` submit. Worse, `Rebuild index` (`SemanticSearch.tsx:186-190`) re-runs the whole embed on one unguarded click. The one control the product gives the user to bound cloud spend is programmatically satisfied on their behalf — the setting appears to work while measuring nothing. There is also no spend visibility anywhere on the Edit surface: `SpendCap` is mounted only inside Providers & Keys (`app/renderer/src/features/ProvidersKeys.tsx:612`).
- fix: Do not mint `confirmBudget` inside the action handler. When `plan.willEgress` is true AND `settings.confirmCloudBudget` is on, render a consent step first — reuse the `BatchConsentCard.tsx:58-67` shape (or the two-step guarded commit at `features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:103-142`) showing `plan.costEst` / `plan.budget.egressBytes`, and only pass `plan.cacheKey` after the user activates the acknowledge control. When `confirmCloudBudget` is off, keep the current auto-echo (that is exactly what the opt-out means).
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM (not high): The Search tab is the only AI surface that collapses the plan -> preview -> commit split its siblings keep, so the per-run `confirmCloudBudget` ack is auto-satisfied without ever showing the cost it is supposed to gate. `app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:101-103` (build) and `:122-127` (search) fetch `index.plan` and echo its `cacheKey` back as `confirmBudget` inside the same click handler; because `index_plan` builds the identical `AiInputs` as the handlers (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/vision_ops.py:750` sentinel == `:550`), the token always matches and `_enforce_cloud_budget_ack` (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/ai_ops.py:256-275`) is satisfied by construction. `plan.costEst` and `plan.budget.egressBytes` (`app/renderer/src/components/useAiJob.ts:33-41`) are fetched and discarded unrendered.

Correctly scoped preconditions (all required, none default-on): the user must have (a) added a cloud provider entry with a key — `providers: []` default at `sidecar/media_studio/settings_store.py:106`; (b) explicitly granted per-provider TEXT consent, which is default-deny per `sidecar/media_studio/models/consent.py:85-87` and enforced per-entry at pool construction (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/providers_ops.py:639-645`, consumed by `vision_ops.py:782`); and (c) not be offline (`vision_ops.py:779-780` plans a local-only pool). On a default install this path embeds locally with zero egress and no ack is ever minted — proven by `sidecar/tests/test_handlers_index.py:507-520`. The gate does genuinely bite when those preconditions hold (`test_handlers_index.py:523-533`).
