Residual bounds that survive this defect (so it is not an unbounded-spend hole): text consent is a separate, non-auto-satisfiable opt-in; the monthly hard cap is an independent gate in the same chokepoint (`ai_ops.py:152-153`) that the renderer cannot mint past, though it defaults off (`settings_store.py:131-133`); and a repeated identical query is served from the vector cache before the gate, egressing nothing (`vision_ops.py:666-683`).

Sharpest remaining instance: `Rebuild index` (`SemanticSearch.tsx:186-190`) re-embeds the entire transcript on one click with no cost shown and no second confirmation.

Characterization corrections: this is a documented, deliberate decision, not a silent one — see the comment at `SemanticSearch.tsx:95-100` and the two tests that assert it (`SemanticSearch.test.tsx:484-504`, `:524-543`), which must be updated alongside any fix. And SemanticSearch is not a lone outlier in mechanism: `app/renderer/src/panels/DirectorPanel.tsx:327` echoes `preview?.perFunction[0]?.cacheKey` the same way, but is defensible because Plan and Apply are two distinct user actions with the preview rendered in between. The defect is the missing preview-then-commit split, and the fix (reuse the `BatchConsentCard.tsx:58-67` ack shape gated on `confirmCloudBudget`, showing `plan.costEst` / `plan.budget.egressBytes`) is unchanged.
- ⚠ scope correction: Confirmed as a real defect; only one sentence of the rationale needs tightening. "The one control the product gives the user to bound cloud spend is programmatically satisfied on their behalf" is a slight overclaim — the monthly soft warning + hard cap is an INDEPENDENT control that the cacheKey echo does not defeat (`ai_ops.py:153` `_enforce_monthly_hard_cap`, surfaced by `features/SpendCap.tsx`). Correctly scoped: "The per-run cloud-budget acknowledgement — the only per-run bound, and the only one enabled by default — is programmatically satisfied on the user's behalf, with no cost figure ever rendered on the Edit surface. The independent monthly cap survives but enforces nothing out of the box (`settings_store.py:131-133`: monthlySoftLimitCents 0, monthlyHardLimitCents 0, enforceMonthlyHardLimit False)." Preconditions worth stating inline: a default install has `useCloud: False` (`settings_store.py:93`), `providers: []` (`:106`) and `consent.perProvider: {}` (`:110`), so `willEgress` is false and no ack is minted; the defect bites the user who has configured a cloud embedder AND granted TEXT consent — precisely the population `confirmCloudBudget` exists to protect.
- ⚠ scope correction: The Search tab (SemanticSearch panel) never reads the `confirmCloudBudget` setting and auto-mints the cloud-egress acknowledgement inside its own click handler, so on this surface the default-on gate is unconditionally inert. `app/renderer/src/features/SemanticSearch.tsx:101-103` and `:122-128` call `index.plan` and immediately pass `plan.cacheKey` as `confirmBudget` to `index.build`/`index.search`, satisfying `_enforce_cloud_budget_ack` (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/ai_ops.py:256-275`) with zero user action, no egress disclosure, and no consent step. Consequence, correctly scoped: the user's transcript segments are sent to a configured cloud embedder — on "Build the search index", on every unguarded "Rebuild index" (`SemanticSearch.tsx:186-190`), and on every cache-missing query (`vision_ops.py:684-697`) — without the per-run acknowledgement the setting promises (`settings_store.py:111-115`). This is an EGRESS/consent and safety-setting-integrity defect, NOT a proven monetary loss: the price table is empty (`sidecar/media_studio/models/provider_pricing.py:36`), curated models are documented free/freemium (`:34-35`), all costs derive from a 1-cent placeholder (`:31`), and `_record_egress_cost` (`ai_ops.py:156-165`) only writes an estimate to a local ledger. It matters because it is the only spend/egress control ON by default — the monthly caps all default off (`settings_store.py:131-133`) — and because two siblings implement the intended two-step correctly (`BatchQueue.tsx:198-213` + `BatchConsentCard.tsx:58-67`; `DirectorPanel.tsx:327` sourcing the ack from separate `preview` state), making this an outlier rather than house style. Preconditions: a user-configured cloud provider with TEXT consent granted (`vision_ops.py:439`) and online; a default install routes local, `willEgress` is false, and the code correctly omits the ack. Severity: MEDIUM. Fix: gate on `settings.confirmCloudBudget` AND `plan.willEgress` and require an explicit acknowledge activation before passing `plan.cacheKey`, reusing the `BatchConsentCard.tsx:58-67` shape — but state egress (provider + that the transcript leaves the machine, e.g. `plan.budget.egressBytes`) rather than presenting `plan.costEst` as a real charge while the price table is empty.

## "Translate" destroys the source-language subtitle track in place, with no warning, confirmation or undo
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:262-264` renders a bare `<button onClick={translate}>Translate</button>`; `translate()` at `Subtitles.tsx:145-182` fires `subtitles.translate` and then `applyTrack(translated)` with no guard. The sidecar overwrites the row: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:159-166` — comment `# Monolingual: replace the source track in place (legacy behaviour).` followed by `project.data["tracks"] = [translated if t.id == track_id else t ...]` and `project.save(save_path)`. The docstring states it plainly at `media_ops.py:110-111`: "The stacked track is added as a NEW track on the project (the source track is left intact); a monolingual translate still replaces in place as before." Cues live inline on the track (`sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:16` — `SubtitleTrack = {id, lang, name, format, kind, cues}`), so the original-language cue text is gone from the manifest once saved. The only non-destructive path is the checkbox at `Subtitles.tsx:275-282`, labelled only "Bilingual (stack original + translation)" — the UI never says that leaving it unchecked overwrites the original. `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_TAB = 'subtitles'` (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:96`), so this is the first panel most users land on.
- why: A user who just spent time transcribing and hand-correcting cues (Subtitles autosaves every cue edit on blur, `Subtitles.tsx:332`) can click Translate once and permanently lose the corrected source-language text. There is no confirm, no undo, and no second copy: the Timeline panel's undo history is per-mount and in-memory (`app/renderer/src/features/Timeline.tsx:100-102`), and no confirmation dialog exists anywhere in the renderer except `features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:106` (the only `role="alertdialog"` in `app/renderer/src`).
- fix: Make the non-destructive path the default: either always add the translation as a NEW track (the `stack_bilingual` branch already proves the sidecar supports it, `media_ops.py:152-158`), or gate the in-place monolingual translate behind a confirm that names the loss ("This replaces the '<lang>' cues on track '<name>'. The original text will not be recoverable."). At minimum relabel the checkbox to state the consequence of leaving it off.
- ⚠ scope correction: "Translate" (with the "Bilingual" checkbox left unchecked — the default) silently overwrites the source-language subtitle track row in place, with no warning, confirmation, or undo. The destructive path is real and is the default: `Subtitles.tsx:262-264` is a bare Translate button, `bilingual` defaults to false (`Subtitles.tsx:66`), and the sidecar replaces the row and saves (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:159-166`, same track id per `features/subtitles.py:379-382`); there is no manifest-level undo (`library.py:546-555`, `_write_json` at `library.py:76-81`) and no confirm dialog on this path (the only `role="alertdialog"` in the renderer is `features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:106`). This is the first panel most users land on (`views/Workspace.tsx:96`).

However the source-language TEXT is NOT destroyed and the loss is NOT permanent. `subtitles_translate` rewrites only `project.data["tracks"]` (`media_ops.py:160-163`); the source-language text also lives in `project.data["transcript"]`, a separate manifest field (written `media_ops.py:438-439`, reloaded `library.py:537-542`) that is a hard precondition for the track existing at all (`media_ops.py:45-47`). One click of the panel's own "Generate subtitles" button (`Subtitles.tsx:234`) mints a fresh-id track from that transcript (`subtitles.py:93`, appended via `tracks.py:117-120`) and restores the source-language cues — executable-proven (post-translate: transcript `['Hello world.']` / language `en`; after regenerate: project langs `['es','en']`).

The genuinely unrecoverable loss is narrower: ONLY the user's hand-corrections, because `subtitles.edit` (`media_ops.py:68-82`) persists cue edits into `tracks` and never back into `transcript` — so a regenerate returns the raw ASR text, not the corrected text (executable-proven: after editing a cue, `hand-correction anywhere in transcript: False`; regenerate yields the raw ASR line). Severity: MEDIUM, not high — bounded to the manual-correction delta, and primarily a missing-affordance/mislabeled-control defect rather than unrecoverable data destruction.

Correctly-scoped fix: relabel the checkbox to state the consequence of leaving it off (e.g. "Bilingual — keep the original as a second track; unchecked replaces the original in place"), and either default it on or gate the monolingual path behind a confirm that names the real loss ("Your manual cue corrections on '<name>' will be replaced. Regenerating restores the original transcript text but not your edits."). Note two constraints the original fix proposal missed: flipping to always-add-a-new-track breaks the deliberately pinned `test_translate_monolingual_still_replaces_in_place` (`sidecar/tests/test_handlers_captions_export.py:139-145`), and `CONTRACTS.md:67` is silent on replace-vs-add so the change is contract-legal. A cheaper, higher-value complementary fix: have `subtitles.edit` also write corrections back into `project.data["transcript"]`, which would make the residual loss zero.
- ⚠ scope correction: The finding stands as written and is NOT an overclaim overall; only one narrow supporting sub-clause needs tightening. "There is no confirm, no undo, and no second copy" should read: "There is no confirm, no undo, and no recoverable copy of the *edited* cues — the project manifest does retain an untouched `transcript` field (`sidecar/media_studio/library.py:541-542`) from which `subtitles.generate` (`media_ops.py:52-55`) can rebuild a RAW ASR source-language track, but `subtitles.edit` (`media_ops.py:68-82`) never writes hand-corrections back to that transcript, so any manual cue correction is permanently lost." Everything else — the destructive in-place replace, the missing warning/confirm/undo, the default-off bilingual checkbox, and the default landing tab — is confirmed exactly as reported.
- ⚠ scope correction: The headline claim stands verbatim. Only one supporting sentence in WHY IT MATTERS overclaims — "there is no confirm, no undo, and no second copy" — and should be scoped to: "There is no confirm, no undo, and no manifest history: `Project.save` is an atomic overwrite with no backup (`library.py:546-555`, `:76-81`). The unrecoverable loss is specifically the hand-corrected (and polish/speaker-labelled) source-language cue TEXT. A source-language track itself IS regenerable, because `translate` never touches `project.data['transcript']` and `subtitles.generate` mints a fresh random track id each call (`subtitles.py:93`), so one click of 'Generate subtitles' returns the RAW ASR cues — with every manual correction lost. Likewise, if the user happened to run Export beforehand, an untouched SRT survives at `exports_dir/<trackId>.<fmt>` (`media_ops.py:91`). Neither is a designed safety net for this operation and neither preserves the corrections."

## Tracks "Remove" permanently deletes a subtitle track and all its cues on a single unconfirmed click
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.tsx:235-237` renders `<button disabled={isBusy} onClick={() => void remove(t.id)}>Remove</button>` as the FIRST button in each row, styled identically to the non-destructive `Burn in` and `Strip` siblings (`Tracks.tsx:238-251`). `remove()` (`Tracks.tsx:111-114`) calls `tracks.remove` immediately. Sidecar: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:248-260` → `sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:124-136` filters the row out of `project["tracks"]`, then `project.save()`. Cues are stored inline on that row (`tracks.py:16`), so the whole cue list dies with it. There is no recovery path: `tracks.add` resolves the object via `find_track(self._find_project_for_track(track_id).data, track_id)` (`media_ops.py:237`), which can no longer locate the deleted id, and `find_track` raises `TrackNotFoundError` (`tracks.py:93-101`). The `availableTracks` "Add" list is fed from a stale `project.open` snapshot taken once on mount (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:266` + `:277`, loaded by `reloadProject` at `Workspace.tsx:163-175`) and is never refreshed after a remove, so the deleted track can still appear there — clicking Add would error rather than restore.
- why: One misclick on a 4-button row destroys a transcript's worth of hand-edited cues with no confirm, no undo and no restore. The residual "Add" affordance from the stale snapshot makes it look recoverable when it is not, which is worse than no affordance at all. Note the sidecar already models a *refusal* for one destructive case (`HardSubtitleError`, `tracks.py:73-79`) — the removable case simply proceeds.
- fix: Add a confirm step naming the track and its cue count before calling `tracks.remove` (reuse the two-step guarded-commit shape of `features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:103-142`), or make remove soft/undoable (keep the row with a `removed` flag and offer an Undo affordance). Separately, refresh `availableTracks` after a mutation so the dead "Add" affordance stops appearing.
- ⚠ scope correction: Tracks "Remove" irreversibly discards a subtitle track's EDIT DELTA on a single unconfirmed click. The row's Remove button (`app/renderer/src/features/Tracks.tsx:235-237`) is the leftmost of four buttons that share one unstyled flex container (`app/renderer/src/features/panels.css:140-144`) — it carries no destructive styling and no confirm, and fires `tracks.remove` immediately (`Tracks.tsx:111-114` → `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:248-260` → `sidecar/media_studio/features/tracks.py:124-136` → `project.save()`). Because cues are stored inline on the row (`tracks.py:179`) and `Project.save` overwrites the manifest with no revision history (`sidecar/media_studio/library.py:546-555`), everything layered on top of the raw transcript is lost: hand edits made via `subtitles.edit` (`app/renderer/src/features/Subtitles.tsx:106-117` → `media_ops.py:68-82`), translation output, bilingual stacks, caption polish and speaker labels (`media_ops.py:52-62`, `:99-166`). SCOPE CORRECTION: the transcript itself survives and `subtitles.generate` (`media_ops.py:36-65`) can regenerate a machine-cue track from it with a fresh id (`sidecar/media_studio/features/subtitles.py:93`), so the loss is the delta, not the transcript. Even so there is no in-app restore: the RPC registry has no subtitle/track import method (`sidecar/media_studio/handlers/composition.py:93-275`), so an exported `.srt` cannot be re-ingested, and the only undo (`director.undo`, `composition.py:216`) is Director-plan-scoped. The residual "Add an existing track" affordance is not a restore: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:266` wires the project's own tracks in as `availableTracks` at `:277` and never refreshes after a mutation (`:163-175`), so a removed id errors at `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:116` (`unknown track`, raised by `_find_project_for_track` at `media_ops.py:237` — not `TrackNotFoundError`). FIX: gate Remove behind the two-step confirm shape already used at `app/renderer/src/features/export/ExportInspector.tsx:103-142` (or the `window.confirm` shape at `app/renderer/src/views/Shorts.tsx:146-150`), name the track and its cue count, and refresh `availableTracks` after any mutation. FILE THIS CLASS-LEVEL: the same unconfirmed-destructive pattern hits harder at `app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:368-384`, where `library.remove` unlinks the whole project manifest (`library_ops.py:145`) with no confirm on a far more prominent surface — that instance should outrank this one.
- ⚠ scope correction: Tracks "Remove" permanently deletes a soft subtitle track and its inline cues on a single unconfirmed click, with no undo and no re-attach path. Tracks.tsx:235 renders Remove as the first button in each row, visually identical to the non-destructive Burn in (:238) and Strip (:249) siblings, which only ever write new sibling files (tracks.py:490 "-hardsub.mp4", :568 "-stripped") and never mutate the manifest (media_ops.py:263-282). remove() (Tracks.tsx:111-114) calls tracks.remove immediately - proven by the repo's own test, where one click yields the RPC (Tracks.test.tsx:181-191) - and nothing gates it in Electron main (the only dialog.* uses in app/main are file pickers: dialogIpc.ts:71, shellIpc.ts:83, dataFolderIpc.ts:90). The sidecar (media_ops.py:248-260 -> tracks.py:131-136) filters the row out and project.save() (library.py:546-555 -> _write_json at library.py:76-81) persists it with an atomic temp+os.replace and no backup. Cues live inline on the row (tracks.py:173-180), so they die with it. SCOPE: only kind=="soft" tracks - a kind=="hard" track is refused via HardSubtitleError (tracks.py:73-79, raise at :132-133, mapped at media_ops.py:255-256). RECOVERY, correctly scoped: there is no undo (director.undo at DirectorPanel.tsx:346-356 is director-plan-only; timelineOps.undo is renderer-local) and no re-attach - there is no subtitles.import RPC (composition.py:128-131 registers only generate/edit/translate/export), so an exported .srt cannot be brought back. Two descriptive corrections: the row has 3 buttons at rest, not 4 (Cancel at :244-248 renders only while that row's burn job is in flight), and the panel sits behind the Deliver cluster's advanced disclosure (Workspace.tsx:84-89), which lowers exposure without changing the outcome. FIX unchanged: add a two-step confirm naming the track and its cue count, following the in-repo precedents at ExportInspector.tsx:103-142 (role="alertdialog", approve/cancel) and Shorts.tsx:146-147 (confirm before the destructive shorts.delete), and refresh availableTracks after any tracks.* mutation.
- ⚠ scope correction: Non-material refinement only (the finding stands as written): Tracks "Remove" permanently deletes a kind:"soft" subtitle track and its inline cues from the project manifest on a single unconfirmed click of the FIRST of THREE identically-styled row buttons (Cancel is a 4th only during an in-flight burn). The project-level `transcript` survives, so a plain regenerated track is recoverable via subtitles.generate; what is unrecoverable is the hand-edited (media_ops.py:68-82), translated-in-place (media_ops.py:160-166) or polished cue set — there is no undo (library.py:546-555 atomic overwrite, no retained version), no subtitles.import (composition.py:128-131), and the stale mount-only availableTracks snapshot (Workspace.tsx:266/:277, setProject only at :167 via the video.id-keyed effect :173-175) guarantees a dead "Add" affordance that fails at media_ops.py:237 via library_ops.py:116. ## Convert silently overwrites an existing sibling file — the destination path is never shown before the run
- surface `Edit phase` · lens `destructive-actions` · verifiers 3
- evidence: The panel shows only `Source: <videoId>` — `app/renderer/src/features/Convert.tsx:172` sets `sourceLabel = videoId ?? path ?? '(no source)'` and `Convert.tsx:177-179` renders it; Workspace passes both so the opaque id wins (`app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:279`). The submit button is a bare `Convert` (`Convert.tsx:309-311`), and the output path is only revealed AFTER the job finishes (`Convert.tsx:333-344`). The destination is derived silently: `sidecar/media_studio/features/convert.py:137` `dest = src.with_name(f"{src.stem}.{ext}")` in the SOURCE's own directory. Only the collide-with-the-source case is guarded (`convert.py:138-141` adds a `.converted` infix); collision with any OTHER pre-existing file is not. ffmpeg is then invoked with `-y`: `sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:157` ("and ``-y`` to overwrite the output") and `ffmpeg.py:160`. `convert.py:41` and `:181` both acknowledge the `-y` unconditional-overwrite property. Default container is `mp4` (`Convert.tsx:39-48`), the single most likely extension to already exist next to a source.
- why: Opening `interview.mkv` and pressing Convert with the defaults writes `interview.mp4` into the same folder and destroys any pre-existing `interview.mp4` — a previously delivered cut, a hand-made export — with no prompt, no "file exists" warning, and no way for the user to have predicted the filename, because the panel never displays a destination. The same one-click reachability applies through the persistent Export action, which jumps straight here (`Workspace.tsx:105`, `:137-140`).
- fix: Show the resolved destination path in the form before the run (the sidecar's `output_path` is pure and could be exposed as a cheap RPC, or mirrored client-side), and either refuse-and-prompt when the destination already exists or auto-uniquify (extend the `.converted` infix rule at `convert.py:138-141` to any collision, not just self-collision).
- ⚠ scope correction: Convert derives its destination silently and overwrites a pre-existing sibling with no prompt and no pre-run disclosure. `output_path` (sidecar/media_studio/features/convert.py:137) writes `<source stem>.<chosen ext>` into the SOURCE's own directory, and the only collision guard (convert.py:138-141, pinned by sidecar/tests/test_convert.py:111-115) covers the self-collision case `dest == src`; any OTHER pre-existing file at that derived name is destroyed unconditionally because ffmpeg runs with `-y` (sidecar/media_studio/ffmpeg.py:160). The trigger is therefore narrower than "any convert": it requires the chosen container/audio extension to DIFFER from the source's extension AND a sibling with the target extension to already exist — e.g. `interview.mkv` with the default mp4 container (app/renderer/src/features/Convert.tsx:39-48) clobbering a hand-made `interview.mp4`. When the source is itself an .mp4 the self-collision branch fires and writes `<stem>.converted.mp4`, so that common case is safe. The renderer never reveals the destination before the run: the panel shows only `Source: <opaque uuid>` (Convert.tsx:172,177-179; Workspace.tsx:279 passes both videoId and path so the uuid4 id from library.py:56-58 wins), the submit control is a bare `Convert` (Convert.tsx:309-311), and the output path surfaces only after completion (Convert.tsx:333-344, populated at :104). No confirm dialog exists in app/main (only dialogIpc.ts:24 and dataFolderIpc.ts:90) and no `out` is injected server-side (media_ops.py:328-334), so nothing else intervenes. Scope correction vs. the original wording: the destination is not unpredictable in principle — the persistent workspace header (Workspace.tsx:308-310) shows the source stem via `{video.title}` (library.py:315) with the full source path as its tooltip, and the extension is the user's own selection — so the defect is the absence of DISCLOSURE (no resolved destination shown, no "file exists" warning, no uniquify) rather than an unknowable filename. `convert.batch` compounds it: convert.py:261-305 applies the same derivation per item with no cross-item check, so two same-stem sources differing only in extension both derive one destination and the later item silently overwrites the earlier item's own output in a single run. Fix as proposed: display the resolved destination in the form pre-run and either prompt on an existing destination or extend the `.converted` infix rule at convert.py:138-141 to ANY collision (including within-batch).
- ⚠ scope correction: Convert silently overwrites an existing sibling file — the destination path is never shown before the run. The Convert panel displays only an opaque 12-hex videoId as its source (Convert.tsx:172, :177-179; library.py:58) and no destination field at all; the sidecar derives `<source stem>.<container>` in the source's own directory (convert.py:137) guarding ONLY the self-collision case (convert.py:138-141), and ffmpeg runs with `-y` (ffmpeg.py:160), so a pre-existing sibling with the same stem and the target extension is destroyed with no existence check and no prompt anywhere in the renderer, Electron, or sidecar layers. The destination is not displayed anywhere before the run; the source path is obtainable only as a hover tooltip on the workspace title (Workspace.tsx:308), and the `<stem>.<container>`-next-to-source derivation rule is never surfaced in the UI, so a user cannot reasonably anticipate which file will be replaced.
- ⚠ scope correction: Convert (and the rail Export view) silently overwrites an existing sibling file: neither surface shows the resolved destination path before the run, and no collision check exists. Verified scope: the destination is derived as `<source stem>.<container>` in the SOURCE's own directory (convert.py:137) and ffmpeg is invoked with `-y` (ffmpeg.py:160), so a pre-existing same-stem file with the target extension is overwritten with no prompt, no warning, and no undo; only collision with the source itself is guarded (convert.py:138-141, pinned by test_convert.py:111-116 vs :67-69). Both entry points are affected: the Workspace "Convert" tab, which labels the source with an opaque uuid (Convert.tsx:172 + library.py:58) and submits via a bare "Convert" button (Convert.tsx:309-311), and the rail Export view, whose two-step "guarded commit" shows only a platform name as its "destination" (Export.tsx:71,95; ExportInspector.tsx:110-115) with `container:'mp4'` hardcoded and explicitly "never shown" (exportModel.ts:211-223). NARROWED from the original wording: it is an overclaim that the user has "no way to have predicted the filename" - Workspace.tsx:308-310 renders `video.title`, which is `src.stem` (library.py:315), with the full source path in a hover-gated `title=` tooltip, and the container dropdown sits in the form, so the `<stem>.<container>` name is inferable in principle. What is never disclosed on any surface is that the output is written into the source's own directory (every sibling feature instead writes to the app-owned `Services.exports_dir` - settings_store.py:84-90, _services.py:74), nor that an existing file is about to be destroyed. Impact is conditional on a same-stem sibling existing (non-mp4 source plus `<stem>.mp4`, e.g. an OBS `.mkv` or camera `.mov` next to a delivered `.mp4`), but in that case the loss is silent and unrecoverable.

## Transcribe error alert renders red text at 4.23:1 — below AA — because .feature-panel .error uses --status-error instead of the AA-safe --status-error-text token that already exists for exactly this case
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `contrast` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Rule: `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1224`, the offending declaration is `color: var(--status-error);` at `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222` on a `background: var(--status-error-soft)` wash (`shell.css:1223`).
Consumer: `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:194-198` renders `<p className="error" role="alert">{error}</p>`; that alert path is live and tested at `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.test.tsx:235-244`.
Plane: panel composites onto `--surface-bg` `#121620` (`app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:14`; `.workspace__body` sets no background — `shell.css:1017`, `app/renderer/src/views/workspace.css:196`).
Measured (script output, calculator validated against the repo's own pinned 3.75:1 figure at `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:298`):
  base   --status-error      on wash/BG: 4.227
  fixed  --status-error-text on wash/BG: 5.961
Text is 13px (`--type-body-size`, `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:145`) at `--weight-regular` 400 → normal text → 4.5:1 required.
The fix token and its rationale already exist: `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:73-80` defines `--status-error-text: #ff6b6b` explicitly because "the solid #e5484d is only ~4.1:1 ... below the 4.5:1 AA floor the DoD pins". Five sibling sheets were migrated (`views/director.css:72-73`, `features/library-provenance.css:50`, `features/keep-copy-control.css:112`, `components/library-cards.css:180`, `components/library-shell.css:56`).
Why CI misses it: the guard at `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:688-698` applies its `RED_TEXT_LEAK` regex (`tokens.conformance.test.ts:649`) only to the 5-sheet whitelist `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (`tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658`) — `shell.css` is not in it, so this leak is invisible. `shell.css` in fact carries 4 bare `color: var(--status-error)` leaks (lines 446, 567, 1222, 1425).
- why: This is the one string a user MUST be able to read on this surface: when `transcribe.start` rejects or the sidecar dies, the alert text is the only explanation of what went wrong. At 4.23:1 it fails WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (AA) for normal text and misses the project's own DoD contrast floor. The failure is not a design trade-off — the correct token, the rationale comment, and the migration precedent all already exist in the repo; this shared rule was simply skipped, and the conformance guard's hardcoded whitelist guarantees no test will ever catch it.
- fix: In `app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222`, change `color: var(--status-error);` to `color: var(--status-error-text);` (keep `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` and the `--status-error-soft` background — the fill/border red is unchanged, so there is zero visual regression to the rail). That lifts the Transcribe alert to 5.96:1. Then close the guard hole: add `resolve(HERE, '..', 'components', 'shell.css')` (and `features/panels.css`) to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` at `app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658`, or better, drop the whitelist and glob every sheet under `renderer/src` so no future red-text leak can hide. Note lines 446, 567 and 1425 will also need triage — 446 is a hover text colour and 1425 is the `.sm-status-discarded` chip, both red TEXT on a soft wash, i.e. the same class of defect on sibling surfaces.
- ⚠ scope correction: Scope correction is a WIDENING, not a narrowing — the finding is valid as written but names only one of the affected surfaces. Correctly-scoped version:

"Error-alert text renders below the AA 4.5:1 floor on EVERY feature panel plus ShortMaker and Timeline — not just Transcribe — because the shared rule `.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1217) sets `color: var(--status-error)` (:1222) instead of the AA-safe `--status-error-text`, on its own `--status-error-soft` wash (:1223). Per the sheet's own section comment (shell.css:1158) `.feature-panel` covers Transcribe / Subtitles / Tracks / Convert / Dub / Assets; `.sm-error` covers ShortMaker and `.timeline__error` the Timeline. Measured 4.227:1 composited over --surface-bg #121620 (tokens.css:31) — and 3.753:1 for any instance sitting on --surface-raised — against a 4.5:1 requirement for 13px/400 normal text (tokens.css:145, shell.css:17). The wash is load-bearing: the same red on the bare canvas is 4.620:1 and would pass, so the failure only appears when the rule's own background is composited in.

Transcribe (Transcribe.tsx:156 + :195, tested at Transcribe.test.tsx:235-244) is a confirmed live instance, not the boundary of the defect. Fixing shell.css:1222 alone remediates all three selectors at once. Sibling leaks at shell.css:446, 567, 1425 are the same class on other surfaces and need the same triage; `.workspace__error` (shell.css:562-568) is byte-for-byte the same defect shape as 1215-1224.

Additionally, the repo does not merely lack a guard — tokens.conformance.test.ts:299 asserts as a MUST that components route alert text through --status-error-text, while the enforcement regex (:649) is scoped to a 5-path whitelist (:652-658) that excludes shell.css, so the stated MUST is unenforced exactly where it is broken."

## Transcribe error alert uses the FILL red token as TEXT — 4.23:1, below the AA floor the repo's own guard pins
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `token-consistency` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:194-198 renders `<p className="error" role="alert">{error}</p>`. Its only style is app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1224 → `color: var(--status-error); background: var(--status-error-soft);`. app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:71-80 splits the token and states the solid red is a text FAIL: "the solid #e5484d is only ~4.1:1 on --surface-raised ... so red STRINGS ... read from this lighter tone instead" → `--status-error-text: #ff6b6b`. app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.conformance.test.ts:296-304 makes it explicit: "a component MUST route alert text through --status-error-text, not --status-error." But the enforcing guard's file list (tokens.conformance.test.ts:648-658, `RED_TEXT_LEAK` + `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS`) contains only the 5 Library sheets — `components/shell.css` is NOT in it, so this leak is unguarded. Backdrop chain is verified: body `--surface-bg` (shell.css:14) → .app (shell.css:70) → .app__main (shell.css:316) → .workspace (shell.css:503) → .workspace__body (shell.css:1017) → .feature-panel (shell.css:1160), none of which set a background. Independent re-derivation using the repo's own channel/relLum/contrast algorithm (tokens.conformance.test.ts:109-127), composited `--status-error-soft` over each plane: surface-deep 4.59 | surface-bg 4.23 | surface-raised 3.75 | surface-overlay 3.24; the same probe gives 5.96 on surface-bg for `--status-error-text`. The 3.75 figure reproduces the repo's own stated "~3.75:1" (tokens.conformance.test.ts:298) — detector validated. Text is 13px (inherits `--type-body-size`, shell.css:17), so the 4.5:1 floor applies, not the 3:1 large-text exemption.
- why: The error string is the only thing that tells the user why their transcription failed, and it renders at 4.23:1 on the plane the Transcribe panel actually sits on — a WCAG 1.4.3 AA failure that the codebase already created a token to prevent and already documented as forbidden. No e2e coverage exists for this surface either (grep for `transcribe` across app/e2e returns zero matches), so nothing catches a regression here.
- fix: In app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222 change `color: var(--status-error)` to `color: var(--status-error-text)`; leave `border-left: 3px solid var(--status-error)` (shell.css:1220) untouched — that is the sanctioned FILL/BORDER use. Then add `components/shell.css` to `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` (tokens.conformance.test.ts:652-658) so the leak cannot return. Note the same bare-red-text leak exists at shell.css:446, :567 and :1425 — those belong to Library/Workspace/ShortMaker surfaces, flag to those lenses rather than fixing blind.
- ⚠ scope correction: SCOPE CORRECTION IS A WIDENING, NOT A NARROWING — the finding was not overclaimed, it was under-scoped. Correct framing: "The shared `.feature-panel .error, .sm-error, .timeline__error` rule at app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1215-1224 routes alert text through the FILL token (`color: var(--status-error)`) over its own `--status-error-soft` wash, measuring 4.23:1 on the `--surface-bg` plane every feature panel sits on — a WCAG 1.4.3 AA fail at 13px that the repo's own tokens.conformance guard documents as forbidden (tokens.conformance.test.ts:299) but does not police outside the 5 Library sheets (:652-658). It is ONE declaration failing identically on 16 render sites across 14 components, not a Transcribe-only defect: Assets.tsx:190 & :195, Convert.tsx:347, Diarize.tsx:167, Dub.tsx:399, NleExport.tsx:122, Recipes.tsx:217 & :222, Refine.tsx:270, SemanticSearch.tsx:216, Subtitles.tsx:355, SystemHealth.tsx:142, Tracks.tsx:285, Transcribe.tsx:195, DirectorPanel.tsx:537, ModelsSystemPanel.tsx:681 — all under `.feature-panel` roots (verified) — plus `.sm-error` (ShortMaker) and `.timeline__error` in the same selector list. Fix = one line (shell.css:1222 → `--status-error-text`), which closes all 16 at once; the guard extension must migrate shell.css:446/:567/:1425 in the same change or the added `LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS` entry fails."
- ⚠ scope correction: app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:1222 routes error-alert TEXT through the FILL red token (`--status-error`) instead of the sanctioned `--status-error-text`, giving 4.23:1 against the `--surface-bg` plane the Transcribe panel actually sits on — 6% under the 4.5:1 AA floor the repo pins for itself at tokens.conformance.test.ts:299. Severity LOW, not high: the text remains legible (a saturated red on near-black, ~2x the repo's own acknowledged 2.4:1 failure), and colour is not the sole signal — Transcribe.tsx:195 carries role="alert" so assistive tech gets the string verbatim, and shell.css:1220/1223 add a red border bar plus wash. No task is blocked and no data is lost. It is also NOT a Transcribe-surface defect: the repo's own leak regex (tokens.conformance.test.ts:649) matches 33 sites across 22 renderer stylesheets, including the byte-for-byte twin banner at jobqueue.css:145-153 that surfaces this same job's failure, so this is repo-wide token-migration debt. Correct remediation is ONE sweep migrating all 33 text uses to `--status-error-text` (leaving every border/fill use intact), then extending LIBRARY_RED_TEXT_SHEETS to the migrated sheets — note that adding components/shell.css to that list requires fixing all four of its instances (446, 567, 1222, 1425) in the same commit, or the guard fails immediately.

## ShortsGalleryModal declares aria-modal="true" but never traps focus or restores it on close
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:76-77 sets role="dialog" + aria-modal="true". The ONLY focus handling is app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47 (`focusOnOpen` callback ref: `node?.focus()`) attached at :85 — it moves focus in but installs no Tab trap and captures/restores nothing. The component does not import the repo's own useFocusTrap; a repo-wide grep shows only three consumers: app/renderer/src/components/FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, app/renderer/src/components/ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44, app/renderer/src/components/DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45. That hook already implements exactly the three missing behaviours (app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:64-108: initial focus, Tab/Shift+Tab cycling, `previouslyFocused?.focus()` on unmount). It is a real full-screen scrim overlay, not an inline panel: app/renderer/src/components/library-shell.css:192-201 (`position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 100; background: var(--overlay-scrim)`). The body holds 6 focusable buttons (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx), so the last tab stop sits deep inside the body. Escape is bound to the dialog div's own onKeyDown (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63-68 and :80), so it only fires while focus is still inside the dialog. The parent's close path does no restoration either: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:424 (`closeShorts = () => setShortsVideo(null)`). The test suite locks in the initial focus only — app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:130 asserts activeElement is `.shorts-modal__close`, with no Tab-containment or focus-restore assertion anywhere in that file.
- why: Two compounding keyboard failures on the Library's only modal. (1) Escape route: with focus on the close button (the first focusable), one Shift+Tab moves focus backward out of the dialog onto the last Library card's "Remove" button — a control sitting behind an opaque scrim that aria-modal="true" has told assistive tech is inert. The user now has focus on an invisible destructive control, and because the Escape handler is scoped to the dialog subtree, Escape silently stops closing the modal. A screen-reader user in a mode that honours aria-modal cannot perceive where focus went. This is a WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) failure. (2) Restore: closing the gallery unmounts the focused close button, so document.activeElement falls back to document.body; the next Tab restarts from the top of the app shell instead of returning to the "N shorts" button that opened the gallery, silently discarding the user's place in a grid that can hold hundreds of videos.
- fix: Replace the ad-hoc `focusOnOpen` callback ref with the existing shared hook, which fixes trap + Escape + restore in one line and matches the three sibling dialogs: `const trapRef = useFocusTrap<HTMLDivElement>({ onEscape: onClose, initialFocus: '.shorts-modal__close' });` attach `ref={trapRef}` to the dialog div at ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:74-81, and delete the now-redundant local `onKeyDown` (:63-68) and `focusOnOpen` (:45-47, :85). The modal is conditionally mounted at Library.tsx:606-615, so mount == becomes-active, which is exactly the usage useFocusTrap.ts:16-17 documents. Add the two missing regression tests next to ShortsGalleryModal.test.tsx:130: Shift+Tab from the close button stays inside the dialog, and unmounting restores focus to the invoking element.
- ⚠ scope correction: The defect is CONFIRMED as stated in substance; three supporting details were wider than their evidence and should be re-scoped:

1. Scrim opacity: the finding calls it an "opaque scrim" rendering the control "invisible". Measured, --overlay-scrim is rgba(9, 11, 16, 0.62) (app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:267) applied at app/renderer/src/components/library-shell.css:200 — 62% dark, heavily obscuring but not opaque, and the backdrop-blur is on .shorts-modal (the panel, library-shell.css:213-214), not on the backdrop. Accurate wording: focus lands on a control heavily dimmed behind a 62% scrim, outside the user's locus of attention, and thus not perceivable as a focus target — rather than literally invisible.

2. Focusable count: "The body holds 6 focusable buttons (app/renderer/src/features/ProducedShorts.tsx)" carries no line cite and is data-dependent — per card a thumb button (:176, only when not playing) plus "Pick best frame" (:204) plus ShortClipActions (:223), plus 2 sort buttons only when shorts.length > 1 (:259-273). The load-bearing claim ("the last tab stop sits deep inside the body") holds for any non-empty gallery regardless of the exact count.

3. Normative citation (the real overclaim): "a WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) failure" is the wrong hook, and it is applied to BOTH failures. Focus RESTORATION has no WCAG success criterion at all, and a missing modal focus trap is properly an ARIA Authoring Practices Guide modal-dialog pattern violation rather than a clean 2.4.3 failure. Correct framing: this violates the ARIA APG modal-dialog pattern AND the repo's own two documented contracts — the shared modal focus-trap contract (app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:1-17, used by all three sibling dialogs) and the "disclosure focus-return contract" (app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:98-100). Drop the Level-A conformance framing; keep the defect.

Correctly-scoped finding, with severity supported by evidence the original did not reach: ShortsGalleryModal declares aria-modal="true" (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:76-77) but installs no Tab trap and never captures/restores focus, and its Escape handler is scoped to the dialog subtree (:63-68, :80) with no document-level fallback anywhere in the renderer. Because the modal is mounted inline (Library.tsx:606-615) after the card list, one Shift+Tab from the close button (the dialog's first focusable) moves focus onto the last LibraryCard's "Remove" button (LibraryCard.tsx:159-166) behind the scrim, where Escape no longer closes the modal; activating it runs handleRemove (Library.tsx:368-384) with no confirmation, which unlinks that video's project manifest and poster from disk (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:145-146) — unrecoverable, since the snapshot restore at Library.tsx:380 only rebuilds the in-memory list. Separately, closing the gallery drops focus to document.body, discarding the user's place in the grid. Severity high is justified by the unconfirmed-destructive-action path, not merely by the lost focus position.
- ⚠ scope correction: ShortsGalleryModal (app/renderer/src/views/ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:76-77) declares role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" but implements only initial focus (:45-47, attached :85) - it installs no Tab/Shift+Tab containment and never captures or restores the previously-focused element, while the repo's own useFocusTrap (app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:75-77, :85-100, :106) already provides all three and is used by its three sibling dialogs (FirstRunChooser.tsx:35, ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44, DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45). EXECUTABLE-PROVEN in jsdom against a validated control: unmounting leaves document.activeElement === document.body instead of the invoking "N shorts" button (LibraryCard.tsx:150-157), while the same probe on a useFocusTrap dialog restores it; Shift+Tab on the close button is not intercepted (defaultPrevented false); and Escape dispatched from outside the dialog does not close it, because the handler is bound to the dialog div (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:63-68, :80) and there is no global keydown listener anywhere in app/renderer/src. Consequence, scoped to the evidence: one Shift+Tab from the initially-focused close button moves focus to the last Library card's "Remove" button (LibraryCard.tsx:159-166, which sits before the modal in document order), a control DIMMED - not hidden - behind a 62%-alpha scrim (--overlay-scrim: rgba(9,11,16,0.62), tokens.css:267) inside a region aria-modal has declared inert to assistive tech, and Escape then stops closing the modal. This violates the ARIA APG modal-dialog keyboard pattern and is commonly mapped to WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A); it does NOT violate WCAG 2.4.11 (the indicator is not entirely obscured). Focusable-stop count in the body is 6 per short with onEdit wired (5 without, 6N+2 for N>1, 1 on the empty branch), not a fixed 6. Severity medium-high. Fix as proposed (swap focusOnOpen for useFocusTrap({onEscape: onClose, initialFocus: '.shorts-modal__close'}), delete the local onKeyDown - safe, no ancestor onKeyDown exists), plus add video[controls] to useFocusTrap's FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR (useFocusTrap.ts:21-28) or the trap leaks while a clip plays inline (ProducedShorts.tsx:174) - UNVERIFIED in a real browser, settle with a Playwright keyboard test.

## LineagePanel drawer implements none of the repo's documented focus-return contract
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `focus-management` · verifiers 3
- evidence: app/renderer/src/features/LineagePanel.tsx:112 renders the drawer as a bare `<aside className="lineage-panel" aria-label={...}>` — no role="dialog", no ref, no initial focus, no keydown handler, no invoker capture, no restore. It is nonetheless a real fixed-position overlay drawer: app/renderer/src/features/lineage.css:45-51 (`position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 40; width: min(420px, 92vw)`), under the comment `/* ---- the drawer ---- */` at :43. It is mounted AFTER the card grid in DOM order — the `<ul className="library__list">` is at app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:579-595 and the panel at :597-604. Opening it does not move focus: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:347-356 (`handleItemClick` only calls `setLineageAsset`), reached from the card's open button at app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:110-115. Closing does not restore focus: app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:342-344 (`closeLineage = () => setLineageAsset(null)`), invoked by the × at LineagePanel.tsx:115-122. The app already has a canonical implementation for exactly this widget shape — its non-modal Jobs slide-over — at app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:100-122, which captures the invoker (`const invoker = document.activeElement` :104), moves focus into the panel (:107), restores it in effect cleanup (:112), and handles Escape (:116-119 with the comment "Escape closes the slide-over (R-L4). It is non-modal, so Tab is NOT trapped."). JobQueue.tsx:100 names this the "disclosure focus-return contract".
- why: The Library's lineage drawer breaks the contract the same codebase defines and honours elsewhere, so the surface is internally inconsistent for keyboard users. In Lineage view, clicking a card opens a 420px drawer pinned over the right edge while focus stays behind on the card's open button. Because the drawer is last in DOM order but first in visual prominence, a keyboard user must Tab through every remaining card's select/open/shorts/remove controls — four stops per card, so ~80 stops in a 20-video library — before reaching the panel that just appeared on top. That visual-order/DOM-order mismatch is a WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) failure. Escape does nothing, so the only dismissal is to keep tabbing to the × ; and activating that × unmounts the focused button, dropping focus to document.body and forcing a restart from the top of the app.
- fix: Mirror JobQueue.tsx:100-122 verbatim in LineagePanel: add a `panelRef` with `tabIndex={-1}` on the `<aside>`, an effect that captures `document.activeElement` as the invoker before calling `panelRef.current.focus()`, restores it in cleanup, and an `onKeyDown` that calls `onClose()` on Escape. Keeping it non-modal (no Tab trap) is correct here since the drawer does not scrim the page — that is the same call JobQueue.tsx:116 documents. Optionally reorder Library.tsx so the panel is not stranded after the grid, or promote it to role="dialog" if it should become modal.
- ⚠ scope correction: The LineagePanel drawer implements no focus management at all - no initial focus, no Escape-to-close, no focus restore on close (app/renderer/src/features/LineagePanel.tsx:112, with no onKeyDown in the file and no global keydown handler in App.tsx) - even though it is a real fixed-position overlay (app/renderer/src/features/lineage.css:45-51) mounted after the whole card grid (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:597-604, grid at :579-594). Severity: MEDIUM, not high.

Scope corrections to the original wording:

1. "the repo's documented focus-return contract" is too strong. The documented a11y item (docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:538, F4) ENUMERATES specific widgets - useFocusTrap for ModelsOnboarding/FirstRunChooser, aria-keyshortcuts for CandidateReview, and Jobs slide-over Escape/focus/aria-controls - and never names the lineage drawer. This is therefore an UNCOVERED GAP in an enumerated per-widget a11y work item, not the violation of a contract that already covers this component. The internal-inconsistency argument still stands on its own evidence.

2. "That visual-order/DOM-order mismatch is a WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) failure" is asserted too flatly. For a NON-MODAL disclosure the ARIA APG pattern deliberately leaves focus on the trigger, so "no initial focus" by itself is not a violation. The defensible normative hooks are narrower: (a) the revealed content is not adjacent to its trigger in tab order (arguably 2.4.3), and (b) focus is dropped to document.body when the close button unmounts itself, which is the concrete, non-arguable defect.

3. The tab-stop arithmetic should be a range, not ~80. Per-card focusable stops are 3 minimum - checkbox (LibraryCard.tsx:101-107), open button (:110-115), Remove (:159-166) - rising to 4 only when the OPTIONAL provenance disclosure is passed (Library.tsx:80 declares it optional; CardProvenanceDisclosure.tsx:42-53 adds one button) and 5 when shortsCount > 0 (:150-157). Worst case (clicking the first of 20 cards) is therefore ~57-76 stops, not ~80.

4. Affected population and reachability should be stated: mouse users are entirely unaffected (clicking another card just swaps drawer content), Lineage view is opt-in and defaults to off (Library.tsx:178 useState(false)), and a partial workaround exists because toggling Lineage view off also clears the drawer (Library.tsx:337-340). The residual harm is real but bounded: keyboard-only and AT users in one opt-in view cannot reach Reveal source / Regenerate / Relink without traversing the rest of the grid, and lose focus to document.body on close.

The proposed fix remains correct, and is better justified by pointing at ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47/:63-68 (same view, same card grid, honours focus-on-open and Escape) in addition to JobQueue.tsx:100-122.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not required (the finding stands as a genuine defect at high severity); supplied only to tighten four loose edges in the wording: "The Library lineage drawer implements none of the three focus behaviours of the disclosure focus-return contract that JobQueue defines in code and pins with three named tests. LineagePanel.tsx:112 renders a bare `<aside className="lineage-panel" aria-label={...}>` with no ref, no tabIndex={-1}, no initial focus, no invoker capture, no restore, and no keydown handler, yet lineage.css:45-51 makes it a real fixed-position 420px overlay drawer mounted AFTER the card grid (Library.tsx:579-595 grid, :597-604 panel). Executably measured against JobQueue as a control: opening leaves focus on the invoking card button (Library.tsx:347-356 -> LibraryCard.tsx:110-115), Escape is inert (0 onClose calls), and closing via the x (LineagePanel.tsx:115-122 -> Library.tsx:342-344) unmounts the focused button and drops focus to document.body; the same probes on JobQueue return focus-in, Escape-closes, focus-restored. Because the drawer is last in DOM order but first in visual prominence, a keyboard user must traverse the remaining cards' controls (~3-5 focusable stops per card depending on shortsCount and the provenance disclosure, so roughly 60-100 stops in a 20-video library) to reach a panel that just appeared on top — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A) per failure technique F85. Scope notes: the contract is documented in code comments and tests (JobQueue.tsx:21,97,100,116; JobQueue.test.tsx:426,432,454) under the id R-L4, NOT in any docs/ spec; role='dialog' is NOT part of the contract, since JobQueue uses role='complementary' (JobQueue.tsx:182) and `<aside>` already supplies that role implicitly, so only the three focus behaviours plus ref/tabIndex plumbing are missing; and Shift+Tab to the 'Lineage view' toggle (Library.tsx:472-479, :337-340) is a second, view-abandoning keyboard escape route. Fix: mirror JobQueue.tsx:100-122 (panelRef + tabIndex={-1} + focus-in effect capturing document.activeElement + restore in cleanup + onKeyDown Escape). Do NOT use the shared useFocusTrap hook here: it traps Tab (useFocusTrap.ts:85-100), which is wrong for a non-modal drawer."
- ⚠ scope correction: Only the word "documented" needs tightening; the defect stands. Precise version: "LineagePanel implements none of the focus-return pattern the codebase establishes in five other overlays. The formally documented a11y requirement (docs/V1.1-FEATURES.md:538 and :67, Lane 0 F4) enumerates its scope as ModelsOnboarding/FirstRunChooser (via useFocusTrap), CandidateReview, and the Jobs slide-over — it does not name LineagePanel, so this is an omission from an established in-repo pattern rather than a breach of a requirement that names the component. The pattern exists in two forms: the shared modal hook app/renderer/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts:71-106 (used by ModelsOnboarding.tsx:44, DirectorOnboarding.tsx:45, FirstRunChooser.tsx:35), and the non-modal disclosure variant at app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:100-122. LineagePanel.tsx:112 has none of it despite being a fixed-position overlay drawer (lineage.css:45-51), and the sibling overlay mounted 2 lines later in the same view (ShortsGalleryModal.tsx:45-47, :63-68 via Library.tsx:606-609) does honour it. Severity medium-high rather than high, because the drawer is reachable only through the opt-in Lineage view toggle (Library.tsx:474-478) which defaults OFF (:178)."

## Batch tab dead-ends on a fresh install: no template is ever seeded, so "Run batch" is permanently disabled with zero explanation
- surface `Make Shorts - gallery / batch` · lens `progressive-disclosure` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `TemplateStore` inherits `RecipeStore` verbatim with NO seeding (sidecar/media_studio/features/templates.py:215-221), and `RecipeStore._read` returns `[]` when the file is absent (sidecar/media_studio/features/recipes.py:166-168). Contrast the sibling store, which DOES self-seed three presets on first read (sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:228-235, seeds at :156-198). Downstream in the renderer: `if (tmpl.length > 0) setTemplateId(...)` never fires so `templateId` stays `''` (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:52, :97); the Template `<select>` renders with ZERO `<option>` children — no placeholder, no empty state (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:303-313); `canRun = selected.length > 0 && templateId !== ''` is false forever (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:258); the primary button is `disabled` with no hint, no `aria-describedby`, and no pointer to the sibling Templates tab (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:316-323). Nothing else in the app writes a template — `client.templates.save` is called only from TemplateEditor (app/renderer/src/features/TemplateEditor.tsx:60). The state is untested: every BatchQueue test mocks exactly one template (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:78-80), and the disabled-Run test only covers the no-source case (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:188-200).
- why: A first-run user opening Make Shorts → "Batch & Templates" lands on Batch queue (the documented default landing, Repurpose.tsx:23-28) and finds the surface's ONE primary action inert, an empty dropdown, and no disclosure of the prerequisite. The fix lives in a sibling tab they have no reason to visit. This is the worst possible progressive-disclosure outcome: the required step is not merely buried, it is invisible.
- fix: Either (a) self-seed one "Make shorts (house style)" template in `TemplateStore._read`, mirroring `PresetStore._read` (export_presets.py:228-235) — the starter already exists client-side at app/renderer/src/features/repurposeTemplates.ts:31-40; or (b) when `templates.length === 0`, replace the empty `<select>` with an inline empty state ("No templates yet — create one in Templates") whose action switches the sub-tab, add a `<option value="">Select a template…</option>` placeholder like the Make picker has (MakeShorts.tsx:213), and give the disabled Run button an `aria-describedby` naming the missing prerequisite. (a)+(b) together is best.
- ⚠ scope correction: MEDIUM / progressive-disclosure + test-coverage: The Batch queue's Template control has no empty state and no seeded default, so a user who has imported videos but never opened the Templates tab sees an empty dropdown and an inert "Run batch" with no disclosure of the prerequisite — recoverable in 3 clicks via the adjacent "Templates" tab, but only by guessing.

Unlike its sibling PresetStore, which self-seeds three presets on first read (sidecar/media_studio/features/export_presets.py:228-235, seeds at :156-198), TemplateStore inherits RecipeStore verbatim with no seeding (sidecar/media_studio/features/templates.py:215-221) and RecipeStore._read returns [] for an absent file (sidecar/media_studio/features/recipes.py:166-168); nothing anywhere seeds a template (composition.py:453-457 wires the store with no seed; the sole writer is app/renderer/src/features/TemplateEditor.tsx:60). So on first use templateId stays '' (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.tsx:97), the Template <select> renders zero <option> children with no placeholder (:303-313), canRun is false (:258), and the disabled primary button carries no hint and no aria-describedby (:316-323). The same surface has a second, equally undisclosed empty state: the Sources fieldset (:287-299) is empty on a fresh install, and selected.length > 0 is the first failing conjunct.

Scope limits that cap this at medium: the missing prerequisite is one click away in an always-visible tab strip rendered above the dropdown (app/renderer/src/views/Repurpose.tsx:28), in a tab labeled "Templates" adjacent at index 1 of 3 (:13, real buttons at app/renderer/src/components/TabBar.tsx:99), reached through a parent tab labeled "Batch & Templates" (app/renderer/src/views/MakeShorts.tsx:50); the editor is pre-filled so saving is one click (TemplateEditor.tsx:27-29); and returning re-mounts BatchQueue (Repurpose.tsx:35), re-running reload() (:107-109) and auto-selecting the template (:97). It is undisclosed, not invisible, and not permanent.

The genuine test gap stands: every BatchQueue test mocks exactly one template (app/renderer/src/features/BatchQueue.test.tsx:78-80), and the test titled "disables Run until a source AND template are chosen" (:188-200) never exercises the template conjunct as false — the zero-template render is unmeasured.

## Library card title has no wrap/truncate rule — long filenames paint over the neighbouring card and add a bogus horizontal scrollbar to the video grid
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `responsive-overflow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: `.library__item-title` at C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845 declares ONLY font-weight/font-size/letter-spacing/color — no `overflow`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `overflow-wrap` or `word-break`. It is the only overflow-unguarded text node on the card: `.library__item-path` directly below it (shell.css:847-854) sets `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, and no other sheet touches the title (grep for `library__item-title` across app/renderer/src/**/*.css returns exactly one hit, shell.css:840). The card is a fixed-floor grid track: `ul.library__list { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(215px, 1fr)) }` (app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:11) with `li.library__item { padding: var(--space-3) }` (library-cards.css:22-28, --space-3: 8px, app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:168), and the list is a scroll container: `.library__list { overflow: auto }` (shell.css:819).

The title is ALWAYS the raw source filename stem: the renderer sends only `{ path: p }` (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:264) -> `library_add` resolves `title` to None (sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:127-129) -> `"title": title or src.stem` (sidecar/media_studio/library.py:315).

MEASURED (headless Chromium via app/node_modules/playwright-core, the real bundled Inter-Variable-latin.woff2 from app/renderer/src/assets/fonts, the exact CSS cascade above, stage width = window width minus the 200px rail at topTabBar.css:16; window minWidth 940 / default 1280 from app/main/main.ts:1038-1041):
  stage 740px (app minimum window 940): gridCols=3, cardW=220px, .library__item-main clientWidth=204px
    - title `Interview_with_Dr_Jane_Doe_climate_policy_final_v3_1080p` (56 ch) renders as ONE 398.6px line inside the 204px box -> ~195px past the card content edge
    - title `My.Very.Long.Video.Name.2026.1080p.WEB-DL.x264-GROUP` (52 ch) -> lines [307.5px, 112.3px]; line 1 overflows 204px by ~103px (dots are not break opportunities in Chromium; only the `-` in `WEB-DL` breaks)
    - ul.library__list scrollWidth=903 vs clientWidth=740 -> ulHasHScroll: true
  stage 1080px (default 1280 window): gridCols=4, cardW=246px, mainW=230px; same 398.6px / 307.5px lines; scrollWidth=1126 vs clientWidth=1080 -> ulHasHScroll: true
  stage 1720px (1920 window): gridCols=7, cardW=225.1px; no container h-scroll, but the 398.6px title crosses into columns 4-5 and visually collides with the next card's title (confirmed in a full-page screenshot: `Interview_with_Dr_Jane_Doe_clima` overlaps card 4, `My.Very.Long.Video.Name.2026.10` overlaps card 5's `2026-07-26 14-32-11`).
  Control: the 6-char fixture title `sample` measures 48.5px -> no overflow, which is exactly what CI captures.
- why: The title is the only human-readable identifier on a Library card, and it is mechanically derived from the filename — so every camera / screen-recorder / download name (Zoom `GMT..._Recording_1920x1080`, scene-release `Name.2026.1080p.WEB-DL.x264-GROUP`, any `snake_case` export) is 35-60 characters with no space to break on. At the app's own minimum window size the primary home surface renders titles that are simultaneously clipped mid-token (no ellipsis, so the user cannot tell they are truncated), painted on top of the adjacent card's content, and reachable only by side-scrolling a poster grid that should never scroll horizontally. Users cannot distinguish two videos whose names share a long prefix — the exact case (`Interview_..._v2` vs `_v3`) where distinguishing matters most.
- fix: Give the title the same treatment the sibling path line and the nav rail already use. Minimal, token-only change in app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840: add `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; overflow-wrap: anywhere;` plus either a 2-line clamp (`display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 2;`) or `white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis` — the rail's own comment states the intent (`app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:78-86`: "truncates rather than widening the rail, so a long surface name can never force horizontal overflow"). Keep the full name reachable: `LibraryCard` already has no `title` attribute on the span (app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:118) while the path span does (LibraryCard.tsx:133) — add `title={video.title}` there. Then add `overflow: hidden` (or `overflow: clip`) to `li.library__item` as a belt-and-braces guard so no card child can ever paint over a sibling.
- ⚠ scope correction: Library card title has no wrap/truncate rule, so long filenames are silently clipped mid-token with no ellipsis and no tooltip — making same-prefix videos indistinguishable — and can add a horizontal scrollbar to the video grid when a long title lands in the rightmost column. `.library__item-title` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845) declares only font-weight/font-size/letter-spacing/color; measured computed style is overflow:visible, white-space:normal, text-overflow:clip, overflow-wrap:normal, word-break:normal, and it is the only CSS hit for the class. Because the app wires provenance (Library.tsx:591), the path line is NOT rendered on the card (LibraryCard.tsx:132) and the path is hidden inside the collapsed `Source` disclosure, so the title is the sole at-rest identifier — and it carries no `title` attribute (LibraryCard.tsx:118, measured titleAttr=null). Title is mechanically the filename stem (Library.tsx:264 -> library_ops.py:127-129 -> library.py:315 `title or src.stem`). At the app's own minimum window (940, app/main/main.ts createWindow) the grid is 3x220px with a 204px content box (library-cards.css:11, shell.css:833-838), and a 56-char snake_case title renders as ONE 398.6px line — 194.6px past the content edge — clipped mid-token as `Interview_with_Dr_Jane_Doe_clim`. The CI fixture `sample` measures 48.5px, so app/e2e/visual/library.visual.spec.ts:30 provably cannot catch this. TWO CORRECTIONS to the original framing: (1) nothing paints OVER a neighbour — `li.library__item` is position:relative with opaque `--surface-raised` #1b212e (library-cards.css:23, tokens.css:32), so the LATER sibling covers the bleed; visible bleed is limited to the ~16px gutter and there is no text-on-text collision at any width (full-page 1920 screenshot verified). (2) The horizontal scrollbar is order-conditional, not unconditional: measured at 940, long-in-col1 and long-in-col2 produce scrollWidth == clientWidth (no scroll), while long-in-last-column and all-long produce scrollWidth 903 vs clientWidth 740 with maxScrollLeft 163. Severity: MEDIUM (ambiguous identification on the primary surface + a conditional cosmetic grid scroll), not HIGH — no content is obscured or lost, and the full name stays reachable via the `Source` disclosure and the open button's aria-label (LibraryCard.tsx:113). Fix as proposed at shell.css:840 plus `title={video.title}` at LibraryCard.tsx:118; the extra `overflow: hidden` on `li.library__item` is not needed.

`.library__item-title` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845) declares only font-weight/font-size/letter-spacing/color — computed `white-space: normal; overflow: visible; text-overflow: clip; overflow-wrap: normal; word-break: normal` — while the sibling `.library__item-path` directly below (shell.css:847-854) is fully guarded with nowrap+hidden+ellipsis. The title is always the raw source filename stem (app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:264 sends only `{path}` -> sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:127-129 -> `title or src.stem`, sidecar/media_studio/library.py:315), and the card is a narrow fixed-floor grid track (`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(215px, 1fr))`, app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:11) whose content box measures 204px at the app's 940px minimum window (app/main/main.ts:1038-1041) and 230px at the 1280 default.

Measured in headless Chromium against the real stylesheets and the real DOM (probe: C:/Users/Prekzursil/probe/lib-overflow-probe.mjs):
- `Interview_with_Dr_Jane_Doe_climate_policy_final_v3_1080p` (56 ch, no UAX-14 break opportunity — `_` is class AL) renders as ONE 381px line (398.6px with the bundled Inter woff2) in the 204px box.
