- NOT affected: names carrying an early hyphen or space — `GMT20260726-143211_Recording_1920x1080` (Zoom) wraps cleanly to [100px, 195.4px] entirely inside the card.

Two distinct symptoms, by card position:
1. A card followed by a sibling in the same row: the spill is visible for only 24px (its own 8px `--space-3` padding + the 16px `--space-5` grid gap) and is then OCCLUDED by the next card's opaque `background: var(--surface-raised)` = `#1b212e` (library-cards.css:29; app/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:32), because `li.library__item` is `position: relative; z-index: auto` (library-cards.css:23) and positioned siblings paint in tree order. The neighbour's content is NOT damaged — the title just looks arbitrarily cut with no ellipsis. Verified both-states: C:/Users/Prekzursil/probe/occl-A-shipped.png (cut at the neighbour's border) vs occl-B-nobg.png (full string appears once the neighbour backgrounds are made transparent).
2. The LAST card in a row has nothing to occlude it, so its spill enters the scrollable overflow region of `.library__list` (`overflow: auto`, shell.css:819) and produces a real horizontal scrollbar (scrollbars are styled, not hidden — shell.css:32-46): scrollWidth 885 vs clientWidth 740 at the 940 minimum window; 1107 vs 1080 at the 1280 default; none at 1920 (7 cols).

Impact is sighted-user-only: the open button's accessible name carries the full title (`cardAriaLabel`, app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:118-126, wired at LibraryCard.tsx:113), so assistive tech is unaffected. But there is no visual recovery path — LibraryCard.tsx:118 has no `title` attribute on the title span while the path span at LibraryCard.tsx:133 does — so two videos sharing a long prefix (`Interview_..._v2` vs `_v3`) are visually indistinguishable.

FIX at shell.css:840: add `overflow: hidden; overflow-wrap: anywhere;` plus either a 2-line clamp (the pattern already used at app/renderer/src/views/shorts.css:342) or `white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis` — the rail label already states this intent (app/renderer/src/components/topTabBar.css:78-86). Add `title={video.title}` at LibraryCard.tsx:118 to keep the full name reachable. `min-width: 0` is NOT needed (`.library__item-main` already has it, shell.css:837, and the title is a blockified column-flex item). A clamp/ellipsis on the title alone removes both symptoms; the extra `overflow: hidden` on `li.library__item` is optional.
- ⚠ scope correction: Library card title has no wrap/truncate rule — long filenames are hard-clipped mid-token with no ellipsis (bleeding into the 16px gutter before the neighbouring card's opaque background occludes them), and when a long-stem card lands in the trailing grid column they add a bogus horizontal scrollbar to the video grid.

`.library__item-title` (app/renderer/src/components/shell.css:840-845) declares only font-weight/font-size/letter-spacing/color — no `overflow`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `overflow-wrap` or `word-break` — while the sibling `.library__item-path` (shell.css:847-854) sets `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`. Because the title is always the raw filename stem (Library.tsx:264 → library_ops.py:127-129 → library.py:315), real camera/screen-recorder/scene-release names of 35-60 characters with no space to break on overflow the card content box: measured at the app's minimum window (940, main.ts:1040), stage 740, 3 columns of cardW 220 and `.library__item-main` clientWidth 204, `Interview_with_Dr_Jane_Doe_climate_policy_final_v3_1080p` renders as one 398.6px line — 194.6px past the box.

Two distinct user-visible consequences:
1. TRUNCATION WITHOUT AFFORDANCE (unconditional). The overflow is occluded, not overlaid: `li.library__item` is `position: relative` (library-cards.css:23) with an opaque `--surface-raised: #1b212e` (tokens.css:32), and the card to the right is always later in DOM order, so it paints over the ink. The user sees the title bleed ~16px into the gutter and then stop mid-glyph with no ellipsis — so they cannot tell the name is truncated, and two videos sharing a long prefix (`..._v2` vs `..._v3`) are indistinguishable. The full name is unreachable: the title span carries no `title` attribute (LibraryCard.tsx:118) though the path span does (LibraryCard.tsx:133).
2. BOGUS HORIZONTAL SCROLLBAR (conditional on a long-stem card occupying the trailing grid column, where nothing paints over the overflow). `.library__list` is a scroll container (shell.css:819); measured scrollWidth 903 vs clientWidth 740 at window 940, and 1126 vs 1080 at the default 1280 — a poster grid that should never scroll horizontally. With a different card ordering the same layout measures no container scroll, so this is content/order-dependent rather than universal.

CI cannot catch either: the visual baseline fixture title is `sample` (app/e2e/visual/library.visual.spec.ts:30), measured 48.5px — well inside the box.

## Thumbnail "pending" is rendered as the permanent-failure glyph, and every card's poster fires a blocking ffmpeg on the sidecar's single serial RPC thread
- surface `Library (video list, import, thumbnails, empty state)` · lens `loading-state` · verifiers 3
- evidence: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/useVideoThumbnail.ts:64 sets `setResolved('')` and only THEN awaits `rpc.thumbnail(videoId)` (:65-71). C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/LibraryCard.tsx:47 computes `showImg = posterUrl !== '' && !imgFailed`, so an empty (= pending) URL takes the same branch as a failed one and renders the terminal fallback at :59-63 (`library__thumb-fallback` ▶). There is NO third state: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/components/library-cards.css:116 `.library__thumb-fallback` and :82 `.library__thumb` carry no skeleton/pending rule (grep for `skeleton` in that sheet returns nothing). Cost side: C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/handlers/library_ops.py:171 runs `code = run(argv, total_sec=0.0)` — a synchronous ffmpeg poster extraction inside a "Direct-return" handler (:151) — and C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/rpc.py:163-164 is `for line in self._in: self.handle_line(line)`, a strictly serial single-thread loop that dispatches (:125) and only then writes the response (:156). Every freshly added video has `thumbnailPath: ""` (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/sidecar/media_studio/library.py:319), and the grid renders every matching card at once with no virtualization or lazy mount (C:/Users/Prekzursil/Documents/GitHub/Reframe/app/renderer/src/views/Library.tsx:580).
- why: On the first open of a library of N just-imported videos, the user sees N identical ▶ glyphs that are pixel-identical to "this video has no poster / poster extraction failed" — the UI reports a terminal failure while work is actually in flight. Simultaneously those N `library.thumbnail` calls queue on the sidecar's only thread, each blocking on ffmpeg, so every other RPC on screen (`readiness.summary` behind the Capabilities chip at Library.tsx:494, `library.list`, `library.remove`, the header Jobs poll) waits behind the whole poster backlog. The screen looks finished and simultaneously refuses to respond — the worst combination for this lens. Exact wall-clock per poster is UNVERIFIED (I did not run ffmpeg); the serialization mechanism itself is confirmed from rpc.py:163-164.
- fix: (1) Give the thumb a real third state: have `useVideoThumbnail` return a status (`'pending' | 'ready' | 'none'`) instead of a bare string, and render a `.skeleton`-classed 16:9 placeholder (the shimmer already exists at components/shell.css:576) while pending, reserving the ▶ glyph for the resolved-empty/onError case. (2) Stop stampeding the sidecar: mount the poster fetch behind an IntersectionObserver so only visible cards request, and/or cap in-flight `library.thumbnail` calls to 2-3 with a client-side queue. (3) Longer term, move poster extraction off the direct-return path into the existing job runner so a blocking ffmpeg can never head-of-line-block the RPC loop.
- ⚠ scope correction: LOW severity, Library posters: (a) there is no distinct pending affordance — `useVideoThumbnail` returns a bare string and sets it to '' before awaiting (useVideoThumbnail.ts:64-71), so LibraryCard.tsx:47 renders the same neutral ▶ placeholder for pending as for no-poster, and library-cards.css has no skeleton rule (0 grep hits) even though the shimmer exists and is used for the list-level load at Library.tsx:553 and the three-state pattern already ships in the sibling CapabilitiesChip.tsx:68-85. The glyph carries no failure semantics (real failure is the "Failed" text badge at libraryModel.ts:96,107; the same ▶ is the empty-state placeholder at Library.tsx:565), so this is a missing-loading-affordance polish gap, not a false failure report. (b) The on-demand `library.thumbnail` calls are uncapped (Library.tsx:580 renders every card, sidecar.ts:446 writes each request immediately with no client queue), so the first-ever render of N poster-less videos serializes a MEASURED 0.23-0.86 s (median ~0.35 s) ffmpeg poster extraction each on the sidecar's single RPC thread (rpc.py:163-164, library_ops.py:171), making user-initiated RPCs such as `library.remove` feel laggy for roughly 0.35xN seconds. Scope limits that must be stated inline: it is once per video ever (library_ops.py:165-167 + library.py:362-375 persist the poster); `readiness.summary` and `library.list` are NOT affected because both precede the cards (Library.tsx:171/220-231/494); the renderer thread is never blocked; and `library.add` already spawns a comparable synchronous ffprobe (0.13-0.38 s measured) on the same serial path. A capped in-flight queue (2-3) plus a `.skeleton` pending state are cheap and still worth doing; the IntersectionObserver and job-runner migration are not justified at this measured cost.
- ⚠ scope correction: Substance stands; three wording overreaches should be tightened (C2-style re-scoping, not a refutation):

(a) "rendered as the permanent-failure glyph" → the ▶ fallback is the app's SHARED "no poster" glyph, not a dedicated error icon (LibraryCard.tsx:41-42 defines it as missing-OR-failed, and the same ▶ is the generic empty-state poster at Library.tsx:565). Correct claim: pending is pixel-identical to missing/failed because useVideoThumbnail returns a bare string (useVideoThumbnail.ts:50,77) with no status channel — the user cannot tell "working on it" from "there will never be one".

(b) headline "every card's poster fires a blocking ffmpeg" is wider than the code → it is every card WITHOUT a cached poster: useVideoThumbnail.ts:55-57 skips the RPC when thumbnailPath is set, and library_ops.py:165-167 short-circuits when data_dir/thumbnails/<id>.jpg exists. The body already scopes this to just-imported videos; the headline should say so too. A warm library issues zero thumbnail RPCs.

(c) the "Capabilities chip waits behind the whole poster backlog" example is the weakest instance at first paint: CapabilitiesChip (Library.tsx:494) precedes the <ul> (Library.tsx:579), so its readiness.summary is written to stdin before the card effects (UNVERIFIED: I did not instrument React 18 effect/write ordering). The head-of-line mechanism is better evidenced by the interval poll at useActiveJobs.ts:47 and any user-triggered library.remove/library.list, which unambiguously queue behind the backlog.

(d) magnitude, for severity calibration: sidecar/media_studio/features/shorts.py:206-217 puts `-ss 1` BEFORE `-i` (fast input seek) with `-frames:v 1`, so each poster is a cheap single-frame grab and the dominant per-call cost is ffmpeg process spawn, not decode. Per-poster wall-clock remains UNVERIFIED (I did not run ffmpeg). N sequential process spawns on the only RPC thread still serialize the channel, so "high" is defensible for the combined defect, but a reviewer could argue medium on the cost half alone. Settling experiment: time N=50 library.thumbnail calls against a cold thumbnails dir and measure the added latency of a concurrent library.list.
- ⚠ scope correction: Thumbnail "pending" is visually indistinguishable from the resolved-no-poster state, and on the first paint after an import each posterless card fires a blocking ffmpeg on the sidecar's single serial RPC thread.

Loading-state half: useVideoThumbnail returns a bare string with no pending value — it is '' both before the RPC (useVideoThumbnail.ts:51, :64) and after a failure (:69-71) — and LibraryCard.tsx:47 collapses pending, resolved-empty, and img-onError into one boolean, so all three render the identical .library__thumb-fallback ▶ (LibraryCard.tsx:59-63; library-cards.css:116, which carries no pending/skeleton rule). The glyph does not claim failure — it is the same generic no-poster mark used for the empty library (Library.tsx:565) — but work in flight is byte-identically indistinguishable from work that is finished with no result. There is no third state.

Cost half, scoped: only cards with an empty thumbnailPath AND no cached data_dir/thumbnails/<id>.jpg run ffmpeg. useVideoThumbnail.ts:55-58 skips the RPC entirely once thumbnailPath is set, and library_ops.py:165-167 short-circuits before ffmpeg when the poster exists — so a warmed library costs zero ffmpeg. The reachable case is the first paint after an import, where library.py:319 leaves every new video at thumbnailPath: "" and Library.tsx:580 mounts all matching cards at once (`visible`, :457-460, is filter+sort with no pagination or virtualization). sidecar.ts:419-453 writes all N frames to stdin with no queue or cap, and rpc.py:163-164 dispatches them strictly serially, each blocking in ffmpeg.py:338 proc.wait() inside the direct-return handler at library_ops.py:151/171.

Consequence, scoped: the renderer stays interactive (search, sort, selection, hover are local), but every sidecar-backed affordance stalls behind the poster backlog — readiness.summary behind the Capabilities chip (Library.tsx:494), library.list, library.remove, and the 5s job.list heartbeat (useActiveJobs.ts:40, :47), which itself keeps enqueuing more work during the stall. Beyond 60s of backlog those queued calls do not just wait, they REJECT (sidecar.ts:73 REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, :431-436), surfacing as spurious failures on operations the user never connected to thumbnails. Per-poster wall-clock is UNVERIFIED (no ffmpeg run), so the N at which the 60s cliff is crossed is unquantified; the serialization and the timeout are both confirmed from source.

Proposed fix is unchanged and well-targeted; the shimmer primitive it reuses exists at shell.css:576.

## Re-running "Start transcription" silently destroys diarization and hand-typed speaker names — no warning, no confirm, no undo
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: Primary action has no guard: `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:176` (`<button onClick={start} disabled={running || !videoId}>`) and `Transcribe.tsx:73` (`setTranscript(null)`) — no confirmation dialog anywhere in the file.
The job overwrites the persisted transcript unconditionally: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:438` — `project.data["transcript"] = transcript`.
Diarization writes into that SAME key: `sidecar/media_studio/features/diarize.py:343` — `self._save_project(video_id, {**fresh, "transcript": labelled})`, and the user's hand-typed friendly speaker names at `diarize.py:376` — `fresh["transcript"] = renamed`.
The sidecar already knows this hazard and guards only the OTHER direction: `diarize.py:338-342` refuses to save when `fresh.get("transcript") != transcript` ("Fail loud instead of last-writer-wins"). Nothing guards transcribe clobbering diarize.
The Transcribe tab is always present and always re-clickable: `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:54` / `Workspace.tsx:298`.
- why: Nielsen error-prevention plus user-control-and-freedom. A user who ran Diarize and renamed SPEAKER_00 -> "Alice", SPEAKER_01 -> "Bob" loses all of it the instant they press the Transcribe panel's only primary button — a plausible action if they want a different language or think the first run was poor. The loss is server-side, irreversible (no versioning, no .bak of the transcript key), and completely unannounced: the panel does not even acknowledge that a transcript exists (see the recognition-over-recall finding).
- fix: Make the destructive case explicit. When a transcript already exists on the project, change the button copy to "Re-transcribe" and gate it behind a confirm that names what will be lost ("This replaces the existing transcript and clears speaker labels"). Cheaper interim: have `_transcribe_and_persist` (media_ops.py:435-444) snapshot the prior transcript to `project.data["transcriptPrevious"]` and expose an Undo in the panel.
- ⚠ scope correction: Not a scope reduction — the headline, surface, severity (high) and proposed fix all stand. Two word-level precision tightenings only:

1. "overwrites the persisted transcript unconditionally" → the write IS gated, by `if not job_ctx.cancelled:` at `media_ops.py:435`. Accurate phrasing: "on any run that completes without being cancelled, the write at `media_ops.py:438` replaces the transcript with no check for an existing one." The cancel gate only prevents persisting a partial run; it gives diarization data zero protection.

2. "irreversible" → split the two losses, which actually sharpens the finding. The stored state is irreversibly overwritten (no `.bak`, no history, `autosave` is debounce-only). The hand-typed friendly names are genuinely unrecoverable human input. The diarization CLUSTERING, by contrast, is recomputable by re-running the Diarize panel at GPU cost — but that is not an undo, and because the roster comes from greedy clustering (`diarize.py:218-220`, `roster(labels)`) a re-run may renumber SPEAKER_NN, so the user cannot reliably re-apply their remembered mapping either. Recommended wording: "the overwrite is unrecoverable — the hand-typed names are gone for good, and re-running Diarize is a re-computation (with possibly renumbered speakers), not an undo."
- ⚠ scope correction: Re-running "Start transcription" silently overwrites the persisted transcript, discarding diarization speaker labels and the user's hand-typed friendly speaker names, with no warning, confirm, or undo. Scope correction: the diarization itself is recomputable (re-click "Label speakers", Diarize.tsx:143) — the genuinely unrecoverable loss is the hand-typed names only (typically 2-4 strings). The consequence is still output-visible, not cosmetic: those names feed exported subtitle cue text via subtitles.py:210-224 gated on `captionSpeakerLabels` (media_ops.py:56-60), so captions silently lose their speaker prefixes. Aggravating factors: the button copy never changes (Transcribe.tsx:177) and neither the Transcribe nor Diarize panel hydrates persisted state (Transcribe.tsx:47, Diarize.tsx:51), so the user cannot see what is at risk; and the sidecar's two other writers of this key already guard it (diarize.py:338-342, shortmaker_ops.py:108-110), making transcribe.start the sole unguarded writer. Severity: MEDIUM (recoverable at the cost of one GPU run plus re-typing, but silent and undetectable until after export), not high.

## The panel never loads the existing transcript — it always renders the blank "never transcribed" state, and the result vanishes on any tab switch
- surface `Transcribe phase` · lens `intuitive-flow` · verifiers 3
- evidence: State starts null with no load-on-mount: `app/renderer/src/features/Transcribe.tsx:47` (`useState<Transcript | null>(null)`); the component's only two effects are the progress relay `Transcribe.tsx:55-63` and the unmount teardown `Transcribe.tsx:147`. There is no `project.open` / transcript fetch.
The data is already client-side: `app/renderer/src/components/api.ts:76` — `transcript?: Transcript;` on `Project`, and Workspace already fetched the project at `app/renderer/src/views/Workspace.tsx:166`, but forwards only `tracks` (`Workspace.tsx:266`) and mounts the panel with just an id (`Workspace.tsx:298` — `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} />`).
Switching tabs unmounts the panel (the `switch (active)` at `Workspace.tsx:268-300` returns a different component), so the rendered transcript is lost.
The rest of the app DOES surface this state: `app/renderer/src/views/libraryModel.ts:108` pushes a "Transcript" badge and `libraryModel.ts:123` announces 'transcript ready' / 'no transcript'.
The sidecar persists it and flips the flag: `sidecar/media_studio/handlers/media_ops.py:436-441`.
- why: Nielsen recognition-rather-than-recall and visibility-of-system-status. The one screen whose whole job is the transcript is the one screen that cannot tell you whether you have one. A user who transcribed yesterday (or five minutes ago, then clicked Subtitles and back) sees an empty panel that reads as "not done yet" — and the only affordance offered is the button that destroys the existing transcript and any diarization on it. This finding is the direct cause of the clobber finding above.
- fix: Pass the already-loaded transcript down (`Workspace.tsx:298` -> `<Transcribe videoId={video.id} transcript={project?.transcript ?? null} />`, mirroring how `tracks` is passed to Subtitles at `Workspace.tsx:271`) and seed `useState` from it, rendering the existing summary/segments immediately. Then relabel the action "Re-transcribe" in that state.
- ⚠ scope correction: Defect and severity stand; only the headline wording needs tightening. Precise version: "On every mount the Transcribe panel renders its empty state regardless of whether a transcript already exists — it never loads one — so the result is lost on any tab switch." (The literal word "always" is loose: within a single mount, after a successful run, Transcribe.tsx:200-218 does render the summary. Also "never transcribed" is not UI copy — the panel renders no such string at all, which is arguably worse than an explicit label.)
- ⚠ scope correction: Wording tightened only (scope and HIGH severity stand, finding NOT an overclaim): "The Transcribe panel never loads an existing transcript — it renders no transcript and no status either way, so a video that was already transcribed is indistinguishable from one that never was, and a completed run is lost on any tab switch. In that state the panel's only affordance, the unguarded 'Start transcription' button, overwrites `project.data['transcript']` wholesale (media_ops.py:438), destroying the per-segment `speaker` labels, the `speakers` roster, and any user-renamed speaker names that diarization persisted into that same object (diarize.py:219-220, 182-198)."

Corroborating: app/renderer/src/features/providersKeys.css:5 and app/renderer/src/features/spendCap.css:3 both assert "the global :focus-visible ring (from components/shell.css) are inherited" — measurably false for buttons; app/renderer/src/panels/modelsSystem.css:58 shows a sibling panel already patching this per-panel.
- **Model-download failures are never surfaced: `assets.ensure` is a long job but all three call sites treat its `{jobId}` ack as completion** — `Settings - Models & System` / `error-state` — `app/renderer/src/panels/ModelsSystemPanel.tsx:566` `await api.assets.ensure([asset]);` — plus `:524` (Apply-recommendation downloads) and `:601` (readiness fix action). `app/renderer/src/lib/rpc/client.ts:393` types it `ensure: (names: string[]): Promise<JobHandle> => rpc('assets.ensure', { names })` — it resolves with `{jobId}` immediately. `sidecar/media_studio/assets/rpc.py:91-92` returns `{"jobId": job.id}` after `ctx.jobs.start(job_body)`. Real failures happen INSIDE that job body: `sidecar/media_studio/assets/manager.py:728` `raise AssetError(...)` when nothing installed, `:731` returns `failed:[{name,error}]` on partial failure, `:686` `guard_network(...)` refuses when Offline mode is on. `manager.py:662` states outright: "Failures raise (-> job.done error payload)". The panel contains no `onJobDone`, no `onProgress`, no `job.status` poll (verified by grep over the whole file). The repo's own contract note forbids exactly this: `app/renderer/src/features/_api.ts:172` "a panel MUST subscribe to `job.done` (via `onJobDone`) to read the result". The correct implementation of this same RPC exists at `app/renderer/src/features/Assets.tsx:103-118`, which uses `waitForJobDone` (rejects on the `{error}` payload). Only mitigation is the Jobs drawer, which prints the bare status word with no reason: `app/renderer/src/components/JobQueue.tsx:213-215`.

# REFUTED (94) — recorded so they are not re-raised

A majority of 3 independent adversarial verifiers **refuted** each item below. They are
listed in full because the whole point of the REFUTED tier is that a later pass can see a
claim has already been examined and rejected, rather than re-raising it. Recovered from the
workflow journal via `docs/validation/tools/join_by_agentid.py`.

Severity is the ORIGINAL claimed severity, not a verdict — a `[critical]` line below is a
critical-sounding claim that did **not** survive verification.

- [critical] Make sub-panel is not a tabpanel: activating the "Make" tab enters an unnamed, unrelated container — `screen-reader`
- [critical] Active sub-tab's aria-controls dangles in EVERY front-door state (critical aria-valid-attr-value) — `axe-a11y`
- [critical] Timeline panel: all cue editing is mouse-exclusive — keyboard users are locked out of Split, Merge, retime and cue-text — `keyboard-nav`
- [critical] Gallery and Batch tabs carry the SAME dangling aria-controls as the known tabpanel-make bug — a one-line fix for the reported instance leaves both broken — `axe-a11y`
- [high] Manual export has no local progress and no cancel for up to 35 minutes — `intuitive-flow`
- [high] Subtitles cue editor: unvirtualised list + full-list re-render (and a needless re-sort) on every keystroke — `perf-render`
- [high] Timeline cue-edge drag: whole lane re-renders and the dragged node is destroyed/recreated on every mousemove — `perf-render`
- [high] Cancel and silent-completion change job state with zero announcement; setMessage('Cancelled') is dead code — `screen-reader`
- [high] Every primary Reframe action disables the button you just pressed — focus falls to <body> for the whole job — `focus-management`
- [high] Approve / Discard / Reinstate / Reset unmount the exact button being activated — focus lost to <body> on every candidate decision — `focus-management`
- [high] No visible focus indicator at all in Windows High Contrast: the single focus ring is box-shadow-only with outline suppressed — `focus-management`
- [high] Library's import/removal toasts ride an on-demand-mounted live region while the app's correctly-implemented, permanently-mounted ToastHost sits unused — `screen-reader`
- [high] Caption-box drag lifts state to MakeShorts, re-rendering the whole front door (including the unmemoized ShortMaker panel) once per animation frame — with a forced layout read in the same handler — `perf-render`
- [high] Library import failures are reported only in a route-scoped fallback toast strip — the app-wide sticky ToastHost is never wired, so failures auto-expire in 6s and are destroyed (or never shown at all) on navigation — `state-persistence`
- [high] Manual export runs up to 35 min with zero progress — the real progress stream exists and the sibling AI flow already uses it — `loading-state`
- [high] Video-list load has no pending state and swallows its error, so "loading", "library empty" and "list failed" are one indistinguishable dead end — `loading-state`
- [high] First transcription can trigger an unlabelled ~1.6 GB model download that no readiness surface reports and Offline mode does not block — `destructive-actions`
- [high] Batch button's accessible name is the literal placeholder "Make N shorts", hiding the real clip count from AT — `screen-reader`
- [high] A failed project.open leaves the Workspace mounted and interactive but projectless, with a bare error string and no reachable retry — `error-state`
- [high] Cancelling a Transcribe or Convert job gives zero feedback — the "Cancelled" message is written into state that is unmounted at that exact instant — `screen-reader`
- [high] In-flight transcription is orphaned by any navigation — unmount aborts the wait, nothing re-attaches, and Start invites a duplicate GPU run — `state-persistence`
- [high] Empty library is indistinguishable from "no video selected" — the front door tells the user to pick a video that cannot exist, with no way to add one — `empty-state`
- [high] Every long-running Edit action disables the control that was just activated, so focus is lost to <body> for the whole job and never restored — `focus-management`
- [high] A library.list failure renders "No videos yet" — a load error is presented as an empty library — `error-state`
- [high] Raw sidecar internal-exception strings are surfaced verbatim, with zero recovery action anywhere on the surface — `error-state`
- [high] Per-file import failures auto-expire after 6s because Library is never wired to the app toast sink, whose error toasts are deliberately sticky — `error-state`
- [high] Gallery red text uses `--status-error` where the repo mandates `--status-error-text`; Delete-hover measures 2.93:1 — `token-consistency`
- [high] Raw sidecar exception messages are rendered verbatim as the Transcribe error text — `error-state`
- [high] Transcribe error state offers no recovery action, bypassing the app's already-wired job.retry + toast pipeline — `error-state`
- [high] Lineage drawer has no Escape, never receives focus, and sits last in the DOM behind ~800 tab stops — its content is keyboard-unreachable in practice — `keyboard-nav`
- [high] Only a dark theme exists — and the Transcribe surface's ONLY focus indicator is a box-shadow, which `forced-colors: active` (Windows High Contrast, usually a LIGHT palette) erases — `dark-light-parity`
- [high] Re-export from the gallery unmounts the whole panel and drops keyboard focus to <body> with no handoff — `focus-management`
- [high] The only recovery offered for reframe provisioning/engine-unavailable failures is a "Retry" that is guaranteed to fail identically — `error-state`
- [high] "Start transcription" disables itself in the same commit it is activated, dumping focus to document.body — and the panel then contains zero focusable controls, so there is nothing to tab to and no keyboard route to Cancel — `focus-management`
- [high] Raw sidecar/ffmpeg exception text — exit codes, absolute paths, up to 500 chars of ffmpeg stderr — is rendered verbatim to the user — `error-state`
- [high] `acknowledged` is set optimistically before `batch.start` and never rolled back — a failed start dead-ends the consent card with its only control disabled — `ipc-boundary`
